p.seg: 1.1 《The Original Origins of the Fixed Laws for the Zhǒngmín, the Meritorious Deeds of Sages and Worthies, the Omens of Departures and Arrivals, the Equilibrium of Qi, and the Annual Successions in the Chronicles of Teachers and Assistants to the Tàipíng Jīnquè Dìchén Hòushèng Dìjūn》
I asked:
"The Sāntǒng rotate and revolve;
there is departing and there is coming.
The people must have a ruler;
may I know his surname and name?"
"Excellent!"
"Why do you ask this again?"
"An enlightened master is hard to encounter,
and a favorable time is easy to let pass.
I cannot bear my eager yearning,
and wish to request to hear of it.
Being ignorant and dim, I venture to speak;
my transgression is heavy, and my fear is deep."
"Alas!
It is not a transgression.
Heaven has moved you to ask,
so as to enlighten those of later times.
Now those who awaken will recognize the orthodox
and cast away the false to obtain the true.
If I were not to speak,
I fear Heaven would be despondent,
and the chaos would not be pacified in time.
Walk calmly and sit down;
I shall explain the Way to you.
You will naturally come to understand it clearly
and have no more doubts.
The Heaven and Earth of the past and the Heaven and Earth of today
have a beginning and an end;
they are the same and not different.
Good at the start and evil at the end,
with flourishing and decline in between,
and one success followed by one failure.
There are the Yángjiǔ and Bǎiliù catastrophes;
after six and nine the cycle is complete,
and when it is complete, there is great destruction.
Heaven and Earth are mixed like ground pulp,
and people and things are crushed and obliterated.
Only those who have accumulated merit will escape it
and forever become the Zhòngmín.
Among the Zhòngmín, in wisdom and knowledge,
there are still differences in rank,
and they have not yet reached perfect unity;
thus they still require a teacher and a ruler.
When the ruler is a sage and the teacher is enlightened,
their teachings will ensure immortality.
Through accumulated refinement, one becomes a sage;
therefore they are called the Zhòngmín.
The Zhòngmín
are of the kind of sages and worthies who possess long life.
The Great Lord of Long Life is titled Tàipíng Zhēnzhèng Tàiyī Miàoqì,
Huángtiān Shàngqīng Jīnquè Hòushèng Jiǔxuán Dìjūn.
His surname is Lǐ.
He is the descendant of the Gāoshàng Tàizhī
and the progeny of the Yùhuáng Xūwú.
In the fifteenth year of Tàihuáng during the time of Xuányuán Dìjūn,
the zhào energy formed in the Bǐngzǐ year.
His form was completed in the first year of Huángpíng, a Jiǎshēn year.
At the Mǎo hour on the Jiǎzǐ day, the third day of the ninth month of the seventh year of Shànghé, a Gēngyín year,
when Punishment and Virtue restrained each other
at the moment of their direct alignment,
he was born in the Běixuán Yùguó,
the Tiāngāng Língjìng,
within the Rénniǎo Gépéngláishān,
amidst the Lǐgǔ valley.
There was the Mother of Shàngxuán Xūshēng,
the Chamber of the Nine Mysteries,
situated on the shaded side of the valley.
When the Mother of Xuánxū first conceived,
she dreamed that mysterious clouds, the sun, and the moon enveloped her form,
and the lightning of the six energies moved her spirit.
Thus, through a subtle resonance with the Way of Yang,
she became pregnant with the Perfected Man.
On the morning of his birth,
three suns emerged from the east.
After he was born,
nine dragons spat forth divine water.
Thus he took his surname from the spiritual valley,
and used Yàojǐng as his name.
At the age of three,
his body embodied the Way and condensed the Truth,
and his words became golden blossoms.
At the age of five,
he would often look up at the sun and rejoice at the beginning,
and face the moon and sigh at the end.
Above, he observed the brilliant splendor of the Yang energy;
below, he saw the waning and decay of the Yin way.
Thereupon he gathered his hún soul and harmonized his pò soul,
guarded his embryo and treasured his spirit,
recorded his essence and filled his blood,
and fortified his fluids and condensed his sinews.
At the age of seven,
he then learned to swallow light and consume the rosy mists,
masticating the root of the sun.
When he reached the age of fourteen,
he possessed a golden appearance and a jade-like face.
He abandoned the secular world and left behind emotions,
embracing transformation to save the world.
His essence resonated with the Tàisù,
and he received instruction from the Sānyuán.
He practiced with the Sāndòng
and his work was based on the Nine Directions.
At the age of twenty-one,
he lived in solitude and blunted his sharpness.
At the age of twenty-eight,
he united with his consort and harmonized his light.
At the age of thirty-five,
he spread the mysterious ford,
and his merit and virtue reached far and wide.
At the age of forty-two,
he received the mandate to be the Hòushèng Dìjūn.
This is the same and not different from those
who attained the Way in the previous heaven and became Imperial Lords.
Since he receives his prophecy now,
he is called the Hòushèng.
The Former Sages and the Latter Sages,
their Way is one.
He ascends to the Palace of Shàngqīng,
wanders in the center of the Palace of Tàijí,
and governs the heavens of the ten directions below.
He seals and holds sway over hundreds of millions of people,
inspecting all the heavens, rivers, and seas,
the sources of the earth, mountains, and forests.
There are none who do not look up to and follow him.
He governs the nine layers and ten tiers;
therefore he is called the Jiǔxuán.
At the age of seventy,
he determined his infinite lifespan,
adapted to the suitability of hiding or appearing,
edited the techniques of immortality,
and compiled the formulas for long life.
He took the precious scriptures, talismans, and diagrams,
the subtle methods of the three ages of antiquity,
and secreted them in jade cases,
attended by divine officials.
Their transmission and reception have rules,
and their concealment or revelation have their proper times.
He handed down plans and established canons
to bestow upon the Zhòngmín.
Those who cannot practice them
are not the Zhòngmín.
Now, since the opening of Heaven and Earth,
the pure wind has gradually distanced itself,
the Qi of Huángpíng has become hidden,
and calamities and pestilences flow across the land.
Since the time of the Shànghuáng,
and from the Three and Five onwards,
warfare, epidemics, floods, and fires
have competed and arisen in turn.
This is all because the myriad people's
hearts are heterodox and their forms are false.
They destroy the Five Virtues
and contend in indulging the Six Emotions.
They give rein to cruelty and display violence,
encroaching upon and insulting one another.
The honored and the humble, the elder and the younger,
the noble and the base are in chaotic separation.
This has caused the two principles to lose their order,
the seven luminaries to deviate from their paths,
and the three powers to undergo strange transformations,
with eerie falsehoods in abundance.
Spirits and ghosts harm each other,
people and things wither and perish,
and disasters and misfortunes arrive repeatedly.
They do not awaken and do not repent,
and ten thousand poisons are allowed to run rampant
beyond counting.
There are four great evils:
War, Sickness,
Flood, and Fire.
When the Yángjiǔ completes its cycle,
if the solitary Yin is exuberant, then floods overflow.
When the Bǎiliù completes its turn,
if the Yang is partially ascendant, then fires arise.
From the time before Yáo,
there is no need to recount further.
From the Táng onwards,
I will now briefly state it.
You should carefully remember and recognize this,
and urgently seek to guard against and avoid them.
After the flood of Yáo,
the fire of Tāng became a disaster.
After this, there have been small floods and fires throughout the land;
when sins are heavy, they are beckoned accordingly,
but these are not the Great Yángjiǔ or the Great Bǎiliù.
Within the Great Jiǔliù,
there must be the major and minor Jiǎshēn years.
The Jiǎshēn year is the appointed time,
when ghosts confront men.
Disasters have different degrees of severity,
and sins and blessings have different measures of thickness.
Since the years and places differ,
the shifts and movements are not the same.
For the average among the average people,
it will naturally arrive according to the schedule.
For those above or below the average,
it can move up or down;
with the advancement or retreat of the upper and lower,
the rising and falling are not fixed.
If one does evil, it is hastened;
if one does good, it is delayed.
Those who are unable to be diligent
cannot attain the Dào.
It is only possible to extend the expected term
according to the amount of one's merit.
Therefore, during the periods of Bǎi Liù and Yáng Jiǔ,
whether they occur sooner or later,
following the regular cycles of the great calendar,
the degree of severity is determined.
Calculating from the Dīnghài year of the Táng era,
another forty-six years pass.
In the interval between,
the year of Jiǎshēn
is the Xiǎo Jiǎshēn.
War, illness, and fire
will alternately cause disasters,
but there will not yet be a great flood.
Minor floods will surge everywhere,
becoming somewhat more severe in those years and lands.
After another fifty-five years,
in the Dīnghài year,
in the interval between,
there is a year of Jiǎshēn.
This is the Dà Jiǎshēn when the three disasters occur together,
and a great flood will wash them away.
Whenever the Xiǎo or Dà Jiǎshēn arrives,
it eliminates the wicked people
and delivers the good people.
The good people become the Zhòngmín,
and the wicked people become minced mush.
Shortly before its arrival,
various demons will arise everywhere in conflict,
pestilential toxins will surge above,
and the fires of war will encircle below.
Floods will appear from no fixed direction,
and the wicked will sink away in succession.
During these fifteen years,
extending up to thirty years,
the disasters of the year will be severe,
and the sages and worthies will go into hiding.
The Shénrén of the Dàdào will further dispatch Zhēnxiān and Shàngshì to go forth and spread the teachings,
guiding the people with great care.
They will encourage the high and exhort the low;
those who follow will become Zhòngmín,
while those who do not follow will sink away,
sinking to become minced mush.
The wicked and evil will all be washed away.
Of the Zhòngmín and those of highest goodness,
only one out of ten will remain.
Of those of middling or lower goodness,
Heaven will destroy more than half;
the remaining half will flourish and rise daily.
This will require a Shèngjūn and a Míngshī;
great ministers will then descend and appear.
After the Xiǎo Jiǎshēn
and before the Rénshēn year,
the Lord of the Xiǎo Jiǎshēn will be a sage and worthy,
strict, enlightened, benevolent, and kind.
Without harming principles or causing disorder,
he will extend years and longevity.
Those who study diligently can become Divine Immortals,
but if they cannot deeply study the Tàipíng Jīng
and cannot long practice the affairs of Tàipíng,
then during the brief time of Tàipíng, their names
cannot be fixed.
For those who practice it, the Sīmìng records them in the Green Register;
the Sīlù must not record them in black text.
Those in black text shall die;
those in the Green Register shall live.
The register of life and death
is in the celestial Míngtáng.
The celestial Way has no favorites;
it aids only the good.
The good ones practice the Tàipíng Way
and achieve Tàipíng.
Achieving Xiǎo Tàipíng,
they join in virtue with the Dà Tàipíng Jūn.
The one whose name is fixed as the Dà Tàipíng Jūn
is Lǐ Jūn.
On the sixth day of the third month in the year of Rénchén,
he will manifest and enter the world,
riding the Sānsù Jǐngyú,
followed by flying chariots and ten thousand dragons.
He will select the good to be the Zhòngmín
and the scholars to be immortal officials.
He will establish rules and institutes,
reward good and block evil,
prevent the roots of sin,
and urge those of meritorious deeds
to be diligent without slackening.
They will attain the state of a Divine Perfected Being
and join in virtue with the Emperor.
Those who slacken, retreat, and fall into evil,
their evil appearances will be recorded daily
to eventually fill the ranks of the minced mush.
The Ultimate Gentlemen and High Gentlemen,
with clear and profound wisdom,
will understand clearly without doubt.
They will diligently increase their progress,
maintain and practice the Emperor's instructions,
and remember the assistants of the great Divine Lord,
none of whom they dare to forget.
The Shèngjūn and wise assistants,
and the divine officials who protect the people,
will naturally attain immortality
and forever remain as Zhòngmín.
Rising to become officials of the immortal perfected,
they will finally ascend to the rank of the Hòushèng.
“The Tàishī of the Hòushèng Lǐ Jūn is surnamed Péng.
He studied the Dào before Lǐ Jūn.
His position is the Tàiwēi Zuǒzhēn.
During the time of the Rénhuáng, the Bǎohuáng Dàojūn and he were often ordered to enfeoff and confer titles upon the myriad people.
He serves as the Tàishī for Lǐ Jūn.
His seat of governance is the Língshàng Guāng Tái of the Běitáng Gōng in Tàiwēi.
Every two thousand five hundred years, he changes his name,
turning and moving through the Tàixū,
and circulating through the Bāmíng.
He ascends to the Unsurpassed
and descends to the Lowest.
Rare is the perfected official who gets to see his radiant countenance.”
“The Shàngxiàng of the Hòushèng Lǐ Jūn is the Qīngtóng Jūn of the Fāngzhū Gōng.”
“The Shàngbǎo of the Hòushèng Lǐ Jūn is the Nánjí Yuánjūn of the Tàidān Gōng.”
“The Shàngfù of the Hòushèng Lǐ Jūn is the Tàisù Zhēnjūn of the Báishān Gōng.”
“The Shàngzǎi of the Hòushèng Lǐ Jūn is the Zǒngzhēn Wáng Jūn of the Xīchéng Gōng.”
"These five people,
are one Shī and four Fǔ.
Those who are Fǔ
act as fathers
and provide support.
They are honored like a father,
and they hold things up so they may proceed;
collectively they are titled Fǔ.
Distinguishing them individually, they are
the Zuǒfǔ and Yòubì,
the Qiányí and Hòuchéng.
The Chéng,
in speaking and initiating matters,
remedies omissions and provides fullness,
making decisions and proclaiming them;
this is the Zǎi.
The Yí,
facing forward with thoughts not yet attained,
providing enlightenment and clarity;
this is the Fù.
The Bì,
surely settles hesitations,
which is the Bǎo.
Supporting the ruler and following the Shī,
moving in a cycle to enter the Dào;
this is the Xiàng.
Observing the omens of the four and five,
they detail all that is feasible or not,
assisting in the expansion of the correct transformation;
collectively they are called Fǔshī.
During times of leisure,
if there are doubts ahead,
ask the Fù.
If looking back there are concerns about omissions,
ask the Chéng.
If there is obscurity on the right,
ask the Bì.
If there is lack of clarity on the left,
ask the Fǔ.
By consulting the four Fǔ,
the Xiàng, Bǎo, Fù, and Zǎi,
success lies with the Shī;
none can be omitted.
Sacred emperors leave behind these models,
so that later generations may follow them.
Upon entering, there is the Bǎo;
the Bǎo handles affairs.
Yīn belongs to the right,
quietly treasuring the truth.
Upon exiting, there is the Shī;
the Shī handles affairs.
Yáng belongs to the left,
movement returning to stillness.
Reaching this point is most difficult,
so I have omitted the Fǔ and Xiàng to speak of the Shī.
Looking forward, there is the Fù;
the Fù is in front,
expounding and discussing the main points.
Looking back, there is the Zǎi;
the Zǎi is in the rear,
deciding between right and wrong.
The remaining dukes, ministers, officials, immortal perfected, sagely ranks, grandees, and office-holders number three hundred and sixty-one,
with thirty-six thousand subordinates,
and three hundred and sixty thousand subordinates leading them,
while the common people are ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, and a hundred million times more.
Always cause the twenty-four perfected ones to secretly teach the children who have the intention;
all are subordinate to the Fāngzhū Shàngxiàng,
and cannot be spoken of in full.
Just sincerely contemplate the greatness,
and naturally investigate the small details."
"Excellent!
Today I asked about my doubts,
and I have heard your commands."
I asked:
"What does Lǐ Jūn constantly practice
that he attained such a high perfected state?
Can the studies and achievements of the Tàishī and the four Fǔ be heard?"
"Excellent!
Do you ask so diligently
for the sake of the foolish, who are lost and do not believe in the Dào,
whose learning is not firm,
who fluctuate and lose their constancy,
falling into low, mean suffering?
Now I shall speak to you of it.
From the beginningless past,
they have accumulated practices for a long time;
every good and every evil
cannot be fully stated,
and speaking of them is of no benefit.
Now I will take what was recently practiced,
through which they achieved high nobility, the Língshū Zǐwén as the essential.
The High Morning Master of the Jade Guardian of Eastern Fluorescence, Qīngtóng Dàjūn,
the Dàjūn purified himself in the Cold Numinous Cinnabar Palace,
within the Yellow Chamber,
for three years,
then ascended to the Shàngqīng Jīnquè.
At the Jīnquè are the four Heavenly Emperors,
with the Tàipíng Dàojūn situated at their left and right.
Dwelling in the Palace of Pervading Perfection of the Jasper Terrace of Grand Space,
the Room of Level Jade,
within the Golden Radiance,
with fifty thousand attendant maidens and various perfected ones,
poisonous dragons and electric tigers,
beasts that reach to the sky,
spreading poison and displaying their might,
guarding the gates and holding the passes,
with giant serpents a thousand fathoms long
guarding the walls and banks.
Flying dragons and rushing sparrows,
the Péng of the Dark Sea and strange birds,
pecking and flexing their claws,
arrayed in the wide courtyard.
Heavenly majesty is brilliant and magnificent,
streaming light in the eight directions.
The wind drums the mysterious banners,
whirling and dancing the yak-tail canopies;
jade trees stimulate sounds,
branches of fine jade make their own music;
many blow numinous songs,
phoenixes cry in the Mysterious Greatness;
divine consorts sing in chorus,
qílín dance and luán-birds march;
the eight sounds of the Heavenly Harmony,
nine harmonies and a hundred gatherings.
Qīngtóng prostrated and crawled forward,
requesting to receive the Língshū Zǐwén,
and the twenty-four orally transmitted secrets contained in the scripture:
the first is the True Record of Contemplation,
to be memorized in the darkness;
the second is the Detailed Preservation of Immortal Prohibitions without forgetting;
the third is Gathering the Flying Roots,
and Swallowing the Essence of the Sun;
the fourth is Ingesting the Numinous Talisman of Enlightenment;
the fifth is Ingesting the Brilliance of the Moon;
the sixth is Ingesting the Talisman of Yin Growth;
the seventh is Restraining the Sānhún;
the eighth is Controlling the Qīpò;
the ninth is Wearing the Talisman of the Imperial Image;
the tenth is Ingesting the Radiant Cinnabar;
the eleventh is Ingesting the Yellow Water;
the twelfth is Ingesting the Circulating Water;
the thirteenth is Eating the Ring-Hardness;
the fourteenth is Eating Phoenix Brain;
the fifteenth is Eating Pine Pears;
the sixteenth is Eating Plums and Dates;
the seventeenth is Ingesting Water Broth;
the eighteenth is Stabilizing Silver and Purple Gold;
the nineteenth is Ingesting Cloud Fat;
the twentieth is Making Silver and Purple Gold;
the twenty-first is Making Stabilization;
the twenty-second is Eating Bamboo Shoots;
the twenty-third is Eating Dried Wild Goose Meat;
the twenty-fourth is Wearing the Talismans of the Five Gods.
Having prepared these twenty-four,
one's transformations are limitless,
transcending beyond the Sānjiè
and wandering within the Liùhé.
Disasters cannot harm them,
and demonic evils dare not trouble them.
All are naturally subdued,
the position reaches the pinnacle of the Ancestors of the Dào,
grace flows to everything,
and both the hidden and the manifest rely upon it.
Those who do not believe and do not follow,
who do not know and do not see,
naturally allow themselves to be in darkness,
eternally at odds with the Dào.
In the charcoal and mud of misfortune and poison,
they are mixed and crushed by afflictions.
With great compassion and thought,
nothing can be done for them.
How pitiful!
Men of intention,
plan early, plan early,
and do not let down these present words."
He said:
"Excellent,
excellent!
Today I asked about my doubts,
and I have heard your commands."
2.1 *Methods for Harmonizing Yīn and Yáng and Following the Dào*
Returning years and not growing old,
the Great Dào is about to return,
and the years of humans will all be verified.
Close the eyes and look back into oneself,
it is pure white and radiant.
It is like the time when dawn is approaching;
the body is peacefully settled on the mat.
As if dwelling in a warm steam,
at this time the sinews and bones do not wish to be moved,
and the mouth does not wish to speak.
Every stretching and bending brings more pleasure,
the heart is joyful,
there is a sense of blending and moistening,
breath flows through the nose,
sweetness arises in the mouth;
these are the signs.
Therefore, those who follow Heaven and Earth,
their governance is long-lasting.
Those who follow the four seasons,
their kingship flourishes daily.
The Dào has no strange words;
one Yīn and one Yáng
are its functions.
Those who obtain its governance prosper,
those who lose its governance fall into disorder;
those who obtain its governance become divine and enlightened,
those who lose its governance cannot practice the Dào.
Contemplate these meanings in detail,
and one will be in harmony with the Dào.
2.2 *Lù Shēn Zhèng Shén Lìng Rén Zì Zhī Fǎ*
When Heaven causes the Dào to give birth to humans,
they receive a single method and a single body,
with seven components crisscrossing Yīn and Yáng,
half Yīn and half Yáng,
thus they can complete each other.
Therefore, what is above resembles Yáng,
what is below models itself on Yīn;
the left models itself on Yáng,
the right models itself on Yīn.
Yáng loves life,
Yīn loves killing.
Yáng is the Dào,
Yīn is punishment.
Yáng is goodness,
Yáng spirits assist it;
Yīn is evil,
Yīn spirits assist it.
If one accumulates goodness without ceasing,
the blessings of the Dào will arise,
making one's days auspicious.
Yáng resides in the head,
Yīn resides in the feet.
Therefore, the ruler values Dào and virtue,
and places punishments below,
taking this as a model.
The petty man, conversely, places Dào and virtue below
and raises punishments above,
also taking this as a model.
Thus, a person is the root and handle of the Dào,
and the leader of the spirits.
One should know this meaning,
and well maintain and nourish it;
then one can achieve longevity.
If one does not nourish the body well,
one will be blamed by various spirits.
When the spirits rebel and leave the person,
how can the body attain goodness?
Doing good, one does not dare to lose the guiding thread,
and does not dare to deceive oneself.
When doing good, the spirits naturally know it;
when doing evil, the spirits also naturally know it.
These are not other spirits,
but the spirits within the body.
Words emerge from the heart and belly,
yet even bystanders can know them;
this is because the spirits within the body report them.
Therefore, rectifying the spirits and quieting the body
is the root of governance
and the evidence of longevity.
The affairs of non-action (Wúwéi)
arise from this.
First study one's own body
in order to know good and bad fortune.
For this reason, those who are worthy, sagely, and enlightened
only study their own bodies
and do not study others;
they contemplate deeply the meaning of the Dào,
thus they can achieve Great Peace (Tàipíng).
The gentleman obtains this and flourishes,
the petty man practices it and collapses.
2.3 *Xiū Yī Què Xié Fǎ*
At the opening of Heaven and Earth, the origin and root are valued;
this is the source of Qì.
To bring about Great Peace,
one must be mindful of the origin and root.
If one does not contemplate its root,
the name becomes greatly troubled,
one cannot succeed in activities,
and disasters arrive together.
This is not due to a person's fault,
but to losing the foundation.
Leaving the root and seeking the branches,
calamities cannot be managed;
therefore one should contemplate this deeply.
As for Oneness,
it is the root of the Dào,
the beginning of Qì,
the place where life is tied and connected,
and the master of all hearts.
If one wishes to know its reality,
it acts as the root in the center,
it is the palace of life.
Therefore one should know it deeply,
returning to benevolence and worthiness to allow it to operate.
The root of a person resides within,
while the branches and leaves are on the outside;
to maintain Oneness is to make everything external return,
urgently causing the internal to be governed,
chasing back what is far,
and governing what is near.
One who maintains Oneness
is assisted by the spirits of Heaven.
One who maintains Duality
is assisted by the spirits of Earth.
One who maintains Triplicity
is assisted by the ghosts of humans.
As for Four and Five,
they are assisted by material things.
Therefore, one who maintains Oneness extends life;
one who maintains Duality meets with misfortune at an appointed time.
One who maintains Triplicity creates chaotic governance;
one who maintains Four and Five sees disasters arrive daily.
Contemplate this meaning deeply;
this is called knowing the Dào.
Therefore, the Oneness of the head
is the crown.
The Oneness of the Seven Rectifiers
is the eyes.
The Oneness of the abdomen
is the navel.
The Oneness of the vessels
is the Qì.
The Oneness of the Five Viscera
is the heart.
The Oneness of the four limbs
is the centers of the hands and feet.
The Oneness of the bones
is the spine.
The Oneness of the flesh
is the intestines and stomach.
If one can firmly maintain Oneness
and know the meaning of the Dào,
obtaining the Dào makes one benevolent,
while losing the Dào makes one greedy.
2.4 *Yǐ Yuè Què Zāi Fǎ*
Use joy to govern the body, protect the form, align the thoughts, focus the mind, and repel calamity.
Now, what role does joy play in the Dào?
Joy can harmonize and combine Yīn and Yáng,
it acts silently in all matters,
and it allows one to attain the root of the Dào.
Therefore, when the Yuánqì is joyful, there is great prosperity;
when Nature is joyful, things become strong;
when Heaven is joyful, the Three Luminaries shine;
when Earth is joyful, completion follows constant laws;
when the Wǔxíng are joyful, they do not harm one another;
when the Four Seasons are joyful, that which is born flourishes;
when the King is joyful, the world is without illness;
when crawling creatures are joyful, they do not harm or injure each other;
when the myriad things are joyful, they maintain their constancy;
when people are joyful, they are not distressed nor do they change their hearts;
when ghosts and spirits are joyful, they benefit the Emperor.
Therefore, joy
is formed by the virtuous qì and essence of Heaven and Earth;
it brings forth the divine spirits.
Thus, stillness produces light,
and light is the means by which one waits upon the spirits.
One who can communicate with the divine spirits
becomes a neighbor to the Dào
and attains longevity and eternal existence.
Seeking the Dào is often laborious,
for one cannot turn back their thoughts.
If one now transforms customs and changes traditions,
directing the focus of their heart,
who then could contend with them?
Does the joy of Tàipíng emerge from within the palace?
It surely purifies and pacifies the state,
stabilizes the body to enter the Dào,
causes the Yídí barbarians to retreat,
and auspicious divine omens to appear.
The hanging images return,
and the malevolent spirits depart.
Now, the spirits of man are born within,
but they wander back out;
if they wander at improper times,
their return causes harm to the body.
If one can pursue them and bring them back,
one's self-governance will not fail.
How is this pursuit conducted?
Make a room empty with no one nearby;
paint images according to the colors of the internal organs,
corresponding to the qì of the Four Seasons,
and hang them in the light of the window to meditate upon them.
Above there are images of the organs,
below there are the Ten Regions (Shíxiāng).
While lying down, focus your thoughts on the nearby hanging images,
meditating on them without ceasing.
The spirits of the five organs can report to the twenty-four seasonal qì,
and the spirits of the Wǔxíng will come to provide aid,
and the myriad illnesses will all be cured.
Men meditate on male figures;
women meditate on female figures;
all use one chǐ as the standard,
shifting according to the Four Seasons.
In spring, ten Azure Boys (Qīng Tóngzǐ);
in summer, ten Vermilion Boys (Chì Tóngzǐ);
in autumn, ten White Boys (Bái Tóngzǐ);
in winter, ten Black Boys (Hēi Tóngzǐ);
during the four transitional months between seasons,
twelve Yellow Boys (Huáng Tóngzǐ).
These twenty-five divine spirits and Zhēnrén together constitute the Dàodé.
Practicing the Law correctly,
Yáng transforms into Yīn,
and Yīn transforms into Yáng;
when Yīn and Yáng harmonize with each other,
then the Dào can be practiced.
Heaven requires Earth to have that which is born;
Earth requires Heaven to have that which is completed.
Spring and Summer require Autumn and Winter,
day requires night,
the ruler requires the minister—
only then can governance be completed.
The minister requires the ruler
to carry out his tasks.
Thus Jiǎ requires Yǐ,
and Zǐ requires Chǒu;
all complement one another.
Practicing the governance of the Dào should be exactly like the movement of Heaven;
if it does not correspond with people,
it is all in opposition to the Tiāndào.
For example, the Eastern Sea (Dōnghǎi) stays low and welcomes water,
so all the hundred rivers flow into it.
Because it attains its Dào,
whales emerge from within it,
and bright moon pearls are born there—
this is the effect of its attaining the Dào.
When followers of the Dào gather,
miraculous methods for extending life will surely emerge,
and great auspicious omens will correspond to it.
When many worthies gather, it brings about peace and order;
when many civil officials gather, it manages minor disorder;
when the five weapons gather, governance suffers a great defeat.
The ruler should maintain the Dào,
the minister should maintain the Dé.
Dào and Dé
are like the outside and inside of a garment.
If Heaven were not vast,
it could not contain the myriad things.
The myriad things are all half good and half bad;
one must tolerate them all.
The human ruler takes this as an image,
and next is the image of the Empress (Huánghòu) and the inner palace.
These two
are the models of the compassionate love of parents.
Thus, when parents raise a child,
they love the good one,
and they pity the bad one;
only then can they harmonize the way of the family.
The sun symbolizes the human ruler,
the moon symbolizes the great ministers,
the stars symbolize the various officials;
many worthies shine together,
and the myriad things are born in harmony.
Thus, the pure is attached to Heaven,
the turbid is attached to Earth,
and Central Harmony (Zhōnghé) is attached to humanity.
I wish for all the myriad spirits of the world to be in harmony and kinship,
no longer acting recklessly to harm people;
for Heaven and Earth to be eternally joyful,
for all the hundred spirits to be glad,
so that people have nothing to suffer from.
The Emperor attains the power of Heaven,
and there is good fortune in his actions;
how could anything interfere?
Thus, the Sage can maintain the Dào.
At the dawn meal during times of clarity and stillness,
all the spirits call out to converse with him,
just as people today call upon guests.
The hundred spirits call themselves heavenly officials and heavenly messengers;
the various essences are earthly officials and earthly messengers;
the hundred ghosts are messengers of Central Harmony (Zhōnghé).
These three
are the messengers of Yīn, Yáng, and Central Harmony (Zhōnghé).
They assist Heaven and Earth in governance,
and together they promote the interests of the Emperor.
The method of guarding the One and Clarity
is the root of longevity.
The ten thousand spirits can be traced to their origin
as they emerge from the gate of radiant light.
At the moment when the One is pure and bright,
just as when fire first arises,
guard it urgently and do not lose it.
At first it is pure red,
eventually it is pure white,
and after a long time it is pure azure.
Penetratingly bright and reaching extremely far and further still,
return to governing the One,
and there will be nothing within that is not bright.
The hundred diseases will be removed;
if one guards it without remissness,
it can be called the art of ten thousand years.
In the method of guarding the One and Clarity,
its clarity possesses the light of the rising sun
and the brilliance of the midday sun;
this is the primary goodness for attaining the longevity of Heaven.
Living peacefully in a quiet place,
for ten thousand generations one will not lose it.
The method of guarding the One throughout time,
and the superiority or inferiority in practicing the Dào.
What kind of thing is the Dào?
It is the head of the ten thousand things,
that which cannot be named.
Within the six poles,
there is nothing that cannot transform through the Dào.
Yuánqì practices the Dào
to give birth to the ten thousand things;
whether large or small within Heaven and Earth,
there is nothing that is not born from the Dào.
Therefore Yuánqì is formless,
to govern that which has form,
and to unfold the Yuánqì,
yet they are not born without following the Dào.
Zìrán
is the spontaneity of the ten thousand things.
If the Dào is not practiced,
it cannot encompass Heaven and Earth
so that each finds its place,
and enable the high to remain unaware of danger.
Heaven practices the Dào
day and night without ceasing,
swifter than wind and rain,
yet it still fears losing the intent of the Dào;
how much more so for a king?
The Sānguāng practice the Dào without ceasing,
thus they are fixed in Heaven and illuminate the eight poles;
if they lose the Dào, their light is extinguished.
The king, the hundred officials, and the ten thousand things correspond to one another;
all living beings dwell together,
and the Wǔxīng observe their errors.
When the king restores virtue,
the Déxīng goes to guard him.
If he practices martiality,
the Wǔxīng goes to guard him.
If he practices gentleness,
the Róuxīng goes to guard him.
If he practices strength,
the Qiángxīng goes to guard him.
If he practices trustworthiness,
the Xìnxīng goes to guard him.
Though they are far apart,
the resonance is close.
Heaven and man are one body;
how can one not be cautious?
2.7 The Method of the Superiority and Inferiority of Practicing the Dào
In spring, the kingly energy should be warm;
in summer, it should be hot;
in autumn, it should be cool;
in winter, it should be cold;
this is kingly virtue.
The Wángqì communicates with the Qi of the emperor;
the Xiàngqì corresponds with the grand councilors;
the Wēiqì corresponds with minor officials;
the Xiūqì is the same as the inner palace;
the Fèiqì corresponds with the common people;
the Qi of the executed or imprisoned corresponds with the criminals in prison;
by their kind, they remotely move and affect one another.
In this Dào, if the Wángqì does not come,
the king's favor cannot be bestowed.
The sage-kings of old used this to contemplate the Dào;
therefore, as for the signs of gain and loss,
they meticulously observed their meaning.
When the king practices the Dào,
Heaven and Earth are joyful;
if he loses the Dào,
Heaven and Earth cause disasters and anomalies.
A king should quietly contemplate virtue and the Dào,
practicing the Dào to stabilize his person,
and seeking longevity through self-cultivation.
Harmonizing the way of husband and wife,
so that Yīn and Yáng both find their proper place,
Heaven and Earth will be at peace.
Heaven and the emperor are more than tens of thousands of miles apart,
yet conversely they correspond through the Dào;
is this not divine?
2.8 The Book of the Divine Secret Formula of Names
Yuánqì and Zìrán
together constitute the nature of Heaven and Earth.
When the six directions and eight quarters are joyful,
then good responses occur;
if they are not joyful,
then evil responses occur.
Shapes resemble the images of their forms,
and echoes harmonize with their sounds.
Tàiyīn,
Tàiyáng,
and Zhōnghé—these three Qi together constitute the Principle;
they move and affect one another in turn.
Man is the pivot and mechanism;
therefore, one should understand this deeply.
If all know to value their life
and nourish their body,
then they will know to respect those above
and love those below.
Rejoicing in life and loathing death,
the three Qi will be joyful
and together form the Tàihé;
thus auspicious responses will emerge together.
Simply gather the many worthies
and contemplate only the Way of Longevity;
this will stabilize those above
and they will become the precious vessels of the state.
One who can nourish their own nature
can nourish the people.
Heaven has no private favoritism in its protection;
its protection depends on trustworthiness.
The spirits have no private relatives;
good people serve as their manifestation.
Within a single body,
one can be a worthy,
can be a spirit,
or can be unworthy;
what is the reason for this?
It is due to errors
and the divine spirit being exposed.
Therefore the Way of Guarding the One
and nourishing one's nature
lies in learning it.
Among the multitude, those who have many auspicious responses
are trustworthy people.
Those without auspicious responses
are people whose conduct is erroneous.
By divination, right and wrong can thus be known.
What is examined by scales and weights
is human sentiment.
Heaven's illumination of man
is no different from a mirror.
Examine this meaning in detail:
to share the same desire as Heaven
and act with the true spirits—how can it not be auspicious?
Accomplishing matters □□,
without missing a tiny fraction,
one wishes to obtain the intent of the Zhōnghé of Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, when Heaven and Earth are in tune, the ten thousand things are at peace;
when the officials are fair, the ten thousand people are well-governed.
Thus, if one exclusively practices Yáng,
then Earth will not fully complete things;
if one exclusively practices Yīn,
then Heaven will not fully give life.
One must unite the three systems;
when Yīn and Yáng are in harmony with each other,
then harmony is found in the center.
When the sages of old governed to achieve Tàipíng,
they all sought the heart of the Zhōnghé of Heaven and Earth.
If even one Qi does not flow,
all matters will go astray.
2.9 The Method of Harmonizing the Three Qi to Raise Up Emperors and Kings
Discussion on Penetrating the Central Harmony of Heaven and Earth,
following the Great Undertaking,
harmonizing the movement of the Three Qi,
causing the King to have no worries,
and the worthy people to all come forth
to assist the rise of Emperors and Kings,
so that Heaven is greatly pleased.
The Zhēnrén asked the Shénrén, saying:
"I wish to enable Emperors and Kings to immediately achieve Tàipíng (Great Peace);
how may I hear of this?"
The Shénrén said:
"Only by greatly following Heaven and Earth,
without the slightest error,
can Tàipíng be immediately achieved,
and auspicious omens will arise together.
Yuánqì (Primordial Qi) has three names:
Tàiyáng,
Tàiyīn,
and Zhōnghé.
Physical forms have three names:
Heaven, Earth,
and Humanity. Heaven has three names:
the Sun, the Moon,
and the Stars, with the Běijí as the center.
Earth has three names:
Mountains,
Rivers, and Level Ground.
Humanity has three names:
Father, Mother,
and Child. Governance has three names:
Ruler, Minister,
and Subjects, for those who desire Tàipíng.
These three should always be at the heart and mind,
without the slightest error,
making them share the same concerns
and uniting them into one family;
then Tàipíng is immediately achieved,
and the extension of years is certain.
Thus the male represents Heaven,
so his heart and thoughts are on the female;
this is the clear evidence of Heaven influencing humanity.
The Minister represents the Earth in this discussion;
the Earth always desires to ascend
to unite its heart with Heaven.
Therefore, all things are born from the Earth,
immediately facing upward without ceasing,
and cloud qi spreads across Heaven to become rain.
Thus a loyal minister’s concern is always on what is above,
earnestly never forgetting his ruler;
this is the clear evidence of Earth influencing him.
The Subjects are the primary subject of the discussion on Zhōnghé;
Zhōnghé
is that which primarily reconciles and harmonizes all things.
Zhōnghé is the chìzǐ (infant);
a child is born because of the father and mother;
its life belongs to the father,
its lineage is above,
and it is entrusted to be born of the mother.
Thus, when wronged, they think of the Ruler and Father.
These three are the images of husband and wife, father and child.
It is proper for them to communicate their words to one another
and combine their efforts and concerns;
then the Three Qi merge to become Tàihé (Great Harmony).
Tàihé then produces the qi of Tàipíng.
If these Three Qi are severed,
and even one qi is blocked and does not reach,
Tàihé will not arrive
and Tàipíng will not emerge.
As for Yīn and Yáng,
the key lies in Zhōnghé.
When Zhōnghé qi is attained,
all things flourish and grow,
the people are harmonized,
and the King governs in Tàipíng.
The Ruler
is Heaven;
if his grace does not descend,
ultimate things have no way to be born,
and people cannot extend their years.
If the Ruler's heart is not unblocked and expressive,
the heart of Heaven cannot reach below;
if the wife and children do not receive the instructions of the Lord and Father,
it becomes a rebellious family.
If the Minister's qi cannot reach,
the Earth's qi cannot be completed;
how then can loyal ministers assist the Enlightened King in governing?
It harms the heart of the Earth;
a widow in her chamber
is often bitter and sorrowful;
good ministers have no way to come forward.
If the Subjects' qi does not reach upward,
how can Harmony Qi arise?
Zhōnghé should harmonize the Emperor's rule,
so that all things that are adjusted obtain their proper order.
Now, if the Three Qi do not communicate well with each other,
how can Tàipíng be achieved?"
2.10 Methods of the King of Peace and Joy
A ruler should transform all things through Dào and Dé,
ensuring each finds its proper place.
If he cannot transform all things,
he cannot be called a ruler.
For example, a husband and wife
together produce a child,
and then they are called parents.
This is also the image of a family;
if they cannot produce a child,
how can they be named parents?
Thus, one who cannot transform and give life to all things
cannot be called the parent of the people.
Thus, Fire can transform the other four phases, making five with itself;
therefore, it attains the image of the Ruler.
Wood’s nature is harmonious and focused,
but meeting Fire, it scatters and becomes ash.
Metal’s nature is hard and rigid,
but meeting Fire, it becomes soft.
Earth’s nature is very soft,
but meeting Fire, it becomes hard and forms tiles.
Water’s nature is cold,
but meeting Fire, it becomes warm.
Fire itself is equal with the Five Phases,
yet it can transform without constant form;
its nature is to move and ascend.
Yīn follows Yáng,
and the Minister follows the Ruler;
furthermore, it attains the power to illuminate and observe clearly,
distinguishing right from wrong.
Therefore, it can be called the Ruler;
the others cannot.
Earth does not transform immediately;
it transforms after a long time.
Thus it is called Hòutǔ.
The other three assist in their duties;
they are the image of the Minister.
There is nothing the Dào cannot transform;
thus Yuánqì preserves the Dào,
then circulates its qi,
and produces Heaven and Earth.
They stand without pillars,
and all things are born without prior categories.
Then it reaches later generations who pass it on,
saying that there are categories.
Compare this to plants and trees growing on the ground;
did they originally have categories?
This is how Yuánqì preserves the Dào and produces things thus.
If Nature preserves the Dào and acts,
then all things find their proper place.
If Heaven preserves the Dào and acts,
it is called Divine and is without limit.
Above, it represents the Ruler and Father of humanity;
there is nothing it cannot regulate or transform;
it truly attains the intent of the Dào.
If Earth preserves the Dào and acts,
the five directions merge with the center,
and all things return to it.
If the Three Luminaries preserve the Dào and act,
then there is nothing they do not illuminate and observe.
If Thunder and Lightning preserve the Dào and act,
they can move the world,
riding upon the qi to come and go.
If the Four Seasons and Five Phases preserve the Dào and act,
they can transform all things,
ensuring they have constancy.
If Yīn and Yáng, female and male, preserve the Dào and act,
they can pass from generation to generation.
In all matters, whether great or small,
if all preserve the Dào and act,
then there is no misfortune.
If today the Dào is lost,
it leads to great chaos.
Therefore, if Yáng is at peace, all things are born of themselves;
if Yīn is at peace, all things are completed of themselves.
When Yīn and Yáng govern the Dào,
the teaching reaches the ministers,
and the transformation flows to the people.
One receives the mandate from Heaven,
receives the physical form from Earth,
and receives teachings from a teacher.
Then one hears the Essential Way of the world.
One who preserves the root becomes King;
one who preserves the stalk becomes Minister;
one who preserves the superficial flowers may be good, yet there is chaos and lack of constancy.
The Emperor and King
is the Son of Heaven.
The Empress
is the child of the Earth;
this is the primary divine qi of Heaven and Earth.
Heaven and Earth always desire to make them joyful,
and not let them suffer in sorrow;
they cherish them thus,
for they are the foremost in the heart, intent, and qi of Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, if the King is in sorrow and suffering,
the qi of the Four Seasons and Five Phases becomes chaotic and erroneous,
and the cycle of life and death loses its constancy.
2.11 Methods of Suspending Images and Returning the Spirit
Indeed, spirits are born within.
In Spring, there are ten *Qīng Tóngzǐ*;
in Summer, ten *Chì Tóngzǐ*;
in Autumn, ten *Bái Tóngzǐ*;
in Winter, ten *Hēi Tóngzǐ*;
during the four seasonal transitions,
there are twelve *Huáng Tóngzǐ*.
These are the internal organ spirits of a man;
female spirits also follow this count.
Men should meditate on the male spirits,
and women should meditate on the female spirits,
both taking one *chǐ* as the standard measure.
Draw them so they are beautiful,
causing people to love them.
If one cannot take joy in the prohibitions,
then the souls and spirits will quickly return.
2.12 *Jiě Chéng Fù Jué*
Since the opening of Heaven and Earth,
baleful *qì* has never ceased.
Why is it that when it seems to cease, it rises again?
Why is this?
Indeed, longevity
is the precious treasure of Heaven.
It is that which is privately bestowed upon those with virtue;
it cannot be obtained through pretense.
If one wishes to know this treasure,
it is when the myriad things within the Six Directions and the Eight Distances of Heaven and Earth
are all free from grievances and entanglements
and are all greatly joyful;
only then can longevity be increased.
If even one thing is unhappy,
there will immediately be injuries and deaths.
Regarding the conduct of ordinary people,
some may strive to do good
but contrary to expectations receive evil;
some may strive to do evil
but conversely receive good.
Because of this, it is wrong for one to call themselves a worthy.
Those who strive to do good yet conversely receive evil
are subject to the *Chéngfù* of their ancestors' transgressions;
flowing disasters accumulated from before and after have come to harm this person.
Those who do evil yet conversely receive good
have ancestors who possessed deeply accumulated great merit,
the flow of which has reached this person.
If one can perform great merit ten thousand-fold,
then although the ancestors may have residual calamities,
they cannot reach this person.
Consequently, these pass on again,
flowing to later generations,
forming the inheritance of the *Wǔzǔ*.
One minor cycle is ten generations,
after which it returns to the beginning.
Some may perform small good deeds but cannot overcome
the disaster of the *Chéngfù* of flowing evil from their ancestors,
leading to extinction in the middle of their lineage without descendants;
it is truly a grievance.
As for *Chéngfù*,
Heaven has three divisions:
for Emperors and Kings, it flows for thirty thousand years;
for Ministers, the *Chéngfù* is three thousand years;
for the common People, it is three hundred years.
All are connected through *Chéngfù*,
one sinking and one rising,
never ceasing as they follow the decline and prosperity of human governance.
If one can now model themselves on this,
and use the governance of the *Tiānshàng Huáng* to sever these burdens,
then reflect deeply upon this and do not forget it.
Ordinary people have three spans of longevity,
corresponding to the three *qì*:
the destinies of *Tàiyáng*, *Tàiyīn*, and *Zhōnghé*.
Superior longevity is one hundred and twenty years;
Middle longevity is eighty years;
Inferior longevity is sixty years.
One hundred and twenty years corresponds to Heaven,
completing one year of the Great Calendar and reaching the boundary of Heaven and Earth.
Eighty years corresponds to Yin and Yang,
distinguishing the eight pairs and such to correspond to Earth,
specifically corresponding to Earth,
and specifically to the myriad things,
where the dead depart
and the living remain.
Sixty years corresponds to the *qì* of *Zhōnghé*,
obtaining the *Dùn* hexagram of the sixth month.
*Dùn*
means to flee or vanish;
therefore, it governs the juncture of life and death.
If one does good without ceasing,
exceeding these spans of longevity is called *Dùshì*.
If one does evil without ceasing
and does not reach the three spans of longevity,
all are considered premature deaths.
Those who die in the womb or before reaching adulthood
are called innocent ones inheriting the *Chéngfù* of their ancestors' transgressions.
Those with many ailments of the head
signify that the *qì* of Heaven is displeased.
Those with many ailments of the feet
signify that the *qì* of Earth is displeased.
Those with many ailments of the five internal organs
signify the warring of the *qì* of the Five Elements.
Those with many diseases of the four limbs
signify that the *qì* of the Four Seasons is not in harmony.
Those with many diseases of deafness or blindness
signify that the *Sānguāng* have lost their measure.
Those with many diseases of cold and heat
signify that the *qì* of Yin and Yang are in angry contention.
Those with many diseases of confusion and disorder
signify that the myriad things have lost their proper place.
Those with many diseases caused by ghosts and entities
signify that the gods and spirits of Heaven and Earth are angry.
Those with many diseases of warmth who die
are killed by the *qì* of *Tàiyáng*.
Those with many diseases of cold who die
are harmed by the *qì* of *Tàiyīn*.
Those with many diseases of sudden death
have a punitive *qì* that is too urgent.
Those with many diseases of *qì* bloating or deficiency of *qì*
signify that the *Bājié* are in disorder.
Now, the Yin and Yang of Heaven and Earth
have internally and solely lost their proper places;
therefore, diseases harm the myriad things.
If the governance of Emperors and Kings is not harmonious,
floods and droughts will be erratic,
and bandits will frequently arise;
if they instead make their punishments even more urgent,
or increase them with more weight and confusion,
forming endless links that cannot be unraveled,
then the people will all cry out to Heaven.
When the local officials' governance is chaotic,
losing its measure and constancy,
the myriad things will be harmed and lost,
which above affects the *Cāngtiān*.
The *Sānguāng* will be turbulent and undergo many changes,
and the ranked stars will move in disorder;
therefore, it is through the *Zhìdào* that they can be saved.
I know that the will of Heaven does not deceive you.
Once the majesty of Heaven is unleashed,
it cannot be restrained.
Gaining guilt before Heaven
causes people to die prematurely.
When Heaven and Earth first opened,
the *Tàishèngrén* each attained thorough understanding in one aspect;
truly and sincerely knowing it,
they no longer had any doubts.
Therefore, they were each able to establish a great legacy,
allowing later generations to cultivate it
without error or mistake.
Thus, even Sages were only proficient in one great legacy
and could not necessarily know the *Tiāndào*;
hence, they each differed in their virtue.
This is like Heaven—
how much more so for humans?
Heaven and Earth each excel in one thing:
Heaven excels at being high, clear, and bright;
Earth excels at being below, heavy, and turbid;
and *Zhōnghé* excels at nourishing the myriad things.
Even they cannot encompass everything,
so how much less can ordinary people?
*Hài* is the northwestern pole of Heaven and Earth;
*Sì* is the southeastern pole of Heaven and Earth.
If the cold of *Hài* does not gather and close according to the season,
then in the coming year, *Sì* will conversely be harmed.
*Zǐ* is the northern pole of Heaven and Earth;
*Wǔ* is the southern pole of Heaven and Earth.
If *Zǐ* does not properly follow storage in winter,
then *Wǔ* will conversely inherit the *Chéngfù* and perish.
*Chǒu* is the northeastern pole of Heaven and Earth;
*Wèi* is the southwestern pole of Heaven and Earth.
If *Chǒu* does not begin to generate according to the season,
then in the sixth month, *Wèi* will conversely receive punishment.
The natural movement of Heaven and Earth
is all like this.
Now, an Emperor or King resides within a hundred layers of the palace,
but if he employs *Dàodé*,
his benevolence and goodness will reach ten thousand *lǐ*,
and the common people will receive his grace.
Fathers will be compassionate,
sons will be filial,
households will be self-sufficient and people provided for,
and they will not engage in evil.
But if the Emperor or King resides within
and loses his *Dàodé*,
then beyond ten thousand *lǐ*,
the people and ministers will lose their roles.
Although they are separated by many ten thousands of *lǐ*,
it all stems from the same single source.
Practicing good words
is not as good as practicing them through one's own conduct.
2.13 *Quē Tí*
Zhēnrén asked Shénrén:
“In my life, I do not know what it is that makes me constantly joyful?”
Shénrén said:
“Have you observed the broad and great Zhēnrén of old?
The reason they were born first and aged later
was because they discarded wickedness.
When a person alone loves the Zhēndào,
the Zhēndào is constantly preserved and wickedness dissolves.
While ordinary people are all exhausted and destitute,
I alone endure long;
this is constant joy.”
“Being luminously joyful alone,
what resentment could there be?
If in the end one cannot achieve long life,
what should be done?”
Shénrén said:
“Accumulated practice brings success near;
thinking of goodness brings life near.
As for the Dào,
it is the scripture of the Wújí.
In ancient times, Shénrén governed it,
using Zhēnrén as ministers
to govern the people.
Thus, the people did not know there was a Tiānzǐ above them,
and they governed themselves through the Dào of zìrán and wúwéi.
Next, the Zhēnrén governed,
using Xiānrén as ministers.
It was rare for the people of that time to know there was a Tiānzǐ,
though they honored their lord upon hearing his instructions.
Next, the Xiānrén governed,
using Dàorén as ministers.
Their practice of governance slightly involved punishments, and laws and decrees were made manifest,
so the people’s hearts were stirred and they felt fear,
and cleverness and deceit began to arise.
Next is the governance of the Bà;
they do not carefully select their ministers,
the people suffer many grievances and disorder arises.
It moves further from order
and closer to chaos,
until it can no longer be controlled.
Therefore, thinking of the Shén brings the Shén;
thinking of the Zhēn brings the Zhēn;
thinking of the Xiān brings the Xiān;
thinking of the Dào brings the Dào;
thinking of Zhì brings Zhì.
When the refined thoughts of the Shèngrén turn to the Xiánrén,
they bring the spirits of the Xiánrén to come and assist them;
thinking of wickedness
brings the ghosts of foolish people to come and delude them.
Whatever a person contemplates
can be brought about;
it merely depends on whether the object of thought is superior or inferior.
Therefore, when a Shàngshì is a ruler,
he thinks of the Shén and the Zhēn;
when a Zhōngshì is a ruler,
his mind is penetrative and he possesses much Zhì;
when a Xiàshì is a ruler,
he has nothing worthy of thought
and merely acts according to whatever command is given.”
2.14 《Quētí》
Zhēnrén asked:
"How can one know whether a Dìwáng contemplates good or evil?"
Shénrén said:
"Is it easy to know?
When a Dìwáng contemplates benevolence and goodness,
auspicious omens appear specifically for them,
and sacred diagrams and texts are produced specifically for them.
The benevolence and brilliance of a Dìwáng are born from wood and fire;
martial wisdom is born from metal and water;
gentleness and harmony are born from earth.
The manifestations suspended by Heaven
are never in error."
Zhēnrén asked:
"Regarding the unique diagrams and extraordinary methods of ancient times,
who is meant to obtain them?"
"The officials or commoners who obtain them present them to the Wáng.
If the Dìwáng's seasonal Qì is harmonious and good,
and the governance is increasingly brilliant,
then those of the Dàoshù and the worthy and wise will emerge to assist them.
The Dào of the Dìwáng
will daily grow stronger and more prosperous.
The Yídí will be extinguished and silenced,
and there will be governance through non-action.
Punishments will naturally cease,
and the people will have no weapons or armor.
Is this not proof of the Dìwáng contemplating goodness?
How could one not know it?
Without even seeing the person,
one already knows it."
Zhēnrén asked:
"How can a Shénrén know this?"
Shénrén said:
"It is achieved through soundlessness.
When a ruler desires benevolence and loves life,
they model themselves after Tiāndào;
when officials desire to be gentle, submissive, and good at nourishing,
they follow Dìdào.
Then good responses will appear.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth do not speak yet endure forever;
their governance is uniquely divine.
Divine spirits do not speak yet are long-lived immortals;
all are brilliant within and dark without,
thus becoming the source of the myriad ways.
As for the divine spirits coming and going,
they have no fixed dens or nests;
they are pure, tranquil, and soundless.
Resting peacefully on a pillow,
divine light is naturally produced.
How can this not be auspicious and joyful?
Those who use their mouths too much exhaust their essence;
those who use their strength too much toil their forms;
those who use martial force too much harm their bodies.
These are the sources of misfortune and disaster.
You must be careful with my words
and not contemplate recklessly.
Contemplating goodness may bring virtue;
contemplating evil will result in self-harm.
Between safety and danger,
the difference is as fine as a hair.
You must beware and avoid cluttered thoughts.
If a person loses the Dào, their life-force is severed;
if one carefully understands the intent of the Dào, their life can be preserved.
Strive to nourish your essence,
and do not consume yourself.
Study under and serve an enlightened teacher,
so that misfortune and chaos cannot arise."
Zhēnrén did not dare to lose any of the Shénrén's words.
Shénrén said:
"Scholars each act for their own sake,
not for others.
Therefore, one should love and be intimate with oneself.
By studying the Dào for a long time,
one becomes a Shénzhēn.
They become completely distinct from the masses;
such is the meaning of these words."
Zhēnrén asked:
"How can one know the efficacy of the Dào?"
Shénrén said:
"Seek resolution from an enlightened teacher
and put it into practice within oneself.
The body transforms and the form changes,
entering the same gate as the Shéndào,
becoming neighbors with the Zhēn,
and sharing the same door with the Shénrén.
Seek it within your own body.
Why do you not see the affliction?
Losing the intent of the Dào
and instead seeking it in the four wildernesses,
searching for it without finding it,
leads to the end of old age.
Thus, one departs from their root
and says the world is without the Dào,
constantly suffering in solitary sorrow.
Departing from one's root
is a great disaster.
If the Great Man loses it, he cannot stabilize his governance;
if the middle scholar loses it, he brings chaos to his ruler;
if the benevolent person loses it, they have no way to be worthy;
if the petty person loses it, they destroy themselves.
What the worthy and sages of old practiced
is the same as today.
What the petty men of old suffered
is also the same as today.
The clear evidence is like this."
Zhēnrén asked:
"How can one know whether a person is about to rise or decline?"
Shénrén said:
"When a Great Man is about to rise,
extraordinary omens appear,
and worthy ones assist him in governance.
When a household is about to rise,
those who seek it find life,
and the goodness of their children can be known."
Zhēnrén asked:
"How does one attract such worthy ones?"
Shénrén said:
"It is all through contemplation.
If refined contemplation does not cease,
then all things will come.
How divine!
When the Dào is used for governance,
how can one not practice it with effort?"
Shénrén said:
"The reason the Sāngāng and Liùjì can be long-lasting and auspicious
is that they uphold the Dào.
Because they do not lose their governance, they are always auspicious.
The longevity granted by Heaven
does not snatch away a person's wishes.
The nature of wood is benevolence;
contemplating benevolence thus attracts the East,
for the East governs benevolence.
All five directions are like this.
Affairs under Heaven
each follow their own kind.
Therefore, if a Dìwáng contemplates tranquility,
their governance will also be peaceful,
summoned by its own kind.
Scholars of old
sought efficacy within themselves;
scholars of today
instead seek efficacy from others.
Scholars of old used it to secure their own lives;
scholars of today use it for superficiality and flowery writing.
They do not accumulate essence within themselves,
but instead accumulate essence in texts;
this is called not knowing one's root."
"Zhēnrén, come forward.
You have come repeatedly to study the Dào;
is it truly complete and sufficient yet?"
"Until now, the Tiānshī no longer spoke of it,
considering it already sufficient.
But seeing the Tiānshī speak again,
I now know there is still insufficiency.
Now my thoughts are exhausted,
and I do not know what I should ask further.
I only hope the Tiānshī will further reveal what I have not reached."
"Very well,
Zhēnrén, come.
What in the world is called wealth and sufficiency,
and what is called poverty?"
"Well,
having much is wealth,
and having little is poverty."
"True,
your words are correct,
yet they are also not truly so."
"What does that mean?"
"If there are many evil, hypocritical flatterers and thieves,
can that be considered wealth?
If ordinary people are many
but sovereigns are few,
can that be called poverty?"
"In my ignorance, I have given my view upon the Tiānshī's instruction;
I did not dare to remain silent,
but I fell short and committed an error."
"If you yourself say you have fallen short,
how could common people know the place of poverty and wealth?
Now I only hope the Tiānshī will instruct my ignorance;
I am like an ignorant infant
who must be taught by parents before having knowledge."
"Excellent,
your words!
You are most humble,
yet you have not lost the way.
Agreed.
Zhēnrén, concentrate your essence,
and I shall speak to you in detail.
The meaning of 'wealth'
is to be completely prepared and sufficient.
Heaven considers all things being born and produced as wealth and sufficiency.
Thus, when the Qì of the Shànghuáng emerged,
twelve thousand kinds of things were all born and produced;
this was called wealth and sufficiency.
In the time of Zhōnghuáng, things slightly decreased,
and the twelve thousand things could not be fully prepared;
thus it was called slight poverty.
In the time of Xiàhuáng, things were even fewer than in Zhōnghuáng,
which was called great poverty."
Without auspicious responses,
good things do not arise,
which constitutes the extreme lowest poverty.
If you wish to know its great manifestation,
it is truly comparable to a farming household
that lacks strange objects or precious treasures,
making it a poor household.
When the ten thousand things cannot be fully provided, it is an extreme lowest poor household;
this is the poverty of Heaven and Earth.
When the twelve thousand things all emerge,
and the Earth nurtures them without injury, it is the wealth of the Earth;
if it does not nurture them well,
causing minor injury, it is the minor poverty of the Earth;
major injury is the major poverty of the Earth;
when good things fear being seen,
are harmed by the terrain and do not grow,
it reaches the state of extreme lowest poverty;
without precious treasures,
and with half of the ten thousand things injured,
it is a cause of great poverty.
If all are injured, it is an empty and void poor household.
This takes Heaven as the Father
and Earth as the Mother;
if these Parents are extremely poor,
then the children will suffer from the distress of poverty.
This corresponds to the governance of a King.
Therefore, in the governance of the Sage Kings of antiquity,
they were able to bring forth the twelve thousand things,
making them monarchs of superior wealth.
If good things are deficient by two-thirds,
they are monarchs of middling wealth.
If deficient by one-third,
they are monarchs of inferior wealth.
If there are no rare, precious, or good things,
they are monarchs of inferior poverty.
If half of the ten thousand things are injured,
it is a declining house.
If all are injured, it is a person of lowest poverty.
The Sages and Worthies of antiquity dwelt deep within secluded rooms
and contemplated the Dào and Dé for themselves;
regarding the extent of poverty and wealth,
why would they need to ask about it?
They knew it of themselves while sitting."
"Excellent, excellent!
Now only the Tiānshī fortunately pities the Dìwáng
who have long been in distress and suffering
and have not been able to carry out their intentions;
by what means can this wealth or poverty be brought about?"
"Excellent, excellent!
Your difficult question
has already entered the essence of subtle words.
However, it is brought about by the successes and failures of what one practices.
Those who diligently practice the Zhēndào,
Heaven produces spirits to assist their transformation;
therefore, heavenly spirits and good things are fully provided.
Those who practice Dé,
the spirits of the Earth's Yáng-nurturing emerge
to assist their governance;
therefore, they have half-wealth.
Those who practice Rén,
the spirits of Central Harmony and Rén emerge to assist their governance;
therefore, they have minor wealth.
Those who practice Wén
are on the staircase to concealment and deception;
therefore, spirits of deception emerge to assist them;
thus, their governance is in minor disorder.
Those who practice Wǔ
receive spirits of bandits and thieves who emerge to assist them;
therefore, their governance opposes the Heart of Heaven
and harms good people.
The Dào
is that which Heaven examines and practices.
Heaven is most spiritual;
therefore, true spirits emerge to assist its transformation.
Earth nurtures;
therefore, spirits of Dé emerge to assist its transformation.
Humans are benevolent;
therefore, spirits of Rén emerge to assist their transformation.
Wén primarily involves mutual refinement and deception,
losing its original root;
therefore, spirits of deception emerge to assist it;
when superiors and inferiors deceive each other with refinements,
their affairs are in disorder.
Wǔ uses punishment, killing, and injury to subdue people;
bandits and thieves also use punishment, killing, and injury to subdue people;
those who use anger, joy, ferocity, and awe to subdue people
are bandits and thieves.
Therefore, bandits and thieves emerge in great numbers,
and their governance is inauspicious.
Bandits and thieves mostly cause harm regarding wealth and goods;
therefore, their governance fails regarding wealth and commodities.
Thus, the superior monarchs of antiquity subdued people with the Dào,
greatly attaining the Heart of Heaven;
their governance was like that of the spirits,
and they were without distress
because they subdued people with the Zhēndào.
Middling monarchs subdued people with Dé;
inferior monarchs subdued people with Rén;
disorderly monarchs subdued people with Wén;
inauspicious and defeated monarchs use punishment, killing, and injury to subdue people.
For this reason, the superior monarchs of antiquity used the governance of Dào, Dé, and Rén to subdue people,
and did not use Wén, punishment, killing, or injury to subdue people.
The reason for this
is that these latter methods are vulgar to use.
A superior Jūnzǐ is like Heaven and Earth;
thus, Heaven loves life and does not injure,
so it is called Monarch and called Father.
Earth loves to nurture all things,
so it is called a Good Minister and called Mother.
Humans should use their hearts for Rén,
loving and nourishing similarly to Heaven and Earth;
therefore, they are called benevolent.
These three are good;
thus, they are able to jointly govern the ten thousand things
and act as their teachers and leaders.
Deception and punishment
cannot be used for governance;
they bring about inauspiciousness daily
and cannot bring about Tàipíng for Dìwáng;
therefore, they should be cut off.
Now, Zhēnrén, entrust my book to a monarch who possesses Dào and Dé;
if they diligently practice it to produce results,
it will immediately correspond with Heaven
and bring about Tàipíng;
this can be called a wealthy house
without doubt,
and can prevent Dìwáng from suffering distress
instead of being called a poor house.
Now, among the common people, they sometimes call each other wealthy houses;
what kind of thing is that?
This is merely the reckless talk of vulgar people.
What 'wealthy' means
is that everything is fully provided.
If one thing is not complete,
then it is incomplete.
Therefore, the Sages and Worthies of antiquity did not demand perfection from a single person,
meaning that one person cannot provide everything;
therefore, they did not demand completeness from them.
Now, in the eighty-one regional states,
things are each lacking and incomplete;
they cannot be constantly sufficient;
therefore, they take from other states.
Now, what kind of wealth does a single household have?
Does the Zhēnrén like following the reckless talk of vulgar people?"
"I would not dare, I would not dare."
"Since you have learned to be cautious in speech,
do not speak recklessly.
Reckless talk
disorders the correct patterns of Heaven and Earth
and cannot serve as a law for people;
be cautious of it."
"Yes, yes.
Now that the Tiānshī has bestowed grace and love,
pitying the Dìwáng in their positions
whose minds are in distress and suffering
and who have not attained the Will of Heaven,
and has explained everything for them,
which can lead to the path of the Tàipíng of the Shànghuáng.
This foolish student has received many books,
which greatly dazzle my youthful ignorance;
I do not know what I should ask further.
May the Heavenly Enlightened Master
set forth all the admonitions in full."
"Excellent, excellent!
However, according to the Law of Heaven,
the number of Yáng is one,
and the number of Yīn is two.
Therefore, Yáng is odd
and Yīn is even.
For this reason, monarchs are few while ministers are many.
Yáng is honored,
and Yīn is humble;
therefore, two Yīn should jointly serve one Yáng.
Therefore, the number of Heaven is one and the number of Earth is two;
therefore, two women should jointly serve one man.
Why must two people jointly nurture one person?
The side of the honored one must not be empty;
when one person walks,
another should stand or sit by their side
to provide for what is lacking.
Therefore, the number one
symbolizes Heaven.
The number two
symbolizes Earth.
Humans
are the children of Heaven and Earth;
therefore, they should symbolize their parents.
Since the world lost the Dào,
many have belittled women
and even cruelly killed them,
causing there to be fewer women than men,
Therefore, it causes the *yīn qì* to be severed,
not corresponding with the laws of Heaven and Earth.
The law of the *Tiāndào* is that
solitary *yáng* without a pair
leads to withered dryness,
causing Heaven to not send rain at the proper time.
Women correspond to the Earth;
when they alone are treated with contempt,
the whole world joins in despising their true mother,
and together they harm and kill the *dìqì*,
causing the earthly *qì* to be severed and cease production.
The Earth is greatly angered and displeased,
disasters and calamities increase,
making the Ruler's governance unable to be peaceful.
Why is this?
Men
are the quintessential spirit of Heaven.
Women
are the quintessential spirit of Earth.
Things affect one another according to their kind.
That the Ruler's governance is not peaceful
is fundamentally not the fault of the Ruler alone.
It is because common people have lost the *Dào* and treat matters lightly,
together committing wrongs.
Their faults are not just one,
but rather of ten thousand kinds;
therefore, it causes governance to be difficult to level and full of errors.
In the nature of Heaven and Earth,
among the twelve thousand things,
human life is the most important.
This harming and killing of women
deeply disturbs the Ruler's governance;
the great blame lies here."
"Now the *Tiānshī* has opened the path to *Tàipíng* for the Ruler,
and the *Tàipíng Zhēnjīng* has emerged.
The Ruler should simply roam without burdensome affairs,
but if harming women is causing these great disasters,
what should be done about it?"
"Excellent
is your question;
you have attained the heart of Heaven.
However, the reason the world despises and hates women
is fundamentally because they hate the faults in their behavior."
"What do you mean?
I wish to hear it,
and attempt to record it on bamboo and silk,
so that for ten thousand generations, no one will dare discard it."
"Excellent,
if you can now record this,
there will never again be anyone in the world who kills women."
"Yes, yes.
I wish to record it,
to eliminate the disasters of the Emperors and Kings;
this is what I delight in,
to save the lives of wronged women."
"Excellent,
you have already gained an increase in your count of years from Heaven."
"What does that mean?"
"Indeed,
saving others is called saving oneself;
killing others is called killing oneself.
Heaven loves you, and it can be said you have gained an increase in your count from Heaven;
the *Sīmìng* has changed your record."
"I do not dare,
I do not dare."
"There is no need to decline further;
this is the natural law of Heaven.
However, as for why the world kills women:
when common people are young and small,
the parents themselves are in distress and hardship,
so they cut off their clothing and food while raising them.
This is not only true of humans;
crawling creatures are all the same.
When they reach maturity or old age, large or small,
each should follow their own strength to seek clothing and food;
therefore, the ten thousand things all leave their parents and provide their own clothing and food.
The worthy obtain joy,
and the unworthy obtain hardship.
Furthermore, children are young,
and their strength grows stronger day by day with surplus.
Parents grow older day by day,
and their strength grows less and insufficient day by day.
Whether the children are male or female,
those with wisdom, worthiness, and surplus strength
should still return to repay the merit and kindness of their parents and provide for them.
Therefore, parents should not have to follow them with clothing and food.
This would be called the weak supporting the strong,
those with insufficient strength supporting those with surplus;
this is called perverse governance.
The young in turn cause distress to the elderly,
being of no benefit to their parents;
for this reason, many parents kill them.
Now, if they kill or harm them simply for lack of clothing and food,
wouldn't it be better to raise them to live
and have them each provide their own clothing and food?
*Zhēnrén*!
This truly wrongs and severs the lineage of Earth;
the stupidity of the people is extreme."
"Now that I hear this,
my heart is greatly saddened and filled with fear.
I know that those who have been wronged are truly many.
What should be done?"
"Indeed,
those who love to learn but cannot obtain clothing and food—
their learning will surely slacken and their progress in the *Dào* will stop.
But if they obtain clothing and food there,
then the worthy will learn without ceasing.
One should make it so that each has their own benefit,
and not cause them to turn back and bring distress and poverty upon each other."
"What do you mean?"
"Now, women have no official palace.
A woman going to a husband
is comparable to a man going to an official post;
she should obtain clothing and food there.
When a woman goes to her husband's family,
they should combine their strength and unite their hearts to manage their livelihood.
Thus they together pass on the lineage of Heaven and Earth,
and until death, their flesh and bones remain together.
They should combine their strength together,
and thereby obtain clothing and food.
Cause the worthy to be joyful,
and cause the unworthy to suffer.
This is comparable to the land:
if the soil is good, its products are excellent,
and Heaven also entrusts things to it;
if the soil is poor, its products are bad,
and Heaven also entrusts things to it;
it does not take away what is grown by its talent and effort.
Heaven and Earth do not take away your merit,
how much less should humans?
If it is like this, then no common person will ever kill their daughter again."
"Excellent, excellent!
One great and deep harm has been eliminated,
and the *Tàipíng* of the Emperors and Kings has arrived."
"*Zhēnrén*, how do you know this?"
"Indeed,
parents and children
represent the ultimate depth of affection in the world.
They should not be distressed or troubled by each other,
nor is it right to kill them.
Is it not that killing their children
corresponds to the *qì* of bandits and thieves;
it is a great rebellion and utterly without the *Dào*.
Therefore, it disturbs the governance of Emperors and Kings most deeply.
Now, as for women,
if they are now allowed to live and not be harmed or killed by thieves,
then great joy has arrived."
"Indeed,
what you say is correct;
it can be said you understand it.
Now, if every family in the world kills one daughter,
how many hundreds of millions of families are there in the world?
There might be one family that kills a dozen daughters;
or some where the child is conceived but not yet born,
and they instead go and harm it.
Their *qì* of resentment knots together and moves Heaven above.
