How could this be without reason?
Therefore, I truly value knowing this.
If people each provide their own clothing and food through their own strength,
then it will cause women to not have divided hearts;
then their intent will be focused on doing their work,
and they will no longer have doubts.
If they suffer without merit,
then it causes people's minds to be constantly out of harmony.
This
is the natural art of heavenly nature.
*Zhēnrén*, be careful with this.
Do not discard this book;
entrust it to a humane and worthy lord.
It can eliminate a great grievance and disaster.
Be careful with the words of my book;
show them to the common people,
and none will be willing to discard daughters again.
This then corresponds to the laws of Heaven and Earth:
one man obtaining two women.
Therefore, Heaven established the law:
the number of *yáng* is odd,
and the number of *yīn* is even.
Since the times of high and middle antiquity,
humans have lost the intent of the *Tiāndào*,
and many harm and kill them,
thus conversely causing there to be many men and few women, an insufficiency.
This greatly opposes the *Tiāndào*,
causing people to bear the inherited burden (*chéngfù*) of one another,
making this the constant custom.
Later generations have intensified the world's evil faults;
it is extremely painful and without the *Dào*.
Men inherit the lineage of Heaven,
and women inherit the lineage of Earth.
Now you have severed the lineage of Earth,
causing it to be unable to be passed on through birth.
In the future, many will be extinguished without later generations.
How heavy is this sin!
These should all give birth to one another and pass on their kind,
but now you sever the lineage of Earth
and destroy the human race;
therefore, Heaven will for a long time sever their generations and kind.
Furthermore, when humans are born, they all contain and embrace the breath of Heaven and emerge fully equipped;
the head is round,
representing Heaven;
the feet are square,
representing Earth;
the four limbs
represent the four seasons;
the five viscera
represent the Five Elements;
the ears, eyes, mouth, and nose
represent the Seven Governors and the Three Lights;
these correspondences are too numerous to record,
and only the Sages know them.
Humans are born fully equipped with Yīnyáng;
when the sun and moon have completed their cycles, they break the placenta and emerge from the womb,
beholding Heaven and Earth so they may grow further,
collectively transmitting the lineage of their ancestors,
assisting Heaven in producing life,
and assisting Earth in nourishing forms.
Now the spirits of Heaven and Earth trust this household,
and thus the divine lineage of Heaven and Earth comes to reside within this person.
If the person instead harms it,
Heaven will greatly blame them.
Since people do not restrain one another,
Heaven has sent me to bring forth this
book to show to future generations.
Once the matter is revealed,
those who continue to act as before
are said to intentionally violate the laws of Heaven;
their punishment shall be doubled,
and the destruction of their lineage is beyond doubt.
Zhēnrén, be cautious of this,
and exert yourself, exert yourself!"
"Yes, yes."
"Since you have now discovered this matter,
if you were to lose or hide this book,
you would be held responsible for the sins of others."
"I would not dare, I would not dare."
"Go now,
and let each plan for their own life."
"Yes, yes."

To the right is the separate explanation of wealth and poverty, the conduct of kings that establishes good fortune, and the prohibition of people cutting off the lineages of the Earth to promote the balance of men and women and restore royal governance.
"Zhēnrén, step forward.
Now that the Qi of Tàihé from Heaven is about to arrive,
and the King's rule is becoming one of Tàipíng,
should people be chaste or should they not be chaste?
In what way should they be chaste?"
"As for chastity,
it means having few passions and desires and not acting recklessly."
"Alas,
the Zhēnrén's explanation is simplistic.
Since the era of Middle Antiquity,
it has been the failing of common people;
their teachers were inwardly jealous
and instead taught the people to act recklessly."
The Zhēnrén asked:
"What do you mean?"
"A 'chaste' man does not bestow seed,
and a 'chaste' woman does not transform.
If Yīnyáng do not join,
then there is extinction and an end to all generations.
Two people together sever the lineage of Heaven and Earth,
coveting a small and false reputation,
yet having no descendants in the future,
and losing their true essence.
This is a great harm to the world.
If you had not received life through the transmission of your parents,
how could you exist?
To turn around and sever it
is something hated by both Heaven and Earth;
such people are called 'great rebels who sever natural principles.'
Their influence causes Heaven and Earth to be separated,
so that Heaven refuses to rain
and Earth refuses to give life and transform. Why is this?"
"If Heaven does not rain,
it is because its 'chastity' means not bestowing;
if the Earth does not produce the myriad things,
it is because its 'chastity' means not transforming.
If Heaven does not rain
and Earth has nothing to produce life,
it is a great calamity and misfortune for the world.
How can this be considered good?
Looking at the Zhēnrén's explanation,
it does not follow the teachings of Heaven and Earth,
causes defiance of the Way of Heaven,
does not take joy in assisting the production and transformation of Heaven and Earth,
and instead desires to sever them.
Regarding the words that come from your mouth,
have you not failed Huángtiān Hòutǔ?"
"I am immature and have many faults.
Having seen the Tiānshī's explanation,
how could I not know the weight of my sin?"
"I shall speak for you:
matters should not go against the Way of Heaven,
yet by using the words of common people,
you do not follow the will of Heaven.
The reason why Yīnyáng are often separated
fundamentally arises from the disharmony between men and women.
Men and women
are the root of Yīnyáng.
If the root is lost in the management of affairs,
how can one obtain good fortune?"
"Now I only look to the Tiānshī.
What should be done?"
"Indeed,
the Qi of Tàipíng from Tàihuáng Heaven is about to arrive,
and one must purely model oneself after Heaven.
Therefore, one man should have two women
to symbolize Yīnyáng.
The number of Yang is odd,
and the number of Yin is even.
Then the Qi of Tàihé will arrive.
If there are far too many women,
then Yin Qi will surge;
if there are far too many men,
then Yang Qi will be without a pair and without a law,
which also leads to disaster. Why?
The numbers of humans should correspond with Heaven and Earth;
if they do not correspond, their strength will be insufficient,
and thus they meet with disaster and harm."
"The King's harem corresponds to the land;
what is the meaning of this?"
"What the Zhēnrén says now
assists my words.
Women
are the spirit of the land.
The King
is the spirit of Heaven.
The main concern is that the land may not receive the spirit of Yang,
and the King's Qi may not harmonize.
To ensure the land does not have areas that fail to transform and produce,
one woman is taken from each Zhōu
to circulate the Qi.
To take joy in transformation and production,
and fearing that his grace might not reach all
or the King's bounty might not be pervasive,
he takes them in correspondence with the land.
When his bounty is bestowed everywhere,
then the breath of Heaven circulates,
timely rain is obtained,
and the Earth is able to produce and transform the myriad things.
When the Qi of Tàipíng arrives,
one must not overvalue 'chaste' people;
their internal isolation is a profound transgression,
making the King's rule unharmonious.
Even common people should not exceed the proper measure;
therefore, there should be one man and two women."
"Excellent, excellent!"
To the right is the way to follow Heaven and Earth,
model oneself after Yīnyáng,
ensure men and women have no grievances,
bring timely rain and cause the Earth to produce life,
and make the King's rule peaceful and harmonious.
“Zhēnrén, come forward.
Now the Qi of Tàipíng is arriving,
wishing to cause the cautious and good to flourish more each day,
and the evil to daily decline and withdraw.
In cases where there are injuries or murders,
or where thieves and bandits break out,
how should governance be conducted?”
“What do you mean?”
“I mean what is known upon arriving at the site of an outbreak.
For example, if a ruler sits with doubts,
and wishes to cause the good to flourish greatly,
and the evil to immediately decline.
When thieves and bandits arise,
to cause them to be caught instantly.”
“How should such governance be handled?”
“Now, Zhēnrén should record this well.”
“Now that the Tiānshī commands it,
how could I dare not speak?
Yet every time I speak, I fail to hit upon the Tiānshī’s methods.”
“Why be so humble? Speak of it.
Since ancient times, Great Sages do not demand perfection from a single person.
If your words now do not hit the mark,
why be humble?”
“Yes, yes.
One should simply reward the good and punish the evil,
making them clearly [distinguished],
then the good will flourish daily,
and the evil will decline daily.”
“Your words are correct,
but do these rewards and punishments not have specific names?”
“I am not as diligent and capable as to speak it in one word;
I do not dare to repeat myself further.
Now, only the Tiānshī can greatly reveal it.”
“Indeed.
You are in charge of recording it;
I shall speak of it in detail for you.
When the chief official arrives at the site of the incident,
he should summon all the people of that district and neighborhood.
Have the former high officials and former subordinates sit facing East.
Have those clear in the Classics and people of Dàodé sit facing North.
Have the filial and fraternal people sit facing West.
Have the cautious sons of farming families stay in the Southeast corner, sitting and facing Northwest.
Have the wicked sons and youths stay in the Southwest corner, sitting and facing Northeast.
The ruler himself sits facing South.
Why must they sit exactly like this?
Each follows its kind;
this is the Tiāndào following human nature to establish goodness.
Thieves and bandits will be easily caught.
What does this mean?
Former high officials and former subordinates are placed in the position of righteousness;
these people have left office and do not serve,
and it is desired that they use righteousness to assist one another.
Those clear in the Classics and Dàodé are placed in the position of clarity,
desiring that they clarify their classics and the Way to assist in observing evil.
The filial and fraternal are placed in their native direction;
the most filial apply their hearts,
therefore they are made to return to their native direction.
It is desired that the filial and fraternal always be cautious and respectful as if at a morning audience.
Things are born in the East;
one rejoices in their daily progress.
The cautious and hardworking sons placed in the Southeast corner:
the Southeast is the land of growth and nourishment;
it is desired that they cultivate all things without laziness.
The wicked sons and youths are placed in the Southwest.
The Southwest
is the land where Yáng declines and Yīn rises.
Evil desires and clever manipulations,
as well as punishments and crimes, arise there.
Therefore, monkeys and apes are clever and nimble;
they are placed in the land facing decline.
Those facing East, West, and North all reside in the front;
the incautious and wicked sons reside behind them.
If there is wine, bestow one vessel to each.
If there is no wine, bestow kind words upon them,
so that they may assist in being acute and clear.
The ruler sits in a secluded place,
residing inside the door and closing himself off.
Call them one by one.
This teaches the multitude starting with rank and status.
Let each say one thing,
and record the names of each subject.
What is said and what is recorded
must correspond later.
Those whose words do not correspond later shall be held liable.
Those whose words do not correspond
are great flatterers and hypocrites;
later, the location of these flatterers and hypocrites will be known.
For those whose words correspond,
bestow rewards upon them after a long time
and promote them.
Why not do so immediately?
It would cause resentment.
To be a ruler or father
and cause one's subjects or sons to feel resentment
is not to be a compassionate father or a worthy ruler.
Therefore, once finished, dismiss all the good people.
The wicked sons and youths, along with the officials, shall pursue and capture the thieves;
if they do not catch them, they must not stop.
Zhēnrén, use this document
to entrust it to a ruler of Shàngdé,
and to show it to ordinary people,
so that each knows there is this teaching.
Then the good will flourish daily,
the evil will decline daily,
and thieves, bandits, and the wicked will be caught.”
“Excellent, excellent.
Why must this be shown in advance?”
“When Heaven is about to bring rain,
there must first be wind and clouds
to let people know.
The reason for this
is to allow people to enjoy gathering and storing.
The reason for showing it in advance
is to rejoice in the good flourishing daily
and the evil ceasing daily.
Now the Qi of Tàipíng is about to arrive.
Fearing that people might do evil and disrupt its governance,
they are awakened in advance.
Governance should emulate Heaven.
Heaven does not hide people's shortcomings,
nor did the Sages of high antiquity do so.
To do so is called 'obscure governance,'
which repeatedly leads to disaster.
It does not attain the intent of Heaven and Earth;
therefore, it is shown in advance.”
“Excellent, excellent.
Why must the ruler reside inside the door and close himself off,
while the speaker stays outside the door?”
“Indeed.
When a person is about to hear secret words,
their heart must not be aware of what is ahead.
If heads and faces are close together,
bystanders will know of it,
causing harm to the one who speaks.
To be a ruler and leader
and receive people's information,
only to later let that person suffer harm,
is called 'slandering the loyal and trustworthy'
and harming the worthy ministers.
Afterward, no one will be willing to speak again.
Information will be cut off,
and the governance will become chaotic and endangered.
Furthermore, the ruler
is Yáng
and resides within Yīn;
the subject
is Yīn
and stays within Yáng.
When Yīn and Yáng harmonize,
it makes the person take pleasure in what is said,
and when they come forward, they will surely be completely truthful.
This is the natural law of Heaven.
Does Zhēnrén know this?”
“Yes, yes.”
“Go forth now,
and do not speak recklessly.
This is the document for attaining Tàipíng.”
“Yes, yes.”
To the right is the secret method for promoting the good, stopping the evil, achieving clear insight, immediately catching thieves and bandits, and obtaining the loyal and trustworthy.
"Zhēnrén, come forward."
"Yes, yes."
"Among the actions of ordinary people in the world,
how many are of great urgency?
How many are of minor urgency?
How many are increasingly disastrous and calamitous, yet not considered urgent?
Zhēnrén should explain this precisely and in detail."
"Yes, yes.
I will sincerely speak what my heart reaches,
daring not to hide anything."
"Go ahead and speak."
"Of all matters in the world,
those that are used are considered urgent,
and those not used are considered not urgent."
"What you say is correct,
and yet it is also incorrect.
I wish to identify those things that are always urgent and cannot be abandoned;
if they are abandoned, the world would be extinguished and devoid of people.
The celestial patterns join and combine;
those that are nameless
are therefore of great urgency.
What you have said now
only briefly accords with human inclinations for the moment,
but instead, in the long term, it causes various disasters and calamities to arise."
"Zhēnrén, come forward.
What I am asking you now
is who are those that are always urgent and cannot be discarded?"
"Now, only the Tiānshī can arrange and list them,
explaining and demonstrating them distinctly.
This foolish student has overreached himself;
if even one word is off the mark,
I dare not speak again."
"Indeed,
what you say is correct.
One should only speak of what they know;
to speak forcefully of what one does not know
will surely lead to one's own exhaustion."
"What ordinary people cannot reach,
whether matters are great or small,
cannot be known by force.
Reaching them is not difficult;
not reaching them is not easy.
Therefore, since the Tiānshī has opened and shown the way to this shallow and ignorant student,
I wish for you to open up its beginnings,
and I will first promise to listen.
In the world, there are two great urgencies
and one minor urgency;
all the rest are not urgent.
Instead, they weary people's ears and eyes;
appearing good for the moment, in the long run
they summon disaster for people.
Ordinary people all suffer exhaustion and failure from them.
What is meant by this?"
"How foolish!
Yet when the people of the world first received their lives and fates,
they shared their bodies with Heaven and Earth,
embracing original Qi within the natural state.
They neither drank nor ate,
living by inhaling and exhaling the Qi of Yīn and Yáng,
knowing neither hunger nor thirst.
After a long time, they drifted far from the Divine Way,
gradually losing its intended meaning.
Those born later could no longer know it.
The True Way became empty,
daily flowing toward the false.
Hunger and thirst then arose;
without drinking or eating, they would die.
This is one great urgency.
Heaven and Earth pitied them
and together produced what can be drunk and eaten;
thus they drank and ate.
Heaven governs Yīn and Yáng,
which must be passed on,
for the lineage of Heaven and Earth must not be interrupted.
Passing it on should resemble Heaven and Earth,
one Yīn and one Yáng.
Thus Heaven caused there to be one male and one female,
their appearances being attractive to each other,
only then being able to give birth.
Why specifically cause one Yīn and one Yáng?
Because the extreme of Yáng can produce Yīn,
and the extreme of Yīn can produce Yáng.
These two pass between each other,
like when cold reaches its end and turns to heat,
or heat reaches its end and turns to cold;
this is the method of nature.
Therefore, they can perpetually generate one another,
generation after generation, without breaking the lineage of Heaven and Earth.
If male and female do not come together,
then the lineage is cut off and there are no future generations.
If there are no people in the world,
how could there be husbands and wives, fathers and sons, rulers and ministers, or teachers and disciples?
By what means would they generate and govern one another?
If there were no male and female between Heaven and Earth,
by what means would they be passed on?
It would become silent and then empty.
This is the second great urgency.
Therefore, Yīn and Yáng
pass on the lineage of Heaven and Earth,
causing it to be without end.
Rulers and ministers
govern disorder;
sages, teachers, and disciples preside over the teachings that connect to Heaven,
assisting emperors and kings in transforming the world.
Therefore, food and drink, along with the union of male and female, are mutually required.
These two are great urgencies.
The Way of Heaven has cold and heat;
if one does not shield and hide oneself,
they will partially injure or kill people.
Therefore, Heaven produced the myriad things
so they can be used as clothing.
Without clothing,
one could only live by hiding in caves to survive,
worrying about being partially injured without being completely extinguished and killed.
This is called a partial urgency.
What is called the great urgency of the Way of Heaven
refers to extinction and death;
no urgency exceeds this.
If a person does not wear clothes,
they certainly cannot eat or drink
or unite Yīn and Yáng,
which is not beneficial for them.
With clothing, the worthy are born;
without clothing, the unworthy are born.
Therefore, clothing
is merely to ward off harm;
thus the sages and worthies of antiquity did not imitate the dark and yellow.
Eating and drinking, and the union of Yīn and Yáng, cannot be cut off;
to cut them off would leave the world without people,
and it could not be governed.
By maintaining these three things,
it is enough to complete one's natural lifespan
and pass on the lineage of Heaven;
where it ends, it begins again,
without ever coming to an end.
Therefore, the sages of antiquity used this for governance.
The rest are not urgent,
and those things that summon calamity and disaster have all been removed.
What is meant by this?
These three correspond to the movement of Heaven.
Male
is Heaven.
Female
is Earth.
Clothing
means to depend upon.
They are how Heaven, Earth, and parents provide the means to support the human form and body.
Beyond these three,
other strange and false things are not necessary for living
or for passing on the kind and generating one another.
On the contrary, having too much leads to falsehood and villainy,
making governance uneven,
preventing the August Qi from arriving,
causing the Way of Heaven to go astray,
and becoming a heavy worry for the superior man.
What the six emotions favor,
everyone takes pleasure in,
without restraining themselves.
As the mind turns to enjoying them,
it consequently leads to disaster.
The superior man loses his administrative orders,
and the petty man turns to theft, robbery, and assassination;
all of this is summoned by these non-urgent things.
The world suffers from poverty and sorrow,
calamities and anomalies arise in succession,
and those at the very bottom deceive those above them;
all of this is considered a great harm.
Where this comes from has a long history;
it is not only the fault of people today, in late antiquity, or in future generations.
It is a burden inherited and passed on,
losing its original truth and reality.
Everything moves toward superficiality and vanity,
consequently returning to cause oneself sorrow and harm,
unable to complete one's natural lifespan.
Those born later have many chaotic affairs,
only because of these non-urgent matters,
which lead to calamitous events.
Therefore, they are always rushing about and cannot stop."
"The reason remote antiquity was governed through non-action,
attained the intent of the Dào,
and attained the intent of the Heavenly Heart,
was that they guarded the Root and did not lose the Three Urgencies.
The reason middle antiquity had somewhat more affairs
was that it had somewhat more diversions.
The reason late antiquity has much more sorrow
is that it has many more diversions, which give rise to evil and falsehood;
furthermore, by striving to surpass one another, they cause each other sorrow,
and thus treachery and villainy arise from within.
Internally they lose their true reality,
depart from their fundamental root,
and turn instead to harm one another,
causing people to become dazed and confused.
Although a Jūnzǐ feels sorrow in his heart
and wishes to joyfully rectify it,
the things done have hundreds of millions of facets,
making it impossible to fully regulate,
thereby throwing his governance into disorder.
Zhēnrén, ponder this meaning deeply."
"Excellent, excellent!"
To the right: Guarding the Three Realities brings balanced Qì; evil and falsehood depart; treachery and craftiness are cut off.
"Zhēnrén, come forward. Among the creeping creatures, how many are of great urgency?
How many are of minor urgency?
How many are not urgent?"
"Indeed,
each has its own urgency;
they have a thousand branches and ten thousand ends,
what are all these urgencies named?
Each creeping thing has its own will;
they cannot be named."
"Zhēnrén is already sorrowful and muddled;
are you intentionally acting foolishly?
Why are you so extreme?"
"Indeed, I do not measure up."
"If you still say of yourself that you do not measure up,
why do you say the common people have lost their way?
It is because they do not measure up to this."
"I only wish for the Tiānshī to explain it to my ignorant and dim-witted self."
"Yes!
All creeping things receive and are governed by the systems of Heaven, Earth, Yīn, and Yáng to be born.
They also alike have two great urgencies
and one minor urgency.
What are they called?
When creeping things first receive the governance of Yīn and Yáng,
they are alike in their hazy breathing,
containing the Qì of Zìrán.
They do not yet know of eating and drinking.
After a long time, they also depart far from their root.
The Great Dào wanes and is exhausted;
the Heavenly Qì cannot constantly follow, protect, and watch over them,
and consequently, they hunger and thirst.
Heaven produces food and drink for them,
and they must also transmit the lineage of Yīn and Yáng.
Therefore, there are male and female,
generation after generation producing one another without end.
If their food and drink are cut off,
and they do not transmit Yīn and Yáng,
there would be no creeping creatures under Heaven.
These are the two great urgencies.
The one minor urgency is this:
those with fur, feathers, and scales also live;
even naked creatures also live.
Those with fur and feathers
are always fine and lovely,
and they ward off cold and heat.
Those with scales
always ward off harm.
These are not necessities for life,
thus they are minor urgencies.
All other behaviors
are entirely places of misfortune.
If one does not guard these three roots
and acts recklessly without cause,
one will entirely meet with death.
This is the law suspended between Heaven and Earth by Zìrán.
Zhēnrén should ponder its meaning.
One who guards these three behaviors
attains the Central Harmony of Heaven and Earth.
Those who lose these three and pursue many diversions
will all suffer misfortune and harm."
"Excellent, excellent!
Since the Tiānshī has already revealed this,
I beg to ask one more thing."
"Proceed."
"Now, regarding those with spreading roots and hanging branches,
they do not eat, do not drink, and do not wear clothes.
What should be done about them?"
"Alas!
Your learning does not advance daily,
but instead, you become more ignorant daily.
Why is that?"
"They also have two great urgencies and one minor urgency.
What are they?"
"Listen clearly."
"Yes, yes."
"The myriad things require rain to be born;
this is their food and drink.
They must have day and night,
one period of sun and one period of shade.
During the day, the Yáng Qì provides warmth;
during the night, the Yīn Qì provides moisture.
Only then can they grow.
Residing in their place,
this is how they harmonize Yīn and Yáng.
Hanging branches and spreading leaves
are their clothing.
Such a thing lives if it has many leaves,
and it also lives if it has few leaves;
this is its substance and ornament.
Therefore, if there is no seasonal rain,
the myriad things under Heaven will not be born.
If there were not a single thing under Heaven,
it would be a great disaster.
This is the first great urgency.
If they do not obtain day and night
to harmonize the Qì of Yīn and Yáng,
things have no way to come to fruition.
If there are no fruits or seeds under Heaven,
it is a great disaster.
This is the second great urgency.
A plant with sparse leaves still bears fruit,
and one with dense leaves also bears fruit;
both bear fruit,
and it is not necessary to have dense leaves.
This is the minor urgency.
That which is the fruit
is its pit.
Therefore, the sages of old guarded the Three Realities,
and their governance achieved Great Peace.
They attained the Heart of Heaven and were long-blessed,
completing their heavenly years.
It was simply substance,
and not necessarily many diversions of black and yellow.
Therefore, those lost in the branches should return to the center;
those lost in the center should return to the root;
those lost in ornament should return to substance;
those lost in substance should return to the source.
The source
is identical to the Primal Origin of Heaven and Earth;
thus there is order.
Those dazed and confused in late antiquity
should think of returning to middle antiquity;
those in middle antiquity who are in disorder
should think of returning to remote antiquity;
those in remote antiquity who are in disorder
should think of returning to the standards and laws of Heaven and Earth;
those who doubt the standards and laws of Heaven and Earth
should think of returning to the form of Zìrán;
those who are deluded by Zìrán
should think of returning to the numinous Qì of the Upper Origin.
Thus, the sages and worthies of old who governed by consuming Qì
dwelt deeply in secluded rooms to ponder the Dào,
contemplating the images of gain and loss,
not daring to depart from the boundary of the Heavenly Laws even by a fraction.
Dwelling in a place of purity and stillness,
having attained the intent,
their governance was immediately peaceful.
How similar they were to Heaven and Earth!
Zhēnrén, deeply contemplate these words of my Dào;
do you understand them?"
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Proceed,
you have already awakened.
If one models my writings to govern disorder,
it can be immediately tested in no time at all.
Do not hide this text,
let the common people know for themselves where substance and ornament have been lost,
deeply contemplate its meaning,
and they should return to the Three Truths,
not bringing sorrow and suffering upon themselves through evil and falsehood.
Zhēnrén, be careful with this!"
"Yes, yes."
To the right: Explaining how the myriad things guard the root;
obtaining the Three Urgencies brings good fortune,
while losing the Three Urgencies brings harm.
"Zhēnrén, come forward."
"Yes, yes."
"When a filial son serves his parents,
and the parents' lives come to an end,
and then he serves them again after that,
should this service be equal to when they were alive?"
"No,
the service should exceed that of when they were alive."
"Why is that?"
"A person is born from their parents
and attains full growth because of them.
Seeing the parents die and depart,
there is no longer a time for their return;
his heart cannot forget them for even a moment.
When they were alive, they saw each other daily;
he received their teachings and commands,
and when going out or coming in, he could report back to them.
Once they have died, they can no longer behold one another;
grieving and thinking of them in constant sorrow,
therefore the service should exceed that of when they were alive."
"What the Zhēnrén says is such,
but it has already greatly lost the reality of the Tiāndào,
straying further and further away.
Now if a Zhēnrén still speaks like this,
it is natural that common people are in the dark,
and clearly they have lost the clarity of the Law of Heaven."
"What do you mean?
Please, Tiānshī."
"Indeed,
when a person is born,
they take the image of Heaven and belong to Heaven.
When a person dies,
they take the image of Earth and belong to Earth.
Heaven is the father.
Earth is the mother;
serving the mother must not exceed serving the father.
Living people
are Yáng.
Dead people
are Yīn.
Serving Yīn must not exceed serving Yáng.
Yáng is the ruler.
Yīn is the subject.
Serving the subject must not exceed serving the ruler.
If serving Yīn conversely exceeds Yáng,
it then brings about rebellious Qì;
if the service exceeds by a small amount, it leads to small rebellion;
if it exceeds by a large amount, it leads to great rebellion.
This is called rebellious Qì,
and it is called rebellious governance.
Its harm causes Yīn Qì to overcome Yáng,
those below to deceive those above,
and ghosts, spirits, and evil things to arise greatly,
collectively riding upon the Way of Man,
many walking in the daytime without avoiding people.
Now this causes diseases to never cease
and ranks of ghosts to never stop their movement.
The great fault lies here.
Do you know this?
Do you know this?"
"I, your humble student, am greatly lacking; have I committed an error or not?
Now that I have heard the Tiānshī speak,
I am moved to a great awakening.
May the Master graciously forgive my diligent and cautious service,
and reveal that which I have not understood.
Now this error is small and minute;
for what reason does it lead to this?"
"Serving Yīn more than Yáng,
and serving the inferior more than the superior,
these are great errors.
They are the utmost extremes,
so how can you say they are minute?
The Zhēnrén is once again failing to understand.
Furthermore, living people
are Yáng.
Ghosts and spirits
are Yīn.
Living people belong to the day;
dead people belong to the night.
If you wish to know the profound depth of this, follow this principle.
If the day flourishes and grows long, then it causes the night to be short.
If the night flourishes and grows long, then it causes the day to be short.
When Yáng flourishes, it overcomes Yīn;
Yīn then hides and dares not appear recklessly,
and then ghosts and spirits are concealed.
When Yīn flourishes, it overcomes Yáng;
Yáng then hides,
and therefore ghosts and spirits are able to appear in the daytime.
Now, living people
are together with the Sun;
wicked ghosts and things
are together with the stars.
The Sun
is Yáng.
The stars
are Yīn.
For this reason, when the Sun appears, the stars flee;
when the stars appear, the Sun has set.
Therefore, when Yīn overcomes Yáng, ghosts and things collectively cause extremely deep harm,
which cannot even be fully named.
This is called flourishing Yīn
and conversely weakening Yáng.
It causes governance to lose order
and conversely harms living people.
This error is extremely heavy;
you should consider it deeply."
"Yes, yes."
"Therefore, the Way of Heaven establishes laws:
the office of Yīn should always be weaker than that of Yáng.
This is just as a minister should be weaker than his ruler;
only then can the minister serve the ruler with obedience.
A child is weaker than their parents;
only then can the child serve the parents with the utmost filial piety.
If the strong cannot be moved or shifted,
the harm caused is extremely deep and severe.
Thus, although a filial child has kindness and love
and cannot forget their parents,
they must not serve them beyond what was done during their lifetime.
Does the Zhēnrén also understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Be careful, be careful!
In all matters, one must not simply follow one's whims and act recklessly."
"Yes, yes."
"If you wish to serve the dead more than the living,
and thus exceed Heaven,
what is that?"
"That is being disrespectful to the Yáng
and instead being respectful to the Yīn;
it is called turning one's back on the high and facing the low;
thus it exceeds Heaven."
"I, your ignorant pupil, am greatly at fault.
May the Tiānshī forgive me!"
"No,
simply calculate and detail it yourself;
all speech and actions should correspond to the Law."
"Yes, yes.
The Tiānshī has enlightened me;
I wish to hear fully the meaning of why one must not exceed their lifetime.
Their burials,
their clothing and goods,

should not exceed what was used during their lifetime.

and even the dead will receive punishment for it.
Sending off the dead without complying with the subterranean registers
leads to questioning that reveals the lack of truth;
instead, it becomes a deceptive act,
so the punishment becomes even deeper.
Showing excessive reverence in performing ominous affairs
actually produces ominous calamities.

"Excellent!

When the Sages of high antiquity managed funerals,

Death and funerals
are the most ominous and evil matters in the world.

therefore, one simply reaches the limit of the heart,
and the food and drink should resemble what was used during the lifetime without being deficient.
Thus, the people of that time were mostly fortunate and without illness,
and all were able to complete their natural lifespan.
In middle antiquity, the sending off of the dead and the management of funerals
slightly lost the standards and measures;
they could not be exclusive,
and they simply reached the limit of their hearts.
Losing the original meaning,
they instead showed a bit of reverence,
flowing into superficial extravagance
to satisfy the living,
while the heart and resources were only half-dedicated to the deceased.
Half of the ghosts of the dead came to eat,
the funeral management slightly deviated from the truth,
and performing the sacrifices
immediately invited evil.
It is unknown what ghosts or spirits came to eat the sacrifice together;
they consequently stayed and haunted people,
so people had many minor illnesses.
Lower antiquity then inherited the minor faults of middle antiquity
and intensified them into great failures;
they did not simply reach the limit of their hearts for their parents.
Instead, they wished to greatly satisfy the living,
creating glory to be seen by others,
acting without law,
and instead acting falsely.
They could not move Heaven,
and as for the deceased,
their ghosts could not regularly come to eat.
Instead, they excessively expanded and promoted the sacrifices
to exceed the standards and measures;
the promotion of Yīn instead harmed and weakened the Yáng.
Unknown ghosts and spirits all gathered to eat,
consequently becoming unrestrained,
acting as harmful thieves
who kill people without ceasing,
even killing one person together.
Seeing the promotion of these affairs without seeing the punishment,
why would they not strive to do it?
Therefore, evil Qì increases daily,
turning back to attack and harm the master;
having become accustomed to being fed, they follow the living without ceasing.
Yīn is strong and Yáng is weak;
they satisfy the living falsely.
Ministers deceive rulers,
and sons deceive fathers.
The King's governance is uneven because of this,
but the people do not realize it;
thus the evil becomes more severe daily
and is no longer restrained.
Therefore, the Sages and Worthies of old in serving the dead
did not dare to exceed the living;
they saw the prohibitions clearly.

"How lamentable,
how lamentable!

"Zhēnrén, come forward.

that now the balanced Qì is about to arrive;
all things must be compliant.
If even one Qì is contrary,
the transition will not arrive.

The Way of Heaven
should promote Yáng and weaken Yīn
to achieve compliance.
To instead promote Yīn and satisfy it while weakening Yáng
is contrary.
Conversely, to revere ominous affairs
invites ominous Qì,
causing the governance of chaos to lose its proper administrative position;

"The Zhēnrén must not hide this book;

That governance is not harmonized
is not the fault of Heaven, Earth, or the Human Sovereign alone;
the blame lies in the fact that every single person among the common people has their own faults,
which are then passed on and inherited,
adding up to many.
All this is caused by failing to maintain the truth.
By departing from the truth
and distancing themselves from the root to turn to false conduct,
they do not realize it.
What does this mean?
The living
is the root.
The dead
is the false.
Why is it called false?
The reality of the person is no longer seen as desirable,
yet the living act for them,
knowingly making false drawings and appearances that exceed their lifetime.
They keep to the empty and do not verify the truth of the matter.
When a person dies,
the Hún and Shén return to Heaven,
and the bones and flesh are entrusted to the earth to rot into mud.
The Jīngshén can be reached through thought
and can still be fed.
The bones and flesh no longer exist;
they are returned to the Earth.
The Earth
is the true mother of humanity.
Human life is between Heaven and Earth;
their root and their affairs when alive are different.
Who knows what their duties are after death?
Therefore, a filial child should serve them according to the root;
only then can they obtain the truth.
What was not enjoyed during life
must not be seen for the dead.
Therefore, one must not exceed the living,
or it will surely cause profound and strange transformations.
Does the Zhēnrén understand?
Be careful, be careful."
"Yes, yes.
Excellent, excellent!
The truth has indeed been revealed!"
"You can be said to know it now.
You may go."
"Yes, yes."

The Greatly Stubborn and Dull, a student of increasing darkness, bows twice and says,

attaining the heart of Heaven and Earth;
it is the first and best,
and thus is called the Dao of the Shànghuáng (Supreme Sovereign).
'Bǐngwǔ Dīngsì wéi zǔ shǐ' (Bǐngwǔ and Dīngsì as the ancestral beginning):
Bǐngwǔ and Dīngsì
are Fire
and they are Crimson;
Bǐngwǔ
is pure Yáng;
Dīngsì
is pure Yīn;
Yīn and Yáng prioritize harmony;
in all things concerning the Yīn and Yáng Qi,
they shall again harmonize the world and cause it to flourish;
'Wéi' (as/for)
means to benefit the emperors and kings,
and to remove inauspicious harms;
'Zǔ' (Ancestor)
means the predecessor,
and symbolizes the virtue of the Sānhuáng (Three Sovereigns);
'Shǐ' (Beginning)
means returning to the original beginning;
therefore, by practicing this Dao,
one shall be able to return to the Shànghuáng (Supreme Sovereign).
'Sì kǒu zhì shì wàn wù lǐ' (Four mouths govern affairs and myriad things are ordered):
A 'four' combined with a 'mouth' (kǒu)
refers to speech (yán);
those who can daily practice and speak the words of my script
shall obtain the characters of the Tiānzhèngjīng (Celestial Correct Scripture),
causing them to grasp its ultimate meaning,
which then accords above with the heart of Heaven,
enabling the myriad things each to find its place
and no longer be in disorder;
thus it says the myriad things are ordered.
'Zǐ jīn yòng jiǎo zhì qí yòu zhě' (The character 'zǐ' with 'jīn' and 'jiǎo' governing its right):
This refers to the character sòng (to recite);
it means if one recites this book without ceasing,
all matters shall be corrected in a single morning,
according above with the will of Heaven,
joyful and constantly happy,
with no more lingering rebellion.
'Qián lóng wù yòng kǎn wéi jì' (Hidden dragon, do not act; Kǎn is the regulator):
'Qiánlóng' (Hidden Dragon)
refers to the heavenly Qi returning to the first nine,
the year of Jiǎzǐ;
it is the day of the Winter Solstice,
when Heaven and Earth truly begin from this point;
'Lóng' (Dragon)
is the shàoyáng of the East,
the spirit of Wood;
therefore, the Way of Heaven emerges because of Wood,
to initiate the phase of Fire;
as for things about to flourish,
they must necessarily open their doors and gateways.
When the Zhēnrén reaches the end of the full period,
he should present this book and cast it into an enlightened place.
'Kāi' (Open)
means to clear,
to pass through,
and to reach;
by opening the south,
one further harmonizes and smooths the Yáng Qi,
dissipating the calamities of inherited burden.
'Qián' (Hidden)
means concealed;
although the Dao has arrived,
it is conversely hidden;
'Wù' (Do not/Not)
implies 'to dare' or
'not yet';
those who first see the text
do not yet know how to practice it;
'Yòng' (Use/Act)
means to govern
or manage affairs;
now Heaven should use this book to eliminate disasters;
when it appeared in the Xuánjiǎ year,
the ruler of that time could not yet deeply trace the meaning of the book,
nor was he able to use it;
therefore, it says 'do not use,'
meaning that seeing the celestial text, he did not dare to believe it exclusively and immediately put it into practice;
but for those who believe and use it,
matters are established, results appear, and there is a response,
which is its clear proof;
it then accords with Heaven,
and thus there is a response.
'Kǎn wéi jì' (Kǎn is the regulator):
Zǐ is called Kǎn;
Jiǎ is Heaven,
the guiding rope (gāng),
and Yáng;
Kǎn
is Zǐ,
Water,
Yīn,
and the regulator (jì);
therefore, Heaven and Earth always unite;
their guiding principles (gāngjì) first emerged in the Xuán Jiǎzǐ year;
this can serve as the governing regulation for a virtuous supreme ruler,
hence it says 'Kǎn is the regulator'.
Thus it is called the Tiānshū (Celestial Script) of the Shànghuáng (Supreme Sovereign),
and below it is the Zhēnjīng (True Scripture) issued for the virtuous ruler;
the book uses a plumb line to sever evil,
taking Xuánjiǎ as the subtle beginning.
In the birth of all things,
all take Jiǎ as the head
and Zǐ as the root;
therefore, it was issued according to the sequence of the first Jiǎzǐ.
'Rén dé jiàn zhī shòu cháng jiǔ' (If a person manages to see it, they shall have longevity and endure long):
'Rén' (Person)
refers specifically to the one person who is the Emperor,
a person of superior virtue who easily perceives and practices the book of the Dao,
relying on the text of auspicious omens,
and not doubting the Way of Heaven;
if he deeply grasps its meaning, he shall have longevity;
'Shòu' (Longevity)
means completing one's natural lifespan;
'Cháng' (Long)
means obtaining the infinite;
'Jiǔ' (Endure)
means to exist for a long time.
'Jū tiān dì jiān huó ér yǐ' (Simply living between Heaven and Earth):
'Jū' (Reside/Live),
to dwell;
for those who dwell between heaven and earth merely to live,
they should study the *Zhēndào* (True Way),
as frivolous and flowery writings cannot sustain people for long;
regarding the various calamities of the *Chéngfù* (Inherited Burden),
the fault lies entirely in the fact that there is no Way of substantive verification,
so today Heaven cuts it off and removes it.
"Governing a million people, immortality can be expected":
"Governing"
means to rectify;
Heaven uses this book to rectify the hearts of the many worthies,
so each may treat their own illnesses,
guarding the truth and casting out depravity;
"immortality can be expected"
means that when the world hears of it,
the *Zhēndào* will suddenly and completely emerge
to assist rulers of virtue;
those who cultivate the *Zhēndào*
follow the method of sustaining people,
therefore it is said that immortality can be expected.
"Those who are good at treating illness should not deceive or endanger":
ordinary people are all foolish,
they do not plan for their own selves,
and instead use depraved and false writings
to needlessly deceive and endanger themselves—
how lamentable!
Instead, they receive heavy punishment from Heaven
and give rise to the great debt of *Chéngfù*,
therefore Heaven causes them to discard frivolous writings
so each may guard what is real and true,
ensuring they practice it diligently from morning to night,
making it so that every person benefits their own self,
and none are willing to deceive or endanger themselves again.
"Rejoice in the *Cháng'ān Shì* (Market of Eternal Peace)":
"Rejoicing"
means nothing is more joyful than the arrival of the *Tàipíng* (Great Peace) Qi from the Sovereign in Heaven;
"in"
is an exclamation of its virtue, which is vastly superior and peerless;
"Eternal" (*Cháng*)
means for those who practice this Way,
their virtue and goodness will grow without end;
"Peace" (*Ān*)
means no longer facing peril or ruin;
those who are able to practice this Way
will have all the punishments of the *Chéngfù* of Heaven and Earth removed,
then there will be *Cháng'ān*, vast and expansive,
without further sorrow;
"Market" (*Shì*)
is the place where the whole world brings people together;
those who implement this book
say that the citizens will greatly prosper and so forth,
comparable to the people in a capital city market.
"Make people's longevity like that of *Xīwángmǔ* (the Queen Mother of the West)":
"making people"
means making emperors and kings into people who possess Heavenly Virtue and love to practice upright writings;
"like" (*Ruò*)
means to follow;
if one can greatly follow and practice my book,
that is the *Tiāndào* (Way of Heaven),
and those who attain it will have great good fortune
and be without fault;
"West" (*Xī*)
means every person nesting and preserving the *Zhēndào* within their hearts;
"King" (*Wáng*)
refers to emperors and kings who can investigate and practice the *Tiāndào*, greatly prospering and ruling as kings;
their governance is good
and is indeed unsurpassed;
"Mother" (*Mǔ*) is the evidence of old age and longevity,
the elder of the spirits.
"Comparable to the four seasons cycling back to the beginning":
"Comparable" (*Bǐ*)
means to compare;
it is like the four seasons passing on and giving birth to each other,
passing on and completing each other,
no longer harming or injuring each other,
and their governance has no punishments.
"A ninety-character plan transmitted to the *Fāngshì* (Masters of Methods)":
"Nine" (*Jiǔ*)
means to investigate
and to exhaust;
for those who can practice this,
their virtue will then thoroughly permeate the hearts of Heaven, Earth, Yin, Yang, and the myriad things;
"Ten" (*Shí*)
means ten times ten corresponding to each other,
a text of non-action;
"Characters" (*Zì*)
refers to the characters of the heavenly patterns above and below,
circulating everywhere, the Way being sufficient;
"Transmitting" (*Chuán*)
means evidence;
therefore, "entrusted characters" were made as a tally of evidence to transmit it;
"Method" (*Fāng*)
means greatly upright;
take this Way and go quickly to deliver it to a ruler who possesses the Way and Virtue,
for it can eliminate the inauspiciousness of *Chéngfù*;
such governance is both orderly and greatly upright;
"Master" (*Shì*)
is a person of simple integrity who can master their own will;
a person of simple integrity
is one whose heart is upright and can be transformed through teaching and assigned tasks,
causing them to go and propagate this Way.
"The explanation of my plan can now be seen.
Does the *Zhēnrén* (Perfected One) understand it yet?"
"Yes, yes.
Excellent, excellent!
Hearing the words of the *Tiānshī* (Celestial Master),
great joy has already arrived."
"It can be said that you already know it."
"Every time this humble student asks a question,
I know I accumulate distress for the *Tiānshī*;
had I not asked just now,
how could I have come to know this?"
"Indeed,
your words are correct.
When worthies and sages have doubts,
they all ask about them,
therefore worthies and sages all have teachers.
One must not carelessly and baselessly force an explanation;
for a forced explanation might suffice for a single word,
but it cannot be sustained through further developments."
"Yes, yes;
this is why this humble student does not dare to force an explanation."
"Your words are correct;
a great scholar is humble
and thus does not lose it."
"Now the *Tiānshī* provides a path for every matter,
stripping away and resolving all doubts,
thereby reaching what was not attained in previous questions.
Now there is something I wish to beg to ask;
it is very lacking in humility,
and I do not know if I should say it or not?"
"Regarding doubts, speak plainly and do not conceal them."
"Yes, yes.
Ancient and modern worthies and sages all have teachers;
now the *Tiānshī*'s Way is overflowing,
from whom then do you take as a teacher?"
"Excellent, excellent!
Your question
can be said to have seen my subtle meaning.
However, when I first began my studies,
I likewise asked questions of teachers,
and it was not just one person.
After a long time, the Way was completed and virtue established,
only then was I able to align my will with Heaven above.
Only after that did I know what Heaven wished to say;
Heaven sent the spirit of *Tàiyáng* (the Great Sun) to come and inform me
and caused me to speak;
therefore, I take Heaven as my teacher.
Even when instructing the *Zhēnrén*,
if Heaven did not wish to speak,
I would not dare to recklessly issue this explanation,
for Heaven would surely execute me.
Does the *Zhēnrén* also realize how truly grave this is?
You must be cautious and prudent about it."
"Yes, yes.
When this humble student asks the *Tiānshī* about doubts,
there is nothing that remains unresolved;
my heart is so joyful that I often cannot restrain my speech.
I wish to beg to ask about one more matter."
"Go ahead and speak of it."
"Yes, yes.
Now the *Tiānshī* has just provided a detailed explanation of the *Chéngfù* for this dim and shallow student;
I do not know if *Chéng* (Inheriting) and *Fù* (Burdening)
are the same or different?"
"Indeed.
*Chéng* refers to what comes before;
*Fù* refers to what comes after.
*Chéng*
refers to the ancestors who originally acted in accordance with the heart of Heaven,
but erred in small ways.
They were unaware of it,
and as the days accumulated over a long time,
these errors gathered into a great amount.
Now, the people born later, though innocent, suffer the punishment for those faults
and successively inherit and are struck by those disasters;
therefore, the former is *Chéng*
and the latter is *Fù*.
As for *Fù*,
the flowing disasters do not result from the governance of just one person;
successive instances of injustice
burden each other from before and after,
therefore it is named *Fù*.
*Fù*
is the burden that the ancestors place upon those born later.
Illnesses likewise inherit and burden each other,
meaning that disasters and harms have not yet been able to be completely cut off.
Those that were cut off rise again.
I reverently received this book from Heaven;
this Way is able to cut them all off entirely.
Therefore, it is truly grave and precious beyond comparison.
Does the *Zhēnrén* know this?"
"Yes, yes.
How fearsome!
How fearsome!"
"Go now
and ask no more."
"Yes, yes."
To the right is the explanation of the Master's Plan Book and the Ninety-Character Secret.
"Before the Zhēnrén,
of all matters in the world, what is right?
What is wrong?"
"If when tested it immediately responds,
and the matter is successful,
and those who have knots of disease find them relieved,
all of these are right.
If the matter is tested and does not respond,
if it is practiced without success,
and those who have knots of disease do not find them relieved,
all of these are wrong;
and this does not apply to only one person."
"Excellent!
Your words are truly right.
Although the words are few,
they can explain hundreds of millions of matters;
I have nothing to add to your words.
Whoever wishes to verify right and wrong
should take this as the law in all cases.
One must not harbor doubts;
this is the Tally for Summoning Trust (Zhào Xìn Zhī Fú)."
"What does this mean?"
"Regarding whether all matters are trusted or not,
why must one necessarily investigate and question them?
The Sages and Worthies of antiquity
merely observed the evidence of what people practiced,
and thus they knew it;
it was as clear as the sun and moon.
You speak of accumulating goodness;
this cannot be changed.
If you wish to know my book,
seek trust and verification in this.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Go forth;
name this the True Contract (Zhēn Quàn).
Be careful not to lose it,
and do not cast it down to the lower realms;
consider it a book of secrets, strategies, and petitions."
To the right: The Verification Book and True Contract of the Tally for Summoning Trust.
"Before the Zhēnrén,
of the people in the world, how many types of destitution (qióng) are there?"
"What do you mean?"
"Regarding those who are ordinary and unchanging,
how many are pressed by destitution?"
"Those who are destitute are numerous."
"Do those destitutions not have specific names?"
"They cannot be named."
"You do not yet know.
The people of the world have Four Destitutions (Sì Qióng)."
"What are they?"
"First, you fundamentally receive life from your parents;
once born,
during the years of youth,
one longs for one's parents and cannot leave them;
this is the first destitution.
When one has grown large and can support oneself,
girls wish to marry
and boys wish to take wives;
unable to overcome their passions and desires,
they love one another and cannot be separated;
this is the second destitution.
Having loved one another,
they give birth to children;
as the husband and wife grow old,
their appearance is no longer lovable,
but their children are young and lovable,
and must be raised;
this is the third destitution.
When the children have grown large
and the parents no longer need to support them,
the parents then become old and cannot walk;
this is the fourth destitution.
After these Four Destitutions,
if one can find an enlightened teacher
and contemplate keeping the Dào, it is still acceptable.
Those with high talent and a heavenly mandate may achieve transcendence;
next, some may attain longevity;
next, some may find a moment of joy for their bodies;
their Húnpò will dwell in the underworld,
where they may find joy again."
"What does this mean?"
"When the underworld receives the newly dead,
it questions them about all they did and experienced during their life.
Based on this, a fixed register is made of their lifetime,
and they are held accountable according to their deeds.
Therefore, matters must be prepared for in advance;
peace and danger are both obtained by oneself.
Zhēnrén, be careful of this.
Do you see this warning?"
"Yes, yes.
The Tiānshī has commanded me with words of the unseen."
"Indeed.
The reason I command and teach you
is that I see you always have good intentions;
fearing the Zhēnrén might grow lax,
I clearly show this to command you."
"Yes, yes."
"Zhēnrén, in your current study,
what term do you set for yourself?"
"I set the end of my years as the term."
"Excellent is your resolve;
it can be said you have attained the intent of the Dào.
However,
in the conduct of ordinary people,
all set the end of their lifespan as the term;
yet there is simply an end in either good or evil."
"What does this mean?
I wish to hear of it."
"Indeed.
Those who maintain good study
and end while wandering in joy
become Joyful Wandering Ghosts (Lè yóu guǐ);
by law, they do not see sorrow or suffering.
Those who end in self-sorrow and suffering become Sorrowful and Suffering Ghosts;
those who end in evil become Evil Ghosts.
These are all matters manifest to see,
which ordinary people can know.
Yet if people are unwilling to do good
and bring joy to their souls and spirits,
their transgression is truly heavy."
"What does this mean?"
"Human life receives the upright Qi of Heaven and Earth,
the Four Seasons and Five Elements,
which come together to form a person;
this is the unified body of the ancestors.
This body dwells within Heaven, Earth, the Four Seasons, and the Five Elements.
The bodies of the ancestors always took joy in goodness and were without worry,
transmitting life repeatedly.
If unworthy descendants instead cause this body of Heaven, Earth, the Four Seasons, and the Five Elements to suffer for a long time,
causing it to meet an untimely and wrongful death,
it even brings sorrow to the Húnpò.
Therefore, foolish scholars do not plan deeply;
the body is not enough to dwell in for long.
Thus, they are made to desire a quick death,
and they do not regret it when they die.
The spirit only feels wrongful pity for itself,
for no reason suffering the anger of these lowly scholars.
Thus, the great Sages and Worthies of antiquity planned deeply and thought far ahead, knowing this to be so;
therefore, they studied without ceasing.
Those who are rulers of men take joy in contemplating the Great Peace (Tàipíng);
attaining the heart of Heaven,
their merit is doubled.
Their souls and spirits can always wander in joy,
merging with the good Qi of Heaven.
Those who cannot bring peace to their rule
find their governance does not harmonize with the heart of Heaven;
not obtaining the intent of Heaven,
they have no merit in the heavens above.
When the end arrives,
their souls and spirits are uniquely rebuked in the underworld,
dwelling together with evil Qi.
Thus, the supreme sage-rulers of high antiquity knew this,
and therefore they exerted themselves.
Foolish people do not plan deeply;
thus in life they are punished by Heaven,
and in death they are punished by the Earth."
"How terrifying!
I, your disciple, am foolish and ignorant;
I do not wish to hear of this."
"Excellent!
Since you have come to study
and do not wish to hear this,
then you should exert yourself in doing good."
"Yes, yes.
The Tiānshī dwells on earth
to enable us to know the heavenly mandate.
Having received your profound teaching and commands,
how can I escape this?"
"Good!
You must simply hurry to transmit my book of the Dào,
enabling the people of the world to practice it.
Let all of them contemplate stabilizing the essence of their bodies
and keeping their thoughts in harmony with the Great Dào (Dà Dào);
moreover, let them know for themselves from where their faults and errors come,
then the debt of Inherited Burden (Chéngfù) shall be eliminated.
Heaven and Earth will be greatly pleased,
and the years shall return to those of high antiquity and even double them."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Go now;
the discourse has come to a brief conclusion.
Zhēnrén, exert yourself and strive;
come again another day."
"Yes, yes."
"When you have the book, contemplate its contents thoroughly from top to bottom;
to study without being refined
is called being indistinct and shadowy (hǔng huǎng).
If one seeks a matter without obtaining its form or image,
and one's contemplation does not reach it, the spirit
will have no way to go there."
"Excellent, excellent!"
To the right: The Tiānshī's admonition that those who do not exert themselves during life and die suddenly will still suffer the punishment of Inherited Burden (Chéngfù) as souls and spirits.
"Before the Zhēnrén,
now that you have come to study,
you should broadly know the meaning of the Dào.
Can those with little knowledge practice it?
Or can those with much knowledge practice it?"
"Indeed,
those who are fully prepared with much knowledge
can practice it."
"Alas!
You have not yet broadly grasped the essential meaning of the Dào within."
"Now, Heaven
is one,
but it conversely acts upon Earth, which is two;
what is the meaning of this?
Now, Earth
is two,
but it conversely acts upon Man, which is three;
why is this?
I, your humble student, wish to hear the meaning of their mutual interaction."
"Indeed.
Earth acts as the messenger of Heaven,
and Man acts as the messenger of Earth.
Therefore, when Heaven is pleased,
it causes all things on Earth this year to be greatly good.
If Heaven is not pleased,
even though Earth desires to nourish them,
it causes things to be bad.
If Earth is good,
then the people living upon the Earth will love goodness.
This is the clear effect of their mutual interaction.
Therefore, those who govern chaos use too many methods
and do not attain the heart of Heaven;
they must return to the original root.
When a person's words are too many and lack truth,
they must return to the essential root;
only then can their words and deeds be established.
Therefore, that which is completed in one word
is the original text;
that which stops after two turnings of speech
becomes chapters and sentences;
that which stops after three words
ends up as an explanation of difficulties;
it begins to distance itself from the truth,
and thus explanations of difficulties arise;
stopping at four words
ends up as mere rhetoric;
stopping at five words
ends up as falsehood;
stopping at six words
ends up as deception;
stopping at seven words
ends up as destruction;
stopping at eight words
ends up as separation from the Dào,
becoming further and further removed;
stopping at nine words
ends up as great chaos;
stopping at ten words
ends up as total annihilation.
Therefore, the classics change when they reach ten,
and through successive transmission, they are ruined and destroyed.
Whenever things are destroyed, one must return to the root;
therefore, return to guarding the One to serve as the primal beginning.
For this reason, the numbers of Heaven begin with one
and end at ten;
this is the natural disposition of the Tiāndào.
Thus, when the Sages of antiquity inquired into matters,
in the first divination,
the fortune or misfortune was correct;
by guarding the root,
the heavenly spirits would descend to inform them.
In the second divination,
the earthly spirits would emerge to inform them.
In the third divination,
the human spirits would emerge to inform them.
Anything beyond this or below
is all deception and cannot be used for divination.
Therefore, when the numbers of hexagrams are excessive, they are not accurate;
when human words and rhetoric are many, they are not precious."
"Excellent, excellent!
Now, because the Tiānshī always takes pity on my inadequacy,
I wish to beg for one more word!"
"Proceed!"
"Why do the numbers stop and end at ten?"
"Excellent!
You deeply hold onto wisdom to ask about this principle.
Indeed,
the numbers of Heaven begin at one
and end at ten."
"Why?"
"Heaven is initially one;
descending to meet with Earth, they become two.
Yīn and Yáng are complete and give birth together.
All things first sprout in the North;
the Yuánqì rises in Zǐ,
turns to the Northeast,
takes root in Jiǎo,
turns to the East,
emerges and spreads,
turns to the Southeast,
and produces all branches and leaves,
turns to the South and flourishes,
turns to the Southwest and moves toward fullness,
turns to the West and ripens,
and turns to the Northwest to end.
When things end, they must again return to the beginning;
therefore it is Hài, where two people together embrace the One to become the beginning of the Sānhuáng.
Thus, Hài
means 'kernel';
it is the beginning of the congealing kernel;
thus water begins to congeal in the tenth month.
Rén
means 'to be pregnant';
having become pregnant, it must inevitably grow and become larger day by day.
Thus, Zǐ
means 'to nourish';
at three, it attains the central harmonious Qì of Yīn and Yáng, and all is fully formed
to return again to the initial beginning.
Therefore, returning to the root
is called Jiǎzǐ.
When the Tiāndào gives birth to things,
they must circulate
and be fully complete, seeing the Qì of Heaven, Earth, the four seasons, and the five elements
before they are formed.
If even one Qì is insufficient,
there will immediately be a deficiency.
Therefore, basing it on the circulation of Heaven and Earth through the eight directions,
the total number comes exactly to ten.
Does the Zhēnrén now understand and know this or not?"
"Yes, yes.
Excellent, excellent!
I truly receive your profound kindness."
"You must not thank me.
Why is that?"
"The merit of a teacher toward a disciple is great and heavy,
comparable to parents giving birth to a child;
it cannot be settled through thanks."
"What does that mean?"
"Before parents have given birth to a child,
a foolish person might simply cast their seed in the wild,
where it attaches to the soil and grows as grass or trees,
and does not know itself that it should have been a human;
how could a chaotic discharge
be able to speak?
It simply becomes grass or trees.
But when Yīn and Yáng are joined,
one is born
and becomes a human;
how is this the same as becoming grass or trees?
Once a person has been born,
if they are negligent and do not serve a good teacher,
but instead serve an evil and lowly, foolish teacher,
that teacher will teach the person evil,
causing them to enter into heresy,
perhaps causing the person's death and extinction,
with their body still bearing residual crimes
that even exhaust their whole family.
Some people are born and do not know to study or inquire,
and thus they become foolish people.
A person without knowledge
merely dies in solitary sorrow and suffering,
and still has transgressions in the underworld.
Their Húnpò sees things but cannot roam in joy;
though the body is dead, they cannot become a good ghost.
Now, a good teacher who instructs people
will cause a lowly, foolish, and base person to become a good person;
if they do good without ceasing,
they become a Xián;
if they are a Xián without ceasing,
they then reach the rank of Shèng;
if they are a Shèng without ceasing,
they then attain deep knowledge of the Zhēndào;
if they guard the Dào without ceasing,
they then attain immortality (Xiān) and do not die;
if they are a Xiān without ceasing,
they then become a Zhēnrén;
if they are a Zhēnrén without ceasing,
they then become a Shén;
if they are a Shén without ceasing,
they then match their virtue with Heaven;
matching Heaven without ceasing,
