while the upper part is lush and flourishing.
None do not joyfully follow Dé and serve the governance.
This is the great and bright effect of governing through Dé."
"Now I have respectfully heard about the use of Dé;
I wish to hear about the use of Xíng."
"Indeed.
In the fifth month, Xíng is at Chūliù,
in Wǔ,
below the earth.
Below, the interior is clear and without Qi;
the space below the earth is empty.
At this time, Xíng is in the chamber;
there are no things inside;
they all reside outside.
In the sixth month, Xíng resides at Liù’èr,
in Wèi,
in the midst of the earth,
not yet emerged or reached out.
At this time, Xíng is in the hall;
at this time, the Qi of Xíng is inside,
and the Qi of Dé is outside.
Among the teeming multitudes, none do not joyfully expose their bodies,
returning to the one with flourishing Dé.
In the seventh month, Xíng is at Liùsān,
the time of Shēn.
Xíng is in the courtyard;
all things do not yet dare to enter,
stubbornly and joyfully residing outside.
In the eighth month, Xíng is at Liùsì,
the time of Yǒu;
above, it has not yet reached the boundary of Tiān.
At this time, Dé is at the gate;
all things are together joyful,
peeping at the gate and joyfully entering,
following Dé and returning.
In the ninth month, Xíng is at Liùwǔ,
in Xū,
reaching the center of Tiān above.
At this time, Xíng is in the roads and lanes;
among all things, none are not about to die or be distressed,
following Dé to enter into storage.
Thus the interior prospers daily,
and the exterior is empty and vanishing.
In the tenth month, Xíng is at Shàngliù,
Hài; at this time, Xíng reaches the six distances and eight boundaries.
In the four wilds, among the teeming multitudes of all things, none do not enter storage and hide,
following the path of Dé to the Míngtáng.
Those that crawl and walk harbor themselves to reside within;
the outer wilds are empty and without masses.
Is this because those who love to use Xíng and punishments see them following and leaving?
But if the heart's intent is to harbor Xíng within
to govern the masses,
then they will daily decrease and become few for him.
Therefore, in the fifth month, harboring one Xíng within,
one group of the masses rebels.
In the sixth month, harboring two Xíng within,
two groups of the masses rebel.
In the seventh month, harboring three Xíng within,
three groups of the masses rebel.
In the eighth month, harboring four Xíng within,
four groups of the masses rebel.
In the ninth month, harboring five Xíng within,
five groups of the masses rebel.
In the tenth month, harboring six Xíng within,
six groups of the masses rebel.
Thus the outside is completely without things,
and all flee to the inside;
this is a clear and proven effect.
Therefore, for those who govern with Xíng,
people are respectful and cautious on the outside but rebel on the inside;
thus the masses daily become fewer.
For this reason, in the eleventh month, harboring one Dé within,
one group of the masses enters and follows.
In the twelfth month, harboring two Dé within,
two groups of the masses enter and follow.
In the first month, harboring three Dé within,
three groups of the masses enter and follow.
In the second month, harboring four Dé within,
the masses of the four directions enter and follow.
In the third month, harboring the five Yáng flourishing Dé within,
five groups of worthy people enter and follow.
In the fourth month, harboring six Dé within,
all things come out and appear together;
none are not teeming,
and both inside and outside return to him.
This is the effect of Tiān’s bright law.
In the second and eighth months,
Dé and Xíng are equal in half;
thus in the second month, things are half-injured by the cold,
and in the eighth month, things are also half-injured by the cold.
During the second month,
Dé wishes to bring its masses out of the gate,
while Xíng wishes to bring its masses into the gate;
both are on the boundary.
Therefore, in the second and eighth months, the Xíng and Dé of all things just happen to meet;
life and death are each half,
thus they are half-injured.
You now joyfully know the constant law of Tiāndì
and the clear evidence of Yīnyáng;
this is precisely it.
Xíng is daily injury and killing;
people detest and fear it,
and one does not obtain the strength of the masses,
yet conversely says there are no people.
Dé is relaxed and gives life daily...
Without using punishments, the myriad things do not feel fear;
instead, they are said to submit and surrender.
They all return to assist the Wáng in his governance.
This is the clear evidence of Tiān,
manifest and beyond doubt.
If people today are not awed or fearful and cannot be governed,
what can be done about it?
Yet, the Sages and Gentlemen of antiquity awed people through the Way and Virtue,
not through physical strength or punishments.
Those who do not delight in doing good
and whose virtue is inferior instead wish to use punishments and frightening awe to assist in governance;
yet they see themselves being abandoned.
Indeed, punishment can only be used to cast off exhaustion and dissolution;
it is insufficient to bring life to the myriad things.
It is clear that the restless multitudes of creatures regard the ruler as their leader.
If people are currently not internally attached
but instead practice deception,
the great fault lies here.
"Now you have come to study continuously for some time;
though the matters you have asked about are numerous
and you have accumulated many texts,
you have not yet been able to purely believe the words of my books.
Have you gained any understanding from this yet?"
Chún bowed his head in respectful greeting:
"My fault is very great;
I have failed the words of the Enlightened Teacher and the Shénrén.
Internally, I am ashamed and perspiring.
I am merely foolish, of little virtue, and extremely lowly.
Though the days I have studied are many,
my mind is suddenly unable to fully penetrate the words of the Enlightened Teacher.
Therefore, I dared to ask repeatedly.
This is very immodest of me.
Have I caused the Teacher worry for a long time?"
"It is only that your study is not yet refined;
you must be careful with it.
Tiān hangs down images to create laws for humanity
and establishes teachings and commands for Dìwáng.
These can be modeled for governance,
and not one in ten thousand will fail.
If you wish to know its meaning,
it is precisely this.
If governance does not follow this law,
it constantly makes Tiān depressed
and indignant without relief;
therefore, there are many calamities.
You must take heed of this.
Those whom Tiān will cause to flourish
take their model from Virtue;
those who will decline and fail
take their law from punishment.
This is what is meant.
My words
carefully align with the compass and square of Tiān, Earth, and Yīnyáng.
They follow the principles of Tiān and Earth,
speaking clearly for Tiān,
recording the use of teachings and commands to show you.
My words
are exactly like a sharp arrow with no difference;
following them leads to daily flourishing,
while opposing them causes commands to exhaust themselves.
The law of Tiān is divine indeed, divine indeed!
For this reason, the Shénrén, Zhēnrén, and Dàshèng of old were able to deeply establish systems and laws
and create standards for Dìwáng
because they all saw the essence of the heavenly patterns.
They alone were internally enlightened to the meaning of Yīnyáng,
and only then followed what Tiān and Earth allowed for governance.
Their hearts aligned with the divine light,
observing what was possible to do;
thus their governance did not fail once in ten thousand times.
Now, foolish officials and people think that the laws of Tiān can be rashly violated,
acting self-indulgently without following the laws and standards;
thus they greatly disturb their lord's governance.
The great fault lies here.
Now that you have obtained the books,
why not examine your heart's intent in detail,
and think upon it carefully
in a quiet room or secluded place?
Contemplate the movement of Tiān;
then you can transmit the teachings of Tiān
to instruct the foolish
and assist Dìwáng in establishing laws and standards.
If you are to raise and use punishments,
you must deeply consider the place where punishments reside;
everyone is seen to depart from them,
leaving them in silent solitude without any crowds.
Thus, winter punishment is in the four wildernesses where there are no people;
the myriad things all rebel against it and hide within,
avoiding it intensely.
Summer punishment is within;
the myriad things all come out and return to Virtue.
Under the ground and inside rooms are empty;
punishment resides silently and alone,
while everything follows Virtue to the wilderness.
When Virtue is outside,
then the myriad things return to the outside;
when Virtue is in the dark and empty spaces, then things return to the inside.
The punishment of Tiān has extremely flourishing majesty;
if it can fortunately suppress and make the people and myriad things submit,
why instead can it not restrain its own crowds?
Is this not strange?
Clearly, punishment cannot be used lightly or rashly.
If one portion of Orthodoxy is harmed,
the breath of Tiān is disordered;
if one portion of Compliance is harmed,
the breath of Earth rebels;
if one Rú is harmed,
the many Rú vanish;
if one Xián is harmed,
the many Xián hide.
All matters are shaken by this.
Therefore, the Sages, Sage Kings, and Dìwáng of old deeply saw these books of Tiān's warnings;
thus they feared them and did not dare to act rashly,
fearing they would not obtain the heart of Tiān
and would be unable to secure themselves.
People of the virtue of Shànghuáng Tiān
alone see the clear effects of the Way and Virtue;
they are not weary of consistency
and do not fear shocks,
and the crowds return to them and attach to them.
Thus they maintain the Way to preserve themselves
and maintain Virtue, not daring to lose it.
Since you have my books to recite and read,
if you have doubts in your heart,
always take one volume of this book,
keep it near you and examine it morning and night,
taking it as a clear warning and proof;
then you will obtain the intent of Tiān's heart.
Those who violate this
are already in opposition to Tiān.
This is like the Qiánkūn of the *Changes*,
which cannot be reversed;
like the movement of the Liùjiǎ,
which cannot be changed;
like the fixed laws of the Wǔxíng,
which cannot be lost;
like the light of the Sun and Moon,
which cannot be covered;
just as the lord resides above
and the minister is below;
thus it cannot be disordered.
This is why the governance of Tiān, Earth, and Yīnyáng
has those who love to practice Virtue.
Perhaps there are foolish people who instead love punishment;
they should constantly observe this book
to resolve their confusion
and strive to teach people to be good Rú,
maintain the Way and Virtue,
and think of setting aside punishments.
My books [...] rectify the laws and standards of Tiān.
Is practicing the Way and Virtue easy?
Is practicing punishment difficult?
If you love them, they increase daily;
if you use majesty, they instead disappear daily.
You, go quickly!
Transmit my books for Tiān,
and do not doubt.
The words of my books do not fail the restless multitudes of Tiān, Earth, and the Liùhé."
"Yes, yes.
I truly return to contemplate my faults,
considering only the high and low,
not daring to lose a single thing."
"Go,
be cautious and careful.
If you cannot distinguish and think in detail about the meaning of my books,
just observe the great divisions of Tiān, Earth, and Yīnyáng.
From the Chūnfēn to the Qiūfēn,
Virtue resides outside.
None of the myriad things do not come out to return to the Wáng outside;
hibernating insects emerge from their holes,
and the people emerge from their houses.
From the Qiūfēn to the Chūnfēn,
Virtue is within.
None of the myriad things do not return to the Wáng within;
all hibernating creatures enter their holes,
and the people enter their houses;
this is the clear effect of governing with Virtue.
From the Chūnfēn to the Qiūfēn,
punishment governs within.
The myriad things all follow and go outside;
the inside is empty,
residing silently and alone.
From the Qiūfēn to the Chūnfēn,
punishment resides outside and governs the outside.
There are no things and no Qi,
empty of crowds;
all enter to follow Virtue.
This is the proof that punishment cannot be used for governance.
Therefore, Virtue shares the heart and strength of Tiān.
Thus, when Yáng emerges, it also emerges;
when Yáng enters, it also enters.
Punishment shares the strength and heart of Earth.
Thus, when Yīn emerges, it also emerges;
when Yīn enters, it also enters.
Virtue shares strength with the life-breath;
thus, when the life-breath emerges, it also emerges;
when it enters, it also enters.
Punishment shares strength with the killing-breath;
thus, when the killing-breath emerges, it also emerges;
when it enters, it also enters.
Virtue is in the same rank as the upward movement of Tiān...
Punishment is ranked alongside the subterranean movement.
Virtue always dwells with the substantial,
and Punishment dwells with emptiness and nothingness.
Virtue always dwells with flourishing;
therefore, when there is external flourishing, it emerges,
and when there is internal flourishing, it enters.
Thus, it enters in winter and emerges in summer.
Punishment dwells with the qi of decline and death;
thus, it emerges in winter and enters in summer.
The qi of death is cold;
therefore, the place where it resides is cold.
Thus, Virtue shares the same qi as the Dìwáng;
therefore, for external kingship, it emerges from Yīn;
for internal kingship, it enters into Punishment.
Punishment shares the same position as the xiǎorén;
therefore, where it resides, there are no shìzhòng.
That to which things return
accumulates the Virtue of the Dìwáng;
it is constantly seen as the object of return,
therefore it is called Dìwáng.
Punishment has never shared a dwelling with things;
it lacks shìzhòng,
thus it cannot be called a jūnzǐ.
For this reason, the shèngrén of antiquity uniquely engaged in deep deliberation,
observing the actions of Tiāndì and Yīnyáng,
taking them as their model and law.
They knew that its great [...] did not fail once in ten thousand times;
therefore, they did not dare to violate it.
This is the clear evidence for rectifying Tiāndì;
can it not be carefully calculated?
Can one not be cautious?
It is the law of zìrán;
it is not for the sake of man.
This is the constant conduct of Heaven and Earth.
Now I have told you everything.
You should repeatedly and deeply contemplate its meaning,
and do not lightly change your actions."
"Yes, yes,
I do not dare to betray this."
"Go,
I have already fully transmitted and entrusted the true words of the law to you;
my worries are resolved.
Removing faults for Heaven,
so as to enjoin the zhìdé,
and to cause the Wángzhě to flourish.
You must not dare to let this be cut off,
or else you will suffer the harm."
"Yes, yes."
The preceding is the secret key based on the Tiānfǎ to clarify the successes and failures favored by the rulers of the past and present.
"This lowly and ignorant one cannot bear it anymore;
what my heart desires to ask
offends the taboos of the Tiān Shī,
and the transgression is most severe.
What my mind desires to say
cannot be stopped;
as a small person, I cannot restrain my wish,
and within my five viscera, I feel agitation and distress.
I beg to ask one great question of doubt.
Since the Tiān Shī treats me with the intimacy of a newborn child,
surely you will take pity on my earnest longing!"
"Walk the Way and speak of it.
Why be so modest?"
"Yes, yes.
Now the Tiān Shī is constantly in spiritual union with Huáng Tiān Hòu Tǔ,
and your heart is in deep accord with the intent of Heaven and Earth,
like overlapping compasses or matching squares,
without the slightest discrepancy.
You know what Heaven and Earth are constantly worried about...
Therefore, this lowly and ignorant one, despite my unworthiness and shame,
dares to come forward and ask in detail,
wishing to know what are the great taboos of the Shén Líng of Heaven and Earth?"
"How wonderful!
Your essence and progress are advancing!
You may now ask what directly enters the heart and mind of Heaven and Earth.
Once people know this,
it will be set in the hearts of worthy men
and will never depart for ten thousand generations.
I have always taken joy in wanting to speak of this,
but had no one to speak with.
Now that a Zhēn Rén asks about it,
my heart is filled with sudden joy,
and I shall distinguish and explain it for you in detail,
not daring to hide anything.
The reason for this
is that I fear the Shén Líng of Heaven and Earth would deeply loathe me,
which would bring great disaster upon my person.
Zhēn Rén, simply sit peacefully and listen clearly."
"What Heaven and Earth suffer from most
is that they loathe people who are un-submissive and unfilial.
What does this mean?
I wish to hear it."
"How wonderful
is your inquiry!
In the central harmony of Heaven and Earth, there are three types of Qì;
internally they together form one family
and conversely work together to govern life
and nourish the ten thousand things.
Heaven is the master of birth
and is called the Father;
Earth is the master of nourishment
and is called the Mother;
Man is the master of managing them
and is called the Son.
The Father should be the master of teaching and transformation according to the seasons;
the Mother is the master of following the Father's actions to nourish them;
the Son receives his life-mandate from the Father
and receives nourishment and food from the Mother.
As a son, one should respectfully serve his father and love his mother."
"What does this mean?"
"Indeed, the Father's teachings have measures and seasons;
thus, Heaven teaches birth and nourishment according to the four seasons,
for beginning and ending have their own times.
Now, when evil people oppose this,
it is like a son being un-submissive to his father.
The Qì of Heaven loses its administrative orders
and does not attain its intent.
Because of these great evil people, Heaven produces disasters and anomalies
to afflict and harm its children.
This is like a family
where the father in anger punishes his son;
thus, transformations occur.
Father and son are not in harmony,
and because of the resentment that the son does not submissively follow the stern father's teachings and orders,
then Yin arises to overcome Yang,
those below deceive those above,
and many rebellious sons are produced.
Ministers lose their offices,
ghostly things rise up in great numbers
to together afflict people,
the treacherous and cunning dwell by the roadside,
and all those belonging to the hidden and un-submissive Yin
find their blame in the opposition to Heaven and Earth.
Zhēn Rén, can one then be un-submissive?
This is the method of nature;
it is like a shadow responding to a form,
or a horse following along without breaking away.
Take heed of this."
"Yes, yes."
"I have now respectfully received the Master's explanation of Heaven's teachings and admonitions;
I wish to hear about offending the prohibitions of the Earth."
"Granted.
Zhēn Rén, listen clearly."
"Yes, yes."
"Heaven
is the Father;
Earth
is the Mother.
Both Father and Mother are the same as humans;
how are they different?
Heaven is also Heaven,
and Earth is also Heaven.
Father and Mother are distinguished only by Yin and Yang, male and female,
but their likes and dislikes are the same.
Heaven nourishes human life;
Earth nourishes the human form.
People are greatly ignorant, obstructed, and dim-witted;
they do not know to honor and respect their parents,
constantly causing Heaven and Earth, who gave birth to these common people,
to have regrets and be troubled without relief."
"What does this mean?"
"How excellent
are your words!
You have deeply grasped the intent of Heaven and Earth.
Great disasters are about to be cut off,
and people will surely find good fortune."
"What does this mean?
May the Tiān Shī distinguish it."
"Indeed,
today the people of the world all together commit harm
and bring grievances to their parents."
"What does this mean?"
"The Qì of the four seasons
is what Heaven carries out;
yet people oppose it,
which is to commit harm against their Father."
"What does this mean?"
"Now people take Earth as their Mother
and obtain clothing and food from her,
yet they do not together love and benefit her,
but instead together commit harm against her."
"What does this mean?"
"Indeed,
Zhēn Rén, listen clearly.
People are exceedingly ill-behaved;
they together pierce and bore into the Earth,
and greatly undertake earthworks,
not following the proper principles.
The deep ones reach down to the Huáng Quán,
while the shallow ones are several fathoms deep.
The Mother internally feels solitary sorrow and resentment,
for her many children are greatly irreverent and unfilial,
and she is constantly suffering from anger and distress,
yet she has no way to convey her words.
In ancient times, the sages' timing had not yet come to speak of this,
so people were allowed to act recklessly,
thinking that the Earth does not feel pain.
But the Earth internally feels solitary pain beyond measure,
and this moves Heaven above,
yet people do not know it.
Distressed and troubled by her children whom she cannot control,
she complains about humans to the Father above.
This complaining has accumulated for a long time,
and after a long time the instances have multiplied;
thus the Father's anger does not cease,
and ten thousand kinds of disasters, anomalies, and strange events arise together.
The Mother, being unhappy,
is constantly angry and unwilling to exert effort in nourishing the people and the ten thousand things.
When both Father and Mother are unhappy,
the ten thousand things and the people die.
Because they did not follow the proper principles,
the blame lies here.
What later generations do becomes more severe by the day;
they do not grasp the intent of Heaven and Earth,
but instead loathe that the words of Heaven and Earth are not in harmony.
Furthermore, they together despise their sovereigns and kings,
saying they cannot bring peace to their internal governance.
On the contrary, each person is personally guilty of transgressions against Heaven and Earth without realizing it themselves;
instead, they push their faults onto their superiors to blame them.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth no longer love humanity.
Seeing their deaths is sudden;
though people have illnesses
and cry out when near death,
their guilt is clear,
and the parents of Heaven and Earth no longer rescue them.
This is because their crimes are deeply transgressive,
and the burden of blame
actually lies here.
The actions of later generations are even more severe than those before;
they imitate one another,
taking it as a constant law.
They are no longer restrained,
nor do they know to forbid one another;
thus disasters increase daily,
and truly they together cause grievance to Heaven and Earth.
Heaven and Earth
are the parents of humanity,
yet the children instead together harm their parents and commit injury and illness against them;
this is no small crime.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth are most resentful of unfilial and un-submissive behavior
and no longer pardon it.
Although human lives are short and the deaths are countless,
there is no cause for grievance.
Does the Zhēn Rén understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Now Heaven has sent you to come and ask in detail,
knowing that I can speak of this.
Zhēn Rén, you must not take yourself lightly,
and you must not fail to be cautious."
"Yes, yes."
"Nowadays, people together harm their parents,
and go against their administrative decrees.
In the mind of the Zhēnrén,
would he still be willing to nourish them for long?
Therefore, Heaven does not show them great compassion."
"Now, I hope the Tiānshī will take pity on this ignorant student and explain in detail:
how is it known that Heaven and Earth are constantly indignant and melancholy,
and that they resent people frequently initiating earthworks?"
"Splendid!
Heaven has caused you to ask such a penetrating question;
it is enough to know that Heaven and Earth have sent you to ask this."
"Yes."
"I greatly fear Heaven
and dare not hide anything,
for fear that my person might suffer disaster.
Now, I shall let you know it clearly,
so that you will forever fix it in your heart
and never forget it.
Nowadays, if a single household initiates works and digs up the earth,
several households will be afflicted by illness:
some may die,
some may encounter bandits or legal officials,
some may face warfare or litigation,
or encounter snakes, wasps, tigers, wolves, or evil birds that harm people.
Large earthworks bring great evil and misfortune;
small earthworks bring small evil and misfortune.
This is because the Earth is indignant
and causes the numinous spirits to produce these disasters.
Thus, many people under Heaven and Earth are ill;
this is the clear proof.
Do you understand?"
"Yes, yes.
However, nowadays there are some who initiate earthworks yet encounter good fortune and no harm;
why is this?"
"Splendid
is your question!
All such acts cause harm,
but if one happens upon good and gentle soil,
it will not immediately bring illness or harm to people;
instead, many in the four directions will encounter misfortune,
and after a long time, it will eventually harm the person.
One who encounters evil land cannot be endured by the Earth,
and it will immediately cause harm.
It also simultaneously harms distant places.
Why is this?
This is comparable to a person of good and gentle disposition;
although they suffer an injustice,
they can force themselves to endure for a moment,
yet their heart does not forget,
and they will harm the perpetrator later.
An evil person cannot endure
and acts immediately."
"Excellent, excellent!
Now, the body of the Earth is massive,
while humans, compared to the Earth,
are extremely small.
What they do is also too small to mention;
how could they possibly cause illness to the Earth?"
"Splendid
is your challenge!
Heaven has caused you to distinguish what is unclear.
How is this known?
By your words being so earnest.
You now wish to speak;
your heart was troubled within,
and you felt relief only upon speaking.
The spiritual essence of Heaven and Earth resides in your belly;
it respects your urge to speak,
though you truly do not realize it yourself.
All that humans wish to do
is caused by Heaven."
"Yes.
I dare not hide anything."
"Your virtue is bright."
"Yes, yes."
"Now you say
that humans are tiny
and their actions cannot cause illness to the Earth.
Suppose a great man is ten feet tall
and ten spans in girth;
in his teeth, there are decay-worms.
They are tiny and not worth mentioning,
yet they reside in the man's teeth.
When the great pain is about to begin,
the person cries out in distress,
and eventually, the teeth all fall out.
The size of a human compared to Heaven and Earth
is like these worms harming a person.
Teeth are even harder than the strength of metal, stone, or bone.
Those worms are merely flesh;
why then are they able to cause illness to this man?
Humans' causing illness to the Earth is just like this.
Do you understand?
Come, the Zhēnrén shall clarify it further for you."
"Yes, yes."
"Suppose a person is over ten feet tall
and over ten spans in girth.
An ulcer-worm is no more than an inch long;
its body is tiny,
so small it is not worth mentioning.
It resides within the person's skin
and bores into it day and night.
The person becomes ill from it
and even reaches death.
The size of a human compared to the Earth
is just like this.
These worms are extremely small;
why then do they instead harm and kill this person?
Is the Zhēnrén being foolish or dim-witted
that his words are so extreme
and seem similar to those of commoners?"
"In truth, I cannot compare."
"If even you cannot compare,
why speak of commoners?"
"I have faults and am ignorant;
I only wish the Tiānshī would hear of my inadequate karma
and fortunately explain the meaning fully for this ignorant student."
"Yes,
I will not hide it.
I know the illness of Heaven and Earth is severe,
so I tell you word for word.
Come, I will tell you one more thing,
to make you perceive it clearly and know it with double clarity."
"Yes, yes."
"Now, even a great man or a strong warrior cannot restrain a scabies mite;
they are so tiny they can hardly be seen.
If there is about a peck of them feeding together on this person,
the person will suffer such pain they cannot lie down,
and in severe cases, they are confined to bed.
Now, scabies mites, fleas, and lice are tiny,
but when they gather in great numbers
to feed together on a person—
though venomous insects kill,
scabies mites and fleas equally cause a person to be agitated and distressed,
unable to sit in peace,
and all produce sores and ulcers.
The size of a human compared to the Earth is just like this.
Do you understand now?"
"Yes, yes."
"Come,
perhaps you see what I have said
as insufficient to serve as a law;
now I shall speak of it for you.
Although humans are small,
the state of their grievances against the Earth
makes one clearly know for oneself
that there is deep blame and responsibility;
it is immediately visible.
Suppose a large neighborhood has a hundred households
and a hundred wells;
a township has a thousand households
and a thousand wells;
a county has ten thousand households

they only delight in making the King sit in peace and travel far.
His governance then attains the heart of Heaven above
and the intent of Earth below.
In the center, it makes all the people without exception rejoice,
with no one suffering grievances or losing their livelihood.
All crawling creatures
move towards his influence and are transformed by it.
There are none who die of plague,
and among the myriad things, none fail to find their proper place.
Heaven and Earth harmonize,
and the three Qì are all pleased.
For this, the Ruler of Men has his lifespan increased and his years added.
The common people should further seek extraordinary methods and special arts for the Emperor.
Texts that were hidden or concealed will all emerge for him.
The whole world responds,
all saying, 'How wonderful!
Excellent!
This has never happened before!'
From the eldest to the infant,
none know how to do evil anymore.
All carry their extraordinary and special methods
to offer them to the Emperor.
When the Emperor obtains them,
he can extend his years.
All cherish their ruler as he grows old.
Because his governance attains the heart of Heaven,
Heaven or Earth might send a spirit carrying medicine to inform him,
'Child, obtain this and consume it.'
Thus, to the end of his life, he shall not know a time of exhaustion.
This is what is brought about by the conduct of supreme good subjects, children, and commoners.
Does the Zhēnrén understand this or not?"
"Yes, yes."
"You can be said to have awakened already.
Therefore, the first-class good subjects and people of the Supreme Emperors of Great Antiquity
acted in this way.
By what means can this be sought
to achieve this upright governance?
By using this Dào of mine,
which is precisely the first-class text of High Antiquity.
If the Zhēnrén thinks deeply on its meaning,
he will obtain the heart of Heaven.
I respectfully received this from the heart of Heaven
to descend and resolve disasters and remove various harms for the virtuous ruler.
I fear the majesty of Heaven;
how would I dare not speak all its words?
Heaven will soon be angry at our writing to the Zhēnrén;
hurry to go and deliver it.
When a virtuous ruler obtains it to govern,
he becomes like Heaven—
how would he be different from Heaven?"
"Excellent! Excellent!
Seeing the Tiānshī's words,
I have come to know that the pure Qì of the Great Peace of Heaven has truly arrived.
The means to bring it about,
the text, has already emerged.
Joyous indeed! What more is there to worry about?
Now the common people are not your concern,
so why is it that you rejoice upon seeing good
and worry upon seeing evil?"
"The reason is this:
when the good Qì arrives,
then the heterodox and evil Qì is hidden.
Then I shall always be at peace
and can be without illness or injury.
When the evil Qì arrives,
then the good Qì is hidden.
This makes me fear disaster and not dare to act.
The whole world is the same.
Therefore, when I see good, I rejoice."
"Excellent
are your words."
"The Tiānshī has graciously taken pity
and already explained the law of supreme good subjects and children.
I wish to hear again the art of supreme filial piety."
"Excellent!
You ask difficult questions.
Now, the first-class supreme good filial son
thinks of his parents growing old and departing.
He resides alone in a quiet place, contemplating and thinking of them,"
One who is always distressed by being in a low position,
where can they obtain the art of immortality?
Formerly, one could have gone with their parents to dwell there,
despising wealth and valuing the Dao just to live.
Thinking of string music and sorrowful songs
to please their parents,
subtly transforming their intentions
to lead them into the Dao,
joyfully hoping to dwell with them forever
without knowing old age,
they constantly seek extraordinary methods for them in unusual lands,
wandering through distant places.
Utmost sincerity then moves Heaven,
and they only stop when their strength is exhausted;
their food, clothing, and wealth are self-sufficient,
and they no longer set aside treasures for future generations.
On the contrary, if one completely distresses their parents
by making them guard such wealth,
for those in the family who die first,
their souls still find no joy in such distress and bitterness.
When eating, they do not seek auspicious blessings,
but only say, "Exert yourself and love yourself in the underworld,
so that you may not suffer through longing for the living masters."
This is called the conduct of the most virtuous filial son of the Tàigǔ Shànghuáng.
When those from the four directions hear of his goodness,
there are none who do not rejoice for him from afar,
and all joyfully think of imitating him.
Consequently, they emulate one another,
and compassionate and filial ministers are produced for the emperors and kings.
The worry of a filial son for his parents
and the worry of a virtuous minister for his lord
should indeed be like this.
What the Zhēnrén has said this morning
is merely conduct that corresponds to mediocrity,
where each person only desires to preserve their own body.
How does this benefit the lord, father, or master above,
and yet you conversely claim to be a person of supreme goodness?
This is merely called being a person who protects and benefits oneself.
If even the Zhēnrén considers this to be good,
how much more so for the common people?
Seeing themselves as acting with caution and trustworthiness,
not violating the king's laws,
and having no criminal reputation,
they cry out and say of themselves
that they have not failed Heaven,
nor failed their lord, father, or master.
Your conduct merely happens to preserve your own body,
yet you conversely and profoundly claim to have merit toward those above,
crying out to Heaven and Earth.
All such people belong to the lowest ignorance;
they cannot be people of supreme goodness.
The reason I am now distinguishing and explaining this in detail for the Zhēnrén
is that I wish for the Zhēnrén to present these writings to a sovereign of supreme virtue,
to deeply demonstrate and instruct the various worthies,
causing them to suddenly awaken
and know for themselves whether their conduct is right or wrong,
and whether it should also be of benefit above to the lord, father, and master, is it not?
Since the Tàishàng and middle ages,
people have become increasingly foolish,
daily possessing more wealth
and engaging in deviant conduct,
yet conversely claiming for themselves to have merit toward Heaven, Earth, lord, father, and master.
These are people of great rebellion who do not understand principle.
Does the Zhēnrén also know of this?"
"Yes, yes."
"You may be said to have already awakened.
To practice goodness today
is truly very difficult;
you must be cautious of it.
If you do not exert effort to spread my writings
to resolve the great sickness of Heaven and Earth,
and to allow the emperors and kings to roam without worry or trouble,
so that none in the world are not joyful,
down even to the plants and trees—
then you have not yet been able to correspond to a person of supreme goodness.
You are merely called a person who preserves your own body;
how then can you be placed within Heaven and Earth?
As for those who desire to joyfully preserve their own bodies,
the petty person is even more extreme in this.
Do you also know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"You may be said to have already awakened;
be cautious!"
"Yes, yes.
Now that the Tiānshī has fortunately taken pity on this ignorant and lowly student who does not understand the Dao,
I wish to hear again about the conduct of a disciple of supreme goodness."
"Indeed.
As for a disciple of supreme goodness,
after receiving Dàodé from the master,
they reflect upon their connection to the master's kindness
and finally manage to become a complete person.
Then they are able to follow worthies for a long time
without losing their place in the ranks.
Some obtain official positions
to repay their parents,
while others are able to go deep into the Dao
and know the arts of self-nourishment.
A person is born from their parents,
achieves Dàodé through their master,
and receives honor and respect from their lord.
Whenever they dwell alone in one place,
they think of how the lord, father, and master are growing old
and that there is nothing with which they can repay them.
They constantly think of acting for the master to obtain extraordinary methods and unusual writings
with which they can repay his merit.
Merely thinking of this makes their heart truly ache
if they cannot obtain anything marvelous.
Thinking of this, they act accordingly,
further learning to serve worthies,
entrusting themselves to their master,
and speaking on his behalf,
perhaps causing the master to obtain a good assistant for the state above,
and further being of lasting benefit to the governance of the emperors and kings.
Conduct like this corresponds to a disciple of supreme goodness from Tàigǔ.
Among later generations, those who are enlightened lords and worthies
are called people of supreme goodness.
As for the Zhēnrén,
for now you can only be said to be easy to teach, cautious, and trustworthy.
If from now on you do not understand the master's heart,
then this
is merely being a submissive disciple
who only strives to complete his own person.
How does this benefit those above,
and yet you are called a good disciple?
The Zhēnrén's words still say so,
but the common people and ignorant men often claim for themselves to have merit toward their masters.
This is certainly the case.
For those who are ministers and sons, as well as disciples who are sons,
if they do not follow the teachings and commands of the lord, father, and master,
they all correspond to the crime of great rebellion
and can no longer be named as such.
The good sons, subjects, ministers, and good disciples spoken of by the Zhēnrén—
their conduct merely happens to not fall into the category of crime.
How foolish you are!
How can this be called 'goodness'?
Therefore, common people are ignorant;
I alone have seen through this for a long time.
Now, measuring it by what the Zhēnrén says,
I already know the reality:
you have lost the correct path
and entered into deviance and falsehood;
you have been deluded for a long time!
Therefore, Heaven alone deeply knows this;
thus it is angry and displeased.
Disasters accumulate;
this is precisely Chéngfù.
If everyone were like the Zhēnrén's words and conduct,
merely preserving their own bodies and not committing wrongs,
while claiming for themselves to have merit toward Heaven, Earth, and others,
this is the extreme of great ignorance.
You must again be cautious of this.
Your words do not yet fully harmonize with the mind of Heaven.
The reason I have had the Zhēnrén speak
was not because of you.
I only wished to observe the gains and losses of common people
and what they consider to be great transgressions.
Therefore, I had you speak of it
to see their crookedness, uprightness, and wrongs.
Do you also know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Go on,
you have already awakened.
When I first became aware of the Zhēnrén,
I did not wish to speak with the Zhēnrén.
Seeing that you are sincere and diligent,
daily striving for goodness,
I have therefore spoken deeply with you
to speak of the intent of Heaven and Earth,
to resolve the distress and bitterness of the emperors and kings,
the grievances of the common people,
and the loss of principle among the myriad things.
Now that I have set forth the legal words and meanings for you,
I no longer withhold anything.
You must only exert yourself to remember them."
"Yes, yes."
"I have previously seen many disciples,
but they could not be spoken with;
therefore, I did not engage in ultimate discussion with them.
Thus, my Dao has never been transmitted outward.
Do you know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Go then,
you understand."
"Indeed.
Since the Tiānshī has taken pity on the disciple,
I have obtained true words without concealment.
If the lord is worthy, then the ministers will be mostly loyal;
if the master is enlightened, then the disciples will mostly be able to speak without concealment."
"Excellent
are your words!
You have attained the meaning of awakening;
continue to speak of it."
"In the present Heaven and Earth, there truly should be the method of becoming an immortal and not dying,
the prescription for not growing old.
Can these also be obtained?"
"Excellent
is the Zhēnrén's inquiry into these matters.
Indeed, they can be obtained.
The amount of the medicine of immortality and deathlessness accumulated in Heaven
is like the accumulation of grain in the Tàicāng."
The number of immortal garments
is comparable to the accumulation of white cloth by the Tài Guān;
the number of residences of the various immortals
is comparable to the houses and mansions of the Xiàn Guān.
They always reside along the Dà Dào,
and therefore they are able to enter Heaven.
As for the Dà Dào,
it allows one to dwell in the guest houses and residences of the gods and spirits.
If a person possesses Dào Dé,
they may dwell in the guest houses and residences of the Xiàn Guān.
Heaven does not begrudge the immortal garments or the methods of immortality,
but they are difficult to grant to people.
If people have no great merit regarding Heaven and Earth,
and cannot cure the great ailments of Heaven and Earth,
nor harmonize the qi of Yīn and Yáng,
and provide no benefit to the Sān Guāng, the Sì Shí, the Wǔ Xíng, Heaven and Earth, or the gods and spirits,
then Heaven does not grant them the methods of immortality or the immortal garments.
These things
are for people of extraordinary and distinguished merit.
Do you wish to know its great manifestation?
It is like a Dì Wáng having grain in the Tài Cāng
and cloth and silk from the Tài Guān.
As for how many dou or hu of grain are in the Tài Cāng,
a person without merit or Dào Dé cannot obtain even a single sheng of it;
and for those people who have committed offenses,
on the contrary, they enter into prison,
where they are still subject to prosecution,
and the details of their crimes are reported;
this is a clear manifestation.
Today people are truly wicked
and do not accord with the Mind of Heaven,
therefore Heaven does not fully reveal its methods and good medicines.
Instead, it daily causes ghosts, gods, and spiritual essences to conduct examinations
and beat those people who are ill-behaved;
therefore the sick never cease
and the dead are numerous.
It is like when the Xiàn Guān manages disorder:
the prisons are full of criminals,
and many die violent deaths;
this is what is meant.
If one has great merit toward the Dì Wáng,
and the palaces accumulate much official grain, cloth, and silk,
one can obtain constant clothing and food.
Now, as for the lives of the Dì Wáng,
they only ever think of governing together with good people;
what would they begrudge or withhold?
The duty of a ruler
is to work with various sages and the gentle to together bring peace and governance to the world.
If a ruler has no sagely ministers,
a father no filial sons,
or a teacher no obedient and good disciples,
the sorrow caused is beyond words.
Therefore, in high antiquity, the Sān Huáng ruled by letting their robes fall and folding their hands,
having no affairs and no worries.
Their ministers were diligent and good;
they worried for their ruler,
frequently feeling pain in their hearts,
and thus they dared to help the ruler pacify the world;
they even sought out celestial immortal methods to give to their ruler,
so their ruler obtained longevity.
Some had great merit;
if their merit was great enough, they could even become immortals together
and together govern the affairs of Heaven.
Heaven would again clothe and feed them;
this is a clear manifestation
and not empty words.
Since middle antiquity,
there has been much jealousy of the Zhēn Dào,
and it has been blocked off;
instead, people deceive one another with Wěi Dào,
making people foolish
and causing sagely ones to be few;
therefore many rulers and ministers are both sorrowful and distressed,
and on the contrary, they are unable to pacify the world;
furthermore, many do not have long lives.
This is not only the fault of the people of current low antiquity;
its origins go back a long time,
and perhaps the greatest fault lies here;
do you also know of this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Therefore, today Heaven accumulates rare methods and immortal garments
beyond counting;
but because people have no great merit,
they simply cannot obtain them.
It is like people having the houses and mansions of the Xiàn Guān,
money, grain, cloth, and silk,
always residing along the Dà Dào
and maintaining a household without hiding away.
Yet those without Gōng Dé
cannot obtain even a single dou of grain,
a single coin,
or a single inch of cloth or silk;
this is a clear manifestation.
Therefore, since high antiquity and middle antiquity,
the Zhēn Dào has daily declined and diminished;
therefore the methods for true longevity and immortality cannot be obtained.
As for those individuals who happen to attain longevity,
they are the most exceptionally long-lived people in the world.
Why is this?
When there is much Zhēn Dào Dé, there is much Zhèng Qì;
therefore people have few illnesses and long lives.
When there is much Xié Wěi Wén,
then there is much Xié È Qì;
therefore people have many illnesses and do not obtain longevity;
this is the natural law of Heaven.
Therefore, of old, the ministers of the Sān Huáng possessed much of the Zhēn Dào,
so their rulers had long lives.
The ministers of the Wǔ Dì had less of the Zhēn Dào,
so their rulers did not have lives as long as the Sān Huáng.
The ministers of the Sān Wáng had even less of the Zhēn Dào
and could not compare to the Wǔ Dì.
The ministers of the Wǔ Bà prioritized merit-seeking, falsehood, and written calamities
and did not possess a single bit of the Zhēn Dào;
therefore many died young;
this is a clear manifestation.
Among them, those who occasionally obtained longevity
were the most exceptionally long-lived people in the world.
Do you understand this well?"
"Yes, yes."
"Therefore, the sages and worthies who perform divination
simply observe whether the Ruì Yìng they receive are good or evil
and then they naturally know of safety or peril, good fortune or ill.
Those who obtain the highest good responses in writing,
their governance is already unsurpassed.
Those who obtain middling responses in writing
already resemble middling people.
Those who obtain low responses in writing
already resemble low people."
"What does this mean?"
"It means that obtaining writings like those of the Sān Huáng
is the highest;
if one obtains the writings of the Wǔ Dì,
it is the middling;
if one obtains the writings of the Sān Wáng,
it is the lower-middle;
if one obtains the writings of the Wǔ Bà,
it is the lowest."
"How can these writings be clarified as such?"
"Excellent
are your words.
Teaching so that there is no punishment and yet self-governance
is the highest.
Issuing instructions and orders
such that people are slightly afraid and respectful of them
is the middling.
Teaching them and using slight punishments to govern them
is the lower-middle.
Teaching much that is false merit,
taking the empty for the real,
losing the proper laws,
superficial submissions of documents,
handling affairs by violently using punishments and penalties,
having many heterodox writings,
and having no Zhēn Dào to uphold—
this is the manifestation of the lowest Bà Dào.
Of old there were sages and worthies
who simply observed the instructions and commands they could obtain from Heaven
and thus naturally knew of superiority or inferiority.
I wish to hear: as for those who are taught,
who is sent to bring it to them?
It may be that Heaven produces worthies for them
to assist in their governance;
this is like when a family is about to flourish,
it will certainly give birth to a worthy son.
Or the Hé and Luò produce corresponding writings and diagrams for them
to serve as certificates and documents;
this is it.
Do you know of this?"
"Yes, yes."
"I shall further clarify it for the Zhēn Rén.
When a family is about to decline,
it gives birth to children who are unlucky and wicked.
When a ruler is about to decline,
Heaven does not produce worthy and good assistants for him.
When a family is about to decline,
the descendants do not like to practice true and correct Dào Dé;
instead they like flattery, falsehood, and superficiality,
and merit-seeking, heterodox, and licentious methods,
thus becoming an unlucky and chaotic family.
Moreover, when a family is flourishing,
they will certainly seek the Zhēn Dào Dé,
rare writings, and extraordinary methods
by which they can save themselves.
When a Jūn Zǐ is about to rise,
Heaven will certainly treat him as a son and grant him true writings, the Zhēn Dào, and true virtue,
and good people will together with him conduct governance.
The Hé and Luò will furthermore occasionally command him;
calamities will daily diminish,
Ruì Yìng will daily arrive,
and good responses will daily increase;
this is its manifestation."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Go forth;
Zhēn Rén, strive and exert yourself.
You should have merit toward Heaven
and should assist the virtuous ruler to be perceptive and wise."
"What does this mean?"
"As for wishing to have great merit toward Heaven,
you are now also a person who has left the world,
not obtaining praise in governance—"
"By what means can one achieve merit toward Heaven?"
"What should be done now?"
"Simply entrust the written documents to the Guīdé Jūn.
The Guīdé Jūn
is the Son of Heaven,
who resonates with the heart of Heaven.
He should use these to govern and repay Heaven's heavy merit,
and thereby stabilize All Under Heaven
and elevate his own person;
then you also will obtain good fortune
and your longevity will be preserved."
"How excellent!
Indeed, indeed."
"Go now,
the explanation of the three conducts is finished.
Show this to the assembly of Worthies and common people,
so that future generations may do good;
it should be like this."
"I would not dare [disobey].
But those who only seek material wealth and profit for themselves
claim for themselves that they are doing good,
and on a higher level, they use this to position themselves before Heaven, the Sovereign, their fathers, and their teachers."
"Regarding the human conduct spoken of by the Zhēnrén,
it may still be considered balanced and above average,
but as for those of the lowest ignorance whose evil natures and evil actions have accumulated in great number,
they are ultimately beyond naming.
Entrust the book to the people of later ages,
let each deeply and truthfully examine their own conduct
to see how they have been beneficial to Heaven, the Sovereign, their fathers, and their teachers,
and whether their conduct has improved,
or if they merely seek their own protection and profit.
Heaven deeply knows the hearts of men!
Therefore, those who are afflicted are numerous."
"Excellent!
I, your humble student, having been able to behold the words of the Tiānxīn Shī,
have already attained great awakening."
"You can be called a person who awakens easily,
but in this world, there are many of the lowest ignorance
who trust their own foolish minds
and no longer believe the words of others.
The fault lies in this, ruining the Tiāndào
and causing the emperors and kings to suffer in distress.
This arises precisely from these men of lowest ignorance
who instead often envy the Zhēndào and virtuous power,
claiming it is unworthy while trusting their own unbenevolent hearts.
Heaven is pained and troubled by this;
therefore Heaven has caused me to produce these writings for the Shàngdé zhī Jūn,
so that he may achieve order himself,
being able to stabilize his person and pacify his governance.
Those who obtain the heart of Heaven,
the Tàigǔ Shànghuáng sovereigns who were deeply favored by Heaven,
did so precisely because of this.
Does the Zhēnrén understand?"
"Indeed, indeed."
"Go,
you already know this,
depart now,
go and reflect upon it."
"Indeed, indeed.
I wish to ask about one more matter."
"Speak."
"The Tiānshī has set forth these writings of law and teaching;
why are they so numerous?"
"Excellent
is your question.
It can be said that you have grasped the intention of the Dào.
However, regarding what All Under Heaven loves or hates,
the principles are equal, but the intentions applied vary.
Therefore, the Dào
is largely the same but slightly different.
One matter is divided into eleven thousand five hundred and twenty characters;
only then is the Tiāndào slightly manifest,
and the Wángdào slightly complete.
If one were to completely explain everything within Heaven and Earth, above and below, in the eight directions, the six harmonies, inside and out,
it must be said that this book would not have the power to record it all.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Indeed, indeed."
"Go,
you already know it.
Entrust this book to the Dàodé zhī Jūn,
cause him to publish it,
so that common people may reflect upon the gains and losses of their own conduct
to heal the afflictions of Heaven and Earth
and to stabilize the emperors and kings;
their governance will immediately become peaceful.
Does the Zhēnrén understand?"
"Indeed, indeed."
"Go now,
exert yourself and do not be negligent."
"Indeed, indeed."
To the right is the assessment for distinguishing the gains and losses of good and evil conduct among sovereign and subject, father and son, and teacher and disciple.
"In the presence of the Zhēnrén,
should ordinary people use strictness, awe, wisdom, and deceit, and constant majesty to overcome and subdue others?
Or is it not appropriate?
You, yourself, speak of this with refinement."
"Indeed, people should certainly use strict majesty, wisdom, and deceit to overcome and subdue others.
Why?
It is by this that people are able to govern and correct others."
"Alas!
Inside, this Zhēnrén only has the knowledge of a common man;
he cannot yet be called a Superior Zhēnrén.
The words he offers are all like those of commoners
and do not enter the Tiānxīn.
When a Superior Zhēnrén offers an explanation,
it must be in accord with the Tiānxīn.
Now, as for using strictness, awe, wisdom, and deceit to overcome and subdue others,
it is not only that the guǐshén condemn and loathe it;
not only do the guǐshén condemn and loathe it,
but the spirits of Yīnyáng also condemn and loathe it;
and it is not only the spirits of Yīnyáng who condemn and loathe it.
Therefore, since the opening of Heaven and Earth,
that which the world has suffered from together
and that which has been governed together
are all those who use these methods to overcome and subdue people;
they do not govern those who are subdued.
Thus, among those who are subdued and suffer grievance,
the guǐshén assist them;
Heaven and Earth assist them;
Heaven and Earth assist them.
Thus, humans
also govern those who overcome others
and assist those who are subdued.
Therefore, in antiquity, the Sānhuáng and the Superior Sages overcame people
by governing them with the Ultimate Dào and Dé;
in overcoming people,
they did not use strictness, awe, wisdom, and deceit.
Now, those who use strictness, awe, wisdom, deceit, and punishments to overcome people
are truly like bandits and thieves.
Bandits and thieves also use these very means to overcome and subdue people;
by what would a Jūnzǐ distinguish himself
or make his uniqueness clear?
Yet the Zhēnrén says one should use these;
is that not indeed foolish?
This is exactly what, since the Middle Antiquity,
has brought disorder to Heaven and Earth.
Do you know this?
Therefore, in High Antiquity, there were lords of Dàodé
who did not use strictness, awe, wisdom, and deceit to govern the people;
in Middle Antiquity, symbols were established,
yet they did not dare use punishments.
In Late Antiquity, strictness, awe, wisdom, deceit, and punishments were used slightly to govern the people,
and there was slight disorder.
Now, under inferior and foolish generals,
the Bàdào flourished greatly;
they used majesty, strictness, and punishments to overawe their soldiers and the masses,
and thus officials and the people frequently rebelled.
Therefore, those who govern by the Dào
live in purity and clarity;
those who govern by Dé
have measure in both advancement and retreat.
But the people of Late Antiquity are difficult to govern in their advancement and retreat,
as they possess much wisdom and deceit.
Heaven governs by the Dào,
so its form is clear
and the Sānguāng are bright;
Earth governs by Dé,
so it endures disgrace;
humanity governs by harmony,
so its advancement and retreat are full of expediency,
because its words are changeable and inconstant.
Heaven's governance is the beginning;
Earth's governance is the middle;
humanity's governance is at the very bottom.
Reaching the lower limit, it must return to the top.
How do we know it has reached the lower limit?
Because its words on advancement and retreat are inconstant,
and its coming and going use different words.
These are the lower limits of the three Qi.
Reaching the lower limit, one must return to the top
and follow the Dào;
only then can Tàipíng be attained,
which is similar to Heaven.
Following Dé leads to middle peace,
which is similar to Earth.
Following harmony leads to small disorder,
which is similar to humanity.
Following strictness, awe, wisdom, deceit, and punishments leads to daily disorder;
thus it is similar to a Bàjūn,
and punishments arise greatly.
Now the Zhēnrén conversely says one should use strictness, awe, wisdom, and deceit;
this is truly something that brings disorder to Tiānyì."
"Now the Tiānshī says
that one should not use strictness, awe, or punishments.
Why then does Heaven sometimes send thunder and lightning to strike and take people?"
"Excellent!
Your challenge
has grasped the meaning.
However, the reason why they are taken
is that the ruler, despite what he should respect and honor,
desires to practice evil
and easily brings grievance to people.
Humans are extremely honorable and important,
yet the ruler conversely makes them eat together with the liùchù;
therefore Heaven governs him.
As for assisting in the subduing of people and their sustenance,
this is what people loathe.
Therefore, in the world, whether great or small,
those who lightly and easily bring grievance to people
will all together be governed,
while Heaven pities and assists those who are subdued.
Thus, when a Jūnzǐ overcomes and subdues people,
he should only use the Dào and Dé;
he must not use banditry and harm to overcome people and cause them grievance.
Now, strictness, awe, wisdom, and deceit
can only be used to prostrate lawless people.
Those who cannot be brought to submission through Dàodé
and who desire to be without the Way
should be subjected to this.
This is like Léigōng taking lawless people;
it cannot be practiced constantly.
This would be governing in opposition to the Tiānxīn.
He who desires to gain the Mind of Heaven and Earth
must practice the Dào and Dé.
Thus, the sages and worthies of antiquity
valued the use of the Dào and Dé,
and overcoming people through benevolence, love, and benefit.
They did not value using strictness, awe, or punishments
to terrify, overcome, and subdue people.
By using such crookedness and perversity to settle majesty and terrify people into submission,
the Qi of Tàipíng from the Shànghuáng will not come to assist humans in governing.
The reason for this is
that under such governance, the people are unaware,
or there are great grievances knotted up,
but they fear him and do not dare to speak.
It is like a bandit or thief snatching a person’s clothes and goods;
the person clearly knows it is wrong but does not dare to speak,
and instead gives the thief good names like 'General' or 'Superior Lord';
this is what is meant.
Some are weak in strength and cannot manage for themselves,
and they also do not dare to speak;
all this is called being closed off and blocked,
which causes the Qi of Yīnyáng and Heaven to become disharmonious.
When Heaven mandates a ruler of men,
his duty is fundamentally to regulate the strong and assist the weak and inferior.
But bandit-like officials instead use this strictness and awe to intimidate them,
and use wisdom and deceit to terrify them.
To allow the balanced Qi to arrive
and for a lord of Dé to govern,
there is fear that these things will disorder the correct Qi.
Therefore, this is shown to the Zhēnrén.
This is to be entrusted to a lord of superior Dé,
to be shown to all worthies and ordinary people,
so that officials and the people may themselves contemplate how to govern,
which should be of benefit to those above.
Be careful not to disorder it!
Does the Zhēnrén understand and know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Very well.
You have already understood.
Go, and always be careful with your words.
Do not speak recklessly.
Heaven is not like man."
"Yes, yes."
"Ordinary people cannot reach this;
it is best for them to be fond of asking questions."
"Yes, yes."
To the right is the differentiation of the methods for overcoming and subduing Heaven, Earth, humanity, ghosts, and spirits—what they condemn and loathe, and what they assist.
"I ask about one matter."
"That which the Zhēnrén doubts,
what sort of thing is it?"
"I study in the morning and return in the evening,
constantly dwelling in a quiet place,
contemplating the essential meanings,
not daring to be negligent.
In the current writings and words of the Tiānshī,
there is often the mention that the Shànghuáng Tàipíng Qì is about to arrive.
Now, what is meant by 'Shàng'?
What is meant by 'Huáng'?
What is meant by 'Tài'?
What is meant by 'Píng'?
What is meant by 'Qì'?"
"What is it that the Zhēnrén now observes or doubts,
that he wishes all at once to challenge and question the meaning of these subtle words?"
"The reason I have come to the Tiānshī to question the meaning of the written text in its entirety
is that the writings often speak of the Shànghuáng Qì being about to arrive,
yet I have not grasped its great essential meaning.
If I do not take this opportunity to ask for a definitive explanation from the enlightened Tiānshī,
I fear that later I will have no way of knowing it;
therefore, I dare not refrain from questioning it in detail."
"Excellent are your words;
they cannot be changed for ten thousand generations.
The time of Heaven’s Ultimate Way, Great Virtue, and Abundant Benevolence has already arrived,
and the Huáng Líng delights in people practicing it with urgency.
Therefore, the Tiānqì has prompted your heart,
causing you to ask day and night.
The laws of Heaven are manifest and clear;
I marvel at this greatly."
"Understood."
"Zhēnrén, sit peacefully.
I shall analyze and explain the meaning of these characters for you in detail,
so they may be transmitted for an infinite time.
Now, for the character 'Shàng',
there is one horizontal stroke;
in the center, another vertical stroke is drawn;
moving upward, it again embraces a 'Yī';
from one and moving up, one obtains three 'Yī'.
It moves upward without stopping
and does not move downward again;
therefore, it is named 'Shàng',
for above this character, there is nothing higher.
Reversing 'Shàng' makes 'Xià'.
As for 'Xià',
there is one horizontal stroke;
likewise, in the center, a vertical stroke is drawn;
moving downward, it again embraces a 'Yī'.
Its movement is then downward,
and it cannot move upward again;
therefore, it is named 'Xià'.
Those whose will constantly desires to move downward
will, after a long time, reach the very bottom
and have nothing lower to go.
This is comparable to that which is turbid;
it delights in moving downward to become Earth;
thus Earth is the lowest
and has nothing lower.
For the character 'Shàng',
it constantly moves upward
and cannot move downward again.
This is comparable to that which is clear;
it delights in moving upward to become Heaven;
thus Heaven has nothing above it.
Therefore, as the law of Heaven,
names are each set by their own characters.
All matters under Heaven are like this.
Thus, when the Sages established laws,
they all imitated the mind and intent of Heaven.
To guard the 'Yī' and delight in divining the upward path—
'Bǔ'
means to ask—
those who constantly delight in moving upward and never stop divining and asking
are on the path of great fortune and the highest level.
Therefore, the character 'Shàng' has one stroke,
with a vertical line going up to 'Bǔ'.
For the character 'Xià',
it has one stroke going down to 'Bǔ'.
'Bǔ' means to ask;
if one constantly contemplates and asks
while moving downward to the extreme where there is nothing lower,
then those who delight in downward gain will never again obtain the upward path.
Thus, regarding the character 'Shàng' which has no further 'Shàng' above it,
it says that one's governance should move upward daily
to harmonize with the heart of Heaven,
until there is nothing higher.
"Excellent, excellent!
The enlightened master has graciously and compassionately explained the character 'Shàng';
I wish to further hear about the character 'Huáng'."
"With 'Rì' and 'Wáng',
and 'Yī' above the 'Rì',
that is Heaven.
Heaven is the number one.
When Heaven obtains the Sun,
it is brilliantly and greatly luminous, and thus there is a King.
Therefore, the character 'Yī' is combined with 'Rì' and 'Wáng' to form the character 'Huáng'.
'Yī' is Heaven,
and Heaven is also a lord and leader;
the Sun is also a lord and leader;
the King is also a lord and leader.
When these three lords and leaders obtain each other, they form the character named 'Huáng'.
'Huáng'
refers to its spirit being abundant and resplendent;
therefore, it is named 'Huáng'.
'Huáng' is number one under Heaven;
there is nothing that can be above it."
"Excellent, excellent!
The master has graciously and compassionately enlightened me on the character 'Huáng';
I wish to hear about the characters of 'Tàipíng Qì'."
"Regarding 'Tài',
it means 'Dà' (Great);
it refers to its accumulated greatness moving like Heaven.
All matters are great,
and nothing is greater than Heaven.
Regarding 'Píng',
it refers to its governance being extremely equal and balanced,
with all matters being fully ordered
and no further wickedness or selfishness.
'Píng'
is comparable to the Earth dwelling below;
it presides over and maintains balance;
such is the Earth’s maintenance of balance.
It is like how people planting good obtain good
and planting evil obtain evil.
If a person is given good and applies effort,
their goods will be many.
If a child loves good,
but people give them little,
then the lack of goods is an evil.
Regarding 'Qì',
it refers to the Tiānqì joyfully descending to give life,
and the Dìqì compliantly and joyfully ascending to nourish.
The law of Qì moves above the Earth and beneath the Heaven;
Yin and Yang obtain each other
and intersect to create harmony.
Combining with the Zhōnghé Qì as a triad,
they together nourish all things.
The three Qì love each other and communicate with each other,
and there is no further harm.
'Tài'
is 'Dà' (Great);
'Píng'
is 'Zhèng' (Correct);
'Qì'
is the presiding nourishment through communicative harmony.
Obtaining this to govern
is Tàipíng and harmonious,
and furthermore greatly correct;
therefore, it is said that the Tàipíng Qì has arrived."
"Excellent, excellent!
Does this speak only of the Heaven, Earth, and Zhōnghé Qì
needing to combine and communicate to govern together?
Should all matters be a triple union to work together?"
"Excellent, excellent!
Your words
have already grasped the law of Heaven.
Sovereigns and Kings imitate this to govern,
and it is like being divine.
Now, I shall explain it in detail for the Zhēnrén;
follow along and record it."
"Yes, yes."
"The Yuánqì communicates with the Zìrán Tàihé Qì;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
in a time when all was indistinct and without form,
the three Qì condensed
and together gave birth to Heaven and Earth.
Heaven and Earth communicate with Zhōnghé;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together give birth to all things.
All things communicate with the Sānguāng;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together illuminate Heaven and Earth.
The Five Phases, Hardness, and Softness of all things communicate with Zhōnghé;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together complete and form the myriad things.
The Yin and Yang of the Four Seasons' Qì communicate with the Zhōnghé of Heaven and Earth;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together bring forth the benefits of the things of Heaven and Earth.
Mèng, Zhòng, and Jì communicate with each other;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together complete each direction.
The high, low, and level parts of the Earth communicate with each other;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together bring forth and nourish the things of Heaven and Earth.
Among the crawling creatures, male and female unite
and together produce harmony and communicate;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they transmit their kind.
Man and woman communicate with each other;
with combined strength and a shared heart, they together give birth to children.
Three people communicate with each other;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together govern a single household.
Ruler, minister, and people communicate with each other;
with combined strength and a shared heart,
they together form a single state.
All these are rooted in the Yuánqì, Zìrán, and the mandates of Heaven and Earth.
In all matters, when the three communicate with each other,
only then can the Way be completed.
Together they produce harmony,
The three matters are always interconnected;
combining their strength and uniting their hearts,
they jointly govern one office
and jointly complete one task;
if even one matter is insufficient, it results in misfortune.
Therefore, if there is Yáng but no Yīn,
life cannot be generated alone,
and governance will also perish.
If there is Yīn but no Yáng,
life likewise cannot be generated alone,
and governance will also perish.
If there are Yīn and Yáng but no Harmony (Hé),
they cannot propagate their kind
and will also perish.
Therefore, if there is Heaven but no Earth,
all things have nowhere to rest.
If there is Earth but no Heaven,
all things have no means of birth.
If Heaven and Earth are connected but there is no Harmony (Hé),
things have no way to accommodate and nourish themselves.
Therefore, a man cannot produce life alone,
a woman cannot nourish life alone,
and without both man and woman, no child can be born;
how then could a family be formed,
and how could they be named "Father" and "Mother"?
Therefore, the laws of Heaven always require the three to combine before completion.
Thus, the sages of antiquity deeply understood the nature of Heaven
and emulated it to govern one another.
Therefore, the Ruler (Jūn) acts as the father,
emulating Heaven;
the Minister (Chén) acts as the mother,
emulating Earth;
the People (Mín) act as the children,
emulating Harmony (Hé).
According to the mandated laws of Heaven,
all bustling creatures
should all have the three combined and interconnected,
combining their strength and uniting their hearts;
only then can they jointly govern and complete a task,
jointly form a family,
and jointly form one body.
Thus, Heaven causes them to depend on one another to function;
not one can be missing.
If a single matter suffers from injustice or stagnation
and does not find its proper place,
then the three are ruined and the result is misfortune.
Therefore, the Ruler (Jūn) needs the Minister (Chén),
the Minister (Chén) needs the People (Mín),
the People (Mín) need the Minister (Chén),
and the Minister (Chén) needs the Ruler (Jūn);
only then is a matter completed.
If one is insufficient,
it causes the three to fail.
Therefore, if there is a Ruler (Jūn) without People (Mín) or Ministers (Chén),
there is no basis for the name "Ruler" (Jūn);
if there are Ministers (Chén) and People (Mín) without a Ruler (Jūn),
they also do not constitute Ministers (Chén) and People (Mín).
If Ministers (Chén) and People (Mín) are without a Ruler (Jūn),
there is also chaos;
they cannot govern themselves
and cannot become good Ministers (Chén) or People (Mín).
These three stand by needing one another;
only by obtaining one another are they complete.
Thus, Ruler (Jūn), Minister (Chén), and People (Mín) should correspond to the laws of Heaven,
the three combining and interconnecting,
combining their strength and uniting their hearts,
to jointly form one family.
This is just as a husband, wife, and child jointly form a family;
they cannot be without each other;
this is the essential Way (Dào) of Heaven.
This is also like a person having a head, feet, and abdomen
to form one body;
none can be removed.
If they are removed, there is insufficiency,
and one does not form a complete person.
This is the natural order of Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, the sages of antiquity took their laws from Heaven;
thus a man must obtain a submissive and good woman to govern with,
and only then will there be good children.
The man
is the Ruler (Jūn);
the woman
is the Minister (Chén);
the child
is the People (Mín).
Therefore, the Way (Dào) of governing a state mandated by Heaven
is to take virtuous and wise Ministers (Chén) as friends;
only with a good woman can one harmonize their children,
and only with good Ministers (Chén) can one harmonize their people.
Only with a good woman can one produce good children;
only with good Ministers (Chén) can one produce good people.
When both the People (Mín) and Ministers (Chén) love goodness,
only then can those above them enjoy long-lasting peace.
If the Zhēnrén (True Man) wishes to know the proof of this effect:
Heaven
is the Ruler (Jūn);
Earth
is the Minister (Chén).
When the rain of Heaven flows everywhere,
if it rains upon good land,
the living things produced are good;
if it rains upon bad land,
the living things produced are bad;
this is what is meant.
Now, parents, rulers, and ministers
still only jointly maintain the great guiding principles.
The great essential is that they actually rely on their children for food and clothing;
if a person has no children,
their lineage is cut off from future generations.
If a Ruler (Jūn) has few People (Mín),
then food and clothing are insufficient,
causing the mind to be constantly filled with sorrow and bitterness.
Therefore, the Way (Dào) of governing a state
is to take the People (Mín) as the root.
Without the People (Mín),
the Ruler (Jūn) and the Minister (Chén) have nothing to govern
and nothing to regulate.
For this reason, the great sages and worthies of antiquity jointly managed affairs
and from morning till night focused solely on the People (Mín) as the highest priority,
worrying for their people.
Like parents in a family worrying about having no children;
without children, how can they call themselves parents?
Without People (Mín), how can one call oneself a Ruler (Jūn)?
Therefore, the law of Heaven
always causes the Ruler (Jūn), Minister (Chén), and People (Mín) to be as one,
their fates to be the same,
and their fortune and misfortune to be the same.
If one office or one matter loses its rectitude,
it results in great misfortune.
Since the Middle Antiquity,
many have lost the guiding principles of governance
and have consequently inherited burdens (Chéngfù);
later generations have thus received flowing disasters of increasing severity.
This truly stems from the Ruler (Jūn), Minister (Chén), and People (Mín) failing in their plans,
not knowing how to think deeply,
nor how to love and connect with one another well,
nor how to combine their strength and unite their hearts;
instead, they cause each other sorrow and bitterness.
The Ruler (Jūn) is but one person
and may reside in deep seclusion;
the injustices and grievances from all four directions
are truly blocked and do not reach him.
Governance fails to obtain the Heart of Heaven;
disasters, changes, and anomalies
accumulate and are not removed.
What Heaven and Earth wish to say,
the human sovereign cannot know;
the great fault lies here.
Without the three combining their strength,
intelligence is cut off,
and evil Qi (Qì) stagnates and is not regulated.
Above, this creates a great enmity with August Heaven (Huángtiān);
below, it creates a great fault with the Earth
and causes great worry for emperors and kings.
Disasters follow one another without resolution;
it is a great harm to the People (Mín)
and a great illness for all things.
This has uniquely accumulated for a long time;
it is not caused by the faults of people today or in the recent past alone.
Does the Zhēnrén (True Man) also know this?"
"I have known this for a long time,
but I truly did not know the cause of it.
Therefore, I asked about these sincere grievances.
Now, what should be done about it?"
"Indeed,
the Qi (Qì) of Great Peace (Tàipíng) is about to arrive.
Governance should obtain the Heart of Heaven,
and then all these evils will be removed of their own accord.
Therefore, Heaven has sent me to speak of it in detail.
It wishes for me to rescue them from their failures
by bringing forth the correct texts;
therefore, it caused the Zhēnrén (True Man) to come and ask about everything.
This is the source from which misfortune arises:
not emulating the natural laws of the original Qi (Qì) of Heaven and Earth,
and not having the three interconnect
while combining their strength and uniting their hearts;
that is why this has occurred.
If the three interconnect,
combining their strength and uniting their hearts,
then Great Joy (Dàyuè) will be established immediately,
and disasters will immediately vanish."
"I wish to hear how governance should be conducted."
"Hasten to emulate the laws of Heaven,
as described above.
The law of Heaven
is that in all matters, the three combine their strength and unite their hearts.
Thus, Heaven uses the Three Luminaries (Sānguāng) as its patterns;
the Three Luminaries (Sānguāng) are always interconnected and shine together,
never again having a time when they are cut off.
Since the Heavenly Bonds (Tiānquàn) were issued,
people have used books as patterns for governance,
emulating the Three Luminaries (Sānguāng) of Heaven.
Therefore, from time to time, Heaven causes the Hé and Luò scripts to appear,
repeatedly commanding them as written records and human patterns.
To joyfully emulate the measures of the profound and ultimate divine governance of Heaven
is to cause the good to rise daily
and the evil to perish daily.
As for books,
they are simply for communicating documents through the three paths where documents travel.
