simply place a sick person before you
to serve as the original text for incantations;
then have each person speak their secret words;
those that can heal immediately
are the true ones;
those that do not
are all false,
corresponding to deviant and wild speech;
they cannot be used as a model.
There are cases where one person uses an incantation and it heals,
but others use it without effect;
such words cannot be recorded.
This person is a leader of ghosts and spirits,
naturally employing them;
this is called "isolated speech"
and is not the true Dào for summoning spirits.
Although humans are distant from Heaven,
if one wishes to know if its Dào is true or not, or right or wrong,
then what harmonizes and corresponds like two halves of a tally is correct;
what does not is wrong.
Burial
is fundamentally the ancestral hilly residence,
known as the initial planting of the root. The residence is the earth,
and the soul-spirits should return there
to nourish their descendants.
If the land is good, then the soul-spirits return to nourish them;
if the land is bad, then the soul-spirits return to cause harm.
When the Qi of the five ancestors ends,
it returns again to become human.
The law of the Tiān Dào
is for Qi to cycle back to its beginning.
If one wishes to know the efficacy of the land,
cast small and humble seeds into the earth;
if they afterwards grow daily and flourish with great goodness,
it is Dà Shēng Dì;
if you place great and good seeds in the earth
and they afterwards grow daily with poor quality,
this is Nì Dì;
if they daily decline and diminish,
this is Xiāo Dì.
Testing this with the burial mounds of five times five, twenty-five families,
those where ten out of ten or a hundred out of a hundred correspond
are the Dì Yīn Bǎo Shū text;
those where nine out of ten correspond
are the Dì Yīn Bǎo Jì;
those where eight out of ten correspond
are the Luàn Shū,
which cannot be used constantly.
Those below this
are Xié Wén,
which are books that harm the common people.
If one wishes to know the truth of it,
record the past to determine matters
and verify future events;
only then can truth and falsehood be distinguished.
One can know that my book
is like Tiān having Jiǎ
and Dì having Yǐ,
unchangeable for ten thousand generations.
The heavy matter of the fundamental root
and its efficacy
is the place of living people;
it cannot be changed carelessly. Once
a matter is completed,
Xié Wén cause harm,
causing disasters and anomalies to arise frequently,
and the many worthy people and commoners suffer extremely.
Therefore, whether great or small,
those who wish to know what is passed down through generations
must know for certain that their mounds
are correct, clarify the causes,
and use them to divine future events.
Set twenty-five mounds as the basic text,
examine them against completed matters,
record the past to verify the present,
and use the evidence of past events for future events.
A true master should carefully contemplate the entirety of the book
to dispel confusion and intoxication;
it is named Zhàn Yīn Fù Wén,
used to know the ancestors
and benefit future descendants,
passed down through ten thousand generations;
be careful not to keep it hidden.
The various types of music
are the means to communicate sounds
and transform the Qi of the six directions and eight extremes.
If the presentation is harmonious, then the response will be compliant and good;
if it is not harmonious, then the response will be combative and contrary.
For sounds each have their own belonging:
East, West, South, and North;
Jiǎ, Yǐ, Bǐng, and Dīng;
the twenty-five Qi each have their own family.
Sometimes there are gathered sounds
that come together to form literary phrasing;
thus we know sound.
Listen to the sounds to know the subtle words,
divine good and bad fortune.
When the raised sound matches the Chuī Máo Lǜ,
then one knows the notes of the strings:
Gōng, Shāng, Jué, Zhǐ, and Yǔ.
Distinguish the distance of the six directions;
regarding the goodness or evil of names,
what can be said?
Those who are refined
can then see the spirits and essences coming to respond to matters.
Therefore, ancient Sages and Worthies tuned music
as a means to influence the categories of things,
harmonize Yīn and Yáng,
and determine the four seasons and five elements.
When Yīn and Yáng are tuned, then the sounds are easy to hear;
when Yīn and Yáng are not in harmony,
but are contrary and disordered,
then the sounds are difficult to hear.
The strings must also be tuned,
ideally using the Jiǔ Jiǔ method,
sequencing the silk strings
so the large and small sounds match each other.
Contemplating this does not harm a person's internal organs or spirit.
If they are not tuned, then the dancing is disordered,
there are no correct sounds,
they cannot be listened to,
and they harm a person's internal organs and spirit.
Thus, divine beings, auspicious omens, and strange objects do not come.
Therefore, if one finds a person who is capable
and excels in sounds,
then they can harmonize and unify the transformations of Yīn and Yáng.
How can one know this?
If the divine brightness comes to respond
and auspicious omens and objects come to assemble,
this is the person.
If not,
they are all disordered sounds
that cannot move or influence,
and thus they do not come.
Therefore, in all matters,
one should find the right person, as if they were a spirit;
if one does not find the right person, it is like wild talk.
If one finds the right person,
regardless of whether the matter is difficult or easy,
all can be carried out.
If one does not find the right person,
regardless of whether the matter is great or small,
none can be accomplished.
For this reason, ancient Sages and Worthies placed importance on their actions
and sought the worthy without any hidden bias,
attaining the standards of the ancients.
If one finds the right person, there is order;
if one does not find the right person, there is chaos.
Ancient texts are numerous,
more than can be written.
Use one matter to illustrate ten,
ten to illustrate a hundred,
a hundred to illustrate a thousand,
a thousand to illustrate ten thousand,
ten thousand to illustrate a hundred million,
and a hundred million to illustrate the infinite.
Matters each have their own family and category;
place the original text of the matter before you,
let those who understand hold to the root,
and let those who are long capable of using it come to explain it.
Observe if their responses are harmonious; those that hit the mark
are all correct.
Those that do not respond and do not hit the mark
are all incorrect.
If you wish to know whether the books and Way of the ancient Sages are accurate or not,
this is comparable to calling a person;
those whose surnames and names are obtained will all respond.
The ghosts and spirits are also like this;
if their surnames and names are not obtained, they do not respond.
Although they might wish to respond in harmony,
there is no way for them to reach out,
so they do not respond.
Thus the ancients called learning Wǎng Jīng.
To be refined
is to refinedly contemplate the images of things and what is appropriate
and then further reflect on their words.
If one contemplates these books and bamboo slips to the utmost,
all matters will be completed.
The volumes and chapters are numerous,
each having its own matters.
One should read them in detail
to further supplement each other
until one obtains the full meaning.
Once it is complete and prepared,
if one does not deeply obtain its essential meaning,
speaking of the Way without efficacy in matters,
then when seeing anomalies, one cannot resolve the battles of Yīn and Yáng.
My book is born for the benevolent and worthy;
it is to be handed over to those with virtue.
When those with virtue obtain it,
they regard it as a heavy treasure.
If one obtains it but cannot read it well
and says it is not the Way,
then they cannot bring joy to their person
or remove troubles and blame.
When the Dà Dào is about to appear,
is it not like being without flavor?
Can its use ever be exhausted?
If the many worthies trace its source,
can they harmonize the hard and soft
and exhaust the positions of Yīn and Yáng?
When all the texts are settled
and each finds its place,
will there no longer be confusion?
When evil is all gone,
and Shàng Dì is greatly joyful,
will the people be without misfortune?
When grace reaches even the small and tiny,
and the myriad things are bustling,
will they not lose their Qi?
Returning again to Tài Chū,
will Heaven and Earth be in their positions?
When evil writings have already vanished,
will they guard the Yuán Qì?
Yī
is the thread of the Way;
Èr
is the horizontal movement of the Way;
Sān has already become chaotic
and cannot be clarified.
My Dào is Jiǎzǐ and Yǐchǒu,
and the Liùjiǎ receive from and follow one another.
The Wǔxíng revolve and follow one another,
and the four seasons cycle and return to the beginning.
Although the scrolls and volumes are numerous,
each and every one has something that can be recorded.
It is like a person’s body,
where the head and feet turn and serve each other.
As one word is dropped, another word arises,
and worthies arrange them in sequence to complement one another.
They unite Yīnyáng through words and speech,
and the inner and outer correspond like the compass and square.
At first, recitation has no flavor, but over a long time,
contemplating it without ceasing, the verification arrives.
Disasters depart from the body and the Shén gathers again;
people naturally become cautious and good, without wicked sons.
This is named "having no punishments,"
for the transformation of the Dào is beautiful in the extreme.
Clearly examine my writings to repel misfortune;
wicked calamities will cease of themselves and the people will naturally enjoy longevity.
If the origin is not attained, there is no end or beginning.
When ten and ten correspond,
it is the Tàiyáng text;
when ten and nine correspond,
it is the Tàiyīn text;
when ten and eight correspond,
it is the Zhōnghé text;
when ten and seven correspond,
it is the text of destruction and chaos;
as for those where ten and six correspond,
they are the texts that encounter the center;
when ten and five correspond,
it is the text of ignorance,
which can be called a text that is half-auspicious and half-ominous;
those where fourteen match
are heterodox texts;
those where thirteen match
are texts of great chaos;
those where twelve match
are texts to be abandoned;
those where eleven match
are texts of alternating matches;
those where ten and ten match,
and everything below, cannot be used,
for they are texts that lead people astray.
According to the degree of harm caused,
it will return to harm the person;
if used for a long time without stopping,
the law will be cut off and the family extinguished.
This is the "ten and ten" text.
The above is the textual method for repelling heterodoxy and attaining the upright.
Chún kowtowed, trembling, and bowed twice.
"What else do you wish to ask?"
"Chún now sees the various books and writings of the Míng Shī and the upright multitude;
they are indeed the Tiān tán.
I am filled with terror
and do not know the order of priority.
By what means can I truly rectify and obtain the reality of these books?"
"If you joyfully wish to obtain their reality,
simply observe the sage words of high antiquity,
the sage words of middle antiquity,
and the sage words of low antiquity.
Combine their language,
observe what they have done,
and it can be known.
Again, observe the Dàoist books of high antiquity,
the Dàoist books of middle antiquity,
and the Dàoist books of low antiquity.
Bring the three together to call upon their similar kinds,
and then it can be known."
"Nowadays, all books and writings
are entirely the Tiān tán.
Why is it that the governance is sometimes in order and sometimes in disorder and lack of peace?
I wish to hear about this."
"However, if one can rectify the words
and clarify the books, there will be order;
if they are not rectified and not clarified,
there will be disorder.
Correct words and detailed discourse must lead to goodness,
while heterodox words and malevolent discourse must lead to evil.
Now your difficult questions do not cease,
for you truly and joyfully wish to know this.
One who wishes to achieve goodness simply rectifies the root.
When the root is rectified, it corresponds to Tiān wén
and attains harmony with the sage words.
The second turn corresponds to Dì lǐ,
the third turn becomes Rén wén,
and the fourth turn becomes the Wàn wù.
The Wàn wù then produce superficiality;
superficiality then leads to disorder and ruin.
Tiān wén and sage books appear from time to time
to examine the Yuán and rectify the Shǐ,
removing errors and establishing reality.
Clarifying the principles of all books
is indeed the Tiān dào.
One who obtains the correct words
corresponds with the heart and mind of Heaven.
Heterodoxy brings forth heterodox and evil Qì,
causing Heaven and Earth to be out of harmony,
the Wàn wù to mostly lose their place,
and emperors and kings to feel anxiety and bitterness.
Order is gained and then lost to disorder again;
therefore, one must urgently examine and rectify it.
Reflecting from antiquity to the present,
writings and documents are already fully prepared.
Yet it is distressing that they are gathered together without being pure,
collected and mixed in disorder.
Therefore, the worthy and the bright are collectively suspicious and confused,
not knowing what to follow or what to believe,
consequently losing the ultimate heart of Heaven
and thus each follows their own contrary views.
This causes them to be far removed from the subtle words and intentions of the Tiān dào,
and all become heterodox words and heterodox writings.
Recording this heterodoxy
results in the inability to rectify Yīn yáng;
calamitous Qì arises continuously.
The internal fault lies here.
I see you asking about it,
and in my accumulated concern I cannot bear it,
so I repeatedly explain its meaning to you in detail.
Quickly record my words
and deeply contemplate them yourself.
In all matters,
to obtain knowledge but be unable to practice it exclusively
is of no benefit.
If you can practice it,
you will remove great punishment."
"When Tiān wén is in disorder
and one joyfully wishes to see order,
it is like a person having a severe illness
who joyfully wishes to see a cure.
How can this be done?"
"However, you yourself are as if foolish;
do you truly have no knowledge?
A severe illness not treated in time
leads to death.
If Tiān wén is not treated and rectified,
it leads to great disorder.
The four seasons lose their Qì,
the Wǔ xíng fight against each other,
and the Sān guāng lack correct brightness.
All lose their proper paths
and consequently suffer destruction and ruin.
The people are in a state of chaotic turmoil,
all losing their dwellings.
The old and weak carry burdens,
and half die prematurely.
The state is in darkness, disorder, and confusion;
the Zhì dào and good virtue are cut off,
and the worthy are hidden and obscured,
unable to save each other.
Is this not a very severe illness?
Therefore, one must strive to rectify it.
Nowadays, foolish people daily study and wander in superficial writings,
alternating in their contradictions
to elevate themselves above others.
They do not deeply understand that this is a great harm,
considering it a small matter.
How can they know that internally this alone constitutes a great illness of Yīn yáng and Heaven and Earth?
The reason the world cannot be governed and rectified
is precisely this.
The Shén qí have things they suffer from,
which is why they caused you to come and repeatedly ask about this.
Upon seeing the books, you should, from morning till evening and throughout the night,
deeply contemplate their essential meaning.
You must not simply take things lightly yourself,
failing to take serious account of Huáng tiān.
Currently, emperors and kings have nowhere to turn their hearts,
and the fault is very great.
Although I am now talking with you, just two people face to face,
and it might be considered a small matter,
internally these are the correct words and discussions of Huáng tiān.
I dare not casually speak empty or false words.
The fault would lie upon my person, and the sin would be heavy,
impossible to remove.
When Shén qí punish a person,
it is not like being able to flee far away and escape from other humans.
Do you dare to follow my light words and convenient speech,
like the common people who display contradictions to elevate themselves?"
"Yes, yes,
I would not dare.
Seeing the Tiān Shī speak,
I am both terrified and joyful.
I truly wish to exhaust my strength,
hoping to attain the heart of the Shén qí,
to resolve the worries of the world,
to bring peace to emperors and kings,
and to make the Wàn wù each find their place.
This is my wish."
"How can your wish alone be good?
It is beyond reach.
However, the reason I always uniquely possess good intentions
is that my learning was originally based on contemplating goodness to attain them.
Therefore, while all people grow old and die,
I alone remain.
While the descendants of my ancestors have all perished,
I alone manage not to die.
Truly receiving a generous lifespan,
I feel ashamed before the sudden urgency,
having no way to prove my worth,
or to repay and reciprocate.
I always think of exhausting my own strength,
not knowing by what means to prove my worth.
Seeing that Heaven and Earth are out of harmony
and wind and rain are not moderate,
I know these are the great illnesses of the world,
and I constantly pity it."
"Now having heard the words of the Shén rén,
I have a great awakening.
I think of exhausting myself unto death to prove my worth to Míng tiān,
to resolve the great illness,
to bring peace to Dì lǐ,
to firmly cause emperors and kings to flourish,
and to make the Wàn wù each find their place.
I think of this as a way to repay the heavy merit of Heaven.
Now I do not know if I am capable of it or not.
I wish to beg for further questions,
not reaching the level of the Míng Shī."
"How good
are your words.
Seeing your words now,
I am still joyful;
how much more so for Heaven?
My books
do not miss once in ten thousand times.
You must simply strive without laziness to order them;
this is the way to reciprocate the merit of Heaven,
have no further doubts.
If emperors and kings practice it,
they will immediately obtain its power,
how much more so for you?
Constantly seeing your words,
I dare not hold back any strength.
Although I am the Xiān shēng,
my aspirations do not reach yours.
Now, as we both share this Heaven and Earth,
I wish to bring peace to it together with you.
If I wished not to speak,
I would fear incurring a heavy fault toward you,
and in turn receiving a heavy punishment from Heaven.
Listen to this in even greater detail,
and I will again repeatedly and completely distinguish the path for you.
Rectifying the writings
is based on the heart of Heaven and Earth
and guarding the Yuán qì.
In antiquity, sage books appeared from time to time,
examining the Yuán and rectifying characters.
The Way turns and follows one after another,
subtle words are explained,
all being the essentials of the Yuán qì.
As for the second turn,"
It is secret language;
three turns form chapters and phrases;
four turns form superficiality;
as for five turns,
they distinguish differing meanings,
each overseeing its own contradictions;
as for six turns,
they form texts of mutual deception.
As for chapters and phrases,
they value small formalities as their basis;
those that go below this
are a great illness.
Thus, they cause the Tiāndào to lose its path,
and for sovereigns and kings to suffer long sorrow,
unable to deeply obtain its principles;
it is exactly this.
You fortunately wish to repay the grace of Tiān,
and return the great merit of Tiān.
As for Tiān,
it does not delight in people giving it money or strange and fraudulent objects;
it only delights in people together ordering its writings
and not disordering them.
Now, I saw when you first came to study,
thinking you would just ask one or two matters and leave;
who would have thought you would wish to complete the Tiāndào?
Even if my words are not perfect,
the Tiāndào can roughly be perceived.
You delight in wanting to rectify Tiān and Dì;
just take the subtle words,
return to examine them in reverse,
and align them with their Origin;
then you will obtain the Tiānxīn,
and can bring peace to the world.
Collect and compare the texts of high antiquity, middle antiquity, and late antiquity;
summon them by category
so they follow one another.
The one who holds the root is one person,
and each naturally has their own original basis.
All books and texts have their own affiliations;
let all people bring forth their talents,
surround them, and discuss them together.
Their original basis, words, and actual circumstances
will all emerge naturally.
Collect the essential words from among them
to serve as their explanation;
call these "chapters and phrases,"
and the true Mind of the Dào will be obtained.
This can be called relieving the sorrow of Tiān;
the great illness is gone.
It can be called removing the suffering of Dì;
it can be called allowing sovereigns and kings to roam while obtaining the Tiānxīn;
it can be called allowing the myriad things each to find their place.
In this way,
not one in ten thousand is lost.
I see your words
and know you are an envoy of Tiān;
I dare not deceive you.
To deceive you now
is exactly called deceiving Tiān.
It would cause Tiān to be displeased
and instead shorten my years;
it would be called betraying my own self,
and being ashamed before Huángtiān above,
and furthermore would be of no benefit to the myriad people.
The blame would be very great.
Strive to remember this;
just remember that I dare not hold back any effort."
"Yes, yes.
Having seen the master’s words,
my heart is filled with fear.
Since I ask about matters for Tiān,
I dare not speak of stopping;
I must still complete it.
May the master fortunately forgive my inadequacies
and show me the difficulties and ease;
thus I dare to ask in detail the reasons why."
"Now that writings have accumulated in great numbers,
I wish to know their truth and falsehood and the reasons for them,
just as you asked the other day.
Those where the tens and hundreds correspond are correct;
those that do not
are all false.
Those that obtain a response when applied are correct;
those that do not
are all fake practices.
To wish to obtain a response
requires that the people and ministers are all good, loyal, and trustworthy.
Why is this said?
If a son is worthy and good,
he causes his parents to be always at peace
and they obtain their proper place.
If a wife is good, she causes her husband to have no faults
and he gains her support.
If a minister is good, he causes the state to be at long peace.
If the sovereigns, kings, people, and ministers are all good,
then they cause Tiān to have no disasters or anomalies;
it is exactly this.
Do you understand
or do you not?
Well, I now wish to discuss one matter with you.
If you now can select from my books,
have you thoroughly reached an understanding?"
"This young one is ignorant
and has not yet grasped the meaning."
"You try to speak of it,
and I will see if you fully understand."
"Now, if in my foolish mind
I wish to use them all in alignment,
with above and below complementing each other,
formalizing the matters,
comparing a hundred to a thousand,
and a thousand to ten thousand,
cross-examining them to think it might be sufficient;
otherwise,
I fear I cannot fully encompass the ancient texts."
"Indeed,
what you say now is truly right.
What you recorded before,
does my book not say:
compare one to ten,
ten to a hundred,
a hundred to a thousand,
a thousand to ten thousand,
ten thousand to a hundred million?
It is exactly this."
"Yes, yes.
I wish to hear who those who compare these
should all be."
"Each should work according to the person;
for matters clear in their root,
rely on that root.
For those who excel in knowing how to use them,
let them surround and discuss them together.
Let the words flow,
and from sovereigns and kings down to the commoners,
all should change their old ways
and follow each other in collective discussion.
Those of minor knowledge meet and gather small parts,
returning them to those of medium knowledge;
those of medium knowledge gather them
and return them to those of superior knowledge;
those of superior knowledge gather them
and return them to the sovereigns and kings.
Then all worthies surround and harmonize the theories,
re-settling them.
This is called planning reaching down to the low;
there are no missed calculations,
no ceasing words,
and no discarded texts.
Minor worthies compare and gather them together
and hand them to medium worthies;
medium worthies compare and gather them for great worthies;
great worthies compare and gather them
and hand them to the sovereigns and kings.
In their ... reasoned texts are formed.
This being without error,
they truly obtain the Tiānxīn
and obtain the differentiated principles of Yīnyáng.
The sovereigns, kings, and various ministers
together know its truth;
this is then later lowered to the people.
Let all under Tiān together recite the correct texts;
in this way, the Tiān-qì is obtained,
Tàipíng arrives,
the qì of Superior Peace comes,
sounds of praise arise,
the myriad things are at long peace,
the common people have no complaints,
and wicked texts all depart by themselves.
Tiān's illness is removed,
Dì's illness is gone,
sovereigns and kings roam,
Yīnyáng are delighted,
wicked qì is hidden away,
thieves and bandits are cut off,
Zhōngguó flourishes,
matching the superior Sānhuáng,
the Yídí retreat,
the myriad things are lush and flourishing,
all under Tiān is extremely fortunate,
and all shout 'Ten thousand years!'
You must not block my texts!"
"Yes, yes.
I dare not hide or conceal them.
Having received the master's words,
I will sincerely report back with them;
to hide them, I fear, would be a grave sin in completing the task."
"Excellent
are your words.
You have already obtained the Tiānxīn;
your name is one who has already repaid the great merit of Tiān."
"Yes, yes.
Sincerely, I will withdraw to a quiet place
to ponder its ultimate meaning
without becoming lax."
"Go now;
doubt no more."
To the right is the Kǎowén Jué.
The Shén Rén speaks,
within the Zhēn Rén,
you have already understood.
Diminish your physical self,
and its meaning will be attained.
Its external order will naturally be correct;
close your eyes and look within,
and commune with the spirit and numinous.
Without speaking,
be at one with the Dào.
Yīn and Yáng cover each other, sealed by Tiān.
The arts of long life can open one's eyes.
You should not be stubborn but should be harmonious and expansive.
Tiān Dì receive harmony as if they were deaf and blind.
If you wish to know its meaning, be like the child in the womb.
Without eating for ten months, the spirit communes.
The Dào of nature has nothing above it.
Without looking, the qì dwells in the twelve layers.
Therefore, returning to the state of an infant brings no misfortune.
The old return to youth and connect with the Dào.
For this reason, the images are drawn in twelve layers.
The upright obtain goodness;
only the unworthy meet misfortune.
The Tiān Dào is always present;
it cannot be lost or destroyed.
Its form is like the four seasons cycling back to their source,
ending old age and returning to the beginning;
thus, there is long life.
You should contemplate its meaning without deviation,
devote yourself to accumulating Dé,
continually practice the Dào,
and naturally become a person of talent.
It is not as good as exerting effort in the Dào and returning it to the right person.
If it is not the right person,
the Dào does not proceed in vain.
Now, the Dào is like the wind;
silently dwell by its side.
If used, it exists;
if not used, it disappears.
The worthy have their place;
the unworthy have their locality.
Death and life reside within the body;
constantly maintain a fixed practice.
Tiān has no faults;
humans seek their own destruction.
Carefully contemplate its meaning
and do not act recklessly.
Tiān grants long life to those who keep the Dào and practice it diligently;
humans are unwilling to do so and thus die.
Fully remember my warnings;
if your Dào is transmitted to the right person, it will be easy to practice.
When the sages and worthies of old transmitted the Dào,
they drank blood to seal their oath.
The Tiān Dào is of profound weight,
yet the foolish treat it lightly.
The Dào is the teacher of all things;
those who obtain it are enlightened;
those who lose it are deluded.
Although Tiān Dì are vast,
they do not lose even a tiny fraction.
The worthy know how to nourish themselves,
which is like speaking together with the spirit.
This is the governance of Yīn and Yáng
and the pivot and mechanism of Tiān Dì.
The sages and worthies of old deeply understood this;
therefore, they manifested it in themselves,
distinguishing the essentials of the Tiān Dào.
Internally, use it to govern the body;
externally, use it to eliminate disasters.
If one does what should not be done,
then one shares in the anxieties of Tiān Dì.
Zhēnrén Chún bowed his head and trembled,
"I now wish to ask something further,
though it is not a matter of the Dào.
Having seen the Enlightened Master’s words,
there is no matter that cannot be explained or resolved,
therefore I dare to risk shame and come forward again
as there is one matter of doubt I may ask.
What is it?"
"Speak plainly,
and I shall explain it to you immediately."
"The great ministers who serve emperors and kings should all be elderly;
youths are essentially not people for governing the world."
"Why do you ask this?
I observe the Qi of Heaven,
and recently it has been continuously out of harmony.
Perhaps the fault lies in the serving ministers being unfaithful,
causing the seasonal Qi to be disharmonious,
the human ruler to be unenlightened,
disasters to occur together,
and the people of the Dào to also be harmed.
Now Heaven, Earth, and the Three Luminaries
are still troubled by this,
so there is no upright brightness;
where can a master of the Dào escape to,
so that he alone remains unharmed?
Therefore, although I alone receive the secret favor of Heaven and live long,
I always dare not guarantee my own safety."
"Since I was young,
I have served masters and asked about matters,
yet none have been able to explain them all fully.
Now I do not fear shame
to ask the Tiānshī once more
to explain and resolve the essential meaning,
fearing that I may never have another chance to know it.
I only hope the grace of the Enlightened Master will be granted,
and out of necessity he will explain to this disciple what he cannot reach."
"Wonderful
are your words!
Seeing your words this morning,
I know the governance of Tàipíng has already arrived.
Nevertheless, I shall speak of it all,
and you shall follow and record it in detail."
"Governance has four methods:
there is the governance of Heaven,
there is the governance of Earth,
there is the governance of humanity,
and when the Three Qi reach their limit,
then there is the governance of the creeping things and all creatures.
I wish to hear their meaning."
"In the governance of Heaven,
the ministers are elderly,
and the ruler serves his ministers as a father
and serves his ministers as a teacher;
now, ministers are of low rank,
so why serve them as a teacher or father?
It is only that their positions are low
while their Dào and Dé are highly respected;
serving them as a teacher or father
is serving their Dào and Dé,
so as to coordinate strategies with them and pacify the world.
In the governance of Earth,
the ruler serves his ministers as friends,
as if sharing the same will and heart;
Earth is Yīn and submissive,
mother and son are of the same rank,
sharing the same origin and the same worries;
though the ministers' rank is low,
their virtue is harmonious,
and they harmonize and pacify the ruler's governance.
In the governance of humanity, its use is lowered,
and the ministers are very young,
like a father giving birth to a son;
as the son is young, he cannot yet devise strategies for the father,
therefore its governance is slightly chaotic.
In the collective governance of the creeping things and all creatures,
one views one's ministers and sons as dogs
or as grass and trees,
no longer knowing how to carefully select ministers to serve,
but simply appointing whoever meets an office;
this is called 'the likeness of a man without knowledge.'
Why is this?
Those who are like-men
only resemble the human form
and merely fill the space;
they do not plan for the ruler,
and thus they are good at contending.
In modeling the governance of Heaven,
the ministers of the world
are all the teachers and fathers of the lord of the state,
and thus they are served as fathers;
a man loves his son,
so how could there be a time of peril?
Teachers and fathers can all resolve the calamities and difficulties of the eight directions for their sons,
so how could there be a time of failure?
In modeling the governance of Earth,
the ministers of the world
are all friends of the lord of the state.
Sharing a common will and joining strategies forms an association,
sharing worries and calamities,
wishing together to stabilize their positions;
Earth
is submissive and receives from above,
fully receiving the will and intent of Heaven,
and all obtain the heart of Heaven;
how could there be a time of instability?
In modeling the governance of humanity,
one obtains the Qi of central harmony,
yet harmony is difficult to know as it may advance or retreat;
it is like a young son
who is unable to plan for his father
and thus deceives his father.
When ministers are young,
they cannot plan deeply for the ruler,
and thus they deceive their ruler.
The young
have used the days and months for only a short time,
and their learning is shallow;
they have nothing to be awed by,
so they deceive,
and thus the governance is slightly chaotic.
In modeling the governance of the creeping things and all creatures,
those who creep lack ritual and righteousness,
and all creatures have little knowledge
and possess no Dào and Dé.
The nature of the creeping things and all creatures
has no hierarchy of high and low;
they merely seek victory over one another,
and thus it leads to chaos and ruin.
Governance modeling Heaven
is benevolent, loves life, and does not harm.
Governance modeling Earth
is submissive and good but results in minor harm.
Governance modeling humanity
seeks mutual benefit and has many desires,
frequently injuring one another
and deceiving one another through negligence.
Governance by modeling the creeping things and all creatures
ultimately has no success;
regardless of being great or small,
it merely seeks victory.
Observing these types of governance
is sufficient to know that the Qi of Heaven's high, low, middle, and extreme points have not lost governance.
Those who desire the first joy should model themselves on Heaven;
those who desire the second joy should model themselves on Earth;
those who desire the third joy should model themselves on humanity;
those who desire the fourth joy should model themselves on all creatures.
Those who model Heaven uniquely enjoy old age and longevity
and obtain the heart of Heaven;
those who model Earth are slightly less long-lived
and obtain the intent of Earth;
those who model humanity have reduced longevity;
and those who model all creatures die,
without a proper time or count.
In modeling Heaven,
the Three Paths communicate through writing;
Heaven has three patterns,
which clearly manifest as the Three Luminaries,
meaning the Sun, Moon, and the array of stars;
the Sun observes Yáng,
the Moon observes Yīn,
and the stars observe the center;
therefore, one should use the three paths to transmit documents
and strive to obtain their brilliance.
When a document arrives for one who has passed,
it has only the name of the master,
and one should not ask who the messenger is.
In modeling Earth,
one uses two paths to transmit documents.
In modeling humanity,
one uses one path to transmit documents,
yet there is still negligent delay.
In modeling the creeping things and all creatures,
one merely sets forth words
and has no written documents.
As for the current state,
did Heaven cause it to be so?
Or did people do it themselves?
It is the fortune of the times.
Nevertheless,
when the governance of emperors and kings is about to reach Tàipíng,
Heaven will cause them to love goodness and rejoice,
modeling the governance of Heaven;
those that will be moderately peaceful
model the governance of Earth;
those that will be slightly chaotic
take the governance of humanity as their law;
and those that will be in great chaos and unmanageable
take the governance of the creeping things and all creatures as their law.
Why is this so?
How should it be saved now?
If Heaven is about to make it flourish,
auspicious omens and extraordinary writings will emerge and be given to them,
causing them to have a great awakening and receiving them;
for those about to decline,
Heaven hides its writings so they are not seen
and also causes them not to love seeking them.
As for worthy ministers,
is it just that they must be elderly?
Not so;
the elderly...
This refers to the Qíjiù who are seasoned in virtue and the Way.
They emulate Heaven, uniquely and constantly maintaining the Way and acting accordingly,
without straying by even the slightest amount.
Therefore, they can bring peace to their sovereigns.
If one is old but possesses no knowledge,
they cannot serve in office.
How should one serve them as a teacher or father?
How as a friend?
How as a son?
How should one treat them as the myriad things?
Serving them as a father
is like a son receiving instruction from a strict father
or a disciple receiving instruction from a wise teacher.
One should obtain the secret strategies, hidden words, and sagely writings from their heart
in order to pacify the world
and to show gratitude to the ancestors,
so that the ancestral temples may receive offerings.
Such virtue repays the great merits of Heaven;
thus, one can win the hearts of the world,
Yīnyáng will be harmonized,
and disasters will cease.
Serving them as a friend is done through loyalty and trustworthiness,
working together on strategies,
and deeply calculating good and evil, difficulty and ease.
Serving them as a son [refers to cases where]
the father may have hidden matters
that he does not dare report to his son;
the son may have hidden faults
that he does not dare report to his parents.
Both end up deceiving each other,
and this becomes a ladder to decline.
As for the myriad things, there is countless great disorder.
All things in spring and summer compete to live;
in autumn and winter, they compete to die,
never allowing each other even a moment's respite."
Chún bowed twice and said,
"The things I have asked are many,
my faults are truly heavy
and quite inappropriate;
I truly have committed faults toward my Master.
Furthermore, I do not dare hide this text.
If I see it and do not put it into practice,
I fear I will commit a fault against Huángtiān.
Where should I place this book now?"
"Since you have asked about it,
you should strive to put it into practice.
If you meet someone capable of understanding it, give it to them,
so they may go and present it to a virtuous ruler.
If sovereigns emulate it
and use it as a method of governance,
it will surely be like divine power.
If one obtains it but cannot deeply reflect upon and use it,
Heaven will no longer blame you."
"Yes, yes,
I dare not go against my Master's words."
"Indeed,
my words must not be greatly defied.
This is because Heaven and Earth wish for peace
and have brought forth the Zhìdào,
causing you to come from afar to inquire fully about this method.
Heaven has caused me to speak
and transmit these words to you;
I do not speak in vain.
If Heaven did not wish me to speak,
and I spoke and leaked Heaven's essential Way without cause,
I would be punished for it.
Since you have received my words
and will go to present them,
there is no harm or doubt.
I tell you with utmost sincerity;
Heaven is bestowing even greater weight upon the sovereigns,
and thus gives this warning.
In the movements of Heaven,
good and bad fortune have their times.
Those who obtain this and practice it
will undoubtedly have good fortune."
"I respectfully ask: who is the person who shall practice this? What is their name?"
"Indeed,
when Heaven bestows things upon the myriad creatures,
there is no favoritism.
The person who asks and is the first to delight in practicing it
is that very person.
The Dàdào is of utmost importance
and cannot be used for private ends.
Those who practice it will have good fortune;
those who do not will face peril."
"I respectfully ask further: what do Heaven and Earth observe or see
that makes them wish to speak at this time?"
"There is indeed something to be seen;
it is not empty talk.
Heaven takes joy in peace and tranquility,
with no illness.
It takes delight in supreme peace.
Thus, it causes the people to be quiet and without evil sounds,
and they do not fight.
When each dwells in their proper place,
then there is no illness and there is joy.
Then Heaven's words are not spoken in vain.
If Yīnyáng are made to fight in reverse,
clashing in confusion and interfering with one another,
harming one another,
so that the myriad things cannot stay in their places,
the sun and moon lose their proper brightness,
and the stars move in disorder,
then Heaven is ill.
It is depressed and troubled;
if its words are not transmitted,
the illness will not be cured.
Therefore, when there is disorder, Heaven speaks.
Small disorder leads to small talk;
great disorder leads to great talk.
For this reason, from ancient times to the present, the Shénzhēn and Shèngrén act as envoys for Heaven.
They receive the heart of Heaven
and are primarily responsible for speaking on behalf of Heaven and Earth.
Since Heaven and Earth established affairs,
this has been the constant law throughout time.
Therefore, the writings of the Sages have always served as the speech of Heaven,
speaking of affairs on behalf of Heaven.
What kind of matters are discussed?
It depends on what is suffering.
When refinement is lost, the Way provides substance.
If substance is obstructed and not getting through, the Way provides refinement.
To treat depravity and evil,
the Way provides correctness and goodness,
causing people to awaken.
Now, Heaven and Earth are supremely honored and naturally divine.
Divinity can bring clarity,
and their position is unsurpassed.
Why do they not remove the illness themselves,
but instead transmit words to humans?
Heaven and Earth
are the parents of the myriad things.
Although the parents act with goodness,
if their children act wickedly,
dwelling in the center
and primarily committing evil and rebellion,
and if their governance of high and low
is contrary and chaotic,
even though the parents are good,
it is still a wicked household.
It is like a wicked son bringing chaos to his father,
a wicked minister to his ruler,
a wicked disciple to his teacher, or
a wicked wife to her husband.
In such cases, they harm one another in great disorder,
and there is no way to see their goodness.
Heaven, Earth, the people, and the myriad things
are fundamentally governing the same matter.
If there is good, all rejoice;
if there is misfortune, all suffer.
Thus they share the same concern.
If they did not share in the matter,
they would not be willing to concern themselves with one another.
Therefore, when Heaven and Earth desire goodness and peace,
they must cause the Shénzhēn and Shèngrén to transmit their words
and bring forth their divine texts
to inform and speak to others.
It is like a sovereign who, wishing for joyful goodness in governance,
then issues good teachings.
This is what is meant.
You wish to joyfully know the heart of Heaven,
to repay the merits of Heaven,
and to rescue the world from calamitous qi.
This book of mine is precisely that.
When you obtain it, reflect upon it well,
and the Heart of Heaven can then be known."
"Yes, yes,
I dare not be negligent.
I hope the Master will again bestow a word or two of instruction."
"Indeed.
Good and evil each affect the person.
The good person benefits their own person;
the evil person harms their own body.
Since you have expressed a desire for goodness
and are concerned about the illness of Heaven and Earth
and the lack of peace for the rulers,
your merit is already extremely great.
Just reflect upon it in detail.
Your practice of goodness is peerless;
do not stop or harm it,
but make your thoughts of goodness follow the constant path like this."
"Yes, yes,
I dare not be negligent;
I dare not be negligent."
To the right is the Fènbié Zhìsuǒ Xiàng Ānwēi Fǎ.
“I have asked a great deal,
and seeing the Tiān Shī speak,
the matters are pleasant and unending,
and there is no time when asking is sufficient;
I again humbly beg for a word or two.”
“Proceed evenly.”
“Now my wish is to obtain the heart and intention of Heaven and Earth, Yīn and Yáng, the people, the crawling creatures, all things, and all affairs,
to always make them joyful and good without end,
wandering daily without duties or troubles,
with their bodies each being correct on their own,
no longer turning to mutual sorrow and suffering,
or blaming and reproaching one another;
is it possible to hear of this?”
“You now speak
of what is most pleasant and extraordinary;
what can be asked
is what is unique in its goodness and virtue.
However, regarding what you asked,
one should still follow the nature of things,
allowing each to obtain its own heart,
and by following what their talents and abilities can reach,
one does not dare to conversely force them to do what they cannot do.
In this way, each obtains what they desire.
When each obtains their desire,
then there will be none who suffer mutual sorrow.
Thus, each obtains their heart’s intent,
and it can be called wandering without duties or troubles.
Between Heaven and Earth,
if one always employs them for what is not their ability,
forcing them to do what they cannot reach,
and making difficult what they are unable to do;
seeing at times what they cannot do
or cannot say,
and instead of showing pity and teaching them,
one conversely reproaches them,
causing them to harbor grievances,
with much anger and litigation,
the people will suffer sorrow, hardship, and poverty.
They then look up and cry out to Huáng Tiān,
‘Indeed a grievance! Indeed a grievance!’
and their Qì moves the six directions.
Therefore, it results in numerous disasters and changes,
accumulating not just once,
and they cannot be suddenly removed,
becoming an extreme harm.
This is to lose the heart and intent of the people of the world.
In the end, conversely, there is no success;
strange portents do not cease.
As for the Qì of Tài Píng,
from where can it come?
Therefore, one cannot achieve Tài Píng;
the fault lies exactly here.”
“Even if one wishes to call it Cháng Píng,
from where can internal chaos be purified and governed?”
“You now ask about this,
wishing to know its details deeply!
By the nature of Heaven and Earth,
all things each have their own suitability.
One should employ them according to their strengths
and what they can do;
as for what they cannot do,
one must not force them.
Although all things together receive the Qì of Yīn and Yáng,
they are like fish that cannot live without water
or swim atop high mountains.
When there is water,
regardless of whether it is high or low,
they can all swim through it.
Large trees cannot live without soil
and grow in the midst of rivers or seas.
Therefore, when the sages and enlightened kings of old assigned tasks,
they took from the five types of soil what was suitable for each.
Thus, the things became fine and good,
and each flourished.
The state became wealthy because of it,
allowing the ancestral temples to have double flavors to eat.
The world was peaceful and balanced,
without any suffering or hardship;
evil Qì ceased
and did not go about causing harm.
If one does not divine or examine the land before planting,
then all things will not be able to complete their natural lifespan.
They all harbor grievances that are not resolved;
consequently, they die young.
This alone moves Huáng Tiān above.
When nothing can be harvested from the myriad things,
then the state becomes extremely poor because of it.
Food does not have double flavors,
the ancestral temples are hungry and thirsty,
and the world is filled with sorrow.
The people mutually harm one another,
ruler and minister mutually deceive each other,
and words differ internally and externally.
The fault precisely begins here.
This is merely when the myriad things do not find their place;
how much more so for people?
That the world cannot be governed correctly
is precisely due to this.
This
is the root of great harm
and the path to peril and ruin.
Can one not be cautious?
Can one not reflect deeply on it in one’s heart?
Therefore, in antiquity,
when great sages and worthies were about to employ people,
they first tested their strengths
and weaknesses,
and only then assigned them their duties
and employed them accordingly.
If that person committed an error,
they then reproached them;
they questioned them on their strengths
and did not exceed their weaknesses.
In this case, it does not move Heaven;
rather, it becomes a way to practice and advance in the learning of this school.
Thus, by being cautious,
one can win the heart of the world.
Now, later generations neglect affairs
and do not reflect deeply on the words of the ancient sages.
Instead, they assign duties inappropriately,
reproaching people for what they cannot reach,
and questioning them on what they cannot see.
The blind cannot see the sun,
and the mute cannot speak;
yet they instead target their weaknesses
and consider them grave errors,
consequently punishing them.
This is not acting for mutual joy, benefit, or protection,
but instead clever manipulation of superiors and subordinates
and mutual harm.
This is the great ruin of the world.
Since ancient times, the lords and rulers of Tài Píng
had no strange or divine Way;
they all simply followed and employed what hearts and abilities could reach.
Therefore, they could achieve the Qì of Tài Píng
and have no people harboring grievances.
When calamity and chaos are about to arise,
it is all because of employing those without the ability,
making them do tasks and duties not their own and reproaching them heavily.
Even if the punishments involve death,
they still cannot manage their duties.
Disasters and changes arise one after another
and cannot be stopped,
consequently resulting in chaos and ruin.
Good and bad fortune, safety and peril,
arise precisely from this.
Therefore, when the ancients selected scholars for the emperors and kings,
they all first inquired and observed,
testing their abilities
to see if they harmonized with the auspicious responses of Heaven and Earth and Yīn and Yáng or not.
Those who could not harmonize
were all considered to be acting falsely.
How do they harmonize?
Great men obtain great responses,
and lesser men obtain small responses.
Wind and rain keep their seasons,
all things flourish beautifully,
the common people have no complaints,
and birds, beasts, and crawling things
are peaceful and quiet;
these are the effects.
Therefore, those who delight in governing and wish to bring peace to the state
must be careful in their appointments.
Heaven produces all things,
each with its own talent and ability,
and each truly has its own suitability.
It is like the dragon ascending to heaven
and the fish swimming in the deep;
this is what is meant.
As for governing,
since Heaven and Earth were established,
it has had ten thousand facets.
Heaven’s changes also vary with the times;
the essential thing is to follow Heaven and Earth and obtain their intent,
obtaining what they wish to do.
Heaven
uses the Sān Guāng as its written records,
with one rising and one declining;
it uses the wind as the ruler of men.
Earth
uses mountains, rivers, and pathways as its patterns.
Mountains exhale Qì,
and waters flow through its meridians and vessels.
Decline, prosperity, movement, shifting, collapse, and merging
use unusual winds as the ministers of men.
Humans
use sounds and words to transmit to one another,
and written records to succeed one another.
The myriad things
speak through their decline and prosperity,
allowing humans to contemplate and know them.
Humans
are in the center of Yīn and Yáng,
acting as the masters and elders of all things,
and what they can create is the most numerous.
They resemble the spirits yet have form,
changing and moving forward or backward.
The ruler should record these anomalies
and speak on their behalf.
Therefore, if a single word does not penetrate,
then there are grievances and knots;
if two levels of speech do not communicate,
there will always be obstructions;
if three levels of speech do not communicate,
there will be further isolation;
if four levels of speech do not communicate,
the seasons will not respond in harmony,
and the creation of life will be erratic;
if five levels of speech do not communicate,
the path of the circulating *Qì* will experience conflict;
if six levels of speech do not communicate,
the six directions will loathe life;
if seven levels of speech do not communicate, there is ruin and failure;
if eight levels of speech do not communicate, it is difficult for many households to reside;
if nine levels of speech do not communicate,
there is mutual injury and theft;
if ten levels of speech do not communicate,
there is mutual change and revolution.
Therefore, one must strive to communicate their speech.
In ancient times there was no writing;
how was it communicated?
Writing then arose as it should,
but it stopped midway.
How many times did Heaven and Earth start,
and how many times did they stop?
It is only that later generations did not see it.
During the *Sān Huáng* of middle antiquity,
they established speech when there was no writing.
In later antiquity, the *Qì* of Heaven and Earth returned,
ending once and rising once.
Only the *Shén Rén* does not know from where old age comes;
having experienced many events,
he knows their principles.
Internally there should be writing,
but later generations did not see it
and claimed it did not exist.
For what reason is there sometimes writing and sometimes not?
When the *Qì* of Heaven is about to fail,
and people are about to be foolish, shallow, and short-lived,
they cannot have anything worth engraving or recording.
Therefore, they were commanded through writing,
so that records could be passed back and forth,
knowing that ancient matters had no writing,
and that people would debate and litigate,
unable to correct each other,
each claiming to be right.
Thus, they caused there to be written documents.
This was only because the people of the time were foolish;
so writing was created for them,
and Heaven produced contracted texts.
“Having seen the Master's words,
I already know this.
I wish to hear how the communication of *Qì* should be handled today.”
“Simply allow the writings of the three paths and eight directions to circulate,
and the speech of the people, officials, and commoners,
and do not delay them arbitrarily.
Urgent matters should be resolved according to the time;
non-urgent matters should follow the ten thousand things of Heaven and Earth.
Wait for the seventh month when things end,
look over them in the eighth month,
change their order in the ninth month,
and if by the tenth month they have not returned,
those who have submitted writings for three years and are entirely faithful and sincere,
seek out such people and employ them.
Such a person is then a *Liáng Chén* of the state,
with sharp ears and bright eyes,
acting as those very senses,
not losing the omens of the four directions.
If a *Dì Wáng* gains such a person,
it is called being peaceful and enlightened;
therefore, such a person must be employed.”
“How should they be employed?”
“One must ask each what their ability reaches,
making each record what they are able to do,
what they are able to analyze,
and what their strengths are,
and employ them according to their natural disposition;
thus, there will be no failure in governance.
Thus, the world's glad heart is won,
its governance daily rises toward *Tài Píng*,
there are no punishments,
no exhaustion of things,
and no aggrieved people.
Heaven and Earth are in *Zhōng hé*,
and all things can communicate with each other.
Thus, one can reach the longevity of the *Shàng Huáng*.
The reason their longevity was great
is that without punishments there was no injury;
many injuries will return to harm the human body.
Therefore, the sages and worthies of high antiquity did not like to use punishments.
Middle antiquity used punishments halfway,
so longevity was halved.
Later antiquity used many punishments,
so longevity alone is short.
The evil of punishment then offends Heaven,
goes against *Yīn* and *Yáng*,
and accumulates to become evil *Qì*,
which returns to harm people.
The reason sages and worthies of high antiquity did not use them heavily
was to cherish their own bodies.
The people of middle antiquity were half-foolish
and lightly used punishments in small ways, so they were halved,
destroying half their lives.
In later antiquity, people were greatly foolish,
so they recklessly used punishments
and took them as constant laws;
thus, many cannot attain longevity;
the fault lies here.
Those who read this book
should go over it repeatedly,
value it, and be cautious with it.
Life and death are grave matters
and cannot be treated recklessly.
A worthy and enlightened son plans for his father;
a worthy and enlightened minister plans deeply for his lord.
If a son is not worthy,
he is unwilling to plan deeply for his father.
If a minister is not worthy or enlightened,
he is unwilling to plan for his lord.
As for these young ones,
it is their own persons;
if that person meets with good or bad fortune,
it flows to later generations;
this is the standard law.
For this reason, when the sage emperors and kings of high antiquity were to employ ministers,
they carefully chose those who possessed *Dào* and *Dé*,
and who did not like killing or injuring.
This was not just a plan for the people,
but a deep plan for their own persons.
Thus, they obtained the heart and intent of Heaven and Earth,
and their actions were as if they were together with the spirits.
This is called examining the selection to obtain the right person,
and thus being a ruler who gains human power.
This moves the spirits of Earth and Heaven,
and the *Tiān shàng zhēn shén* will love them,
and thus they will have a long life.
Favoring the use of punishments then combines with *Yīn* *Qì*;
*Yīn* is for killing,
so one cannot attain a great life span.
The *Tiān zhī mìng*
can be roughly seen and known;
the things that Heaven, Earth, and people loathe are the same.”
Right: Gaining the glad hearts of Heaven, Earth, the people, and all things, leading to the state's rise, the family's peace, and a world without litigation.
“Can the *Dà mìng* be known now or not?”
“Although it can be known,
having seen the Master's comparison of words,
my great confusion is already resolved.
But I cannot help but
wish you would be thorough once more.”
“Indeed,
the intent of my *Dào* can be seen.
When you obtain the book and read it,
you will often suffer from not being familiar with it;
those who are familiar with it will know it all naturally.
If one does not think well on its ultimate meaning
and does not read it precisely,
even if one obtains my book,
it will be of no benefit.
To obtain it and not practice it diligently
is no different from not obtaining it at all.
To see food and not eat
is no different from having no five grains.
To see a drink and not drink,
thirst still cannot be saved.
This is not something that can distress others;
it returns to harm oneself.
How can one not be thorough?
Thus, the sage exerts effort in thought,
and the *Jūn zǐ* exerts effort in learning,
never ceasing day or night,
like the joy of wanting to emulate Heaven,
revolving without stopping.
When a hundred rivers flow together,
they then form the rivers and seas.
You should be cautious with my recorded words;
I have already warned you repeatedly.
If you are devoted,
your heart can be seen.
Perform good deeds together with the many worthies,
and be careful not to monopolize its market.
A market with few people means what is sought cannot be found.
Thus, if people do not study broadly,
what they see will not be clear.
Therefore, even if they are made to see the *Zhēn Dào*,
if they do not obtain its essential meaning,
they will not believe in the *Dào*,
and their doubt will not be firm.
All of this lies in the reason why people exhaust themselves.
Therefore, one should deeply contemplate its meaning
in order to save and assist oneself.”
Right: Concerning the aims of longevity and life span.
When Heaven bestows tasks,
each has its laws and regulations.
Mandates have those to whom they belong,
and the Dào has that which can be accomplished.
Emerging either early or late,
their gradual arrival is seen in advance.
For example, all things begin to sprout in Zǐ,
grow in Mǎo,
hang their branches in Wǔ,
reach completion in Yǒu,
and end in Hài.
Although affairs are seen in advance,
they cannot yet be guaranteed.
Each affair has its potential for action;
when the radiance first appears
but the affair itself has not yet arrived,
the path is opened beforehand.
When Heaven hangs down its signs,
they always reside in front;
they never follow behind.
Finding the right person to open the way
is what it means to receive divine help and assistance.
If there is no opening and no breakthrough,
and actions are taken without success,
then it is not the right person.
Taking this as clear proof,
when the Dào is examined and spoken of,
not one in ten thousand fails.
If it is the right person,
clarity will open for them;
if it is not the right person, it will be closed.
If the right person is truly found,
then illnesses can be removed,
disasters and anomalies will naturally vanish,
the Yídí will naturally surrender,
and without needing weapons or armor,
all will naturally dissipate.
The life of all things
each has its own potential for arrangement;
finding the right person, it moves of its own accord;
if not the right person, it hides itself.
In all matters, if the right person is not found,
one must not force action.
If it is not one’s own,
one must not force the taking.
If it is not one’s land,
one must not force planting;
if planted, it will not grow.
To say the seed is not good
when internally it has not found its place—
how can it endure for long?
The six poles and eight quarters
each have what is suitable for them;
their objects all appear,
and every matter is different.
Just as Jīnxíng resides in the West
and Mùxíng resides in the East,
if each finds its place, it flourishes;
if it loses its place, it perishes.
Therefore, all things must adhere to the soil to grow;
they cannot adhere to Heaven.
Conversely, the sun, moon, stars, and celestial markers adhere to Heaven,
and thus they can produce light.
The Dào is like this.
Thus, there is the person whose star is in the sky;
at times there is brightness,
but falling to the earth, it conversely lacks light;
this is because it is not in its proper place.
Therefore, it disrupts the constant Dào.
What can be done emerges without reckless action;
if it is the right person, it is clear;
if it is not the right person, it cannot be carried out.
The Dào is deep, distant, and immeasurable;
those who lose it fail,
and those who gain it flourish.
If one wishes to know their own prosperity or decline,
observe if the Dào can be manifested
and if the spirits can be aroused.
Internally, there are signs of longevity to observe;
by this, not one in ten thousand fails.
This is a Shénshū.
For the period of returning years,
its Dào is of supreme importance;
how could one not reflect upon it?
Thus, pass it to those who are benevolent, worthy, and clear-sighted,
and try letting them practice it for their own lives.
If it is the right person, everything should emerge together:
the worthy and wise come together,
Shénshū arrive together,
extraordinary methods emerge on their own,
and everyone is filled with joy—
then it is the right person.
Take this as the proof.
If it is not as these words say,
or if it is only seen beforehand
but cannot be practiced,
it should be left for those who come later;
the Dào does not emerge recklessly.
If there is truly a destination,
simply ask the person
and let them reflect for themselves.
Where the Dào can return
also cannot be forbidden,
nor can it be commanded;
let it go where it may,
and observe its success.
The Dào cannot be empty.
Although this is so,
talent is not as good as strength,
and strength is not as good as acting without ceasing.
All affairs under Heaven
fail due to being tested;
Heaven, Earth, and the divine spirits all test people,
so people also imitate the Dào of Heaven and test one another.
Those who see the good
have a fate that is already good;
those who see the evil
have a fate that is already in doubt.
From ancient times to the present,
if one does not move Heaven with perfect sincerity,
it is called "forcing a request."
Sometimes one might still obtain it;
but if forcing it fails,
it truly is not one's own.
How can one force the taking?
The matter is already disharmonious and not good,
being contrary and disordered.
Human fate has three grades.
Entrust the Dào to the wilderness,
and give it to those who can use it.
If those are unable to use it,
give it to the capital,
or cast it into the cities;
be careful not to block or end it.
If later generations have no heirs,
pass the books to the worthy and holy, as well as to Dàoshì.
Without master or name,
give it to those who can use it.
The Dào naturally has its destination;
it is not for each person to attach their own words.
Just as great trees return to the mountains
and flowing water returns to the sea,
this cannot be forbidden;
heavenly nature makes it so.
Those who follow it flourish;
those who oppose it fail and perish.
When Shénshū wish to emerge,
they also cannot be hidden or stored away.
Finding the right person, they will surely be manifest;
without the right person, people are as if deaf, dumb, and blind;
the body is not pleased,
and there is no light in the eyes.
One joys in carefully reading this text.
The period of the Yāngtiān for flourishing and extending life—
the numbers are all within this.
The Qi of Tàipíng
has all already appeared;
people's benevolence, love, prudence, and goodness
have all emerged;
the worthy, holy, and clear-sighted
are all already pleased;
extraordinary writings from distant regions
have all been entrusted;
strive to act without laziness
to assist oneself;
enlightened kings and holy lords
have all thereby flourished;
the Yídí have retreated and surrendered,
and all have departed.
The myriad people are most fortunate
and all are without complaint.
Heavenly longevity has already proceeded,
and no one feels wronged anymore;
the old depart with their lives fulfilled,
and the young are thus preserved.
These books shall be passed down for ten thousand generations without end,
transmitted from children to grandchildren.
Daily teaching one another,
it is called the Zhēnwén;
it shall not change for ten thousand generations,
making people auspicious.
When the Dào is completed and reached,
it becomes natural;
where there is fortune, it arrives of its own,
and none dare refuse it.
Great men obtain it to bring peace to the state;
middle scholars obtain it to become good ministers;
lesser people obtain it to escape harm.
To the right is the Tōng Dào Yì Shì Fēi Zhī Cè Wén.
The original text of the prophecy regarding responding to the principles of Heaven, harmony between above and below, the elimination of natural disasters, and the severing of treachery and falsehood.
The people of high antiquity
all had open hearts, clear eyes, and penetrating ears.
They knew future events in advance
and contemplated deeply what had not yet occurred.
They could move even the inanimate
and were eminently distinct by nature;
there was no action they took that was not successful.
What they said and the paths they followed
were all sincere and far-reaching,
never losing the heart of the Huáng Xū.
They longed for the wisdom of the Wú Jí
and the words of the Wú Jí.
They knew the lifespan of humans, their progress and retreat, and their length and shortness,
as each had its allotted portion.
Constantly using Yīn and Yáng,
they harmonized with the cycles of growth and decay.
Taking the essentials from above, below, and the middle,
they held covenants with the various Shén.
However, none were allowed to violate the great taboos of Heaven and Earth.
What they offered and what they received
had to accord with the will of Heaven.
Documents were used for mutual reporting,
reaching up to the Tiān Jūn.
When the Tiān Jūn received a document,
he saw that their self-constraints were clear.
Only then would he issue a decree,
telling them not to harbor self-resentment.
The upright and honest advanced naturally;
they were heard even without reporting.
Their voices resonated and penetrated;
they followed the laws of above and below,
and none missed the appointed time.
Fearing they might fall short,
there was never a time they did not reproach themselves.
They constantly feared that errors might be observed and recorded.
The Shén reported to each other without cease;
if there were faults, they would be dismissed from service.
Therefore, instructions are repeated,
and the language of the documents is reiterated;
one should not deviate from what is said.
This is what Heaven requires to be upheld
and what the Shén Qí look up to.
All is according to the law;
they never dare to rest.
Fearing lack of comprehension,
and since what is received is not just one thing,
all should open their hearts and minds,
for fear of violating the deadline.
Among the Shén, there are high and low ranks;
superiors and inferiors serve each other.
If things are not as said,
it is immediately noted as negligence.
Their hearts are full of sorrow and concern,
always like being hungry or thirsty for food.
When the Tiān Jūn speaks,
only after understanding does he issue teachings,
enabling them to govern one another.
Documents are numerous;
one must grasp their meaning,
and afterwards, each will have proof.
The people of high antiquity,
regarding loss, gain, and future matters,
inside and out, above and below,
observed the four directions.
Beyond the four corners of the universe,
they saw the fundamental principles.
As years and months push each other forward,
divine powers begin anew;
when would there ever be an end?
The degrees of the stars' numbers
each have their own principle;
they have never shifted.
Events always follow upon one another;
there is no further doubt.
All knew where good and bad fortune originated;
therefore, they established the calendar and records.
Three hundred and sixty days,
calculated in large and small increments;
when the count does not reach the full fraction,
this is a xiǎo yuè.
Spring, summer, autumn, and winter
each have their distinct principles.
The clepsydra markers move up and down;
the water flows slow or fast.
Distinguishing between the new and the old,
making each recognizable,
without missing even a tiny fraction.
Each month is set in its place.
Among the èr shí sì qì, the preceding and following markers are seven or eight terms each;
there are also seven or eight long days
used for coming and going.
Sacrificing to the Tiān Shén Dì Qí,
they cause the hundred officials to follow the timing of the water clock;
it is proper not to miss it.
If it is missed, it is considered non-responsive,
and the crimes charged would be many.
Therefore, day and night are divided
according to the length of the sun's path.
One hundred marks make the period,
and there must be no error.
In a kingdom with virtue,
the days are long
and the water flows slowly;
one inch is divided into ten parts,
corresponding to the legal numbers.
Nowadays, many kingdoms do not use this;
the days and months are slightly short,
with one mark being only eight or nine tenths.
Thus, for the elderly, the years and months,
which should make them weak, instead appear vigorous,
but their years are naturally thin;
how can they sustain a long time?
If a kingdom has many ministers,
the mechanism of governance moves slowly and calmly;
those born later receive blessings,
briefly gaining a chance to see and breathe.
If they are not upright but have evil,
they will again be struck down.
The brightness of Heaven and Earth
resides in the South.
Sì and Wǔ share the same house;
Lí is the true eye.
Regarding the affairs of the Míng Táng,
the sun shines brightly from south to north.
The progress and retreat of Yáng energy
also does not lose its constancy.
Yīn and Yáng press against each other,
reaching the region of Zǐ.
Cold and warmth meet directly,
illuminating nature thoroughly;
it is very pleasing.
The Way of nourishing life:
Shǎo Yáng and Tài Yáng,
Wood and Fire flourish together,
each obtaining its wish;
what then is there to dispute?
Inside and outside sustain each other
without losing their names.
Above, it reaches the Huáng Yào;
below, it reaches the soundless.
Silent and natural,
the myriad things flourish and bloom,
perfectly clear and knowable.
Accomplishing without exertion,
that which Heaven looks up to
should receive its name.
Where the astronomical instruments point,
life and death have their appointed times.
Sī Mìng upholds the registers;
ledgers and counts are communicated in documents,
so that no one is summoned inappropriately.
They seek the divine ledgers to verify the truth
and then report to the Tiān Jūn.
The Tiān Jūn has overall command.
The Shén who report
never leave his side;
they are respected internally and externally,
and they do not dare to act on private interest.
What is sent up and what is sent down
each does not miss its time.
The officials of Tài Yīn
do not dare to slacken or stop.
Guarding the gates and pavilions of the camps,
fearing they might speak of their own affairs,
they always uphold what is good as the essential Way.
Recording names on tablets,
they act once instructions are received
without missing a tiny fraction.
In the time of high antiquity,
there was wisdom and deliberation that illuminated everything
and saw everything.
Receiving the Way of the Shén Míng,
it was clearly knowable;
there were also their own laws and measures,
never losing their constancy.
Since the Tài Chū,
calendars have had variations in length,
which are profoundly deep and essential.
From ancient times to the present,
the essence of producing a calendar
lies in where it stops and what it accomplishes.
Always using the mind to observe and calculate,
what is accomplished and made below never fails to be completed,
with numbers corresponding as precisely as a plumb line,
calculating years by accumulating days and months,
using large divisions as the basis of the calculation.
Now Heaven and Earth are having a great and joyful harvest year,
and the Dìwáng should sit peacefully without worry.
The common people should only wander about without affairs or minor duties.
The five grains are no longer as they were before;
they have no price.
Everyone in the world starts making good wine to drink with one another,
and the marketplaces reach a great extreme.
This is named "Shuǐ lìng Huǒ xíng,"
and it causes injury to the Yánghuà.
Whenever a person drinks wine and gets drunk,
wild pulses then manifest,
buying and selling lose their proper function,
and people fight and kill one another,
or injure and rob.
Some arrive early at the market
but only return when it is late;
some are caught by wicked people;
some fall from high places;
or some are harmed by chariots and horses.
If we deduce the harms of wine, they are of ten thousand kinds,
and they cannot be fully recorded.
Consider that within the four seas,
how many markets are there?
Within a single month,
they consume hundreds of millions of dǒu and hú of the five grains,
and moreover, people are killed or injured for no reason;
this happens every day.
Some who are solitary thus have their lineage cut off;
some form grudges that bring harm to their parents;
or disasters are spread to their descendants.
County officials and senior clerks
cannot manage based on reason;
they beat their chests and cry out to Heaven,
moving the Huánglíng,
causing the Qì of Yīn and Yáng, the four seasons, and the five elements to fall into disorder.
This further hinders the rule of the Shànghuáng Tàipíng monarch
and causes the Tàihé Qì to flow backward.
For no reason, the people are allowed to make wine,
wasting the five grains
and leading to such calamities.
If a virtuous monarch
issues instructions and clear commands,
saying to the officials and people:
"From now on,
anyone who dares to drink one dǒu in the market for no reason
shall receive thirty lashes
and three days of penal labor;
those who drink two dǒu
shall receive sixty lashes
and six days of penal labor;
those who drink three dǒu
shall receive ninety lashes
and nine days of penal labor."
Each penalty follows the amount of wine measured in hú.
The same applies to the wine shops.
All shall be made to repair city walls, roads, and official residences.
The reason for assigning the repair of city walls, roads, and official residences
is to perform great earthworks.
Earth overcomes water;
this suppresses and cuts off the harm,
preventing Water from excessively harming Yáng.
Water is Tàiyīn;
it represents the people.
Conversely, it makes them rise over the King,
damaging the Yángjīng,
and the harm is deep.
By repairing the roads,
one takes the flourishing of the Dàdào;
judging by similar categories,
Tàipíng will gradually be established.
Examining Heaven and Earth, Yīn and Yáng, and the myriad things,
those above and below love and govern each other,
establishing merit and achieving fame,
causing the mind to govern the family,
making it so people no longer hate each other,
but always rejoice in being of one heart and one will.
This causes the Tàihé Qì to emerge daily of its own accord,
leading to the great rise of peace.
The Liùjí will be of one heart,
and the Bāfāng will be of one plan.
If the governance is like what people desire,
none will fail to respond and be pleased.
Grounded in the Yuánqì of Heaven and Earth
and harmonizing with the positions of Yīn and Yáng,
evil and wickedness will silently vanish.
Those who were contrary will all become compliant.
This clarifies the ultimate way of the Dàlíng,
which the gods and spirits love.
Above, I explain the Way and Virtue for Huángtiān;
below, I distinguish the measures for the mountains and rivers;
in the middle, I establish laws and measures for the Dìwáng.
The moderately virtuous can thus give rise to good intentions.
Thereby, the great faults and grievances of Heaven and Earth are resolved,
so the Dìwáng are no longer anxious and distressed,
the people love each other,
and the myriad things each find their proper place.
There are naturally constant rules of the heavenly laws that are not hidden.
In ancient times, the Shèngdì and Míngwáng
valued their ministers,
loved scholars in retirement,
and benefited the people,
never harming or injuring them.
Ministers were also loyal and trustworthy, not deceiving their lord.
Therefore, governance was like that of the spirits.
Thus, a virtuous father always thinks of bringing peace to his son,
and a son always thinks of bringing peace and joy to his father.
