When the two combine their strength and are of one heart,
there is nothing in the family that cannot be achieved.
If they do not combine their strength and are not of one heart,
the way of the family falls into disorder.
They lose their duties and affairs,
becoming empty, poor, and desperate.
Because of fighting and discord, they separate and leave,
eventually coming back to harm one another.
Even biological fathers and sons are born of the same body, blood, and Qì,
and their limbs and bodies are connected like this—
how much more so for the gathering of scholars of different surnames from throughout the world who serve as ministers, teachers, and fathers?
Therefore, the Shèngrén see the minute and know the manifest;
thus they emphasize caution and vigilance.
A Shī
is Yáng.
He loves his disciples
and guides and teaches them with the good way,
making them know to value Heaven and love Earth,
to respect those above and benefit those below.
The disciples respectfully serve their teacher,
being compliant, diligent, loyal, and trustworthy without deception.
When the two combine their strength and are of one heart,
they map out the old laws and measures of ancient and modern times,
practicing the words of the Shèngrén,
and clarifying the divisions and principles of the realms of Heaven and Earth.
They cause the myriad things to each find their place,
accumulating virtue without stopping.
Thereby they become excellent assistants to the Dìwáng,
joining their strategies and governing together to achieve Tàipíng.
If they do not combine their strength and are not of one plan,
if they do not transmit the essential way to each other,
but instead desire superficiality and external talk,
deceiving and endangering each other,
going against the principles of Heaven,
and disordering the words of the Shèngrén,
then the Liùjí will not be distinct and clear,
and this will become a great disaster for the world.
If a Dìwáng takes such a person as a teacher,
he will lose his principles and laws,
and instead become a great enemy to Heaven and Earth,
failing to obtain the intent of the Shénmíng;
this is a great harm to the world.
Human life is fully endowed with Yīn and Yáng.
Movement, stillness, anger, and joy all have their proper times;
there is a time before the union of female and male.
This Yīn and Yáng should primarily serve the efficacy of generating life.
The Tiāndào is completed through the union of three,
therefore a child walks after three years.
Three times three is nine,
and the Way of Harmony is fulfilled.
Before knowing the union of female and male,
the thoughts of that time cannot yet be enacted.
The number of Heaven is five,
the number of Earth is five,
and the number of Man is five;
three times five is fifteen,
and the internal hidden Qì moves.
Four times five is twenty;
merging with the Qì of the Sìshí, there is a desire to enact.
The Sìshí govern generation,
therefore there is a desire to enact generation.
Five times five is twenty-five,
and the Qì of the Wǔxíng is sufficient to permit enactment.
Five times six is thirty, and one becomes strong.
Therefore, Heaven causes one to constantly think of enactment,
in order to connect with the system of Heaven and Earth,
and to propagate the species.
At thirty years, one reaches release.
When old, one naturally declines;
the young should stop and be secluded in the inner chambers.
Of all the crawling creatures under Heaven,
humans alone purely resemble Heaven and Earth;
the rest are not able to do so.
Therefore, in one day and one night, Heaven and Earth together nourish the twelve thousand things and make them all live.
Night is deep;
day is dry.
That which is deep
is Yīn;
that which is dry
is Yáng.
Heaven and Earth daily together nourish these twelve thousand things to completion.
According to the law of Heaven,
Yáng joins essence to become the enactment of two Yángs,
which then descends into the Earth to follow each other
and together generate the twelve thousand things.
Among them, two thousand
are Jiāruì and good things.
Now, as for the twelve thousand things,
each possesses its own essence and spirit
and has its own ruler or leader.
They should all walk together upon one Dàdào,
and then they can circulate freely.
The Tiāndào goes up and down,
going to pay court to its ruler,
just as people share one great road
to go and pay court to a king.
The spirits of the twelve thousand things
are generated together with Heaven and Earth
and emerge together along one Dàdào.
There are large ones, medium ones, and small ones.
What does this mean?
It means that since the twelve thousand things vary in size,
their ways also vary in size;
each generates itself, accommodates itself, and moves along.
Therefore, the Upper Way is ten thousand paces wide by law,
the next is one thousand paces wide by law,
the next is one hundred paces wide by law,
the next is ten paces wide by law,
and the next is one pace wide by law.
These five ways correspond to the five directions;
they should together descend and be born on Earth,
together pay court to Heaven,
and move together along one way.
Thus the Dàdào is ten thousand paces wide,
accommodating the Medium Way of one thousand paces,
the Small Way of one hundred paces,
the Máodào of ten paces,
and the Máodào of one pace.
Things vary in size,
and each accommodates its own coming and going.
All receive the enactment of Heaven from above
and in turn generate and enact upon the Earth below;
when emerging, they should all ascend together to pay court to Heaven.
Therefore, the Dàdào can only be expanded;
it must not be recklessly contracted.
If contracted, things will immediately fail to accommodate each other.
Some will not be able to live,
and some may be injured or die.
Those who cannot be born or emerge
cause people to have their lineages cut off without descendants.
The injured injure others,
and the dead kill others.
The Shèngrén of old did not dare to abandon or sever the Dàdào
because they clearly saw the prohibitions of Heaven.
By what means, my child, can the Tiāndào be injured?
The Dào
is Heaven,
it is Yáng,
and it governs generation.
Dé
is Earth,
it is Yīn,
and it governs nourishment.
When many of the myriad things cannot be born,
one then knows the Tiāndào is injured.
When there are those that are not born,
one then knows that there is suppression and severance.
If one thing is not born, one lineage is severed;
if many are not, many are severed;
if few are not, few are severed.
According to the number of things,
one knows how much the Heavenly system is injured.
When the Dào flourishes, it governs generation,
and all the myriad things are born.
When Dé flourishes, it governs nourishment,
and all the myriad things and the people are all nourished,
without grievances or knots.
Among the Five Books (*Wǔshū*), those that are good
use *Qīng* as the base and *Dān* for the characters;
why is this?
My *Dào* is the faithfulness of *Dānqīng*.
*Qīng* generates *Rén* and possesses a heart;
Red is *Tàiyáng*,
the correct color of *Tiān*.
My *Dào* is *Tàiyáng*,
the Way of *Rénzhèng*,
which does not desire to cause harm.
The *Tiānzǐ*
is the heart of *Tiān*;
the *Huánghòu*
is the heart of *Dì*.
Now, the heart
presides over correctness.
*Tiān* covers all without exception,
produces all without exception;
whether great or small,
all receive their mandate to be born from it;
therefore, it is called *Tiān*.
*Tiān*
is the truth of the *Zhìdào*;
it does not deceive people.
It is what the myriad things should love and be close to.
In the exercise of its intentions,
it should accumulate sincerity and faithfulness,
only ever desiring to benefit and not to harm,
not failing a single thing;
therefore, it is *Tiān*.
Now, the *Dìwáng*
are the sons of *Tiān*
and the leaders of people;
their conduct should emulate this.
A son
should receive his father’s teachings, commands, and strict orders,
acting according to them.
Then his affairs will accord with his father’s heart and will,
and he can be considered a member of a good family.
If he does not receive his father’s teachings and commands,
the affairs of his household, great and small, will not be governed,
and it will become a poor family.
Wealth will instead scatter in the four directions,
constantly suffering from not accumulating;
affairs will be in chaos,
disasters and anomalies will arise one after another,
resulting in great sorrow and suffering;
the fault lies in this.
In ancient times, when the *Dìwáng* were about to act,
they first looked up to observe the heart of *Tiān*,
receiving instruction within;
only then would they act.
Now, the conduct of the *Huánghòu*
should precisely suit the *Tǔdì*;
for *Dì* supports all things without exception,
both great and small return to it.
Within it there is no distinction of good or evil;
it encompasses and nurtures them all.
The *Huánghòu*
is the child of *Dì*
and the heart of *Dì*.
The heart worries over all matters.
A child should receive and emulate the mother’s conduct like the mother;
only then is he a filial child.
The correspondence between *Tiān*, *Dì*, and the *Huánghòu*
is like an echo to a sound;
if the failure is small, the consequence is small,
and if the failure is great, the consequence is great.
If there is even a hair’s breadth of discrepancy,
it is because the will does not accord with the mother.
In ancient times, when the *Huánghòu* was about to take action,
she would first contemplate *Hòutǔ*,
which encompasses and nurtures all.
There is nothing it cannot endure,
and there is nothing that lacks constancy;
finding peace in this,
she accorded with the heart of the *Tǔ*.
If she loses this,
then disasters and anomalies arise one after another,
punishments cannot be restrained,
*Yīn* becomes excessive and *Yáng* deficient,
and the myriad things do not flourish;
the fault lies in this.
If these two persons act correctly,
then the *Shénzhēn* will appear,
the *Zhēndào* will emerge,
the worthy and wise will all be in their positions,
and all good things will return to the state.
*Yuánqì* is *Yáng*;
it governs birth.
Spontaneous transformation is *Yīn*;
it governs the nourishment of all things.
Heaven (*Tiān*) as *Yáng* governs birth;
Earth (*Dì*) as *Yīn* governs nourishment.
The sun and the daytime
are *Yáng*
and govern birth;
the moon, stars, and night
are *Yīn*
and govern nourishment.
Spring and summer
are *Yáng*
and govern birth;
autumn and winter
are *Yīn*
and govern nourishment.
*Jiǎ*, *Bǐng*, *Wù*, *Gēng*, and *Rén*
are *Yáng*
and govern birth;
*Yǐ*, *Dīng*, *Jǐ*, *Xīn*, and *Guǐ*
are *Yīn*
and govern nourishment.
*Zǐ*, *Yín*, *Chén*, *Wǔ*, *Shēn*, and *Xū*
are *Yáng*
and govern birth;
*Chǒu*, *Mǎo*, *Sì*, *Wèi*, *Yǒu*, and *Hài*
are *Yīn*
and govern nourishment.
Likewise, all nines
are *Yáng*
and govern birth;
all sixes
are *Yīn*
and govern nourishment.
Men
are *Yáng*
and govern birth;
women
are *Yīn*
and govern the nourishment of the myriad things.
The male is *Yáng*;
it governs birth;
the female is *Yīn*;
it governs nourishment.
The ruler is *Yáng*;
it governs birth;
the minister is *Yīn*;
it governs nourishment.
Regarding all affairs under Heaven,
they are always one *Yīn* and one *Yáng*;
thus they can generate each other
and thus they can nourish each other.
If one *Yáng* does not bestow birth,
then one *Yīn* is but a void
with nothing to nourish;
if one *Yīn* does not receive transformation,
then one *Yáng* has no means to bestow the governance of birth.
If the *Yáng* *qì* is unified, cut off, extinguished, and does not flow,
it is a cause for great resentment in Heaven.
If one *Yīn* does not receive transformation,
it cannot give birth,
which is a great fault.
That which is called the resentment of Heaven
is when *Yáng* does not like to bestow
and there is nothing produced,
but instead it likes to kill and harm its offspring.
The fault of Earth
lies in *Yīn* not liking to receive transformation,
so there is nothing to emerge, nourish, or grow;
thus it faults people
by instead harming their nourishment and growth.
If Heaven does not provide rain in season,
it is an evil and unlucky Heaven;
if Earth does not generate and nourish the myriad things,
it is an evil and unlucky Earth.
If a man does not bestow birth, he cuts off the lineage of Heaven;
if a woman does not receive transformation, she cuts off the lineage of Earth.
Regarding the Way (*Dào*) of *Yīn* and *Yáng*,
to be extinguished and without descendants
is a great misfortune.
It is as if Heaven and Earth were suddenly destroyed
and Heaven and Earth no longer existed.
For this reason, Sages (*Shèng*) and Worthies (*Xián*) love the essential writings of Heaven.
Heaven
is the essence of all Ways (*Dào*).
Worthies love the Way (*Dào*),
therefore they are ranked after Sages.
Worthies enter the True Way (*Zhēn Dào*),
therefore they are ranked after Immortals (*Xiān*).
Those who know and can become Immortals must be True (*Zhēn*),
therefore they are ranked after the True.
Those who know the True must attain the Divine (*Shén*).
The Divine,
above, share the same form and follow the same principles as Heaven;
therefore Heaven is called Divine
and can employ the Divine.
The Divine
are the officials of the August Heaven (*Huángtiān*).
Divine Beings (*Shénrén*)
are the primary heart of August Heaven.
In the nature of Heaven and Earth,
the clear governs the turbid,
and the turbid must not govern the clear.
Essential light is the heart of the myriad things;
clear-sighted rulers use the heart to examine affairs
and must use clarity and brightness.

Now, what do *Shénrén*, True Beings (*Zhēnrén*), Immortals (*Xiānrén*), Men of the Way (*Dàorén*), Sages (*Shèngrén*), Worthies (*Xiánrén*), the common people (*Mínrén*), and slaves (*Nǔbì*) each resemble?
*Shénrén* resemble Heaven;
Heaven moves and illuminates, knowing everything.
*Zhēnrén* resemble Earth;
Earth is direct and sincere and does not deceive Heaven,
but simply follows what people plant without changing it.
*Xiānrén* resemble the four seasons (*Sìshí*);
the four seasons
transform all things
and have no constant appearance,
sometimes flourishing and sometimes declining.
*Dàorén* resemble the Five Elements (*Wǔxíng*);
the Five Elements can be used to divine good and bad fortune
and are skilled in matters of safety and danger.
*Shèngrén* resemble *Yīn* and *Yáng*;
*Yīn* and *Yáng* resemble Heaven and Earth in managing affairs
and harmonizing the myriad things;
Sages must also harmonize the myriad things,
fulfilling the heart of Heaven
and acting in accordance with *Yīn* and *Yáng*.
*Xiánrén* resemble mountains and rivers (*Shānchuān*);
mountains and rivers govern the circulation of *qì* to distant regions;
Worthies must also facilitate communication for the Emperor (*Dìwáng*) in all six directions.
The common people (*Fánmín*) resemble the myriad things;
the myriad things live everywhere without distinction of high or low,
and wherever there are people,
thus they resemble the myriad things.
Slaves are born in declining ages;
they resemble the weak and submissive grasses and trees
who always dwell in the lower reaches
and thus cannot stretch themselves;
slaves always dwell below
and thus cannot stretch themselves,
therefore they resemble grasses and trees.
Therefore, a slave who is a Worthy can become a good person;
a good person who loves learning can become a Worthy (*Xiánrén*);
a Worthy who loves learning without ceasing
is next to a Sage (*Shèngrén*);
a Sage who learns without ceasing
knows the gates of the Way of Heaven (*Tiāndào*);
entering the Way (*Dào*) without ceasing
achieves the state of immortality
and becomes an Immortal (*Xiān*);
an Immortal not ceasing enters the True (*Zhēn*);
becoming True without ceasing enters the Divine (*Shén*);
the Divine not ceasing then shares the same form as August Heaven (*Huángtiān*).
Therefore, the highest *Shénrén* reside in the Purple Palace (*Zǐgōng*) at the North Pole (*Běijí*),
sharing the same image as the Supreme Emperor of Heaven (*Tiān Shàngdì*);
they are called the Divine Heart of Heaven (*Tiānxīn Shén*).
Being Divine and not ceasing,
they then transcend Heaven and go above,
only receiving the entrusted *qì*,
having sounds and teachings but no form,
belonging to the realm above Heaven
and concerning themselves with the affairs of Heaven above.
From the *Shénrén* on down,
they together worry about the space between Heaven and Earth within the Six Harmonies (*Liùhé*),
together harmonizing so that there is no illness or suffering.
I wish to hear, within the vast and distant six poles between Heaven and Earth,
what is the most good?
Within the thirty-six thousand Heavens and Earths,
longevity (*Shòu*) is the most good.
Therefore, Heaven (*Tiān*) is first,
Earth (*Dì*) is next,
*Shénrén* are next,
*Zhēnrén* are next,
*Xiānrén* are next,
*Dàorén* are next,
*Shèngrén* are next,
and *Xiánrén* are next.
These eight
all align with the heart of August Heaven (*Huángtiān*),
sharing its intent and combining their strength;
these are all Heavenly People (*Tiānrén*).
They are those whom Heaven wishes to employ in service;
within Heaven, each is appointed to an office,
therefore their thoughts and concerns are always similar,
and these are the people whom Heaven loves and nourishes.
Heaven
greatly desires longevity and eternal life;
Immortals (*Xiānrén*) also desire longevity
and also desire life;
those who desire life do not dare to do wrong,
each planning for their own self.
The Liùfāng Zhēnrén Chún and others respectfully bow and speak:
"We wish to ask regarding the laws of Heaven,
but we do not dare to speak abruptly.
Only if the Huángtiān Shī opens the gateway
and allows us to voice our words?"
"Speak of it,
and have no doubts."
"Yes, yes.
Now, only the Tiānshī can resolve for the Sovereign the inherited calamities of his ancestors,
and establish below that which can make a ruler flourish,
while completely removing all types of disasters, strange occurrences, transformations, and inauspicious things in the world.
Now, we humble students wish to assist Heaven,
so that the Qì of Tàiyáng may remain brilliant,
the Sovereign may flourish daily,
the treacherous and cunning may be exterminated,
evil people may not act,
robbers and thieves may be cut off and disappear,
and ominous portents may hide themselves
and never emerge again.
May we hear of this?"
"Excellent
is the question of the six disciples;
Heaven allows the Zhēnrén to speak.
Granted. The Jūnzǐ is already without worry,
and the base people and ominous ministers do not dare to act.
The means of overcoming them has already appeared,
and the disasters will naturally be extinguished and subside.
Now, I will detail the Tiāngé laws for all the disciples,
ensuring they do not deviate by even a tiny fraction.
Follow along and record it."
"Yes, yes."
"Indeed,
the laws of Heaven manifest as signs,
and the Sages of high antiquity always modeled themselves after them
and did not dare to depart from them.
Therefore, they always suppressed the inauspicious,
cut off the crafty and cunning,
and prevented ominous ministers from acting.
All of this was done by following the laws of Heaven.
If you wish the Yáng Qì to flourish daily,
for the Fire to be greatly brilliant,
and never to know a time of decline,
you must urgently cut off the source of Metal Qì
and not let it become dominant.
When Metal Qì is cut off,
then Wood Qì can become dominant,
Fire Qì will be greatly brilliant,
and there will be no time of decline."
"What does this mean?"
"Indeed,
the Sovereign should urgently abolish weapons.
Weapons
belong to the category of Metal;
this is why they must be urgently abolished.
Nowadays, on the contrary, rulers frequently grant their ministers knives and weapons.
Weapons are of the Metal category,
yet the Sovereign grants them as dominant things.
The name of this dominance is 'Metal Dominance.'
When Metal is dominant, it suppresses Wood and causes Fire to decline.
When Metal is dominant, it causes the Jiǎ and Yǐ Wood phases to have no Qì.
When Wood's Yǐ Qì is cut off,
then Fire is not brilliant.
When Wood is dominant, Earth cannot be produced.
When Fire is not brilliant, then Earth Qì flourishes daily,
the Earth Qì moves frequently,
and there are ominous signs;
therefore, they should be urgently abolished and exterminated.
Do not grant metal items or weapons to the soldiers,
in order to suppress and cut off the inauspicious in this way."
"Heaven's suppression is truly no different from the spirits.
We wish to hear: if Metal flourishing suppresses Wood,
why does it conversely cause Fire to decline?"
"Excellent
is your difficult question;
it can be said you have entered the Dào.
The Zhēnrén wish to joyfully know its great effects.
Therefore, if in Spring one follows by raising Metal weapons,
then one injures the Jiǎ and Yǐ Wood phases.
This makes the Celestial Qīng Dì unhappy
and the Celestial Chì Dì greatly enraged,
and Bǐng, Dīng, Sì, and Wǔ become non-compliant.
Wishing to avenge the resentment of their parents,
they cause the Fire phase
to have many disasters and strange transformations,
producing inauspiciousness, ominous harms, and treacherous cunning.
This law conversely causes the Fire's governance to be confused and chaotic;
it is unacceptable.
The great calamity lies here."
"Excellent, excellent!
We wish to hear why there must be many ominous people and ministers, and crafty thieves?"
"I shall explain it again for the Zhēnrén,
to let you know it clearly.
According to the Tiāngé laws,
when parents are harmed,
the children must avenge the resentment.
In a family that seeks revenge,
inauspiciousness will surely gather.
False flatterers, crafty ones, and youths capable of lawlessness
are the ones who can avenge resentment and commit rebellion.
Therefore, by granting Metal weapons
and suppressing and injuring Wood,
the governance of Fire cannot be peaceful.
This
is the constant Tiāngé law;
it cannot be altered by human will.
If the six Zhēnrén do not believe my words,
just urgently abolish Metal weapons.
If anyone dares to hold them,
they shall all be heavily punished.
Then immediately, fire disasters will be extinguished and removed,
and governance will instantly become peaceful.
Everyone under heaven will say, 'Excellent!'
The reason for this is that
Fire corresponds to the Sovereign;
therefore its transformations and abnormalities are the most severe.
The other four phases cannot compare.
If you wish to further know its clear effects,
of the Five Stars, Yínghuò
produces the most severe abnormalities;
this is the clear proof.
The other four stars cannot compare.
You should cherish my books and my writings;
the laws of Heaven do not err by a tiny fraction."
"Yes, yes."
"Proceed.
I shall further clarify and detail the laws of Heaven for the six disciples.
Therefore, if Metal Qì is completely exterminated and cut off,
then Wood Qì will become greatly dominant.
Below, it suppresses the position of Earth,
and Yellow Qì cannot rise.
Thus, in Spring, Wood is dominant and Earth is dead.
Therefore, in Spring, Heaven forcefully cuts off Metal Qì at Wù,
so Wood can succeed in raising Fire Qì,
which then becomes brilliant and flourishing.
Then Metal Qì is imprisoned,
and crafty people are cut off.
When Metal is imprisoned, then Water Qì rests.
Yīn does not dare to harm Yáng, which then generates below.
Be careful that there are no disasters or changes.
When Wood Qì is dominant without Metal,
it can flourish and take charge,
and Earth Qì dies.
The people and ministers born will be loyal, cautious, and trustworthy,
not daring to do wrong.
This is the contract and document of the Tiāngé laws.
This is the constant nature and constant movement of Heaven and Earth.
Do you understand it?"
"Yes, yes."
"Proceed,
you already know it.
Now I will again clarify the laws of Heaven for the six disciples
to make □□.
Today, the world follows weapons,
which is Metal Qì.
Furthermore, rulers sometimes grant knives and weapons at the beginning of the year,
or when they travel and reside in the four directions,
they conversely grant Metal weapons.
The ruler
is the dominant one.
By granting Metal weapons to people,
it is called 'Dominant Metal.'
When Metal is dominant, then Water is the assistant.
When Metal is dominant, it harms Wood;
when Water is the assistant, it harms Fire.
The Northwest
is Yīn;
the Southeast
is Yáng.
Shǎoyīn becomes dominant,
and Tàiyīn becomes the assistant.
These are called the two Qìs;
together they overcome their Yáng.
Calamities are produced below,
the crafty do wrong,
and when Yīn Qì moves, there is much wild talk and thieves arise.
This is the Tiāngé law.
Do the six disciples understand?"
"Yes, yes."
"Indeed,
the six Zhēnrén already know it.
Revere the laws of Heaven."
"Yes, yes.
Now we wish to ask: the Southeast
is Yáng;
why is it the Dì Hù?
Now, the Northwest
is Yīn;
why is it conversely the Tiān Mén?"
"Indeed,
gates and doors
are where the Qì of Heaven and Earth is first born
and where all things exit and enter.
Therefore, the Southeast
is the extremity of Yáng.
At the extremity of Yáng, Yīn is born;
therefore, the Southeast is the Dì Hù.
The Northwest is the extremity of Yīn.
At the extremity of Yīn, Yáng is born;
therefore, it is the Tiān Mén.
If the Zhēnrén wish to know the effect,"
If the initial Nine arises at Jiǎzǐ,
and the initial Six arises at Jiǎwǔ,
this is what it means.
Therefore, the Way of Heaven is like a cycle;
that which completes its circuit returns again to the beginning,
and how could there be an end?
When the King gains the opportunity to act,
the subtle Qi follows and arises accordingly."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"I shall again explain one matter in detail for the Liù Zhēnrén.
When a King mobilizes a great army,
he causes the Wood Element to be greatly terrified and lose its Qi,
then Earth gains dominance and arises.
When Earth gains dominance, then Metal becomes greatly assisted;
when Metal is greatly assisted, it causes weapons and armor to be frequently moved.
The Qi of Qián and Duì arises,
and the Yídí and cunning thieves of the northwest frequently arise;
this is the law of nature.
The divine spirits of Heaven and Earth
cannot forbid it.
Therefore, the urgent task is to suppress and cut off Metal objects
and not allow them to flourish and circulate."
"Excellent, excellent!
Having seen the Shī explain the laws of Heaven,
I know they are to be feared."
"If you know to fear them, then there will be good fortune."
"Now the Brilliant Master of August Heaven fortunately pities my ignorance and delusion,
and my lack of understanding of the Dào,
so he has detailed the laws of Heaven for me clearly.
Now, are these for a single ruler alone?
Are the laws of the world
all like this?"
"Indeed,
Heaven takes this as the permanent standard law.
Nevertheless,
the Wood Element and Fire Element
do not arise recklessly;
Jīnyuè causes currency to frequently gain dominance and thieves to circulate,
creating a great harm
and making governance difficult to pacify.
On the contrary, it causes the Metal Qi to gain great dominance,
becoming extremely harmful.
If one can respond to my heavenly laws
and cut it off, there will be immediate good fortune.
Governance will flourish,
ominous ministers will be eliminated,
for the laws of Heaven do not deceive people."
"I wish to hear the essential secret of why Heaven takes this as the standard law."
"Indeed,
how detailed
is the questioning by the Liù Zǐ.
Truly, Heaven and Earth take the East to be Shàoyáng,
where the ruler first arises,
therefore the sun rises in the East.
They take the South to be Tàiyáng;
Tàiyáng
is the ruler,
therefore Lí is the sun,
and the sun is the ruler;
the South
is Fire,
and Fire is the ruler;
the South is Summer,
and Summer is the time among the four seasons of greatest nurturing and growth,
the place where gestation and flourishing reach their peak;
its virtue is the greatest,
therefore it is the ruler;
such is the standard law.
Nevertheless,
the sound that is Jué
is unified with the East;
the position that is Fire
is unified with the South.
Now that the Qi of Tàipíng has arrived in abundance,
Heaven ought to raise the Yang Qi,
so when I see the Liù Zhēnrén questioning matters,
I know it is Heaven that causes it.
Therefore, I have explained in detail for the Liù Zhēnrén the method for the circulation of the Tàiyáng ruler;
may the Zhēnrén be cautious."
"Yes, indeed."
"Today the Tiānshī has painstakingly and compassionately set forth the Heavenly Laws in full for this humble student,
and I wish to ask one more thing.
When a Dìwáng grants an audience to his ministers,
down to the common people.
According to the Heavenly Law,
being the father and mother of the people,
when he sees his ministers,
they are the worthy sons of the King,
and thus help the King govern Heaven and Earth.
As for the common people,
they are the King's unworthy sons who reside at home,
primarily managing the fields and livelihoods for the King.
When meeting them,
there should certainly be something to bestow upon them;
if nothing is bestowed, then grace and love do not descend to the people and ministers,
leaving the 'infants' with nothing of the Dào to recite.
What should be done about this?"
"Excellent!
These are the words of a Zhēnrén.
Indeed, when meeting the worthy, bestow upon them written texts;
when meeting the hungry, bestow upon them food;
when meeting the cold, bestow upon them clothes."
"For what reason are the worthy bestowed with written texts?"
"The reason for bestowing written texts is that
patterns are born in the East
and made manifest in the South.
Thus, heavenly patterns are born in the Northeast,
and thus script emerges from the Northeast,
and Heaven reveals its images.
The tiger has patterns,
and its home is in Yín;
the dragon has patterns,
and its home is in Chén;
they carry these and ascend to Heaven,
and the hexagram Lí constitutes elegant patterns moving in the South.
Therefore, the Sānguāng form patterns,
and the Rì is the greatest brilliance.
Thus, patterns are born in the East
and flourish in the South.
Thus, the Rì rises in the East
and flourishes in the southern regions.
Heaven mandates the Dìwáng,
who should take Heaven as his model and law.
Therefore, he should bestow written texts to bring about prosperity.
Tàiyáng
is the movement of Fire.
When the Rì rises,
Fire can distinguish and perceive the right and wrong in written patterns;
texts are also that which records the right and wrong of the world."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Go forth,
for the Liù Zhēnrén have already attained great awakening to the Tiāndào."
"Now the Illustrious Master of August Heaven has provided the complete Dào and laws for Heaven.
Since nothing is left obscure,
I wish to hear what kind of texts should be bestowed?"
"How detailed!
The six of you ask about matters on behalf of Heaven.
Indeed, it should be like this.
In all matters, there is often the hardship of not being [blank],
yet for those who delight in modeling themselves after Heavenly Laws
and wish to swiftly attain Tàipíng,
they should simply gather the authentic scripts and documents of the Dào from high, middle, and late antiquity,
collect the most virtuous among them to create a Tiānjīng,
and bestow it upon the various worthies,
causing each to distinguish and recite it.
Now, considering the essential meanings of ancient and modern times,
and the great righteousness for transforming the people and ministers,
what should be done?
Thereby allowing each to nourish their nature
and secure their person.
If it is so,
none of the Great Worthies or Rú will fail to be pleased.
Having no ill intent,
each will only contemplate and know the laws of Heaven and Earth.
This will then cause people to honor and love their Lord above,
and also cherish their own bodies,
deeply knowing that an enlightened Lord is rare and precious.
Among them, the great worthies and humane ones
will constantly fear their Lord’s aging,
and will separately seek out remedies from extraordinary and remote regions,
and present them back to their Dìwáng.
Therefore, one should bestow the writings of Dàoist texts."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"You have already understood it.
Nowadays, some act carelessly,
bestowing weapons, armor, and metal objects.
Those who receive them return and each thinks of profit,
which leads to the rise of martial spirit above,
which flows down and transforms the simple commoners.
This then causes profit-seeking to arise,
weaponry to flourish and Metal to become dominant;
craftiness emerges,
bandits arise,
and Metal takes charge of affairs.
Its harmfulness injures the phase of Wood
and disrupts the spirit of Fire.
This is the natural pattern and law of Heaven.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, yes.
I wish to ask, why not bestow other written scriptures and books?"
"Indeed,
other books are not texts of the Correct Dào;
they cause the worthies and Rú to become deeply deluded,
providing no benefit to government affairs,
and not nourishing their nature.
Such scriptures and books are superficial and shallow,
yet the worthies and Rú recite them daily;
therefore, they should not be given to them.
However, one may equally gather the virtuous parts of the sacred scriptures of high antiquity,
the virtuous parts of the sacred scriptures of middle antiquity,
and the virtuous parts of the sacred scriptures of late antiquity,
using them as texts to be bestowed.
But I fear they are not the Dào of nourishing nature,
causing people not to respect themselves,
and instead becoming preoccupied with mere writing.
Nevertheless, all texts that are virtuous
can be bestowed,
causing them to recite and practice by modeling themselves after them,
so that they may be transformed into the virtuous."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"The Liù Zhēnrén have already realized it."
"Today the Tiānshī has fortunately spoken to me, your humble student,
and I wish to ask about the meaning of bestowing food upon the hungry
and clothing upon those who are cold.
Now, those who are hungry think of food,
and those who are cold think of clothing.
Once this inner knot is resolved,
they will think of their sovereign
and will not forget him even until they are old.
They will think of dedicating themselves and exhausting their efforts,
not daring to have a divided heart.
When kindness and love permeate the common people,
if they should obtain any extraordinary or unusual texts on the good Dào from distant lands,
they would not dare to hide them.
They will think only of presenting them to their lord
to grant him a long life.
Therefore, one should bestow these upon them;
this is called 'providing for the destitute and rescuing those in urgent need.'
A worthy person loves texts,
a hungry person loves food,
and a cold person loves clothing.
When a ruler of men bestows gifts upon his subjects,
he must strive to ensure each obtains what they desire;
then the whole world will be satisfied and submissive."
"Excellent, excellent!
For this reason, the Tiānxìng (heavenly nature) values Dào and Dé above and places Xíngfá (punishments) below.
Thus, the East represents the Dào,
and the South represents Dé.
The Dào governs birth;
therefore, all things are born in the East.
Dé governs nourishment;
therefore, all things are nourished in the South.
According to the Géfǎ (standard laws) of Heaven,
all things return to Dào and Dé.
Thus, the myriad things all emerge from the Southeast and move upward,
and the six Yáng Qi of the four directions of Heaven and Earth together produce life at the hours of Chén and Sì.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, yes.
The laws of Heaven place Xíng (punishment) below;
therefore, the Northwest is Shǎoyīn,
and Tàiyīn represents Xínghuò (punishment and disaster).
Xínghuò
governs injury and killing.
Thus, things are injured, grow old, and decay in the West
and die in the North.
The Qi of Heaven is in conflict,
and the six Yīn are without Yáng;
things all hide away in inner burrows,
fearing Xíng and the rising of Huò,
not daring to come out and be seen.
The Tiāndào (Way of Heaven) loathes the low;
therefore, the livestock
all eat what is foul and discarded.
For this reason, the Shèngnrén (sages) of antiquity observed the clarity of Heaven's laws;
thus they honored the Zhēndào (True Way), Shàndé (Good Virtue), and extraordinary texts, while placing Wǔ (military force) below.
This is a clear effect.
Nowadays, Xínghuò and Wǔ arise from the Northwest, yet people honor them;
this is called Yīn overriding Yáng,
and the lowly overriding the noble.
This results in many battles and conflicts.
It causes the people and ministers to be disloyal
and is of no benefit to the King's governance.
Is such an administration not difficult?
Does the Zhēnrén perhaps know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"You may be said to have awakened.
Thus, the Shèngxián (sages and worthies) of antiquity always honored Dào, Dé, and texts,
and they always placed them in the highest and most virtuous positions,
while weapons and war preparations were placed in low positions.
When a person lived alone,
they would place texts upon the bed
and weapons beneath the bed.
In this way, the Yídí (barbarians) would naturally surrender
and thieves would daily vanish."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Proceed;
you may be said to already know this.
You six disciples must carefully reflect on the meaning of my writings
to present them to a sovereign who values Dào and Dé
and to show them to the various worthies.
My words do not fail Heaven, Earth, or the wise and virtuous.
You may go;
my discourse has slightly concluded.
If there are other matters of doubt,
then return to ask about them."
"Yes, yes.
Now the six Zhēnrén have received the strict teachings of the Tiānshī;
we will respectfully return each to our secluded places
to contemplate the Tiānshī’s words.
However, we all have something we do not understand;
we ask the Tiānshī to reveal the secret to us."
"Speak, what is it?"
"Now, Heaven naturally has the Qi of the four seasons,
and Earth naturally has the positions of the Wǔxíng (Five Elements).
Their Wáng (Prosperity),
Xiāng (Assisting), Xiū (Resting),
Qiú (Imprisoned), and Fèi (Exhausted) states have their own times.
Now it is only that humans rise up and use them.
How can this cause their Shēngqì (Life-giving Qi)
and their Wáng and Xiāng states to mutually conquer and harm one another?"
"How preposterous!
Alas! Although you six have studied daily,
it has been of no benefit.
Instead, you have become even more foolish,
almost like ignorant people.
Why is this?
As for the laws of Heaven and Earth,
the flourishing and decline of the myriad things actually follow human actions.
In whatever matters people act together,
and whichever things they value and use,
these all become Wáng and Shēngqì.
What people leave to Xiū and Fèi
all declines and becomes Qiú.
Therefore, that which is promoted by human action
becomes the sovereign, leader, or teacher of men.
The things that people compete to use
all become noble and without equal.
The things that people leave to Xiū and Fèi
all become lowly and without market value.
Thus, whatever people in the world promote and use
naturally becomes Wáng and Shēngqì;
it does not necessarily require the Qi of the four seasons or the Wǔxíng.
Therefore, in the law of Heaven,
the rise and fall of humans
is the rise and fall of the myriad things.
Nobility and lowliness depend entirely on humans.
Thus, the Shèngnrén of antiquity knew the Géfǎ of Heaven
and dared not recklessly violate it.
In High Antiquity, people
deeply knew the venerable Dào,
used the Dào,
and promoted the Dào;
thus, at that time, the Dào was Wáng.
In Middle Antiquity, it was discarded and not practiced,
so the Dào became Xiū and Qiú
and was no longer seen as noble.
In Middle Antiquity, when they promoted and used Dé,
then Dé was Wáng.
In Late Antiquity, they discarded supreme Dé,
and so Dé again became Xiū and Qiú.
Thus, if humans promote and use texts, then texts are Wáng.
If they promote and use Wǔ, then Wǔ is Wáng.
If they promote and use money, then money is Wáng.
If they promote and use wealth and goods, then wealth and goods are Wáng.
Whatever the people of the world promote and use
naturally becomes Wáng and Shēngqì.
That which they together discard and do not use
all becomes common material.
Why must one wait for the Wáng state of Heaven's four seasons and Wǔxíng before it becomes Wáng?
Why does your study not become clearer daily,
but instead becomes increasingly dark and ignorant daily?
If even a Zhēnrén's focus is like this,
then the fact that common people together violate Heaven's prohibitions
and say it is not so
is truly to be expected.
Judging by your case,
human ignorance has indeed lasted long.
If the Zhēnrén’s words were correct, such as my explaining the laws for Heaven
or resolving the Chéngfù (inherited burden) of disasters flowing from previous kings for a virtuous ruler—
would there be errors that make them unusable for people?
If there were errors,
how could they be put into practice?
If you six have doubts
and wish to know the great efficacy of my Dào,
to know whether it is truly true or not,
quickly present it to a wise and enlightened sovereign of Dào and Dé.
Let him put it into practice,
and it will immediately resonate like an echo with Heaven and Earth.
This is the clear effect and proof for that person.
If even you Zhēnrén still cannot deeply understand
that humans can cause things to flourish or decline, advance or retreat,
then compared to you,
how are the common people in their darkness any different from the blind?"
"Now that we have seen the Tiānshī explain it for us, your humble students,
we have understood.
Do we have any faults?"
"Once a person has studied,
they should strive to reflect upon the essential meaning
and not merely practice the words.
To know the words but not the secret meaning
is something resented by Heaven, Earth, and the Dào.
Let the students be refined and cautious in this."
"Yes, yes."
"Go now;
remember these matters of Heaven's governance.
They can suppress the cunning and the ominous.
Do not let a virtuous sovereign lose these texts on governance."
"Yes, yes."
"I am greatly ignorant and have things I do not understand every day.
This life in darkness bows and prostrates twice,
to ask about one great doubt."
"What is it?"
"The books frequently say that the Shàng Huáng Qì of Heaven is about to descend,
yet until now I do not know what this Shàng Huáng Qì is."
"That you would deeply doubt this
can be called having attained the intent of the Dào.
Listen clearly,
and I shall describe it in detail for the Zhēnrén.
Heaven has Sān Huáng,
Earth has Sān Huáng,
Man has Sān Huáng;
Heaven has Wǔ Dì,
Earth has Wǔ Dì,
Man has Wǔ Dì;
Heaven has Sān Wáng,
Earth has Sān Wáng,
Man has Sān Wáng;
Heaven has Wǔ Bà,
Earth has Wǔ Bà,
Man has Wǔ Bà."
"What does this mean?"
"Heaven's Sān Huáng are like the Sān Guāng,
Earth's Sān Huáng are like the high, low, and level,
and Man's Sān Huáng
are like the ruler, ministers, and people.
Heaven's Wǔ Dì are like the Wǔ Xīng,
Earth's Wǔ Dì are like the Wǔ Yuè,
and Man's Wǔ Dì are like the Wǔ Xíng and Wǔ Zàng.
Heaven's Sān Wáng are like the Sān Guāng,
Earth's Sān Wáng are like the high, low, and level,
and Man's Sān Wáng are like the ruler, ministers, and people.
Heaven's Wǔ Bà are like the Wǔ Xīng,
Earth's Wǔ Bà are like the Wǔ Yuè,
and Man's Wǔ Bà are like the Wǔ Xíng and Wǔ Zàng."
"Tiān Shī, please have pity on this ignorant student,
and since I cannot help but ask,
show me the Tiān Fǎ.
I wish to hear how their superior and inferior qualities compare."
"Excellent!
Your difficult question
can be called attaining the intent of Heaven
and entering the Heart of Heaven;
it may remain bound and attached for ten thousand generations without departing.
Now, of the Sān Huáng of Heaven,
the superior ones are like the Sun,
the middle ones are like the Moon,
and the inferior ones are like the Stars;
their superior and inferior qualities are as far apart as this.
Of the Sān Huáng of Earth,
the superior ones are like the Wǔ Yuè,
the middle ones are like level ground,
and the inferior ones are like low fields;
their superior and inferior qualities are as far apart as this.
Of the Sān Huáng of Man,
the superior ones are like the ruler,
the middle ones are like the ministers,
and the inferior ones are like the people;
their superior and inferior qualities are as far apart as this.
Of the Wǔ Dì of Heaven,
the superior ones
are like three parts
out of four of the Sun;
the middle ones
are like three parts
out of four of the Moon;
the inferior ones
are like three parts
out of four of the Stars.
Of the Wǔ Dì of Earth,
the superior ones
are like three parts
out of four of the Wǔ Yuè;
the middle ones
are like three parts
out of four of level ground;
the inferior ones
are like three parts
out of four of low fields.
Of the Wǔ Dì of Man,
the superior ones
are like three parts
out of four of a great state;
the middle ones
are like three parts
out of four of a great minister;
the inferior ones
are like three parts
out of four of the people.
Of the Sān Wáng of Heaven,
the superior ones
are like two parts
out of four of the Sun;
the middle ones
are like two parts
out of four of the Moon;
the inferior ones
are like two parts
out of four of the great stars.
Of the Sān Wáng of Earth,
the superior ones
are like two parts
out of four of the Wǔ Yuè;
the middle ones
are like two parts
out of four of level ground;
the inferior ones
are like two parts
out of four of low fields.
Of the Sān Wáng of Man,
the superior ones
are like two parts
out of four of a great state;
the middle ones
are like two parts
out of four of a great minister;
the inferior ones
are like two parts
out of four of the people.
Of the Wǔ Bà of Heaven,
the superior ones
are like one part
out of four of the Sun;
the middle ones
are like one part
out of four of the Moon;
the inferior ones
are like one part
out of four of the great stars.
Of the Wǔ Bà of Earth,
the superior ones
are like one part
out of four of the Wǔ Yuè;
the middle ones
are like one part
out of four of level ground;
the inferior ones
are like one part
out of four of low fields.
Of the Wǔ Bà of Man,
the superior ones
are like one part
out of four of a great state;
the middle ones
are like one part
out of four of a great minister;
the inferior ones
are like one part
out of four of the people.
Thus the Tiān Dào is not far;
the three and five each return to themselves.
Therefore, Heaven has Sān Huáng and Wǔ Dì,
Sān Wáng and Wǔ Bà;
Earth also has its own Sān Huáng and Wǔ Dì,
Sān Wáng and Wǔ Bà;
and Man also has his own Sān Huáng and Wǔ Dì,
Sān Wáng and Wǔ Bà."
"Why is there such variety in degree?
I wish for the Tiān Shī to resolve the secret meaning."
"Indeed.
Heaven, Earth, and Man are originally the same Yuán Qì,
divided into three bodies,
each having its own ancestral beginning.
Thus, the Sān Huáng
are the ancestral head;
the Wǔ Dì
are the sovereigns of the middle restoration;
the Sān Wáng
are the mediocre sovereigns;
and the Wǔ Bà
are the final, exhausted, inferior, and declining
qi of rising punishments, danger, and disorder.
Therefore, when arriving at the Wǔ Bà,
they only possess one part out of four,
and the lineage of the Tiān Dào is nearly severed.
Below this level,
it is so faint and small that things can no longer restrain or control each other;
it is like the extremely weak being unable to control the strong,
the soft being unable to control the hard,
and the few being unable to control the many.
The Dào is about to fall into great chaos
and can no longer be ordered.
Therefore, it must begin again from the higher levels."
"What does this mean?"
"Indeed.
The Jiǔ Huáng
all begin to sprout in the North;
the Wǔ Dì begin to be born in the East;
the Sān Wáng flourish in the South;
and the Wǔ Bà are harvested and completed in the West.
When Heaven gives life to all things,
the Yáng Qì follows the Yuán Qì,
sprouting from the union with Tài Yīn.
When life is to emerge and reach out,
it flourishes and is born in the East;
once born, it must become lush and grand,
thus it is most vigorous in the South;
once lush and grand, it must bear fruit and be completed,
thus it is harvested and completed in the West."
The Way of Heaven and Earth, Yin and Yang, is all-encompassing.
If things could not reach fulfillment,
they would simply die;
but since roots and seeds must be born again,
it causes Yin and Yang to act together,
entering the Tiānmén together,
merging their Qi at Qián,
and starting anew from the beginning above.
This is the natural disposition of Heaven and Earth."
"Excellent, excellent!
Why do Heaven, Earth, and Man not share the Sānhuáng, Wǔdì, Sānwáng, and Wǔbà?"
"Excellent,
it is rare for you to grasp this meaning.
Heaven, Earth, and Man are divided into three houses,
each in a different place.
The way of the Huáng
is like a family having a father;
the way of the Dì
is like a family having a mother;
the way of the Wáng
is like a family having a son;
the way of the Bà
is like a family having a daughter-in-law.
Now these three houses are in different places;
how could they share the same father, mother, son, and daughter-in-law?
If people were divided into three houses,
could they share a father, mother, son, and daughter-in-law?
Does the Zhēnrén understand?"
"Yes, yes."
"Be careful with this,
and do not recklessly or wrongly question it.
The Way of Heaven has its own fixed standards and laws;
one cannot simply oppose it with force.
I dare not fail to exert my efforts."
"Yes, yes.
Although I ask about these matters every time,
thereby violating the taboo name of the Tiānshī,
if I do not ask, I have no way of knowing them.
I wish to beg for one more word."
"Proceed."
"Currently there are forty-eight divisions;
what are the actions of these forty-eight divisions like?"
"How excellent and detailed
your inquiry is!
Those whose actions attain the Tiānxīn
will not have disasters or anomalies arise.
Those who lose the essential Way of Heaven
will have unending disasters and anomalies.
Thus, across tens of thousands of generations, past and future,
they transmit the Chéngfù to one another.
One who is good at being a ruler
can cause disasters and faults to subside on their own
and dissolve what has been lost.
As for those who reach the essential Way of self-cultivation,
they instead allow evil Qi to circulate
and spread throughout the world.
Thus these remaining disasters are born,
and instead become the convergence of the distress of Chéngfù."
"What does this mean?"
"It is so;
listen carefully to my words."
"Yes, yes."
"In Heaven, the superior ruler is like the sun,
the middle one like the moon,
and the lower one like the stars.
On Earth, the superior ruler is like the Wǔyuè,
the middle one like level ground,
and the lower one like low-lying fields.
Among men, the superior ruler is like the sovereign,
the middle one like the minister,
and the lower one like the common people.
For those who possess wholeness,
their people and the myriad things
are all without illness and at peace;
there are no thieves, deceivers, or flatterers.
Heaven and Earth have no disasters or anomalies;
this is called the 'Superior Excellence,'
possessing wholeness.
For those who possess three parts out of four,
three parts of the people are peaceful, good, loyal, and trustworthy;
one part suffers injury or death,
or becomes thieves,
together creating evil anomalies and strange occurrences,
the amount of which follows this one-fourth.
For those who possess two parts out of four,
half of the people and the myriad things are ill
and untrustworthy;
half the people have deceitful hearts,
and the strange anomalies of Heaven are half.
For those who possess one part out of four,
three parts are entirely ill,
without honesty, being deceitful and flattering;
all are thieves,
without any heart for mutual benefit;
only one part is good."
"Heavenly anomalies continue without end,
appearing here and there,
and will not leave the boundaries of those divisions.
What is the reason for this?"
"Excellent
is your question.
To cause one to have everything,
their Virtue and the Way must reach everywhere.
Where Virtue reaches, it can control things;
thus it perfects the myriad things,
and all receive its Virtue and Way;
therefore all is level and peaceful.
For those who possess three parts out of four,
their Virtue and Way do not reach one part;
therefore that one part is unlucky.
For those who possess two parts out of four,
half of their Virtue and Way fails to cover everything;
therefore half is unlucky.
For those who possess one part out of four,
their Virtue is meager,
reaching only one part
and not the other three parts;
therefore three parts are unlucky.
Thus ancient Shèngrén, emperors, and kings, wishing to know their own quality,
used this to divine it,
and not one in ten thousand failed.
Regarding where it does not reach,
why is there illness?
When the Way and Virtue cannot reach,
there is no non-action and no ruler;
because the myriad things have no leader, they fall into chaos,
and there is much illness, craftiness, and villainy,
and thieves do not cease.
The ancients used this to divine their governance,
to know the thickness or thinness of their Virtue,
observing with which things their Qi corresponded.
By this they deeply knew the success, failure, decline, or prosperity of their governance,
as clearly as the sun and moon."
"Excellent, excellent!
How can one save them from these failures?"
"Excellent;
since the Zhēnrén now knows the Tiānjīng,
you should stop these spreading disasters and the Chéngfù of the myriad things."
"By what means are the disasters stopped?
May the Tiānshī teach the assembly of worthies,
so they may attain the Qi of the Shànghuáng."
"Indeed,
each should discuss the True Way to its conclusion
and each should contemplate the Chūyī to govern their own toil and illness;
then they will return to excellence,
and everything will be possessed."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Proceed,
let the Zhēnrén take heed of these matters."
"Yes, yes.
I have respectfully received the precepts of the forty-eight divisions.
What is the length of their practice of the Way?"
"How detailed is your question.
I dare not be otherwise than detailed;
the Way of Heaven is extremely weighty,
and the Master's instructions are extremely strict;
therefore I dare to ask about them one by one."
"Excellent,
knowing the conduct of a disciple
can help one understand the intent of the Way of Heaven.
Now, the Way of Heaven has three aspects,
corresponding to Tàiyáng, Tàiyīn, and Zhōnghé.
Those of excellence travel the outside;
the next travel the middle;
the next travel the inside.
The Bà have no Way;
they merely borrow the path. The inner way of the Sānwáng is the shortest.
The Tiānhuáng of great excellence travels the furthest outside.
The Jiǔhuáng share one way in sequence;
the inferior are on the inside.
Those of excellence walk without shifting;
the next shift slightly;
the next perceive slightly.
The fifteen Dì share one middle way.
Those of excellence travel the outside;
the next travel and perceive;
the inferior travel and are hurried.
The nine men of the Sānwáng
share one inner way and travel on horseback;
the next are slightly hurried;
the inferior gallop.
The fifteen Bà mostly borrow the innermost, extreme path;
those of excellence are as if flying outside;
those in the middle are as if flying and hurried;
the inferior are like an arrow.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Excellent, excellent!
Come forward, Zhēnrén;
you asked about this matter;
why are you so detailed?"
"Indeed,
since my birth,
I have wondered why years are sometimes long and sometimes short,
why the sun is sometimes thick
and sometimes thin,
sometimes forward and sometimes backward.
If I do not ask the Tiānshī,
I fear I will never know;
I wish to hear its meaning."
"Excellent."
These are your words.
Now, those that are substantial
are the days of Tiān;
the next in substance
are the days of Dì;
the next in substance
are the days of Rén;
and those that are the most thin
are the days of the Wànwù.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Go now;
do not inquire further to the end.
This matter
is your private concern;
it is not that it is difficult for me to explain it to you exhaustively.
The world will have no use for it,
nor is it of benefit to the Dìwáng regarding the calamities of chéngfù,
or the sorrow and suffering of the Bǎixìng;
therefore I do not distinguish and speak of it for you,
not because I begrudge it."
"Yes, yes.
I have often violated the Tiānshī’s taboos
and have committed a great transgression."
"No need for modesty;
for one who joyfully desires to know the affairs of Tiānshàng
and comes with a private intent,
I shall explain it all for you."
"Yes, yes."
"Go now."
To the right is the method for distinguishing the merits and demerits of the conduct and cycles of the Jiǔhuáng, Shíwǔdì, Jiǔwáng, and Shíwǔbà.
"Before the Zhēnrén,
how many sins do ordinary people have?"
"Ordinary people do not commit offenses;
what sins or transgressions could they have?"
"Alas,
how dim-witted and blind the Zhēnrén is!"
"My humble self is not enlightened;
since birth, I have never heard
that a person can have sins without committing illegal acts."
"What you say is true
and accords with common records.
But you do not see that ordinary people actually have six great sins
that cannot be eliminated.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations.
The Zhēnrén studies,
yet fails to see these obvious sins;
is your study not afflicted by confusion?"
"My humble self was negligent;
I was not troubled by it."
"You are indeed negligent.
Common people die harboring resentment and knots of grievances.
Truly, they are exhausted and ultimately ignorant,
yet they realize it only after death.
Since the opening of Tiāndì,
ordinary people are blind at first and enlightened later;
what principle is there to criticize in this?"
"I wish to hear of them."
"Very well.
When a person accumulates the Dào infinitely
but is unwilling to teach others to open their eyes and seek life,
this sin cannot be eliminated.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations.
The reason for this is
they cut off the Dào of Tiān giving life
and become an enemy to Tiān.
When a person accumulates Dé infinitely
but is unwilling to exert effort to teach others to preserve Dé
and be cautious in nourishing their nature,
this sin cannot be eliminated.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations.
The reason for this is
they cut off the nourishing Dé of Dì
and become an enemy to Dì;
they are a person of great fault.
When someone accumulates hundreds of millions in wealth
but is unwilling to rescue the poor or help those in urgent need,
causing people to die of hunger and cold,
this sin cannot be eliminated.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations.
The reason for this is
that these resources belong to Zhōnghé;
they are what Tiāndì uses to practice benevolence,
circulating them to provide sufficiency for all
so that people are not destitute.
Now, on the contrary, someone hoards them and cuts off the flow,
preventing them from being distributed everywhere,
and becomes an enemy to the harmonious Qì of Tiāndì.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations;
in the end, wealth cannot be hoarded for long
and must be passed on.
Tiān produces people
and causes them to have knowledge,
to love the good and hate the evil.
Fortunately, having knowledge,
if one knows that Tiān has a Dào yet conversely disdains the Dào,
and is unwilling to study it diligently to save oneself;
or though one might attain long life,
which resides in the body inherited from ancestors through Tiān's lineage,
yet one conversely treats oneself lightly
and does not study, merely watching death approach;
then suddenly, when death is near,
one harbors self-resentment,
this sin cannot be eliminated.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations,
causing living beings to be ultimately ignorant
and become enemies to Tiān.
The reason for this is
that Tiān exerts its own strength to practice the Dào;
therefore it is always auspicious,
while losing the Dào leads to calamity and death.
Although Tiān loves people and desires them to enjoy goodness,
and attaches the Dào to the human body,
if a person is unwilling to exert effort for the Dào,
they are called a person without the Dào,
and Tiān has no reason to grant them the Dào and longevity.
This causes the Dào of Tiān to be cut off;
therefore they become an enemy to Tiān.
Man is born knowing that virtue and goodness are right,
yet if they are unwilling to study diligently to practice Dé,
but instead disdain Dé and dislike self-cultivation,
treating themselves lightly and doing wrong,
this sin cannot be eliminated.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations.
The reason for this is
that they are contrary to Dì.
Dì loves Dé and nourishment,
yet this person neglects these matters,
does not find joy in loving Dé,
but only loves their ancestors' physical body,
and thus becomes a fault against Dì.
Tiān produces people
and fortunately grants each person their own physical strength,
with which they can provide their own clothing and food.
But if they are unwilling to exert effort to do so
and instead bring about hunger and cold,
they betray the body of their ancestors.
Lightly resting their strength and doing nothing,
though strength could obtain clothing and food,
they instead constantly complain of sorrow, suffering, hunger, and cold.
They only constantly look up to wealthy families,
depending on them to survive;
this sin cannot be eliminated.
Sometimes the person themselves suffers the consequences;
sometimes they flow down to future generations.
The reason for this is
that Tiāndì produces all resources that can nourish people,
and each should gather them according to their strength,
taking enough to be sufficient without being destitute.
If instead they rest their strength and do not work, treating themselves lightly,
or if what they seek is obtained through discord,
all such acts are like forcibly taking others' things,
becoming an enemy to Zhōnghé;
it is clear that their sin deserves death.
These are the six great sins that Tiān detests;
these sins cannot be eliminated.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes.
I wish to hear from the Tiānshī:
which of these sins is the most serious?"
"Alas!
Why are you becoming more foolish day by day?
These are all sins that destroy the family line.
Why talk about which one is heavier?"
"My humble self is very surprised by this
and does not know the essential meaning.
Now I only ask that the Tiānshī further reveal it,
to bring about a great awakening,
and a deep understanding of its meaning,
so that I dare not commit them again."
"Very well,
what the Zhēnrén says is good.
My words are about to appear;
the Zhēnrén should follow them and exert effort to remember them."
"Yes, yes."
"Very well.
Now Huángtiān possesses the Dào,
and uses it to bring forth all things;
the teeming multitudes
all look up to it for their life-mandate.
Now if a Dàróu Dàorén,
who perhaps deeply understands it in silence,
keeps it stored within their belly
and is unwilling to exert effort to teach others;
teaching people the Dào
is like giving fire to others;
if a few people come to take it,
it does not harm the original flame;
even if infinite people come to take it,
it still does not harm the original flame.
Now, fortunately, it can be shared
to teach the people under Tiānxià,
assisting Tiān in producing life,
assisting Dì in nourishing forms,
assisting Dìwáng in cultivation and correction.
Furthermore, it causes each person to harbor the Dào,
to seek life and loathe death,
causing the governed to assist in governing people,
so they no longer break the law
or commit evil, wicked acts.
Their hearts are good,
then they assist Tiāndì and the Dìwáng in nourishing the twelve thousand things,
and each will enjoy long life.
When people harbor a benevolent heart
and no longer lightly harm or injure the myriad things,
then Tiān will be greatly pleased by it,
Dì will be greatly delighted by it,
and the Dìwáng will find great joy and be without worry.
Would such merit not be immensely great?
If one person teaches and transforms a hundred foolish people,
and those hundred people all return to the Dào,
each teaching ten thousand people,
and those ten thousand all teach others,
then a hundred million people will have been transformed.
If a hundred million all teach,
the teaching will be infinite.
This goodness
above accords with the mind of Tiān,
and below penetrates to the infinite;
there will be no people who do not enjoy life and practice goodness.
The Dìwáng may travel without administrative burden.
How then would it harm anyone
to not exert effort in showing and instructing one another?
Now that people are fortunate enough to receive the instructions and warnings of the former masters,
Having attained and deeply harboring the Zhìdào, yet closing it off and cutting it off,
not using it to teach or demonstrate to others,
causes people to have nowhere to entrust their lives,
all resulting in violent deaths and the accumulation of grievances,
which is called severing the Tiāndào,
so that many people lose the Way and act recklessly.
Heaven also cannot sustain life for long,
and Earth also cannot provide nourishment for long.
Now, if people do not know the Way,
the petty people without the Way often treat themselves lightly,
together committing rebellion and insurrection,
violating Tiānwén and Dìlǐ,
rising as bandits and thieves to harm and wound one another.
They violate the Wángfǎ,
becoming a heavy sorrow for the Jūnzǐ,
with disorders so numerous they cannot be managed.
The Jūnwáng ponders this day and night,
becoming dejected and suffering in self-sorrow,
causing Heaven and Earth to lose their rectitude,
so that disasters and strange anomalies do not cease,
leaving a burden for the Dìwáng,
of which I have not yet been able to speak fully.
Indeed, severing the Tiāndào
is a crime of great rebellion,
too many to be recorded.
Therefore, I merely raise its main principles,
to show the Zhēnrén what is right and wrong;
is it not clear that such a heavy crime deserves death?
Even in death, there are still remaining transgressions,
which is why they flow down to later generations.
How lamentable!
The Zhēnrén should be cautious of this.
Only the Zhēnrén knows this one Hài,
and can be said to have already attained long-lasting auspiciousness
and distanced himself from misfortune and harm."
"Yes, yes,
I do not dare to depart from your instructions."
"Indeed,
you are already worthy and enlightened,
and you know the Tiānmìng.
You will certainly choose life and leave death,
and doubt no more."
"Now I have respectfully heard the mandate regarding the Tiāndào;
I wish to hear the instructions regarding the Dìdé."
"Indeed,
the Earth possesses Dàdé,
solely by following the Tiānzhīdào
and delighting in nourishing the myriad things;
of all the teeming creatures,
none fail to receive its grace and virtue,
being nurtured and completed within it.
Therefore, those of great gentleness and Dàdé
should act in imitation of this.
Fortunately, through the merit and power of former teachers,
they have attained and harbored the infinite virtue of the Shàndào.
Now, using virtue to teach others
is like approaching a great body of water to drink.
If a few people go to learn virtue,
it does not harm its source;
if infinite people go to learn virtue,
it also does not harm its source.
If one teaches them with effort,
making all ordinary people know how to maintain gentleness and embrace virtue,
each will cherish and nourish their own body.
The good ones among them can above assist Heaven in nourishing things that are about to grow,
and below assist Earth in rearing things that are nearing completion,
all uniting their strength and hearts,
with no ill intentions.
Those among them who are greatly worthy and enlightened, whose minds are easily opened,
can then be transformed and elevated
to serve as assistants to the Jūn,
those who are worthy can serve as teachers for high officials,
and those below who are ignorant
can still serve as teachers and leaders among the common people.
There is no one among the common people who does not love transformation through virtue and becoming good.
If teaching is done in this way,
it will above be beneficial to Heaven
and below be beneficial to Earth,
serving as the root of Dàhuà,
assisting the Dìwáng in nourishing the people,
and ensuring they do not commit evil deeds.
The Jūnzǐ can then sit with folded robes and be without worry.
His merit will be manifest and great,
Heaven and Earth will love him,
and he can be transferred to official positions.
Nowadays, some harbor great and vast virtue,
but instead feign ignorance and close it off,
severing the path of Dàodé,
not assisting Heaven in nourishing what is about to grow,
not assisting Earth in nourishing what is about to be completed,
and not assisting the Dìwáng in harmonizing the various people.
Now, this causes the ignorant later generations
to become dark and without knowledge,
unable to distinguish white from black,
dying one after another without changing,
finally becoming petty people,
unable to tell east from west,
neglecting themselves and treating themselves lightly,
following one another in doing wrong,
with villainy and treachery accumulating.
Superiors and inferiors can no longer teach one another,
all is dark and confused,
without any taboos or restraints.
Above, they violate Tiānwén;
below, they violate Dìxíng.
Their actions go against the Sìshí
and disorder the Wǔxíng.
They are a great sorrow for the Jūnzǐ,
they cause harm to the petty people,
they become bandits and thieves,
or ultimately bring about their own ruin,
bringing disgrace upon their parents,
and consequently having no future generations.
For now, I only raise the main principles for the Zhēnrén,
showing its beginning,
to make the masses awaken and urge themselves on.
If one is unwilling to teach long-lasting virtue,
this is called severing the Yǎngdào of Earth,
and such are its crimes.
This is to die a senseless death,
and there are still remaining crimes,
which is why they flow down to later generations.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"How lamentable!
How lamentable!"
"Since the Zhēnrén knows early on to lament,
it can be said that he will obtain life.
Only be cautious of it."
"Yes, yes.
I have respectfully received the prohibitions of Dàodé;
I now wish to hear about the conduct of the Rénzhě."
"Indeed,
all wealth and materials produced by Heaven and Earth
already belong to humanity;
making them rootless,
neither attached to Heaven above
nor attached to Earth below.
Materials
are the possessions of Zhōnghé;
they are meant to be circulated,
floating to and fro,
their function being to provide for the destitute and rescue those in emergencies.
Now, those who accumulate gold, silver, and precious things,
the families of great wealth,
may have hundreds of millions of kinds or more,
accumulating until they rot and decay.
If those who are worthy and wise practice giving to poor families,
they are simply delighting in the name of Rén.
They assist Earth in nourishing forms,
and assist the Dìwáng in preserving good and cautious people.
A family of hundreds of millions
could provide for ten thousand households;
by giving away the old and receiving the new,
without a heart for greedy profit,
their virtue will permeate Heaven and Earth,
and be heard of in distant places.
They can still always obtain new things,
while that which is rotting and decaying is removed.
Among them, the greatly worthy
will have their merit reported daily to the Dìwáng.
Among them, the lesser worthy
will be daily praised in their villages.
Those among the greatly ignorant who do not repay the favor
are at most two or three out of ten;
how could this make one deeply poor?
If one does not stop doing good,
the greatly worthy, gentle, and enlightened will recommend them,
their name will be known throughout the state,
and the number of people across the four seas speaking of them will block the roads.
When enlightened kings and Shèngzhǔ hear of it,
they will be greatly pleased to see assistance in nourishing the people,
and consequently issue an edict to summon them,
raising their position to that of a Dǐngfǔ.
Because of this, they attain honor and nobility,
without end for generations to come.
They are still considered of Dàrén,
rare in the world.
Above, they do not fail their ancestors;
below, they do not fail their descendants.
Heaven and Earth love them,
the hundred spirits benefit them,
the Dìwáng treats them like an enlightened friend,
and neighbors look up to them as parents.
Their merit is manifest in Heaven and Earth
and will never depart;
their emolument is manifest in official positions
and they will never again be lowly;
their name is manifest among the myriad people
and will never be extinguished.
Indeed, can one not practice Rén?
There may be some who happen to obtain good and wealthy lands,
and also obtain the wealth of the Zhōnghé of Heaven and Earth,
accumulating hundreds of millions of kinds,
with precious things, gold, and silver in the hundreds of millions,
but instead they seal it up and hide it away in dark rooms,
causing it all to rot and decay.
When they see the poor and destitute come to ask for help,
they scold them and do not give;
even if they give, they do not grant it immediately,
and they must demand a double return.
And while some merely increase it once,
or perhaps four or five times before stopping,
they give it to the wealthy
and cut off the poor,
causing them to die of hunger and cold.
Not following the proper principles,
they instead turn to mock them.
This creates resentment with Heaven,
blame with Earth,
and great enmity with humanity;
the hundred spirits detest them.
The reason for this is that
these goods and wealth are what exists within the Zhōng Hé of Heaven and Earth,
to be used collectively to nourish humanity.
These families merely happen to encounter the place where it gathers,
like rats in a granary
who always have enough to eat on their own;
the grain in this great granary
originally did not belong to the rats alone.
The wealth in the inner treasury
was originally not intended to be given to only one person.
Those who have insufficient
should all be able to take from it.
Foolish people are ignorant;
they think they should possess it alone forever,
not knowing it is the collected provision for all people,
and all should obtain food and clothing from it.
They cherish it but react with erratic anger and joy,
refusing to use their strength to help the destitute or rescue those in crisis,
causing ten thousand households to be cut off,
with nothing to plant in the spring
and nothing to harvest in the autumn;
their accumulated grievances all cry out to Heaven.
Heaven is moved by this,
and Earth is shaken by it.
By not assisting the Jūnzǐ in helping the destitute and rescuing those in crisis,
they become the most inhumane people between Heaven and Earth.
People may seek it for sacrifices,
yet they still do not give it;
the hundred spirits loathe them
and wish to end their lineage.
The local priests are resolute;
they wish for their death.
When bandits hear of them,
they raise weapons and rush there,
attacking their gates.
The family is distressed and dies until all are gone,
yet they stubbornly refuse to give,
instead burying it deep in the earth
so that people cannot see it.
Without cause, they cut off the world's wealth
and lack the utility of things upon the earth,
instead creating a "great accumulation" beneath the earth.
Heaven greatly detests this,
Earth is greatly pained by it,
and it is considered a great calamity.
As the goods of Zhōng Hé are cut off and daily become fewer,
they sit by as it becomes insufficient,
and those who die of hunger and cold are numerous,
creating heavy enmity with people.
Now, Heaven only loves Dào,
Earth only loves Dé,
and Zhōng Hé loves Rén.
All things have the duty to reside upon the earth and under the heavens,
to circulate and provide for all.
When people have insufficient,
instead it is seen being buried,
sick and suppressed, unable to come out and be seen.
For Heaven and Earth
originally do not take pleasure in wanting wealth for themselves.
Heaven takes pleasure in human life,
and Earth takes pleasure in human nourishment.
Ignorant petty people
instead obstruct the wealth of the Zhōng Hé of Heaven and Earth,
preventing it from being distributed sufficiently,
killing what Heaven has produced
and harming what Earth has nourished.
Without cause, they bury and hide this wealth,
making the state poor
and lacking resources for use,
unable to rescue or preserve the lives of the people.
It causes a ruler of virtue
to have a hollow governance.
Gold, silver, precious items, and goods are for use;
human labor accumulates much,
truly appearing as toil,
and it should be used for the state.
To discard it without cause
takes it away from above and below;
Earth, moreover, does not take pleasure in obtaining it,
considering it a great sickness
and a "great accumulation."
Now, foolish people are exceedingly inhumane;
with crimes such as these,
should they not die?
Among them are those who are suddenly never satisfied,
litigating and complaining of their own grievances,
instead seizing the wealth of the few, the weak, and small families,
truly not knowing how to stop.
I still only see the Zhēnrén in confusion,
just lifting the main thread
and seeing the beginning.
The faults of the greatly inhumane are many,
they cannot be fully recorded,
making it difficult to provide resources;
the Zhēnrén should consider this deeply.
Therefore, the Sān Qì of the Zhōng Hé of Heaven and Earth hate them;
even in death, there are remaining sins
which shall flow to their descendants.
Does the Zhēnrén realize this?"
"Yes, yes.
How terrifying!
I do not wish to hear more."
"If the Zhēnrén disregards these words,
Heaven will certainly take your life
to make you aware and enlightened;
loathe it and you shall live.
Command yourself to be cautious in all matters."
"Yes, yes.
I have respectfully received the precepts of Dàodé Rén,
and I wish to hear about the meaning of those who have knowledge but do not like to study the True Way."
"Excellent
are your words!
Heaven produces humans,
and fortunately, they may have worth and knowledge
so that they may study and achieve long life.
Since Heaven has the Dào,
it takes pleasure in sharing it with people;
Earth has Dé,
and it takes pleasure in sharing it with people;
Zhōng Hé has wealth,
and it takes pleasure in nourishing people.
Therefore, when humans take pleasure in seeking the True Way,
the Zhēnrén comes naturally.
Doing so without ceasing
is like consulting with the spirits.
If one daily sings of doing good,
goodness will naturally return to them.
If one diligently serves the many worthy ones,
the many worthy ones will together show and teach them,
and it will no longer be distant.
One can preserve their person,
not betraying the lineage of the ancestors;
while others all die young and end,
one alone can complete their natural lifespan.
While others all have a bad reputation,
one alone becomes a good person.
Becoming a teacher to the masses,
one's name is heard in distant lands,
inwardly cherishing and possessing the true Dàodé Rén.
Assisting Heaven in producing things,
assisting Earth in nourishing forms,
and assisting Emperors and Kings in transforming the people.
A superior teacher can then transform infinite people,
making all foolish people keep to the Way and not commit wrongs.
A middle teacher can transform ten thousand people.
