A minor teacher can transform hundreds or thousands of people,
bringing benefit to the ruler
and making the petty people know the prohibitions
so they do not commit wrongs or hide evil.
Above, they move Heaven to obtain office,
not betraying their ancestors
and not disgracing their descendants.
Such is the nature of learning;
how could one not do it?
Therefore, the sages and worthies of old
all regarded urging people to learn as a great concern,
to assist Heaven and Earth in production and growth
and to assist Emperors and Kings in governing disorder.
Between this Heaven and Earth,
this is what it means to be called a good person.
There may be some foolish people
who are born with desires
and possess knowledge but refuse to work hard at studying the True Way.
Instead, they prefer superficial vanity
and act to deceive people.
As children, they deceive their parents;
as ministers, they deceive their ruler;
as subordinates, they deceive their superiors.
This is called deceiving Heaven,
and such sins and faults cannot be removed.
Or there are those who instead love mundane affairs and fighting,
following each other in doing wrong.
Seeing a Zhēnrén,
they instead mock him greatly,
saying there is no point in learning.
Thus they remain in darkness,
foolish with nothing to be known.
Furthermore, they love to win but are incapable,
harshly claiming Heaven and Earth have no laws
and the worthy and soft have no knowledge.
Giving rein to their desires and acting upon them,
above they violate the celestial patterns
and below they violate the terrestrial principles.
Their comings and goings have no moderation.
Returning home, they do not serve their parents;
the many fools gather together
and thus become wicked sons.
When appointed as senior officials, they cause trouble,
and in return, their parents are executed—
If they cannot reflect and think for themselves,
and thus flee and become bandits and thieves,
going about harming, wounding, and killing people,
never stopping,
this is precisely what Heaven detests,
what Earth blames,
what emperors and kings worry and suffer over,
what the hundred deities loathe,
and what parents find exhausting.
This is the great disaster of harming others,
cutting off the lineage of one's ancestors.
If now one does not strive to learn the Zhēn Dào,
but behaves in such a manner,
in the mind of the Zhēnrén,
should they not indeed deserve death?
Death leaves behind excess guilt,
which flows down to their descendants;
they will still be known as the generation of an evil person,
the offspring of a bandit.
Should evil indeed flow to those born later?
Now, I am merely raising the main points for the Zhēnrén;
their evils are too numerous to record,
and it is difficult for them to provide for wealth and resources.
Does the Zhēnrén perceive and know this?
The Zhēnrén should be cautious."
"Yes, yes,
I am greatly distressed!"
"If you know distress,
you have already moved away from evil."
"I have respectfully heard the four matters in detail;
I wish to hear the next in sequence."
"Indeed.
When Heaven gives birth to humans,
it makes them complete before bringing them forth,
always delighting in their practice of Dào and Dé.
If a benevolent person is fortunate enough to have knowledge,
they can learn virtue.
Heaven and Earth nourish the myriad things with virtue,
and they delight in people emulating this.
Therefore, the virtuous people of high antiquity endured humiliation,
emulating the way Earth nourishes things.
When people learn to do this,
their minds and intentions are always joyful;
they no longer like harming or wounding.
When they see a matter, they are cautious;
those who act daily are good,
and no longer desire to do evil.
Things of the same kind gather together,
becoming more lofty and distant day by day.
Practicing this for a long time,
they become people of abundant virtue.
No one fails to respond to them,
and the masses turn toward them.
If they gather caution, obedience, and goodness without stopping,
they consequently become a Dà Róu Shī.
Their virtue then assists Heaven in nourishing things that desire life,
and assists Earth in nourishing things that desire to grow.
Furthermore, they enjoy assisting míng wáng in transforming the people,
making them cautious
so they no longer know what is ominous or evil.
Those who practice virtue on a small scale
may transform hundreds or thousands of people;
those who practice virtue on a large scale
may transform ten thousand people or more.
Consequently, they cause ten thousand people to turn into teachers of virtue,
and their transformation is limitless.
If they practice virtue without stopping,
there is no ordinary person who does not rejoice.
Heaven and Earth love them
and increase their lifespan.
The ghosts and gods like them
and thus together benefit and protect them.
Those with merit
possess the virtue of lords and officials;
they do not delight in harming the masses.
They delight in and like it;
what they seek is to dwell in constant solitary joy,
with no one desiring to harm them.
This originally stems from learning obedience and goodness to practice virtue;
reaching this point,
their name is heard in distant lands,
their merit is manifest in Heaven and Earth,
they do not fail their ancestors,
and they do not bring shame to those born later.
Now, some people may fortunately have knowledge
and know in their hearts good and evil,
yet they conversely treat themselves lightly,
not striving to learn to practice good virtue,
but instead following the evil of the vulgar, foolish, and ignorant.
They like using their vigor to value martial prowess,
their words are always ominous,
and the words they speak are contrary,
wishing to use them to subdue others.
They call themselves eloquent,
but there are those more eloquent than they;
people call themselves brave and powerful,
but there are those more brave and powerful than they.
Therefore, regarding all matters under Heaven,
each has something that subdues or exhausts it;
thus they can be controlled.
When a great fire is about to rise,
it seems as if it cannot be restrained,
but if it meets water, it dies.
When a person does what is not good
and is in a moment of anger,
it seems as if they cannot be controlled,
but if they meet prison, they are exhausted.
If one uses their mouth and seems unrestrained,
illness will cause them to submit.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth govern people,
all having their own laws and measurements.
People may have knowledge,
but they are unwilling to love learning;
instead, they treat themselves lightly and do wrong.
Where they dwell is ominous,
and no one loves them.
Heaven and Earth loathe them,
the hundred deities hate them,
and emperors and kings find them a source of worry and suffering.
These people do not become good people,
but naturally become bandits and thieves.
In death, they even become evil ghosts.
Though they used their strength to be overbearing,
in death, none of it can be used.
These principles are known to everyone,
yet people treat themselves lightly and do not do good,
defiling the lineage of their ancestors,
failing the children born later,
and thus they are categorized as ominous and thieving people.
No one is willing to converse with them;
travelers do not wish to share the road with them.
What fault is this of the child?
They inherit the evil of their parents' chéng fù,
and are still perhaps called the child of a bandit,
or may even consequently meet death.
Zhēnrén, come!
People treat themselves lightly
and do not like learning virtue from a míng shī,
but instead follow petty people.
Their faults reach such a state;
should they not indeed deserve death with excess guilt?"
"How fearful!
Tiānshī, there is no need to speak further;
thinking of it has already made my heart suffer and ache.
I saw people not learning
and thought it a small matter;
how could I have known it leads to this?"
"People are very foolish,
similar to vulgar people.
If people do not plan deeply,
death will leave behind excess guilt.
Since the Zhēnrén has already performed merit for Heaven and Earth,
be cautious."
"Yes, yes."
"You must not treat yourself lightly.
I have merely raised the main points
and shown the beginning.
The evil of not learning
does not only end here.
When you obtain my writings,
awaken and reflect on them deeply yourself."
"Yes, yes.
If I can truly return to a quiet place,
I will refine and examine them in detail."
"Indeed,
that is correct.
To learn without refining
is no different from a dream."
"Yes, yes.
I have respectfully received the instructions on my tasks;
I wish to hear the teaching regarding those who have strength in life but do not act."
"Indeed.
Heaven and Earth together give birth to crawling things,
and make all of them have strength,
taking qì from the four seasons and emulating the Wǔxíng.
Strength was originally meant for self-movement and lifting,
and one should follow this to provide clothing and food.
Therefore, a person of constant effort
works at it day and night without slackening,
gathering without stopping,
regardless of large or small things;
those who obtain them love them.
All things naturally possess jīngshén,
and they also like people to love them;
if people love them, they then come to return to them.
This is like the Dōng Hǎi loving water;
it dwells at the lowest point,
and all the waters of the world gather there,
thus allowing it to become the sea.
The jūnzǐ exerts effort without ceasing,
thus becoming the head of accumulated wealth and goods,
and his family consequently becomes wealthy with nothing lacking.
His ancestors then obtain good food,
his descendants become prosperous and sleek,
and the whole family shares in the benefit.
If one exerts effort without stopping,
though the four directions be poor and empty,
everyone will come to receive his work,
because his foundation is already greatly accomplished.
If he gives and bestows without stopping,"
The crowd praises them greatly,
their name is heard in far-off places,
and their achievements are prominent throughout Heaven and Earth.
They constantly exert their strength to relieve the destitute and save those in emergencies,
assisting Heaven and Earth in loving all things,
and assisting the sovereign in nourishing the people.
Their saving of the poor and needy never stops,
so Heaven and Earth increase their lifespan.
All the hundred spirits come to receive offerings,
and there is no one in this household who is not pleased and joyful.
Because of their virtuous conduct,
some attain high office,
bringing no disgrace to their ancestors
and not failing their descendants.
Some people have strength but conversely take themselves lightly,
not considering it their duty.
They could have achieved wealth,
but instead, they engage in fighting and litigation,
recklessly and lightly committing inauspicious acts.
Seeing that their own strength can subdue others,
they continue to act without stopping,
and eventually become sons of great evil.
When the family reaches the peak of poverty,
they arise to become thieves and bandits.
Then hunger and cold arrive together.
Being unable to restrain themselves from doing evil,
among them, the unworthy sons immediately die of hunger and cold.
Using their courage and strength, they go about harming people,
seeking what is not theirs,
and seizing objects that do not belong to them.
Furthermore, they frequently injure and harm others,
incurring the resentment of Heaven,
the blame of Earth,
and the enmity of the Jūnzǐ.
Emperors and kings are distressed by them.
As they continue to do this without stopping,
the hundred spirits detest them
and no longer grant them benefit or protection.
Heaven does not wish to cover them,
Earth does not wish to support them.
Calamities and harms arise daily,
and they die by the roadside;
or they languish in prison,
bringing execution upon their parents
and misfortune to their wives and children.
The six relations and the local neighborhood all wish for their death.
There is still residual guilt,
which flows down to their descendants.
Some become the offspring of beggars,
or the children of thieves and bandits,
becoming a great blemish for future generations.
Zhēnrén, standing before me,
such are the faults and responsibilities.
Should they not deserve death with residual guilt remaining?"
"I see the Tiānshī speaking of these matters,
and I am extremely alarmed and my heart aches,

"If the Zhēnrén knows heartache,
he shall live.
If you do not suddenly have a great awakening,
your death will not be long off.
Be careful!
My words must not be violated.
He who violates them will be destroyed.
It is not I who kills him;
his own actions bring it upon him.
Do you also know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"I have laid out these six matters for you,
but I have not yet spoken of one-ten-thousandth of them.
Xián Mǎn, having received my Dào,
you should think deeply and plan far ahead.
Do not conversely be negligent and take yourself lightly,
failing to be forgiving and do good.
Apply yourself to learning.
If you think of doing good yet do evil,
then you will instead be a lowly person.
Each should plan for their own life.
Among these are six capital crimes
and six great virtues.
All are modeled within the self.
Doing good will surely result in good.
He who easily commits evil
will daily gain unlucky and evil offspring.
Discipline yourself and plan for yourself.
None should find joy in self-indulgence.
Be careful of it, think on it.
Ponder it, contemplate it.
A worthy and wise heart
must be easy to open.
Dào, Dé, benevolence, and goodness
are entrusted to those who possess Dào and Dé.
Calamity and evil are entrusted to those who do not plan deeply.
This is the standard law.
If everyone can model themselves after my written words to correct themselves,
then there will no longer be evil people in the world.
This is the Dào of the ultimate cavern of the remote past in Heaven.
It can transform people.
Once people know it, they will all do good
and never return to their evil ways.
The superior man delights in life
and can learn the true Dào.
Dà Mǎn and the great worthy can learn Dé.
The person who loves to give can learn Rén.
The person who has knowledge can learn wisdom.
The person who has ability can learn capability.
The person who has strength can learn power.
If one can use all of these together,
thinking on them and maturing in them,
they will have already distanced themselves from calamity and evil.
Heaven and Earth will love them,
the six directions will nourish them,
and the emperors and kings will have nothing more to do.
Then there will be long journeys and good governance.
Does the Zhēnrén also know this?"
"Great joy has arrived!
I am very greatly pleased."
"You can be said to delight in goodness and know it.
Therefore, the sages and worthies of old
taught without stopping
because they saw the clarity of Heaven's prohibitions
and each planned for their own life.
Thus the teachings of the sages and worthies
fill the world with their words.
Are you alone not aware of this?"
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Therefore, the sages, worthies, and superior men of old all studied,
exerting themselves in study day and night without stopping,
for they also clearly saw the teachings and commands of Heaven and Earth.
Thus they did not dare to easily do wrong
and did not dare to take themselves lightly and not exert themselves in study.
Thus they obtained long-lasting good fortune and no harm.
These various worthies and extraordinary men
were originally all without knowledge,
but attained it through diligent study.
The various wicked and evil people here
are all so because of their failure to exert themselves in study
and because they took themselves lightly and acted carelessly.
My Dào
is the gate of good and bad fortune.
Do you also know this?"
"Yes, yes.
Thus, to collectively mention all from the highest even unto the lowest,

"Alas!
How is your mind not aware!"
"Seeing the Tiānshī speak continuously,
I am now even more dazed and do not know myself.
What constitutes being aware,

"Now I shall make you know and practice it.
Zhēnrén, standing before me,
as for the method of Heaven's governance,
it is to transform people to be good."
"From the top to the bottom,

"Its methods have ten thousand facets,
each with a different meaning.
However, even if a Zhēnrén is as upright as this,
common people are hard to awaken;
they have been deluded for a long time."
"I have faults;
only the Tiānshī can correct them."
"Indeed.
To assist the emperors and kings in governing,
there are generally ten methods:
the first is governance by Yuánqì,
the second is governance by Zìrán,
the third is governance by Dào,
the fourth is governance by Dé,
the fifth is governance by Rén,
the sixth is governance by Yì,
the seventh is governance by Lǐ,
the eighth is governance by Wén,
the ninth is governance by Fǎ,
and the tenth is governance by Wǔ.
It ends at ten.
Why?
Things begin with Yuánqì
and end with Wǔ.
Wǔ means cutting and felling;
therefore, Wǔ is the lowest.
Thus, things arise from Tàixuán,
culminate in Tàiyáng,
and end in death at Báihǔ.
Thus Yuánqì is in the north,
while Báihǔ resides in the west;
this is what it means.
Therefore, Heaven uses Yuánqì to govern
and uses the fēngqì to nourish things.
Earth governs through Zìrán;
thus, those who follow good obtain good,
and those who follow evil obtain evil.
Humanity
follows and receives the central harmony of Heaven and Earth
to govern with the Dào,
taking the lead in the Dào of action.
In all matters, there is thoroughness and interaction.
These three matters correspond to the omens of Heaven, Earth, and Humanity.
Those who go below these three matters..."
Virtue and benevolence are like chapters and sentences;
but going beyond benevolence and descending further,
often brings harm and makes intentions difficult to fulfill.
Therefore, my practice of the Dào is always joyful.
Above, it is rooted in the natural precepts of Heaven;
in the middle, it discards the nature that has not yet prematurely perished.
The constant principle for the birth of all things
is to reach completion in the middle stage;
upon reaching the end, they fall into disorder.
Those who have fallen into disorder cannot be restored to order;
therefore, one must begin from the source above.
Thus, Heaven always guards the root,
while Earth guards the middle.
With one revolution,
humans guard the lower part.
With three revolutions,
numerical cycles thus disorder the Dào.
Does the Zhēnrén already understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"You now have doubts."
"Following the teacher, I may speak;
I dare not have doubts."
"Zhēnrén, step forward.
When Heaven is about to assist the emperors and kings,

When it is about to benefit the people and ministers,
what is used as proof?"
"O Tiānshī,

Several times I have spoken but failed to hit the mark;
I have incurred many faults,
so I dare not speak again."
"Be humble!
Proceed."
"Yes, yes.
When Heaven is about to assist the emperors and kings,
it grants them exquisite texts.
Now these can be used to govern;
using them puts an end to transgressions.
They correspond with Yīnyáng
and will benefit the minor officials.
It grants them good officials
who will benefit the people,
allowing them to give birth to good children."
"The Zhēnrén's words are correct.
Is there yet another extraordinary explanation?
That was already the ultimate.
When Heaven desires to raise up a virtuous ruler,

Therefore, the Zhēnrén has come to undertake these studies.
They should be entrusted to cautious and good people
to awaken their hearts
and make them contemplate.
Entrust them to the ruler of great virtue above

Together they will understand the meaning as it is explained

When the common people receive it,

smoothing out what is uneven.
It is not only about Heaven, Earth, and the ruler.
The fault originally lies with the leader of the people;
the leader personally incurs heavy faults and blame from Huángtiān Hòutǔ,
all stemming from one person.
Sometimes there are those who learned first and obtained the Zhēndào,
but they do not strive to transform and teach others.
Dàróu fortunately knows Virtue first,
but does not strive to transform others.
Families that accumulate wealth
are unwilling to strive to practice benevolence through giving.
When a person is born with intelligence sufficient for learning
but is unwilling to strive in their studies,
seeking the Zhēndào to attain longevity.
When one has ability sufficient to study Virtue
to transform their own person,
but is unwilling to strive to study Virtue to transform themselves.
When one has strength but is unwilling to strive in work to sustain themselves,
on the contrary, they fall into poverty and distress.
These are the six great faults.
Heaven and man have uniquely accumulated these for a long time.
Since the opening of Heaven and Earth,
they have inherited and carried these burdens for one another.
For those born later, it is especially severe;
accumulated in great numbers, they gather to become a great harm.
This causes both Heaven and Earth to lose their rectitude.
Emperors and kings have long worried and suffered in their minds, yet there is no order;
before and after, there is no peace.
Heaven greatly hates this.
Therefore, I urgently transmit the words of Heaven.
From Tàigǔ until now,
Heaven and Earth have had pains and sufferings,
troubled and blocked.
Ordinary people cannot know this.
All have Shénshèng transmit their words;
it is not only me.
The Zhēnrén should not find this strange.
Now that I have left the world,
I cannot carelessly return to be seen among the people.
Therefore, I transmit these books and entrust them to the Zhēnrén.
When the Zhēnrén receives them,
he has already left the secular world
and can no longer be a teacher among the people.
Therefore, the Zhēnrén must seek out good people who understand and entrust the books to them.
Now, hasten to go and entrust them to the virtuous ruler.
Those who dare not go to entrust them or who cause delays shall be punished.
How serious this is!
Now Heaven should resolve illnesses and bring peace to the emperors and kings,
causing the ruler of Dào and Dé to clearly show them to all the worthies
to transform the people.
Each reflecting on their own faults
to resolve the punishment for the Chéngfù of their ancestors.
Making ordinary people each plan for their own lives,
not allowing them to be negligent or careless.
Then afterwards, Heaven will be greatly pleased,
and order will be established and peace attained.
You may harbor doubts,
thinking that my words are not greatly truthful or trustworthy.
My writings are only proven true through testing.
The reason for this is
that there are hundreds of millions of scrolls of ancient texts,
yet their governance has always been unable to achieve Tàipíng.
Now let the worthy and enlightened Róuzhǎng
alone harbor doubts,

If a brave warrior is not tested,
how can one know his great strength?
If one sees a text but does not test it in use,
how can one know its divinity?
I received the words of Heaven
to test the Zhēnrén.
From now on,
whenever ordinary texts are received,
all should be tested immediately.
One must not again vainly set forth false words.
Heaven greatly hates this,
and Earth greatly suffers from it,
regarding it as a great illness.
Truly it is a matter of grievance and indignation.
Consequently, it prevents all things from flourishing,
causing many disasters and premature deaths.
People cannot live out their natural lifespan.
Emperors and kings are distressed,
and officials and commoners are in chaotic disorder.
They no longer care for one another.
The great blame lies here;
these are the six crimes.
Those who possess the Dào are jealous of the Dào
and are unwilling to strive to teach the foolish.
Those who possess Virtue are jealous of Virtue
and are unwilling to strive to transform the foolish.
Those who possess wealth and accumulate it are jealous of wealth
and are unwilling to give it away.
Heaven gave birth to all people so they might practice giving.
Heaven possesses knowledge.
If one is unwilling to strive to study the Zhèngdào to avoid being in extremity, but instead meets with teaching,
on the contrary, they laugh at it.
Those who have ability
but are unwilling to strive to learn and apply the teachings they meet,

Those who have strength
but are unwilling to strive in work

Seeing parents teaching them,
on the contrary, they criticize them.
Therefore, I command the Zhēnrén to quickly see this text,
causing all the worthies to each deeply contemplate and remember the common people.
Each reflecting on their own great faults.
Does the Zhēnrén finally understand the commands?"
"Yes, yes.
Now that the Shénrén has set forth the law for Heaven,

and spread it among the populace?
Why must it go from the top down?"
"Excellent, excellent!
Now that the Supreme Tàipíng Qì is about to arrive,

Therefore, it proceeds from the top down.
If it does not proceed from the top down,
then it becomes contrary Qì,
causing governance to be without peace.
This is mainly because of contrary Qì,
because things are not in accord.
Does the Zhēnrén wish to add more to this?"
"I dare not."
"Therefore, it must proceed from the top down.
Do not ask again."
"Yes, yes.
Go and be cautious in your affairs,
each planning for your own self.
These are the six great faults.
The Tiāndào is extremely strict;
one must not act recklessly.
Heaven dwells above and watches humanity."
"Yes, yes.
I wish to ask one more thing.
When ordinary people have obtained the essential Dào and essential Dé..."
"Where should it be placed?"
"It should be presented upward to the ruler."
"Why must it be presented to him?"
"The Essential Dào is that which brings peace to the ruler;
using it to govern ensures one attains the Heart of Heaven.
The Essential Dé is that which nourishes the ruler;
using it to govern ensures one attains the Intent of Earth.
To truly know it yet be unwilling to present it to the superior
is in all cases a lack of respect,

"Why is it so severe?"
"Observing the way you handle matters and plant your words,
it is as if you know nothing at all.
To be a son and yet not be observant,
to be a subject or minister and yet not be loyal or trustworthy,

If a Zhēnrén speaks,
how could there be anything equal in such gravity?
The learning of a Zhēnrén,
why does it not deepen daily,

"This very foolish student truly did not see."
"You still say you did not see;
common people are obscured and hidden,
concealing their essential Dào and Dé,
conversely causing their ruler to grieve and suffer from foolishness and darkness;
the fault lies in the true Dào and Dé being obscured and not circulating.
Furthermore, the Essential Dào
is that which matches Heaven;
the Essential Dé
is that which matches Earth.
Foolish people cut them off;
Heaven detests them,
Earth loathes them,
and their faults are not absolved.
The Zhēnrén is fortunate to be uniquely favored by Heaven and granted longevity,
yet his learning is conversely incomplete,
thus reaching the prohibitions of Heaven.
Those who handle such matters should be cautious."
"Yes, yes."
To the right is the Scripture of Heavenly Instruction on Harmony, which enables people to always be auspicious and avoid misfortune.
"The time for my departure is set;
I offer one word of admonition to you six disciples.
The Dào is all-pervading;
it has no above or below,
no exterior or interior.
Guard its harmonious Qì,
and its name is Shén;
if you seek it nearby, you will gain greatly;
if you seek it far away, you will lose it.
Therefore, the ancient rulers and kings who were good at governing
began from within the belly;
truly able to employ the Dào,
governance was naturally achieved.
In action, they did not lose the laws, measures, and numbers;
the myriad things regulated themselves.
It is nearby in the chest and heart,
yet scatters to fill the four seas.
The ancient sages called it the Essential Dào.
Governance delights in desiring non-action;
be careful not to lose this,
for this is the plumb-line to correct the worthy.
Now I emphasize this repeatedly to instruct you.
You six have asked about my books for successive days;
although the Dào is divided into different paths,
they should share a single purpose.
Yet if the tongue can encompass the six directions completely,
the Kingly Way is complete,
explaining the myriad things,
each having different meanings.
Heaven and Earth attain great peace through it;
rulers and kings attain non-action through it.
My book knows the heart of Shén,
pervading the six directions and eight quarters.
Since descending and coming to submit,
all harbor good hearts
and no ill intentions.
Its essential knot resides nearby within;
it is like the myriad things:
the heart is inside,
the branches are outside.
When the interior is flourishing,
then the exterior flourishes;
when the interior withers, then the exterior withers.
Thus the ancient Sages, Sovereigns, and Kings of the Imperial Way,
wishing to correct the pervading extremities of the six distances and eight quarters,
conversely first corrected the interior.
Correcting the exterior by means of the interior,
ten thousand upon ten thousand things respond,
hundreds of millions do not escape;
those who try to correct the interior by means of the exterior
lose it in ten thousand ways.
Therefore, the Great Sages of old taught people to think deeply and plan far ahead,
closing their nine apertures,
resting their four limbs,
making themselves undifferentiated,
like a ring without an end,
like a child in the womb without duties or affairs;
only then can they attain its principle.
My Dào entirely takes this as its great essence.
Therefore, it returns and makes each task guard its own root.
When Heaven is about to bring forth humans,
it fully entrusts the True Dào to their physical form.
Thus, it depends on a teacher to open it, guide it, and learn it,
then one can be made to know everything;
if one does not open their gates and windows,
even if they receive the True Dào of Heaven,
they will know nothing at all.
It is like an infant being born;
thrown into a room,
if not guided to learn about affairs,
there is nothing it can know.
The reason people differ
is only because of the different customs of the eight quarters,
thus their knowledge and learning are not the same.
If one person can learn,
circulating throughout the exterior and interior,
then they will know it all.
I am about to go far away to some place;
there will again be things to transmit;
I cannot always sit peacefully
guarding all of you disciples.
You six should carefully read my book for yourselves;
from top to bottom there are complexities;
for those things which do not resolve your thoughts,
examine the source of ancient texts to clarify them.
The one who walks upward knows it through Xuánzhēn,
the one who walks downward knows it through Shùnzhēn,
the one of the east knows it through Chūzhēn,
the one of the south knows it through Tàizhēn,
the one of the west knows it through Shǎozhēn,
the one of the north knows it through Yōuzhēn.
The Dào is a Great Unity with minor differences;
therefore it can distinguish Yīn and Yáng without limit,
transforming into eleven thousand five hundred and twenty words.
The harmony of the myriad things is partially complete,
yet it has not fully investigated the Yīn and Yáng of Heaven and Earth,
or the absolute void without exterior or interior.
Therefore, just examine its non-being,
uphold its main thread,
see its beginning,
allowing it to be modeled and recorded.
Recording the past and recording the present,
its essential disorder is naturally the same as what the spirit-sages recorded,
like overlapping compasses or matching squares;
although separated by hundreds of millions of years,
it is as if speaking face to face.
Thus it can be made the Constant Scripture of Heaven and Earth,
and serve as the Divine Way for Yīn and Yáng.
Do not wonder why my book is so repetitive from beginning to end.
The reason for the repetition
is the fear that something might be missed.
Furthermore, the Way of Heaven is extremely strict;
once spoken, I dare not be incomplete;
to circulate it partially or not at all is called Jiāndào,
and is a severe transgression.
I truly pity this.
Although this is repetitive,
it is like the Sages of High Antiquity,
the Sages of Middle Antiquity,
and the Sages of Late Antiquity,
who were all born in different ages,
yet their words followed one another,
speaking with repetition,
further clarifying by comparing with each other;
only then can the Way of Heaven be fully known;
this is what is meant.
Go now;
I must travel in haste.
Take great care in holding the Heavenly Treasure,
and transmit it to the right person."
To the right is the admonition to the six disciples.
The Zhēnrén bowed twice and said:
"Your humble servant has always been treated by Tiānshī as his own child.
Your grace and love have deeply permeated me.
Having been able to urgently seek your audience day and night,
your heavenly merit is supreme
and cannot be thanked enough.
Now I wish to again pose questions on secret essentials,
the hidden Way of Heaven,
yet I also dare not speak of them abruptly."
"Speak of them calmly.
Since you are asking about matters for Heaven,
you should exhaust them to the end
and must not abandon them midway and stop."
"Yes, yes.
Your humble servant sees that what Tiānshī says
has no end or limit.
Thus, your disciples all recognize and understand through Heaven's grace
that Tiānshī deeply and thoroughly knows the interior and exterior of Heaven and Earth and the essence of Yīn and Yáng.
All the disciples fear that once we part from the Master,
there will be no one again to question about doubtful matters.
Therefore, we boldly risk offense
to ask for the prophecies that can stabilize the state for a long time,
so that the lord of men may always rule by non-action,
having no more worries.
He should only ever sound the zithers,
make music, and roam,
being as secure as Heaven and Earth,
never again having times of peril. May we hear of this?"
"Indeed,
are you Zhēnrén thinking of progressing?
How deep and subtle is what you ask,
seeking the diagrams and prophetic texts that penetrate Heaven and Earth.
A single word from them cannot be changed for ten thousand generations.
The Tiāngōng is distressed by many disasters and sorrows;
is that why he sent you Zhēnrén to come and ask about these doubts?"
"Yes."
"I shall now detail for the Zhēnrén the great essentials of Heaven's rules
and the secret texts and formulas,
to let them □□.
The Zhēnrén should follow and record them."
"Yes, yes."
"Indeed,
August Heaven takes the four seasons as its branches,
and Thick Earth takes the Five Elements as its body.
The branches govern waxing and waning,
and the body governs the rules.
Distributing these nine spirits,
they circulate throughout the world,
penetrating the heights and depths,
their transformations difficult to see.
They are the precious treasures of Heaven and Earth
and the gateway for all spirits.
They have their own fixed constancy
and must not be recklessly violated.
Those who follow them will have long-lasting good fortune;
those who disrupt them will long be in conflict with Heaven and Earth."
"Yes, yes.
We wish to hear their meaning;
can they be seen?"
"Excellent
is what you Zhēnrén have said.
I am about to detail the Way for you,
but you must all refine yourselves
and sit peacefully to contemplate my words."
"Yes, yes."
"The prophetic standard of Heaven's constancy
takes the South as the fixed position of the lord.
Therefore, the Sun in the South is the lord,
Fire in the South is the lord,
Tàiyáng in the South is the lord,
of the four seasons,
midsummer in the South is the lord,
of the five sacrifices,
the stove in the South is the lord,
and of the five viscera,
the heart in the South is the lord.
As for the lord,
the law dictates he should wear red,
which is the phase of Fire.
For this reason, when the lord has strange portents,
they always correspond to Yáng
and do not correspond to other phases.
In Yáng, the Sun is the brightest,
being the chief of all lights;
thus, Heaven's prophecies always use the Sun to divine the lord's rise and fall.
Do the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes,
we are coming to know it."
"The law for the lord of men
is that he should always seek to share a home with the benevolent;
those with a heart should carry out governance.
Those with whom he can rule together
should always practice the Way and love life.
The small, young, and weak,
along with the elder ministers who are worthy and accomplished,
the lord should nurture them
and should not harm them.
Thus, the East loves life
and the South loves nurturing.
One who uses the mind without benevolence
cannot be worked with for long;
one who is not enlightened
cannot be made a lord or leader.
Thus, the East is Wood, benevolence, and possesses a heart;
the South is Fire and enlightenment.
According to the law of Heaven,
emperors and kings who rule should always use the Way and Virtue.
Thus, the East is the Way,
and the Way governs life;
the South is Virtue,
and Virtue governs nurturing;
thus the South governs nurturing.
As for governance,
it should imitate Heaven to transform through culture.
Thus, the East is culture;
the dragon appears bearing it.
The South is manifestation;
thus it is precisely refined culture.
Manifestation
is great brilliance;
thus culture is born in the East
and made brilliant in the South.
Thus, the patterns of Heaven
are red;
red
is Fire.
Benevolence and the lord move upward;
the Sun should be high and bright
to act as a model for men.
Thus, when Wood and Fire move,
they always ascend;
this is the image of the lord.
Thus, residing in the East,
one relies on benevolence to ascend;
the ruler, therefore, should reside in the South.
Thus, the East is Shǎoyáng,
the beginning of the lord's birth;
thus the Sun rises in the East.
The South is Tàiyáng,
the peak of the lord's brilliance.
Shǎoyáng is the lord's home and parents;
Tàiyáng is the lord's person
and the lord's position.
Shǎoyáng is the lord's home;
Wood is the parent of Fire.
The lord takes Shǎoyáng as his home,
and Fire is called the child of Wood.
Do the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"You already know it.
Shǎoyīn is the minister;
the minister bends and yields through righteousness,
submitting to Tàiyáng.
Thus Metal bends and yields according to Fire,
being what people can desire;
the one who acts as minister always bends and yields through righteousness,
assisting the lord in what he wishes to do.
Thus Shǎoyīn is called the minister.
Do the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Tàiyīn is the people;
the people flow and do not stop.
Thus water flows and does not know rest.
As for the people,
their duty is to be responsible for the livelihood of the state, kings, and nobles.
Thus water
should follow to generate and nurture Wood.
The East
is the lord's home.
Do the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Good,
you already know it."
"In the prophetic standards of Heaven:
Shǎoyáng fears Shǎoyīn.
Thus the minister,
on the contrary, is in charge of recording the affairs of the state, kings, nobles, and officials.
Tàiyáng fears Tàiyīn.
This is why when a state has the Way and Virtue
and the lord and ministers are worthy and brilliant,
then the people follow.
When a state lacks the Way and Virtue,
then the people rebel.
This is why the great essential of governing a state
is to consider a numerous populace as wealth
and a sparse populace as great poverty.
Do all you Zhēnrén understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Good,
you have already realized it."
"The standard laws of Heaven
are divided into six divisions.
The Southeast and above belong to Heaven;
therefore, when the ten thousand things are born, they all move upward.
Crawling creatures and the common people all come out and dwell in the open;
they belong to Heaven.
Therefore, Heaven creates their colors:
the exterior is azure, symbolizing Wood,
and the interior is red, symbolizing Fire.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Proceed;
it is already understood."
"The standard prophecies of Heaven and Earth state that
the West and the North
below belong to the Earth.
Therefore, when the ten thousand things reach autumn and winter,
they all fall and return to the soil.
The common people and crawling creatures, when reaching autumn and winter,
all enter holes and dwell there.
Therefore, regarding the Earth's colors:
the exterior is yellow and white, symbolizing Soil and Metal,
while the interior contains Water and is black,
symbolizing the northward movement.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"According to the standard prophecies of Heaven,
the positions of the East and South are honorable;
above, they belong to Heaven
and govern administration;
they are the lords, elders, teachers, and fathers.
The positions of the West and North are humble;
they belong to the Earth
and are the subjects,
the back palace,
and the common people.
Therefore, Jǐ
is the back palace of Jiǎ.
Jiǎ is Heaven,
the fundamental position of the King;
therefore, Jiǎ is the Xīnxīng.
The Xīnxīng
is Fire
and is the King.
Thus, the East is also the ancestor of the King.
The Xīnxīng
is Fire;
its movement belongs to the South.
This is like the sun rising in the East
but having its position in the South.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Proceed;
you already know it."
"The standard prophecies of Heaven state that
Bǐng is the leader of Fire,
the most Greatly Luminous,
and the position of the Lord.
Xīn belongs to Bǐng;
Xīn
is the back palace of Bǐng.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Proceed;
you already know it."
"Now, Jǐ is also an Empress,
and Xīn is also an Empress.
What does this mean?"
"Excellent
is your inquiry;
it grasps the essential meaning of Heaven's prophecies.
However, Jǐ is paired with Jiǎ.
Jiǎ
is the father of Bǐng;
thus, Jǐ is the palace of the Grand Empress (Tàihuánghòu).
Xīn is paired with Bǐng.
Bǐng
is the son of Jiǎ.
Thus, Xīn
is the palace of the Junior Empress (Xiǎohuánghòu);
Bǐng
is the legitimate son of Jiǎ,
the Lord of the Mandated Sovereigns.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Proceed;
the Zhēnrén already knows it."
"Gēng belongs to Yǐ;
this is the son-in-law of the feudal lords and kings of the state.
Rén belongs to Dīng;
this is the son-in-law of the Emperor's sisters.
Guǐ belongs to Wù;
this is the maternal family of the state's Grand Empress (Tàihuánghòu)."
"Excellent;
the Zhēnrén already knows it."
"Now that the Ten Stems (Shígān) have been explained,
each with its own affiliation,
I wish to hear how the Twelve Branches (Shí’èrzhī) of the Earth should be described."
"How good!
However, in the laws of Heaven,
although Yin and Yang circulate,
those who interact with one another each have their own homes.
The laws of Heaven are uniform;
they do not move their entire households to follow one another and then stop.
Jiǎ takes Yín as its home;
Yǐ takes Mǎo as its home;
Bǐng takes Wǔ as its home;
Dīng takes Sì as its home;
Wù takes Chén and Xū as its home;
Jǐ takes Chǒu and Wèi as its home;
Gēng takes Shēn as its home;
Xīn takes Yǒu as its home;
Rén takes Zǐ as its home;
Guǐ takes Hài as its home.
Therefore, the Way of Heaven
governs through cyclical movement.
The Way of Earth
is stillness.
Thus there are divided lands,
but conversely no divided people;
for there is territory but no absolute state.
Therefore, Heaven and Earth do not shift permanently,
yet Heaven, conversely, completes one full revolution in a day and a night,
taking this movement as its constant.
Thus the Twelve Branches (Shí’èrzhī) each reside in their own places
and do not move along with the Ten Stems (Shígān).
Do you know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"The Way of Heaven and Earth,
the Four Seasons and the Five Elements—
their Way is self-sufficient.
They rotate and change terms,
circulating through the unseen realms
without ever ending.
Only the great spirits and sages of antiquity knew this from time to time.
I wish to explain it all to you,
but it would be difficult to provide the resources for it,
and further, it would be too verbose,
which would instead cause more confusion,
making a Lord of Earthly Virtue (Tǔdé zhī Jūn) feel dazzled and disordered,
not knowing what to follow;
therefore, I stop.
I do not begrudge explaining it to you all,
but the explanation would be without end.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Proceed;
you have gained some awakening.
If a virtuous lord relies on my heavenly prophecies to govern,
he will not fail once in ten thousand times.
For this reason, the Way of Heaven
has fixed boundaries.
Taking the East and the South as symbols of the sovereign King,
they belong to Heaven;
therefore, he is named Tiānzǐ.
Taking the West and the North as symbols of the back palace, the common people, and the subjects,
they belong to Earth;
thus the Earth is the back palace.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"According to the standard prophecies of Heaven,
the East fears the West.
Therefore, since the opening of Heaven and Earth,
if a King follows the methods of warfare
and raises the Qi of Metal,
the military division will cause the symbol of the Lord to be without Qi.
Fire will greatly decline,
and his governance will be calamitous and chaotic.
If the Zhēnrén wishes to know the verified truth of the heavenly prophecies,
from high antiquity and middle antiquity to late antiquity,
when the lords of men abandoned the Way and Virtue
and raised the use of Metal Qi and the methods of warfare,
their governance was entirely calamitous,
with many bandits and inauspicious omens.
For this reason, the sages of high antiquity deeply understood the fixed laws and symbols of Heaven;
therefore, they did not dare to govern using weapons, armor, and military divisions.
If an Emperor or King desires lasting peace and auspiciousness,
he should follow these heavenly prophecies,
urgently confine and sever metal weapons and military preparations,
and urgently promote the use of the Way and Ultimate Virtue
to symbolize the laws of Heaven,
to match the heart of Huángtiān,
and to permanently suppress and eliminate all treacherous, cunning, and inauspicious classes;
the response will be immediate and without doubt.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
“The method of Heaven’s omens is that,
although the *Tàiyáng* is the ruler,
he conversely greatly fears the *Tàiyīn*,
which is the movement of water.
That which is the sweet and fine of water
is wine.
Wine
is the king of water,
its leader,
and the finest of all drinks.
Its *qì* belongs to the *Kǎn* position,
and at night it rules over thieves and robbers.
Therefore, to follow wine is called indulging in unbridled behavior;
it is the king and leader of water,
and when water is king, the *Tàiyáng* declines.
Does the *Zhēnrén* wish to joyfully know the detailed truth of Heaven’s omens?
From high antiquity downwards,
and since middle antiquity,
those rulers who liked to indulge in wine
could never achieve *Tàipíng*.
Their governance conversely fell into chaos,
their officials were involved in many battles,
which led to thieves and robbers—
this is the clear effect.
For this reason, when a virtuous ruler of *Tàipíng* is governing,
the essence of fire should be bright,
and it is not suitable to follow the *Tàiyīn*,
allowing the virtue of water to be king
and thereby harm his governance;
therefore, wine should be cut off.”
“I wish to hear about the specifics of the ban;
what kind of wine should be cut off?”
“Only cut off market wine.”
“What has the *Tiānshī* observed or seen
to specifically ban market wine alone?”
“Indeed.
As for the market,
it corresponds to the movement of water.
Therefore, the people and goods of the four directions
all flow and gather at that place.
This is why the rivers and seas
are also the kings and leaders of water;
for all the wealth and goods of the hundred rivers
also flow and gather there.
Water
is the movement of the *Xuánwǔ* of the North;
therefore it is greedy
and repeatedly plunders people’s wealth and goods.
The market is also where the flow of the five directions gathers to trade for profit,
leading to categories such as the cunning and thieves,
who all arise from the market,
because water rules *Kǎn*.
By the law of Heaven,
things of the same category correspond to each other from afar;
thus the market acts as the movement of water.
If one indulges in wine there
and gives it in large quantities,
it is again called the king of water.
Market people also obtain wine and rejoice in its kingship;
this is called the ‘double kingship of two waters.’
Its faults are six-fold:
it suppresses and weakens the fire *qì* of the *Tàiyáng*,
causes the ruler’s governance to decline,
and conversely leads to sinister ministers.
Does the *Zhēnrén* know this?”
“Now seeing the *Tiānshī* explain it,
I am confused and do not understand;
I wish to hear the great secret.”
“Excellent
are your words.
Since the *Zhēnrén* have come from afar on behalf of Heaven to inquire
and to resolve the harm of *chéngfù* for the virtuous sovereign and emperor,
I shall withhold nothing.
All of you sit peacefully;
I shall explain everything separately for the *Zhēnrén*
and speak of the great essential meaning.”
“Yes, yes.”
“The secret of Heaven’s omens is that
when gold and jade are used for affairs,
and the people greatly promote military departments,
Wood exhausts the original *qì*,
and Earth becomes king.
When earth is greatly raised in construction,
this is the palace of the *Tàihuánghòu*.
The *qì* belongs to the Northwest;
when the *Tàiyīn* becomes the great king,
then sinister ministers are born,
who create an Inner Palace (*Hòugōng*);
losing the way, they rise up and soar.
When Earth is king, Metal is the assistant;
they again follow each other, rising up and soaring.
When the *qì* of *Sì* and *Xīn* both prosper and become king,
they soar and rise greatly.
By the standard law of Heaven,
this produces many sinister things in the Inner Palace;
this is not the fault of the Inner Palace itself,
but is called governance losing the omen of Heaven,
losing its major boundaries,
and conversely causing disasters to return and cover each other.
This is since the opening of Heaven and Earth;
the timing of the previous masters had not yet reached the point
where they could explain the great boundaries of Heaven in detail.
This caused emperors to lose the legal governance of Heaven
and led to the birth of these disasters and changes.
Does the *Zhēnrén* deeply know this?”
“Yes, yes.”
“The omen of Heaven is this:
those who indulge in wine
are of the category of water.
The market is the movement of water,
a place where the people’s king greatly gathers;
if one indulges in wine at the market,
it is called the great king of water and wine.
When water is king, fire has little *qì*;
when fire has little *qì*, it turns into ash;
when it turns into ash, it transforms into Earth;
it is then called Fire
entrusting its *qì* to Earth.
Earth becomes king and rises from the ground,
belonging to the Northwest along with Metal and Water.
The *Tàiyīn* belongs to the people,
and ministers conversely become king.
Afterward, sinister ministers are born,
the *qì* of *Sì* again acts,
the Inner Palace commits offenses,
and again moves and rises up.
Its disaster leads to theft,
and there is no time of relief from thieves and robbers.
Each is due to indulging in water,
causing injury to the *Yáng* virtue.
The reason I now explain this separately for the *Zhēnrén*
is seeing that you have come to ask
with great sincerity and diligence,
knowing that *Huángtiān* wishes to help the virtuous ruler.
Therefore I clarify for the *Zhēnrén* the great divisions of governance of Heaven and Earth,
which should be emulated
and not violated again.
Violators will again fall into confusion and chaos.
Do you know this?”
“Yes, yes.
I wish to ask about one doubt.”
“Speak.”
“Now, within the gathered crowds and wealth in the capital,
does the capital also correspond to the movement of water?”
“Alas!
In the studies of the *Zhēnrén*,
why are you at one time clear
and at another time ignorant?
You have not reached it.
But how could you reach it all?
As for the capital,
it corresponds to the center of Earth,
the place where Fire can peacefully reside.
It is not like a market,
which is only a place to gather wealth.
The capital is where the *Dào* and *Dé* should be gathered together,
along with *Rén* and *Xián*,
to jointly govern the world.
Why do you say the ruler of the capital
should only gather wealth and goods?
How very foolish you are!
If you think my words are untrustworthy,
I shall explain it for you.
From the capital of ancient times to the present,
whenever *Dào*, *Dé*, and *Xián* were gathered,
all the world was at peace under their rule.
But those who only gathered rare treasures and wealth without the wise and enlightened were all in chaos.
In the *Zhēnrén*’s mind,
could the capital be like a market,
just a place to gather wealth and nothing else?
Do you understand now?”
“Yes, yes.”
For the various Zhēnrén, I establish the Chóngmíng Tiānchèn Géfǎ.
The sun is born from Shǎoyáng,
and flourishes in Tàiyáng;
the moon is born from Shǎoyīn,
and flourishes in Tàiyīn.
The sun,
the essence of Heaven
and the radiance of Yáng,
is therefore called the Ruler,
and its position is in the South;
the moon,
the essence of Earth
and the radiance of Yīn,
is therefore the Minister,
and its position is in the North.
The South is day,
and the North is night.
For this reason, when the sun attains dominance and governs,
the moon and the night wither and shorten;
when the moon attains dominance and governs,
the sun and the day wither and shorten.
Thus, when the Qì of the North flourishes,
the Qì of the South withers;
when the Qì of the South flourishes,
the Qì of the North withers.
Therefore, one must urgently halt the Jiǔwáng,
so as to sever the withering Shuǐ and Jīn.
Does Zhēnrén Chóngmíng understand this?
"Yes, yes."
“The pattern of Heaven’s divisions is as follows:
that which is Yáng is Heaven,
is Male,
is the Ruler,
is the Father,
is the Elder,
and is the Teacher.
That which is Yīn is Earth,
is Female,
is the Minister,
is the Son,
is the Common People,
and is the Mother.
Therefore, the Southeast is Yáng,
and the Northwest is Yīn.
If the Zhēnrén wishes to know the verified truth of heavenly prophecies:
since the opening and creation of Heaven and Earth,
whenever military armaments have been unrestrained,
whenever kings have been allowed to indulge in wine,
or whenever kings have been made to follow the governance of women,
following their words to a great extent,
and making them rule the king,
then Shǎoyīn, Tàiyīn, and Earth will belong to the Northwest.
Those who follow these commands
will all eventually face disorder and suffer ominous harm.
Benevolence, gentleness, the Dào, Virtue, the worthy, and the clear-sighted Sages all belong to the Southeast;
they belong to Yáng
and belong to Heaven.
Those who follow these words will eventually see everything brought into order.”
“I wish to hear why the worthy and the Sages belong to the Southeast.”
“The essence of Fire is the Heart;
the Heart is the Sage.
The essence of Wood is Benevolence;
therefore its image is in the East.
The Southeast is what nurtures and grows all things;
the worthy and the Sages are gentle and bright, and they also nurture all things,
never harming them.
Thus, the worthy and the Sages take gentleness and brightness as their nature;
they are entirely benevolent and bright.
Benevolence is like Wood,
and Brightness is like Fire;
therefore, they are all situated in the Southeast.”
“Excellent, excellent!
Having seen the words of the Tiānshī,
I have attained great understanding.”
“Furthermore, regarding the method of the patterns of heavenly prophecies:
the Southeast is where the Tiāndǒu Gāng of the Celestial Dipper points.
When calculating the four seasons,
all Kings receive their mandate there.
The Northwest belongs to Earth;
it is the Dǒukuí bowl.
That which is tied to it is the breath of death and extinction.
Therefore, if Shǎoyīn, Tàiyīn, and Soil are allowed to rule
and overcome that which is Yáng,
it is called ‘reversing Heaven and Earth,’
and thus it leads to much disorder.
Does the Zhēnrén understand this?”
“Yes, indeed.
We several humble students,
because the Tiānshī has pitied us,
have been told the secrets of heavenly prophecies.
I wish to ask about one matter
in a single word.
Currently, the South is Yáng,
yet the Yì conversely derives Xùn, Lí, and Kūn there;
the North is Yīn,
yet the Yì conversely derives Qián, Kǎn, and Gèn there.”
“Excellent!
Your challenge is profound.
You have perceived the subtle intention of Heaven.
However, as for the Yì,
it is based on the subtle breaths of the Yīn and Yáng of Heaven and Earth,
taking the Yuánqì as the beginning.
Thus, at the South, where Yáng is at its peak, Yīn is born,
so it records its Yīn;
at the North, where Yīn is at its peak, Yáng is born,
so it records its Yáng.
These subtle breaths
are not yet able to rule or sustain affairs.
Therefore, in the Yì, for Chū Jiǔ of Zǐ,
it says ‘Hidden dragon, do not act,’
as it cannot yet rule or sustain affairs,
so one should not act.
This
is merely the beginning and the head of the Yuánqì.”
“Excellent, excellent!”
“Proceed;
the Zhēnrén has already understood.
Now, the heavenly prophecies I record
record the Great Divisions of Heaven,
which are able to rule and sustain the breath of celestial governance
and serve as the guiding principles for the world.
Does the Zhēnrén understand this?”
“Yes, indeed.”
“What I say now
is precisely what the rulers of the world should follow as their law of governance.
What you asked about
is the beginning of the primordial breath.
Now that the Zhēnrén has seen my words,
there may be some doubts;
therefore, I shall explain the Eight Boundaries of Heaven and Earth in detail for all the Zhēnrén.”
“Yes, indeed.”
“Regarding the boundary of the Sun:
because the Sun rises in Mǎo
and sets in Yǒu,
the South is Yáng
and the North is Yīn.
Regarding the boundary of the Gate of Heaven and the Door of Earth:
because Xùn first arises in the Southeast corner
and Qián first arises in the Northwest corner,
the Northeast is Yáng
and the Southwest is Yīn.
With Zǐ Chū Jiǔ
and Wǔ Chū Liù, the East is Yáng
and the West is Yīn.
Lìchūn is in the Northeast corner,
and Lìqiū is in the Northwest corner;
thus the Southeast is Yáng
and the Northwest is Yīn.
These are called the Eight Boundaries of Heaven and Earth,
which distinguish the positions of Yīn and Yáng.
Does the Zhēnrén understand?”
“Yes, indeed.”
“Proceed;
you have understood.
For this reason, in the Great Division, the Southeast is Heaven
and the Northwest is Earth,
and Earth must follow and obey.
If a king allows Earth to suppress Heaven, it is the reversal of Heaven and Earth,
and thus it is ominous.
If Heaven is allowed to carry out its affairs
and the King allows Earth to be submissive, it is accordance;
each attains its proper place,
and thus it is auspicious.
When the Zhēnrén receives this book,
reflect on it, reflect on it,
and entrust it to a ruler of superior virtue.
If he reflects on my text and puts it into practice,
it will be no different from the divine,
and Heaven will immediately provide help and assistance.
I have finished explaining the evidence of the heavenly prophecies to you briefly;
I wished to give a grand explanation for the Zhēnrén,
covering what is above Heaven and below Earth,
the Eight Extremes of the deep caverns, and the arrangement of the constellations,
explaining each one by one.
But the circulation of the subtle Way of Heaven
might instead cause a person to become confused
and not know where to go,
subsequently causing the True Dào to be cut off and not used,
with no means to resolve the disasters flowing from antiquity,
further causing those above to grieve.
Therefore, I only speak to you of the Great Divisions that are easy to know,
to make you aware, and that is all.
Thus I do not speak of the subtle things that are difficult to know;
it is not that I begrudge them.”
“Yes, indeed.
I beg to ask one more secret matter.
Just now, the Tiānshī explained the Ten Celestial Stems of Heaven to your humble student,
noting that they all have pairings.
The twelve branches of the Way of Earth
likewise have Yīn and Yáng, odd and even;
why is it that only Heaven receives pairings?”
“Excellent!
Your challenge
can be called reaching the essence of the Dào!
However, regarding Earth:
it is only in comparison to Heaven
that it is pure Yīn and dwells alone,
though it naturally possesses its own Yīn and Yáng.
The laws of Heaven and Earth
correspond to each other above and below:
Heaven has Zǐ,
and Earth also has Zǐ;
Heaven has Wǔ,
and Earth also has Wǔ;
Heaven has Kǎn,
and Earth also has Kǎn;
Heaven has Lí,
and Earth also has Lí;
their correspondence is like this.
Therefore, Chǒu and Wèi
are the back palaces of Yín.
Shēn belongs to Mǎo;
it is the son-in-law of the marquises and kings.
Hài is paired with Chén,
and Mǎo is paired with Xū.
Chén and Xū
are the wives within the household of the Grand Empress.
Yǒu belongs to Wǔ;
it is the Small Empress.
Zǐ belongs to Sì;
Sì is the son-in-law of the Emperor’s younger sister.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?”
“Yes, indeed.”
“Therefore, the Stems are the Emperors and Kings,
and the Branches are also the Emperors and Kings.
Thus, Yín
is the branch of Jiǎ,
which is why Chǒu and Wèi are called the back palaces.
Wǔ is—”
is the branch of Bǐng,
therefore Yǒu is called the Hòugōng.
Mǎo
is the branch of Yǐ,
therefore Shēn is called the son-in-law of the Hóuwáng.
Chén
is the branch of Wù,
therefore it is called the family of the Tài Huánghòu.
Hài
is the branch of Guǐ,
therefore it is called the daughter-in-law of the family of the Tài Huánghòu.
Zǐ
is the branch of Rén,
therefore it is called the son-in-law of the Dìwáng’s younger sister.
Sì
is the branch of Dīng,
therefore it is called the Dìwáng’s younger sister.
This is the method of correspondence and harmony between Heaven and Earth."
"Excellent, excellent!
I wish to hear about these lords Chén and Xū;
why is it that Wèi alone, if male, then they gather together,
and if female, then they marry together?
Why is this?"
"How subtle
is your challenge!
However, Heaven is ultimate Yáng,
and Earth is ultimate Yīn.
Earth is numerous,
being the leader of all things Yīn.
Yīn is usually of even numbers,
therefore they are paired."
"Now Wù and Jǐ both belong to the Earth,
why are they not paired?"
"Well asked!
As for Wù and Jǐ,
they are the fifth stems,
the Yáng of the Earth,
and their positions belong to Heaven,
therefore they are not paired.
Does the Zhēnrén understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Proceed,
you understand it.
Now the Zhēnrén's challenge is correct.
Now the characters of the Wǔxíng revolve and supplement one another
so as to complete all matters under Heaven.
When you obtain my book,
categorize and reflect upon its profound meanings yourself;
for the directions of above, below, the six sides, and the absolute voids are all prepared.
Therefore, the Shèngrén sees one thing and knows ten thousand,
the Dàxián sees one thing and knows a thousand,
but the fool, though shown with effort, remains solitary and confused,
unable to attain the truth of the Dào.
Therefore, the Dàodé is entrusted to the Zhēnrén.
Does the Zhēnrén understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Proceed,
you understand it."
"I wish to ask about one more matter.
If the Four Seasons of Heaven
and the Wǔxíng of Earth
all speak of the families of the Dìhuáng, Hóuwáng, and Hòugōng,
and the Heavenly Dào is entirely matched with them,
is there also a match among them for the common people and the myriad things?"
"Excellent
is your question!
It can be said that you have perceived the essence of the Great Dào.
However, these matches are the same.
As for the Wǔxíng,
at the top are always Dìwáng,
next are the Xiàng,
and next is the subtle Qì.
The flourishing Wáng state
is the position of Dìwáng.
The assisting Xiàng state
is the position of Great Ministers.
The subtle Qì
is the position of minor officials.
The old Qì that follows the Wáng state
is the position of Wáng and Hóu.
The declining Qì that follows the old Qì
is the position of the Zōngshì.
The ailing Qì that follows the declining Qì
is the image of the Zōngshì committing offenses and losing their status.
The imprisoned Qì that follows the ailing Qì
is the image of the common people and the myriad citizens.
The deathly Qì that follows the imprisoned Qì
is the image of slaves and servants.
The vanishing Qì that follows the deathly Qì
represents the mounds and tombs of the deceased.
Therefore, Heaven hangs down the images,
the Four Seasons and Wǔxíng circulate,
each with one rise and one decline.
The people and myriad things all follow the law of Heaven's images,
also having one rise and one decline.
Therefore, the myriad citizens and common people
are all descendants of the hundred Wáng;
when they rise, they become lords of men,
and when they decline, they become commoners.
Does the Zhēnrén understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"You already understand it."
The above uses Heavenly Prophecies to bring long-lasting peace to the state, to govern uncanny ministers, and to eliminate treachery, falsehood, and craftiness.
The Zhēnrén respectfully asked:
"I wish again to compile and correct all the various texts written by the Master from before and after,
to prevent students from speaking recklessly.
May I hear your instruction on this?"
"Excellent!
How you have become increasingly practiced and familiar in a single day!
Indeed, the methods of my Dào
come forth to regulate the Yáng
and enter to regulate the Yīn;
they come forth to regulate conduct
and enter to regulate the shén;
they come forth to regulate the many books
and enter to regulate the many diagrams;
they come forth to dispel disasters
and enter to rectify the self;
they come forth to regulate the learning of the Cháotíng
and internally to regulate entering the inner chamber.
In all things, there should be limits.
Diligent and eager students, each according to their talent and ability,
might conversely lose the constant laws;
external learning then leads them into superficiality,
which they cannot restrain;
internal learning then fails to correspond with the correct path,
returning instead to great heterodoxy.
Now, many students often suffer from a great ailment,
yet they cannot know it themselves.
Those who are fond of external learning,
whose talent is excessive,
mostly fall into superficiality,
causing the Dào to become greatly heterodox;
and lacking the correct texts,
they conversely call it the True Way,
further deceiving one another.
Those whose talent for internal learning is excessive
mostly fall into great heterodoxy,
thinking themselves to have attained it;
they do not speak with those around them,
conversely losing the laws and measures and transmitting reckless words.
Now that you have doubts,
you have therefore come again to ask about this.
Now, because your intent is good and sincere,
and you are diligent and without worry,
I shall establish rules and measures for them,
so that each has limits and degrees that can be deliberated upon,
serving as boundaries to be guarded.
Contemporary and ancient texts are numerous,
and cannot be fully limited.
In all learning, those who delight in obtaining true matters
must not deviate from their root.
Those who learn from the kǒu jué of a master
must not deviate from their master’s words;
this is the first great essential.
As for the great harm in learning:
conforming to external chapters and sentences
becomes daily more superficial, resulting in merely ornate writing and reckless speech;
entering internal texts and conforming to tú chèn,
one truly cannot deeply grasp the core and essential meaning,
conversely speaking in error.
Those who study cháng shēng and go forth,
yet conform to superficiality,
conversely deceive one another;
those who conform to the internal but do not grasp the essential meaning
conversely sink into great heterodoxy.
Since you have come to ask repeatedly,
I therefore lay out the texts for you
and show their limits;
those that conform to the laws and measures
are correct;
those that do not conform
are incorrect;
this is clear.
By this, one may know them.
In all writings intended as tiān tán,
those that correspond ten out of ten are correct;
those that correspond nine out of ten are slightly heterodox;
those that correspond eight out of ten are slightly disordered;
anything below this is not true
and cannot be used.
These are called disorders of the tiān wén and dì lǐ;
the Yīn and Yáng are not pleased,
the myriad things struggle and fight,
and the people suffer great calamity.
In the method of meditating on yǎng xìng,
if one internally sees the form and appearance
with clarity, it is correct;
if one externally sees the various spirits of the myriad things,
it is incorrect.
Those who learn about all matters
should always keep to the original text
and seek the explanations of various Worthies to stabilize them;
this is correct;
those who keep to various chapters and sentences but forget the original matter
are incorrect;
they have lost the intent of the Tiāndào.
Those that cause a person’s body to transform into a shén
are correct;
if the body lacks the Dào and does not become a shén,
yet one claims to command spirits,
this is incorrect;
it is merely a technique of using documents to drive them.
Explanations where the beginning, end, and middle of all matters are consistent are correct;
those that are not consistent are incorrect.
Upon entering the chamber, one first eats little,
then after a long time eats qì,
and then is liberated and disappears;
this is correct.
In seeking the Dào,
if one claims to have attained it and does not return,
yet there are those who inquire,
this is incorrect.
All who leave and return,
and are able to teach and answer questions, are correct;
whereas those who cannot teach or answer questions
are likely just dead.
Keeping to qīng jìng in a secluded chamber,
those who succeed are correct;
those who claim to have attained the practice of the Dào
yet speak with angry words
are incorrect;
they are people who have lost their jīng.
Entering into learning and becoming daily more virtuous,
surpassing one's former self and attaining the Dào—
this is correct;
entering into learning and conversely becoming daily more wicked,
becoming neither loyal nor trustworthy—
this is incorrect;
they have fallen into great heterodoxy.
Reading books and seeing their intent,
while keeping to a master to seek the kǒu jué and demonstrations of explanations—
this is correct;
reading books without the master’s kǒu jué,
while conversely claiming to possess profound and solitary knowledge—
this is incorrect;
internally, they have lost the significance and intent of the Dàdào.
Having studied and attained the Dào,
yet still serving various masters and Worthies without sloth—
this is correct;
this is the method of daily progress.
Thus, the ancient Shèngshī already knew the Dào,
yet they still served masters,
not daring to stop;
even after leaving a master, they read the texts without sloth.
Studying and then alone claiming to have obtained the essential meaning,
no longer striving to read the ancient texts and sagely words,
claiming oneself to be right
and not serving various sages and enlightened ones—
this is incorrect;
they are people of the lowest stupidity.
In all human learning,
exhausting the depths of what can be sought and learned—
this is correct.
The myriad things are all like this;
once the myriad things are born,
those that can fulfill their lifespan and bear fruit
are correct;
those that can only be born
but do not fulfill their lifespan,
and have no reliability or fruit—
these are incorrect.
Doing good and obtaining what is truly appropriate is correct;
not obtaining what is truly appropriate,
but being right on the outside and wrong on the inside, is incorrect.
Following and reading my books completely,
without departing from the plumb line and ink marker,
and obtaining their reality—
this is correct;
reading books and producing eccentricities,
having much talent but not obtaining the essential reality—
this is incorrect.
When Heaven has wind and rain and the myriad things grow in season—
this is correct;
when there is wind and rain and the myriad things are instead harmed—
this is incorrect;
there is poison.
Practicing the scriptures and the Dào and becoming daily more prosperous—
this is correct;
not daily moving toward prosperity,
but conversely moving daily toward decline—
or where the internal practice has lost the intent—
this is incorrect.
Therefore, by the nature of Heaven and Earth,
if one does good,
and it is not immediately seen in one's own person,
then it flows to future generations,
to clarify one's conduct;
if one does evil,
and it also does not immediately stop at one's own person,
it must flow to future generations,
also by erroneous signs clarifying one's conduct.
Therefore, for those who do good or evil,
it will certainly be seen.
However, for those who do good,
it is like facing the sunrise;
they will yet become manifest and bright;
for those who do evil,
it is like facing the sunset;
they will yet become dark and obscured.
This is the natural quality of the Yīn and Yáng of Heaven and Earth.
Heaven generates the myriad things,
and manifests each according to its conduct.
It is not concealed.
Therefore, those who are good ascend;
their fate belongs to Tiān,
just as living people belong to Tiān.
Those who are evil descend;
their fate belongs to the Earth,
just as the dead are evil;
thus they return below to Huángquán.
This is what is meant.
He who obtains my book
should entrust it to a Shàngdé Jūn.
Since I possess this book,
how could anyone dare to obstruct or intercept its transmission and reading?
The Tiāndào governs Tiān;
it cannot be fully known,
nor should one listen to and believe only the words of a single person.
I have now, for your sake, established the writings of the ancient Shèng;
I now further require their matching schemes,
clarifying how the beginning and end of the book follow one another to corroborate each other.
Since the opening of Tiāndì,
although the Xián Shèng were born in different ages
and were far removed from one another,
the things they detested were the same.
Together they spoke for Tiān
to save the world from its gains and losses;
their words are similar,
just like overlapping compasses and matching squares,
successively illuminating one another,
as it must be.
When things of the same category gather and arise,
the principle is always that they summon each other through the comparison of categories and images;
this is a clear effect.
Because there were failures in the past
and successes later,
I have examined and aligned the similarities and differences to form these writings.
By holding to the ancient to illuminate the present
and jointly discussing these matters,
one uses the inner texts
to illuminate the outer texts,
and uses the outer texts
to return to examine and connect them to the inner texts.
Thus they may be transmitted for ten thousand generations
without repeating offenses against Tiān.
The words of one person
cannot be followed alone.
The words of many people,
which deeply plan and take the sayings of the ancient Xián Shèng,
are internally identical to Tiān;
they are jointly established and set forth.
The Dìwáng will daily become more enlightened and resolve difficulties,
all confusion, disorder, disasters, and evils will be eliminated,
Tiān will have no further grief,
those who act together will flourish,
while the disasters of those who resist and oppose will not be removed.
To the right is the Xuézhě Déshī Jué.
The Zhēnrén bowed twice,
"May I ask about one matter?"
"Indeed, speak of it."
"Today the Tiānshī, on behalf of the Qi of Tàipíng, has come forth to bestow the Dao and De,
in order to bring prosperity to the Supreme Sovereign.
Above, there are rulers who love the Dao and De,
and this reaches down to the ignorant and lowly common people.
Its grace thus penetrates the Liùhé
and permeates the Bājí;
there is nothing it does not encompass.
Now I, Xiánróu, have received the Master’s teachings and studied them.
When I contemplate practicing the Dao,
what is its ultimate end at the highest level,
and what is its final limit at the lowest?"
"Excellent!
The Zhēnrén’s question
is truly subtle and essential.
Do you wish to hear of the ultimate depths
and understand the progress and retreat of the divine spirits?"
"Indeed, I am ignorant and obscured;
I am incapable of reaching the core of matters.
I only ask that the enlightened Tiānshī record and demonstrate it."
"Agreed.
The Dao has nine degrees,
distinguished by different names.
Now I shall explain their meanings in detail for the Zhēnrén;
follow along and record them,
and do not allow anything to be lost."
"Yes, Master."
"Indeed.
The first matter is called Yuánqì Wúwéi,
the second is Níngjìng Xūwú,
the third is Shùdù Fēnbié Kějiàn,
the fourth is Shényóu Chūqù Ér Huánfǎn,
the fifth is Dàdào Shén, which corresponds to the four seasons and five elements,
the sixth is Cìxǐ,
the seventh is Shèmóu,
the eighth is Yángshén,
and the ninth is Jiāxiān.
Each of these nine matters is further divided into nine,
making eighty-one sections in total.
If one uses their various forms and different writings secretly,
they together form one great root,
using spirits as messengers
and humans as portals.
Now I shall categorize the secret keys for you,
but they cannot all be recorded in advance.
Contemplate their meaning for yourself.
The top three-times-nine, twenty-seven,
can allow one to transcend the world.
The middle three-times-nine, twenty-seven,
can allow one to employ true spirit officials.
As for the bottom three-times-nine, twenty-seven,
their ways are often deviant,
and their spiritual essence cannot be constantly employed.
They make a person feel dazed and confused.
Among them are occasionally unrefined people
who often lose their way and speak wildly,
as if they have lost their Qi."
"Now, hearing the Master's words,
I am dazzled and confused, not knowing east from west.
I wish for you to explain them separately for me, your lowly student."
"Indeed.
The first of the highest, Yuánqì Wúwéi,
is to contemplate one's own body
without performing a single action,
but merely thinking of one's body as hollow and white,
as if abandoned to the Qi and formless.
Always taking this as the method,
once accomplished, there is nothing one cannot do and nothing one does not know.
Thus, when a person lacks the Dao,
they are merely human;
but once they obtain the Dao, they transform into a Shénxiān.
Their spirit ascends to heaven
and changes along with heaven;
this is what is meant by 'nothing one cannot do.'
The second is Xūwú Zìrán,
which is to guard the form in a state that is hollow, void, and spontaneous,
without any strangeness.
Within the body, it is illuminated with white;
from top to bottom, it is like jade,
without any blemish.
Practicing this for a long time
is also a technique to transcend the world;
this is second only to the image of Yuánqì Wúwéi.
The third is Shùdù,
which is to accumulate essence and look back at oneself,
counting from the hair down to the feet,
distinguishing the five fingers,
and observing the appearance of the body, both outside and inside;
none go uncounted.
Knowing its intent,
one should always keep this in mind
without missing even a tiny fraction.
This is also a minor technique for transcending the world,
second to Xūwú.
The fourth is Shényóu Chūqù,
which is to contemplate the spirits of the five viscera
as they enter and exit by day;
seeing them travel about,
one can speak with them.
Thinking of following the spirits back and forth,
one also clearly sees the body.
This allows one to know good and bad fortune;
it is second to Shùdù.
The fifth is Dàdào Shén.
When a person's spirit goes out,
