it corresponds with the five elements and four seasons:
green, red, white, yellow, and black.
All join with the visceral spirits
in their coming and going.
The spirit officials of the four seasons and five elements serve the person;
this is called 'Possessing the Dao'
and can subdue all evils.
The sixth is Cìxǐ,
which involves striking the ground with a probe.
The spirits of the Dao each have their own regulations;
using their family methods,
one worships spirits who come to visit.
Half are like the true
and half seem deviant.
It often makes people fond of trickery
and cannot be constantly used;
eventually, it distresses people.
The seventh is Shèmóu,
where the spirits of heaven and earth, the four seasons,
the altars of soil and grain, and mountains and rivers
descend upon the person.
It makes the person dazed
and prone to speaking wildly of those spirits.
It is violent, vengeful, mad, and deviant;
it must not be practiced recklessly.
The eighth is Yángshén,
which means its spirits are vast and drifting.
Its way has nothing to bind to;
the essence and Qi of the world descend upon the person.
It makes the person speak wildly;
half is like the true
and half is like the deviant.
The ninth is Jiāxiān.
In Jiāxiān, one only sees ghosts
and there is no true Dao.
If there are those who are summoned,
they are only the ghosts of the dead.
This is the lowest extremity of the Dao
and is called the way of the Xiàshì.
Those who obtain the higher Dao
can also employ the lower;
but those who obtain the lower Dao
cannot employ the higher."
"Now I wish to hear why there are these high and low levels."
"Indeed.
This
is caused by human conduct.
Those who guard the root obtain the high levels;
those who like the spirits of the body wandering in and out obtain the middle;
and ignorant people damage their root to guard the branches,
so those who follow wandering spirits from elsewhere obtain the low.
Those who guard the root can see all of them;
those who guard the middle see half;
and those who guard the branches cannot return to the Dao of self-reflection.
Therefore, all students
must find an enlightened master.
If they do not find an enlightened master,
they will lose their way.
Thus, from master to master it is passed,
firmer than metal or stone.
If it is not passed through a master,
it is called reckless action
and will lead to misfortune and evil.
Zhēnrén, be careful, be careful!"
"Yes, Master."
"Therefore, in ancient times, the highest students were sages and worthies.
Finding an enlightened master was called 'Rebirth';
those who did not find an enlightened master
were called 'Disturbers of the Classics.'
Thus, worthies and sages all served masters to achieve success.
Without a master,
the Dao does not arise on its own."
"Wonderful, wonderful!"
"If the Zhēnrén wishes to know the effect,
it is like a person living in a neighborhood of great worthies,
which makes that person a great worthy;
living in a neighborhood of middle worthies
makes that person a middle worthy;
and living in a neighborhood of the unworthy
makes that person unworthy
and always failing to measure up.
This is what it means.
Those who study this Dao
must examine it minutely and in detail.
This is the essential Dao of Heaven.
Be careful, be careful!"
"Yes, Master."
"Go forth;
the Dao returns to its person
to be entrusted to the worthy and enlightened."
"Yes, Master.
This is the essential Dao of the divine secrets."
To the right is the Textual Formula for the Gain and Loss in the Nine Sections of the True Way (Zhēndào Jiǔshǒu Déshī Wénjué).
The Zhēnrén asked the Shénrén:
“In receiving the Dào, what should one take as a precept?”
The Shénrén said:
“The Dào indeed has a great precept,
and one must not fail to be cautious regarding it.
When one is about to obtain the Dào
and is on the verge of its completion,
one then forms bonds with the various gods,
becomes a neighbor to the spirits,
sees them when going out and coming in,
and loves them
as father and son love each other.
Now, the Dào
is a weighty matter.
Sometimes the gods regret giving it to a person
and wish to take the Dào away.
Therefore, they first test the person
to see if the person is firm.
They come together to deceive the person,
making the person speak recklessly.
Once they obtain his words,
he should keep them tightly closed
and cautiously avoid transmitting them.
Then he can obtain long life
and, in time, obtain the Zhēndào.
If he transmits them, he will waste away day by day,
and it also causes people to love life yet hate harm.”
The Zhēnrén said:
“I wish to hear the meaning of wasting away day by day.”
“When the spirits waste away,
the body then dies.
The Dào of Emptiness and Absolute Profundity (Xūwú Juédòng zhī Dào)
always wishes to make people love life and hate killing.
If one keeps the mouth closed and does not leak secrets,
then one may live for ten thousand times ten thousand years.”
The Zhēnrén asked the Shénrén:
“I wish to hear the prohibitions against leaking secrets.”
The Shénrén said:
“Thus:
if a great person leaks them, he loses his position;
if a person of middle standing leaks them,
his vital breath is severed;
if a lesser person leaks them,
his lineage is exterminated.
The reason it is so
is that Heaven and Earth use this to distinguish themselves and for their own privacy;
therefore, the spirits value it even more highly.”
“If Heaven and Earth did not deeply know the Dào of Absolute Profundity,
how could they be divine?
How could they have long life?
Record this;
I tell you,
refine it, value it, and be cautious with it.”
The Zhēnrén said:
“Yes, yes,
I do not dare to speak recklessly.”
The Zhēnrén bowed his head and said:
“I wish further to hear how they intend to ruin a person—
how is that done?”
The Shénrén said:
“Thus:
when there is an evil intent in a person’s heart,
it causes a Great Evil (Dàxié) to come and deceive him.
If the person can remain firmly closed
and not listen to its words,
then it is auspicious;
if he listens to its words,
then it is ominous and harmful.
If a ruler of men listens to it,
he will hate his ministers,
saying his ministers are disloyal and untrustworthy and wish to rebel.
If a minister or son listens to it,
he will hate his ruler or father.
The evil comes to deceive him,
saying ‘You shall now become a sage,’
or ‘You shall now become a ruler of men.’
If a common person listens to it,
it causes him to say of himself that he shall be greatly honored.
If a father listens to it, he hates his son;
if a son listens to it, he hates his father.
It distorts and changes its words
to delude the human heart and mind,
speaking of things that are partly good and partly evil,
disordering a person’s governance,
causing sudden joy or sudden anger.
This is the Great Flattery of Evil;
it seeks to harm people.
From ancient times until now,
among all those who study longevity,
none can escape these words.”
The Zhēnrén asked:
“What should be done?”
The Shénrén said:
“Close the ears and do not listen;
close the mouth and do not speak.
This is merely flattering evil;
there is nothing worth listening to.
If one listens to it, then the Zhēndào departs;
once it departs, one dies.
If you wish to endure long,
be cautious
of these words. I have already experienced this for you before;
how many have been struck by this Dàxié!
I always rectify my own heart
and no longer use it.
This Dàxié often accumulates,
wishing to observe whether a person is firm.
This Great Slipperiness of Evil often deludes;
it then enters a person’s belly,
moves the person’s heart,
and causes the person’s heart to act recklessly.
From time to time one becomes angry or joyful
and cannot restrain oneself;
all are led astray by the evil.
Being pushed by the evil,
the multitudes are brought to destruction. Those who have fallen to this are numerous;
if one truly obtains the weighty precept,
the heart also cannot be moved.
This is not only for those who study the Way.
When the common people have inconsistent joy and anger,
it is the same as what you may experience.
Be cautious and refine yourself.”
The Zhēnrén said:
“Yes, yes.”
The Zhēnrén said:
“My own person was once struck by the Dàxié,
which caused me to want to run and
say that I should become a master of men,
and later that I should become a flying transcendent and ascend to heaven.
I accepted its words
and believed them with great joy.
Afterward, for three months, I suffered from a fit of madness.
I saw a Shénrén and Heavenly Master (Tiānshī) speak,
and my heart felt great delight and joy.
I personally experienced such a thing;
I nearly had a severe illness.
Later the madness stopped by itself and I was healed,
and thus I obtained several thousand years of life.
Now I am fortunate to again see the Shénrén
and repeat the precepts of the Way,
to behold the gateway,
hoping to attain long endurance and become an official of the heavens.”
The Shénrén said:
“If you hold your heart’s intent as firmly as this,
why worry about not ascending to the Nine Heavens (Jiǔtiān)
and traveling through the Twenty-five Heavens (Èrshíwǔ Tiān)?
Now, all those scholars who have ascended to heaven
were able to hold their hearts firmly and secretly
and could not be led astray.
All those who can be deluded and led astray
instead die early
and cannot be saved.
If you wish to obtain long life,
read this text and take it as a weighty precept;
this is a precept of life and death,
and one must not fail to be cautious.
Therefore, the sages and worthies of old who first attained transcendence
did so by the power of not listening to this.
Those who study the Dào but instead do not obtain it and do not endure long
all suffer because they listened to this
and encountered its malice.
The Great Spirits of the Heavens are not malicious;
it is what a person does
that makes them return to this harm and restriction,
and thus they have no great blessing.
When they should live, they instead die,
turning into enemies of heaven.
Now the writings I have taught to the Zhēnrén
can all lead to great longevity.
Some may attain transcendence;
just cautiously maintain yourself
and do not let this become a harm.
If you can truly focus your heart,
you can live for ten thousand times ten thousand years.”
The Zhēnrén said:
“Yes, yes.
I do not dare to do wrong;
I request to receive the bright precepts.” The Shénrén said:
“You love the Dào like this;
once you succeed in your practice,
you will have obtained the ladder to heaven.”
The Zhēnrén asked:
“Is this the only precept?
Or are there more profound ones?”
“There are further precepts of the heavens,
which firmly caution a person.
They specifically caution against words used to deceive people together,
saying that a person will become honored and noble,
using this to caution a person.
For this reason, it causes a person to touch upon prohibitions
and be executed for it.”
Again, people are repeatedly tested with *yù nǚ*,
who are made to wander together with them.
Those who stop will together laugh at the person's lowliness
and return to harm the person's body.
But if a person remains constantly silent,
for ten thousand years there will be nothing to hear.
If one alone guards the end of their life,
what harm can there be?
Between death and life,
it depends solely on this."
The *zhēn rén*
said, "Indeed, indeed."
The *zhēn rén* asked:
"Why do you specifically send evil spirits to test people?"
The *shén rén* said:
"The *dào* is weighty
and difficult to give to others.
Their resolve must be firm.
For those who would die for it,
their wishes will not be taken away.
Those who transcend the world in the heavens
do not crave honor or wealth.
For those who only take pleasure in living,
there is no extraordinary *dào*.
Remember my admonitions,
my son.
My words must not be forgotten for ten thousand generations.
Even if one travels upward through the exhaustive and flawless heavens,
the admonitions are all like this;
there is nothing more extraordinary."
The *zhēn rén*
said, "Indeed, indeed.
I dare not deviate from the boundaries of the rules."
The *shén rén* said:
"If it is truly as you say,
you have already attained the *dào*.
The auspicious advance daily,
and the evil shall cease.
By maintaining the heart like this,
the divine precepts are completed.
When the task is finished,
you will ride the clouds and drive dragons,
wandering throughout the eight extremities.
The *dà dào* is level and broad;
you have already attained it.
Your life shall be of infinite longevity."
The *zhēn rén* said:
"Indeed, indeed."
The *shén rén* said:
"The *dào* is truly great, with no inside or outside.
But there is always the fear of being harmed by great evil.
If one does not listen to even a single evil thing,
where can evil cause defeat?
Thus, ancient emperors and kings who loved the *dào* and studied it
and did not listen to the evil
all attained ten thousand upon ten thousand years of life.
Those who listened to and used evil words
all met their own defeat.
My *dào* has ten thousand facets;
you must know all their benefits and harms."
The *zhēn rén*
said, "Indeed, indeed.
Having now received the words of the *shén rén*,
will I obtain long life in an instant?"
The *shén rén* said:
"Without deep caution,
the outcome will be disastrous,
and the *dào* cannot be attained."
The *zhēn rén* said:
"Does my life have a predestined fortune?
It is a stroke of luck
that I have encountered the *shén rén*."
The *shén rén* said:
"True.
The six types of people each have their own destiny.
The first is the *shén rén*,
the second is the *zhēn rén*,
the third is the *xiān rén*,
the fourth is the *dào rén*,
the fifth is the *shèng rén*,
and the sixth is the *xián rén*.
All these assist Heaven in its governance.
The *shén rén* presides over Heaven,
the *zhēn rén* presides over Earth,
the *xiān rén* preside over wind and rain,
the *dào rén* preside over teaching, transformation, and fortune,
the *shèng rén* preside over the governance of the common people,
and the *xián rén* assist the *shèng rén*
in managing the records of the myriad people
and providing aid where the six harmonies are deficient.
Thus, every person’s life has its own destiny.
A noble destiny cannot be made lowly,
and a lowly destiny cannot be made noble.
If you wish to know the truth of it,
consider that although a fish relies on water,
it cannot fly because of the water's vapors.
A dragon also relies on water,
but does it not rely on the water's vapors to ascend to the blue clouds and become a messenger of Heaven?
Nobility and lowliness truly depend on destiny.
Fools speak recklessly.
Ancient *shèng rén*, emperors, and kings,
those of great excellence,
no longer recorded or questioned false words,
knowing them to be such;
in the end, nothing could be done about them.
This is like teaching a person without the *dào*
and ordering them to fly suddenly—
how could they possibly fly?
Those who can fly
are only the *xiān rén* who have attained the *dào*.
When the common people play together
and say, 'I can fly,'
they actually cannot fly;
such are those who speak recklessly.
The *zhēn rén* said:
"Excellent!
I have been enlightened on this matter."
The *shén rén* said:
"You yourself were like a fool;
can the mandate of Heaven be obtained through force?"
The *zhēn rén* said:
"Indeed.
But can this *dào* also be learned?"
The *shén rén* said:
"Indeed.
Those with a heavenly mandate
can learn it and will surely attain great capacity.
A *zhōng xián* who learns it
can also attain great longevity.
A lower fool who practices it
can attain a short longevity.
If you wish to know its efficacy,
it is just like an ordinary person studying.
A *dà xián* who studies can attain a high office,
a *zhōng xián* who studies can attain a middle office,
and a fool who studies can become a minor clerk.
Does the minor clerk not serve the common people in white robes?
Speaking from this perspective,
one should still strive to learn."
The *zhēn rén*
said, "Indeed, indeed.
In my practice,
I have never dared to be lax."
The *shén rén* said:
"True.
Effortfully believe in the *dào*.
Between Heaven and Earth,
each takes what is appropriate,
and there is no recklessness."
The *zhēn rén*
said, "Indeed, indeed.
I request to honor Heaven and respect Earth,
revere those above and love those below,
and follow the four seasons and five elements in my actions;
I dare not do what is wrong."
The *shén rén* said:
"Excellent, excellent!
You have grasped the essence of the *dào*.
I shall not teach or show you again."
To the right is the text for attracting good and removing evil to make people receive the precepts of the *dào*.
The *liù fāng zhēn wén* all bowed twice and asked:
"We previously heard the *tiān shī* say
that the *tài píng qì* is about to arrive.
To harmonize Yin and Yang,
one must first harmonize the spirits and deities,
returning them to their respective places.
We have deeply reflected on the *tiān shī*'s words;
those who can turn back their light and illuminate within
can see them one by one.
Those people are numerous;
how can this be achieved?
Can the various *dào shì* who can turn back their light
gather them together?"
"Ah!
Most excellent.
The *huáng qì* of Heaven is about to arrive,
and emperors and kings shall rule with folded arms and no worries.
Therefore, Heaven has sent various *zhēn rén* to inquire about the essentials of the Supreme *dào*,
which can be used by an enlightened ruler of great *dào* and virtue to completely remove the lingering disasters and inherited burdens of former kings,
as well as the evil Qi between Heaven and Earth,
and the harm caused by ghosts, calamities, and various misfortunes.
This is why the *zhēn rén* have come,
to personally ask about these essentials of the Supreme *dào*.
Do the disciples also know themselves?"
"Suddenly, we do not know ourselves."
"If you suddenly do not know yourselves,
why do you ask about it?"
"Reflecting on the teachings and commands of the Tiānshī,
regarding those parts I do not understand,
I do not currently know for myself
how it is possible to gather all these profound, void, tranquil, and light-reflecting spirits to be able to see evil ones.
Wondering about this,
I have come together with others now to ask about it."
"Excellent!
The Zhēnrén has progressed in diligence
to know to doubt this.
Heaven has sent you
to fully inquire on behalf of the Déjūn about how to resolve the matter of evil ones."
"I shall."
"Now I shall speak fully for the Zhēnrén,
distinguishing and explaining the essential meaning;
sit peacefully and record it together." "Yes, yes."
"Heaven and Earth naturally possess divine treasures,
and all naturally have divine essential light.
They take on colors according to the Wǔxíng,
and rise or decline according to the Qì of the Sìshí.
They serve as messengers for Heaven and Earth to complete the people and all things.
Between the Yīn and Yáng of Heaven and Earth,
there is nothing that is not transformed by their virtue and born therefrom.
Those who grasp the meaning can see it immediately;
those who do not grasp the great essential meaning
have no portal through which to know it.
Those who can greatly open and use it will have great good fortune
and can eliminate the ailments, suffering, and evil categories of people between Heaven and Earth.
For those who do not know the great law,
the spirits cannot be obtained by vainly or emptily summoning them,
nor can they be obtained or used in vain or emptiness."
"I wish to hear the meaning
so that it may be passed down for ten thousand generations without error."
"Excellent
is your question.
However, if one wishes to wait for and obtain the technique,
there is naturally a great law.
The Qì of the Sìshí and Wǔxíng enters the human belly
to become the spirits of the human Wǔzàng;
their colors correspond to the colors of the Sìshí of Heaven and Earth.
Paint them in human form;
make them a triple combination.
The flourishing Qì color covers the outside,
the assisting Qì color is next,
and the subtle Qì resides most within.
Make them manifest as leaders.
First fast and abstain, staying in a secluded and peaceful place;
contemplate them and keep them in mind.
Create painted images of those persons,
their height as you wish.
For the five persons,
create them together on five feet of plain silk.
Make them good and virtuous;
men contemplate men,
women contemplate women;
the painted images should be like this.
There are already many books on this,
not just one version.
From top to bottom, deliberate on the meaning of the texts and act accordingly,
using the written word to transmit and clarify it subtly.
Although my books are numerous,
they naturally have major divisions.
Books are gathered according to their categories,
and characters clarify each other;
then you will fully obtain the essential meaning."
"Yes, yes."
"These essential spirits of the Sìshí and Wǔxíng
enter to become the Wǔzàng spirits of humans
and go out to become the essential spirits of the Sìshí and Wǔxíng.
Those close to humans
are called the spirits of the Wǔdé,
which are similar to the human visceral spirits.
Those distant from humans
are called the Yánglì,
with the name Soldiers and Horses of the Sìshí.
They can be used to ward off evil
and also move according to the decline and flourishing of the Sìshí Qì.
The method
is to prepare painted images for them.
The figures also wear triple layers of clothing:
the flourishing Qì is on the outside,
the assisting Qì is next,
and the subtle Qì is most inward.
All wear caps and headbands and ride horses;
the horses also follow the colors of the Wǔxíng in their preparation.
First paint the images on one side,
two Zhàng in length,
on five pieces of silk, sparsely painting five times five, making twenty-five riders;
do it well.
The riding spirits of the East hold spears;
the riding spirits of the South hold halberds;
the riding spirits of the West hold bows, crossbows, and axes;
the riding spirits of the North hold shields and knives;
the riding spirits of the Center hold swords and drums.
When contemplating them, one should first see these internal spirits,
then see these external spirits.
Or one might first see the Yáng spirits and later see the internal spirits.
Seeing them is favorable.
This
is the method of the formless.
One also must obtain the oral instructions and teachings of a teacher.
At the very top, there is a gateway; those who know it
will then find it easy.
It is said,
that to make it easy to summon and easy to accomplish,
one should stay far from people,
doing it in a convenient and quiet place;
it is easy to gather them.
If close to people, it will surely be difficult to accomplish.
When the Dào is accomplished,
it is said to gather the 'Bright Great Transcendent Light-Reflecting Spirits of the Profound.'
The forms of illness will not be many.
If they are many, it is auspicious;
if few, it is ominous."
"If there are some that cannot be reached
or cured and resolved,
how many must be obtained for it to be acceptable?"
"The highest number is ten thousand;
the middle is four or five thousand;
the lowest is dozens or hundreds,
such as over a hundred."
"Why so many?"
"Ah!
Is the Zhēnrén being foolish again?
Sit peacefully,
and I shall speak the great essential meaning for you.
Now, following the Chéngfù,
Heaven and Earth have many disasters,
and the calamities and misfortunes caused by ghosts, old spirits, and corpses are not just one.
Furthermore, there are wind, dampness, ulcers, and scabies.
In the current late age, the flowing disasters are numerous
and cannot be fully named.
One person may have a hundred diseases,
or several dozen diseases.
Suppose each person has their own strengths
or their own weaknesses.
Or each can remove one disease.
Like a master of divination who knows the causes,
they remove one disease caused by misfortune or curses.
A great physician skilled in medicinal prescriptions
removes another disease.
An acupuncture master skilled in needling the meridians
removes another disease.
Or someone skilled in moxibustion
removes another disease.
Or someone skilled in incantations
removes another disease.
Or someone skilled in sacrifice
removes another disease.
Or someone skilled in employing spirits to guide them and see ghosts
removes another disease.
Here are seven people,
each removing one disease,
which only removes seven diseases.
In this late age, people have many diseases;
one person may have dozens of diseases,
and there are even those who say they have a hundred diseases in their body,
all of which are pain and suffering.
Even if all the skilled masters
each remove one disease,
this only removes seven diseases.
The remaining diseases stay as they were,
not completely removed.
The strength of the seven masters is exhausted,
but these remaining diseases are not gone.
They still afflict the person,
who eventually reaches exhaustion.
Therefore, many die,
unable to save themselves from distress.
How long is a human life compared to its natural span?
How many diseases does one see?
How much distress does one encounter
through the rise, decline, progress, and retreat of life?
The laws of Heaven
are like the rise and decline of the Sìshí and Wǔxíng.
The Eight Trigrams, Qián and Kūn,
are the substance of Heaven and Earth,
yet even they have times of rest, imprisonment, waste, exhaustion, and low Qì.
How much more so for humans?
Humans
resemble Heaven and Earth,
following the Sìshí, Wǔxíng, Liùhé, and the eight directions,
rising once and declining once,
without any end to this cycle.
Therefore, one should prepare in advance,
saving the source of good and bad fortune.
In safety, do not forget danger;
in existence, do not forget perishability;
in order, do not forget chaos.
Then one can endure for a long time.
For this reason, in the method of treating evil,
do not say a person's diseases are not many.
If one person can remove one disease,
then ten people remove ten diseases,
a hundred people remove a hundred diseases,
a thousand people remove a thousand diseases,
and ten thousand people remove ten thousand diseases.
How could one person's body
have ten thousand diseases?
Therefore, one is able to completely treat and resolve them all.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Therefore, I teach them to take precautions in advance;
those who complete the Way are those who gather them."
"Yes, yes."
"Well,"
"you know this."
"Well,"
"I shall clearly set it forth for the Zhēnrén."
"As for the illness treated here,"
"it is the great evil of ghosts and spirits,"
"which together act as bandits."
"Now, when emperors and kings are at peace,"
"they always maintain a Jūnshī. Soldiers"
"are for preparing against others;"
"if they instead act without righteousness, they become treacherous bandits."
"Thus, if one man dares to die,"
"ten men dare not oppose him;"
"if ten men dare to die,"
"one hundred men dare not oppose them;"
"if one hundred men dare to die,"
"one thousand men dare not oppose them;"
"if one thousand men dare to die,"
"ten thousand men dare not oppose them;"
"if ten thousand men dare to die, they can travel freely in all directions.
To prepare for illnesses and injuries,"
"the Jūnshī maintain twelve thousand men,"
"in order to prepare for the extraordinary."
"As for those two thousand men,"
"they are merely maintained to replace those who rest or desert,"
"and thus can they be brought to submission."
"Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Well,"
"you already know this."
"I beg to ask one thing of the Tiānshī:"
"now that the Qi of Tàipíng is about to arrive,"
"should not the evil Qi naturally cease and be removed?"
"It is so,"
"your words are correct,"
"and yet they are also incorrect."
"Indeed,"
"when the Qi of Tàipíng arrives,"
"evil certainly should dissipate of its own accord."
"However, since the opening of heaven and earth, a long time has passed,"
"and evil Qi is vast and numerous,"
"being transmitted through generations as Chéngfù."
"Even though the governing Qi of Tàipíng has arrived,"
"how could it all be suddenly and completely removed in a single day?"
"Therefore, one must prepare for it in advance."
"If one waits until the methods are
exhausted,"
"and only then seeks out skilled craftsmen,"
"it will already be far too late."
"In high antiquity,"
"everyone knew the Zhēndào,"
"and there was little evil Qi at that time."
"Since supreme and middle antiquity,"
"people have become increasingly foolish,"
"fond of superficial flashiness,"
"and they do not practice the Zhēndào."
"Furthermore, there is much evil Qi, wild spirits, and calamities,"
"so people often come to a sudden end"
"before their natural lifespan is reached and die."
"This is all because their minds are foolish and darkened,"
"not knowing how to prevent it at the root."
"Now that a Shàngdé Jūn governs,"
"Heaven loves him,"
"and does not wish for so many of these foolish people to reach such an end."
"He should be made to fulfill his great virtue,"
"and be of one heart with Heaven."
"Thus, Heaven has sent the various Zhēnrén to ask about their doubts,"
"and has ordered me to set forth for them the methods"
"to suppress and ward off evil, inauspiciousness, and demonic wickedness."
"Therefore, I have spoken of this in detail for the Zhēnrén."
"Now, the Zhēnrén conversely says it will disappear on its own without preparation;"
"this statement is wrong,"
"and is known as the talk of a Jūnzǐ who is greatly mistaken."
"Your words cannot be used."
"What do you mean?"
"Well,"
"if there is a great emergency"
"and only then do you seek it out,"
"it cannot be obtained suddenly,"
"and it causes people to fall into distress."
"Thus, the words of the Zhēnrén are a great error,"
"and cannot be used."
"Only when grain is accumulated to fill the granaries"
"can one be prepared for hunger."
"Now I explain this clearly for the Zhēnrén,"
"so that it may not be forgotten for ten thousand generations."
"Yes, yes."
"If you only teach people to plant grain when they are already hungry,"

"waiting for the rice to be ready"

"By then, they will have already died of hunger and distress."
"Or if one fails to plant in the spring,"
"and in winter, feeling hungry and thinking of food,"

"the planting will not grow."
"How could this be done in time to save lives?"
"Not only is the individual in distress,"

"This is one great folly of the Zhēnrén,"
"the great effect of having no knowledge of the Míngmíng."
"Well,"
"I shall tell you of another matter:"
"The reason people dig wells"

"One should dwell near a spring"

"If one is facing death from thirst"

"One is already finished."
"This question of the Zhēnrén"
"is a second instance of foolish darkness."
"I shall tell the Zhēnrén of another matter:"
"In ancient times, people lived in caves,"

"When there is no wind or rain,"

"This is the third folly of the Zhēnrén."
"I shall tell the Zhēnrén of another matter:"
"Since supreme and middle antiquity,"

"When the unexpected occurs"

"This is an effect of the Zhēnrén's severe foolishness and darkness."
"Well,"
"I shall tell the Zhēnrén of another matter:"
"Now, the Jūnshī and weapons"

"Therefore, they should be placed in scabbards,"

"Yes, yes."

"Proceed.
You have already awakened.
Therefore, I am especially urgent. This
death
is the greatest misfortune in the world.
