the inferior fool does not awaken,
but instead laughs at my writings for not being prepared in their roots,
and thus they exhaust themselves.
For Heaven, Earth, and the Emperors,
nothing surpasses this.
Now that the Tàipíng Qì is arriving
and a ruler of Yáng Dé is governing,
they should obtain longevity.
Whenever people in the world die,
it is no small matter.
Once dead,
through all eternity one can never again see Heaven, Earth, the sun, or the moon;
the vessels and bones become mud and earth.
Mortal life
is a weighty matter.
When people dwell between Heaven and Earth,
everyone gets one life
and cannot get another life.
Those who get another life are only those people of the Dào
who die and return to life,
the ones who achieve Shījiě.
As for these,
they are favored by Heaven and Earth;
among ten million, there is not even one.
Therefore, once a common person dies,
they cannot live again.
Thus, one should greatly prepare for it.
Even in years of Tàipíng Qì and joy,
there is still evil Qì.
It is like a family that, although good,
still has wicked people within it;
they just tolerate each other.
For this reason, one should increasingly gather masters of Dào and arts;
if things are not right,
they should always eliminate it.
If it is not quickly eliminated,
then it will grow.
Therefore, I teach you to prepare beforehand and increase their numbers.
The reason Great Learning increases the number of people of Dào and Dé
is to prepare so they may be obtained;
if one does not store and gather them beforehand,
they cannot be obtained suddenly when sought.
If there is an emergency
and one wishes to ask about parallels between past and present,
without having a prior abundance of people of Dào and Dé,
no one will be able to suddenly respond and explain.
This causes the ruler to be darkened and obscured;
when there is a sudden matter of doubt
and asking about it does not resolve the distress in time,
and only afterward does one go to seek sages and masters of arts in distant regions,
how can that compare to the earnestness of those present before you?
Does the Zhēnrén know this?" "Yes, indeed."
"Proceed.
You have already had a great awakening."
"Although every time I speak there is blame and reprimand,
if I do not ask, I will again not know.
I wish to have one matter resolved."
"Speak of it."
"Now, if these people at high levels number ten thousand,
at middle levels several thousand,
and at low levels several hundred,
how can they be suddenly obtained and suddenly perfected?"
"Excellent
is your question.
Just teach ten or so people to achieve it with goodness,
and they will naturally pass it on to each other,
with urgent effects
and those who achieve success.
Let the sovereign of superior Dé and Dào value and love them;
bestow rewards upon those who have merit,
and the multitude will then desire it.
When they desire it and follow in great numbers,
make them practice it,
and let all respect and love those who succeed.
The spirits and essences of the four seasons, five elements, Heaven, and Earth,
seeing them respected and loved,
will all be pleased and happy,
making people fortunate and prosperous.
The virtuous ruler will long enjoy that auspicious blessing,
and all from the sages down to the commoners and fools
will strive and desire to do it.
Thus the practitioners will increase daily;
over a long time,
great and small will all be transformed.
When everyone can do it,
then select from among them those with the greatest merit and gather them all;
appoint those with great merit to their positions,
and give rewards to those with small merit.
No one in the world will not want to do it.
I only fear there will be too many
to be recorded.
Why worry about there being too few?
How can the Zhēnrén be so greatly foolish, dark, and ignorant!
One matter is greatly resolved:
Do not employ those who are merely fond of big talk;
such people are of no benefit to others.
Simply test their methods;
those who consistently have success
are people who have obtained the intent of the Dào
and are of great trustworthiness.
Know that those who have only words
and no great effects
are those who have not obtained the intent of the Dào and speak falsely;
they are greatly glib people
who cannot be used,
for they are disturbers of the Dào.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Go now,
be cautious and take heed.
Recite and read my books,
think only on the meaning of their beginning and end,
follow them by their categories,
use them to prove each other,
and to complete each other.
Then you will have a great understanding
and know the direction and purpose of my Dào."
"Yes, indeed."
"I wish to ask for a major clarification:
why does the deity of the East hold a spear?"
"Indeed,
you need not have asked,
for the Zhēnrén must surely know this himself."
"The reason I ask is that
the Tiānshī fortunately pities later generations and provides methods for them;
if I do not ask, then later generations will be unable to know the definitive meaning of the Heavenly Way."
"Indeed, this is because
it is an image of Heaven,
and all things follow their respective categories.
In the East, things first begin to sprout and emerge,
all arising with sharpness,
piercing the earth to come forth.
Their essence resembles a spear,
hence it is represented by a spear;
when its divine officials arrive,
they take this as their tally.
In the South, the myriad things hang their branches and spread their leaves like halberds,
hence its essence is divine and holds a halberd;
when its divine officials arrive,
they take this as their tally.
The West corresponds to bows, crossbows, and axes.
The West is the image of Heaven’s crossbow and killing.
Now, bows, crossbows, and axes
are also the chief among things that wound and harm;
therefore, when its deities arrive,
they take these as their tallies.
The North corresponds to inlaid shields and knives.
The North is where things lie low, hide, and flee.
The shield is that by which one protects the body;
as for the knife,
it is what the lowly carry,
often used to harm others while fleeing,
and is not something a superior Jūnzǐ possesses;
therefore, when its deities arrive,
they also take these as their tallies.
The Center
corresponds to thunder, drums, and swords.
The Center
is Earth,
the master of the Wǔxíng.
The drum is also the leader of the five weapons,
and the sword is what people of Jūnzǐ status and Dàodé carry;
it is also the chief of the five weapons.
Therefore, when the deity of the Center arrives,
they take this as their tally.
These are the tallies and credentials of the true trust of Heaven and Earth's spontaneity.
It is like a human being who must have a head;
responding to this, they hold their tallies.
True and trustworthy tallies and credentials match when they arrive;
if it is not like this,
then it is not the deity of that specific operation.
If other deities falsely come to match,
it would all result in chaotic governance;
over time, the governance becomes chaotic and difficult to stabilize,
hence all seek trustworthy tallies and credentials.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Indeed, indeed."
"This explanation is simple yet profound;
although it might seem trivial,
it actually corresponds and harmonizes with the Qì of Heaven, Earth, the four seasons, and the Wǔxíng."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Proceed,
the Zhēnrén knows it now."
To the right is the Secret Formula for Repelling Evil People and Transforming Them All into the Way to Save Lives from Death.
By upholding Dàodé and accumulating goodness,
one then fully permeates the essential Qì of Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and spirits,
as well as the Qì of the people, crawling creatures, the myriad things, the four seasons, and the Wǔxíng.
Always interacting with them,
there is none who does not know their goodness.
The Ward of Great Compassion and Filial Piety, Number One:
As for compassion and filial piety,
thoughts emerge from within
and are issued from what is stored;
they can be attained without learning,
for they are the arts of spontaneity.
One’s actions are identical to the heart of Heaven,
and one’s intentions harmonize with Earth.
Above, they benefit emperors and kings;
below, they serve as prosperous leaders for the common folk.
They can bring about the Qì of harmony
and serve as a primary model for others.
Their conduct is as clear as red and blue pigments,
therefore they are ranked first.
The Ward of Illustrious Dàodé and Great Gentleness, Number Two:
Being clear about the classics of Dàodé,
serving as a leader for the hundred surnames,
studying the good Way,
and skillfully accumulating virtue,
one does not attract bandits or thieves.
Above, they benefit the transformation wrought by emperors and kings;
this is most truly auspicious.
The Ward of Filial Piety, Fraternal Duty, and Beginning to Learn Transformation into Goodness, Number Three:
Beginning to study with the desire to do good,
with hope and aspiration in the heart,
abandoning the heterodox and approaching the orthodox,
yet one has not yet fully completed benevolent conduct or transformation.
The Ward of Diligent Children of Farming Families, Number Four:
Diligent and hardworking children of farming families
work from dawn
and rest at sunset.
Not avoiding toil and hardship,
they have daily accumulations.
The household is harmonious,
supporting their parents.
Obtaining the benefits of the soil
and following the Way of Heaven,
they dare not do wrong,
benefiting the local officials.
The Ward of Greatly Unbenevolent Children
and Unrighteous Youths Fond of Weapons and Gathering for Wickedness, Number Five:
Unrighteous people
and unbenevolent children
do not follow principles or the Way,
cursing Heaven and striking the Earth,
and not supporting their parents.
They always carry weapons when they go out,
terrorizing the village.
Frivolous youths,
they are of no benefit to the transformation of Heaven and Earth,
instead becoming a great harm.
They should be captured with concerted effort,
cast away into ditches and drains,
and not allowed to be buried.
The Ward of Disharmony Within the Family,
Deceiving the Old and Doting on the Young,
and Sharing Food while Maintaining Separate Wealth, Number Six:
The family will surely be ruined,
kin are not in harmony,
they are unable to instruct one another,
falsely spreading rumors back and forth,
and avoiding each other.
Turning their backs on the fundamental and pursuing the trivial,
their disaster is beyond salvation.
The Ward of Repenting Errors and Abandoning Weapons, Number Seven:
Born in an impoverished neighborhood,
rarely hearing or seeing anything of the Way,
they do not know good from evil.
Having committed errors against the world,
their conduct does not match Heaven.
Relying on an enlightened ruler
to lead me toward goodness;
in youth not knowing how to study,
and only repenting in adulthood.
Let good people and worthy scholars use a five-foot pillar;
eventually, they will leave the ward.
Students should investigate and ask about this,
and in one day all the people will become good.
The Ward of Repenting Errors and Realigning with Goodness, Number Eight:
Family education was not completed,
and misfortune and chaos all arose.
Relying on an enlightened ruler
who knows my circumstances,
ordering me to repent my errors,
I have instead become a teacher of others.
The Ward of Greatly Evil People, Heterodox, Greedy, and Corrupting Transformation, Number Nine:
Parasitic officials, heterodox, evil, and greedy thieves,
deceiving those above and harming those below, great flatterers.
Known as official-thieves,
they have the form of a human
but the disposition of a greedy beast.
Benefiting neither Heaven, Earth, nor Yīnyáng,
their disasters are deep, and they should be executed and eliminated.
The Ward of Removing Errors, Returning to Orthodoxy, and Repenting Deeds, Number Ten:
Repenting errors, changing conduct, and transforming the heart.
In youth having no good disposition,
disasters frequently arose.
Correcting errors in the evening that were made in the morning,
they are called good people.
These Ten Wards
are the laws of the ancient worthies and sages,
taking joy in people doing good,
ensuring they do not rob or harm each other,
wishing for each to live out their natural lifespan,
returning to the Way,
preventing and cutting off the root of evil,
so as to witness the Qì of Tàipíng."
Divine beings are all regulated by standards;
their root is the *Tàixiāng*,
and the *Tàixiāng* is linked to the *Dìwáng*,
who thereby rectifies the movements of Heaven.
The secondary root is linked to the *Huánghòu*,
who thereby harmonizes with the patterns of the Earth.
The middle root is linked to the various *Shèng*,
who thereby govern *Yīnyáng*.
The fine and small roots are linked to the *Shùmín*,
who thereby govern the myriad things.
When great men practice this, they achieve greatness;
when middling men practice this, they achieve mediocrity;
when small men practice this, they achieve smallness;
all can attain correctness.
When the *Dìwáng* practices *Dàodé* and it flourishes,
the Sun shines with great brilliance;
with little *Dàodé*, there is little brilliance.
When the *Huánghòu* practices *Dàodé*,
the Moon shines with great light;
with little *Dàodé*, there is little light.
When the various *Xián* practice *Dàodé*,
the stars and celestial movements shine brightly;
with little *Dàodé*, there is little brightness.
When the four roots all practice *Dàodé*,
all under Heaven is at peace,
auspicious omens appear,
and the great light reaches far.
Observing celestial phenomena from afar,
wind and rain are timely and good,
the *Yídí* submit their hearts,
and disasters dissipate of their own accord.
Now, having received the *Tiānshī*’s writings on *Dàodé*,
they are transmitted to the diligent people;
causing the diligent people to return,
above there is a ruler of great benevolence and *Dàodé*,
who can balance the principles of the world and long secure their person.
The *Dìwáng* personifies the foremost noble son of *Shànghuáng Tiān*,
and the *Huánghòu* is the foremost noble daughter of the Earth.
Indeed, as most divine and noble persons,
their duty is to reside within the hundredfold enclosures,
yet conversely, they worry about the world ten thousand *lǐ* away,
receiving Heaven's mandate to be the head of the lineage holding together *Yīnyáng*, the six harmonies, and the eight directions.
In the honored positions of Heaven and Earth,
they are entrusted by the divine spirits,
and from above to below, penetrating to the extremes, all things that crawl and move,
none do not submit their hearts.
Thereupon, the Supreme *Língbǎo* audience was established;
those able to know the will of Heaven
and officials clear about the stars and celestial cycles
are named the *Tàishǐ*.
Their duties must not be neglected;
day and night, they take turns observing the waxing and waning of the celestial *qì*,
and the successes and failures of the Three Luminaries,
taking joy in receiving Heaven's commands and warnings to ensure their own peace.
In the eleventh month, they cultivate the *Huángzhōng*,
guiding the *qì* from below the earth to communicate upwards,
taking joy in obtaining the intent of *Hòutǔ* to ensure peace.
They construct the *Míngtáng* in the place of *Tàiyáng Bǐngwǔ*,
creating eight windows and four passages for it,
taking joy in communicating with the *qì* of the eight directions and four seasons,
wishing to unite with the auspiciousness of the eight winds and the four seasons' *qì* to ensure their own peace.
Clearly opening the four gates,
they take joy in obtaining extraordinary writings and exceptional strategies from under Heaven,
rarely seen objects,
and the unusual arts of the wise and bright,
which can secure the world long-term and eliminate calamities and anomalies.
When ancient sages were on the throne,
they constantly strove to seek recluses and those who were wise and gentle,
so that they could govern together.
I wish to hear about the four seasons being honored;
however, *Wángqì* is the leader of the peerless *qì*,
to which all other *qì* are attached,
and it is the lord of all that is honored and noble.
*Wángqì* is Heaven,
it is the Sovereign,
it is the Emperor,
it is the King,
it is *Tàisuì*,
it is *Yuèjiàn*,
it is *Dǒugāng*,
it is *Qīnglóng*,
it is *Dàdé*,
it is flourishing prosperity,
it is the *Dìwáng*,
it is the Supreme King,
and it is the master of birth and growth.
Therefore, wherever *Wángqì* resides,
there is nothing among the myriad things that does not submit to its kingship;
wherever *Wángqì* dwells,
all things rule and live;
those it turns away from all die,
which is due to *Yuánqì*.
Thus, when *Wángqì* is in *Yáng*, *Yáng* is regnant;
when it dwells in *Yīn*, *Yīn* is regnant;
when it dwells in Heaven, Heaven is regnant;
when it dwells on Earth, Earth is regnant;
wherever it resides, that becomes regnant,
receiving the mandate to preside over governance.
Thus, the ancient sages and kings
were in the East in spring,
the South in summer,
the West in autumn,
the North in winter,
and the Center in the sixth month;
when the cycle of *qì* was complete, they had an audience with Heaven,
for *Wángqì* is thus more honored than Heaven.
Opposing the *Yuèjiàn* is named *Pò Dàhào*,
and opposing the *Dìwángqì* is named death and extinction.
*Yuánqì* establishes the positions;
*Dìwángqì* is the foremost *qì*,
and its dignity must not be recklessly opposed.
The position one step behind the *Yuèjiàn* is "Closed";
as for "Closed,"
it is where Heaven presides over closing off the rear,
lest the *Yīn* resting *qì* come forward to act with craftiness and deceit
and interfere with the *Dìwáng*’s establishing *qì*;
therefore, its rear is closed.
As for "Open,"
it is the law of Heaven,
which does not take joy in harm or injury.
Therefore, opening what is behind
is to instruct the resting *qì*,
so that if there are any who act craftily, they may joyfully use the opening to withdraw.
If they do not leave, they shall be seized;
once seized, they will be interrogated, and their guilt established;
once a crime is established, it cannot be removed,
leading to death and peril.
Therefore, the fifth position behind is "Peril";
peril means being near death.
Therefore, the sixth position behind is "Breaker";
that which is broken by the Heavenly Dipper dies;
thus the *Kuí* presides over death,
reaching the ultimate peril.
Therefore, *Dìwángqì* arises in *Shǎoyáng*,
and *Tàiyáng* constantly guards the *Dǒujiàn*.
Death *qì* arises in *Shǎoyīn*,
and *Tàiyīn* constantly guards the *Dǒukuí*.
Therefore, the six positions behind are where Heaven constantly rests and empties them,
sharing the same *qì* as the Earth,
presiding over closing and hiding away,
where treacherous people and evil spirits dwell together;
one must not recklessly open them.
Ancient worthies loved life,
and all their *qì* belonged to the front of the Dipper,
moving in tandem with the course of Heaven;
therefore, their days were auspicious and full of *qì*.
All those who are crafty, treacherous, and evil
all resemble *Yīn* *qì*
and belong to the rear of the Dipper;
therefore, their days decline,
and what they do is inauspicious.
*Yuánqì* is indistinct and self-so,
condensing together to form the One,
which is named Heaven;
dividing to produce *Yīn* and forming Earth,
which is named Two;
because Heaven is above and Earth below,
*Yīnyáng* combine and bestow life upon humans,
which is named Three.
The three lineages are born together;
nurturing all things is named "Wealth,"
Wealth produces Desire,
Desire produces Evil,
Evil produces Treachery,
Treachery produces Cunning,
and Cunning produces harm; if it does not stop, there is chaos and ruin;
if ruin does not stop, governance cannot be restored,
because when exhausted, it returns to its root;
therefore, it is named *Chéngfù*.
The Way of Heaven has no personal heart;
when it encounters the unworthy, there is chaos,
and when it finds the wise and bright, there is order.
Ancient *Dìwáng* obtained the wise and bright, and thus the Way flourished;
they did not dare to have the stupid and unworthy as close advisors.
Quickly deliver this text of mine to a ruler of superior virtue to put into practice.
Those who are penetratingly bright are radiant;
question them through the interaction of the three *qì*;
if their divinations are ten out of ten correct,
and all that they govern is well-ordered,
this is the foremost excellence and brightness,
and they can serve as an envoy for the *Dìwáng*.
If their divinations are nine out of ten correct,
and one *qì* is chaotic and disordered,
they can serve as an envoy for the *Zhūhóu*.
If their divinations are eight out of ten correct,
and two *qì* are chaotic and disordered,
they can serve as an envoy for common people.
Anything below this
is named "disrupting the Correct Way of Heaven";
there will surely be grievances and knots;
spirits and essences will hide and flee from sight;
it cannot be governed,
and one cannot harmonize the *qì* of *Tàipíng*.
If you wish to obtain the Way, reflect on these writings;
the method for seeking the Way has stillness as its root;
acting as the root,
accumulating essence without ceasing is the gateway of the spirit.
When the five virtues harmonize, one sees the *hún* and *pò*;
when the spirit of the heart is brightened, the *Dàdào* is revealed;
first knowing peace and peril, observing one's neighbors.
The multitude of spirits assemble in great numbers like clouds.
Thus is the Cháng Shòu Jūn who never ceases.
Ah, the Dà Dào does not require arduous effort.
The form is like withered ashes, guarding the soul and spirit.
When the soul and spirit do not depart, one exists forever.
That which revolves returns to the beginning, a ring without end.
To abandon the root and seek the branches brings trouble to the Dào.
The masses lose it and cannot remain whole.
Reflect on its meaning and do not lose the true words.
Clarity and stillness are the root, not the use of money.
Should one not deeply value the words of an enlightened Míng Shī?
By obediently receiving the teacher’s words, one does not die.
The foolish oppose the teacher and become neighbors with ghosts.
Failing to obtain the Zhèng Dào, they enter the gates of calamity.
Consequently, they never return, as the spirit departs.
Flesh and bones rot in the mud while they are called ancestors.
Life is already extinguished, reaching a great end.
The arts of the common and foolish
all emerge from within.
They have their own laws and regulations.
Making the substantial the root and foundation.
Seeing the spirit, one lives.
And also has no suffering or sorrow.
The spirit dislikes toil and violence.
Peace the heart and stabilize the intent.
Be careful not to die a sudden or violent death.
After a long time, one naturally becomes still.
The ten thousand ways all emerge together.
Existing forever and not dying.
Concluding together with Tiān.
Practicing it ensures harmony.
Becoming one with the Dào.
The worthy hold fast and do not set it aside.
All matters are then completed.
Common thoughts are cast away.
Forging a bond with the spirit.
Riding the clouds and driving dragons.
Sharing a room with Léi Gōng.
The body transforms and becomes a spirit.
Its appearance is like that of Tài Yī.
Contemplate the words of the book in detail.
Be careful not to lose discipline.
The way of concentrated meditation
is accomplished in a secluded chamber.
Do not seek glory or status.
The will daily becomes more harmonious and refined.
Opening the darkness to reveal a penetrating white,
resembling the brightness of day.
At the time when one does not study,
it is like looking at lacquer at night.
East, West, South, and North—
one is lost within the room.
This causes the worthy and sagely to be alarmed and terrified.
The heart alone trembles with fear.
When the Wǔ Shǒu are strong, one does not die.
Being content with poverty and finding joy in low status allows one to endure.
To be low and yet seek high status hinders the Dào.
Be careful not to hope for high office and heavy salary.
If one forcefully seeks official rank, the Dào immediately perishes.
It is better to set aside sleep and rest long upon the bed.
Without eating, one becomes naturally enlightened.
A hundred evils all depart, and one keeps far from disasters.
Guarding stillness without stopping, one will not perish.
Fortunately, one may have a long life and practice for a long time.
Do not dare to be self-indulgent and lose constancy.
Seeking it without stopping, one becomes a Dào Wáng.
The arts of governing and living each have different methods.
Although their affairs differ from the common people, they do not hinder each other.
When those above love life,
the lives of the people are long.
Common teaching says that above the Dào there are benevolent superiors.
When a Shèng Zhǔ contemplates the Dào,
transformation flows down to those below.
Causing the people to be pure and honest.
There will never be disasters or calamities.
The people not dying
is due to the enlightenment of those above.
If there is no Míng Jūn above, the teachings will not spread.
Unwilling to practice the Dào, they instead love weapons.
If a household has an evil son, the family perishes.
Holding weapons to accost people, staying by the roadside.
Waiting for people's vulnerability to steal their belongings.
Xiàn Guān are uneasy, and bandits roam.
By observing the people, one can see that those above can be enlightened.
When the Rén Jūn loves benevolence,
those below seek longevity.
When those above are not benevolent,
those below are mostly deviant and crooked.
All are caused to die young,
not knowing the joy of life.
When the lowly and foolish love virtue,
it is due to the teachings and orders from above.
Those among the people who love the Dào,
it is because their ruler is enlightened.
They all desire longevity,
and stay far from disasters.
Fasting and being pure,
they cast away all weapons.
Ruling through Wú Wéi,
they reject what is inauspicious.
When a Shèng Zhǔ greatly flourishes,
his people are close to one another.
Grace reaches even the lowly and foolish.
This is their Wáng.
Tiān Dào loves life,
thereby bringing peace to those above.
The lowly and foolish do not contest the blessings of those above.
The world is extremely fortunate,
none fail to return to the Wáng.
Those among the people who do not love the Dào,
it is because those above are not enlightened.
Secretly harboring treacherous hearts while acting openly.
They do not love practicing virtue,
instead, they love weapons.
Fathers and sons are separated,
living by the roadside.
They cannot obtain longevity,
but accumulate deaths and funerals.
If a family has an impoverished son,
he is like a tiger or a wolf.
When those above have no virtue,
there are the calamities of weapons.
When the lowly and foolish become rulers,
transformation does not spread.
When many of the people love the Xiān,
the Dì Wáng are enlightened.
Tiān sees their governance,
and grace flows downward.
Creeping things and breathing creatures,
all are covered in light.
Tiān is the way of loving life,
therefore it is the Tiān Jīng.
Accumulating virtue is the Dì Jīng.
Dì loves to nourish,
therefore it is the Dì Jīng.
Accumulating harmony and loving to give is the Rén Jīng.
Hé Qì flows back and forth.
When people have wealth, they share it,
giving extends to all who come and go.
Therefore harmony is the Rén Jīng.
In ancient times, those who were about to seek knowledge,
all corrected their root.
It is like planting a tree.
One must seek a good seed for the root
and place it in good soil.
When it grows,
root, tip, branches, and leaves are all good.
The root is the Běn Shī,
and the branches and fruit are the disciples.
Therefore, in ancient learning,
all first focused their thoughts on the root,
and then they studied its Dào.
Thus, what can be done
matches the Tiān Xīn.
Therefore it is auspicious.
If in planting a tree one does not select a good tree
and plants it in bad soil,
how could the branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit
be beautiful?
This is why
one starts by straightening the body,
correcting the nature and the intent of the Dào,
returning to and resting in the Yuán Qì,
and returning to bring peace to the body.
Reflecting on the ancient methods
and what the Xiān Shī practiced,
how they were able to govern themselves.
Once the plan is set and the intent is ultimate,
one will naturally obtain it.
First, bring peace to the form.
When first beginning to practice it,
it is like the play of an infant—
not using muscle or strength,
but using only good intent.
Contemplating in detail why the ancients alone enjoyed long life,
their self-governance and singular intent,
and how they obtained it.
It was only through the Zhì Dào,
binding deviance and removing treachery.
It is like a spirit;
there is nothing strange or bizarre.
The root is correct, and by practicing this,
one thus obtains the Tiān Xīn
and does not betray the intent of Dì.
The Sì Shí complete their cycle,
the Wǔ Xíng are at peace,
and descendants do not inherit Chéng Fù.
Each harbors Zhì Dé,
no longer knowing how to be deviant or evil.
Entering the room and dwelling alone,
reflecting on the root of the scriptures and the Dào.
In all necessary comings and goings,
the worthy first obtain its meaning,
and the next follow them.
Consequently, all enter the Dào together
and distance themselves from deviance.
Entering the chamber to contemplate and preserve,
the five organs shift and move,
following the brothers of the *Yīn* and *Yáng* months—*Mèng*, *Zhòng*, and *Jì*.
Moving in response to the *Qì*,
they follow the transformations of the four seasons, the five elements, and the *Tiāndào* as a constant.
To lose *Qì* is to die;
to possess *Qì* is to live.
All things follow this,
and the human way is preeminent.
Therefore, the five organs are established
to rise according to the *Qì*.
The *Tiāndào*, by means of the *Qì*, soars as the preeminent.
The *Zhēnrén* accumulates *Qì*
and gathers divine brilliance;
thus, the Way always proceeds alone in the end.
The ten thousand people lose *Qì* and thus die.
Those who perish are lowly;
those who live are noble.
If you, my child, guard the Way, you can endure long,
transforming along with the *Qì*.
Heaven is the constant;
do not be anxious for fame and profit;
the Way proceeds of itself.
The *Tiāndào* always lives and never perishes;
the *Dìdào* maintains the two masters of death and destruction.
The sages and worthies of high antiquity held office;
middle-ranking scholars measured themselves in the mountains;
low-ranking scholars died like insects among the common folk.
When a worthy sees this book
and contemplates these words deeply,
first finding them difficult and later easy,
their body will also be without affliction.
By guarding virtue and completing the Great Way,
through study and having passed through the *Jiǔ Shì*, one becomes a *Shénrén*.
Their thoughts are always completely different and distinct from ordinary people;
morning and evening they never think of the earth below,
but desire to hear of heavenly affairs.
Only when the mind contemplates heavenly duties
can one then descend to the *Jiǔ Shì*.
Accumulating essence with sincere exhaustion, one transforms naturally
and changes their appearance;
this is a *Shàngtiān Shèngrén*.
It is clear that they must no longer manage the worldly affairs of the common people.
My book enables high scholars to pursue life
and is not seen by low scholars;
I dare not act or speak recklessly.
My book is for the Way;
it is able to exhaust the aspirations of people,
allowing the worthy and the unworthy to each fulfill their talents.
To reach death without any regrets
is for each to fulfill their *Tiānmìng*.
Those who desire longevity and joy to endure long
should contemplate the intention of the *Zhèngdào*
and may proceed.
Those who do not enjoy enduring long
should pursue mundane affairs,
merely seeking joy for their own persons.
Examine your conduct and mirror it against your person;
you will know for yourself the laws of gain and loss.
The worthy, bright, and wise may encompass Heaven and Earth
and accumulate books without limit,
yet if they cannot increase their own longevity or life,
this is called emptiness
and lacks the actual Way.
As for the masters of practitioners,
after a long time, they still exhaust themselves.
Even if one's learning can everywhere teach astronomy and geography,
fully understand the nature of all things,
and have all books prepared and gathered,
if they cannot serve their parents or respect their sovereign,
this knowledge is of no benefit.
Think carefully on these words;
good and bad fortune can then be known.
This is to act with simplicity,
which immediately allows a person to know their own gain and loss.
What is urgent in learning?
Therefore, two matters are presented
to clearly distinguish the signs of a scholar's intentions of loss and gain.
Since the *Kāipì*,
there have been two urgent matters in conduct.
It is fine to want to know the rest,
and fine not to know them.
What Heaven, Earth, and the Sages strive for,
and what should be promoted to achieve great gain,
are *Shòu* and *Xiào* as the most urgent.
*Shòu*
is to share the same excellence as Heaven and Earth.
*Xiào*
is to share the same power as Heaven and Earth.
Therefore, the long-lived have eternal life,
sharing the same essence with Heaven.
The filial
obey their superiors below,
sharing the same sound with Earth.
These two matters
obtain the intent of Heaven and Earth,
and misfortune will naturally depart.
Deeply contemplate this intent;
it is the principle of *Tàipíng*
and the essential for longevity.
Many desire to do good,
but few seek to live.
Therefore, parents
are the root of life;
the sovereign
is the gate through which glory and honor are granted;
the teacher
is the source of wisdom
and the inexhaustible profession.
These three
are the gateways to *Dàodé*.
Parents
transmit the ancestral lineage of the *Yīn* and *Yáng* of Heaven and Earth;
the teacher
understands the intent of Heaven and Earth
and unties the knots of mundane affairs;
the sovereign
should support Heaven,
follow *Yīn* and *Yáng*,
always strive to obtain their intent,
and take the principle of the Way as their duty.
Thus, these three
are the gateways of *Xìngmìng*.
Deeply contemplate these words,
and all harms shall be removed.
*Shòu* and *Xiào*
are what the *Shénlíng* love.
Lack of *Shòu* and *Xiào*
is where a hundred calamities converge.
This Way is natural and requires no effort;
to know its effect,
it always follows the good or evil of human intentions.
The mind and intention plot matters within,
and they are echoed without.
To know this Way,
it is precisely the response of shadows and echoes.
The heart and intention are the gateways to good and bad fortune.
In ancient times, the rulers of *Tàipíng*,
their principle was simply to use the mind and intention for good,
and then their ministers would be good;
if the intention was mistaken,
the ministers obtained would also be mistaken.
The heart and intention
are the *Shūjī* of Heaven and Earth;
they must not be moved recklessly,
for that causes the *Héqì* to be disordered
and disasters to arise daily.
The Liùfāng Zhēnrén all bowed repeatedly, saying:
“Previously, we received the instructions of the Tiānshī to gather and jointly submit a memorial with strict orders.
We returned to our respective places
and concentrated our minds to ponder the meaning.
For seven days and seven nights,
the six Zhēnrén met three times for discussion,
and all had things they did not understand.
During the three open discussions,
three times we witnessed changes in the light of falling stars in the sky.
First,
we saw a falling star exit the Tiānmén
and enter the Dìhù.
Second,
we saw a falling star exit the Tàiyáng
and enter the Tàiyīn.
Third,
we saw the Lièxiù stars flow into the Tiānyù.
Because these three appeared together, we deliberated on them.
We fear that the Tiānshī’s three-fold written doctrines
may be cut off by those below,
preventing them from reaching the heights.
This would cause Heaven’s anger to flare up repeatedly,
and the Shànghuáng Qì would be unable to descend.
This causes the virtuous rulers and kings of Dàodé to be burdened by the Chéngfù of the previous kings’ residual disasters without end,
and thus they suffer in distress.”
“Alas!”
the Tiānshī said, “The six Zhēnrén have come together on behalf of the Huánglíng to inquire about matters.
How much more diligent they are towards Heaven!
I have seen what the disciples said,
and there is nothing more I can add for the Zhēnrén.
Now, try to explain for yourselves the meaning of those falling stars.”
“The six disciples are ignorant and obscured,” they replied,
“but how could we dare not speak?
Initially, the first falling star exited the Tiānmén
and entered the Dìhù.
The Tiānmén
is Yáng
and the Jūn;
the Dìhù
is Yīn
and the Mínchén.
Now the Mínchén do not flow upward to attach themselves;
instead, the one above bestows grace upon those below.
Since doors and gates are primarily for communication,
and now the lower portal does not move upward
but instead the upper gate communicates through the gate downward,
we know this represents the petitions of those below
being met with obstruction and cut off,
unable to travel upward.”
“Well said, Zhēnrén!” the Tiānshī replied.
“I have nothing to add to it.
Although the task is arduous,
please explain the other two matters.”
“Yes, yes.
The second matter:
we saw the Tàiyáng star flow into the Tàiyīn.
Tàiyáng
is the Jūn;
Tàiyīn
is the Mínchén.
Tàiyáng
is Míng;
Tàiyīn
is Ànmèi.
Now, darkness should flow upward into great brightness.
This is comparable to the Mínchén being in darkness and obscurity,
ignorant, distressed, and impoverished;
they should go upward to attach themselves to the bright king and sagely ruler
to seek redress for their grievances.
Now, on the contrary, the great brightness flows downward into the darkness.
This symbolizes that when imperial edicts bestow grace,
those who carry them downward are cut off.
It is dark and not bright;
those governing below are internally chaotic and they alone obscure their superiors.
It also symbolizes that those close to the common people,
the local officials in charge,
together hide the disasters and anomalies of Heaven and Earth,
preventing them from reaching the profound heights.
They join with the Mínchén to deceive their superiors,
which serves as evidence of their collective treachery.”
“Excellent, excellent!
I have nothing to add to the words of the six sons.
Although the task is arduous,
please explain the third matter.”
“Yes, yes.
The third matter:
we saw the Lièxiù stars flow into the Tiānyù.
The Lièxiù
are good and upright stars,
yet they flow into the prison of Heaven.
The Prison
is the place where Heaven names and punishes crimes.
We fear that the noble scholars and good people who wish to do their best for the monarch
by submitting memorials to communicate the discourse of Heaven and Earth
are instead hated by the local officials in the remote lands far from the capital.
These officials later use other matters to harm them;
therefore, the Lièxiù flow into the prison.”
“Excellent and profound!
I have nothing to add to the words of the six sons.
Now that the six sons are inquiring about matters,
what a great passion they show!
Are you not weary or fatigued?”
“We do not dare to be.
We often hear the Tiānshī say
that the Zhēnrén come on behalf of Heaven to inquire about matters.
If we were to stop now,
we fear that Heaven’s words would not be communicated.
Now, the lives of ordinary people are tied to Heaven and Earth.
If Heaven and Earth are not pleased
and instead harm the sick,
then we would not be able to complete our natural lifespan.”
“Excellent.
The words of the Zhēnrén are correct
and not mistaken.
Now I will speak for the Zhēnrén,
and I also do not dare to be negligent or stop.
I and the Zhēnrén are equals;
we all have lives tied to Heaven and Earth.
If I remain silent and do not speak,
or if I start speaking and then stop,
Heaven and Earth will likewise harm me.
Therefore, in my speaking, I also do not dare to talk recklessly or stop.
Very well, I shall explain it all in detail for the six Zhēnrén.
Now that the six Zhēnrén have recently emerged from their caves
and are thinking on behalf of Heaven
about how to remove Heaven’s ailments,
and thinking on behalf of a virtuous ruler
about how to resolve disasters and secure one’s person,
the six Zhēnrén should speak their thoughts to the utmost.
Say everything you wish to say,
and do not let it be suppressed.”
“Yes, yes.
Regarding what the Tiānshī has commanded,
how could we dare not use even our meager ‘sparrow and mouse’ wisdom
to say everything?”
“Speak your heart's fill.”
“Yes, yes.
Now, what the world fears
is that people keep their mouths closed because they do not dare to speak recklessly.
Nowadays, the sun, moon, stars, and planets
are the divinities of the Lièxiù close to Heaven,
yet even they fear one another.
Therefore, when the sun comes out,
the stars immediately hide themselves,
not daring to be seen out of fear of its majesty.
Within the four borders,
there is a stern emperor,
and the world is in awe and terror.
Even those very far from the capital
fear the imperial edicts and dare not speak.
If a province has a powerful official,
the whole province dares not speak.
If a commandery has a powerful official,
the whole commandery dares not speak.
If a county has a stubborn and powerful official,
the whole county dares not speak.
If a village or pavilion has a stubborn and powerful Tíngzhǎng,
even that one pavilion’s jurisdiction dares not speak.
This Tíngzhǎng
is only the smallest of officials;
how much more so for those who are ministers?
All fear being harmed
and each only seeks their own escape.
Even if they have good intentions,
they do not dare to reach the superior on their own,
causing the path to be cut off.
Now, if even one neighborhood has a stubborn and powerful person
who always controls the justice of that neighborhood,
that neighborhood will likewise not dare to speak,
fearing they will be resented and harmed.
If even a single family has a stubborn, powerful, and martial person who always controls the affairs,
that family will likewise not dare to speak.
A family is close,
sharing the same bloodline
and born of the same kind,
yet they are oppressed and fearful of each other like this;
how much more so for those who are unrelated?
Now, since the Supreme and Middle Antiquity,
much of Dàodé has been lost.
On the contrary, people mostly govern each other with majesty and force.
They oppress and coerce one another with power.
If anyone does not obey,
later they will surely suffer great harm,
the injury being very deep
and flowing down to their descendants.
Therefore, although the people see the anomalies and omens of Heaven’s disasters,
they are terrified of those nearby who have jurisdiction over them
and do not dare to speak recklessly.
Because of this, the burden has accumulated for a long time,
and people have transmitted and received this Chéngfù from one another.
By Late Antiquity, this became even more severe.
If any small person wishes to submit a memorial
to reach the emperor on their own,
those nearby who hold power over their lives immediately kill them.
If they are not harmed immediately,
later they will surely be harmed through the commissions of others.
Therefore, all the Mínchén tie their tongues and shut their mouths as if mute.
Though they see sorrow and injustice
or witness evil, they dare not communicate it upward.
Therefore, today the emperor’s hearing and sight are cut off.
And celestial portents increase daily,
which is a clear proof.
Now, people are personally born of their parents
and receive their mandate from Heaven and Earth.
Taking Heaven and Earth as parents,
seeing that they have disasters, portents, good, and evil—
these are the conversations of Heaven and Earth,
wishing to have these words spoken.
People are still all terrified and afraid,
moreover, they are harmed by those closely connected to them,
not daring to speak or leak matters;
thus they instruct each other,
jointly turning their backs on Heaven and Earth,
and cutting themselves off together,
not conveying what Huáng Tiān and Hòu Tǔ wish to say.
Together they obscure and wrong Heaven and Earth,
causing their words to be blocked,
so that Heaven and Earth long harbor resentment and distress without being heard.
Now, though a Dì Wáng is divinely sagacious,
he is the source of a single person,
yet he dwells within a hundred layers of people,
and beyond ten thousand lǐ.
Within the hundred layers,
even if one wishes to go and convey words,
they are coerced by those nearby
and cannot reach the destination to convey them.
A Dì Wáng may have the benevolence and sagacity of ten thousand times ten thousand people,
but people are each coerced, threatened, and afraid of consequences.
Heaven and Earth are the most divinely sagacious;
people look up and look down upon them,
yet they merely rely on them before their eyes to explain themselves.
How can a Dì Wáng be more divinely sagacious than Heaven and Earth?
We six humble students once encountered a fierce tiger in a remote wilderness.
All six of us stopped in our tracks and dared not move;
our mouths dared not speak,
our heads dared not move,
and our eyes dared not blink.
Such is the coercion and fear that people feel."
"Excellent, excellent!
Now seeing the words of the six Zhēnrén,
I understand that Heaven alone has long suffered from illness, pain, and grievance,
and its words cannot be conveyed.
Although it creates ten thousand times ten thousand strange portents as conversation for the Dì Wáng,
the assemblies below block them,
so they cannot reach above,
resulting in long-accumulated distress in solitude.
Therefore, it now inspires the Zhēnrén,
teaching them carefully,
ordering this matter of submitting writings.
Thus the Zhēnrén are fearful and diligent;
they are the messengers of Heaven."
"Yes, yes."
"I revere the awe of Heaven;
I shall now contemplate the essential meaning for you and explain it fully.
Of the matters the six Zhēnrén ask about,
which one is usually the most severe?"
"We six humble students,
for seven days and seven nights,
have together contemplated this matter of submitting writings.
We gathered for discussion three times
and three times witnessed falling stars,
taking them to be Heaven's announcements, instructions, and orders
causing us to ask.
Furthermore, we six all practiced the ingesting of qi,
but it could not be swallowed or passed through;
the qi rebelled and rose upward.
At that time,
our ears and eyes became dizzy and dark without sight.
We all found it strange and discussed it among ourselves,
not knowing what kind of great terror and fright it portended.
We only hope the Tiānshī will explain it to us humble students."
"Excellent!
The Zhēnrén have indeed grasped the full meaning.
Seeing the words of the Zhēnrén,
I now know of the Sāndào Shū.
Why is it that the assembly of Zhēnrén is again being blocked?"
"We wish to hear your decisive explanation."
"Indeed.
The nine orifices correspond to the divisions of the Jiǔzhōu.
Now the Zhēnrén say themselves
that while ingesting qi, it was blocked and would not pass,
and there was dizziness, darkness, and no light;
this means the great and small of the Jiǔzhōu are coercing each other,
so that those below cannot convey their words of urgent matters to those above.
As for qi,
it is the means to connect the lives of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things.
Heaven and Earth
use qi and wind to transform the lives of the myriad things.
When the qi is blocked and cannot pass,
it is a sign that the Way of Heaven is closed,
and it is a clear proof of the lack of communication.
Heaven wishes for the Zhēnrén to be careful in this matter,
thus it uses this qi to move and affect the Zhēnrén.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Go on,
you have understood it now."
"Yes."
"Heaven has announced to the six Zhēnrén to instruct me to speak out fully!
Sit comfortably, the six of you;
I shall speak and explain the Way fully for all the disciples.
For those who fear the senior officials of their Zhōu and Jùn and dare not speak:
the good and wise men within one Zhōu should seek each other out,
gather to discuss, and submit it in another Zhōu;
if they fear their Jùn,
they should gather to discuss and submit it in another Jùn;
if they fear their Xiàn,
they should gather to discuss and submit it in another Xiàn;
if they fear their Xiāng or Tíng,
they should gather to discuss and submit it in another Xiāng or Tíng;
if they fear their Lǐ,
they should gather to discuss and submit it in another Lǐ.
All are within the proper method.
As for those who prohibit or intimidate others,
they shall be punished according to the severity of the crimes and portents reported,
and an additional degree shall be added to the original crime."
"Why is it so heavy?"
"It should not be considered heavy;
I still fear it is too light.
Now Heaven and Earth love a virtuous Dì Wáng
and wish to speak fully for him.
Humans are born of Heaven and Earth,
yet they turn their backs on Heaven and Earth,
cutting off Heaven's conversation,
causing Heaven to become ill,
so that the malaise accumulates and is not removed,
and the distress cannot be relieved,
when it tries to speak and report to its son;
this is a heavy crime of Great Rebelliousness.
The subjects and ministers
are the messengers of the Dì Wáng,
his hands and feet;
they should primarily extend the hearing and sight of the Sovereign King,
enabling the one above to attain peace and be without worry,
and together they should match the Heart of Heaven.
When Heaven is joyful, it will cause the Sovereign to prolong his years.
Now, on the contrary, those dwelling below are disloyal,
turning against Heaven and Earth,
cutting off the hearing and sight of the Dì Wáng,
causing him grief and suffering,
so that he constantly blames himself for governance losing its rectitude,
while disasters and portents occur in profusion,
and he is in danger and without peace.
All these acts correspond to being unfilial, disloyal, untrustworthy, and greatly rebellious.
By law, they should not receive amnesty;
how then can this be considered heavy?
When Heaven's conversation cannot pass through,
Heaven and Earth are greatly enraged,
harming and killing all things;
this is to destroy Heaven and Earth,
and it results in a year of great ill-fortune.
A state that is cut off and has no hearing or sight
is a state in great peril.
This crime is beyond description;
therefore, it is a transgression deserving of death.
Do the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Go on,
you have understood it now.
The reason I dare not □□ is
that I see the six of you coming to inquire about matters,
and I realize and understand you are messengers of Heaven;
thus the Zhēnrén dare not □□.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"Now, the name of not □□
is to mislead the one above.
When a virtuous Sovereign sees the writings,
he should order those who submit the petitions
to cause those who □□ have merit
to be bestowed with rewards for their virtue.
If it is like this, then everyone under Heaven will be joyful
and happy to exhaust their strength,
together submitting petitions to speak of matters;
do not let a single person speak alone,
all should be ordered to gather for discussion.
When one person speaks, there may be falsehood, fabrication, or flattery;
this is known as causing the one above to lose sight of reality,
and it must not be listened to, as it is a great transgression.
Comparing the consecutive years of submitting petitions,
there are frequently those with sincerity
and those with great merit.
When many superior men gather,
the usual problem is that they are not numerous enough;
when only two or three gather,
there are certainly and inherently many who are treacherous and false.
Why is it that there is no treachery or falsehood?"
"We wish to hear of it."
"Indeed, when there are many, those who submit the petitions naturally fear each other,
fearing that the matter might be leaked
and their strengths or weaknesses seen.
Should they instead deceive the one above,
they would be reported by those beside them.
Therefore, they exhaust the truth and verify □□,
only then daring to speak of it.
If it is not □□, they dare not speak.
Moreover, they dare not hide anything,
all fearing and dreading future consequences;
for this reason, all of it is sincere.
It is comparable to a hundred households in a single Lǐ joining together to deceive."
Among men, women, children, and adults,
there will be those who leak secrets,
and in the neighboring villages there will be those who know of it.
Those in the village who are worthy, enlightened, and fear consequences
will not dare to conceal it,
for fear of being implicated in the matter.
How much more so for a zhōu, a jùn, a xiàn, a xiāng, or a tíng?
When a jùn has an extraordinary occurrence,
how could it be hidden clearly in the open?
It will still be grasped by others, its merits and flaws known;
thus good and evil are both fully revealed.
Heaven then greatly rejoices,
disasters are removed,
and it is no different from flowing water.
Do you know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Furthermore, in grand collective deliberations,
none dare to be deceitful.
If one or two people wish to deceive,
the others will certainly not follow them.
If there are those who wish to deceive and are untrustworthy,
the crowd will immediately record and report them together.
According to the law, they should be considered those who turn their backs on Heaven and Earth,
deceive the Emperor,
and are treacherous, false, and guilty of great rebellion and waywardness.
Heaven resents them,
and people loathe them;
their crimes must not be pardoned.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Indeed,
you have already realized it.
Once the report has been submitted
and they return to their homes, if there are those who resent their actions
or
wish to harm the one who submitted the report,
then their names on the left side shall be called the Yuàn Zhāng,
and their transgressions will not be removed.
In this way, the reports of the three paths have circulated through,
and none dare to block or cut them off.
In this way, Heaven and Earth are already pleased,
the disasters and calamities of the Chéngfù borne by the Emperor
are greatly removed,
and the world is at peace.
The qì of the Shànghuáng all arrives
to assist the Dé Jūn in governance; □□
it will not fail the six Zhēnrén."
"Yes, yes."
"Indeed,
the essence of the six Zhēnrén has greatly advanced;
they have removed illness for Heaven,
they have removed the juncture of calamities for the Emperor,
their merit is already manifest in Heaven,
and the King becomes daily more powerful and enlightened.
The six Zhēnrén, in doing good,
have already obtained the correct method.
You should exert yourselves,
be cautious, be cautious!"
"Yes, yes.
We wish to ask for one Dà Jué;
may the Tiānshī show it to us.
We wish to know if the circulated reports
have thoroughly reached and permeated the spiritual realm;
may we hear of this?"
"Indeed,
there is naturally a great verification;
the Way of Heaven does not deceive people.
Each thing is sought according to its kind.
Let the Dé Jūn frequently send trustworthy officials
to ask among the people if there are those with ulcers, leprosy, or scabies.
If there are none,
but if there are many who have ulcers, leprosy, or scabies,
then the circulated reports have not yet thoroughly permeated the spiritual realm.
If they suffer from having surplus insects eating people—
when insects eat people,
then insects are governing people.
Truly, below there are surplus ministers and subjects without the Way or virtue;
they are like insects,
conversely eating the people.
This is the effect of insects governing people.
If there are none with ulcers, leprosy, or scabies,
then it corresponds to good people being in office
and no more insects.
In this matter, not one in ten thousand is missed."
"Excellent, excellent!
Is it only by this that it is made clear?
Is there more?"
"All the zāiyì of the world
arise according to the state of governance.
Each has its cause;
simply ponder the matter with focus,
and you will naturally know it.
Why speak only of ulcers, leprosy, and scabies?
Other disasters only manifest among the ten thousand things,
but insects eating people is the most severe;
thus I use it as proof."
"Excellent, excellent!
Had we not exerted ourselves to ask the Tiānshī,
there would be no way to know this."
"Looking at you Zhēnrén now as you speak,
you already know it yourselves;
you are merely being modest."
"We would not dare, we would not dare.
We six ignorant Yì Shēng have again received the Tiānshī's strict instruction.
Each of us will return to a quiet and convenient place
to contemplate its essential meaning.
Now, the Tiānshī's writings
cause everyone, great and small,
down to the slaves and servants,
to all gather and discuss to jointly submit reports on zāiyì and good and evil.
Isn't this perhaps too cumbersome?
We Yì Shēng wish to hear the reason for this."
"Excellent!
You six people ask about matters for the sake of Heaven;
be detailed and cautious,
for Heaven causes you Zhēnrén to speak.
However, the reason for including even the commoners, slaves, and servants is that
in the present legal realm of Heaven,
ten thousand lǐ is a different Heaven and Earth;
five thousand lǐ again has small differences;
