as this is the origin of the Dào;
if you devotedly guard the Yī,
it is the source of benevolence and worthiness;
the Way of Heaven practices the Yī,
and is therefore complete;
the Way of Earth practices the two,
and is neighbor to ghosts and spirits;
carefully knowing Wúwéi,
one is most divine with its Dào;
deeply contemplating these matters,
the Zhēnrén is the first;
close your Jīnquè,
and do not let it go out the door;
silent and without sound,
it nourishes the essence and spirit;
when the spirit and Qì are complete,
it is the gate to the Way of Immortality;
how easy is the Dàdào,
it is no longer troublesome;
the Way of Heaven has no favorites,
it returns to the benevolent and worthy.
To the right is Wúwéi.
The law of Zìrán
is thus connected with the Dào;
guarding it brings good fortune,
while losing it brings disaster.
It is like the myriad things which grow and complete themselves;
one root with ten thousand branches has no spirit.
Deeply contemplate its meaning and the Dào will reveal itself;
all share the ancestor Hùndùn and emerge from the Miàomén;
neither increasing nor decreasing, they guard Zìrán.
Every living thing naturally has a spirit;
with one thousand eight hundred breaths, humans are most honored;
therefore, one can avoid death and become a long-lived immortal;
the reason for an early end is losing Zìrán;
even birds and beasts have their measures, how much more so for humans?
The foolish despise the intent of the Dào,
and are connected below with the earth;
the benevolent and worthy value the Dào,
and suddenly ascend to the gate of heaven;
the Way of the Spirit is undying;
the Way of the Ghosts ends there.
If you wish to practice it,
it is like a ring without an end.
Be careful not to have strange eccentricities,
which only increase harm to oneself;
also, do not recklessly abandon it,
which leads a person to death.
The nature of Heaven and Earth
uniquely values Zìrán;
each follows their own affairs,
and none dare to oppose them.
The Dào flourishes through Wúwéi,
through emptiness, nothingness, and Zìrán;
high scholars delight in it,
while low scholars resent it.
Learn in detail from a Shī,
and do not speak recklessly;
with a Shī, the Dào is clear;
without a Shī, it is difficult to transmit.
If learning does not follow the Master's instructions,
the gentleman does not speak of it.
To act recklessly is to cause chaos;
harming the body brings misfortune.
When the Dào is fully prepared,
it then becomes Zìrán.
To the right is the warning for the complete accomplishment of the Dào.
To the right is the formula for flourishing above, removing harm, and the double text.
To the right is the instruction for the honored to be without worry and for evils to be removed naturally.
To the right is the method for those of virtuous conduct to have prosperity and to be supported and sustained.
To the right, store this in a secluded place and the spirits will bless it.
As for those who practice the Dào,
they take instructions from the internal and external inscriptions upon entering the chamber.
When the number of days is full,
open the door and enter to observe it;
those who have inscribed themselves on the inside,
do not enter to observe them;
those who have not inscribed themselves on the inside,
then let people enter to observe them.
Open the door and enter to observe;
those who wish to leave, then let them leave.
For those who circulate the books of the Three Ways,
all take instructions from collective discussion,
to serve as Tiānxìn;
thus such a person is established above.
For those who are upright and divine spirits,
they take instructions from the profound illumination of millions of people,
to serve as Tiānxìn.
For those who wish to rectify ordinary texts,
they take instructions from collation,
to serve as Tiānxìn.
For those who wish to know the textual trust of my Dào,
they take instructions from practicing it with diligent speed,
which will correspond with the echoes of Heaven.
The good will flourish daily,
and the evil will diminish daily;
this serves as Tiānxìn.
For those who wish to appoint good people,
they take instructions from nine people.
For the question of whether the entry into the chamber is successful or not,
take instructions from profound illumination.
The form is without manifestation or concealment;
this serves as Tiānxìn.
For those who wish to know if the body has achieved the Dào without dying,
take instructions from whether the body has already become a spirit;
if so, one has transcended the world;
this serves as Tiānxìn.
For those who wish to thoroughly understand the meaning of my written texts,
read them entirely from top to bottom,
and the heart will naturally become clear and greatly enlightened,
with no further doubt.
Once the meaning is grasped,
one cannot let it go.
For those who wish to test my books,
and see their truth or falsehood,
use them to govern until the days approach Tàipíng;
this serves as Tiānxìn.
For those who wish to know if longevity can be attained or not,
take instructions after Tàipíng has arrived.
If Tàipíng has not yet come,
the calamities passed down from ancestors will cause harm,
making it difficult to demonstrate one's life-destiny;
this serves as Tiānxìn.
For Tàiyáng wishing to know Tàipíng,
take instructions from Duànjīn.
For Water and Fire wishing to suppress treacherous ministers and prevent sorcerers from acting,
take instructions from the Duànjīn wine of the market.
For those wishing to obtain the method for the great flourishing of the Way of Heaven,
take instructions from collating the various texts and the formulaic words of ordinary people.
For those wishing to obtain good medicine,
take instructions from collating ordinary medicinal texts and testing them.
For those wishing to quickly attain Tàipíng,
take instructions from bringing forth all true texts and severing evil and false texts.
For those who wish to contemplate so that people no longer kill or harm women,
take instructions from having each dwell in their own place,
according to their strength for clothing and food,
and do not let them return to distressing their parents or being rebellious.
For those wishing to remove diseases and greatly open the Dào,
take instructions from swallowing characters written in cinnabar.
For those wishing to know the instructions for collective circulation of books,
follow the text,
be repeatedly careful,
and restrain them well.
Practice it for one day,
and it will eliminate a hundred harms that trouble people's hearts;
in a single morning, all will be turned and rectified;
this serves as Tiānxìn.
"May I ask, regarding ruì,
what kind of term is it?"
"For what reason are you acting foolishly?"
"I do not dare to be intentionally foolish;
I truly lack understanding.
I hope the Tiānshī will not abandon me
but will instruct me with a single word."
"Very well,
sit peacefully.
Ruì is
clarity,
stillness,
uprightness,
correctness,
focus,
and oneness.
The mind is at one with Heaven and Earth
and does not violate the seasonal ordinances."
"I wish to hear how one knows of this clarity, stillness, uprightness, correctness, focus, and oneness."
"Excellent
is your question.
Indeed, the nature of Heaven and Earth,
from antiquity to the present,
is that the good brings about the good,
the evil brings about the evil,
the upright brings about the upright,
and the heterodox brings about the heterodox;
this is the way of nature,
and there is nothing strange about it.
Therefore, when the human mind is upright, clear, and still,
its perfect sincerity moves Heaven;
when there is no ill intent,
auspicious responses and good things appear because of it.
If you wish to further know its great reliability:
the great sages and worthies of old all applied their minds with clarity, stillness, focus, and oneness;
thus they were able to bring about auspicious responses.
All heterodox people apply their minds with flattery and falsehood
and have no good responses;
this is the great and clear evidence of Heaven and Earth.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, yes.
Are there also negative responses?"
"Indeed, the heterodox bringing about the heterodox
is also a response.
Discord brings about discord,
and harmony brings about harmony;
this is the clear effect of Heaven's response."
"Excellent, excellent!
This humble student understands."
"May I ask, when a person does good,
when superior filial sons, superior loyal ministers, and superiorly obedient disciples consider what to present to their ruler, father, or teacher, what should they present?"
"They should present extraordinary information, precious treasures, and rarely seen writings; those who can present these are the superior ones."
"Being a loyal minister, filial son, or obedient disciple is always a joyous thing;
why not present common information but instead present extraordinary information?"
"The superior already possesses common information;
why is there a need to present it again?"
"This humble student does not understand the meaning."
"Very well, I shall let you know the truth of it.
Of all that comes from the world and is treasured,
that which has never been seen before and is truly precious,
if presented to one's ruler,
this is being a superior loyal minister.
Presenting never-before-seen fine food to one's parents
is being a superior filial son.
Presenting never-before-seen teachings to one's teacher
is being a superiorly obedient disciple.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, yes.
I wish to hear about presenting common matters,
things the superior already possesses,
and presenting them repeatedly;
what of that?"
"Indeed, if one intentionally presents such things,
the offense will not be removed."
"Why is it so serious?"
"You must be an unlearned student.
That which people commonly have,
they grow tired of if it is repeated;
why must it be presented again?
Presenting what people are tired of
is called intentionally slighting the superior.
When an inferior intentionally slights their superior,
in your opinion, should they not be held liable?"
"This humble student has realized it."
"Therefore, when one obtains auspicious responses and good objects,
or rarely seen treasures,
one should present them to the ruler, father, and teacher.
As for what the superior already possesses,
be careful not to present it.
For this reason, from antiquity until now,
when the great sages determined all matters,
they discarded the common and took the extraordinary,
thereby attaining the intent of Heaven and Earth;
this is what is meant.
Do you understand?"
"Excellent, excellent!"
"May I ask the Tiānshī, how does one know when the Books wish to be manifested,
and how does one know when they wish to be hidden?"
"Do you wish to clarify this?
Use disasters and illnesses as evidence.
If they are brought out and people fall ill,
then Heaven wishes them to be hidden;
if they are hidden and people fall ill,
then Heaven wishes them to be circulated and manifested."
"How can this be further clarified?"
"By the fact that Heaven circulates the qi of the four seasons
to give life to and nourish the myriad things,
following the intent of Heaven.
Whenever things delight in emerging
but are instead hidden away,
it is a great misfortune.
Whenever things desire to be hidden
but are instead brought out,
it is also a great misfortune.
These are all acts of rebelling against the Mandate of Heaven,
and great disasters will follow.
If you wish to joyfully know the pleasure of my Heaven's circulation,
do not fail to use this as a sign.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Therefore, from antiquity to the present,
when undertakings are not handled with detailed care
and the intent of the Heavenly Way is lost,
Chéngfù arises.
Therefore, it causes the people to reach a state of being governed without the Way,
collectively throwing the correct Way of Heaven into chaos.
When human governance deviates,
the people and the myriad things suffer much injustice."
"I wish to ask about being without the Way;
it is a law carrying a heavy death penalty.
Why does the Tiānshī not establish laws of heavy punishment and death,
and penalize each according to their crime?"
"In the matters of the world today,
it is considered fair to penalize each according to their crime."
"Now the Tiānshī does not penalize them for being without the Way;
why is that?"
"It is not permissible."
"For what reason?"
"The ancestors only committed small errors and lost the Way;
such conduct existed,
but it was not enough to warrant punishment.
Later generations inherited the burden through Chéngfù,
and the accumulation became a fault.
Even if they commit capital offenses,
their heterodox, false, and hollow conduct
was learned by the later generations from the earlier generations.
Although they have lost the Heavenly Way
and govern without the Way,
these methods have all been passed down from teacher to teacher
and taught to one another.
It was not a single person who created this fault;
therefore, one cannot impose heavy punishment upon them.
When considering the crimes and faults of the people of later antiquity,
they are all sufficient to warrant death.
Furthermore, in the laws of the divine and sagely,
one cannot suddenly impose heavy punishments on people,
as it would exterminate the human race.
Therefore, Heaven sent me down
to reform their conduct
and remove their responsibility.
Without an overt change,
Heaven, Earth, and Man shall govern them together,
causing spirits to inflict illness and disasters upon them.
When people of later generations see this,
it is the clear effect of the teachings I received from Heaven.
Do you understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Very well,
the conversation is finished and the words of Heaven have ceased.
Transmit this to the Déjūn."
"Yes, yes."
"Go now;
do not ask again."
"Yes, yes."
To the right, the essential instructions on the explanation of auspicious responses end here.
"Heaven has two hands,
which always work together to accomplish all things.
If one hand is diseased or evil,
then no task can be completed.
Heaven greatly resents this,
Earth regards it as a taboo,
and the world falls into chaos without success,
all because this one hand is evil and does not combine its strength.
All matters will be entirely disordered,
and the six directions will not be at peace,
also due to the fact that these two hands are diseased or evil
and do not combine their strength.
Good and bad fortune, safety and danger,
all stem from these two hands.
Does the Zhēnrén also know this deeply?"
"I have not reached that level.
Only if the Tiānshī explains the essential meaning
so that I may know it,
will I truly understand.
Otherwise, I will remain in eternal darkness and confusion,
with no way to know it.
A teacher
is the foundation of the teaching and transformation of all things in Heaven and Earth.
Though it is difficult,
how can you not speak of it?"
"Excellent!
Such is the Zhēnrén’s request to ask about these matters.
Has Heaven sent you to be the primary questioner?
Your words are essential and □□.
Very well. Sit peacefully,
and I shall explain the meaning in detail for all the Zhēnrén.
If the world takes this as a model and acts upon it,
there will be no more unlucky or chaotic events.
The various spirits in Heaven call the strategy of the 'Two Hands' the 'Essential Record.'
If the state practices it, it will long endure;
if commoners practice it, they will be wealthy for a long time.
The essential Dào is about to emerge;
it is near, within the body of every person.
Now, I shall explain it piece by piece for the Zhēnrén."
"Yes, indeed."
"Heaven and Earth
are the two hands that govern the creation and birth of all things.
The Four Seasons
are the two hands that govern the transmission and nurturing of all things.
The Wǔxíng
are the two hands that govern the completion and mutual handing over of all things.
Men and women, husbands and wives,
are the two hands that govern the succession of Heaven and Earth, Yīnyáng.
Teacher and disciple
are the two hands that govern the teaching and communication of all writings, matters, the Dào, and virtue.
Ruler and minister
are the two hands that govern the management of all matters, the people, and all things.
Here are six matters;
I have only raised the main outline;
I have shown only their beginning;
they could not be fully recorded.
All matters that depend on each other for completion
are like these two hands.
In Heaven, this is called 'Overlapping Compasses and Layered Squares';
all must correspond to each other.
If one hand is evil or unequal, nothing can be accomplished;
in Heaven, this is called 'Governance of Great Chaos.'
To the six directions and eight remotes, it is called 'Widowers, Widows, and the Severance of Lineage,'
and things decline day by day.
The lack of success
is due to these two hands not combining their strength."
"Excellent, excellent!
May I ask why Heaven designates this as the 'Two Hands'?"
"How wonderful
is your question!
You have grasped the meaning.
'Two hands'
refers to their being equal and combining strength,
neither advancing too far nor pulling back;
only then can subsequent matters be completed.
If the two hands do not combine their strength,
matters cannot be completed.
Therefore, all matters
should take these two hands as a model;
each role must be filled by the right person.
Combining strength and sharing the same heart,
modeled after these two hands,
the Qì of good fortune, peace, and Great Peace will arrive immediately.
For those who do not model themselves after these two hands,
for billions of years the Qì of Shànghuáng Tàipíng will not be able to emerge.
The Qì of Tàipíng always desires to emerge,
just as Heaven always desires to use these two hands,
but they have not been harmonized or regulated for a long time.
Thus, they are blocked and cannot pass through;
the governance that emerges is sorrowful and blameworthy.
The fault lies in these two hands being out of harmony.
If the two hands are harmonized,
this Qì of Shànghuáng Tàipíng will emerge,
and the before and after will reach each other without being apart.
Excellent, excellent!
Therefore, if Heaven and Earth do not combine their strength,
the myriad things and matters have no way to emerge.
If the Four Seasons do not combine their strength,
all things have no way to grow.
If the Wǔxíng do not combine their strength,
all things have no way to reach completion.
If ruler and minister do not combine their strength,
all matters have no way to be properly managed.
If husband and wife do not combine their strength,
descendants have no way to grow,
and the family way has no way to be established.
If teacher and disciple do not combine their strength,
all entanglements have no means to be untied,
the Dào and virtue have no way to flourish,
the obscuring mists have no way to be cleared,
and the great transformation of the six directions and eight remotes has no way to be carried out.
Therefore, all must combine their strength,
like two hands;
only then can there be passage.
If not like two hands,
then misfortune arrives daily.
Though one tries to treat it,
it is of no use;
there is still no way to achieve success.
There is only empty, long-term sorrow and bitterness,
and daily misfortune.
Therefore, in all that models these two hands,
selection and appointment must obtain the right person;
if the right person is not obtained,
the spirits in Heaven
call it 'Half-Dead.'
By not using one hand and working alone,
how could one possibly succeed or complete a task?
The Zhēnrén has come from afar on behalf of Heaven to ask.
For all doubtful matters, you should deeply contemplate this meaning with a 'Red Heart.'
The heart is born of fire;
return it to fire.
If you govern and model yourself for the people,
you will extend your years and increase your longevity;
not one in ten thousand will fail.
I am not deceiving you.
Show this to the virtuous ruler,
show it to the commoners;
let the worthy ones each contemplate its meaning,
and none will dare to violate it.
To use it is called 'Self-Enrichment and Self-Nurturing';
to not use it is called 'Self-Worry and Self-Suffering.'
How divine!
My Way
is pure Heavenly intent.
One can only advance and not retreat;
one can only follow and not oppose.
Following it is purely attaining the heart of Heaven;
opposing it leads to chaotic matters.
Chaotic disasters are tumultuous;
if human intent goes west
while Heaven's intent goes east,
it is called being at odds with the intent of Heaven."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Go now;
you may be said to have already awakened and understood."
"Before the Zhēnrén,
nowadays when ordinary people recommend scholars
to be presented to the Dìwáng
and entrusted to the state,
how much good fortune is there if the right person is obtained,
and how much calamity is there if the right person is not obtained?
What can be accomplished if the right person is obtained,
and if the right person is not obtained,
what can be overturned?
May the Zhēnrén please clarify and respond."
"Indeed,
obtaining the right person brings four types of good fortune,
and failing to obtain the right person brings four types of calamity.
If the right person is obtained,
Heaven, Earth, the six directions, and the eight remote regions are at peace;
if the right person is not obtained,
Heaven, Earth, the six directions, and the eight remote regions are not at peace."
"I wish to hear the essential meaning of this."
"Indeed,
if the recommendation of a scholar obtains the right person,
the superior is able to govern with principle,
achieving success and remaining in constant peace,
providing daily benefit to the superior;
this is the first great good fortune.
The recommended person can be given responsibilities
and becomes a useful vessel;
this is the second good fortune.
Becoming a useful vessel,
they can manifest and clarify the Way of their teacher,
and grace reaches their teacher;
this is the third good fortune.
The recommended person handles affairs faithfully and effectively,
causing the superior to trust and employ them once more;
this is the fourth good fortune.
They work together with combined strength and one heart,
and what they do achieves success daily,
becomes clearer by the month,
and flourishes more each year.
Heaven and Earth are pleased and joyful,
auspicious responses all manifest,
and evil things are hidden away.
When Heaven and Earth are pleased, then the various gods are joyful.
If this is maintained without being lost,
above, one can transcend the world;
in the middle, one can govern peacefully;
and below, one can be made whole and complete,
fulfilling one's natural lifespan.
When the recommendation of a scholar obtains the right person,
the goodness is like this;
in Heaven, this is clearly the Xùmìng zhī Fú."
"May I ask for what reason it is precisely named the Xùmìng zhī Fú?"
"Indeed,
as for the reason it is the Xùmìng zhī Fú:
when the recommendation of a scholar obtains the right person,
danger is changed to peace,
chaos to order,
failure to success,
calamity to good fortune,
and death to life.
Above, it reaches to transcending the world;
in the middle, it achieves order through peace;
and below, it allows one to fulfill their natural lifespan
and keep their physical form whole.
Now, if the recommendation of a scholar does not obtain the right person,
above, there is no benefit to the Dìwáng,
the state is made to fall into disorder,
the Dìwáng is distressed,
Heaven and Earth are displeased,
and ten thousand kinds of bandits and disasters arise;
this is the first great calamity.
The recommended person cannot manage their duties,
using flattery and deceit to lie daily.
For a long time, their position is unstable,
and they cannot protect their natural lifespan;
either Heaven, Earth, ghosts, or gods harm them,
or they are murdered by others.
Humiliation reaches their parents,
and the evil flow reaches their wife, children, and descendants.
Having fallen among the base types of the world,
they are eventually recognized for their faults as an evil person;
this is the second great calamity.
If the person is evil,
then their learning is discarded,
defiling the legacy of former teachers, sages, and worthies.
Misfortune reaches their teacher;
this is the third great calamity.
Furthermore, the one who recommended them is untrustworthy,
together they deceive their superior.
Presenting the wrong person
disturbs the celestial patterns
and defiles the constellations.
Heaven detests them,
Earth resents them,
the ruler of the state hates them,
and the sages and worthies condemn them.
Such a one is a child of great flattery and deceitful words in the world;
they should be held responsible for these matters.
If they are not executed by Heaven, Earth, ghosts, and gods,
then people will surely harm them.
Humiliation reaches their ancestors,
and misfortune reaches their wife, children, and descendants;
this is the fourth great calamity.
Committing these four great calamities
by presenting the wrong person
causes the Dìwáng to be distressed
and governance to be chaotic.
All harmful Qì stirs and arises,
and cannot be stopped.
Order is lost from beginning to end,
and they transmit the burden of negative consequences to one another.
Heaven and Earth are greatly enraged,
the various gods battle,
the six directions are unhappy,
and the eight remote regions fall into disharmony.
Order is never restored,
and in Heaven, this is named the Jiǎnnián Duǎnmìng zhī Fú."
"For what reason is it named the Duǎnmìng zhī Fú?"
"Indeed,
when governance should be long-lasting,
it instead becomes short;
when years should be many,
they instead become few.
In undertaking affairs, one encounters calamity,
which provides no benefit to the self.
Heaven and Earth are displeased,
removing counts from one's life and reducing one's years;
therefore, in Heaven, it is named the Duǎnmìng zhī Fú."
"Excellent, excellent!
This humble student has heard your command."
"Indeed,
you may be said to [truly] know it.
Be careful with this heavenly text and show it to virtuous rulers,
show it to ordinary worthies,
and let it reach down to the common people.
Those who are superiors seeking scholars
must be thorough;
those who are subordinates recommending scholars
must be loyal.
Future generations shall transmit (
and thoroughly) recite this text,
binding it within their hearts.
If in the urgency of recommending scholars one does not follow this,
Heaven and Earth will no longer be pleased.
To know this and yet intentionally violate it,
how heavy is that transgression!
Let the Zhēnrén be careful with this."
"Yes, yes.
I sincerely receive these instructions
and do not dare to violate the prohibitions;
I shall practice them with all my strength."
"You may be said to be careful in affairs
and to have attained the mandate of Heaven."
The above is the Tiāndì Shǒucè: Gòngshì Sìjí Sìxiōng, Duǎnmìng Fú, Xùmìng Fú, and the Ānguó Dé Tiāndì Xīn Qúnshén Xǐ Chèn.
Only the Way of high antiquity
involved cultivating the self and rectifying the person;
they did not dare to violate what the Shénlíng recorded,
and only then did they dare to seek life and search for survival from Tiānjūn,
not daring to be self-indulgent,
for fear that their life would not be preserved whole.
Daily they contemplated the intent of life,
acting as ministers to the Shén,
manifesting their category.
They desired to offer words of complete loyalty and uprightness,
and together with the various Shén who presided over the departments,
each clearly distinguished right from wrong;
only then did they dare to trust in the principles of the crooked and the straight,
never forgetting this for a single moment on any day.
Above there are Zhānrén
who fully know right from wrong;
what could be hidden,
and what could there be that is not believed?
Therefore, they were able to regulate themselves,
seeking and contemplating the fundamental root,
never having even a small boundary of ungoodness.
They only cherished the fact that they were human,
relying on and looking up to Yuánqì,
enabling even the wriggling creatures
not to witness categories of calamities and anomalies.
But humans have betrayed the trust of their oaths,
neither side trusting the other,
and therefore there is unrest.
Within the central harmony of Tiāndì above and below,
each has its own trustworthiness;
humans do not know the essentials of this,
yet they say, "Why alone is there good and evil?"
Calamities and anomalies all arise from this.
Humans consume the Qi of the Wǔcháng;
there is nothing they do not receive,
nothing they do not rely on,
and nothing they do not practice;
why alone do they not reverently know that in antiquity there were Zhīrén who reached and caught up to the Way?
This is to lose the good and follow evil,
causing life not to be preserved whole;
why alone should it be this way?
Therefore Tiānjūn says
that there is good and there is evil,
and the good can be made uniform.
The reason for this
is that there must be distinctions;
one cannot simply follow oneself.
Good should move upward,
and evil should meet with punishment;
how can it reach the same level as the good?
Speaking from the human perspective,
it can also be known
that there are naturally those who are upright.
Therefore, evil is established to make clear the intent of Tiāndì, the four seasons, and the Wǔxíng,
making it known that completing life is of great weight,
and increasing the years of one's life.
When humans attain the Way of birth and completion,
they receive and apply its prohibitions,
not daring to violate taboos.
Speaking of it this way,
Heaven knows the foolish are very shallow and has no intent of retaliation,
yet they go against what Heaven enacts,
testify against what Heaven enacts,
or add to the wickedness people practice;
among their kind, they conversely sustain evil and loathe the good.
Therefore the Shèngrén know the meeting of Yīnyáng,
and the Xiánrén regulate the crooked and the straight,
explaining what is not yet known
and enabling each to know their lot and boundaries without resenting one another.
The good naturally have long lives,
and the evil naturally have short lives;
how can there be any doubt or resentment?
Are humans inferior to the six domestic animals, birds, beasts, or creatures in the water?
To think that humans are without proper form
is how Heaven makes it.
Heaven equally desires to make them do good
and does not desire to make them do evil.
It is as if good and evil share their suffering and joy.
Wealth, honor, longevity, and old age
are performed by Heaven above;
if one cannot distinguish between the good and the ugly,
letting ignorant people gain Qi and raise their voices,
saying, "I am equal to you all,"
why reach such a point in practicing good?
Therefore, advance and increase the good
to enable long life;
those who are shallow consider it all the same.
Compared to the evil who lose their lives,
only then do they wish to rectify and repent for their faults,
seeing the good and engaging with it,
and seeing evil and retreating from it.
Day and night, they restrain themselves and reflect,
and what was owed is repaid.
A minor life can become equal to others;
though not transcending as an immortal,
one can complete what was received
and not die in the middle of one's years;
this is acceptable.
What common people excel at is but a moment.
They do not think of long life,
which can reach up to the Zhìshì;
having the heart to seek life,
they therefore do not do evil.
Heaven sees their goodness
and allows them to act in peace,
further seeking wealth and having descendants;
although they do not get everything,
there is still something to hope for.
Why do evil and quickly perish,
while thinking one should be able to complete one's years?
They do not know Heaven sends Shén to record it;
whether faults are great or small,
Heaven knows them all.
In the registry books of good and evil,
which are checked by year, month, and day,
they calculate and subtract life-units and years;
if their evil does not stop,
they will see the Guǐmén.
The Dìshén summon and interrogate them
to see whether their words match their deeds;
they are further painstakingly punished,
and only after punishment do they submit.
Their names are submitted to the Mìngcáo for confrontation;
when the calculation is exhausted, they must enter the earth,
and the offenses flow to future generations.
Is this not caused by evil?
Why do people not desire to live?
When people lack illumination, they are like this;
what is there to resent or blame?
Like a child of ten months,
why alone should one be ungood,
practicing evil without ceasing?
How can one last long?
The schemes of foolish scholars—
why do they not even align with small goodness?
They practice the Fùdào of minor, non-urgent matters,
which is what ordinary people do,
each with a different scheme,
thinking themselves in the right;
but what they touch and violate
is all for the sake of gaining advantage from others,
and others do not wish to be used for their gain.
Good benefits obtain life, yet only for a moment;
evil benefits do not last long;
without goodness, one does not dwell long upon the earth.
Therefore, does Tiāndì make it known or not?
Heaven makes people do good,
therefore it gives them life,
yet they conversely do evil.
Therefore, the Guǐ who preside over evil follow them for a long time without leaving;
even if there is a release, they do not stop;
other Guǐ fall upon them
and immediately cause incidents;
thus they follow the person without ceasing.
Do you know this or not?
This book first advances the good and repels the evil;
it is a text of the past and present.
If one does not follow long life but turns to evil,
nothing can be done,
and the Guǐ will be able to report it clearly.
Therefore, those who have faults
sink their forms into the earth,
their spirits are not at peace,
not knowing where they will end up;
whose fault is this?
People should carefully think and reflect on their actions,
choosing what is peaceful and not wrong.
The words and phrases spoken
are repeated over and over;
what is spoken is not just one matter,
therefore they are repeated.
Human life is as close as your own body;
why beat your breast and look up to cry out to Heaven?
If you have a body and do not purify it yourself,
whom should you purify?
If you have a body and do not love it yourself,
whom should you love?
If you have a body and do not complete it yourself,
whom should you complete?
If you have a body and do not think of it yourself,
whom should you think of?
If you have a body and do not reprove yourself,
whom should you reprove?
Reflect again on these words,
and do not resent the Guǐshén.
Seeing good, they report good;
seeing evil, they report evil;
each is different.
Do you know this again?
The words pause for a bit;
if evil does not cease,
the written reports will not end,
stopping only when the person perishes.
This warning shows that doing evil
is to betray one's own body,
not to betray others.
Do you know this again?
Act in accordance with what is said,
and think of it without letting it leave the heart,
for to depart from it is to meet with ruin.
It cannot be set right again;
being in the same ranks as ghosts,
how can one survive?
To think of life and obtain life,
this is wisdom.
Evil will eventually come to an end;
it cannot remain for long.
Do you know this or not?
To speak further:
as humans dwell between Heaven and Earth,
and all have attained the status of being human,
how can they forget the grace of Heaven and Earth?
What kind of person is this?
Their foolishness is such that
they cannot change;
what more can be hoped for?
If one desires a response from Heaven,
one should reproach oneself,
acting with deep sincerity and shedding tears.
Say: "I have received the grace to be human,
which is utterly distinct from the myriad things.
Heaven has made us different,
able to speak and converse,
to see the beautiful and the ugly,
and to know what is good or evil and what is permissible or not.
One should be meticulous and cautious.
If one's words go against the decrees of Heaven,
leading to disobedience,
then one is a person of great rebellion and wickedness.
How can Heaven long engage with such a person?"
Therefore, baleful deities are stationed.
Looking at antiquity, the returned words are as stated:
the person themselves does not love goodness.
Tiānjūn said:
"Documents have already been sent without cease.
The presiding departmental officials have descended to collect the soul;
the bones and flesh are handed over to the Dìzhǔ.
It will take no time at all.
Evil people should not be heard of repeatedly.
Therefore, I restrain my majestic wrath
and return to refinement,
to transform their evil,
gather all goodness,
and place it within,
setting heart against heart."
The deity said:
"I have received the instructions of the Heart of Heaven
to make the presiding spirits follow the hearts of humans.
There must not be the slightest escape.
For every good and evil deed, there is a flanking deity who perceives the heart."
The deity's words became even more sorrowful;
not knowing fortune or misfortune,
one fears being in the department of the wicked.
Day and night I contemplate,
not knowing where I should place myself;
therefore, I dare not have any ungood intentions.
"If only the deities would grant me some leeway,
allowing me to reproach myself.
If I do not heed the divine warnings,
I will not resent being executed."
Tiānjūn sent a Great Deity to descend and say:
"This person has reproached himself and repented of his errors;
he does not violate the prohibitions.
Grant him time, grant him time.
If there is evil later,
it will not be too late to take him."
Seeing the words of the deity,
he sighed deeply day and night,
fearing that his personal transgressions were not yet fully eliminated.
Having long been disconnected from the Tàiyáng Qi
and remaining in the ranks of death,
his condition became even more grave,
and he did not know what to do.
Having received the instruction but not yet fully understanding,
he reflected on himself in a quiet and secluded place,
reproaching himself for his faults and debts,
so as to offer apologies to Heaven and Earth, the Sìshí, the Wǔxíng, and all the presiding deities.
Tiānjūn listened
and ordered him to contemplate further.
The people of high antiquity
all possessed wisdom and foresight;
they did not dare to violate prohibitions.
They cultivated and corrected themselves,
fearing any lapse.
Any action was seen as failing to follow the mandate,
losing their allotted years.
For this reason,
they did not dare to slacken even slightly.
For every transgression, there was a penalty;
thus, they reflected on themselves and cherished themselves,
respecting the prohibitions
and not daring to have any intention of violation.
Facing further questioning,
his heart was constantly trembling with fear,
and he lost his spirit in disappointment.
Having failed the Heart of Heaven,
if his words were even slightly unsuitable,
it would result in tedious complexity,
and he would be interrogated for verification.
What is said and what is believed
can lead to a good reputation;
but if the person themselves lacks trustworthiness,
it long ago depleted their lifespan.
Therefore, thinking on it again,
I do not lose my heart.
Deeply pained and terrified,
I do not dare to be at ease.
Setting aside my ego and acting,
I am always full of longing,
desiring to act in harmony with the lineage of Heaven, Earth, the Sìshí, and the Wǔxíng,
not daring to have the smallest error.
Feeling inner indignation,
one must deeply understand the ultimate meaning from beginning to end,
not losing the norm.
Thinking of grace and not deviating from sincerity,
desiring life and hoping to survive—
how could any small evil be heard of above?
Committing my body to serve in succession,
how could I dare have any thought of slackening?
I fear I cannot attain the ultimate meaning of the one above,
and I do not know what to do.
My heart becomes even more anxious;
being at ease brings no benefit.
Heaven-given longevity is hard to obtain;
once lost, it cannot be regained.
Having been far from the common world for a long time,
yet suffering a setback halfway,
looking back at what is below
makes one feel dejected.
Thus, I can only restrain myself in fear and trembling.
Always fearing that one day, any unsuitability, large or small, will lead to rejection,
sorrow and gloom are in my heart,
as I blame myself for my errors.
Having received Heaven's grace
to carry out my previous mandate,
I dare not forget my thirst and hunger for it,
seeking only to live.
May the Great Deities compassionately examine me,
recording and showing the common people.
Receiving Qi from the Tiānchú,
riding upon the Qi of Heaven.
Yet my conduct is shallow regarding what I preside over;
the prohibitions are many,
and there must be no loss.
Although my person is lowly
and unworthy of honor or favor,
it is not because of unworthiness
that I should be viewed with suspicion.
Truly, I use my heart to seek progress and survival.
I only hope the Great Deities will pardon and examine my words,
allowing me to see the creation of the Sìshí and Wǔxíng,
and to see the sun and moon again, which is hard to repay.
I hope I will not be abandoned halfway.
A person in trepidation,
I dare not distance myself,
tossing and turning on my pillow and mat.
The Great Deity said:
"Since this person has transformed himself through his own discipline like this,
why worry that there will be no one to protect him?"
"In the past, there was such a person;
Heaven assisted and pitied him,
keeping him close.
Now he is seen attending to affairs for a long time,
possessing much wisdom.
Whatever he says
is entirely in accord with the heart of Tiānjūn.
Continue doing as you have done."
Shēng prostrated himself, weeping, and said:
"Having received the instruction and awakened,
I take the sincerity of the ancients as my goal,
advancing in what is known.
There is nothing I do not embrace or hear;
how would I dare compare myself to the people of old?"
The Great Deity said:
"Communicating with a person of faith like this
is intended to let them emulate each other's conduct,
though there are times when people cannot keep up."
Shēng said:
"The Great Deity's guidance is extremely clear.
Among many like me,
I alone have been treated differently
and allowed to have enlightened thoughts.
This grace is extremely heavy.
When will you teach me more, Great Deity?"
The Great Deity said:
"Thought comes from within;
exert yourself and think on this as a repayment."
Shēng said:
"I myself do not know what to offer up;
though Heaven has rare and fine treasures,
I think of offering them up.
Seeing the command, I exert myself and contemplate;
this is what can be sincerely received.
These words are not mere verbal repayment but have substance.
I sincerely contemplate day and night
and dare not slacken."
The Great Deity said:
"The warnings are many,
and the admonitions are not asked of by only one person.
Communicating this far and wide..."
"It is truly a rebirth;
these words are especially met with deep compassion."
Tiānjūn heard this
and called the Dàshén, saying:
"From where did this Shēng originate,
to have brought forth such extraordinary words from the Dàshén?"
Dàshén said:
"Seeing that this scholar is exceptionally faithful,
I have thus explained the difficulty and ease of the Dào for him."
Tiānjūn said:
"When you see good, promote it,
enabling him to reach this level;
this is as it should be."
Dàshén said:
"Tiānjūn summons and questions this faithful Shēng."
Shēng said:
"I dare not hope to reach the left side of Heaven;
I only wish to be in a place without official duties
and exert my own strength in loyalty alone."
Dàshén said:
"All must have a department to govern;
then the principle of trust will be seen."
"If it is so, it is truly a stroke of luck
and a great portion;
I would not dare to have even a small part that does not measure up."
Dàshén said:
"Since this Shēng has undergone transformation
in this way,
he should advance further
and can reach the level of the Xiāngǔ."
Shēng said:
"I do not dare to seek Chángshòu;
it is what people covet."
Dàshén said:
"This is the will of Heaven."
Shēng said:
"This is originally due to being protected by the Dàshén;
I dare not lose the Dàshén’s admonishments."
Tiānjūn knew that these two were mutually advising and correcting each other;
he considered it especially good
and had them teach one another.
Only when the Shèngrén of high antiquity practiced the Dào,
did it emerge from nature.
Their hearts knew the governance of the heavens,
and they had foreknowledge of all that was carried out.
Sounds and voices were thoroughly understood,
and they even knew physical forms;
they looked within themselves and their hearts were clear and their minds enlightened.
They knew the matters that should be saved;
the intersection of good and bad fortune
was clearly discernible.
With joy in their hearts,
they knew they had received the blessings of Heaven.
They were made to see the deeds of former conduct,
all with sincere and thorough admonishment.
Pondering for himself the grace and favor received,
having been in the company of the Liùshén for a long time,
he was frequently given instruction and warnings
to keep him from danger.
Gazing out at the four quarters,
penetrating above and below,
he became increasingly compassionate.
With a joyful heart,
he was granted an extension of time
and attained what he had not heard before;
all of this was the transformation wrought by the grace and power of Tiānjūn and Dàshén.
Dàshén said:
"This is known by all the spirits;
those whose lives are extended have a mandate,
and the records are true.
Before birth, the person’s year, month, day, and hour are pre-recorded in the Bureau of Chángshòu;
as the years increase,
their names are circulated,
and the Běijí Zhēnrén governs them.
The bones and body are transformed,
the body becomes light and lustrous, emitting light.
In the twilight, the medicine is obtained
to complete the essence.
Wherever one is, transformation occurs;
nothing is not accomplished.
Emerging from the profound and entering the mysterious,
within the space of a single hair,
there is nowhere one cannot penetrate."
Shèngrén said:
"Indeed, this follows the mundane;
seeking sustenance from the earth
and the emergence of the Yīnshén—
how could one not take this seriously?
Regard it as easy and thus light;
then this ease is superior.
The grace of the Dàshén cannot be repaid.
The merit is greatly bestowed;
thinking of the great grace,
I cannot bear my inadequacy.
To be granted such profound breath and rest
is not something words can repay."
Dàshén said:
"This is the mandate and lot endowed by Heaven to humans;
it is simply not something the Dàshén’s will has fashioned.
Seeing good and recommending it
is the blessing of the spirits;
what is there to repay or thank?
Lest there be doubts later,
for those who apply prohibitions and restraints,
let the Shèngrén know the teachings and warnings
so that later people may clearly understand them.
The Shèngrén possesses innate knowledge
and needs no commands."
Shèngrén said:
"Having already received the report,
although I am listed in the records of life,
there will certainly be areas where my guidance falls short."
Dàshén said:
"The words of this Shēng are appropriately modest;
this is as it should be."
"The Shēng again offers words,
complete from beginning to end.
Only the Dàshén has fulfilled the intentions of grace.
The Shēng sees his lot among humans,
yet dares not excuse himself
or be arrogant.
I request to exert my efforts again in a quiet place;
let the Dàshén’s teachings be applied,
wishing to keep in mind those Shēng who have not yet reached this level."
Dàshén said:
"Your words are complete and understood from start to finish;
there are no other warnings.
At this parting, each should act according to what has been said."
Shēng said:
"Since the day I received the warnings,
I have not dared to relax for even a moment,
though I fear I may not be able to finish them completely.
Only by receiving support
can I breathe and regain hope.
This is deeply etched in my heart;
may the Dàshén from time to time remember and instruct me—
this is no small grace."
Dàshén said:
"What this Shēng says should be praised."
Shēng said:
"Yes, yes.
I dare not use my body for self-protection."
Dàshén said:
"For one who has achieved a name,
diligent progress is beneficial;
you will also concurrently govern more than one department."
Tiānjūn heard this,
the words exchanged between the Dàshén’s warnings and the Shèngrén;
for a person of knowledge,
one should not be negligent or lax.
Life can reach a longevity beyond reproach.
Each return to your department;
when you see good, you should recommend it to the Dàshén.
Shèngrén said:
"We both receive the instructions of Tiānjūn;
we will exert our strength to be effective,
and while being effective, we dare not grow weary."
Tiānjūn said:
"One who completes others completes himself."
"Yes, yes."
Only the people of high antiquity who attained the *Dào*,
also since before laws and regulations arose, have had records and registers.
These records and registers consist of texts on long life,
and they must wait for the year, month, and day when it is time to ascend.
They are transmitted in the *Zhōngjí*.
*Zhōngjí* is also called *Kūnlún*.
The presiding officials of each department go to record the names of those people,
and none may be omitted.
They are frequently sent to move and shake their limbs and joints,
bending and stretching, turning and leaning,
repeatedly teaching and admonishing them.
They are commanded to follow the spirits in bending and folding,
and they are given medicine to drink.
Their bones and joints are opened and refined,
so that although they are not seen at all times,
it is known whether they can remain firm or not,
showing that their will does not waver.
They cherish life and loathe death,
thinking of practicing as spirits in the heavens.
Officials are frequently sent to verify the number of years they have lived,
and then they are ordered to pay obeisance and receive the texts for those who are deficient.
Words emerge from the thoughts of the heart,
letting them know the prohibitions of their conduct.
These are transmitted and shown to students.
If they do not use the divine texts,
saying they have brought the books themselves and are nearly finished,
the spirits then know their mutual speech,
which also spans years and months.
After accumulating one thousand three hundred and twenty days,
they are then brought to see the *Dàshén* together,
communicating with the *Yuánqì*
and practicing *Zìrán*.
The *Tiānjūn* reviews the registers and gives secret commands
that in their conduct they must not have private, mutual trust.
To influence the heart and change the intent
so that they act without error.
The *Dàshén* says:
"The provisions granted to the various spirits have already been calculated.
Always on the last day of the eighth month,
record clearly the registers of intake and output received by the mountains, seas, mounds, ponds, flowing waters, the *Hé*, bridges, the *Huái*, the *Jǐ*, the *Jiāng*, and the lakes.
The *Tiānjūn* has rewards and gifts, which are recorded in the registers and signed.
The *Tiānjūn* previously personally re-counted and communicated with the *Zàngjīnshìshǔ*.
Let people with the right heart be in charge of what the *Tiānjūn* asks;
they should always follow the teachings
and be untiring day and night.
Order the people in charge of the chamber not to lose the departments they seek,
and separately make it known who the people with the right heart are who should receive.
It is necessary to finalize the records and registers.
There should be envoy spirits in charge of tallying the names of all those who should ascend or descend.
One hundred days beforehand, all must be documented and submitted without omission.
If the documents do not correspond,
and the *Jìcáo* does not report it, they shall be punished together.
First, command that they do not violate the divine books.
It is said that after this book is released,
in the eighth month of the third year,
it should then be shown to common people.
If there are people of faith who possess the *Dào*,
it can certainly be shown to them."
The *Tiānjūn* gave a teaching, saying:
"This person previously had *chéngfù*;
command the spirits to resolve and remove it
and to collect and store it.
For those who have not stored it, store it for them."
The *Dàshén* says:
"This person has been poor, distressed, and empty for a long time,
and I fear he cannot sustain himself.
Having gained the *Tiānjūn*'s trust,
he then commands the spirits to store it.
For those who do not store it, when their master has not yet stored it,
I fear it will not be as spoken.
Previously he begged for a command to pay obeisance and thank for the grace received;
although the day and month have not yet arrived,
let all know of it one month beforehand."
The *Tiānjūn* says:
"Send the subordinate spirits, generals, and troops into the fields and lands,
and do not miss the time to store.
Record their names,
and order the *Dìzhǔ* to be respectful and cautious.
Cause divine spirits to come and go,
and if they have desires or requests they wish to fulfill,
listen to them.
If there is faith in them,
afterwards, one should be cautious about it."
The *Dàshén* says:
"If it is so, it will surely be known throughout the four seas.
Those who love the *Dào* will support and uphold one another;
they will serve and respect it."
The *Tiānjūn* says:
"People of merit
will naturally be respected."
The *Dàshén* says:
"This person's years are not yet full,
and the appointed time has not arrived.
I request that when the time arrives, he be taught how to offer thanks.
At that time, before he has ascended,
his house will be empty,
and he will have nothing to clothe himself with.
Let those who possess the *Dào* provide food
until the time comes to stop."
The *Tiānjūn* says:
"This is but a small matter.
Use the *Tiānguān* to provide for the household,
for those who have a household and have the right heart."
The *Dàshén* says:
"I request it be as you have spoken.
Command the *Tiānguān* to provide what is due.
This person has been empty for a long time;
give him food so that he is satisfied."
The *Dàshén* says:
"Order that the *Tiānguān* spirits provide for the names
and do not let them be in want."
The *Tiānjūn* says:
"Very well."
Only the people of high antiquity all received Heaven’s response.
Having sincerity, they could achieve their goals.
Thus they were commanded to receive the Mandate
and were protected and watched over by the spirits.
For fear that there might be damage or deficiency,
they examined it day and night.
Seeing them do good,
the spirits assisted in their joy
and did not wish to hear of their evil.
They were frequently placed in the Department of Longevity.
In their hearts, they were moved to do good;
there were no times of evil.
They were caused to advance in goodness
and had intentions of filial piety, loyalty, and obedience.
What they inherited and what they practiced
they did not dare to do by their own will alone;
they acted by following the teachings.
People called it a lack of knowledge,
but I also saw and knew it.
People have the great kindness of goodness
and have compassion to contemplate it;
they strive to better themselves.
Like a person who has long been regarded with suspicion,
those who are most evil perish first.
Because of this, they diminished, measured, and restrained themselves,
fearing they might offend evil people.
Day and night they were in fear and trepidation,
not knowing what to do.
Heaven creates humans to know good and evil.
When practicing good with sincerity,
Heaven does not wish for people to have an evil reputation.
Because of this, they desire life and loathe death,
and also do not dare to violate the prohibitions,
as if it were a harm to their own bodies.
Therefore, through the causes and conditions of the *Tiānqì*,
one is able to communicate through the words and language of the intermediaries,
knowing human feelings and intentions.
Seeing their lack of goodness,
they retreat to blame themselves,
fearing there are documents or a defiled name stored within.
Like the intention of a person at that time
bestowed upon others,
they truly do not dare to face the truth or manage the complications,
but are able to reproach themselves for what was practiced.
If they do not obtain the people’s favor,
faults will be many and difficult to remove.
Therefore, people come to repent and change their circumstances;
at that moment, the path is open,
and they believe that life can be obtained again.
Unintentionally, Heaven sent the *Dàshén*,
who found the divination particularly bad.
Entering the earth first,
they use this to comfort themselves,
enduring in secret and not daring to face evil.
Though the standard words have slightly different meanings,
having already received Heaven’s grace,
they borrow a brief moment
to allow for recovery and rest,
long having the hope of living;
this is an allotment from Heaven.
Thus they obtain a portion of the intention,
for life does not remain for long.
For this reason,
one is again increasingly despondent, with a heart of shame and regret.
Wishing to see the *Tiānshén*,
they seek mercy, instruction, and precepts
to illuminate unknown matters
and prepare for the future.
One should harmonize with the *Tiānxīn*,
then one may attain minor fulfillment of wishes.
Those who covet higher things and have calculated thoughts
contemplate both good and evil
and receive an unseen command.
Then they see the *Dàshén*
and speak for themselves of the bitterness and sweetness of life.
Ordinary people seeking the mundane also covet the superior;
therefore, they cultivate and rectify themselves.
Only let the *Dàshén* command and spur their deficiencies,
causing them to awaken and look to the precepts by their side.
May the *Dàshén* have pity, examine, and search for the living ones.
The *Dàshén* said:
“Why begrudge the prohibitions and precepts?
You should know them deeply by yourself.
Each person’s words should express the actual truth of their feelings,
but I fear it is not as you say.
Consider it carefully again.
Plans come from the heart;
you should contemplate it maturely once more.”
The living one, *Shēng*, said:
“I feel fear since it has reached my own person;
how could I dare not let it come from my heart?”
The *Dàshén* said:
“If so, then it is expressed.
For now, return to a quiet place;
only when you think there is a deficiency should you seek.”
*Shēng* said:
“My endowed knowledge is rare, sparse, and little;
I have not yet attained the great penetrating precepts.
Crawling and needing instruction,
only then do I dare to come forward and see you.”
The *Dàshén* said:
“If you wish to exhaust your sincerity,
there is merit that can be attained.
Strive and contemplate by yourself;
since you were born,
the efficacy that has advanced
will resolve the *Chéngfù* of the ancestors.
When the *Chéngfù* is removed and resolved,
and faults are exhausted, you shall also ascend.
What is there to doubt?
For now, be cautious of what you say

all belong to the Earth Prefecture (Tǔfǔ).
Lifespan has a fixed period;
aligning with the Sage, one obtains sageliness;
aligning with the Worthy, one obtains worthiness.
This is the constant law of Heaven;
emolument and destiny naturally correspond.
Some even become Immortals (Shénxiān).
In the years of Yín and Shēn,
those people are like tigers.
The Sun and Moon align,
and they cannot be compared at all.
The reason it is so
is that Yín represents patterns;
it is in the domain of Wood,
and the fierce beasts of the mountains and forests
naturally cannot be withstood.
It is only suitable for purity;
Heaven dispatches them to hunt,
and they should not be seen frequently.
Many are those who fear them,
and they are named "Tigers."
When the year is within Yín,
the life is also long.
When three Yín combine in birth,
then it can be long-lasting.
Shēn is its clash,
not perishing at all.
Much evil and fear of the night,
only able to climb up and down trees,
those they fear are many.
Their destiny lies in Metal,
committing harm and injuring people.
Therefore, their lifespan is made short;
this can be known.
Serving the spirits with neglect and disorder,
essences and evils, loathing and fear, are inconstant,
with few auspicious times.
For destinies in Mǎo and Yǒu,
each aligns with its month,
and those months are again the same.
Mǎo rules the East,
binding destiny to the Eastern Stars.
There is much that lives and grows:
people’s food and drink.
Mǎo therefore refers to the Eastern direction;
True Mǎo is the center of the East.
Spring produces flourishing glory;
Summer grows its fruit.
Nothing is not bestowed;
none are not covered by virtue.
Therefore, the Eastern Star is named Benevolence (Rén);
it cannot bear to injure.
Heaven cherishes people’s years,
so they again obtain longevity.
The West is truly Yǒu, which is again in the domain of Metal;
delighting in carrying out battles,
they cannot obtain longevity.
Doing evil naturally,
how can they live long from this?
Even if they obtain the phases of King (Wáng), Minister (Xiàng), and the Month Establisher (Yuèjiàn),
it is merely as it is.
Its six or seven evils
daily lose more than half of them;
this can be known.
For those born in the periods or years of Sì and Hài,
each is placed in its month,
and again takes its name as the cause.
With heavy Yīn and no Yáng,
the life is naturally not long.
When the three Yīn meet and the time also aligns,
therefore, speaking of Sì and Hài,
the Binding Master opens the hidden.
Hài rules the Northwest,
while Sì rules the Southeast.
Whatever direction is taken or action done,
few obtain what is appropriate.
Managing life is difficult to advance,
and the lifespan is difficult to lengthen.
Therefore, it is said the Ten Patterns (Shíwén) circulate and communicate,
and the Ten Stems (Shígàn) name the achievements;
they are again suitable for Heavenly Calculation (Tiānsuàn).
Calculating their short and long,
they are mutually deduced to determine destiny.
How can the movement of Heaven be followed at one’s own will?
Therefore, today’s people of Great Virtue collectively receive these patterns.
Registers are bound to the Constellations (Xīngxiù);
destiny lies in the Heavenly Bureaus (Tiāncáo).
There are ledgers for the external and internal;
above, below, and in the eight directions,
all have patterns and principles.
How can one act at one’s own will?
People do not grasp these numbers,
and instead say, “How have I failed Heaven?”
Doing good can live out the years of one’s life;
doing evil loses the long and approaches the short.
If evil and wickedness do not stop,
disaster reaches those not yet born.
How can there be hope?
One’s actions obtain it for oneself.
Their destiny is also thin,
not exhausting their calculated lifespan;
it is placed in the pavilion in Heaven,
to be bequeathed to good people.
One can warn descendants to be cautious of this.
Returning to the correct path and repenting of faults,
one can again complete their years.
Each is distinct and clear.
Calculating what they have done,
do not resent the Heavenly Spirits (Tiānshén).
Strive to do good,
and descendants will extend their years.
If not, it is of their own doing;
one should not resent Heaven.
Correcting again and contemplating again;
those who later doubt again
should be set right.
Only the conduct of the Tàishàng shànrén,
is to know in advance the exterior and interior of Heaven and Earth,
the coming and going of Yīnyáng,
and the guiding principles of the Dào.
They give rise to thoughts from within
and do not forget the principles.
They act in accordance with Heaven,
not daring to have any doubts.
By this, they achieve success,
and offer great benevolence in service to Heaven.
Their contemplations reside within themselves,
and their actions are without error or debt.
They subtly receive from Zìrán,
and frequently see warnings such that what comes before and after can be known.
If a person violates these themselves,
they have no cause for resentment.
From ancient times until now,
there have been few trustworthy people;
their faith is a desire to deceive one another,
not considering the consequences.
Thus, Heaven and Earth are caused to be dark with anger without ceasing;
the Worthies and Sages, having knowledge, repent of their own accord.
Heaven knows this and teaches them.
They do not follow human words,
but instead look upon each other with ill intent;
they do not follow admonishments,
only wishing to please themselves.
Such people are ignorant,
worse than livestock.
For this reason,
one should blame oneself for faults;
from where does debt arise?
Thinking of others day and night,
yet not understanding the debts incurred by one's actions,
what cause is there for resentment or blame?
It is only that one is without merit,
not calculating one's own faults,
recklessly doing what should not be done.
Not receiving the Great Teaching,
but instead acting willfully,
one causes one's own life to be short;
what cause is there for resentment or blame?
One should often think of the people of high antiquity who attained immortality and transcended the world;
from where did their thoughts arise?
Looking at the books, they all speak of loyalty and filial piety,
reverently serving parents,
harmony among brothers,
having no discrepancy between exterior and interior,
superiors and inferiors in accord,
and knowing the prohibitions of Heaven.
The Spirits preside over the principles;
they report one's transgressions
without ceasing.
By cultivating oneself and self-reflecting,
one then attains life.
One's mandate of life has a term;
how can one act willfully?
Thinking of this, the heart aches,
tears fall and soak the clothes,
without any cessation.
Day by day, one cherishes the years of life,
fearing one will not attain longevity.
Seeing long-lived people and questioning them,
they say they possess loyalty and filial piety,
and do not lose the intent of Heaven and Earth.
They assist the birth of the Sìshí
and the completion of the Wǔxíng,
not daring to harm things that are meant to live.
They do good and do not infringe upon others,
they have no deception or opposition,
and in sincerity and trust, they dare not have any debt.
Their conduct is established among the people;
they dare not fail their kin or disadvantage their neighborhood.
Whenever they go out, they report to one another.
They return in due time,
and never lie heavily drunk in the marketplace.
The Worthy and Wise follow one another,
paying no heed to the foolish.
They consider the benevolence of Heaven and Earth,
not daring to expect a reward,
only reproaching themselves.
If there are further transgressions
arising from Chéngfù,
one reproaches oneself for many years,
and then [the heavens] are moved.
In worldly life, there are many transgressions and debts,
with no resolution at all.
One walks in sorrow and bitterness,
not knowing where to stop.
Every time one sees others have faults,
one returns to reproach oneself,
not knowing where to settle.
Longing to see the writings of righteousness
and their good warnings,
by the fortune of one's fate,
one encounters the warning scriptures and texts of the Tiān Dàshén.
Thinking and calculating repeatedly,
one considers one's many faults,
without any cessation.
Bowing one's head and beating one's breast while wailing,
one has a body but cannot rectify oneself,
and instead has much resentment.
The prohibited books are extremely weighty,
yet one touches them oneself,
causing one's life not to be long.
Morning and night, one repents.
Hoping to live a little longer,
one dares not do evil,
but thinks further of practicing kindness and charity.
Receiving its principles,
one has no evil words,
only showing tears,
moved to sorrow in the heart.
The Tiānshén hear of this,
and come down to say:
"Who is this person?
Why are they so sorrowful?"
They glimpse the people of Great Virtue,
whose lives are extended and long-lasting.
Asking them, they say:
"This person only acts in response to the mind of Heaven
and accords with the intent of Earth;
therefore they attain longevity."
Returning to the quiet chamber to contemplate this,
just as the words of the Tàishàng dérén,
one therefore examines oneself.
Causing the Spirits to see one's self-reproach and repentance,
the Spirits return to Heaven and speak the Way, saying:
"There is a person repenting of faults, walking with tears,
without ever stopping.
They fear they will not live,
and for this reason they reproach themselves."
The Dàshén hear of this
and say the Tiānjūn often commands the various Spirits, saying:
"If there is a person of merit and goodness who is loyal, filial, and compliant,
let what is said promote that person alone."
Consequently, they report to the Tiānjūn.
The Tiānjūn says:
"I have heard that this person has reproached themselves and repented of faults
for many years.
This was originally a common person,
yet they reproach themselves for faults without ceasing,
becoming a person of the highest goodness.
Let the Dàshén frequently go to observe them,
to know how their conduct is and if they have good intentions.
For those to be promoted, place their life years in the Shòucáo,
observe what they do,
and then they may compensate for their deficiencies."
The Dàshén says:
"This person has reproached themselves for a very long time,
their Chéngfù is removed and resolved.
I request that when there is a vacancy, they be promoted to fill it,
with the title of Tàishàng shànrén,
so they may report on those below who are insufficient."
The Tiānjūn says:
"The conduct of a Tàishàng shànrén
must certainly be according to these words.
Let the Dàshén frequently command them,
guard and watch them until they become a Spirit and ascend,
but all must wait for their allotted years and not be infringed upon."
The Dàshén says:
"This person originally had no record in the registers,
but having received the command to be in the Shòucáo,
I request to wait for a vacancy above,
to fill it according to the order of years,
without overstepping."
The Tiānjūn says:
"On the day they attain the order to fill a vacancy,
frequently submit their name and do not miss the term."
The Dàshén says, "Yes, yes."
Only the conduct of the Tàishàng rénrén,
is to accumulate merit and pile up deeds in Heaven.
Heaven then listens and trusts,
causing them to assist the Dōnghuáng in arranging things meant to be born,
with flowers and fruits to provide food for the people,
enabling them to be warm and well-fed.
Their bodies grow large,
they nourish one another in succession,
Yīnyáng joins and meets,
men and women take form,
the old and young follow one another,
receiving their mandates from the numbers of Heaven.
In the stars, the Èrshíbā xiù complete one another in cycles;
the sun and moon shine and observe so that none may escape,
alternating in giving birth to one another,
how could there be any cessation?
But people do not know this,
thinking each is their own master.
Although there are designated masters,
they examine and maintain one another.
The reason for this is that
human life has short and long spans;
through spring, autumn, winter, and summer,
there is further birth, death, and impermanence.
Therefore they are made to master one another,
transferring and inquiring of one another,
increasing or decreasing the count of longevity,
and transferring or bestowing it upon one another.
Therefore it is said the Sìshí, Wǔxíng, Sun, Moon, and Stars all hold one's fate;
for the good, it is increased,
The wicked withdraw on their own;
with their faults, large and small, calculated,
there are naturally constant laws.
Executing the law as it proceeds,
how could any escape?
Above the heavens and below the earth,
they correspond to each other like the outer and inner layers;
furthermore, various deities are installed and made to serve together.
Therefore it is said that the Tiānjūn issues edicts to the Cáo,
each transferring records to one another,
becoming in turn the Zhífú,
and they must not have the slightest personal bias.
Observing the lower from the upper,
how could there be any error?
People with a true nature
naturally have no evil intent;
though they may have small faults,
they return to repent for those matters,
and the transgressions are then removed and dissolved.
There are registers into which documents are constantly entered;
the wicked are assigned to the Lower Bureaus,
the good are reported as good,
and the wicked are reported as wicked.
The spirits of fortune and calamity
each follow according to where one is entered;
if the wicked can repent on their own,
their names are transferred into the Bureaus of Goodness.
If the good do evil,
they are moved back into the Bureaus of Evil;
how can there be any relief or rest?
Among the living people on earth,
there are those in the womb not yet born
whose names are in the Register of Immortality.
When their years are full and their conduct is completed,
the living ones are recorded,
and they are only submitted when they have a guarantor.
The reason for this is that
their lifespan is difficult to await and is highly valued,
therefore the guarantor is held accountable for any faults along with them.
For this reason, those who are not loyal, filial, or obedient and have no merit
have no one to guarantee them;
they merely exist for the sake of the achievements of their ancestors,
to allow for sacrifices to be maintained.
If they uniquely do not stop doing evil,
how can they have descendants to provide offerings?
As for those who eat filth,
how can they possibly serve with the Great Spirits of Heaven for long?
Among those in the filth who correspond to the heavenly scripts and measurements,
Heaven sends spirits to teach them.
When the years and months are fulfilled,
Heaven commands the Guardian Spirit of the Great Granary of Heaven
to cut off their consumption of material things
and have them receive the Qì of the Great Granary of Heaven for food and digestion,
causing them to become light and transform into spirit-beings,
emerging from the profound and entering the dark mystery;
they then submit their names,
and are no longer in the standard ledgers.
How can they seek life,
and how could ordinary people know of this?
If a person is naturally good and does not lose the Heart of Heaven,
the Great Spirits will move their heart,
making them rejoice in cultivating life,
while worldly people are naturally greedy for it.
The reason for this is that
when one practices evil without a single moment of goodness,
merely coveting fine clothes and chariots,
following one another in self-satisfaction,
their lifespan will not be fulfilled,
yet Heaven and Earth do not strip away their desires.
The wicked shall also not for long gaze upon the sun, moon, and stars of Heaven.
They shall return to the Long Night;
how could they remain for long?
Such a person cannot take themselves as a teacher to do good;
Heaven knows they have done evil for a long time past,
and so causes them to eat material food.
Thus they are hidden beneath the earth,
governed by the Earth Spirits,
and prevented from being born again.
Therefore, this is shown through writing,
merely to let it be known.
Some undergo Shījiě and divide their form,
their skeletal body being separated.
The corpse remains in one body,
while the spirit becomes the person's corpse,
causing people to see it,
and all say they have already died.
Later, those who know
see that they are still present;
this is a person of Shījiě.
After a long time, having accumulated years,
they are next promoted to those who ascend to heaven in broad daylight.
When their years are many and their merit is completed,
they are reborn with illuminating light,
assisting the Heavenly Spirits everywhere.
They return to dwell within the clouds,
and in all the regions under their jurisdiction, there are Shījiě Xiānrén,
who govern and know the matters of humans and ghosts.
In a household that possesses the Dào,
those who depart receive enfeoffment,
becoming the venerable ones of ghosts named Dìlíngzhī,
and they are also allowed to wear purple, mugwort, green, and yellow.
Their governance has higher and lower levels,
and they are transferred to various posts;
but if even a fragment of evil is heard of them,
they are demoted to the ranks of ghosts.
Do you know this?
Therefore it is said that death and life are different paths;
how can they be compared?
Go now; I will cease my words and thoughts for a while;
for what is missing or insufficient afterward,
I shall speak of it.
As for the conduct of the Highest Good Person (*Tàishàng Shànrén*),
it is to manifest and know the matters that should be performed by Heaven and Earth.
Each has a primary focus,
each has its specific words,
each cultivates its affairs,
each perfects its spirit,
each establishes its merit,
each practices its loyalty,
each organizes its patterns,
each bestows charity upon people,
each guides their own advancement,
each attains the core heart of Heaven and Earth,
and each does not fail the generative and transformative powers of the Four Seasons and Five Elements.
This accords with the Highest Good Person (*Tàishàng Shànrén*).
They are the trust of Heaven
and the protection of Earth.
All attain the core of Central Harmony.
They know the internal and external movements of human emotions.
They act upon receiving orders
and dare not lose the intent of the Great Sage (*Dàshèng*).
Below, they dare not violate the prohibitions of the various gods.
They constantly think of perfecting others
and making them joyfully become good people.
They cause them to attain the heart of Heaven and the intent of Earth,
stabilizing the internal through the external,
achieving success within the body,
enabling them to attain longevity
and be placed on the Register of Immortality,
allowing them to serve and hold office alongside the Great Deities (*Dàshén*).
They can distinguish right from wrong,
are loyal and sincere to Heaven,
and reflect the sun, moon, and stars.
They do not lose the laws and measures
and do not lose their will and intent.
They constantly seek to sustain life,
thinking of upholding the transformations of Heaven
and also knowing the principles of Earth.
Their hearts are thus filled with joy.
They also know the registers of good and bad fortune
and the matters of survival and ruin,
desiring to share the same path with Nature (*Zìrán*).
They act with little evil or greed.
Seeing the warnings of the Great Deities (*Dàshén*),
they feel pity for those who do not yet know,
illuminating their shortcomings
so they may reach the Record of Longevity.
They see the Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) and receive the gift of life,
remaining long upon the Register of Immortality.
They perform the affairs of Heaven above
and understand the principles of Earth below.
Regarding what they see and hear,
their eyes are bright and their ears are sharp.
They know from afar the infinite matters of coming and going.
Their documents and petitions are well-communicated,
and they also know the essential mysteries.
This is the wish of the Highest Good Person (*Tàishàng Shànrén*).
Only the Great Deities (*Dàshén*) of Heaven clearly know these specific wishes.
They yearn for Nature (*Zìrán*),
recording and aligning with the life-breath (*shēngqì*) in their actions,
without end.
It is often said that Heaven does not snatch away a person's wishes,
and Earth does not snatch away a person's peace.
Thus, Nature (*Zìrán*) dares not impose even a hair's breadth of constraint,
nor do the various gods find it laborious to deeply record their writings.
Day and night, they think of their transgressions and burdens,
fearing they might not match the intent of the Lord of the Highest (*Tàishàng Jūn*).
What would they begrudge or cherish
so as not to exhaust their loyalty, sincerity, and filial piety?
