They should say of themselves that they have received grace and bounty,
attained glory and splendor,
and do not look for reward.
Heaven's heart deeply loves them,
yet they only blame themselves for their faults,
being rarely forgiven.
May the Great Deity (*Dàshén*) forgive and warn them;
they cannot help but yearn for this
and dare not distance themselves.
They constantly worry alone about not repaying grace
and having sins return to their bodies,
fearing they cannot be absolved through explanation,
feeling only grief and distress.
Even if they are shown forgiveness and examined,
let them be allowed to reflect upon their own burdens.
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) said:
"The Highest Good Person (*Tàishàng Shànrén*) reflects on faults and blames themselves.
When their petitions and words emerge and are heard above,
it is because their words reach that far;
I only fear they do not know what to say.
The Trust of Heaven (*Tiānxìn*) especially excels and honors them;
they can attain infinite longevity.
They should again keep their hearts focused from afar and not forget the portion of great bounty granted by Heaven."
The Lord of the Highest (*Tàishàng Jūn*) praised this,
saying that one who loves life by nature
disregards wealth and lust.
Seeing those who are living,
they constantly think of being with them for a long time.
When would they ever act recklessly or against the Way (*Dào*),
or have an unfeeling mind that does not repay heavy grace?
"I only cherish my life since birth
but have not seen the Great Portion.
Only by receiving the grace of teaching and warning
can I know the principles of my portion.
I should be said to know my fate,
not resenting Heaven,
nor daring to resent myself and thus hinder my life.
If our hearts are joined,
would there be a time for greed?
I only fear the exhaustion of my lifespan
and not seeing the distribution of Heaven's great bounty.
May you again command and warn this ignorant life
so that having knowledge and forethought may be a great grace;
it is not something words can repay.
I only engrave this thought in my heart,
constantly keeping it within.
Not forgetting it even in hunger or thirst,
I seek warnings to find life,
only hoping for forgiveness and examination."
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) said:
"I originally advanced myself from among the gods to the Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*)
without any small error.
I have the instruction of merit in assisting Heaven and Earth,
and my records are above with the Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*).
When would I ever forget you?
I request to present the person's petition of self-reproach,
having for many years yearned for the transformations of Heaven.
Is this person on the registers or not?"
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"Those who blame themselves are all in accord with Nature (*Zìrán*),
and they are also the good ones aided by the gods.
Let the person in charge of the Heavenly Documents and Registers (*Tiānwén Jí*) look into it;
if there is self-reproach,
then the spirit of the living registers shall be told to command the inspection of the writings.
The files and registers do contain this person."
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"If a person naturally performs good
and does not violate prohibitions,
it is brought about by the person's conduct.
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) shall further examine them in detail;
if there is any deficiency in their implementation, report the name."
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) said:
"Since the Great Beginning (*Tàichǔ*),
those among the gods with merit who attained the intent of Heaven have been advanced,
but there are many vacancies.
Given this person's conduct,
their name should be provided to fill a position."
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"The duties within the departments are many and troublesome;
calculate their merit and remove their faults,
and ensure they never again violate what they have said."
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) said:
"This person of the Highest follows what is upright,
and their transgressions and burdens are particularly few."
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"Reflect on this again;
if there are any who have not been praised or recommended,
hold the Trustworthy Guarantors (*Bǎoxìn*) responsible for filling the vacancies."
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"The matters of this group
must be examined with precision."
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) said:
"I request that it be as the petition says.
Before a hundred days have passed,
the various gods in Heaven will compete to recommend them.
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) reports this intention."
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"If it is so, let each person who can be sent be sent.
Send them to oversee affairs.
If they are subsequently valued,
those who are trustworthy shall be appointed as True Beings (*Zhēn*)."
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) said:
"I request to dispatch a divine messenger to summon them to come up,
first transforming their physical form."
The divine messenger went and transformed them into a brilliant and radiant essence.
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) took this report to the Lord.
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"The person has already transformed into a god
and is standing outside the gate, not yet entered."
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said,
have them go to the Office of the Chief Official (*Zhǔzhě Cáo*) to be presented.
The Great Deity (*Dàshén*) spoke,
reporting what was said.
"Yes, yes.
I request that the report be handled as stated;
it is appropriate to then observe their conduct."
The Lord of Heaven (*Tiānjūn*) said:
"It shall be as the Great Deity (*Dàshén*) has reported."
Only people of the highest knowledge [Tàishàng],
can foreknow the matters of Heaven [Tiān],
that which should be implemented,
and that which should be upheld.
Matters arise naturally;
when the Original Qi [Yuánqì] is added together and reaches maturity,
it is clearly known.
They transform their hearts
to make them natural
in all that they do.
Therefore, having knowledge, they know the internal and external;
in their actions of exiting and entering,
none fail to be accomplished,
none fail to find their place,
and none fail to transform in due time.
They reverently look up to the Awesome Deity [Wēishén]
to complete their work
and to make known their Virtue [Dé].
They never distance themselves from loyalty and trustworthiness
and have never been lax.
Day and night, they are anguished and fearful,
not departing from their inner selves,
inclining their thoughts and longing to achieve success
so that they may meet with the Great Deity [Dàshén].
They communicate in words and speech,
practicing what he teaches
and advancing what they know.
Constantly thinking of success
and receiving grace from the deity,
they extend their life and increase their years.
Therefore, they are granted knowledge
to look from within to without.
What is there they do not know?
What is there they do not see?
They see the heart and clearly perceive every thought.
They desire only the Way of long life,
longing to ride [celestial chariots]
and serve as messengers for the Great Deity [Dàshén].
Wherever they arrive,
they dare not talk back;
arriving exactly on time,
they long for their hearts to open.
Receiving the words of the deity,
acting as the deity acts,
and knowing the deity's ways,
they strive for self-confidence
and only then dare to come forward and speak,
seeking only to be granted life.
They dare not seek high office,
seeking only to be pitied.
Although they see matters of survival and ruin,
their inner hearts are fearful.
Receiving the Great Teaching [Dàjiào],
they must immediately communicate it,
bestowing grace and spreading benefits,
benefiting those above
and benefiting the people.
Their names are recorded in the registers [Lùjí],
and they always remain in the state of immortality.
Their hearts then joyfully and playfully contemplate,
devoting all their effort to the place of the Lord of Heaven [Tiānjūn].
Having accumulated merit over the years,
they only then come forward to speak.
They hope only that the Great Deity [Dàshén] will compensate for their deficiencies,
knowing that while their own words are humble, the subject is great.
Therefore, they strive to advance,
receiving the secret mysteries [Yǐmì].
Diligently serving at the gates and chambers,
they dare not rest,
desiring to receive instructions and admonitions [Jiàojiè]
and to be informed of their inadequacies.
They wish for inspection and examination
and do not go against what is said,
making it necessary to heed the words and commands of the Great Deity [Dàshén].
People of the highest knowledge [Tàishàng]
already illuminate and see much themselves,
yet they cannot yet fully know the divisions and boundaries of Heaven [Tiān];
what, then, is the full range of prohibitions?
The deities of Heaven [Tiān] illuminate it all,
as the people of the highest knowledge [Tàishàng] have said.
It is only that they wish to know what is spoken, the path, and the actions to take;
what is there to doubt?
The Lord of Heaven [Tiānjūn] said:
“I constantly command the various deities that those people who desire loyalty, filial piety, sincerity, and trustworthiness and who have merit
should have their names submitted.
These are the people of the highest knowledge [Tàishàng],
whose rank and appearance are sought after;
therefore, they clarify themselves with their hearts.
It is only feared that they speak for themselves through writing and ink;
how could the instructions and admonitions [Jiàojiè] of Heaven [Tiān] be withheld?
It is often said that it is distressing to have no one to receive the books,
fearing that the external and internal do not correspond.
If one wishes to advance their knowledge and reflection
and to inquire broadly and attain deep understanding,
this is also what should be known.
Go and listen to what the Great Deity [Dàshén] says.
Heaven [Tiān] has grave prohibitions
which one cannot but be cautious of,
one cannot but be respectful of,
and one cannot but be fearful of;
only then is it acceptable.
Indeed, the prohibitions are numerous;
one must know their essentials
and furthermore open the ears and eyes and apply the heart.”
“Yes, yes.”
Thus, there came from within
the Great Prohibitions [Dàjiè] of Heaven [Tiān]:
“All those who wish to be advanced
and who seek to live long should advance what they know.
To have knowledge and not speak,
as if only listening,
is to lack the heart to advance oneself.
If the heart has knowledge and thoughts,
those thoughts should be advanced and presented.
If there is a will within,
one should advance and present that will;
if there is sincerity,
one should advance and present that sincerity;
if there is filial piety,
one should advance and present that filial piety.
This is to attain the very heart of Heaven [Tiān];
one must not fail to advance all of it.
The Lord of Heaven [Tiānjūn] foreknows human sentiments;
it is not permitted to have something not advanced
and fail to speak of it.
Hiding knowledge and concealing ability,
Heaven [Tiān] detests such a person
and prevents them from appearing in the Register of Longevity [Shòují].
Do you know this or not?
Not only will they not appear in the Register of Longevity [Shòují],
but they will first lose their Essence [Jīng],
which will leave their body,
and they will lose their allotted years.
Can one not be cautious?
The reason people of the highest knowledge [Tàishàng] are as they are
is because the Lord of Heaven [Tiānjūn] knows who has knowledge and who does not;
he knows it himself.
What doubt is there?
Just carefully contemplate the words of the deity
and do not go against those words, that is all.”
The person of the highest knowledge [Tàishàng] said:
“I am lowly and foolish and strive to ask about things I cannot reach,
desiring to receive that which I do not know.
How could I dare to hide knowledge or conceal ability?
If I let the Lord of Heaven [Tiānjūn] and the various deities hear of this,
it would lead to the loss of my life and my years,
and my longevity would not be long.
This is the root of transgression and disaster;
even destroying my body would not suffice for atonement.
How could I dare to advance it?
May the Great Deities [Dàshén] illuminate and forgive my inadequacies.”
The Great Deity [Dàshén] said:
“People who seek life and loathe death
also naturally have intentions and wills that are unacceptable,
fearing times of confusion.”
The student [Shēng] said:
“I myself do not know the text of the prohibitions.
Yet I have received the grace and favor of the Great Deity [Dàshén],
who teaches me in this way.
How could I dare to rest
and not advance what I know and what is to be said?
May the Great Deity [Dàshén] record this or not.”
The Great Deity [Dàshén] said:
“It is not easy to recommend one;
it requires a guarantor and trust.
If you satisfy the heart and will of the Lord of Heaven [Tiānjūn],
only then can you hope for life.
You must examine this carefully.”
“I, the student [Shēng], truly desire life,
therefore I exhaust my loyalty and sincerity.
I dare not become lax or rest;
I contemplate my faults and blame myself.
How could I dare to lose track of day or night?”
The Lord of Heaven [Tiānjūn] heard this
and said:
“These are the words of a person of the highest knowledge [Tàishàng].
I know this record and text.
This person's name is in it;
there were deficiencies, but now it is complete.
Command the Deity of the Register of Life [Shēngjí zhī Shén]
to examine the records and registers for this person.
Although he has a name
and is naturally good and very knowledgeable,
he must fulfill his allotted years.
Do not lose track of his years and months, Deity.”
“Yes, yes.”
Only the purposeful people of *Tàishàng*,
each know their assigned department;
each has their own path,
their own conduct,
their own service,
their own advancement,
their own reports,
their own words,
their own destination,
and their own actions.
Their hearts are not tied to the internal,
but they constantly think of fulfilling loyalty, trustworthiness, and filial piety.
Truly having merit before Heaven,
accumulating deeds over the years,
without ever slackening.
Forgetting personal favors and roles,
they constantly think of cherishing life;
being protected by the various gods above,
they dare not exercise even small personal preferences.
Always harboring a heart of awe,
never feeling complacent,
they hope to receive the precepts of *Tàishàng*
to preserve their lives;
how could they dare forget the bestowal of the Great Role?
May the various *Dàshén* slightly look upon what is lacking;
the heart always yearns for the affairs of *Tàishàng*,
what ought to be practiced,
according to the rules and standards,
manifesting trust naturally,
looking out to the four borders,
and reaching into the four corners.
Receiving what Heaven knows,
expressing what has not yet happened,
the heart contemplates the *Dàshén*’s memorials and communications,
what is advanced and reported;
they dare not judge it with their own minds,
but always consult with the various gods
whether it may be adopted or not,
always fearing they might not gain the trust of the gods' inner hearts.
Considering oneself to be fundamentally a person without error,
if from within there arises yearning,
always in a life without harm to preserve the body,
previously desiring its radiance,
reaching up to the sounds of the essence-less and formless,
penetratingly reaching *Tàishàng* as a messenger's advancement,
not daring to forget and slacken, thereby hindering the Great Transformation.
May the gods examine their desire for life;
they dare not depart from the left side of the *Dàshén*.
Seeing the precepts,
the heart opens and the eyes brighten,
desiring to be within the records of longevity,
increasing their lifespan,
thinking of advancing with merit,
personally attending to it,
not daring to trust themselves
and arbitrarily dictate right and wrong,
or struggle over insufficiencies.
Those who look up are always diligent,
only asking for compassion to illuminate and warn them.
When could the thought of kindness and love ever slacken?
The heart wishes to see the divine day and night,
desiring to know any lapses in the prohibitions,
so as to stir their heart,
making them see those areas where they fall short.
This is not something reported by words or speech;
only hoping to be examined,
with the thought piercing through the diaphragm.
The *Dàshén* said:
"This is a purposeful person of *Tàishàng*,
also doing what is appropriate.
Seeking the heavy precepts and prohibitions of Heaven—
for a person who possesses knowledge is naturally clear and understanding,
distinguishing the principles—
why is there a need for spoken precepts?
Holding the heart to aim at the heart,
there is no room for private interest.
Observing the lower from above,
one naturally knows what one governs.
Now, the purposeful person of *Tàishàng*
is close to Heaven,
trusted by the Heavenly Deities;
one should just maintain the intent of the heart,
always in fear of losing it.
As for the rest, the heart naturally knows it;
strive to communicate and inquire widely,
do not fail in what is said."
"People of knowledge have much clarity,
but I fear at the time they may not live up to their words;
why worry about not reporting to each other?
Such a person has a heart to reflect on their own transgressions.
Simply consider the before and after,
and longevity naturally emerges from within,
resonating with the heart of *Tiānjūn*.
I give a few warnings to the purposeful person, saying:
'I was born originally as a person of the wild fields,
seeing long life and aging transformations,
again encountering the bright scenery,
where the nourishing fluids flow in and out without loss,
and I have not seen any lapse.
Students are many,
but those who achieve are few—nearly non-existent.
The reason for this is
they do not hold their hearts with meticulous care and they speak lightly;
their registers of fate are not suitable,
therefore they are rare.
Now I see these matters of previous conduct,
and increasingly correct my ways and change my integrity,
opening the heart to remain committed.
Desiring to open the voice,
to hear well, cherishing longevity and years,
for this reason I dare not rest or slacken;
may the *Dàshén* only examine my shortcomings.'"
The *Dàshén* said:
"The purposeful person shall be granted a registration;
let us petition the records of the Bureau.
Those with names shall be reported to *Tiānjūn*,
for the *Dàshén* cannot act on their own."
*Shēng* said:
"May the *Dàshén* only illuminate and deliberate upon it;
I dare not distance myself
or lean toward the outside,
I will surely devote myself personally."
The *Dàshén* said:
"I shall take the case of the purposeful person and report it;
if there is a name registered,
why worry about not responding?"
*Shēng* said:
"May the *Dàshén* report it;
on the day of completion,
I will devote my life and fate;
what need is there to expect a return?"
The *Dàshén* reported the matter to *Tiānjūn*, saying:
"The purposeful person of *Tàishàng*
all hold their hearts firmly and meticulously,
their will always desires faith in the high;
I command the presiding deity to observe them.
If there be such a person,
let them advance and report to the *Dàshén*.
I command the master to observe them;
regarding the one whose name and document are present:
before this person was born,
their name was already present."
The *Dàshén* returned and reported:
"This person had a record before being born;
it is only by the grace of *Tàishàng*."
*Tiānjūn* said:
"People with records shall be promoted;
they take responsibility for their *Chéngfù*,
and the *Dàshén* sends a *Dàshén* to remove the tally of *Chéngfù*,
to transform their hearts,
changing them into deities,
and when their years are full, they shall advance upward."
The *Dàshén* said:
"This person’s years and calculations are full;
counting the overdue period, it is nearly a hundred days;
as it was not fixed before,
therefore they are halted for now."
*Tiānjūn* said:
"I command the *Dàshén* to bring them up for now,
placing them in an interim post;
if there is a vacancy for a True One, have them fill it;
for they can extraordinarily exhaust their essence and fulfill their will,
knowing how to eliminate burdens while practicing."
The *Dàshén* said:
"I request to bring them up as *Tiānjūn* has said;
once more refining the count of their longevity and calculations,
the enlightened ones shall ascend to Heaven in broad daylight."
*Tiānjūn* said:
"This is what is appropriate for a purposeful person;
I wish to let them have something to govern."
The *Dàshén* bowed in agreement.
Requesting the command to be rectified,
the affair follows the original text.
The *Dàshén* said:
"Report to the Bureau of Ascension."
The audience-seeker reported to the *Dàshén*, saying:
"Please command the Presiding Bureau."
The Presiding Officer having reported:
"Let them be appointed to an interim post;
if there is a vacancy for a True One, have them fill it."
*Tiānjūn* said:
"As the Bureau has reported."
To the right: Seeing good deeds in Heaven; whether they should be hidden or not results in good or bad fortune.
In ancient times, there were the formless Shénrén,
who studied and sought the Shēngdào.
Thus, above, they shared the same will as the Wěiqì,
and in their thoughts, they constantly yearned to obtain the longevity of long life,
never daring to lose the intent of the Wěiqì in their contemplation.
Settling at dusk and inquiring in the morning,
they held firmly to and cherished life,
keeping it always in mind and never forgetting.
They periodically looked back and observed themselves,
exhausting the utmost of loyalty and integrity,
following and upholding the will of the Wěiqì.
This allowed their upward path to be clear and penetrating,
clearly hearing unseen things from the four directions
and the sound of the Xīshēng;
as they moved in and out, up and down,
all was according to laws and measures.
The various spirits and Jīngqì
all came of their own accord to serve and observe their expressions.
Fearing they might lose their intent or connection,
they all possessed a heart of awe.
Their clothing and footwear became perfectly suited to them;
as they bestowed kindness and spread grace,
it was heard throughout the heavens and the earth.
Beyond the four directions, the six poles, and the eight frontiers,
reaching even the Xiānshēng,
each weighed the errors of good and evil, abundance and scarcity.
Covered by great grace,
they respectfully received and carried out commands,
which moved the stars and luminaries.
With boundless resources
and boundless virtue,
they selected the pure and good
to shield and conceal themselves.
Their wishes were fulfilled,
their hearts were naturally blessed and unblocked,
and they received the gift of living a boundless lifespan.
Peaceful and indifferent, with little ornamentation,
they kept their physical bodies whole in their thoughts;
how could there be any slackening or rest?
Others cannot know me,
and I do not hear of them;
with no salary and no merit,
by what cause could one be arrayed together above with the Wěiqì?
For this reason, they cherished, loved, and nurtured themselves,
and extended their benevolence even to the very young everywhere—
how could there be anyone who did not receive it?
They only contemplated their own movement within the Zhōnghé of Heaven and Earth,
illuminating and reaching the sun, moon, and stars.
They drew light from before them;
the Èrshíbā Xiù took their turns on duty,
observing the people's use of the Zhīgàn,
while good and bad fortune were recorded in patterns.
But people know little;
they consider themselves wise,
but in their movements and stillness,
they provide no benefit to Heaven.
Disasters and punishments strike for violating prohibitions,
leading even to the destruction of the family,
the severing of the lineage without succession,
and ancestors left without sacrifices—
is it not only that their lives are not preserved for long?
What can be done about such people!
They act without following the Gǔwén,
believing themselves not to have offended the Guǐshén.
This causes the Sānqì to be in disharmony;
there is also the matter of fate's thickness or thinness.
They cannot fully and deeply contemplate calamity,
so the spirits of the Sānqì are sent to command and warn them.
Those who take heed are good;
those who are not good prepare themselves for the underworld,
with calamity flowing down to their descendants.
Heaven decrees this for those who are un-submissive;
they practice evil and abandon good—
how could they long endure?
The Huángshàng does not wish to see them,
and swiftly cuts short their years.
People do not realize this about themselves,
and instead resent the Cāngtiān.
When has Heaven ever treated one unjustly?
Man seeks this for himself.
Having absolutely no wisdom or foresight,
they have the lives of dogs and sheep—
how can they expect to long encounter fortune?
Caught in the same net as birds,
they bump against the mesh,
and their greed for food harms their bodies.
The crowds follow one another,
not cherishing their years.
If among them there is one who knows,
they depart for the land of no-harm beyond the four borders.
How is it that only they obtain this?
It is also within the Mìng zìrán.
Though they reside in places without people,
it is their fate that is preserved.
In this world, there are few who repay this grace;
it is the fate of the times.
How painful, what can be done!
They say to themselves, "How have I failed Heaven?"
Among the people of antiquity,
not one in ten thousand matches them.
They are greedy for wealth and lust,
disregarding impending trouble,
until disaster reaches the womb itself.
They do not see the sun, moon, or stars;
what a pity and how painful!
They leave themselves incomplete,
and their fate becomes tied to the earth.
How destitute are such people!
There are also others of their kind;
plants, trees, birds, and beasts are the same.
They do not think to correct themselves or straighten their intent;
they utter evil words without restraint.
Above, there are spirits who record; below, they lack Líng.
Above, nothing is hidden;
their master sits there.
Each should strive,
seeking the intent of the warnings and commands of the spirits,
and the meeting point of good and bad fortune—
how could there be no retribution?
Therefore, the Shénrén are commanded to establish protections and prohibitions for the people,
to let them see the taboos of life and death.
Life is what the Yángqì bestows;
in the registers, there is the Zhēnshénxiānlù.
Those with faults are removed from it.
What the Yīnqì bestows
is promptly placed in the Sǐbù.
Deeply contemplate and think upon this;
do not lose the Tiānwǎng,
extending down to the Dìlǐ.
One must understand human feelings,
the internal and external of coming and going,
when to advance and when to retreat,
and not bring blame upon others.
Then each may gain an increase in years,
reaching even to their descendants.
After receiving the warning,
be extremely cautious with your words.
Those who do evil remain below,
and those above do not look upon them.
The people of the mundane world
have little filial piety and little loyalty;
they are greedy for what they desire,
plundering and taking what is wrong.
Those who have a murderous heart
never let it leave their lips—
how can they hope to live?
Calamity and blame will surely come;
it is only a matter of sooner or later.
Uphold what is recorded by the celestial patterns and the spirits;
one must certainly keep away from evil.
One must not test oneself;
testing life brings life,
testing death brings death,
and death will surely come without doubt.
Therefore, I speak carefully again,
telling you over and over:
do not associate with the ignorant
who have minor dissenting words.
The Chángshēng zhī dào
is near at hand within the Sānshén.
The Sānqì combine to form a person;
if they do not form,
they scatter and become earth,
lying at the same level as tiles and stones,
broken into pieces in unseen places,
unable to be compared with those who are whole.
The Sānmìng zhī shén
are close within the heart.
What do they cherish, what do they love?
Instead, they are greedy for physical ruin,
being displayed to the public in the market—
when will they ever return to life?
Parents feel pity and concern,
wives and children suffer hardship,
distant relatives are pleased by it,
and neighbors regret that it happened so late.
Death flows down to future generations.
If one can correct oneself and do good,
their passage through time will again be long;
where Zhìchéng is applied,
things follow their natural course.
Be extremely cautious of the internal and external,
and the space between Yīnyáng.
The creation and growth of the Sìshí
must not be destroyed.
Between Heaven above, Earth below, and the Zhōnghé,
all have their own masters.
For people of knowledge,
the methods of signs are what they ponder.
The living share the same will as the Tiāndào;
the evil cause their own years to perish—
can one not be cautious?
The words of the Shénrén
all receive Heaven's response;
one must not resent for oneself.
The period for extending life
reaches up to those who do good,
allowing them to complete their Tiānnián.
The evil descend into the Huángquán.
Contemplate this, contemplate this, and do not transmit it recklessly.
Those who are evil transmit and receive evil,
suffering its calamities.
In death and life, they occupy different places,
and none dare to speak a word.
If one acts without goodness,
do not resent others;
since there are always those who record such deeds,
there is no reason to feel resentment again.
Read the book and understand its meaning;
be cautious and reverent toward the divine book.
The spirits and ghost messengers
all act for a cause.
For those of a destined house who are able to see this text,
be careful not to harm yourselves
or deceive and wrong good people.
When Heaven reduces a person's lifespan
and they fall ill with sickness,
there is no need to seek help
by troubling doctors and distressing shamans.
When the register is due to be cut off,
what further doubt can there be?
Examine it carefully and contemplate it;
reflect on it and consider it.
Thus one may avoid suffering calamities;
once calamity and misfortune arrive,
there is no longer any rescue.
The Zhēnrén holds this book to show it to the ignorant,
that they may change themselves for the better;
do not despise the words of the book.
What was said before and after
is all repeated and emphasized.
The reason for this is that
death and life change one's fate;
if the prohibitions are not spoken,
there is no way to survive. □□
Naturally,
one should only know the sincerity of the heart and love the text,
and understand what is said.
Therefore, let one guard the One within the body
to complete one's natural lifespan.
By guarding the One and reflecting on faults,
one shall again obtain an extension of time.
The ways of Heaven are hundreds of millions,
yet few attain their truth.
Regarding the Hétú and the Luòshū,
those who discard them are numerous.
The reason for this is
they do not believe their texts.
Few achieve immortal transcendence;
they simply remain common people.
Now, because of the teacher of the three divine beings,
for those whose hearts are moved again,
divine spirits attach to people,
not wishing for the earthly Qì to summon them.
Contemplate and reflect upon its meaning in detail;
do not doubt this text.
Repeatedly, the teacher of the divine beings
has received the teachings of Heaven;
therefore, through those listed in the records,
the meaning of the book is thoroughly understood.
Heaven has four cardinal points,
Earth has four cardinal points,
therefore the sun and moon pass and push one another in succession.
The stars have their degrees and measures,
observing and examining right and wrong.
People have noble and lowly status,
and lifespans have length and shortness;
each receives their destiny from the *Liùjiǎ*.
Births occur early or late,
with stipends appropriately matched.
Good and evil dwell in different places,
without missing even a tiny fraction.
Common people do not know this,
and instead claim there is no truth.
Only by harmonizing with the spirits and divinities
can one be called a human being.
Gaining the heart and mind of the spirits and divinities,
one can then become a ruler of men.
Days and hours have their correspondences,
and allotments reside in their respective departments.
Those who obtain the response of Heaven
are raised up by the *Tiānshén*.
Those who obtain the response of Earth
are nurtured by the *Dìshén*.
Those who obtain the response of *Zhōnghé*
are assisted by human ghosts.
Obtaining good responds with good;
the good naturally praise and elevate one another.
Obtaining evil responds with evil;
the evil naturally follow one another.
All have their roots and foundations,
pervading everywhere above and below.
The waters of mountains and seas that flow through
each have their departmental boundaries.
Each desires to obtain people of good nature who are not rebellious to serve as their registered households.
The spirits of the dry land
also desire to obtain good people.
Each applies prohibitions and taboos
that reach up to Heaven.
If one commits evil and violates them,
they naturally bring about their own demise.
In families of great evil,
regardless of status,
they are hated by ghosts and spirits.
One can only correct oneself;
do not slander the spirits.
The *Tiāndào*, *Dìdào*, and *Réndào*
do not prohibit good in vain.
Divine essence and *qì* can still be lent to people;
the evil do not lose their records,
which are then reported to those above.
When transgressions accumulate in great numbers,
*Tàiyīn* takes charge of the records.
According to the severity of the law,
all are recorded as transgressions in the ledgers.
People do not know it themselves,
thinking there is nothing else to it.
In the *Tàiyáng Míngtáng*,
the registers are communicated many times.
Again, they reach the departmental heads;
the spirits also communicate many times.
The *Tiānshén* departments record deaths,
reducing years and eliminating people from the world.
These cannot be contemplated in detail.
Value the good so that it brings good;
evil naturally returns to one's own person.
Regarding the management of life, Heaven knows there is little wisdom,
so it created the writings on applying good and evil and saving life,
to caution both those before and after.
Do not lightly speak evil words
or make them the start of conversation.
In every movement and every step,
there are immediately calamities and faults.
Therefore, this text is sent down to show you,
to make you reflect on its meaning,
and to prevent you from resenting yourself.
The court and the *Tíngwèi* establish laws,
but people violate them themselves.
Do not hate those in charge;
hating them makes the life-ledger thin, preventing long life.
When there is a desire to kill someone,
the ledger records serve as evidence.
Then they are ordered into the earth,
where they are immediately interrogated and punished.
When documents are interconnected,
how could anyone escape?
Strive to distance yourself from evil
and do not associate with it.
Then you may live a little and complete a full lifespan.
For those who are disloyal or suffer illness,
even if they are struck by madness or heterodoxy,
there will be some who survive.
The laws and mandates of the prohibiting spirits in Heaven
are just like those of *Zhōnghé* and the underground.
Flowing in the four directions and moving sideways,
all follow the same legal patterns;
why should there be any doubt?
If a living person has merit toward Heaven,
but their descendants are baleful,
their calculated lifespan will be reduced.
They might not die immediately,
but after the calculations are exhausted,
there is no hope for their survival.
Rulers of states and fathers of the people
should provide teachings and guidance,
guiding them in good and evil,
and striving to obtain the truth of their circumstances.
Do not disregard the lives given by Heaven,
nor cut off the lineages of the human world.
Punishments should follow the appropriate laws.
Frequently consult the worthy and wise
to serve as the beginning and end.
Let majestic divinity clothe the ruler;
the spirits should not inflict violence.
Previous writings have already said this;
it is proper to emphasize it again.
Thus rulers and fathers can extend their lives to later generations,
and life will flourish forever;
be careful not to be greedy for killing.
At the time it may seem acceptable,
but later one suffers its calamities.
Officials, regardless of rank,
and common soldiers because of their roles,
should clarify their affairs
and not become a source of suffering for the people.
Those who are exceptionally capable of respecting and loving *Dàodé*, *Rén*, and *Ēn*
unite their virtue with Heaven,
share their intent with Earth,
and bring benefit to *Zhōnghé*.
They desire to behold the good spirits and divinities.
Each has their own trustworthiness;
do not deceive the simple-minded.
In seeking long life and survival,
one can avoid self-inflicted bitterness and sorrow.
Think of practicing the affairs of Heaven;
raised up by spirits and divinities,
one can achieve *Xiān* and *Dù* with long life,
forever beholding the sun, moon, and stars.
This is the great grace of Heaven;
one should not commit even a small evil.
Furthermore, instructions are sent down:
for those who commit evil without stopping,
their households will eventually be destroyed.
Therefore, the command is issued again,
so that there will be no violators.
Those who violate are all youths with thin destinies.
When people want to do wrong,
one should explain and resolve their ignorance and delusion
so that they do not encounter misfortune.
If they constantly refuse to listen to others' words,
they will later regret it themselves;
this is the blessing of the speaker.
The *Xīngxiù* watch over people;
one must not do wrong.
Each will report what they see;
for the good, long life is beyond doubt.
Teach and caution later generations
so they can provide offerings to their ancestors;
otherwise, they will lose their own names.
Do not violate the prohibitions of Heaven;
do not violate the punishments of Earth.
Follow the four seasons in obedience
and have no reputation for killing.
Regarding what the *Wǔxíng* complete,
each should keep to their own part
and have no bad reputation.
Do not treat those above or below lightly;
all take turns governing one another.
Ensure there is no suddenness or violence,
and then there will be a prominent name.
Keep these thoughts in the heart;
be careful not to let them leave the body.
If the *jīngshén* scatter and leave,
heterodox ghosts will startle the person.
Keep the mind focused to preserve oneself
and do not forget one's name.
Each will have their own joy;
strive for the *Dào* and seek goodness,
increase years and extend lifespan,
and one can achieve long life.
Be careful, be careful!
Do not carry out punishments unjustly.
Though it may be labor for the mind at first,
later one will receive honor for it.
Teachers have good and evil qualities.
Remember the root to complete the end.
If disciples are not submissive,
they too will lose their names
and fail to achieve *Xiān* and *Dù*.
Violating the spirits of the earth's punishments
is how evil increases;
they will not receive birth.
Be careful and again be careful.
Within a single body,
divine light naturally arises.
Let the internal and external be one,
with every action and word in obedience,
and do not lose sincerity and trust.
The *Wǔshén* are within,
knowing the shortness and length of things.
One must not lightly offend,
for there are always records.
If there are minor faults,
they are reported up to the Míngtáng,
and the form and spirit are detained.
One is questioned regarding their deeds;
serious offenses are not overlooked,
and minor ones result in a reduction of years.
If the spirits do not report truthfully,
they will later be held accountable;
there are also legal punishments.
This applies not only to the deeds of the living;
refined spirits and ghostly beings are also subject to this.
In ancient times, for those who knew not to dare offend, the human and divine counts were sent down.
Calculated among Tiān, Dì, and humanity,
if there is no merit, do not expect a reward.
The hearts of worthies and sages should illuminate their scrolls.
The scrolls contain warnings and prophecies,
while the wicked act in opposition.
Those who cherish life are protected by Tiān;
those who cherish nourishment are aided by Dì;
those who cherish benevolence are loved by all people.
To act beyond this,
evil will surely encounter harm.
Tiān knows their wickedness
and thus sends malevolent deities and ghostly beings to wait for them.
They enter into the human body,
flowing outward to the four limbs, head, face, abdomen, back, chest, flanks, and the Qīzhèng.
Reported up to the Míngtáng,
seventy-two colors appear;
this is the corpse of death.
The Wǔzàng become diseased,
and their departure has a fixed time.
Be careful with food and drink;
do not let wind and cold invade.
By following virtue in one's conduct,
this results in a full lifespan of years.
Tiān desires for people to live;
Dì desires for people to be nourished;
people desire for people to be charitable.
For those who do evil, their calamity cannot be averted.
Therefore, they are informed by the Tiānshū,
ordering the people not to violate the prohibitions.
The Qi of Tiān issues words through people;
each should wash away impure conduct.
Be careful of this and do not forget.
Afterward there will be joy.
Otherwise, there is no need to further exist ... as said.
The words of the divine sages of old
do not lose the guiding principles
and naturally possess laws and measures.
Let those who are ignorant take heed;
this warning is especially deep and thorough.
Whether the penalties for the faults of one's life are heavy or light,
they all arise from the person;
it is not merely an empty matter,
but something that is always received for a reason.
Natural disposition is spontaneous
and cannot be deceived.
Contemplate this deeply without setting it aside;
when one's conduct is perfected, one becomes a celestial deity.
Transformations have their timing
and do not lose the guiding principles;
the Qi of the four seasons
must not be violated.
There are always spirits and essences;
there is no longer any negligence.
If it is thought that things are not made clear,
Heaven uses the spirits of divination to act,
ensuring that one does not report falsely,
and only then can those above survive.
Otherwise, one is punished and exiled to sell vegetables in the Dūshì,
unable to show one's face,
despised by the base and ugly,
and looked down upon by the masses;
if the fault is heavy and the punishment deep,
it lasts for forty years.
Only then may one return to serve as a messenger for the various gods;
for medium faults, thirty years,
and for lesser faults, ten years.
Deprived of what they govern,
each has their own allotted order;
if they can change their hearts and blame themselves,
they can endure for a long time.
Do not change the words of Heaven
and bring calamity upon yourself;
can you not contemplate this deeply?
For the sake of future scholars of the transcendents,
whether their planning is deep or shallow,
the blame lies within themselves;
do not resent the words of the gods.
In all actions, whether internal or external,
be careful to avoid errors and losses;
examine carefully what you have received.
Being commissioned by Heaven,
one cannot act of one's own accord;
one must always follow orders
and must not linger long.
There will always be inquiries and rebukes
in a very short time.
If the fault is heavy, the messenger is dismissed;
the records of the earth note what is received,
with names as on a register;
one must not stay or stop.
Where there is a vacancy,
those from below will fill it.
The reason for this is that
even those whose hearts are fully devoted to becoming divine transcendents may still be dismissed;
how much more so for the foolish?
From now on,
one may avoid committing offenses.
Heaven rebukes the faults of humans,
and ghosts and gods act as its messengers;
those who do not follow Heaven's teachings
will immediately encounter calamity and blame.
There is no need for whips or rods;
one naturally receives it through one's own actions.
If one thinks it is not so
and is viewed with doubt,
one cannot remain for long;
therefore, these words are spoken again
as a warning to be cautious.
Do not emulate worldly people
who reconcile with each other over wine and meat and then stop;
the Way of the transcendents is of the utmost importance,
which is why people are told this.
If there is a mandate, it should be preserved;
spirits send each other as messengers,
riding clouds and driving dragons,
stopping only after circling everywhere.
Heaven has its teachings and commands,
which must be carried out.
If one does not lose the laws, then distorted and negligent records are avoided;
evidence is set in place,
and one should not simply submit oneself.
Heaven also rests;
each receives their punishment,
and there should be no resentment.
As reported by the gods:
do not recklessly offend the children of Central Harmony between Heaven and Earth,
as each does not respect themselves.
Do not resent Heaven or blame Earth;
those above and below detain each other.
It is also like the laws of the people:
if the testimony is not truthful,
those below feel resentment,
and it will not last long;
the various gods in Heaven will compete to speak of it.
How much more so should ordinary people personally uphold the laws of Heaven
and follow the harmony of Heaven?
With inexhaustible grain
and inexhaustible clothing,
those with merit will advance again.
One can govern all those who have reports to make;
the year is fixed;
follow the text and act,
and do not have doubts.
Each has something to report;
do not let both sides be balanced in mutual resentment;
those who recommend others together will be punished
and become even more lowly.
Although they do not descend at the right time,
being sent by the Great Spirits,
if they do not follow the divine intent,
they are immediately handed over to the Tǔzhǔ,
and cannot ascend again.
Thus, when there is a vacancy
and one does not occupy it,
the upper, middle, and lower ranks are integrated as one.
Act cautiously according to these words;
the longevity of the lost body
is connected to the soil.
The "soil"
is not the soil of the earth;
it has its own ominous spirits guarding its activities.
As a messenger for the Lord of the Celestial Soil,
if one does not act as spoken,
one will immediately see suffering.
Even divine transcendents have faults and errors;
how can the people act as they please?
Therefore, the Sīmìng is commanded
to be near within the heart,
not far from the person;
it serves as the dwelling place for the spirit and essence.
Good and bad fortune are within oneself;
why bother to avoid them from afar
and bring turmoil and disaster upon oneself?
In urgent times, one cannot survive;
when life has not yet ended,
but the calculated span is exhausted,
seeking far-off help is of no use.
The assembly of spirits under Heaven
governs the knowledge of life and death;
if the spirits themselves make slips or omissions,
they in turn receive the calamity.
Therefore, the lives of the people
are not allowed to be long-lasting.
Thus, divine persons are sent
to show these writings.
If one receives the warnings and stops evil, and the spirits do not report upward,
one may still briefly eat the various grains.
Be careful not to burn mountains or break rocks,
extending to the grasses and trees,
or to break flowers and wound branches.
When they are sold in the marketplace
and metal blades are applied to them,
stems and roots are both destroyed.
Their Mother then becomes angry
and reports upward to the Father,
showing no pity for the years of humans.
Humans also need grass to provide for themselves,
but they should only take that which is withered and fallen and does not flourish;
this is to follow the constant norm.
Heaven and Earth give birth and growth
just as humans wish to live;
why act willfully
and bring calamity upon future generations?
People of knowledge
should not violate the prohibitions.
There are those who naturally harm others;
if one only looks up to completed deeds
and does not take the young to feed people,
life can be slightly lengthened.
At the end of the registered life,
do not raise weapons
or harm and intimidate human life.
Heaven mandates that such a person
cannot live for long.
Evil following evil
troubles the spirits,
refined Qi, and ghostly beings,
and none of them can rest.
Is this not caused by the faults of humans?
When evil was done in former times,
the calamity reaches down to the descendants.
Therefore, when children are born,
it must be on an inauspicious day;
or during the time of pregnancy,
there are thunder and lightning bolts;
or it occurs at the quarter, full, new, or dark moons;
or on days of Xuèjì or Fǎnzhī,
to join Yīnyáng.
If the birth of the child is unsuccessful,
there will surely be disaster and calamity.
This is summoned by the Qi of the earth,
yet people instead resent the Cāngláng.
When evil is repaid with evil,
what more can be expected?
Not knowing how to change and transform,
one’s own lineage shall naturally face extinction without a household,
and in death, one shall not be equal to the multitude.
Regional officials and regular soldiers treat this group by
specifically bringing them to a wilderness and unclean place,
where they barely manage to be covered with earth.
They are eaten by foxes and dogs,
their skeletal remains are not collected,
but are abandoned by the roadside.
Soul and spirit both suffer,
laboring without rest.
Perhaps attached to grasses and trees,
and eaten by the six domestic animals,
when will they be reborn?
That evil is punished and good is rewarded is known by all;
why not change oneself?
Tiān rewards those with merit
and does not give to those without virtue.
Think on it, think on it;
rewards and punishments can be known.
Naturally one may die alone in extreme suffering.
The lifespan associated with good and evil shall wax and wane.
Examine it carefully and be cautious of it
so that one may avoid being blamed.
Therefore, I give this weighty warning
to make one repent on one’s own.
The convergence of good and bad fortune
are ten thousand lǐ apart.
Therefore I send down this text
to command and warn one another.
Do not resent Tiān or blame Dì;
good and evil shall be distinguished.
Record this text for one another
so that you may know evil and practice good.
The soul and spirit are extremely weary.
The foolish do not know this,
so the words of the text are earnest and repeated,
told again and again to one another.
Do not create misfortune for future generations.
Use this to prove yourself;
what further resentment or blame could there be?
There is nothing further to regret,
as each obtains their proper principle.
This text should be circulated
and must not cease.
For those who know, the years of suffering are reduced;
the foolish may write the book themselves,
but if they do not follow its words,
they only bring suffering upon themselves!
In the time of high antiquity,
Shénshèng Xiānzhī came to manage affairs,
governing together with Heaven.
Distributed throughout the four directions, above, below, and in the center,
each had their own deployment,
with ranks and orders of high and low.
Above and below looked toward one another,
and things were accomplished without sternness;
all was good.
Fearing there might be unworthiness,
they were all of one mind.
Heaven had teachings and commands,
and they rushed to carry them out,
using cloud-vapor as their chariots
and riding upon flying dragons.
The Shénxiān who followed them
had their own ranks and rows;
all held registers and documents,
remaining orderly without movement.
Fearing they might be questioned,
their every move followed regulations,
and they attained their proper course of action.
In spring they moved the breath of life,
in summer they promoted growth,
in autumn they harvested,
enabling the people to provide offerings,
and in winter they stored surplus grain,
allowing for continuity again,
never having a moment of laxity.
Of the bestowals of the Shénlíng,
none failed to receive glory;
their grace reached even the crawling insects,
and the plants and trees were also thus.
Is this not the grace of those above?
Each attained their own place.
They ensured there was always a surplus of food,
the new and the old succeeding one another.
How could one forget this?
Having obtained the help of the people,
they ensured the spirits felt no resentment.
Good people were immediately rewarded;
they naturally considered it their duty to provide for one another,
for Heaven made it so.
One must not hoard or hide wealth,
causing others to suffer hunger and cold.
Therefore, wealthy families were commanded
to lend and provide for the poor,
returning the new for the old,
so that all might live and grow,
passing this down to their descendants.
The Shénlíng grant protection and aid;
is this not the distribution of great grace?
Ignorant people lack knowledge
and are unwilling to show gratitude,
thinking their positions are merely as they should be.
On the contrary, their hearts and minds are unsettled;
they forcibly take from others to glorify themselves
and have no intention of repayment.
Without regard for hardships and disasters,
they think they can complete their natural lifespan.
Therefore, this text is again compiled.
Shénrén and Zhēnrén seek good people
who can transmit the writings and know how to use them;
then such people may obtain an extension of life and an increase in longevity,
furthermore aligning with Heaven and Earth
to together transform into Shénlíng.
They may again ride upon chariots
and travel everywhere above, below, and in the center,
flowing through the six directions.
Is this not good?
Why not reflect deeply?
Do not forget within
where the spirits reside.
They observe what people do;
do not be self-righteous.
Know that there is a limit,
and one should succeed in service,
leaving calamity and approaching fortune;
one should not have even a small unworthiness toward the heart of Heaven.
The spirits of Heaven and Earth, the four seasons, and the Wǔxīng directly record the span of human life;
how can one not respect them
and think of repaying their grace?
Those who do not wish to do good deeds
turn against the heavenly spirits.
The heavenly spirits cause the wind and rain to be unseasonable,
and the movement of Qì to shift;
when it should be cold it is instead warm,
and when it should be warm it is instead cold.
Plowing and sowing are not done at the proper time;
the farmers are resentful
and are unwilling to manage things for others.
They treat the various grains with contempt
and use them to feed dogs and pigs;
the farmers then depart.
In a nation with virtue,
those planting there receive a small harvest,
trees wither and fall,
and the people have no surplus grain.
They then harm and plunder one another,
doing no more than struggling for dominance.
Not thinking of the true future,
they further become poor people;
having nothing to harvest,
they follow one another as wandering refugees.
Before they can reach a land with cheap grain,
they starve by the roadside,
their heads dizzy and eyes darkened.
They walk frantically,
having gone without food for days,
and dying of hunger, they are left unburied.
Families, whether great or small,
all suffer disasters,
yet they conversely shout their grievances at Heaven.
Their country becomes empty and desolate,
the granaries have no stored grain,
meat is scarce,
and there is no stored money.
Year after year it becomes more severe,
with nothing to provide to the imperial court.
Those exempt from duties are many,
yet nothing enters the storehouses.
The Sīnóng receives empty documents and has nothing to distribute as rations;
food is snatched away and stipends are removed.
Zhōngguó has little to use,
and the people look up to the state,
but none can bestow anything.
There comes a time when life is difficult to sustain;
all of this is what Heaven loathes.
The Earth cannot long sustain them;
do the wicked people know this?
The Zhēnrén must urgently entrust this text to nations with virtue,
letting each person blame themselves and gain knowledge;
then they may again complete their natural lifespan.
To be without knowledge is the same as the beasts.
Longevity cannot be obtained by force;
one attains it through their own conduct.
Do not feel resentment toward Heaven.
Carefully study the writings
and always think of filial piety, loyalty, trustworthiness, benevolence, and charity.
When there is a fault, blame oneself.
Thus you shall have descendants;
the scriptures do not speak empty words.
For a nation without virtue,
Heaven will not provide protection.
The Jīhéng will move with urgent speed,
and the sun and moon will press on with diminished light.
For a nation with virtue,
the Jīhéng will be slow and steady,
and the sun and moon will be radiant.
This is the working of Heaven;
the Jīhéng, the sun, moon, and stars
should all be good and bright.
If they instead become diminished,
it is caused by human conduct;
what is there to resent or blame?
All share the same Heaven, Earth, Sun, Moon, and Stars;
those who witness the trustworthiness of Heaven and Earth see their brightness.
When the Wǔxīng lose their regularity,
weapons and armor run rampant,
the Yídí invade the interior,
and captives rebel.
When the state dispatches military commanders,
those with the mandate return,
while those who lose the mandate do not;
this is the fault of the Dàrén.
If sons are unfilial
and the state has few loyal ministers,
and conduct is not pure,
it causes mutual conflict
that only stops at the end of the year.
Therefore, the Dòngjí zhī Jīng is bestowed,
named Tàipíng.
Those who can follow it will obtain its blessings;
those who cannot should reflect deeply on their own.
Keep the body together without straying;
retribution and response always occur and do not wrong people.
Those who do not follow this bestow evil upon others.
It is often said that among people there are no noble or lowly;
all are born of Heaven.
It is only that the records of their mandates are not preserved.
Love them, be cautious with them, and think of them.
Be careful not to impose what is improper and thus wrong people,
or to encroach and plunder what is not yours.
This is what Heaven does not reward
and what Earth does not sustain;
Xiōngshén will follow them,
and they shall not live long or live in joy.
Those who neglect themselves should not hope for life;
they have no record for long life at all,
yet they forcibly enter the houses of Shénxiān to fast.
They perform all kinds of sacrifices to the Shénlíng,
seeking to be granted transcendence as immortals.
When the immortals and spirits examine the registers and records,
they find you have no name of the living,
so the spirits will not enjoy the food of your prayers and sacrifices.
They wander about begging,
but as for the Shénlíng,
those spirits are angered by them.
They will be eaten by fierce beasts,
and their bones and flesh will be finished.
Gnawed by foxes,
they do not return to their hometowns.
Neighbors in the same county and adjacent houses
instead claim to have attained immortality,
but there is no reliable news or confirmation;
how can they prove themselves?
Speaking from this,
it is difficult to distinguish clearly.
There should be reported news,
and only when the multitude sees it
is it considered an ascension.
Otherwise, they suffer their punishments,
claiming they have attained just a little;
such people are mad or wicked and may be cast down,
yet people instead take them as genuine.
All enter the records of death,
descending to the Huángquán,
unable to follow their own will.
Those with virtue and measure
have a registry while alive;
when their years are full and they should ascend,
there will always be those who welcome them.
The young and ignorant have no knowledge;
how can they manage to go there?
They merely waste resources
and abandon their families, discarding their bodies in the wilderness.
The Dào is natural and people's fates are interconnected;
it cannot be sought by force.
If one causes oneself suffering
and does not manage a livelihood or support parents,
even if wives and children see one as a worthy man,
one only fears that being unfilial, disloyal, and lacking in trust
might allow one to just finish one's allotted years,
with no punishment underground, only peace.
If there is surplus property
passed from children to grandchildren,
it should also be provided for use;
do not cause yourself suffering.
Whether descendants are worthy or unworthy,
they each live their own lives;
do not leave calamities to one another—
this is good conduct.
Therefore, this text is recorded to show the wise;
the foolish ignore it, prone to reckless anger and joy.
Keeping far from punishment and avoiding calamity is the mark of a worthy person;
if three admonitions do not hit the mark, one may stop.
Heaven blesses the good
and does not favor the wicked.
Each should be more cautious
and not resent or blame one another.
Each plans for their own person;
actions should be known to everyone,
with no faults that burden Heaven.
As is appropriate for the records,
carefully avoid seeking by force,
for seeking it is of no benefit.
The reason for this is
that for wicked and rebellious people,
Heaven does not grant its blessing.
Do not depart from your dwelling or city walls.
The joints are connected like paths through fields,
the tendons govern the desire for life to strengthen the walls,
the vessels govern the coming and going as a network for the bones,
and the flesh inside the skin is the clothing for the vessels.
The spirit guards within,
overseeing the good and evil of humans.
What need is there for distant worries?
The Qīzhèng oversee the gates of the spirits.
Seeking the Dào results in life;
do not depart from your dwelling.
Transformation harmonizes its virtue with the spirits;
what more of the Dào is there to seek?
Therefore, good writings are placed in the celestial records.
The records of immortals and ordinary lists are different.
At the time of ascension,
the spirits in charge of the records and the guarantors arrive;
then one knows the leaders of their department receive and carry out the teachings.
Each has an order of precedence,
and one must advance to where one is going;
one is not allowed to follow one's own will.
The multitude of spirits govern together,
striving to select those who harmonize with the heart of Heaven.
Those who preceded others in birth
all have hearts of clear vision
and have no sense of boundaries.
What they do and how they live
is not yet known to people.
They all precede Heaven and Earth,
transforming above and below,
and none lose their Dào,
though the spirits do not possess all these qualities.
Thus, the principles and laws were established,
with years and months alongside,
each placed on the left and right.
The stars are distinguished,
each having its own dominion,
striving to advance their loyalty
and directing the division into departments.
Seeing good, one should advance;
seeing evil, one should retreat.
What is there to doubt?
Exert yourself in your actions
and do not be led astray by the spirits.
Thus success is attained,
and one can be called a Tiānjūn.
Those who preside over Heaven manage the registers
and do not lose the measure;
the spirits in charge of departments look to the four directions.
The directions have the cycles of Mèng, Zhòng, and Jì,
alternating their duties above and below,
named the Tàisuì.
Tàiyīn follows behind,
presiding over knowledge of geography.
Further, the four seasons are established
to bring forth all that exists,
distributed across the wilderness,
with late and early grains and grasses.
Living near others does not grant longevity to distant people,
yet they also endure for a long time;
even the small trees of the sacred groves maintain themselves.
Executed across changing generations,
it extends even to grandchildren.
The reason for this is
that the dwelling place is not at peace;
by leaving the old for the new,
the spirits can return.
Humans have destiny-trees growing in the celestial soil, each passing by.
For those born in the three months of spring, the destiny-tree is the mulberry;
for those born in the three months of summer, it is the jujube or plum;
for those born in the three months of autumn, it is the catalpa or stem-wood;
for those born in the three months of winter, it is the locust or cypress.
These are what the common people belong to.
Each has an official in charge of the tree;
when the destiny is about to end,
the tree is only half-alive;
when destiny ends, it withers and falls,
and the official in charge fells the tree.
How can that person find a way to live?
To desire long life without death,
one must change one's heart and will
and transplant one's tree near the Tiānmén,
named "Long Life."
Divine officials preside over it;
all are pure, tranquil, and radiant,
naturally growing in the place of Heaven,
protecting the spirits' honor and glory.
One must only avoid destroying one's name.
Heaven has a constant mandate,
and honor is received generation after generation.
Although they do not descend to protect,
they eventually know their own essence.
The reason for this is
that being far removed from the mundane for a long time,
they must carry out the affairs of the Heavens
and must not make any errors.
The various spirits examine each other
like a marking line with ink;
how can they follow their own will again?
Therefore, they do not descend.
One should not find this strange.
Merit and labor shall be seen,
for they are not equal to the mundane;
though people think it is of no benefit to the family,
internally they receive its glory—
is this not good?
Therefore, it is shown to later generations
to make their hearts awaken.
Reveal the books without hiding them,
or there will be punishments in due time.
Do not associate with flattery and deception,
or have a heart that is not filial and obedient;
if all actions do not match the words of the book,
you will again face questioning and blame—
how can one not be cautious?
When transmitting, transmit to the right person,
so they may be vouched for and recommended.
Do not violate the divine books,
do not test the divine words,
and be careful with the words of the spirits;
all are rewarded or punished by Heaven.
Do not lightly violate them;
otherwise, there will be later calamities.
Small violations only bring minor rebukes,
but great errors cannot be saved.
Therefore, the various spirits are made to oversee each other and report opportunely;
if there is anything untruthful,
it shall again be dealt with.
Matters should be interconnected
and cannot be kept private.
Therefore, the spirits are made to inspect and maintain one another.
If you regret it later, why must you doubt now?
If you stop midway,
you will also be examined.
If you do not confess the true situation,
but only confess after the examination, you will be sent down.
Therefore, both advancing and stopping are examined.
Otherwise, things remain as they were—
this is what it means.
One must not lightly violate this
and have no doubts.
The divine law is of great weight,
thus one must be cautious and thorough regarding it,
mindful and reflective of it;
the way of long life and lasting vitality—
how could one not take it seriously?
Therefore, this text is issued to demonstrate
that those who should apply supplementation to the void
perform good deeds for this purpose,
and they shall always follow the succession without any neglect.
Doing good yields merit and increases one's years;
there is no longer any cause for doubt.
When would the Way of Nature ever reach an end?
One must only awaken and transform to govern oneself;
even a loss of a hair's breadth or a tiny fraction will immediately be scrutinized.
Heaven has music to delight the various spirits,
and the spirits also listen to it.
Those who are good receive rewards;
those whose melodies and tunes do not harmonize are also disciplined.
Each has their own master;
there cannot be a lack of beginning and end.
If things are not accomplished,
all eat from the Heavenly Granary
and are clothed by the *Sīnóng*;
changing clothes according to cold or warmth,
likewise, the *Yáng* is noble and the *Yīn* is humble.
From coarse to fine, delicate items, treasures of gold, silver, silk, fabric, pearls, and jade,
each is distributed equally,
with no arbitrary rewards;
they are only for those with merit.
One may not receive heavenly clothing and food without merit.
The previous text has already stated this;
now it is repeated again
to ensure there are no resentments
and no suspicions;
this is the weighty command of the Heavenly Divine Spirits.
At the end of the year, the records are audited and submitted.
From mountains, seas, and the dry land,
the various sacrifices and local shrines,
each submits what has been obtained;
nothing may be lost or omitted.
The various guardians of residences and dwellings
observe the transgressions of the people,
submitting monthly records throughout the year.
The *Sīnóng* and the ritual officials
shall immediately transfer and hand over the written documents.
The Legal Department of the *Dà Yīn*,
calculates the inherited burdens,
removing life-units and reducing years.
After one's life-units are exhausted,
the *Yīn* spirits of the Earth are summoned,
along with the *Tǔfǔ*;
they take custody of the physical remains
and examine the *Hún* and *Shén*.
They must fully submit the registered documents,
checking whether they correspond or not;
should the presiding officials act with treachery or self-interest,
punishment and demotion follow the severity of the examination.
If the text in each register is not what Heaven has commissioned,
then ghosts, spirits, and refined essences
may not inflict illness upon people.
Immediately, based on this, they shall restrain and admonish one another,
and expose one another's actions.
Transgressions as high as to warrant death
lead to being sentenced above or below to labor at river bridges, mountains, or seas,
each following the severity of the law,
each according to the specific matter,
without any omission.
Each has presiding senior officials of the commanderies, counties, and postal stations,
who observe according to the law,
not wrongfully harming or oppressing ghosts, spirits, or refined essences.
In this manner, from top to bottom,
the documents are circulated collectively,
each according to the old ordinances.
From antiquity to the present,
each has its respective division and department,
circulating above, below, and sideways,
having that which they receive and take.
Always following the standard without fail,
how could one not see the secrets of life and death?
Let each be cautious,
do not offend the divine spirits;
each according to their duty,
be careful not to neglect or forget the mandate.
Records may be inscribed:
the good shall be promoted,
the evil shall be demoted.
At the convergence of good and bad fortune,
each attains what they desired.
One can only follow and obey;
one must not go against the intention.
If the mind and intention are not upright,
and one instead resents the divine messengers,
one's actions will bring their own consequences;
why harbor resentment or enmity?
People are difficult to transform;
their knowledge is insufficient,
and so they all suffer calamity.
They commit crooked deeds that fall short of the mark,
yet conversely fill their mouths with self-praise.
Their handling of human affairs is utterly without wisdom or foresight;
they only see what is before them,
and do not consider what follows.
They attract disaster and lose those they love,
slandering and mocking good people.
They think Heaven does not exist above,
and Earth is not below,
knowing nothing of ghosts and spirits.
Among those who keep records,
they may resolve human resentments and enmities,
offering much wine and dried meat,
indulging themselves in sweetness and beauty.
While it may seem acceptable at the time,
later they will be spoken of by others;
with loose mouths they curse and revile,
imprecating in unprincipled ways,
deceitful and slanderous.
They steal other men's wives and daughters,
watching for them day and night.
They seek out opportunities for convenience,
selling things to feed themselves;
they desire fine clothes and shoes,
and compete in contentious debate.
They do not follow principles or reason;
yet they wish to live and thrive—
how could they last for long?
Such foolish people could be called Infamous Sons.
When senior officials hear of them,
they order subordinates to seize them,
and swiftly execute punishment upon their bodies.
The disaster reaches both close and distant relatives,
all sharing in the blame.
When poor, one should exert oneself;
do not act restlessly.
This is the record of a person's life-mandate,
received at birth.
If evil ghosts follow them,
how can they remain for long?
These types are numerous,
meeting at various times,
inevitably being caught without stopping.
The reason for saying this
is that evil ghosts will take them.
Be cautious of even minor errors;
if one is not cautious, it is one's own doing.
Evil must not be committed;
it is what people resent and blame.
At the time it may seem fine to oneself,
not thinking of the consequences;
when seeing a warning, one should stop,
then one may return to a bit of life
and complete one's remaining life-units.
There is a record of good and evil,
from where longevity arises,
the period for increasing years;
it is essential to be good!
If one does not see the worthies and saints,
one's wisdom and foresight are nonetheless sufficient.
Cherish life and loathe death;
reaching up to the *Xiānshì*,
longevity can span many years.
Why abandon the world?
Calamities flow from birth;
the child in the womb conversely says, "I am born from the same parents as the others."
This is all resenting Heaven and blaming Earth.
Good and evil should be distinguished;
they cannot be mixed together.
The pure and the turbid are separated,
like a lord and a servant.
Therefore, those who walk the Great Way live;
those who do not become dust.
Ancient and modern times are similar.
There is also good,
and there is also evil;
they are passed down through generations
and have never ceased,
being only a matter of more or less.
Heaven knows there is much rebellion,
therefore it has issued this text to emphasize it.
After knowing the warnings,
there need be no doubt;
when hundreds and thousands correspond,
when would there ever be a mistake?
It is only because Heaven and Earth follow the initial beginning
that they form essence and spirit,
upholding Zìrán,
and generating all transformations,
so that none fail to flourish.
Because there are arrangements,
the sun, moon, stars, and planets
and the Jīhéng govern the seasons,
while the Wǔxīng are made
to each hold their direction
and each perform their tasks.
Clouds and rain are distributed,
the people care for and manage agricultural matters,
and the Yuánqì returns and remains.
All the grains, plants, trees, and crawling, breathing, and squirming creatures
all contain Yuánqì.
The flying birds and walking beasts,
and those born in water are likewise;
they allow the people to use them for offerings and for their own food.
But only take those that cause harm to provide for oneself;
as for oxen, horses, mules, and donkeys that are no longer fit for work,
provide them to the world.
When the Dìqí have a surplus,
they gather to share and eat.
Do not kill those fit for work
or those of young age;
this is the conduct of Tiān
and what the Shénlíng rely upon.
The myriad people are foolish and dull,
killing and wounding at will;
even those pregnant in the womb
who should be born are instead killed.
This is called severing life
just to feed human mouths.
At the time of their death,
they are all terrified,
knowing for certain they will not survive.
Therefore, Heaven truly pities and sympathizes with them,
establishing prohibitions and restrictions,
and those who violate them are held liable.
Even the Liùchù still show manifest love
and cannot bear to harm one another;
yet humans, conversely, do not cherish themselves,
becoming thieves and captors instead.
What they take is not just one kind,
wildly using metal blades to kill people without being held liable.
Although they are not immediately executed,
Heaven accumulates their transgressions;
killing and destruction do not cease,
the destruction of corpses flows down to those not yet born—
such ones will also not encounter good fortune.
The Guǐshén loathe them;
with the overseers before them,
when will there be an escape?
Therefore, the records of good and evil are of great importance,
so that one simply does not transgress.
Divine People and Zhēnrén show this text to the masses,
as righteousness should not be hidden;
making them know not to resent themselves,
the characters are made clear according to custom.
It can be known that Shèngxián do not transgress,
but it is feared the foolish will not cease.
Teachers have predecessors and successors;
do not forget the root.
Contemplate the root while approaching the new,
longing and admiring as at the beginning;
this is the Way of Life.
Merit has small and large degrees,
and what is received differs.
One should discover the secrets not yet known,
the meanings not yet known,
the thoughts not known,
the words not yet known,
and the intentions not yet known.
Making both clear
is the Will of Heaven.
The Way of generation and growth
emerges from this.
Seeking trust from Tiān,
seeking trust from the Earth,
seeking trust from Zhōnghé,
seeking trust from the Sìshí,
seeking trust from the Wǔxíng;
these are all the reports and trusts obtained by Heaven.
Not missing a tiny fraction—
do you know this?
This is the transformation submitted to by the formless Zìrán of delegated Qi.
Therefore, the Sāntái and Qīxīng
assist in rectifying Heaven's majesty,
and the sun and moon illuminate and examine right and wrong,
ensuring Zìrán exists,
so that afterward there are none who regret midway.
Therefore, repeatedly command all the presiding lords,
ordering each to be clear;
accepting punishment without resentment
is what is meant by this.
Do not be caught in right and wrong;
others will return to being upright themselves.
Prohibitions have no small or large;
they can be taken as models.
Not forgetting these words brings long-lasting fortune;
one should carefully apply and practice them
without losing one's standard.
Therefore, words are used to test oneself.
This book might not yet be used,
and emperors and kings might not yet believe it.
With flatterers at their side,
the book's principles are not seen.
Disasters arise together;
where will the people find rest?
The Tàipíng Zhī Shū will see its principles realized again after three Jiǎzǐ,
but it is better to offer ten admonitions to make it known.
Moreover, contemplate living and seeking knowledge;
the knowledge of Sages and Worthies can be reached.
The Shèngrén should promote the worthy
and then seek life,
not disliking what comes next.
The records of Shénxiān are in the Běijí,
connected to Kūnlún.
In the ruins of Kūnlún, there are Zhēnrén;
ascending and descending have constancy.
The Zhēnrén preside over those whose names are in the registers,
their names recorded in order.
The lofty and bright attain the high,
the middle attain the middle,
and the low attain the low;
there are absolutely none who slap their cheeks and beg.
A predecessor serves as the teacher;
respect them as a ruler,
and call them a father.
