Therefore, the roles of teacher, ruler, and father must be clear;
the minister must be loyal,
and the disciple must be obedient.
Respectfully follow those above
to pass upwards and reach higher levels.
Therefore, Heaven does not forget the grace of the predecessor,
Earth does not forget the nourishment of the predecessor,
and humans do not forget the benevolence of the predecessor.
Thus there are loyalty, filial piety, and trustworthiness;
thinking of life without malice to bring oneself closer and clarify oneself.
The light of Heaven shines down below the Huángquán,
and the light of the earth shines up toward the heavens;
the light of Zhōnghé unites above and below.
Therefore, when the three lights obtain each other, they harmonize.
Heaven names the three lights as sun, moon, and stars,
shining down upon Zhōnghé and beneath the earth
without any rest.
In a country without virtue,
Yīnqi obscures the sun,
causing it to have no light.
The people are terrified,
grains have little growth,
floods and droughts are erratic,
and people again drift as refugees to lands with grain.
Heaven truly pities them,
ordering them to reach a place of life.
With an enlightened ruler, the country flourishes;
refugees return to till abandoned lands,
various grains can be sown,
growing to maturity,
and the people again obtain food.
They again offer to their ancestors,
and the Guǐshén find peace.
Among them are the sagely and wise
who seek out the Shénxiān;
the ledgers and registers
have their names within.
They shall again ascend to be officials of Tiān,
inspecting among the people,
harmonizing wind and rain
to ensure peaceful governance,
showing this book to future generations.
Therefore, one should do good,
which is beneficial to Heaven.
From this point forward,
one can warn descendants;
the period of extending life
can be reached.
Although the book is repetitive,
Heaven greatly loves humanity,
wishing to let them complete their years;
exhorting repeatedly,
it belongs to the divine.
Good deeds are immediately reported above,
while evil causes one's name to be lost.
Do not violate this book;
think of good, with the heart and diaphragm contemplating,
never abandoning the intention.
One should seek the will for life and always contemplate its fulfillment.
The reason why this is so
is that it is within the reach of human will.
Strive and refine it,
each following their own wish;
Heaven also does not force what is not desired.
Beneath the earth, it moves alongside;
the four directions are also like this.
The infinite Tiān,
the infinite Earth,
and the infinite realm are likewise;
the infinite light,
The light of the Wújí is also like this.
Yet the small is ultimately a major division of Tiān.
If one wishes to contemplate the matters of the heavens,
the heavens contemplate Zhōnghé,
and Zhōnghé brings peace to them.
If one wishes and thinks of seeking nobility,
the Guìshén will honor them.
If one wishes and thinks of seeking wealth,
the Fùshén will enrich them.
Between suffering and joy,
always reflect upon them,
and be meticulous and cautious in what you say.
The ways of Tiāndào are hundreds of millions;
they reside in what people do,
and do not snatch away people's desires.
The way of birth and nourishment is truly worth observing,
while the way of death
is what the Guǐ worry about.
The Xiōngshén are uneasy;
they immediately receive it, and it is difficult to express in writing.
There are writings in the heavens
that seek the root of life.
What humans desire
is why these writings were brought forth,
to make them available for reflection.
If there are faults, repent of your own accord,
following these writings.
If not, then so be it,
but do not speak recklessly.
Spirits and divinities are before and behind you;
there is no time when they release their watch.

To the right: The heavens prospering the nation, descending to reverse [evil], illuminating the Ancestral Master, the Way of the Xiánshèng, the Xǐshén of Heaven and Earth coming forth to assist in human governance, causing people to have longevity, and repelling the Sìyí.
"I ask: when the Qi of Tàipíng arrives together,
and the people should only enjoy themselves facing each other daily,
using musical instruments as a norm,
thereby transforming one another through harmony and attunement,
above it benefits the state,
causing the Qi of Tiān to be harmonious and attuned,
always delighting in the longevity of the state,
and the world also receives its virtuous teachings without blame.
As for obtaining or not obtaining this joy,
how is it to be made clear?
As for harmony or lack thereof,
what serves as the proof?
I wish to ask the Tiānshī in detail about these matters,
but I fear being stagnant,
and that there are things which are not [lacuna].
Therefore, I ask repeatedly before and after,
not daring to be negligent,
fearing the wrath of Tiān."
"Excellent!
You ask about matters for the sake of Tiān;
daily you become more skilled and practiced,
attaining the will of Tiān.
The Zhēnrén will surely increase their longevity boundlessly,
for it is what Tiān protects.
Yes, sit peacefully,
and I shall once more explain the meaning in detail for all the disciples,
making it clear and distinct,
so that it may be known.
Regarding music and joy: those who possess them in small measure and attain a small part of their meaning
use them to gladden people;
those who possess them in moderate measure and attain a moderate part of their meaning
use them to gladden governance;
those who possess them in great measure and attain the full measure of their meaning
use them to gladden Heaven and Earth.
Those who attain the method of gladdening people,
people will feel joy for them;
those who attain the method of gladdening governance,
governance will achieve peace for them;
those who attain the method of gladdening Heaven and Earth,
Heaven and Earth will achieve harmony for them.
When Heaven and Earth are in harmony,
then all things will be without illness because of it,
the multitude of spirits will always be joyful because of it,
and there will be no time of wrath."
"This rectifies the qì of Tàipíng until it arrives,
bringing the joy and delight of complete music.
Therefore, when music achieves the notes of the great jué and upper jué,
the Qīngdì is greatly delighted,
and then benevolent Dàodé emerges.
All things find joy in life,
and the Qīngdì comes out to travel.
The qì of the liver remains free of disease,
and the refined spirits of the liver emerge to appear among the types of the East.
All that is evil is entirely removed,
and all that is good comes forward to assist in transformation.
Jade maidens in green clothing bring rare prescriptions to bestow upon people—
this is the clear effect.
Let the Zhēnrén ponder this meaning in detail."
"Yes, yes."
"Thus, when the upper jué note is attained,
it is used to transform what is above;
when the middle jué note is attained,
it is used to transform what is in the middle;
when the lower jué note is attained,
it is used to transform what is below.
Attaining them brings about transformation.
Regarding the zhǐ notes of the South,
when the large, small, and middle are all in harmony,
then all things find joy in growth.
Within the South, none fail to be delighted by Dàodé;
evil things are removed,
and good things all come forward.
The red qì is entirely joyful,
and the Red God comes to travel.
The heart remains free of disease.
The spirits of the heart emerge to appear,
waiting to welcome the jade maidens in red clothing who come
to bestow rare prescriptions upon people—
this is the great effect.
Thus, when the harmony of the yellow qì and the gōng note is attained,
the goodness of the gōng note also fully arrives,
and evil things all dissipate and leave.
When the harmony of the shāng note is attained,
the goodness of the shāng note also fully arrives,
and evil things all dissipate and leave.
When the harmony of the yǔ note is attained,
the goodness of the yǔ note also fully arrives,
and evil things all leave.
Let the Zhēnrén himself ponder the essential meaning of this,
which results from describing the effects of original conduct.
The reason for not explaining the Wǔfāng
to the fullest extent
is that they are extremely profound.
When a superior scholar sees them,
he naturally grasps their meaning,
using one to sustain ten thousand.
When a middling scholar attains them,
it is feared he may become overly delighted.
When a lesser person attains them,
they might speak recklessly.
Therefore, they are not fully revealed,
so that ordinary people may each contemplate the meaning for themselves.
Let the superior scholar use one to sustain ten thousand
to know the meaning thoroughly;
it is also not necessary to explain everything to him.
Let the middling scholar also diligently come to know it;
it is also not necessary to explain everything to him.
If a lesser scholar should attain it,
he might instead speak recklessly;
it is also not necessary to explain everything to him.
Therefore, one forms thoughts with care,
lightly raising the main principles
and showing the matters
to ordinary people,
so they may each contemplate the meaning;
then there can be thorough understanding between above and below without error.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Therefore, the superior scholar cultivates music
to practice Wúwéi and transcend the world.
The middling scholar cultivates music
to harmonize with the common people and bring order.
The lesser scholar cultivates music
merely to provide pleasure to others and obtain food.
These three types of people each understand the meaning;
when the Tàipíng qì arrives,
listen to what they do,
follow their performance on the qín and sè,
and be careful not to forbid it.
For if the qì of joy does not emerge,
governance will be difficult to pacify.
If it is difficult to pacify, the qì will be contentious, leading to many punishments.
Music leads to joy,
while punishment leads to punishment;
it is like the verification of shadow and echo,
not erring by even a hair.
All music
is for the purpose of stopping anger.
All anger
is for the purpose of stopping joy.
These two attack each other;
thus, when there is joy, anger stops;
when there is anger, joy stops.
Therefore, anger gives rise to punishments and penalties;
it is the root of conflict.
Joy and music
are the gates of Dàodé.
Thus one should follow them,
allowing the root of Dàodé to grow,
and not stop it.
To stop it
will instead give rise to the gates of punishment and calamity.
This
is where good and bad fortune emerge,
and where safety and peril originate.
Thus music
is Yáng;
punishment
is Yīn.
Yīn and Yáng
are contrary to each other.
When Yáng flourishes, Yīn declines;
when Yīn flourishes, Yáng declines.
Yáng
is the ruler;
Yīn
is the minister.
When the ruler is robust, the ministers are submissive,
and the people are easy to govern.
When the minister is robust, the ruler's governance is insulted and disordered.
This is the natural law of Heaven.
Thus one should follow the joy of the ruler
to satisfy the subjects and ministers
and stop their frequent anger.
People of later antiquity were foolish
and did not deeply understand this meaning;
instead, they often cut it off.
Thus they caused the Yīn qì to flourish
and the Yáng qì to decline.
When Yīn qì flourishes, there are many bandits and thieves,
and criminals are never-ending.
All of the myriad things fail to thrive
and are mostly harmed by Yīn;
the great fault lies here.
When the qì of music rises, Yáng qì flourishes
to cut off these harms.
When the ruler's qì is robust, it leads to prolonged life and longevity,
and those above will live long.
Relaxation and music
belong to Heaven above.
Urgency, anger, and punishment belong to Earth below.
When that which is above is promoted and practiced,
the myriad matters are orderly.
When that which is below is promoted and practiced,
the myriad matters are in disorder.
Let the Zhēnrén take heed of this;
can these words not be deeply pondered?"
"Yes, yes."
"You can be said to know this deeply.
Transmit it to show the people of later antiquity,
so that each may ponder its meaning.
Be careful not to block or cut it off.
When there is music, the Dàodé of the Wǔfāng all emerges;
when there is anger, the evils of the Wǔfāng all emerge.
When there is music, the Dàodé of Heaven and Earth all emerges;
when there is anger, the evils of Heaven and Earth all emerge.
Thus when Heaven and Earth are joyful,
good responses emerge.
When Heaven and Earth are not joyful,
evil responses emerge.
Thus when the Wǔfāng are joyful and harmonious,
the good responses of the Wǔfāng emerge.
Thus when the Wǔfāng are not joyful but angry,
the evil responses of the Wǔfāng emerge.
This is no small matter;
therefore, I say do not cut it off.
Let all ordinary people together contemplate its meaning,
and with a single awakening, bring it all forth;
then the qì of delight and joy will arrive,
and the qì of urgency and anger will depart."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Go,
for you already know this."
To the right is the celestial oral formula for distinguishing the good and bad fortune produced by music and anger.
The preceding text was originally missing.
When parents suffer from illness,
their hearts are filled with sorrow.
They bow their heads before the physician
and speak words that supplement their filial duty.
They serve with reverence and respect,
using all the family possesses
to offer and present to them.
They praise that person with respect;
when the physician sees this,
his heart respects that person.
He focuses his mind on seeking authentic, fresh, and superior medicine,
distributing the portions so that the instructions are clear,
welcoming the physician to remove the illness.
They often shed tears while speaking,
apologizing for their faults to Tiān.
They strike themselves in a plea for mercy
and bow their heads to the ground,
not avoiding tiles, stones, mud, or dirt.
Thus they always manage to bring peace and safety to their parents.
They teach their children and wives to always remain before the parents,
preparing rich, sweet, and crisp foods
so they may eat whatever they desire.
Even if the parents are from a merchant family
and lack certain possessions,
the descendants endure hardship
to exhaust all the family has,
showing extraordinary personal filial piety before them.
Relatives and neighbors,
seeing their filial goodness
and knowing they have nothing left,
come in turn to provide supplies.
They help call and welcome the physician, providing mats,
and labor together with them day and night.
Knowing their state of safety or peril, they inquire and care for them;
observing their recovery and hearing small, good words,
their hearts rejoice for them.
This is what filial piety brings about.
Tiān sees their filial heart
and allows for healing,
returning them to their usual state,
whereupon the heart is filled with joy.
When they are once again able to eat grain,
they fast and engage in trade,
offering all they have up to Tiān.
They return to thank their Xiānrén;
whatever curses they had received
are immediately ended with fragrant and pure offerings.
They dare not break their word.
This is the proper conduct for a filial son.
The common people hear of this goodness,
but they are unable to practice it.
Those who can practice it
have a nature that arises from Zìrán.
Tiān endows their mandate
to make them filial and good,
to be passed down through descendants.
Their livelihood makes progress,
and they do not practice harming others.
They benefit their parents.
Guests, in-laws, and neighbors
are repaid by the filial one,
who does not forget their kindness.
This is the goodness of such a person.
The years of one's parents
cannot be known in advance.
One should make preparations and wait,
reducing and saving on small expenses
so that every year there is a surplus,
stored in an unseen place.
Do not let senior or junior officials know of it.
Due to requisitions and levies,
which exhaust a person's property,
if the filial heart was not thorough,
there would be nothing left.
When the parents' years are exhausted,
there would be nothing with which to provide for their sending off,
which would again mean failing to complete the intention of filial piety.
A person who practices filial piety
thinks of completing their merit.
Their merit is manifested to the Tàishàng
and heard in the Dìtíng.
Recommended by the Zhōu and Jùn,
they are suddenly graced with honor.
Is this not brought about by filial piety?
Descendants inherit this,
lasting for infinite generations.
This mindfulness of kindness without forgetting
is favored by Tiān.
Tiān sends Shànshén to constantly follow and protect them.
This is what filial piety brings about.
One person in their family shall attain long life and transcend the world.
Later generations respect them,
and they can be free of misfortune and calamity.
Each ends their life at a full age,
with none dying prematurely.
Is this not good?
Among what is brought about by goodness,
what is not accomplished?
What is not achieved?
What is not obtained?
What is not mastered?
Strive to practice it;
do not be negligent or weary.
This is the blessing of a good person.
A filial and good person
is also not harmed by others;
if someone harms a filial and good person,
Tiān will punish them for it.
This is more severe than what is before one's eyes;
this may be known.
One may wish to know the goodness of being good
and know the filial piety of being filial,
yet suffer from being unable to emulate them.
This comes from Zìrán.
Tiān grants a registry of goodness;
goodness and filial piety are naturally passed down and received.
They surpass and elevate each other;
how could there be an end to this heart?
People naturally respect
a good and filial person;
they also do not offend or overcome others.
Their reputation spreads to the eight distant regions.
When vacancies occur among the senior officials of the Zhōu, Jùn, and Xiàn, they are filled.
Knowing in advance of a good and filial family,
the Xiàn recommends them.
The senior officials, following human sentiment, wish to hear of their filial goodness
and send officers to comfort them.
There are also those who are diligent
and go in person to visit them,
observing their conduct and intentions to recommend them.
Every year they are graced with honor,
wearing high virtue as their girdle.
Descendants inherit this,
and they are named a "Family that Transmits Filial Piety,"
having no wicked people.
Not only are they filial at home,
but it extends to both internal and external relations.
As officials, they are all filial to the Jūn,
increasing their loyalty and sincerity.
They often hold high positions
and are filial to the Cháotíng.
If the Jùn or Xiàn produces rare or false goods,
they use their own family wealth to purchase them,
taking what is good without troubling the people
and without using forced labor.
The Jùn and Xiàn are all compassionate and filial;
the Wǔgǔ become abundant and ripe,
and there are no people who die prematurely.
Tiān harmonizes the wind and rain for them,
making them timely.
These are the filial and good people of Tiān,
whom it prevents from encountering disasters.
The people are transformed by their example;
they all have hearts of nourishment and obedience.
Tiān does not go against their intentions.
This is goodness upon goodness,
and loyalty and filial piety upon filial piety,
which are thus brought to completion.
This makes the unfilial people of the world emulate them
and establishes filial intentions.
A Dàmìng pardons the world,
and all offenses that should not have been committed are entirely removed.
To children who are filial, fraternal, and diligent in farming,
they are granted colored silk, wine, and meat.
Senior officials pay them respect,
making their filial conduct clear
so that people may see it.
When onlookers see this,
those with hearts can advance in love.
With good intentions, they love one another.
These are all the benevolent provisions of the world,
making the people obedient.
This is goodness resulting in goodness,
and filial piety resulting in filial piety.
If the root is unfilial, the end is unfilial;
if the root is evil, the end is evil.
As for the good, their wishes are all for longevity,
reaching the end with white hair.
At the high end, they reach one hundred and twenty;
at the low end, over one hundred years.
This is what goodness and filial piety bring about;
these are not just empty words.
Not only does Tiān love them,
but the Sìshí, the Wǔxíng,
and the Rì Yuè Xīng Chén all favor them,
shining upon them
so that they do not encounter evil.
Their goodness is like this;
can it not be valued?
Of the people Tiān creates,
few can be truly good and filial.
They alone achieve longevity for themselves
and also obtain high office—
all brought about by practicing filial piety.
Not only to speak of blessings,
this book is issued
to show the living people.
For those who wish to follow its laws,
Tiān will again grant longevity that can be passed down,
to be preserved by their descendants.
When the book is issued, one must practice filial piety;
regarding those who transcend the world through filial piety,
next, they look forward to official titles and ranks.
Of all matters under Tiān,
filial piety is the most supreme and the first,
something others cannot reach.
By accumulating merit and piling up deeds,
succeeding one after another,
without any loss,
those known as people of rebirth
receive the grace of their parents
and again see the writings on filial obedience.
Tiān determines their records and registers
and places them among those who do not die;
this is a household of filial piety.
They also obtain further transcendence:
ascending to Tiān to carry out the affairs of Tiān,
again recording loyalty, filial piety, and all that is respected,
assuming offices for Tiān,
their honor and favor being seen daily.
In Tiān, they are named Xiàoshàn Shénrén,
and all are respected by the spirits.
When there is a request for fine food, it is presented to them first,
leaving behind their filial conduct;
in this, they have no peer.
Their lifespan is limitless,
and their essence and radiance increase daily.
Above, they see the limitless Tiān;
below, they see the limitless Dì;
traveling horizontally, they see the limitless borders.
They also know of things that have not yet happened,
and all the spirits follow their instructions and commands,
not going against their will,
but together recommending and reporting them.
When the Tàishàng zhī Jūn sees that their filial conduct is peerless,
He places them close to Him, both inside and out,
and the spirits respect and honor them even more.
Therefore, it is said that those whom Tiān loves,
the spirits respect;
those whom Tiān hates,
the spirits place in danger.
This is what can be known;
as for the rest, each should apply their own mind,
choose what is advantageous for themselves,
and follow what is appropriate.
The words of the book rest for a moment;
consider what follows,
and when good is attained, it shall come forth again,
so that nothing is omitted or lost.
Only the Tàishàng Zhī Jūn possesses laws and regulations;
he is enlightened and perceives with penetrative clarity.
It can be known that there is nothing he does not penetrate,
pre-knowing events that have not yet occurred.
Before the divine spirits have spoken,
he pre-knows what they intend.
When the spirits see this pre-knowledge,
they dare not deceive or mislead,
clearly knowing their place.
If one further speaks the words of the Tàishàng,
how could there be any who are not moved?
People together respect and fear him,
yet their hearts do not fully follow his ways.
This is to know that he perceives their intentions.
The reason it is so is that
the Tàishàng is entirely divine;
those who are born and those who are transformed,
those who should be born and those who should live,
all can be known through the divine registers in their proper order,
stating their status and rank.
How could there be anyone who does not follow?
Above the Jiǔhuáng are the Jiǔjūn.
As for the Jiǔjūn,
they are the kin of the Tàishàng.
Each has their own conduct,
bestowing grace and distributing charity.
When the various spirits follow them,
the various spirits respect their actions,
and there is none that is not accomplished.
Minor spirits who eat cannot know the intentions of the Jiǔhuáng,
how much less those of the common world?
If the heart is sagely and the ears are sharp,
only then can one observe the writings, records of emoluments, and plans.
The direct records and documents
naturally emit a refined radiance.
They all use gold for tablets,
and silver forms the writing.
These registers are within the Tiānjūn,
and the Zhōngjí has a duplicate.
The remaining documents and writings of the various departments
are all recorded on memorial tablets,
their writing appearing naturally,
the spirit following the characters,
giving the names a brilliant light.
Whenever there is speech,
it is immediately illuminated and known,
never contradicting what was said.
When the Shénrén and Zhēnrén receive the words of the Tiānjūn,
they speak of them in detail;
the Shénrén above and below
all know the affairs of the common people.
The Tiānjūn knows what the spirits say,
never deviating from the standards of the written word.
The Dào of spontaneity—
what is not known,
what is not transformed?
In action and error, there is naturally no selfishness.
They eat and drink from the celestial kitchen,
their clothes are of pure essence.
What more could they seek?
This is the conduct of the Tàishàng Zhī Jūn.
Great spirits and minor spirits
each have their own conduct,
they all fear and respect each other,
daring not to have selfishness.
They freely see what is sought,
shaking the heart that has intentions,
knowing if what they do can be accomplished,
not confusing or deluding their intentions,
causing each person to follow their ultimate intent.
Saying: "You all receive from the Xiānlù,
and your lifespan shall be infinite."
With sashes of gold, silver, and purple script,
being enfeoffed as marquises with fiefs,
and further bestowed with colorful silks, gold, silver, pearls, and jade—
attaining whatever the heart desires.
Is this the Dào of the immortals?
One knows if a person is steadfast or not.
Sometimes they present the forms of beauties and Yùnǚ,
making them seductive and compliant,
to see if the will remains unswerving.
Then they cause the forms of family members
to appear in changed forms,
with the mind following and thinking of their descendants;
this is the Dào of failure.
Or they manifest in deep mountains and great valleys,
places with many birds, beasts, tigers, and wolves,
and deep waters to transform the human heart.
Or there are poisonous insects and creatures,
causing the person to kill them.
If one is afraid and dares not ascend high mountains,
nor enter great valleys and deep waters,
the Dào is also not accomplished.
These signs are to warn people;
they are to see if they are among those who do not ascend,
or if they can especially strengthen the heart and focus the mind.
When facing delusions,
they do not turn away and their will remains firm,
following the path in and out, up and down,
through deep mountains and great valleys.
Though the water be deep and vast,
the heart feels no fear.
When seeing beautiful forms,
the will is not greedy or longing.
When the forms of family members
try to detain them,
they do not follow their words,
but only seek the Dào of life.
They advance to see the Tàishàng,
with a heart full of loyalty and filial piety,
having no concern for the world below;
this is what can be accomplished.
Warning the masses:
mostly take the essential writings.
Heaven also trusts the virtuous,
causing the immortals to deliver them.
If the person is naturally virtuous,
how could Heaven deceive them?
The reason there is deception
is that the person is suspicious,
forcefully seeking from the immortals things of no benefit,
seeking peace without merit—
how could they not be deceived?
It is that Heaven values life,
loves true sentiment,
especially values a firm will,
and considers that life requires the Sānmíng.
As for the Sānmíng,
it is the heart.
It governs the Míngtáng,
penetrating the light of the sun and moon;
it is called the Sānmíng attaining the Dào.
If the heart and will do not look back,
there are also records and plans;
they cannot be sought by force.
Those who ascend to heaven in broad daylight
naturally possess their truth.
Their nature is naturally virtuous,
their heart naturally has illumination.
When shaken, their warning intent does not lean toward evil,
they do not look upon or consider things like wealth and profit,
their clothes are coarse,
just barely covering the body—
this is the conduct of those who ascend to heaven.
Heaven approves of their goodness,
and thus commands benevolent spirits to follow and protect them,
so they do not fall into evil.
The celestial spirits love them,
and thus they accomplish their work.
This is brought about by the conduct of the person;
the person naturally does not covet worldly pursuits or material goods.
Heaven knows their ultimate intent,
and according to the registers, their names are true;
they naturally have benevolent stars.
At the time of their birth,
they naturally do not do evil.
Heaven again approves of them,
desiring transformation to assist the Tiānjūn in governance.
Celestial writings are made clear and penetrative,
conduct has no private secrets.
When conduct is observed for a number of years,
it finally enters the glorious registers with a name of life;
fitting the intention of the Tàishàng,
one can describe their merits and conduct,
assisting where they fall short—
this is also what the spirits should support.
Heaven trusts in filial piety and virtuous sincerity,
conduct being without blemish or flaw.
Therefore, in broad daylight, there is a reception,
brightness before and after,
witnessed by the masses of people;
this is the accomplishment of their merit,
causing others to see virtue.
Among those of the broad daylight,
out of a million people,
not even one person may attain it.
One who can attain it
is protected and trusted by the great spirits of Heaven.
Others cannot compare.
As for those who undergo Shījiě,
out of a million people, only one emerges.
Merits have different sizes,
they recommend each other in turn,
the person should be made to be loved and valued by Heaven.
Internally, they become the confidants of the Tàishàng,
recommending them for their trust and efficacy,
each achieving their merit and fame—
is this not good?
On the day the Tiānjūn issues instructions,
the spirits do not distort his words.
This is the Tiānjūn attaining virtuous trust and efficacy,
deeply knowing what has not yet occurred,
without a hair's breadth of deception.
If all lifespans are shortened,
all undergoing minor deliverance later,
further thinking of those whose words did not finish their meaning,
one further thinks to speak of them.
It is only that in the world from antiquity to the present,
most things do not conform to human expectations.
If one only wishes to satisfy oneself,
one will not be loyal in attending to affairs.
Regarding what is said and discussed:
if there is pleasure without anything extraordinary,
and seeing others do good,
one speaks with a smirk—
how does this benefit matters?
With flippant speech and easy words,
even father and son deceive each other.
While before one's eyes they are silent,
once they turn away and follow behind,
their words may be good or evil;
such behavior cannot be a model
and is of no benefit to the world.
The world is merely filled with dust and grime;
talk is but the stirrings of the self,
and no one responds to good books.
In their hearts they say, "I am good,"
yet their actions do not correspond;
they do not follow what is virtuous,
their language is vacillating,
and cannot be trusted or verified.
Such is called an imprudent person;
how can they progress for long?
They cannot be ranked alongside those with virtuous hearts and firm wills!
Those who seek life and find death difficult
do not wish to see these wicked people,
yet the wicked do not know themselves;
they think, "I am strong,"
and that few can surpass them.
Instead, morning and night, they wait to seize ill-gotten wealth
rather than working hard to obtain it,
thinking they can remain forever within the *Zhōnghé*.
When they speak with others,
bystanders see them
and do not find their words remarkable.
The spirits hear and know this;
they also observe their actions and movements.
Their hearts know their own evil;
they cannot sustain goodness for long,
and the spirits return to tell the celestial gods.
They say that in the *Zhōnghé* there are people of flippant speech and easy words
who cannot sustain goodness for long;
in a mere moment,
evil words appear again,
and they have no trustworthiness.
They only use flattery and falsehood to reproach one another;
how does this benefit anyone?
They are made to eat various grains
and wear silks and linens,
changing clothes according to winter and summer;
their food must please the palate,
and their clothes must please the body.
There are profits to be gained in the market,
yet they are unwilling to seek them [honestly],
even though they could support their elderly parents.
Getting out of bed the next morning,
they do not know where they are going.
Flaunting and selling what they have,
they alternate as hosts and guests;
they sit with legs splayed in taverns,
joking and laughing,
singing and dancing loudly.
Thinking themselves strong,
they whisper head-to-head,
discussing right and wrong
until their wealth is exhausted
and they have nothing left to support themselves.
They band together for wrongdoing
and eventually become wicked people
who cannot be restrained;
casting themselves into evil,
how could they have even half a day of goodness?
They are of no benefit to the household
and cause grief and suffering to their parents;
brothers, wives, and children
must constantly worry about them
without any end.
They attack, seize, and rob
without ever stopping,
yet they expect to live for many years
and to reach white-haired old age.
They do not know that Heaven dispatches observing spirits
to reside at their sides
and enter their bodies
to account for their actions.
If their deeds are auspiciously bad,
their years shall be cut short;
they cannot be allowed to last long.
They loudly commit evil
and have no wish to stop.
Up to the *Xiànguān*,
they are captured and executed by the law,
unable to live for long.
In the company of death,
how could they live again?
Or they are harmed by ghosts and spirits.
Their parents think of them
and are often seen weeping alone and keeping solitary watch,
with no one to assist them.
In old age, they are abandoned;
their food and drink are wretched,
rarely tasting rich or fine food;
their clothes and shoes are worn through with holes,
with no one to mend them.
This is the extreme of evil;
as months and years pass
and the emptiness persists for a long time,
their faces become ugly and wicked,
no longer resembling the color of a human being.
Acting as a son in this way
makes the parents have nothing to rely on in old age,
and relatives are unwilling to acknowledge them.
The deeds of such wicked people bring destruction upon their superiors;
relatives suffer because of them,
and this is called *Bì*.
When such a son dies, there is no funeral;
with no shroud or coffin,
he is simply buried.
Eaten by foxes,
his bones are abandoned in the wilderness.
When will one ever see you in clothes and with food again?
Thus one can know that the consequences of good and evil deeds
are brought upon people by themselves;
why should they complain or blame others?
How extremely foolish are the people of the world,
not considering the vast difference between life and death.
In life, there is life-breath,
and one sees the brightness of the heavens, the earth, the sun, the moon, and the stars.
For the dead, will there ever again be a time of knowing the heavenly light?
In the deep darkness,
how could there be a time of light?
Foolish people do not plan deeply,
causing their descendants to incur blame;
the disasters are beyond rescue,
and the calamities flow to future generations—
whose fault is this?
If a person does not transform
and brings about the loss of their own years,
should they not follow the deeds of the *Xiānshì*?
Actions and speech
should always have order and discipline,
benefiting parents,
allowing them to become healthy and plump,
their clothes perhaps becoming fine,
and their faces glowing.
This is the filial conduct of a son;
his strength is not used for evil.
Should one not also repay the kindness of the parents who nursed and fed them?
If you as a son are not filial,
will the son you beget be filial?
You gain good from good
and evil from evil,
just as a mirror reflects a person;
do you think your true situation is not known?
Thus there are writings on good and evil,
sharing the same ink;
what is the difference between longevity and its absence?
How great is the distance between them!
Living people endure for a certain number of years;
only when their life-force is exhausted do they reach the end.
Afterward, as ghosts,
they may not yet be subjected to interrogation.
Wicked people die early;
in the underworld, they are interrogated and punished,
held accountable for what they should not have done.
Suffering in places of torment,
they see no time of joy.
Being ghosts,
why is it that they alone have no time of pardon?
This is the extreme of evil;
being a ghost is yet more evil—
where can they find reliance or rest?
Having no food at home,
they resort to begging
and chasing the aura of fugitives;
this naturally cannot last long.
In the underworld, they also desire good ghosts and have no use for the wicked.
Thus, each should contemplate goodness
and not lose their proper measure;
only then is it acceptable.
If not,
what else could one hope for?
People should align their plans
and share the same desires with life;
would Heaven not deem this good?
Why instead do they commit evil?
Those of wicked deeds
cannot long behold the heavens, earth, sun, moon, and stars;
therefore they are hidden beneath the earth,
unable to share the joy of good ghosts,
being thus separated.
The repetition in these writings before and after
is because of a sincere hatred for these wicked people;
they simply must not live for long.
Those of virtuous nature
are protected by Heaven.
Their descendants are born consistently virtuous.
Under the sun, there are no taboos,
and it furthermore aligns with the *Yuèjiàn*.
At a time when the sun, moon, and stars shine brightly,
for one who lives by this,
why worry about not attaining longevity?
This is brought about by virtuous conduct.
In thoughts that distinguish between good and evil,
those who act appropriately will naturally find ease and peace.
Heaven does not oppose what humans do.
Reflect upon it, and reflect upon it again;
ponder it, and ponder it again.
One may go forward or withdraw.
For those who do not naturally cherish life,
nothing can be done.
The words of the text can be understood;
clearly discern any doubts.
One causes oneself extreme suffering;
be mindful of life and do not be remiss.
Be extremely cautious in what you say.
The words pause slightly again
to allow for reflection on what follows.
If there is anything unsatisfactory,
then discuss it once more.
Only those of sage-like virtue
each have their own sayings,
each has their own words.
Each distinguishes their abilities,
each ranks their own achievements,
each completes what is appropriate for them,
making themselves trustworthy,
and honoring the words of Tiān.
Causing Tiān to love humanity,
and to have grand achievements,
gaining the innermost heart of Tiān,
this is the wish of those with sage-like virtue.
Now, all people wish to receive from Tiān,
wishing to obtain its intent,
without having words of resentment.
Therefore, let each follow their own will,
let there be no wrongful speech, so they may be at peace with themselves;
this is to abundantly gain human sentiment,
making the reciprocal trust match their knowledge and consideration,
and following what is appropriate.
For humans to dwell in the world
is greatly difficult;
at every movement, they should uphold what is spoken,
never deviating from the standard,
and if they do not blame themselves,
but instead resentfully criticize the words of others,
this is to act without balance.
If each has words of resentment,
it causes Tiān to be indignant and not love humanity,
saying that lifespan is impermanent.
Therefore, in the world, there are people of sage-like heart and Dà Hé,
who make known its intent,
making people know where their faults come from,
making each person reform themselves.
Thus, human longevity emerges from within,
and does not reside in others.
Therefore, it is said that the Sīmìng
is as close as the chest and heart,
not far from the person,
overseeing the right and wrong of humans;
when there is a fault, it immediately retreats,
never missing the moment,
it immediately reduces a person's years of life.
For those who know they are not good to one another
and wish to hear its warnings,
it enables them to attain tranquility;
amidst their errors,
it makes them reflect on its intent,
causing them to receive punishment by losing years of life,
so that they are not left with resentment.
Tiān is greatly magnanimous, gentle, and patient with people;
punishment is not meted out in a single morning.
Only after faults have accumulated to a great many
does it then send down to the department of the presiding officials
to seize the person's hún and shén,
to interrogate them on what they have done,
which did not correspond with Tiānwén,
and they further practiced deception;
deceiving even after confessing their faults,
such crimes cannot be pardoned.
Therefore, instructions are again issued to enlighten and explain,
explaining that performing evil
results in disasters and anomalies,
merely to make them reform themselves;
if they do not use these words,
how can they remain as humans among the people for a long time?
Thus, distinguishing good from evil
is merely to make each person not resentful.
Tiān establishes prohibitions
merely to make people not violate them.
Yet if they intentionally violate them,
having been warned by the Tiānshén,
how can they long remain equal to other people?
By acting in such a manner,
is this the way to make people not die?
Do they think Tiān knows nothing?
The conduct of common people
is so unworthy of being adopted,
how can they be placed within Zhōnghé for long,
and be allowed to eat what is edible?
On the contrary, those protected by the Shànshén
only stop when their years are fully exhausted.
Not cut off by Tiān during their human lifespan,
this is the proof of their goodness.
Having performed good deeds for a long time,
why worry about not completing one's natural lifespan?
Thus it can be known that people themselves are unable to strive to do good,
and so they harm themselves.
Why are these evil people so exceptionally extreme,
thinking they can long share the same fate?
Unexpectedly, the Tiānshén urge them on,
making them descend into the earth;
after entering the earth,
when will they ever emerge to life again?
Beneath the ground, they further draw and seep into each other,
further losing their corpses;
can these people who again fail to obtain the blessings of Tiān
be counted again?
While acting, let each plan for their own person,
not increasing the suffering of later generations;
this is to be a person of middling goodness.
If not,
one wishes to be an evil person,
whom Tiān does not protect
and whom Dì does not wish to support.
One should be extremely cautious of this,
letting there be no transgressions or burdens,
only then can one be called a person.
One can act for parents and descendants,
able to continue practicing kindness and bestowals,
and can again obtain an increase in years,
with essence and flower moist and lustrous,
and vital energy and strength healthy and powerful;
this is brought about by doing good.
Evil naturally declines and falls,
so why should there be any doubt?
From now on,
one should carefully observe the waning and waxing,
distinguishing between good and evil,
and consider what kind of conduct is within the heart;
if one follows what is convenient and peaceful,
Tiān does not oppose what people do.
Ponder it again and again;
if one is not compliant but acts in opposition,
yet seeks long life,
how can such conduct long be seen by the Tiānshén,
the Sun, Moon, and Stars?
How would they be willing to shine upon them for long?
Though protected by the Tiānshén,
one instead struggles and wishes to endanger them;
whose fault is this?
Should it not be a person of good conduct and filial obedience?
Such a person immediately possesses salary and rank,
eating from the Sīnóng,
long caring for the people as their children,
making those above and below serve each other;
this is one who is honored by the people.
This is brought about by goodness.
Evil naturally fails to preserve the body;
how much distance is there between them?
Look at these test writings;
if one does not use their words,
but acts only for one's own pleasure and satisfaction,
is this not being a wrongful person?
If one has evil and cannot transform oneself,
yet claims to have filiality and goodness,
having a heart of loyalty, sincerity, and trust,
while expecting reward from Tiān;
having illness and seeking healing,
while having performed too much evil,
with no time of release,
could one be pardoned for long or not?
Therefore, this text is composed,
wishing to make common people
each not resent the punishment they receive.
Those who cherish life and seek survival
naturally do not perform evil deeds and lose their years.
Obtaining the book and seeing the warnings
makes them know to avoid prohibitions,
merely so they do not encounter evil.
If in this way they can reform themselves to do good,
they can long behold Tiāndì, the Sun, Moon, and Stars,
and be equal with others;
is this not good?
Instead, they do not cherish their lives,
thinking that after death they can obtain life again.
It is like a person who does not know they are doing evil,
thinking themselves to be acceptable.
In speech, they wish to be equal with others,
in clothing and food, they are the same as those in their group;
can this last for long or not?
Those who fear death
do not dare to violate the text of these warnings;
this is also what the plan for official salary brings about.
If that person's appearance is slight and has little merit,
one should correct their destiny; if it should be straightened, then straighten it,
what is there to look back on?
Go, and let each be cautious and strive,
considering the matters of safety and danger in what they do,
the warnings in the book can also be naturally understood.
The text of the Tiānshū wishes to make people do good,
and does not wish to hear of their evil.
Therefore, if one's own destiny is thin and incomplete,
it is not something to be greatly surprised about.
Reflect on it again in detail,
and do not be negligent.
Tiān has a Register of Life,
which is also desirable.
Dì has a Register of Death,
which is also very detestable.
Between life and death,
there is no comparison;
is this known or not?
Knowing evil, one should be cautious and blame oneself,
for one must not lose their lifespan for even a moment;
it is very regrettable.
When speaking and uttering sounds with others,
by doing good, one gains people's hearts and minds.
This is what Tiān considers good;
let no evil words come forth.
and leave blame to oneself.
Likewise, when exhaling breath and speaking,
one must wait and choose words carefully before uttering them.
If there is not even a single small unkind word,
then life can be extended.
Especially if one can contemplate and practice the matters of Heaven,
obtain the essential words of the Tiānshén,
use their admonitions,
and make one's movements and actions worthy of contemplation,
then one can change the register of fate
and be transferred to the department of long life.
One should again cultivate the self and rectify conduct,

they humbled themselves,
not expecting to live,
yet he could not bear to harm them,
so they thanked him again.
The Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) said:
"Tell the officials of the Bureau (Cáo) to go down immediately,
do not delay,
and let the Divine Messenger (Shénxíng) supervise them."
The Bureau (Cáo) said:
"The messengers will be sent down as the Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) commanded."
The Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) ordered the Bureau (Cáo)
to inform the Great God (Dàshén) again,
to look at the written petition
and let the various gods see it.
The Bureau (Cáo) passed the document to the Great God (Dàshén),
who sent it down to his subordinates,
each following their duties;
seeing those with merit and good,
those eager to advance should be advanced.
Previous matters are all reported and can be known.
The Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) ordered the Great God (Dàshén) saying:
"Quickly observe this person
to see if his words correspond with those of the Divine Messenger (Shénxíng) or not."
The Great God (Dàshén) said:
"I was sent to see the person,
counted his days,
observed his effectiveness, and returned.
On the day I was commanded,
I observed the meritorious person of Central Harmony (Zhōnghé),
and returned to report just as the Divine Messenger (Shénxíng) said."
The Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) also noted such meritorious people,
yet the gods under his command did not report in time.
The Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) realized this
and expressed his intent;
is this not an encouragement?
Having received the banishment to Central Harmony (Zhōnghé),
from now on,
this can serve as a warning.
If there is merit and it isn't reported,
and the Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) hears of it,
one will receive the punishment of personal banishment.
Each should be careful in their duties and send gods
to guide and transform the person,
making them a god
and increasing their refined light (jīngguāng).
Look at the registers;
if the person is not listed above,
record their name and submit it.
The Great God (Dàshén) received the order and returned to the Bureau (Cáo),
checked the files and names, and found this person.
He told the Bureau (Cáo)
that the records contained this text
and requested to check the Heavenly Lord's (Tiānjūn) internal register
to see if they corresponded.
The Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) brought out the document to look at it;
it was the same as the external document.
He ordered it to be submitted immediately.
The Great God (Dàshén) said:
"I am not sure if the years are complete;
I request to go back and examine it carefully."
The Heavenly Lord (Tiānjūn) said:
"The Great God (Dàshén) sets up eyes and ears,
yet does not see everything."
"...and speak of returning to the investigation?"
Dàshén apologized regarding his official duties.
Tiānjūn said:
"Hurry the investigation and return quickly."
Dàshén then investigated that person;
their years were already full;
there were unexplained lapses and irregularities,
and they should be held liable and submit to the punishment for their crimes.
Tiānjūn said:
"For now, let him wear the official cap and oversee the duties;
do not be negligent again.
Consequently, summon that person and bring him up;
let him not lose his efficacy in the minor post,
so that he may know how to achieve and offer merit."
"Yes, yes.
I request to act according to the instruction issued by Tiānjūn."
"Agreed.
Dàshén shall bring the person up,
appoint him to a minor post,
and observe his conduct."
"The time passed is still short;
I request to further investigate the actual facts;
if there is great efficacy and trust,
and if there is truly a vacancy, appoint him to fill the vacant position."
Tiānjūn said:
"I understand what Dàshén has reported;
do not have any thoughts of negligence."
Dàshén said:
"Yes, yes;
I request to send a messenger deity to go and oversee it clearly."
Tiānjūn said:
"Good."
Only in Heaven are there sagely and enlightened people,
all of whom have departmental duties,
each fulfilling their loyal conduct,
not failing those above,
each exerting their utmost strength in all they do,
and not losing their purpose.
They all pre-know the actions of the Tiānjūn,
always inclining their ears to listen,
wishing to know his intent,
and always observing the storehouses, bureaus, and literary departments,
so that separate commands may be known.
Seeing that the Lord summons at no fixed time,
they dare not go out privately;
only when there is official business do they move,
always reporting their intentions to one another,
and only then daring to go out.
Wherever they travel and wherever they traverse,
having received orders to inspect those places,
they dare not linger for even a moment.
Only after completing their duties do they dare to speak of personal matters,
sincerely returning to their tasks and not daring to act selfishly.
If it is not right to preserve their lives,
they spare no effort day or night and reproach themselves,
always fearing they might be of no firm use.
Each must govern their own person,
wishing to correspond with the intent of the Tàishàng;
when would they ever dare to be slack,
fearing they might lose what is appropriate?
Advancing themselves daily through service,
they do not require the words of the spirits.
Thus, wishing to perfect themselves
and desiring to achieve long-lasting vision,
they serve alongside the various gods of Heaven;
regardless of being great or small,
all are mutually aware.
Can they carry out unrighteousness?
They do not act solely on their own authority,
fearing there might be suspicion;
they inform one another of every move,
for when would there be a time to rest?
The reason it is so
is that each person has their own will,
each has their own thoughts,
each has their own accomplishments,
and their plans are different.
Each has their own view,
each has their own origin,
each wishes to obtain something,
and each knows their place;
thus their minds are clear.
Regarding the matters of these bureaus,
it is essential to value life,
for life is of the first importance.
The rest is decided by one's own actions.
The Qì of life attaches to the human body,
and they never leave one another.
Guarding and completing each other,
the spirits also value obtaining their names.
Transforming, entering, and exiting
through spaces without holes,
they are freely small or large.
Ordinary worldly people
do not see the forms of the spirits,
but the spirits know one another;
their forms are all made of Qì,
so what is there that cannot be accomplished?
Among great spirits and small spirits,
their refined light increases or decreases,
and there are always differences.
If their lifespan increases by nine,
they will have those years.
Practicing goodness in the great transformation,
their lifespan is also without limit;
at the top, there is nothing above,
at the bottom, there is nothing below;
entering and exiting without gaps,
with no outside and no inside,
their image is like a circle.
Stopping when they wish to stop,
moving when they wish to move,
their breathing creates spirit,
and their radiance is glorious and flourishing.
Their ascent and descent have fixed periods;
when it is time to move, they return according to the season.
They also cannot be completely free,
for they are constrained by ranks of honor and humility.
Each serves the other,
each has registers and records,
each has their duty,
and each should have the proper heart.
Holding to their will without deviation,
they clarify what they do.
Each shows their merit,
each presents what they know,
having nothing private;
they receive instructions for every action,
and do not fail the words of instruction.
Diligently pursuing their purpose,
they act without ceasing,
stopping only when they receive a command.
This is the vow of the living spirits,
who always have talismans and passes as proof of their conduct.
Wherever they conduct inspections
and receive provisions,
they must not exceed the written documents,
following the specified amounts.
In the relay stations of Heaven,
there are naturally registers;
those who should not stay must not stay.
This is the Tiānjūn's constant teaching not to act recklessly,
fearing that the officials guarding the stations might use their authority.
Since officials have ranks of honor and humility,
one must not forcibly or deceitfully claim a high position
or claim to stay long in the relay stations.
The officials always receive the Tiānjūn's commands;
when passing through a relay station,
they submit their name, rank, and affiliation,
and there must be no concealment or deception.
The Tiānjūn also knows this himself;
how could they clarify things for each other privately?
Each is treated according to their level.
If they do not follow the orders and commands from above,
and reports are frequently submitted,
this results in the loss of refined light,
and their lifespan is reduced;
this can be known.
One should be cautious of the time,
not daring to follow one's own desires
and fail to receive the teachings of those above.
The spirits of Heaven
continually inspect and recommend one another,
also without a time of rest.
Those who follow, whether of high or low rank, should know these prohibitions;
sagely and enlightened people naturally do not violate them.
Fearing that those who follow or those above might not see these warnings,
these writings are sent throughout the world to make the prohibitions known.
This is the Tiānjūn's great grace,
for he fears there are those who might violate them.
Because the Tiānjūn wishes to perfect the heart of goodness,
look at these writings
and also tell the worldly people.
Although worldly people are few in understanding,
they should know that within the Zhōnghé,
each has their own taboos.
The documents are sent throughout the world,
among the people in the Zhōnghé,
to the farmers on the roads,
to the gatherings at the village altars,
to huts, residences, and official dwellings,
and to gates, doors, wells, and stoves;
there Punishment and Virtue each govern their respective matters,
and there must be no evil.
Again looking at the records and registers,
their names are recorded,
accumulating many sagely and enlightened matters of principle.
Furthermore, let the Tiānjūn in the Míngtáng know;
if they again subtract from people's years,
even leading to death,
can one not be cautious?
The reason these writings are frequently sent down
is that people born later
do not believe previous words.
Therefore, through people of knowledge and deliberation,
those who do not violate prohibitions bring this forth
to let the worldly realm know it;
if one does not follow the words of the book,
one's life cannot be kept whole.
The registers of evil accumulate more day by day,
seldom having a time of reduction.
Therefore, a command was first given to write warnings,
not to let people violate one another;
violating them makes life short—
there is no doubt.
One should follow the words of the book;
small faults can still be remedied and resolved,
but from where can a pardon be obtained for great faults?
The warning texts are not just one scroll;
one should be extremely cautious and doubly cautious.
The celestial writings cannot be treated as one pleases;
among people with knowledge,
few are those who violate them.
If there are occasionally lapses,
Heaven also pardons them
and does not place them in the ranks of the wicked.
If one does evil without stopping,
it becomes linked to the register of death,
and is transferred to the Tǔfǔ,
hiding their physical remains;
when will they ever come out again?
The refined souls are detained and imprisoned,
questioned about what they did during life;
if their words do not match,
they will again face torture and punishment,
and the soul and spirit suffer to the extreme;
whose fault is this?
Coming together from human life,
why commit evil deeds?
Each should properly guard themselves.
Heaven bestows lifespan on humans;
it cannot be obtained a second time.
Doing evil decreases one's years;
when would there ever be a time of benefit?
This time is presided over by the divine;
Tiān Jūn obtains the evidence
and does not dare to overlook people’s evil deeds
so as to allow them to live long.
Do they think it is not known?
These writings have repeatedly warned people;
since the people do not reform,
it simply causes their years to reach their end.
Not wishing to do good,
they themselves cause their own lives not to be preserved;
what indeed can be done for those who do not stop doing evil?
One may write a brief explanation
and consider what follows;
if anything remains incomplete,
then consider it once again.
Only people with resolve
have hearts that are not confused.
Following the transformation of Tiān,
they should be guided by teachers.
Letting each follow their wishes
is to follow the heart.
The twelve thousand myriad things are all born within the land of Zhōnghé,
flourishing and growing large.
All return to cover themselves,
shading their own roots below.
Their flowers and fruits provide for the body and mouth,
assisting their grain provisions,
allowing for sour, salty, vinegar, and bland flavors at will.
Transforming water into salt
allows for the seasoning of various tastes.
Using beans to make dòuchǐ
assists salt in creating flavor.
Thickness and thinness are at one’s pleasure.
Leafy vegetables and various things
that should enter the mouth
are all provided for the people to eat.
Using them for warmth and satiety,
growing their appearance and form,
so that descendants may succeed one another.
Furthermore, using the liùchù that are not employed for labor,
allowing them to be eaten;
fatty, beautiful, sweet, and crisp varieties are all made available for food.
These are the spirits who serve Tiān,
harmonizing and balancing,
making each follow their wishes,
not depriving them of their peace.
Is this not spreading grace and bestowing benefits upon the people?
Is it not?
Why is it that Tiān bestows but does not seek recompense?
When should Tiān ever seek recompense for its bestowals?
It is only because the common people receive great grace but do not return to offer thanks
that it is sought.
Tiān eats the essence of Qì;
naturally, it does not necessarily require the people to provide thanks and offerings,
it values their intention.
Yet, conversely, they do not think of the Qì of Tiān creating and completing
so they may eat.
If there is knowledge among the people but they do not repay, it is like this;
they themselves should act as the envoys of Tiān.
Those who serve their duties
travel among the people,
sending flying insects to issue orders,
urging the farmers to attend to the crops,
while the Bùgǔ cries out day after day.
Making the people use its words,
in families regardless of size,
those who can eat grain encourage one another morning, night, and all day long,
and when the marshes are spread for planting,
Tiān makes them grow large.
Timely rain and wind sway them,
making branches and leaves move;
their bodies complete and full day by day,
they shall ripen to provide food for people.
Is this grace not heavy?
From year to year,
when is there an end?
Yet, conversely, they collectively fail to be filial and obedient
and have rebellious hearts.
What benefit is this to Tiān?
Why long nourish evil people
and let them see edible things?
Do they think Tiān knows nothing?
Why should it long nourish unfilial, evil, and rebellious people?
Therefore, Xiōngshén are placed to follow them.
Unfilial, evil, and rebellious people move,
causing people to face heavy prohibitions.
Their crimes lead to heavy calamities,
and no time of pardon is seen.
Thinking people should be like this,
why do they violate it,
leading themselves to a short life
and losing their allotted years?
Should one not observe that only filial and virtuous people obtain longevity and have descendants?
Good and evil should be compared;
lack of longevity and lack of longevity are comparable;
not being born and death should be suspended and not practiced.
Practicing good with filial piety and compassion
allows each to complete their years,
or even gain increased life.
Descendants follow in succession,
without times of premature death.
Tiān uses this as the result of virtuous and filial conduct.
Should it not be compared?
Why do wrong?
Is it bestowed upon people?
Tiān greatly detests it,
immediately causing life to be cut off.
Descendants receive the blame;
this is caused by evil.
What can they hope for?
Tiān delights in good people
and has no use for evil children.
One should reflect on the words of the books;
their text is complete and sufficient.
One can protect oneself
and will surely obtain the blessings of Tiān.
One can be without long suffering and self-sorrow,
letting worry fill the belly.
Furthermore, there is the Qì of worry that knots and does not unravel,
day and night sorrowing bitterly with great sighs,
thinking of money and wealth dispersing and vanishing,
fearing they cannot be long preserved.
Illness continues for years,
not leaving the pillow and mat,
uncured by doctors,
with knotted Qì unraveled.
Calculating and thinking of it,
day and night becoming weak and inferior,
food and drink again become scarce,
unable to digest grain,
the wǔzàng are uneasy,
and the pí does not grind.
This is precisely in the part that is not whole, with short breath,
and food cannot go down.
The household looks upon them;
it is called difficult to survive.
For families with money and wealth,
they have some stores and attendants;
without money,
property is exhausted,
inside and out are completely poor,
and they cannot help one another.
When the end of life arrives,
no coffin is seen,
and they are buried completely in the earth.
One must manage a living to have money and wealth
before it can be spent.
In extremely poor families,
wealth is gone and people flee;
when can they be reunited?
The household is separated,
and they cannot save one another again.
Consequently, no coffin is seen;
they become guǐ without coffins or outer shells,
floating without a home,
and also without anyone to provide food again.
Dying to become guǐ,
starving and begging for food,
without any time of stopping.
This is caused by evil deeds,
yet they do not know they have lost their clan.
Alas, how painful!
Dying with nothing to rely on.
These are people of accumulated transgressions and calamities
who bring themselves to have no household or later generations;
Tiān is also greatly pained by them.
Therefore, it allows for a Yífùzǐ,
unknown if male or female.
When the child is born and not yet grown,
the mother leaves to remarry.
Upon reaching adulthood,
the child asks distant and close relatives,
"Where are my parents?"
The relatives say,
"Your father was young,
his parents could not restrain him.
He followed frivolous people,
disregarded his family,
robbed people and committed banditry,
and did not stop himself.
The xiànguān executed him,
or he wandered to other places.
His property was exhausted,
and he did not return to his hometown.
Long in a different commandery,
it is uncertain where he went;
whether he is dead or alive cannot be known."
All the families suffered from this poison;
relatives, both paternal and maternal, have all gone far away.
"When your mother was pregnant,
seeing your birth provided continuity,
her heart was again joyful.
But the elders of the house
had nothing to rely on,
were so poor they could not provide for themselves,
so they sent her to serve others.
She followed a husband as a traveler
and has no date of return."
The Yífùzǐ says,
"All people rely on their parents to live,
yet I alone was born without seeing my parents."
Upon reaching a mature age,
the child asks where the father is.
People say,
"Your father committed evil,
abandoned his parents from afar,
and wandered in other regions.
Whether he is dead or alive is unknown;
his location is nowhere to be found.
Those who come and go have heard he is already dead,
but they do not know where.
His parents worried about him,
fell ill and did not rise again,
and thus did not fulfill their human potential.
Property was exhausted,"
Both the external and internal are in complete decline.
The fault lies with my remaining relatives who are distant and cold,
and who originally shared no bond of kindness with me.
I can only look up to Tiān and cry in grief,
with tears falling to soak my clothes.
My father committed evil deeds,
which led him not to return to his home.
I blame and reproach myself,
without any relief or end.
At that time, as a wandering traveler,
I hired myself out to a wealthy family
to serve as their slave.
Earning several thousand a year,
my clothing was provided from that;
what little remained was carefully kept.
After accumulating for over ten years,
I was able to use it for myself to return to my hometown.
I sought and memorialized my father,
weeping and moaning morning and night;
having no one else to rely on,
how great was the pain!
Because my father did evil at that time,
it caused his son to have nowhere to rely.
My tears fell in streams,
and naturally, there was never a time when they were dry.
Tiān was greatly moved by my sorrow,
always keeping me strong and healthy,
and making my livelihood profitable.
It allowed me to take a wife
and further have children and grandchildren,
so that my heart finally found a little peace.
I further spoke to my son, saying,
"My father committed evil deeds
and remained far away in another land without returning.
At that time, when people came and went,
I asked diviners about him;
uncertain of whether he was dead or alive, I knew not where he rested,
so I sought and memorialized him wherever I was.
After many years of traveling and making a living,
Tiān took pity on this destitute man
and caused profits to come in.
Having a bit of money,
I then sought a wife to help me in making a living,
and because of that, I have you.
I detested that my father did evil in his youth;
therefore, I admonish you.
From this day forward,
you must only do what is good.
Do not follow my father’s example and go far away to other places.
Therefore, I reflect on my faults again;
Tiān had pity on me.
You must strive in your heart to do good;
do not engage in idle wandering.
Manage your livelihood with order;
do not take the wealth of others.
Being just enough to sustain life is sufficient.
Each should attend to their duties;
do not drink wine recklessly
or debate right and wrong,
lest you face loss again.
Think carefully on the words of your parents,
so that you may be without blame.
Tiān above will hear and know of it;
by becoming an even better child,
you can obtain a long life and reach the full span of your years.
I have made this great admonition for you
to serve as a warning.
The various Shén will hear and know of it,
and they will report upward to Tiān.
Tiān will command good Shén to follow you;
your livelihood will progress,
your wealth will increase again,
the children you bear will be healthy,
and you will become even more prosperous.
This is the grace of Tiān.
During the Chūnqiū festivals and the Là sacrifice,
always offer to Tiān to repay its kindness.
Since you do not slacken,
strive to do good,
and you will naturally obtain your blessings.
Be cautious in what you say and do,
and again, moderate yourself.
The Tiānshén are always by a person's side;
one must not speak wildly.
Be careful of even small errors;
lack of caution leads to the loss of one's life.
Upon seeing an admonition, one should reprove oneself
and not blame others;
this precept can be understood.
Those who wish to obtain a long life
must not neglect these words of admonishment."
Humans living in the world
each have what is appropriate for them
and each have what they achieve.
None are deprived of their wishes,
following what they find convenient and peaceful.
Being at ease in what they enjoy,
whether as merchants or farmers.
Some wish to be officials,
or to be physicians, shamans, artisans, or masters;
each is allowed to reach fulfillment.
All paths lead to success,
providing what is useful for the people.
This is the transformation of the Tiānshī;
what could fail to be accomplished,
allowing them to support themselves?
One should remember to serve what Tiān performs:
the distribution of grace
and the rewards of the four seasons,
ensuring that fragrance and purity never cease.
This is to repay the grace of Tiān.
When good is practiced for a long time,
one is loved by the Shénlíng.
This is brought about by good conduct;
who would not follow?
Therefore, Tiān is always above,
overseeing human right and wrong,
causing spirits to go to and fro
to know what humans do.
Good and evil are immediately reported;
how could there be any error?
Those with a little knowledge might think otherwise,
so Tiān shows them its shadows and echoes,
making them hear sounds as proof.
Wind and rain, slow or fast,
are all made known;
how could there be doubt?
Movements and actions are varied,
yet writing and ink follow one another
and do not lose the Law.
Humans should also know what is permissible and what is not;
how can they be self-indulgent and not follow Tiān?
Tiān personally receives the spontaneity of Yuánqì,
following its instructions and commands,
not daring to have the slightest intention of violation.
Fearing any error,
and that which the people achieve as their work.
If they violate the Law of Tiān,
they cannot avoid the net.
Thus, the Mandate of Tiān serves as a self-admonition
that they should live long
and be equal to good people.
Can one find freedom in the midst of things?
Therefore, spirits are made to follow behind the evil-doer,
overseeing their improper actions,
and immediately reporting these matters.
No matter how large or small the fault,
it is heard above by Tiān.
These are the person's own faults;
why resent the writings of Tiān?
The books contain warnings, but if one does not apply them to their conduct
and only panics when falling ill,
how can they be exempted?
Truly the folly of the people
is of no benefit to Tiān.
It causes the spirits to toil and be troubled,
while physicians and shamans perform exorcisms.
They desire to seek life
but did not forget to commit faults in their time.
When they were committing evil,
it was just like this;
why did they not immediately repent and blame themselves?
Seeking life only when already ill;
afterward, many perish.
Regarding all prayers and sacrifices to the Shénlíng:
light offenses are released,
but heavy ones are not forgiven.
Instead, many summons are issued,
calling upon the spirits of fraudulent illness,
kowtowing and beating oneself,
desiring to seek life.
Though petitions are sent repeatedly,
if the name of death is fixed,
how can one escape again?
The houses of physicians and shamans
only want people’s money,
claiming the illness can be cured,
demanding many fat and beautiful things as well as wine and dried meat.
They call upon Great Spirits,
relying on their sent spirits
to bring about your escape from death.
Their names are not personally presented on the records;
wealth is exhausted
and then they lose their lives.
Pleas from the shaman's house:
if after three times it is not granted,
and the illness is not cured,
why plea again?
Serving calamity will surely lead to further calamity;
the responsibility lies afterward.
Xiéshén claiming to be Zhèngshén act wildly with decapitation and killing,
killing even if it is not the intended person.
Grievances and lawsuits reach up to Tiān,
and the Tiānjūn adjudicates them.
Killing the family that serves the spirits;
descendants suffer while seeking blessings for the sick.
They desire to seek life,
but if the calling is improper,
they instead suffer the calamity.
Those in families serving Xiéshén say of themselves,
"My spirit is a Zhèngshén," for they are taught these words.
But as for the essence of a Xiéshén,
when would it ever dare to go before the Tiānjūn
to plead for a person?
They only waste people’s wine, food, dates, and snacks.
When falling ill,
they instead falsely accuse the house of the Xiéshén.
Those who are cured
are said to be among the ranks of those who do not die.
If the matter has not been reported above,
one may be cured;
this is Tiān curing them of its own accord.
How can the house of the Xiéshén take credit
and claim they cure many people's illnesses?
Yet they demand fat and beautiful things from people.
Seeing what the Xiéshén do,
they are summoned to go above
to be interrogated about their hidden crimes.
If the hidden crimes are many and great,
they will not live.
For those who serve spirits, if the spirits do not come and go
and the person is not fit,
their spirit is daily exhausted;
this is the Xiéshén's own calamity.
The shaman's house takes the leftovers of the Xiéshén
to provide for their family;
with fat food and fine clothes,
they think they can last long.
The spirit once punished them;
how can they hope to live and have longevity?
Having received many hidden things from the spirit,
they cannot be forgiven again,
and their descendants perish along with them.
Instead, they speak of their faults,
"killing my descendants,"
or they themselves hope to last but soon the household perishes.
People should daily correct themselves;
they should not blame Tiān.
The people of this generation
act very foolishly and shallowly.
When ill and about to die,
they do not return to Tiān.
Confessing faults, beating themselves and kowtowing,
with the family, large and small,
helping each other to seek mercy.
After a number of days,
Tiān forgives them,
granting them time
to let them recover and rest.
If they violate again later,
kowtowing is of no use.
This should be known.
Strive to do good
and do not enter into forbidden areas;
then you can live out the longevity of your full years.
