Do you understand this?"
"Yes, yes."
"Furthermore, the Five Tones (*wǔ yīn*) each have something they draw upon and activate:
some draw upon Heaven,
some draw upon Earth,
some draw upon the sun, moon, and stars,
some draw upon the four seasons and Five Elements (*wǔ xíng*),
some draw upon the mountains and rivers,
and some draw upon the people and myriad things.
When sounds move, they all cause something to be shaken
and each leads to a certain effect.
For this reason, in harmonization,
those who grasp the meaning bring about good,
and those who do not grasp the meaning bring about evil.
When moving sounds,
the essential spirits of the myriad things all come first to pay homage and only then do they move;
one observes their physical forms.
Therefore, when moving musical sounds,
one must always strive to understand the matters at hand
and carefully grasp the meaning;
then Great Peace (*tài píng*) can be achieved,
and inauspicious *qì* can be removed.
Let the Realized Person (*zhēn rén*) examine this carefully."
"Yes, yes.
May I ask, regarding musical sounds,
how does their movement guide things?"
"Excellent!
Your questioning of these matters
has grasped the essential meaning.
For example, in spring, when things first move,
the *Dà jiǎo* string moves the *Jiǎ* stem.
When the *Jiǎ* day is above, it draws upon and moves the Year Star (*Suì xīng*);
when the Heart Star (*Xīn xīng*) is below, it draws upon and moves the Eastern Peak (*Dōng yuè*).
As for *qì*, it shakes Lesser Yáng (*shǎo yáng*);
as for sound, it shakes the Wood Element (*mù xíng*);
as for the spirit, it shakes *Gōumáng*;
as for animals, it moves the Azure Dragon (*Cāng lóng*);
as for position, it guides the Azure Emperor (*Qīng dì*);
and as for the spirit, it brings the Green-Clad Jade Maiden (*Qīng yī yù nǚ*).
Penetrating above and reaching below,
all things of their kind come to pay homage,
delighting in those musical sounds.
By explaining one thing to seek its kind,
it is infinite.
If you meticulously search for the essential meaning yourself,
you will naturally obtain it all.
Combine this with all written texts
to serve as a model.
Therefore, in raising music,
those who grasp its highest meaning
can transcend the world;
those who grasp its middle meaning
can achieve peace
and remove disasters and harm;
those who grasp its lower meaning
can bring joy to people.
Those who grasp its highest meaning
can delight the gods and spirits;
those who grasp its middle meaning
can delight the essential spirits;
those who grasp its lower meaning
can delight their own bodies.
If all meanings are obtained,
the Emperors and Kings above can roam without care,
music arises and punishments are cut off,
and the essential spirits are satisfied with one another."
"I wish to hear the secret meaning of how music arising causes punishments to be cut off."
"Excellent
are your words.
Indeed, music
is the essence of Great Yáng (*tài yáng*);
punishment
is the essence of Great Yīn (*tài yīn*).
When Yáng is flourishing, Yīn submits;
when Yīn is flourishing, Yáng submits.
Therefore, when music flourishes, punishments are cut off.
For what reason is music Yáng,
and punishment Yin?
When sounds are harmonious,
that direction is harmonious, good, and successful.
When sounds are not harmonious,
that direction is inauspicious and evil.
At such a time,
listen intently to the sounds.
One who knows sounds
knows all the good and bad fortune of matters;
one who does not know sounds
likewise cannot know them."
"Musical sounds
are the speech and conversation of music.
Whether divining the distant or the near,
all should be harmonized with them.
The days, times, surnames, and names;
the divisions and boundaries;
Prosperity, Assistance, Rest, and Exhaustion;
these are mutually combined
to form speech and conversation.
One who is proficient listens to them without error."
"Excellent, excellent!
I ask how music may be used to eliminate disasters, craftiness, and wickedness,
taking the laws of Heaven and Earth as the model for calculations.
Should the Dì at late or early hours strike and play his musical instruments
and begin singing the sounds,
in order to dispel the atmosphere of sorrow and suffering
and bring about Tàipíng?"
"Excellent is your question regarding the laws;
how exceptionally clever it is.
Huángtiān has long been pained by disasters
and pities the sorrow and suffering of sovereign Dìwáng.
Has it sent a Zhēnrén to take charge of inquiring about all matters of doubt?
Indeed, indeed.
Sit peacefully;
I dare not hide anything.
To hide it, I fear, would bring Heavenly punishment,
causing me to suffer severe blame for a long time,
which would not benefit my natural lifespan.
Sit peacefully and listen carefully;
I shall distinguish and explain its ultimate meaning for you one by one.
The Tiāndào is like a cycle;
it goes around and begins again.
When initiating music,
one should always follow the season to augment the Wángqì.
Establish the resonance where the Dǒu points;
face the direction of the resonance
and set the musical sounds in motion.
It is also acceptable for people to sing;
each should do so according to their specific tone.
The calculations use the Liùjiǎ and Wǔxíng.
The five, the Liùjiǎ, and the Wǔxíng
are the numbers of Heaven and Earth.
Shíqì
are the resonances of Heaven and Earth,
and that which they cause to arise.
For instance, on the day of Lìchūn,
the Dǒu points to Yín.
This is called the time of Shàngdì;
first strike the Dàjiǎo.
At the middle of the month, it points to Jiǎ.
In the second month, the Dǒu points to Mǎo;
at the middle of the month, it points to Yǐ.
In the third month, it points to Chén.
Other movements follow this pattern.
Each follows its Shíqì in order;
late or early hours serve as the measures.
First strike the Dìyīn and Dìxián;
next, the Wángyīn and Wángxián;
next, the Xiāngyīn and Xiāngxián;
next, the Hòuyīn and Hòuxián;
next, the Zhǐyīn and Zhǐxián;
each according to its number.
This is called receiving the teachings of Heaven
and according with the breath of Earth.
Heaven and Earth themselves take pleasure in using this;
how much more so should humans?
Humans
are the most noble of all things
and are the children of Heaven.
Heaven takes pleasure in humans using its numbers with solemn respect;
Earth takes pleasure in humans using its numbers with careful obedience.
This is comparable to the obedience of a filial child
who follows the teachings of their parents.
How could the parents not love and cherish them?
Now Heaven has purposely caused you to come and inquire.
I am in charge of speaking for Heaven
and establishing the numbers for the Superior Tàipíng.
I dare not leave anything out.
I strictly fear the punishment of Heaven and Earth,
I dare not deceive the Zhēnrén,
and I dare not hide anything.
Only if I am not asked will I be silent;
whenever I am asked, I speak of it.
I see the Zhēnrén inquiring about matters [...];
I understand that Heaven wishes to speak,
so I tell you everything in detail.
Once the Zhēnrén attains my Dào,
contemplate its meaning deeply
to pass it down to the people of future ages,
so they may follow its model and act accordingly,
to eliminate all kinds of disasters,
above to pacify the breath of Heaven and Earth,
and below to assist sovereign Dìwáng in their governance.
Let the hearts of common people
be at peace and not turn to evil;
let the twelve thousand things each find their proper place.
Is this not joyful?"
"How great! How great!"
"The Zhēnrén can be said to understand it."
"I ask about the matters of the Liùdòng and Bāfāng:
which are the most auspicious and good,
and which are the most ominous and evil?"
"Excellent is your inquiry.
Now listen carefully;
I shall explain its meaning for you.
That which is most mutually accordant and joyful is good and auspicious;
that which is mutually antagonistic and sorrowful is ominous and evil.
Mutual accordance and joy produce good sounds;
mutual antagonism and sorrow produce ominous sounds.
Thus music is its own joy.
Mutually accordant joy is good music.
Only on auspicious occasions should music be played;
ominous and evil matters must not have music.
If there is music, it is called music in name only,
and ominous events will increase daily.
Therefore, when the time augments the breath of the Dìwáng, the Xiāngqì, and the Wēiqì,
these are all auspicious matters before the Tiāndǒu.
What Heaven and Earth take pleasure in,
they wish to see arise;
what Heaven and Earth share
is then put into use.
Thus one should find joy in it, accord with it, and make it flourish.
As for the breaths of Rest and Exhaustion,
Heaven and Earth together discard and weaken them;
thus they should be discarded
and are not suitable for raising music.
Playing music for them goes against the heart of Heaven and Earth;
this is called great rebellion
and does not accord with the Shíqì.
Shíqì
is the correct Shíqì of Heaven.
Heaven and Earth serve as the law.
The breaths of Prosperity and Assistance govern Tàipíng;
the breaths of Imprisonment, Exhaustion, and Extinction govern ominous years.
The breaths of Prosperity and Assistance give birth to much
and produce many good things.
Therefore, in years of Tàipíng,
all things are fully born
and there are many good things.
This is the clear proof
and the great effect of Heaven and Earth.
The joyful and good effects of Heaven and Earth
are then seen among the people and the myriad things;
this serves as the great effect and verification.
Therefore, the sages and worthies of old used this to deeply observe themselves,
knowing the gains and losses of their own conduct.
They clearly used similar categories, similar matters, and similar breaths to observe and judge.
When they obtained signs of similar breaths and categories,
they would transform their nature and change their conduct,
not daring to do wrong.
The language of Heaven and Earth
uses these as its effects;
it does not whisper directly into a person's ear.
By observing what is obtained through signs and categories,
one can know for oneself.
Breaths of Imprisonment, Exhaustion, Death, and Extinction produce little
and accomplish no good things.
Therefore, in ominous years,
little can be born,
there are no good responses,
and no good things;
this is because they share the same matters and the same breath.
Therefore, those about to reach Tàipíng
may fully perform music;
such music accords with and finds joy in the Wángqì,
and the Píngqì arrives.
As for those ominous years of which I previously spoke,
they must not perform music
and must not raise music without cause.
Breaths of Imprisonment and Exhaustion are in rebellion against Heaven and Earth;
thus, in ominous years and for ominous matters,
music must not be performed.
Therefore, the breaths of Prosperity and Assistance
are where Virtue resides.
The breaths of Imprisonment and Exhaustion
are where Punishment resides.
"Therefore, a sovereign who possesses virtue and loves life,
Heaven causes him to be able to create music;
a sovereign without virtue
cannot create music.
This is clear proof from Heaven.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, yes.
How fearsome!
Today I have fully questioned the Tiānmíngshī,
and thus fully understand the intent of Heaven's music;
before asking,
I thought creating music was merely a minor matter
that ordinary people and ordinary affairs could all do.
Having asked today,
henceforth I shall not dare to move or act recklessly."
"Excellent, enlightened student!
It can be said that you understand the principles of documents and are profound,
having grasped the intent of Heaven.
When Tàipíng arrives,
calamitous breaths will all depart."
"I respectfully and repeatedly ask again about the doubts in my heart."
"Proceed;
speak plainly and do not avoid anything."
"Yes, yes.
Now, the breaths of Heaven and Earth
are half-flourishing and half-resting,
comparable to day and night,
without end or cessation.
Can music be performed all day long?
Or can it only be performed in the Wángxiāng
when the Wángqì is present?"
"Only at the moment it begins,
it should start with the sovereign breath,
and not start with the Xiūqì.
The year is thus,
the month is thus,
the day is thus,
and the hour is thus."
"Now your humble student has not yet grasped the full meaning,
but if one wishes to celebrate the year with music,
and the year is at Mǎo in the east,
one should make music in the second month of spring.
If one wishes to celebrate the month,
it should be applied to each respective month;
for the day, use the flourishing day;
for the hour, use the flourishing hour.
If it is like this, it can be said that the Dào of Heaven is attained,
and calamitous breaths will depart.
If it is not like this,
it will all constitute a disruption of Heaven's regulation,
giving rise to ominous calamities.
Therefore, the sage kings of antiquity
deeply knew the heart and intent of Heaven and Earth,
and did not dare to celebrate ominous matters with music.
If ominous matters are celebrated with music,
then ominous matters will increase and flourish daily;
when they increase excessively, they cannot be saved;
therefore, one should not celebrate them with music.
When Heaven bestows nature,
each thing naturally has its Jīngshén.
Rejoice in the good,
and the good Jīngshén arrives;
rejoice in the evil,
and the evil Jīngshén arrives.
This is the nature of Zìrán;
there is nothing strange about it.
It is only that foolish people do not deeply consider it."
"Excellent, excellent!
The Zhēnrén wishes to know its great effect;
this is comparable to the Dào of Heaven.
All those that are pure and clear delight in returning to Heaven;
all those that are heavy and turbid delight in returning to Earth.
Each follows its own kind;
there is nothing to find fault with.
Therefore, by rejoicing in the good, one obtains good;
by rejoicing in the ominous, one obtains the ominous.
It is like water flowing downward
or fire rising upward,
without missing by even a tiny fraction.
Let the Zhēnrén entrust this book to a sovereign of virtue
to show it to ordinary people.
Now that the Tàipíng breath has arrived,
Heaven promotes the good,
causing all to rejoice in the good;
there must no longer be those who rejoice in ominous matters without cause.
Those who rejoice in ominous matters
are making themselves enemies of Heaven
and a misfortune to Earth;
their transgressions will not be removed.
Now, Heaven above names those who rejoice in ominous matters
as people of great rebellion.
The ominous breaths of Heaven
and all the misfortunes within the Earth shall all come down and return to them."
"May I ask, if there is a sudden emergency
where music must be used
to celebrate an auspicious matter,
and there is no time to wait,
but it must be applied toward the Wángxiāng in front of the Dǒuqián,
what should be done?"
"How excellent
your questioning of this matter is;
you have grasped its essential meaning.
Indeed, have the musicians reside in the Wángxiāng;
if they cannot reside in the Wángxiāng,
have the musicians and the assembly
also face the flourishing direction and petition it,
also using its tones,
and also using its numbers.
If only based on the person's surname and name,
uphold the pitch-pipes and the calendar;
if the tones and the breath correspond,
one can also accord with the breaths of the flourishing and assisting times,
and by following that person, cause music to be made;
it can also be done this way.
Those who act like this
all follow and apply the teachings of Heaven and Earth,
causing there to be no disasters or harms.
If it is not like this,
if there is a convergence with ominous or imprisoned breaths,
then ominous matters will all arise.
Furthermore, in raising tones and leading music,
one should also use the auspicious,
auspicious tones and good matters.
Now, the breaths of flourishing and assisting
are comparable to humans having a sovereign or king;
they also do not wish to hear of ominous matters,
ominous words,
or ominous tones.
The reason for this is that
the breaths of flourishing and assisting are what August Heaven uses to preside over life,
presiding over the completion of good matters,
thereby assisting Heaven in generation and completion.
Evil tones and ominous matters
do not assist Heaven in the generation and completion of all things.
Therefore, the Wángqì does not wish to hear them with pleasure;
neither do the breaths in front of the Dǒuqián.
None of them wish to hear them with pleasure.
Therefore, the sages, worthies, and sovereigns of antiquity
all accumulated good words and good deeds,
and did not admit ominous or evil matters.
These were called calamitous words,
and the crime was punished by death;
even if the crime was not sufficient to merit death,
they simply detested the inauspiciousness of such calamitous words,
and therefore killed them.
Does the Zhēnrén realize how grave this prohibition is?"
"Yes, yes.
How fearsome!
How fearsome!"
"Since you know to be fearsome early,
you may exist long;
if one does not know how to be fearsome,
it is the root of death.
"First, it is said: first, harmoniously and joyfully move the Dìqì of Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons;
multiply each matter by three to please Heaven,
making Heaven greatly pleased and joyful,
the sovereign will live to a grand old age,
calamitous evils will be extinguished,
Heaven's disasters and harms will all be removed,
the Tàiyáng breath will not be combative or wrathful,
and the borders of the state will be at peace.
Those who know to always first move in harmony and joy,
the Dào of Heaven will flourish because of them,
the true spirits will emerge because of them,
and people living in seclusion or caves
will all delight in coming to assist the upright, ...
"Second, it is said: first, harmoniously and joyfully move the Wángqì of Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons;
multiply it twice to please the Earth,
the breath of Earth will be greatly pleased,
and not be combative or wrathful,
causing the king to live long,
cunning rogues, thieves, and military weapons will vanish,
and goodness will flourish within the borders of the state.
Those below will all delight in following and obeying those above,
the worthy ones among the people will all come forth
to assist in governing the state,
and the Earth spirits will harmoniously nourish, ...
"Third, it is said: first, harmoniously and joyfully move the Xiāngqì and the Wēiqì,
making the breath of central harmony greatly pleased and joyful,
so that the lord, ministers, and people are compliant and prudent,
each maintaining their proper place;
then sycophants, hypocrites, and thieves will not arise,
and the borders will be preserved.
Therefore, the breath of harmony flourishes daily,
the Wángqì is generated,
and all things love the good.
"Fourth: Be cautious not to activate or take pleasure in the *qì* of death and destruction,
which brings about severe banditry and thievery,
and many instances of sudden death.
The state borders will be constantly in peril and difficult to pacify,
bringing about numerous evil *qì* and ghostly entities,
causing extreme harm,
which, when severe, is called 'Chaos and Disturbance.'
The *qì* of extreme *yīn* leads to rebellion and inversion;
be cautious, be cautious.
"Fifth: Do not activate or take pleasure in the *qì* of imprisonment and abandonment,
which mostly leads to banditry and thievery,
matters of prisoners and litigation,
where punishments and crimes are numerous and confused,
making it very difficult to find peace.
The people will harm and wound one another,
leading to many people with chronic illnesses.
"Sixth: Do not activate or take pleasure in the *qì* of decline and cessation,
causing many people to become frail and ill.
Furthermore, it produces deceitful and cunning people who cheat one another,
with much evil gossip and slander;
the state will have little wealth,
and the people will mostly be in poverty.
If one takes pleasure in the three divisions of the subtle *qì* of the *Shàngdì*, the *Shàngwáng*, and the *Xiāng*,
then Heaven, Earth, and Humanity will rejoice,
bringing timely moisture,
and removing all categories of disasters;
this is called 'Following the Good *Qì* of Heaven, Earth, and Humanity,'
and it brings about good matters.
If one takes pleasure in the lower three divisions,
the *qì* of death, destruction, imprisonment, cessation, and decline will bring about rebellious disasters;
though Heaven rains,
evil harms will be very numerous,
and cannot be forbidden or prevented.
If one stirs up and takes pleasure in these various types of abandoned *qì*,
then evil *qì* will be greatly released,
worthy scholars will go into hiding,
County Officials will lose control of governance,
people and ministers will be difficult to govern,
and many affairs will be in turmoil;
one must not fail to be warned and cautious.
In all matters of Heaven and Earth,
there are fixed and constant laws.
In a region that has *qì*,
one who turns toward the honored wishes to see music; in a region without *qì*,
those in decline or death should not see music.
Therefore, those who take pleasure in the good are called 'Accordant Governance' in Heaven,
and those who take pleasure in the evil are called 'Rebellious Orders' in Heaven.
Those of Accordant Governance obtain the power of Heaven,
while those of Rebellious Orders obtain the punishment of Heaven.
Those who obtain the power of Heaven achieve longevity;
those who obtain the punishment of Heaven achieve misfortune and blame.
The reason this is so
is that Heaven’s governance is like a shadow or an echo;
it does not snatch away what people find peace in.
To take pleasure in good is to obtain good;
to take pleasure in evil is to obtain evil;
what more needs to be said?
Indeed, good and evil, safety and peril,
each follows its own kind,
without ever failing to do so,
but the foolish simply do not consider it.
Thus, for those who take pleasure in the *Dào*, the *Dào* comes to gather;
for those who take pleasure in *Dé*, *Dé* comes to gather;
for those who take pleasure in the military, the military comes to gather;
for those who take pleasure in correctness, correctness comes to gather;
for those who take pleasure in the heterodox, the heterodox comes to gather;
when has it ever not been thus?
Therefore, I have deeply considered the laws of Heaven
in order to warn the *Zhēnrén*. □□
Indeed,
the laws of Heaven must not be violated.
Therefore, I repeatedly and carefully instruct you."
"“Yes, yes.”"
"“The reason the music for the *Dìqì* for the worthy is tripled:
The *Dìqì* is the most honored and supreme,
symbolizing the honor of Heaven,
therefore the music for it is multiplied.
Heaven
controls Earth and Humanity,
therefore it is tripled,
to symbolize Heaven, Earth, and Humanity.
When Heaven, Earth, and Humanity see music, they arise and become ordered,
and all things each find their proper place;
the twelve thousand types of auspicious responses and good things will all emerge together,
therefore music is performed for them first.
When listening to this music, one should listen in detail with a focused mind,
sitting upright and contemplating for a long time,
with joy and delight in the heart,
feeling deeply pleased.
With loyalty, trust, and ultimate sincerity,
without any evil intent,
it is as if one were sitting facing the *Dìwáng*,
not daring to be heterodox or devious.
Heaven responds to such conduct,
and all types of sinister evils and disasters will entirely depart.
Since Heaven is the most honored
and the *Dìqì* is the authority,
it is naturally the law narrated by Heaven;
thus, achieving Great Peace is not difficult.”"
"“Excellent, excellent!”"
"“As for why the music for the strings for the *Wángqì* is doubled:
The *Wángqì* symbolizes Earth.
Earth and Humanity dwell together,
therefore the music for it is doubled,
to take pleasure in Earth.
When Earth and Humanity see music and feel joy,
then all things together will achieve order."
"Furthermore, *Dì* (Earth) is lowly,
so its music is less than that of *Tiān* (Heaven)."
"Excellent indeed, excellent indeed!"
"Moreover, *Wángqì* (Kingly Qì) is weaker than *Dìqì* (Imperial Qì);
it is one rank lower than *Dìqì*,
so it has less [music].
The law of the succession of ranks between the honorable and the lowly
is its natural division."
"Excellent indeed, excellent indeed!"
"The reason the music for *Xiàngqì* (Ministerial Qì) and *Wēiqì* (Minute Qì) consists of one row
is that *Xiàngqì* and *Wēiqì* resemble *Zhōnghérén* (Central Harmony Humans).
Since *Zhōnghérén* are lower than *Tiān* and *Dì*,
their music is less.
Humans are the masters who manage the myriad things for *Tiān* and *Dì*.
When humans are joyful, they are pleased and happy to do good;
when they do good, the myriad things are well-managed.
When humans are not joyful, they do evil;
when they do evil, the myriad things become calamitous."
"Excellent indeed, excellent indeed!"
"Furthermore, humans
are the leaders of the myriad things of Central Harmony.
If their leader is joyful and manages things well,
then the affairs of the myriad things will be well-managed.
If their leader is in disorder, then the things will be in disorder.
Therefore, one must first make their leader joyful,
to accord with the Way of making *Tiān*, *Dì*, and humans joyful."
"Excellent indeed, excellent indeed!"
"For this reason, the *Qì* of the highest goodness is the most honorable and good;
thus its music receives a triple layer
to celebrate goodness.
For this reason, in ancient times, when the *Dì* (Emperors) and *Wáng* (Kings) ruled with goodness
and attained the heart and mind of *Tiān*,
they received triple music;
this is clear evidence of it.
Now that the *Tàipíng* (Great Peace) *Qì* has arrived,
they are taught to raise music.
The *Qì* of decline and disorder corresponds to years of calamity;
therefore, one must not raise music.
If one raises music then,
it is called raising music for calamity and decline,
which in *Tiān* is called Great Rebellion;
it is the root of disasters
and the source from which misfortune arises.
Can one not be cautious?"
"Excellent indeed, excellent indeed!"
"Therefore, the next level of music is double-layered.
*Wángqì* is not like *Dìqì*,
so its music is less.
For this reason, for a rule with less goodness,
the music for it declines and is reduced.
The reason it declines and is reduced
is that when *Qì* declines and is not of great goodness,
one does not dare to have triple or much music.
Within it, there is calamitous *Qì*,
so one does not dare to provide the full complement of music.
It is like a household that has seven parts good and three parts evil;
in their hearts, they are not joyful because of this;
this is what is meant."
"Excellent indeed, excellent indeed!"
"Now, with seven parts good and three parts evil,
goodness is more and evil is less,
so how can one stop the music?
Even though the person is joyful in their heart,
when they occasionally think of the three parts evil,
then they are not purely joyful;
this is natural disposition.
Only when goodness is complete
and there is not a single worry remaining,
is there then great joy.
Thus, music is used to celebrate goodness,
not to celebrate calamity."
"Excellent indeed, excellent indeed!"
"My words are the bright contract of *Tiān*;
the book does not lose a single point.
Therefore, the next level of music is of a single row.
*Xiàngqì* and *Wēiqì* have little which is peaceful;
human virtue is the least,
and is not like the *Qì* of *Tiān* and *Dì*.
Thus it is minute and small,
not like *Tiān* and *Dì*,
so its music is less.
*Xiàngqì* and *Wēiqì* have little which is transformed.
Now in the *Zhōngguó* (Central Kingdom),
there is certainly much evil and little goodness;
therefore, they do not dare to provide the full complement of music.
Otherwise, it would be called celebrating calamity and evil.
Since their goodness is little,
their music is little.
The reason it is little
is that they only celebrate the goodness within,
but do not dare to celebrate the calamity and evil within.
To celebrate the calamity and evil within
would be like a petty person
who has seven parts calamity and three parts goodness.
For the three parts of goodness, they are allotted three rows of music.
But having seven parts of calamity and evil, they conversely have seven parts of sorrow and suffering;
being depressed and uneasy, how can they follow with music?
The reason for this is that
using ten out of ten as the rule,
the ten is then divided into three.
*Dìqì* is ten out of ten good;
*Wángqì* is two parts good and one part evil;
*Xiàngqì* is two parts evil and one part good.
Thus, *Dìqì* resembles *Tiān*.
