The Tiāndào does not deceive people;
it must always strive for utmost sincerity.
If the Tiāndào, which does not deceive, is used to deceive,
then after a long time, the days will be ruinous and declining.
Heaven's way of practicing the Dào
does not delight in drowning, filth, or disgrace,
and does not desire to selfishly benefit from others.
Heaven is indeed supreme,
and the Dào is even more superior to it.
The Dào is the master and law of the Tiānhuáng;
it is even higher than Heaven.
Therefore, Heaven and the Dào preside over the cultivation of correctness
and are the elders in all matters.
Therefore, they can harmonize Yīnyáng,
regulate the wind and rain,
correct day and night,
and arrange the ranks.
Between Heaven and Earth,
none do not receive grace and mandates,
each obtaining their proper place.
Now, the low and foolish practice the Dào,
but on the contrary, they act with deceit, arrogance, folly, and madness.
They together confuse and disorder the Tiāndào,
and destroy the head of Heaven's transformation.
On the contrary, they go about begging and seeking people's goods,
providing no benefit among the common people,
drowning, defiling, and disgracing the Tiāndào.
They do not benefit the common people internally,
so they cannot be taken as models for masters.
On the contrary, they cause later generations to teach one another;
whenever they speak of the Dào,
they cause people to be foolish, mad, arrogant, and deceitful.
Furthermore, they go about being drowned, defiled, and disgraced while begging;
because of this conduct, they are named,
and called the Dào of the foolish, mad beggars.
On the contrary, they cause ordinary people to together curse Heaven,
to together despise the correct Dào,
and to cut off the Great Transformation.
Heaven greatly detests this,
and the Dào greatly hates this;
those in Heaven do not wish to see their forms.
Now, the great upright Qi of the Shànghuáng Dòng has arrived;
the sun, moon, and stars are arrayed, all doubling their brilliance.
The Dào and Heaven should regulate the wind and rain,
harmonize Yīnyáng,
and cause all things each to obtain their proper place.
Those of former times who by chance attained the Dào and ascended to Heaven
have no positions in which they could serve.
When questioned in Heaven, all were found to have transgressions
and cannot work together with the divine.
You all reside upon the earth,
yet you are still seen and called foolish, mad beggars.
You do not suffice as masters for emperors and kings;
how then could you suffice as masters in Heaven?
Heaven detests this;
the Great Dào declines and falls into ruin.
The blame lies with the people of later antiquity who learned from one another but lost the laws and measures.
Heaven is distressed by this
and is greatly dejected.
The Tiāndào does not flow through;
therefore, I was sent down to converse with the Zhēnrén
to distinguish the gains and losses of the Dào.
Desiring that the people under Heaven all awaken at once,
all knowing the intent of Heaven,
changing their conduct,
changing their hearts,
and no longer violating Heaven's prohibitions;
then the students will succeed.
If they practice their former conduct,
Heaven will not let them ascend;
they will certainly return once more
to die in the lands of the five disgraces,
giving up their lives in the soils of the five defilements,
in the severed caverns and uninhabited wilds of madness,
where above there are no Sānguāng
and below there is no good soil."
"Why is this?
I wish to hear it;
why is their transgression so heavy?"
"It is not a punishment from above.
The Tiāndào acts as the law;
each follows its own kind,
and the lower realms seize them."
"If it is so, why not kill them immediately
instead of waiting until this point?"
"One might wish to immediately exterminate and kill them,
but these people say of themselves
that they desire longevity and are of utmost faith;
one might wish to kill them midway,
but on the contrary, they would wail to Heaven and cry to Earth,
saying of themselves that they are greatly wronged,
yet not knowing themselves where their transgressions originate.
Therefore, Heaven examines them and banishes them,
afterward casting them into the soils of the five disgraces and madness
to cause them to know themselves.
If you wish to know the truth of the matter,
compare it to a wise king examining people's transgressions and responsibilities;
he is not willing to kill them immediately.
He still must send them to prison according to the size of their crimes,
great crimes to great prisons,
and small crimes to small prisons to be dealt with,
to cause the person to submit
and to die only after they know their own guilt,
so they have no resentment and nothing to say.
If their words are not fully exhausted,
they will certainly say they are wronged
and die harboring resentment.
Therefore, under the lords of the Wǔbà,
many of their people and ministers died harboring resentment.
If you wish to know how Heaven administers punishment, it is like this.
Does the Zhēnrén understand?"
"How terrifying!
How terrifying!"
"If you know shock and terror,
this is the gate to life."
Not knowing fear and alarm
is the root of death.
You, be cautious with my words;
my words are the very weapons of Heaven
and cannot be slandered or offended.
Slandering or offending them causes a person harm:
small slander brings small harm,
and great slander brings destruction.
A word of caution to the Zhēnrén:
people of the later ages have accumulated ignorance;
they trust their own ignorant hearts
and, by claiming things are not so, they bring themselves to ruin.
I personally travel by way of the heavens
and know what is below [□□],
without missing one in ten thousand.
I dare not deceive you;
to deceive you would be not to fear the Zhēnrén,
but rather to fear the majesty of Heaven.
Therefore, my words are to be trusted and trusted again.
The reason I speak repeatedly and with such weight
is for fear that the stubborn will miss the way.
Thus, I repeat myself to make the words more literary [□□].
Matters of Heaven
are truly distant and difficult to know;
therefore, these writings from time to time descend to harmonize with the Earth.
If there is good on Earth,
then there is good in Heaven.
If there is evil on Earth,
then there is evil in Heaven.
Therefore, when humans do good on Earth,
Heaven also responds with good;
when humans do evil on Earth,
Heaven also responds with evil,
for their Qì communicates upward.
The five Qì are connected, and above and below are the same;
the Liùjiǎ are related, and above and below are the same;
the Shí’èrzǐ harmonize and are manifest above and below;
there is no far or near, for all communicate with each other.
If those below are good,
those above are bright;
if those below are evil,
those above are ominous.
Thus, the Wǔxíng arise below,
and the Wǔxīng shine brightly above.
This
is how Heaven instructs the people under Heaven.
It is the same for all the Sānguāng.
Heaven again communicates with the Sānguāng beneath the Earth:
when the Sānguāng are bright below,
it is the same in Heaven.
When it is bright above in Heaven,
it is the same on Earth.
The two respond to each other,
harmonizing to form the constant path;
when there is great good in Heaven,
it is the same on Earth.
Just as Heaven has the Liùjiǎ and Shí’èrzǐ,
it is the same on Earth;
as Earth has the Liùjiǎ and Shí’èrzǐ,
it is the same in Heaven.
Therefore, above and below always respond to each other,
not erring by even a tiny fraction.
May the Zhēnrén be cautious of this.
Although my words are distant,
be careful not to keep them hidden or stored away;
show them to students,
and when transmitting them, one must fast and purify.
Be cautious of this.
Follow the text as the law
and do not recite them from memory."
"Yes, yes.
I wish to ask, Tàishàng, since mid-antiquity,
among those who teach each other the Dào,
why do many, on the contrary, leave their homes and abandon their kin,
deserting their wives and children?
Why do many, on the contrary, beg for food,
feign madness and deceit,
or eat excrement and drink urine?
Later students often teach these things to one another,
and they all have masterly methods,
so they are not merely baseless."
"Excellent!
Your difficult question
has touched upon its wicked meaning.
Heaven detests this;
did Heaven teach you to ask about it?
How coincidental those words are;
for what reason did you ask this?"
"I have wondered about it for a long time
with no one to question,
and I have always felt troubled by it."
"Excellent.
Has Heaven indeed made you the one in charge of asking about such matters?
Very well. Open both your ears,
and I shall explain it to you in detail.
When High Heaven first brought forth the Zhēndào,
it was not like this.
All practiced filial piety and cared for their parents,
continued their lineage and had wives and children;
they maintained a proper appearance
and did not feign madness
or eat excrement and drink urine.
They all followed the Dào,
and their actions conformed to the law.
The highest scholars served as teachers and assistants to emperors and kings,
nourishing their kind
without anyone being harmed.
At that time,
comparable to the Sānhuáng and Wǔdì,
they moved according to the Zhèngdào,
striving to benefit one another and not to harm or injure.
Thus they were able to walk the Zhèngdào
without hiding themselves.
When the Sānwáng brought disorder
and the Wǔbà were about to rise,
rulers, ministers, and commoners began to deceive and disrespect one another;
thus some falsely feigned madness.
Still fearing they would be recognized,
they begged for food
and ate excrement and drank urine;
these are the actions of the destitute and desperate,
and the words of the destitute and desperate.
The Dào also has its phases of decline and prosperity,
comparable to these Sānhuáng, Wǔdì, Sānwáng, and Wǔbà.
In later antiquity, the Bàdào was often seen,
begging, abandoning one’s kin,
deserting wives and children,
and eating excrement and drinking urine;
this is the decline of the Dào
and the arising of the Bàdào.
Therefore, the Sānhuáng and Wǔdì mostly attained the Dào and ascended to Heaven;
some achieved Shījiě,
and some departed in their physical form.
The Sānwáng lived long lives,
but among the Wǔbà, none attained the Zhèngdào;
they all fought in battles and died in the wilderness.
Now, in later antiquity, those who keep to this Bàdào
will also all die in the wilderness;
this is what is meant.
I do not deceive the Zhēnrén;
this is the Hegemon phase of the Dào,
the same as the Hegemon-kings;
how can such a one ascend to Heaven?"
"Excellent, excellent!
This foolish student's heart
is truly, truly enlightened now.
I did not expect that the Dào also has a Hegemon phase.
Since the Tiānshī has explained it,
only then do I know it."
"Truly, truly [□□]!
You may be said to be enlightened."
"May I ask, what should the students of today
do?"
"Now, the Tiāndào is greatly complete.
From now on,
it is different from the past.
If one wishes to cultivate the Bàdào methods of mid-antiquity,
the Zhēndào cannot come.
The Zhēnrén should be cautious and wary of this!
If you desire to exist forever in joy,
cultivate according to my writings.
If you miss by even a tiny fraction,
your life will not be preserved whole;
can one not guard it?
At the origin of the Dào,
the Huángdào has already arisen;
the light of fire practices it,
and the Bàdào is cut off.
Though Heaven is vast,
it naturally has its divisions and principles,
displaying the writings to common people
so they may discuss them together.
What should belong to the superior belongs to the superior;
what should belong to the middle belongs to the middle;
what should belong to the inferior belongs to the inferior;
what should be shared by all is shared.
Why not look at its sincerity and truth [□□],
which is comparable to speaking with Heaven."
"Excellent, excellent!
The Qì of the times is balanced."
"How does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Seeing that Heaven has personally sent the Tiānshī down to speak,
I know that the Qì of Heaven is balanced."
"Excellent, excellent!
You have grasped the meaning."
"I wish to ask about one or two more matters
and dare not say much more."
"Go ahead and speak of them."
"From now on,
where should one seek the Dào?"
"Seek it in a quiet room;
do not distance yourself from your parents or leave your wife and children.
Do it gradually
until deviant leakage stops;
if there is no good within and there is deviant leakage,
there is nothing to be gained,
and on the contrary, one will die early.
Let each examine the truth
and act so as not to betray Heaven.
People can be deceived,"
Heaven cannot be deceived,
so do not worry about people doing wrong.
Let each person govern themselves by this.
Those who dare not follow the *Dào*
are indeed evil people,
those who wish to deceive and act falsely.
Judging by this,
not one in ten thousand will be missed.
If students are like this,
treachery and craftiness will be extinguished,
and good people and evil people can be clearly seen.
This is titled the *Huángtiān Jiǎnshì Shū*,
at the highest level, one can transcend the world,
at the middle level, one can become an assistant to emperors and kings,
and for the lowly and ignorant who are stubborn,
they can become cautious children among the common people.
*Zhēnrén*, value this knowledge highly."
"Yes, yes."
"I wish to hear how one who is flawed and narrow can attain the *Dào* and depart?"
"Indeed,
once the *Dào* is completed, one simply departs.
If the *Dào* is not yet completed,
daily attend to your father and mother,
protect your wife and children,
gradually, day by day,
act with clarity and stillness,
and then you will naturally know its meaning.
Let the worthy ones together contemplate these words."
"Yes, yes."

To the right is the *Tiānshàng Jiǎnshì Wén* for flourishing the *Dào* and severing wickedness, for abandoning hegemony and continuing life; people spontaneously change their hearts, treachery and craftiness vanish, they attend to their parents and protect their wives and children.
"I beg to ask the Master of the *Huángtiān Shàngdòng Jí*,
since the Master has been merciful to pity this ignorant and unworthy student
and has spoken of the affairs of Heaven,
it is truly beyond what this minor person would dare to hope for.
Since I have already received this
and the path has been opened
to allow me to know of Heavenly affairs,
I wish to hear what all is pleasing to Heaven
and what is forbidden,
that I might receive its precepts.
I will truly contemplate their meaning day and night
and dare not violate them,
in order to show them to later generations."
"Excellent is your question;
you have grasped the essential meaning.
*Zhēnrén*, sit calmly;
I shall speak of the *Dào* for you;
it can be passed down for ten thousand generations
without ever passing away."
"Yes, yes.
I receive your command with great gratitude."
"Do not give thanks.
You ask these questions for the sake of Heaven and Earth,
and I speak on behalf of Heaven;
this is not your private matter;
both of us are engaged in public business;
why is there any need for thanks?"
"I wish not to give thanks,
yet I fear that treating the *Dào* and its affairs lightly would distress the Master,
but giving thanks might also violate taboos or seem lacking in humility."
"I only fear that as the writing increases and the words become many,
it will become difficult to understand;
therefore I stopped the *Zhēnrén* from speaking.
Words
are the handle of the *Dào*,
the source from which writing arises;
do not be distressed,
I will now distinguish them for you."
"Yes, yes."
"Now in Heaven, the *Shànghuáng* and the *Dòngpíng Qì* have both reached a peak of flourishing,
the *yáng* days are bright and clear,
evil *qì* has ceased and rested,
correct *qì* then proceeds,
that which is decaying vanishes,
and the *Dào* and *Dé* are *yáng*."
"Heaven strictly forbids and cuts off the burning of mountains, forests, and groves;
why is this?
I wish to hear of it."
"Indeed,
mountains
are *Tàiyáng*,
the nexus of the land,
and its ruler.
Among those that spread roots,
trees are their elders,
they too are rulers,
and they are its *yáng*.
Fire is also the ruler and elder of the *Wǔxíng*,
and it too is its *yáng*.
When three rulers and three *yáng*s
meet, they conversely cause each other to decay.
For this reason, Heaven commands a strict prohibition on burning mountains, forests, and groves;
if trees are not burned, then *yīn* is within.
*Yīn* is called the Mother,
therefore it supports from below."
"Why does Heaven cause *Zǐ*, *Chǒu*, and *Yín* to be the first to manifest and flourish in abundance?
When they flourish, Fire becomes King;
when Fire is King, the sun becomes even brighter;
when *Bǐng* and *Dīng* flourish,
*Sì* and *Wǔ* are pleased;
why is this?
I wish to hear of it."
"This is the pattern of Heaven,
its nature.
When the Mother is abundant and King,
then the Son is Minister.
When the Son is Minister,
then one receives *qì* for a long time and attains longevity,
therefore Heaven brings it to a halt.
When *yáng* is abundant, then *yīn* treachery vanishes daily;
when *yáng* decays, then *yīn* treachery rises daily.
Thus, the treacherous and crafty always rise at night;
this is the great proof that when *yáng* decays, treachery arises.
Therefore Heaven wishes to eliminate treachery,
and so forbids it;
this is the natural method.
It is so in Heaven,
and it is so on Earth."
"Excellent, excellent!
I beg to ask, why is it that when the three *yáng*s meet, it results in misfortune and decay?"
"Excellent is your question;
you have grasped the meaning.
Now, the three *yáng*s correspond to Heaven *yáng*, Earth *yáng*, and Human *yáng*.
When all three are purely *yáng*,
there is not a single *yīn*;
when all three are purely rulers,
there is not a single minister;
when all three are purely male,
there is not a single female;
this is called the path of extinction,
the way of having no descendants.
They dare not further transmit their kind,
nor can they further generate one another,
therefore it is unlucky.
This is what is called having Heaven but no Earth,
having a sun but no moon,
having an above but no below,
having an exterior but no interior;
Heaven names this the *Lìbài zhī Jì*,
therefore it loathes and forbids it."
"Excellent!
This ignorant student has asked about this,
and I fear it greatly."
"That you know to fear it
is the root of life;
not knowing to fear it
is the gate of misfortune."
"Yes, yes."
"May I ask if it is permissible to burn the grass of the lower fields?"
"Heaven does not forbid burning it.
It should be burned."
"For what reason alone should it be burned?
I wish to hear of it."
"Indeed.
Grass
is the *Yīn* of wood
and corresponds to *Yǐ*.
Wood
corresponds to *Jiǎ*.
*Jiǎ*
is *Yáng*,
belonging to the same category as wood,
and thus they correspond.
*Yǐ*
is *Yīn*,
belonging to the same category as grass,
and thus it corresponds to *Yǐ*.
*Yǐ* fears metal,
and metal harms wood.
If wood is harmed, then *Yáng* declines;
if *Yáng* declines, then falsity and treachery arise;
therefore it should be burned.
Furthermore, Heaven says
that *Yǐ* is also *Yīn*,
grass is also *Yīn*,
and the lower fields are also the *Yīn* of the earth.
When these three *Yīn* come together,
they conversely produce treachery together.
Therefore, when *Xuánwǔ* resides in the center of the *Yīn* of the North Pole,
the extreme of *Yīn* conversely generates *Yáng*.
Fire
is *Yáng*.
When *Yīn* obtains *Yáng*, it is harmonious and auspicious,
giving rise to good affairs.
Therefore, Heaven instructs
to burn the grass of the lower fields to please the *Yīn*
and to raise up the *Yáng*;
for this reason it is burned.
It is the same in Heaven.
*Jiǎ*
is the wood of Heaven.
*Yǐ*
is the grass of Heaven.
What are *Yín* and *Mǎo*?
Indeed, *Yín* is also *Yáng*,
the wood of the earth.
*Mǎo*
is *Yīn*,
the grass of the earth.
These four matters all travel eastward.
But the *Yáng* is called 'wood'
and the *Yīn* is called 'grass';
this is the law of nature
and the scripture of Heaven.
I dare not deceive the *Zhēnrén*.
You resolve doubts by asking questions for Heaven;
I explain matters for Heaven.
We two share a duty
to jointly manage *Yīn* and *Yáng*,
to remove the ailments of Heaven and Earth,
so that the *Dìwáng* do not suffer in distress,
and the twelve thousand things each find their proper place,
none failing to rejoice and emerge to be seen,
with no one harboring grievances or knots."
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Indeed,
the *Zhēnrén* can be said to know the *Dào*."
"I dare not, I dare not."
"Indeed,
for one who studies and asks about the *Dào*,
what need is there for thanks?"
"Yes, yes."
"Bind it to your heart and mind,
and never let it leave you."
"Excellent, excellent!
Through study and questioning, the proper calculation has been obtained."
"Now that the benevolent and balanced *Qì* of Heaven has arrived,
there is a constant fear that the people may intentionally violate the seasonal ordinances and cause harm.
Now the various gods of Heaven are jointly recording those who are fond of killing and wounding,
the sons of hunting, shooting, and fishing,
who do not follow the Way of Heaven and do not do good.
Of those who are habitually fond of killing and wounding,
Heaven greatly blames them,
Earth greatly loathes them,
and the host of gods greatly condemns them.
There is fear now that the common people's accumulated ignorance
can no longer be restrained,
and they will collectively pollute and disorder the *Dònghuáng* balanced *Qì*.
Therefore, in this great urgency of Heaven today,
the various gods of the departments jointly record them;
daily following their conduct,
they jointly record even the smallest matters to examine them.
Every three years, including the intercalary month, there is a mid-term examination;
every five years, there is a grand examination.
Those whose transgressions are heavy shall be prosecuted;
for those with small transgressions, years are subtracted and their lifespan-counts are snatched away.
Every three generations there is a major correction;
every five generations there is an annihilation.
Therefore, today Heaven has gathered documents of the three paths of conduct,
and the host of gods jointly records transgressions
to cut off the fondness for killing, wounding, and punishments
and to raise up joy.
It is the same on earth.
May the *Zhēnrén* fortunately do good
and constantly desire to have virtue toward *Huángtiān*,
while pitying the distress and suffering of the *Dìwáng*.
That the seasonal *Qì* is not in harmony
is truly due to the fault of people being fond of killing and wounding,
hunting, shooting, and fishing,
jointly promoting punishments,
and constantly possessing intentions that collectively oppose Heaven and Earth.
This has caused a long period of deviation, disorder, and disharmony,
such that the *Dìwáng*, past and present,
have suffered distress therein;
this is a heavy transgression.
If the *Zhēnrén* fortunately desires to always have merit toward Heaven
and have kindness toward the *Dìwáng*,
know that Heaven is currently accumulating a loathing for this sickness.
The host of gods has instructed me with these words;
therefore, I now entrust this text to the *Zhēnrén*,
to return it to a virtuous ruler
and show it to the world.
When people obtain this text, let each deeply reflect,
ponder their faults and errors,
and contemplate what the text says about Heaven.
Now that the auspicious and balanced *Qì* has arrived together,
it does not delight in people being envious or thievish.
I know Heaven has these words;
I now dare not fail to pass them down the path.
If I do not speak, I fear I would be considered envious or thievish,
and the harm would be upon my own person;
I dare not commit such an offense.
Therefore, I report these matters;
let all *Zhēnrén* be cautious.
If a *Zhēnrén* does not speak,
the harm will be upon your person;
if it is shown to ordinary people
and an ignorant person wishes to violate it,
the harm will be upon their own person,
and Heaven will no longer place excessive blame on the *Zhēnrén*.
From now on,
Heaven shall raise up and employ the host of gods
to carry out examinations and governance of the people.
In Heaven, documents of the three paths are also gathered and circulated to record transgressions;
the gods also use documents of the three paths to record transgressions;
therefore, humans also use documents of the three paths to record transgressions.
Thus, humans take their patterns from Heaven,
and Heaven takes its patterns from humans.
Heaven, Earth, and humans have their affairs,
patterned after the numinous spirits,
and also patterned after the methods of those affairs in their actions.
Therefore, when the refined *Qì* of ghosts and gods admonishes, people also admonish;
they always arise simultaneously with Heaven, Earth, and humans.
For this reason, the spirits act in response to the *Qì* of Heaven;
refined things arise in response to the *Qì* of the Earth;
and ghosts contend in response to human governance.
These three
are the rapid messengers of the central harmony of Heaven and Earth;
they move and act following the *shénqì*;
they come and go in response to the seasons;
they penetrate through without any gap,
and their coming and going are in places difficult to know.
Therefore, the current transmission and governance of the Way of Heaven
is different from that of remote antiquity.
To use the present to divine the ancient mostly fails to hit the mark;
to use the ancient to divine the present no longer corresponds.
Thus, ancient texts have withered and are difficult to use again;
using them does not yield consistent hits.
Furthermore, there is a place where the truly authentic texts are gathered.
Therefore, Heaven says
to examine and compare before and after, combining the three,
taking what is central and good to clarify matters and harmonize intentions.
Thereafter, the Way of Heaven will be corrected,
the Way of the King will be complete,
all heterodoxy and evil will depart,
the *Dìwáng* will have great joy,
and there will be no incidents,
as people themselves act cautiously to obtain the intent of Heaven.
Does the *Zhēnrén* know the weight of this matter?"
"Yes, yes."
"Excellent!
You know its intent."

To the right: Regarding Heaven's prohibition of fire so as to promote life, the cessation of punishments, injuries, and killings, and the halting of hunting, shooting, and trapping which do not follow the seasonal *Qì* of Heaven and are loathed by Heaven; recorded as being currently known as the text of the *Chìchū* receiving the tallies and starting anew.
"I, a lowly and ignorant student, wish to ask a question.
Today, the Tiāndào should be complete,
with nothing it does not possess and nothing it does not encompass.
Looking toward the heavens,
why is it that at this time everything is meant to be born, yet punishments and executions are so urgent?"
"Excellent is your difficult question!
You have grasped the essence.
I have always been very fond of your words.
Your words
always stimulate my thoughts
and cause my Dào to flourish.
If you were not able to ask such difficult questions,
who else would ask them?
Therefore, the Tiāndào has long been severed and closed, not flowing through,
and Heaven suffers greatly from this.
I have long been despondent,
wishing to speak but having no one to speak with.
Consequently, the Tiāndào has lost its proper order for a long time.
Year after year,
until now.
The celestial cycle gives birth to a sage and causes him to speak,
so that those without knowledge may completely remove their ailments.
Thus, Heaven has caused a Zhēnrén to come of his own accord
to meet with me,
so that for once the complete words of Heaven may be spoken.
Your questions always uniquely and deeply grasp the intent of Heaven.
Sit peacefully,
and I shall explain it all to you.
I would prefer not to speak,
but I fear the majesty of Heaven.
Therefore, having received your question,
I wish to speak immediately,
with nothing to hide.
Does the Zhēnrén also know of this?"
"Yes, indeed."
"In that case,
you are enlightened.
Now, as for why the heavens desire everything to be born and grow,
yet punishments and injuries are urgent:
the Tiāndào always possesses three graded Qì.
The first loves life
and is called Yáng.
The second loves completion
and is called Hé.
The third loves killing
and is called Yīn.
Thus, Heaven presides over the name of giving life;
Man presides over the nurturing and completion of it;
completion is named killing,
for it kills and then stores away.
Heaven, Earth, and Man, these three share the same merit,
and their affairs are interconnected.
Without Yáng, there is no birth;
without Hé, there is no completion;
without Yīn, there is no killing.
These three require each other to form one family,
together completing the twelve thousand things.
Yet the Tiāndào has its beginning, end, and middle.
Now,
since the initial rising of the Tiāndào,
the Great Cycle has returned,
coming to belong to Man and to Yáng.
Yáng loves life and dislikes killing.
That which lives requires joy
to harmonize the heart into one and give life to one another.
But if there is the Qì of killing within, it causes injury immediately,
and they cannot give life to or complete one another.
If you wish to know the truth of this,
compare it to a child in the womb;
it cannot suffer even a small harm,
or it will immediately be injured and die.
Once dead, it does not live again,
and one person is lost.
If such injuries continue without ceasing,
then lineages will be extinguished without future generations,
and the succession of a family will be cut off.
Therefore, there is a great urgency regarding punishments and killings.
The Tiāndào is not always like this.
It is urgent now,
so I shall once again clearly distinguish it for the Zhēnrén,
to make the people of this lower antiquity greatly realize the Tiāndào.
Now, there is no desire for killing to resolve matters;
that is why I speak so clearly for the Zhēnrén.
Ordinary people follow me,
but they merely practice literary compositions without substance and craft clever words.
Therefore, I shall again set forth the evidence of Heaven's punishments.
Now, Jiǎzǐ
is the rectification of Heaven;
the days begin to return to their source at the Winter Solstice.
Yǐchǒu
is the rectification of Earth;
things begin to spread their roots.
Bǐngyín
is the rectification of Man;
at dawn, people begin to rise,
opening their doors to attend to their duties.
These three
are the initial beginnings of the birth of Heaven, Earth, and Man,
the very root of all things.
The initial birth belongs to Yáng;
Yáng is the original Qì of Heaven, Earth, and Man.
Thus, Qián, Kǎn, Gèn, and Zhèn
are on the northeastern face.
The Hé among them is between Kǎn and Gèn,
where Yīn and Yáng combine to give life in the center.
Therefore, for all who are pregnant,
the head is below and the feet are above;
the fetus dwells in the middle of the belly,
slightly below the point of Hé.
When Yáng combines, life is the first to emerge,
sending out its form and Qì
to be cast into other directions.
This governs the place where the three Qì of Heaven, Earth, and Man are first born,
the renewal of all things;
throughout the heights and depths, the Qì of punishment and killing must not dwell within.
If the Qì of Virtue and the Qì of Yáng are established,
then the ten thousand things will successfully come to life;
if there is baleful Qì within, they will be injured immediately.
Thus, punishments must be removed and discarded.
Now, the Tiāndào is renewing its Great Cycle,
and pure Yáng governs Heaven and Earth from above to below;
therefore, punishments and executions are urgently cut off.
Heaven is called Shén;
Yáng is also called Shén.
Thus, today Heaven causes the Shén to govern humanity.
Does the Zhēnrén wish to know if my writings correspond with Heaven?
From now on,
those who violate my writings
or who are fond of punishments and killings
will be examined by Heaven.
Humans will also press them more urgently,
and the Shén will also examine them.
Heaven above and Earth below are in different places but share the same plan;
though ghosts and Shén do not share a home with humans,
they also share the same plan.
This means the Píngqì of Heaven is about to arrive.
The initial Qì of Heaven begins anew in the heavens;
the initial Qì of Earth begins anew beneath the earth;
the initial Qì of Man begins anew in the center.
These three Qì are all beginning to be born at once.
They do not wish to see the baleful Qì of punishment and evil,
but all wish to see the Qì of joy.
Therefore, from now on,
Heaven and Earth take joy in severing punishments.
Does the Zhēnrén know this?"
"Yes, indeed.
I, an ignorant student, was dim-witted;
I thought that Heaven acted urgently because it loathed the evil of men,
and thus forbade punishments and killings.
I did not realize it was the Qì of Heaven, Earth, and Man in gestation,
the original source of the new beginning.
Hearing the Tiānshī explain it,
I am greatly awed and terrified."
"Since you know awe and terror,
you may be called awakened,
for you know the intent of the Tiāndào.
Excellent!
Be sensible and cautious toward this text;
be careful not to sever it, lest you bring harm to yourself."
"Yes, indeed;
I would not dare, I would not dare."
"Go now and value it.
Whenever people study,
each acts for their own sake,
striving to follow the Tiāndào."
"Yes, indeed."
"Bring forth these celestial prohibitions and do not hide them."
"Yes, indeed."
"I wish to ask, why is it that the Tiāndào precisely now takes this as the Great Cycle
and the Original Beginning,
and thus establishes a great number of examined and corrected texts?"
"Excellent is your difficult question!
It greatly grasps the heart and mind of Heaven.
Indeed, now
the five Yáng are ascending,
and it is the beginning of the five Fires.
The highest of the Fires
ascends to become Heaven,
and becomes the color of the sun and moon.
The red of fire is the same color as Heaven.
Heaven's color is red,
and fire is also red;
that which is red is called Shén.
Heaven and the Shén are always prosperous,
for they possess the origin of all things.
For this reason, the eleventh month is the Rectification of Heaven,
and it is the same in the heavens.
Therefore, the Qì of things is red;
as for redness, the sun begins to return.
Its initial nine Qì belong to Jiǎzǐ,
which is the senior head of the Liùjiǎ.
Jiǎ is the essence
and the heart of all affairs;
thus, Jiǎ emerges first from Zǐ.
Therefore, it emerges above as the Xīnxīng.
Thus, the essence and spirit of fire
constitute the human heart.
The human heart is divine and sagely;
the divine and sagely human heart is the most noble, true, and good.
Therefore, the divine and sagely human heart is capable of creating all things."
It serves as the original head of the beginning.
Therefore, the law of the divine and sagely
arises entirely from the heart
and explains everything.
Thus, that which is the peak of redness
is Heaven,
is the Sun,
and is the heart.
Heaven, the Sun, and the heart are always bright
and illuminate and observe everything.
Therefore, from this time forward,
for those who practice this Way,
all things wicked and evil shall be utterly eliminated.
Now, the birth of Yáng
occurs within the dark and mysterious.
For this reason, Yáng Qì arises in the north,
emerges in the east,
flourishes in the south,
and declines and vanishes in the west;
such is the law of Heaven's action."
"How wonderful!
I wish to hear why the birth of Yáng in the present
is precisely within the dark and mysterious?"
"All living things return to their root;
only when Yīn and Yáng combine can they produce life.
Therefore, those who are to be born
all return to their very beginning.
Before Heaven and Earth were divided,
at the time of the first arising,
there was no above or below, no sun, moon, or the three luminaries;
above and below were cavernous and dark,
and in that cavernous darkness, there were no distinctions or patterns.
Although there were no distinctions,
within it there were naturally above and below, left and right, exterior and interior, Yīn and Yáng,
all held together
without being separated.
Just as Yīn and Yáng hold each other and begin to produce life together.
Their bestowal is vast and obscure,
and also without distinction.
Once they have emerged into life,
only then are the head and feet complete.
Thus we know the beginning of the initial birth of Yīn and Yáng is like this.
Therefore, when people now are about to transform and bestow life,
they all go to dark, mysterious, and quiet places,
for Heaven causes them not to forget their root.
When humans first received the laws of Heaven and Earth,
that was their precedence;
therefore, Heaven causes them not to forget it."
"Wonderful, wonderful!
Having seen the words of the Huáng Tiān Shī,
I now understand the distinctions and patterns."
"You may be said to be easy to enlighten."
"May I ask why Yáng and Fire alone are paired?"
"Those that circulate Qì each have their own groupings;
it is not only fire.
Metal and Fire are the primary pairing,
being the leaders of the Chì Dì.
Does not the *Tiān Cè Shū* say:
'Bǐngwǔ and Dīngsì are the ancestral beginning'?
A beginning
is the precedence,
the head;
therefore the book speaks of the ancestral beginning.
The beginning of all things
arises from the Red Heart.
The Heart penetrates and illuminates to know affairs;
Yáng begins within Yīn,
and also penetrates and illuminates.
Therefore, Water
is dark on the outside but bright on the inside, penetrating and illuminating,
because it contains Yáng essence within.
Thus Yáng first arises in the north,
and Yīn first arises in the south.
In the eleventh month, the ground below is warm;
in the fifth month, the ground below is cold."
"Since Yīn and Yáng first arise,
why do they not arise in the heavens but precisely within the earth?"
"Wonderful
is your difficult question.
However, the Earth is the mother;
the father bestows upon the mother,
therefore it is within Yīn.
The bestowal of Yáng essence
likewise originates from Heaven.
Yáng,
in its initial transformation of Qì, is subtle and difficult to see;
it enters into Yīn to take form,
and only then does it become manifest and visible.
Therefore, one records it within Yīn
and does not record it in Yáng."
"Now when it rains or snows,
these are likewise the ways of bestowal and transformation;
one speaks of them because they are visible.
Yáng bestows essence subtly—
is it then invisible?"
"Wonderful are your words,
but it is difficult to grasp the meaning.
I wish to explain it clearly for the Zhēnrén.
I fear that if the Heavenly Way were fully revealed,
for that reason I would not speak of it to you.
However, I fear the Zhēnrén would feel resentment.
To be a teacher
or a superior to men is difficult.
Please sit peacefully;
I shall explain it slightly for you.
When Heaven creates rain and snow and is about to act,
it is at first but the breathing of Qì;
when Yīn and Yáng intersect and obtain each other, they then bestow.
It can be seen at this time:
the Heavenly Qì descends,
the Earthly Qì ascends,
and they combine their bestowal.
Therefore, rain and snow have form and are visible."
"May I ask:
now there are times when mountains crumble or clouds rise,
which are all visible;
yet it is said they cannot be seen—
why is this?
I wished not to ask,
but I suffer from feeling dejected;
therefore I now ask fully.
Though it may be that as a disciple I am not humble,
without asking there is no way to know;
I must ask
so that there may be no doubts."
"Very well.
I shall explain it slightly for you,
but it cannot be fully exhausted.
Now, clouds and rain or the crumbling of mountains—
these are the great anger of Yīn,
which cannot restrain itself and harms Yáng.
These are transformations into ominous events,
not beneficial transformations.
They cause harm to the Way of transformation;
it is a failing of Yīn,
a wounding by Yīn.
Let the Zhēnrén ask no further,
for the Heavenly Way cannot be scrutinized and spoken of in its entirety.
Ponder its meaning yourself."
"Yes, yes."
"You may go."
The Zhēnrén bowed twice and said,
“I respectfully ask the Tiānshī about the Dào.
As the Qì of Tàipíng arrives,
who is suitable for the Dào?
Who is not suitable for the Dào?”
“Excellent
is your question.
Regarding the Dào and people,
it is like wind and rain;
those who practice it find it good,
those who do not practice it simply stop.
One who loves to practice it
is the right person.
One who does not love to practice it
is not the right person.
One who practices without effort
and finds it easy to open and penetrate
is the right person.
If there is no opening or penetration,
and after a whole day there is no success,
then that is not the right person.
If practicing it leads to good fortune
and not practicing it leads to misfortune,
that is the right person.
If one does not practice it
and yet remains naturally fortunate and good,
suffering no illness or pain,
but after beginning to practice it,
on the contrary, suffers illness and pain,
then that is not the right person.
Furthermore, when ordinary people nourish themselves,
they must examine matters in detail.
The Dào
is the tally of the upright person.
Illness and ghostly entities
are the pathways of depravity and evil,
the bandits who rob and kill good people.
Some, seeing a person about to enter the correct Dào,
will conversely become angry with them
and struggle against them.
For such a person, the correct Dào
instead brings misfortune and does not produce good;
they are instead at peace among their own kind.
One must be careful and detailed in refining oneself;
attaining the Dào brings good fortune,
while losing the Dào brings misfortune.
The mandate of life and death
cannot be easily changed by oneself,
so one must be careful and detailed.”
“Excellent, excellent!
This humble disciple now understands.”
“Indeed.
Since the Zhēnrén has asked about doubtful matters,
I shall tell the Zhēnrén the essential words of Heaven.
The reason my Dào can nourish for a long time is that
if a person delights in Dào, delights in Dé, and delights in Rén,
is indifferent to worldly affairs,
and solely desires life,
the Dào is truly long-lasting in nourishing and protecting these two types of people.
For those below this level,
my Dào does not nourish them for long.”
“Why is that?
The Dào of humanity covers everything;
why does it only favor these three types of people
and not favor the rest?”
“Indeed.
Excellent is your challenging question;
you have grasped the intent.
When the Great Dào emerges,
all people receive its grace,
extending even to the plants and trees.
None are not transformed into goodness;
all attain what they need
and each completes their natural lifespan.”
“But as for those without Dào and Dé and who are not Rén,
they cannot be nourished for long.
Why is that?”
“Indeed,
it is simply because they do not love Dào, Dé, and Rén.”
“As for those who love Dào, Dé, and Rén,
why is it that they alone can be nourished for long?
I wish to hear the reason.”
“Indeed,
you are one who understands the matters of life!
Your question touches on the ultimate secret.
Listen carefully;
I shall explain its meaning to you in detail.”
“Yes, yes.”
“Indeed,
those who love Dào, Dé, and Rén—
these three types of people all have mandates from the Three Systems.
One who delights in and loves the Dào
has a mandate belonging to Heaven.
One who delights in and loves Dé and its cultivation
has a mandate belonging to Earth.
One who delights in and loves Rén has a mandate belonging to Humanity.
These three types of people
correspond to the systems of Yīnyáng and Zhōnghé.
They all have names on the registers;
therefore, the various gods in Heaven
say that my texts can nourish them.
If one's conduct is not like this,
they also have no name on the registers;
therefore, my texts cannot nourish them for long.
Now that the Qì of Tàipíng has arrived,
there is no room for treachery or selfishness;
thus, treacherous and evil people are not nourished for long.
This is unlike the previous times of internal chaos,
when evil people could be encompassed and nourished.”
“I wish to hear the full explanation.”
“Indeed.
When treacherous and evil Qì emerges,
living conditions conversely can nourish treacherous and evil people for a long time;
however, they cannot nourish good people for long.
This is because the harms are many
and the good are few.
It is comparable to when great cold arrives and heat Qì declines.
Now that the correct Qì has arrived,
it cannot nourish treacherous and evil people for long.
This is comparable to when Yángqì arrives and Yīnqì vanishes.
When the Tàiyáng supreme Red Qì arrives,
it is the kingly essence of Fire.
The king of Fire
is the light above that becomes the Sun.
The Sun
illuminates and examines treacherous and evil people;
thus it is said that they cannot do wrong,
and thus evil people are not tolerated.
Furthermore, the Dào governs birth,
Dé governs nourishment,
and Rén governs the use of the heart-mind and thus love.
Spring brings birth,
Summer brings nourishment,
and people use their heart-minds to manage
and nourish the growth of the myriad things.
Therefore, what Tàiyáng births and nourishes for growth
involves the most arduous use of the heart-mind.
This is what it means.”
“Excellent, excellent!
This humble disciple has heard your command once more!”
“Indeed.
Sit peacefully,
and I shall further refine the explanation for you.”
“Yes, yes.”
“First: learning the Dào.
The great measure lies with Heaven,
the middle measure lies with the spirits,
and the small measure lies with people.
Second: learning Dé.
The great measure lies with Heaven,
the middle measure lies with the spirits,
and the small measure lies with people.
Third: learning Rén.
The great measure lies with Heaven,
the middle measure lies with the spirits,
and the small measure lies with people.
Fourth: learning for office.
The great measure lies with Heaven,
the middle measure lies with the spirits,
and the small measure lies with people.
Fifth: liking to accumulate wealth and property.
The great abundance lies with Heaven,
the middle abundance lies with the spirits,
and the small abundance lies with people.
Now, regarding these five matters,
whether great, middle, or small in measure,
they all result from efforts that return the mandate to Heaven,
return Dé to Earth,
and return Rén to humanity.
If you maintain these three matters to cultivate yourself,
with a worthy heart and good intentions,
contemplating and reflecting upon them,
the self can then be perfected.
By accumulating and gathering them,
spirit will naturally arise.
By guarding and nourishing them,
the Dào will naturally be completed.
By delighting in and loving them,
the self will naturally flourish.
The Dào of Heaven has no favorites or outcasts;
it is entrusted to good people.
For this reason, Heaven itself exerts effort to practice the Dào,
completing one cycle every day.
The reason it completes a cycle is that
when all things are born,
they are all born by modeling themselves on the Liùjiǎ, the Wǔxíng, and the four seasons.
If one Qì does not arrive,
some things will be incomplete,
and thus their life will be insufficient and imbalanced.
If those who are lords, superiors, or parents
are imbalanced, it is a great transgression.
Therefore, Heaven completes one cycle daily
and personally oversees its movement.
The reason it personally oversees its movement is this:
for example, the branch Zǐ is Shuǐ.
If there is only Shuǐ Qì but it has not completed the cycle,
then the Qì of the Wǔxíng is insufficient,
and the Qì of the four seasons is not complete;
therefore, Heaven moves to oversee it.
Jiǎ is added above it,”
There is the Wood Phase (Mù Xíng),
and there is the Spring Breath (Chūn Qì).
When Bǐng is added above it,
there is the Fire Phase (Huǒ Xíng),
and there is the Summer Breath (Xià Qì).
When Wù is added above it,
there is the Earth Phase (Tǔ Xíng),
and there is the breath of the center of the four seasons.
When Gēng is added above it,
there is the Metal Phase (Jīn Xíng),
and there is the Autumn Breath (Qiū Qì).
When Rén is added above it,
there is the Water Phase (Shuǐ Xíng),
and there is the Winter Breath (Dōng Qì).
When the five bodies are complete
and the four breaths are manifest,
then all things attain life.
When Heaven and Earth distribute transformations evenly,
and the noble and humble, the great and small, are all as one,
then there are no litigants;
thus, one can be the ruler and the parent of the people.
Those who practice the Way (Dào), Virtue (Dé), and Benevolence (Rén)
should model themselves on this;
thus they attain the Will of Heaven (Tiān Yì).
One must not act recklessly or treat oneself lightly.
The Way of Heaven (Tiān Dào) acts as a model in this way,
how much more so for humans?
Therefore, the superior scholar (Shàngshì) models themselves on Heaven—
is that not their Way (Dào)!
The middle scholar (Zhōngshì) models themselves on Earth—
is that not their Virtue (Dé)!
The inferior scholar (Xiàshì) models themselves on humans—
is that not their Benevolence (Rén)!
Those who fall below this level
do not belong to the rank of humanity;
therefore, they share a lack of constant life with birds, beasts, grasses, and trees.
When the Perfected Person (Zhēnrén) obtains my writings,
they should deeply contemplate the essential meaning.
By following it without fail,
they achieve harmony and work together with Heaven.
Those who oppose my writings
are the resentment of Heaven and Earth;
I also cannot tolerate them.
What my writings abhor
is exactly this.
Let the Perfected Person (Zhēnrén) be cautious with this,
entrust it to superior scholars (Shàngshì),
return it to the local officials (Xiànguān),
and show it to ordinary people.
From now on,
Heaven is different from antiquity."
"Excellent, excellent!"
To the right is the Formula for Distinguishing the Appropriate and Inappropriate from the Tàipíng (Great Peace) Writings.
May I ask about not eating yet being full,
attaining great longevity,
even to the point of eternal existence?
This is the way to enrich the state and preserve the people.
Regarding the desire not to eat,
one must first place the methods for guiding life at the forefront to retain the breath (qì).
After consuming the medicine of breath (qì),
after three days there is slight hunger;
after seven days, minor hunger;
beyond ten days,
this is a minor achievement, let there be no doubt.
One has already left death and approached life.
After consuming the medicine of breath (qì),
for all foods that are tangible objects, hard and difficult to digest,
take one meal as the limit.
When consuming intangible things,
moderation and small amounts are good.
After one hundred days, one can cease eating;
this is called the Way of Inexhaustibility.
It is known as assisting the state in nourishing the people
and assisting Heaven and Earth as the master of sustenance.
Consuming little is auspicious;
consuming much is inauspicious.
Not eating at all is also inauspicious,
as the intestines and stomach will become blocked.
The method for clearing the intestines:
one meal is appropriate;
a second meal is an increase;
a third meal is inferior;
a fourth meal causes intestinal distension;
a fifth meal causes great hunger to arise;
a sixth meal is greatly inauspicious and evil.
A hundred illnesses arise from this,
and in years of great famine, one shall die.
After a thousand days of moderate eating,
the large and small intestines are all full,
and ultimately there is no waste material.
This causes all illnesses to be removed from a person,
their complexion becomes better,
and there are no prohibitions or precautions needed.
In ancient times, those who attained the Way (Dào),
and the elderly, all did so through not eating.
Rulers, ministers, and commoners can sufficiently stabilize their bodies and minds,
manage their duties;
the wealthy can sufficiently preserve their wealth,
and the poor can sufficiently sustain their bodies.
If a gentleman (Jūnzǐ) practices this,
they will rejoice in good years
and not perish in disastrous years.
It is said that humans have three lives (Sānmìng),
but they do not know it themselves;
eating three times a day sustains them.
If one does not eat in the morning, one life is cut off;
if one does not eat at noon, two lives are cut off;
if one does not eat in the evening, three are cut off.
If one stops eating for three days,
nine lives are cut off.
Having no hidden goods
and no treasures remaining
is due to hunger.
Great wickedness and evil arise;
all begin from this.
Use my Way (Dào),
and the myriad things will govern themselves.
In auspicious years, one can promote benefits;
in disastrous years, one can preserve the people.
One should always wrap the belt tightly to gather the intestines,
making it advantageous for walking.
Between Heaven and Earth,
all things each have their own spirit.
Brightness above belongs to Heaven,
as the stars,
through which safety and danger can be observed.
The nature of Heaven and Earth
naturally has its own standards and laws;
the measures of the *liùjiǎ*, the Five Elements (*wǔxíng*), and the four seasons
can be used to divine and uncover future events,
to provide salvation from decline and disorder,
and to prevent things before they happen.
When a minister sees the decline of his ruler or father
and saves them,
making them prosper once again,
this is a great merit.
If one deeply knows of their decline
but does not save them,
or even speaks perversely and departs,
it is called inciting calamity,
and the guilt cannot be removed.
Third case:
if a minister knows his ruler has faults,
and sees impending disaster but saves him,
so that he no longer suffers misfortune,
this is a great merit.
Knowing but not saving
is called inciting disaster,
and the guilt cannot be removed.
Fourth case:
knowing the ruler’s governance has lost its essential meaning
and disasters arise consecutively,
yet one helps to rectify it,
this is what is appropriate.
To be a minister who understands affairs,
knowing yet not saving,
the guilt cannot be removed.
Fifth case:
if a minister knows his ruler is young,
and his worthiness has not yet reached the level of affairs, yet one saves him
by assisting him in becoming knowledgeable,
this is what is appropriate.
Knowing but not assisting him in becoming worthy,
and instead saying he is inadequate,
is called being disloyal;
it weakens his superior,
and the guilt cannot be removed.
Sixth case:
if a minister knows his ruler is old
and has a heavenly term and worries for him,
seeking for him the assistance of great worthies from distant regions,
extraordinary strategies, and esoteric texts,
allowing the ruler to extend his years,
this is a great merit.
Knowing but being unable to do so,
and instead speaking of auspiciousness and misfortune,
one's error is great.
Seventh case:
for those below knowing those above are in danger,
have lost the principle,
or have become forgetful,
and together they save and rectify it,
this is considered a great merit.
Knowing but not saving,
excusing oneself to avoid it and departing,
is to be a person who is not compliant with loyalty and filial piety;
the guilt will reach their descendants.
Eighth case:
if parents are ill,
and one with the knowledge of divination or physiognomy
can exert all effort and essence
to find a way to save them;
knowing but not saving,
Heaven will impose a great punishment.
Ninth case:
when parents are old and their lives are nearly finished,
if a son knows the end of his parents' term is near,
and seeks for them worthy teachers and extraordinary methods
so they may become strong and robust,
this is what is appropriate for a filial son.
This is like eating the food of others
and returning the food to them,
and thus there is great merit.
Tenth case:
knowing a person's misfortune and decline
and that a great calamity is coming and saving them,
allowing them to rise again,
giving them marvelous methods and extraordinary strategies
along with esoteric texts and good deeds,
so they no longer have sorrow or suffering,
this is considered a great merit.
Knowing but not acting,
the guilt cannot be removed.
Now, for one who is a son,
to see his parents in mortal danger and abandon them,
dwelling in pleasure and avoiding bitterness,
this is simply the same as birds and beasts.
How could such a one govern the Three Powers (*sāncái*)
or succeed Heaven and Earth?
Therefore, the Sage (*shèngrén*) appears
to bestow teachings and warnings,
to encourage people to do good,
and to cut off misfortune and evil,
in order to save from the disasters of Heaven and Earth,
causing the Three Luminaries (*sānguāng*) and Five Elements (*wǔxíng*)
and the stars to follow their proper order;
is this merely empty words?
Now, Heaven above has fully issued these documents
to transform and remove various disasters
and to bring about goodness;
therefore, I personally instruct and command the Perfected One (*zhēnrén*) to release the book.
Now, Heaven above has taught me to speak grandly
without any concealment.
Now, Heaven and Earth are completing a great cycle and beginning anew;
disasters should naturally dissipate and vanish,
leaving no further trace of their kind.
Therefore, people are taught to collect and compare the good parts of ancient and modern writings
to make them the Scripture of the Ultimate Profundity (*Dòngjí Zhī Jīng*),
establishing goodness that cannot be changed again;
even sages and worthies cannot again match its phrasing.
For phrasing
is the language of Heaven, Earth, Yin (*yīn*), and Yang (*yáng*).
Thus, I instruct and warn the worthy rulers of men,
desiring to make them practice diligently to achieve Great Peace (*tàipíng*).
As for why it is said to be concealed and stored,
the worthy ruler obtains it and hides it in his heart,
applying it to all under Heaven,
nurturing the myriad things and achieving Great Peace (*tàipíng*).
When merit is attributed to the High Sovereign (*shàngdì*),
then it is more solid than stone chambers or deep caves.
Heaven produces good things
and they must return to a good place.
Just like pearls and jade,
they must be treasured by emperors and kings.
As for coarse and evil things,
the masses discard them.
How much more so when a person does good,
how could Heaven not love them?
How could emperors and kings not value them?
Now there is the Heaven of the Infinite above,
the Heaven of the Infinite in the middle,
the Heaven of the Infinite below,
and the Heaven of the Infinite that moves sideways.
Now it acts as the law;
furthermore, the *qì* of the three paths gathers for collective deliberation,
responding to the positions of Heaven, Earth, and Man.
Then Great Peace (*tàipíng*) arrives,
Heaven rejoices,
and then emperors and kings live long.
Its Way and divine spirits protect Heaven and Earth;
the good *qì* all responds accordingly.
Way and Virtue (*dàodé*) arrive daily,
evil and falsehood retreat,
and calamitous ministers and treacherous idlers are eliminated.
Mediocre ministers are all removed,
ten thousand types of goodness come naturally,
the Five Elements (*wǔxíng*) are in harmony,
and the four seasonal *qì* are timely and good.
The method of governance
arises from the root.
As for the root,
between Heaven and Earth, man resembles spirit.
Spirit resembles man,
and each having their own quarters,
gathering the good and evil of pavilions, districts, townships, and counties.
What is liked and what causes suffering
each have their root.
All matters are examined closely,
observing one another's shortcomings;
shortcomings and strengths, gains and losses,
are as clear as the sun and moon.
Therefore, the great teaching is for collective deliberation,
where the worthy and the unworthy together settle the matter.
Therefore, in the provinces, counties, townships, and villages of the world, collection boxes are set up,
inviting the myriad people each according to their talent to write,
speaking directly of suffering, benefits, harms, and whether things are feasible,
delivering their writings and casting them into the boxes.
The senior officials then compile them to present to the Son of Heaven,
to let him know the people's likes and dislikes, the worthy and unworthy, and the benefits and harms,
so they can be collectively deliberated upon and managed;
then the *qì* of Great Peace (*tàipíng*) will arrive,
bringing fortune to the ruler and the myriad people,
and the twelve thousand things will each find their proper place.
The Tiāndào has times of leisure and times of urgency;
human affairs are also thus,
having leisure and urgency.
When the Tiāndào is urgent,
then wind, rain, thunder, and lightning arrive without the passage of a single hour;
when the Way of Humanity has urgency,
one also hurries and runs, arriving without the passage of a single hour.
Those who are urgent respond to the laws of Heaven according to the time and thus submit to what is above;
a petition is submitted and returned to the original department,
and there are rewards and punishments.
Those who are leisurely must take eight months as one day to submit to what is above;
such is the law in Heaven.
Now, the laws of Yīnyáng are thus,
and the Way of Humanity is also thus.
Within the abdomen of every person,
each has a Tiānzǐ,
and within the five Qì, each has a king.
Heaven has five Qì,
and Earth has five positions.
One of the Qì governs action,
while the one who acts as king governs the upholding of correctness.
All matters reside within a person's abdomen,
which is itself named the Xīn.
The Xīn is the king of the five viscera,
the root and foundation of the Shén,
and the ultimate of the entire body.
It governs the upholding of goodness;
the Xīn does not delight in acting recklessly or admitting heterodoxy and evil within.
If a person can uphold goodness
and reside in Qīngjìng,
outwardly not recklessly seeking correctness,
they will inwardly and naturally meet with the king within the abdomen;
this is called the clarity of being able to look back and see one’s Xīn.
The Xīn is the king;
meeting it will surely extend one's life,
and all actions will be orderly.
Those who cannot see the king
are all heterodox;
they no longer communicate with the king,
and all their actions result in failure.
Furthermore, they will meet an early end.
Now the virtue of Tàiyáng is flourishing;
it desires to make all above Heaven and below Heaven,
limitless above
and boundless below,
extending sideways through the eight caverns, inside and out.
True spirits and true essence-light all emerge to assist the sovereign's rule,
and bring about the Qì of the Shànghuáng's Dòngpíng,
which has never been seen before.
Good people will have long lives,
the myriad things will no longer suffer premature death or personal grievances,
and heterodox spirits will all vanish;
under Heaven there will no longer be those who are violently oppressed or ill.
How could such things be heard?
Excellent is your question!
Heaven causes all heterodoxy, falsehood, and malevolence to be severed,
and allows true matters to emerge.
In all illustrations, each has its own spirit;
true matters have true spirits,
heterodox matters have heterodox spirits,
good matters have good spirits,
and evil matters have evil spirits.
Families that accumulate heterodoxy
will surely suffer heterodox harm later;
families that accumulate true texts and the true Dào
will surely have those who transcend the world later.
Therefore, truth and falsehood are each brought about by their respective essences.
Thus Heaven has auspiciousness and inauspiciousness;
auspiciousness brings auspicious spirits,
and inauspiciousness brings inauspicious spirits.
Earth also has auspiciousness and inauspiciousness;
auspiciousness brings auspicious spirits,
and inauspiciousness brings inauspicious spirits.
Now the Sānhuáng and Wǔdì each have relatives and brothers;
the Sānwáng and Wǔbà each likewise have relatives and brothers.
With slight differences,
each follows its own kind;
when the age flourishes, they are high;
when the age declines, they are low.
They are like day and night,
arising in succession;
from the opening of Yīnyáng
until now, they have not ceased.
The poor are Xiǎorén,
and the wealthy are Jūnzǐ;
they alternately serve and manage one another.
These are the relatives of Heaven and Earth.
If the myriad things do not flourish,
there are a few things among them that resemble this,
but in reality they are not.
Heaven has the Liùjiǎ, the four seasons, the five elements, the hard and soft, the female and male, and the first, second, and third months of the seasons;
they together form relatives and brothers and serve them with respect,
not losing their intent,
in order to transform all under Heaven,
causing it to be a master of goodness.
Rén, Yì, Lǐ, Zhì, Wén, and Wǔ alternately act as relatives and brothers.
As for Dào and Dào acting as relatives and brothers,
all Dào then unite greatly into one,
alternately confirming and producing one another.
Today, if one's self has attained the Dào,
then all people of the Dào will come;
relatives and like-minded people unite as one family,
all harboring good intentions.
All, whether great or small, no longer harm one another;
disasters all depart and there are no calamities.
If sovereigns practice this,
all under Heaven will flourish and prosper.
They rule through non-action with dangling robes and folded hands,
transcending the world with long life.
If officials and commoners practice this,
their principles will become clearer daily.
Every Dào will emerge,
and none will fail to produce light.
Dào and Dào act as relatives, transmitting and practicing together.
Therefore, with the Dào one summons the Dào,
using the Dào to seek the Dào,
then one takes the Dào as relative and brother.
Exalting transformation in this manner,
then all under Heaven will love life and hate killing.
How could there be any who lack the Dào?
As for Dé and Dé acting as relatives and brothers,
today if one's self upholds Great Dé,
taking Dé as one's intent.
All people of Dé will practice humility in serving one another,
and people of Dé throughout the world will all emerge.
Taking this as the law,
one sits peacefully without concern.
If sovereigns practice this,
their state will be wealthy;
if officials and commoners practice this,
nothing will be unmanaged.
By summoning Dé with Dé,
Dé will naturally come.
As for Rén and Rén acting as relatives and brothers,
today if one's self practices Rén.
All those who practice Rén will naturally come to seek one another;
by summoning Rén with Rén,
people of Rén will all come.
If sovereigns practice this,
all under Heaven will be Rén;
if officials and commoners practice this,
none will fail to be close to one another.
This is what is meant by Rén and Rén uniting as one family;
this is to be relatives and brothers.
As for Yì and Yì acting as relatives and brothers,
using Yì to seek Yì,
today if one's self has already achieved Yì.
All people of Yì
will all come and return to it,
uniting through Yì.
If sovereigns practice this,
suffering and joy will be halved;
if officials and commoners practice this,
life and injury will be halved.
Using Yì to seek Yì,
this is to be relatives and brothers.
As for Lǐ and Lǐ acting as relatives and brothers,
using Lǐ to seek Lǐ,
today if one's self has already achieved Lǐ.
All people of Lǐ will come;
those who walk will maintain their integrity,
but the living will be uneasy,
within the abdomen there is emptiness,
and outwardly one is made to be like a ring,
hurrying, running, kneeling, and rising,
not hearing the command.
The days are short,
and clothing is all thin.
If sovereigns practice this,
they will be sorrowful and vexed;
if officials and commoners practice this,
their duties will be chaotic.
The robust will lack strength,
and the old and weak will injure their sinews.
Lǐ and Lǐ being close to each other,
this is to be relatives and brothers.
As for Wén and Wén acting as relatives and brothers,
today if one has already achieved Wén.
Using Wén to seek Wén,
people of Wén will all arrive like floating clouds,
accumulating inside and out, gathering like mountains.
If utmost sincerity is lacking,
great falsehood will emerge from it.
If sovereigns practice this
to manage their affairs,
they will sometimes gain and sometimes lose.
If officials and commoners practice this,
they will deceive one another,
recklessly saluting one another;
ten thousand kinds of harms, changes, and diseases will arise,
and people will have shorter lives daily.
Deceiving one another with Wén,
threatening one another with Wén,
taking from one another and producing one another in turn,
this is the relative of Wén.
As for Wǔ and Wǔ acting as relatives and brothers,
today if one has already achieved Wǔ.
Using Wǔ to summon Wǔ,
all people of Wǔ will come to gather.
Their Qì is bold and assertive,
Their weapons are brilliant,
their strength is doubled,
their eyes are wide open,
and their desire for anger cannot be restrained.
*Wǔguǐ* dwells in their corners,
seeking only victory,
and no longer cherishing their lives.
If a gentleman practices this,
his governance becomes increasingly ominous each day;
if officials and commoners practice this,
they will slaughter the world of men.
There is no good intent;
in governance, harm is amassed.
This is using martiality to breed martiality;
it is the kinship of martiality.
When sophistry and sophistry become kinsmen and brothers,
today it has already become *Dàbiàn*.
All those who possess sophistry come to join it.
Sophistry and sophistry interact with each other
without end.
One word becomes a hundred words,
a hundred words become a thousand words,
a thousand words become ten thousand words.
Exchanged back and forth,
mouths and tongues are in chaotic confusion like clouds;
there is no truth.
If a ruler of men practices this,
his administration will have ten thousand facets;
officials and commoners will have nowhere to place their lives.
To seek sophistry through sophistry
is to be kinsmen and brothers.
When laws and laws become kinsmen and brothers,
today they have already become a maze of laws.
To seek laws through laws,
all the legalistic people of the world gather.
Matters great or small are all governed by laws;
among the common people, there is no one without guilt.
From birth to old age,
how many offenses does a single person commit?
There are none without guilt.
Using this to treat people,
nineteen out of twenty gentlemen will suffer a violent death.
Using this to govern the world,
great chaos cannot be stopped.
Discussing how kinsmen and brothers seek each other in this way,
each follows its own kind.
The root of order and chaos,
and the foundation of *Tàipíng*,
can be known by examining these nine matters
The various gods in Heaven say:
for those who love to practice the Way,
the *Dàoqì* of Heaven and Earth comes forth to assist them;
for those who love to practice Virtue,
the *Déqì* assists them;
for those who practice Benevolence,
Heaven gives *Rénqì* to assist them;
for those who practice Righteousness,
Heaven gives *Yìqì* to assist them;
for those who practice Ritual,
Heaven gives *Lǐqì* to assist them;
for those who practice refinement,
Heaven gives *Wénqì* to assist them;
for those who practice sophistry,
*Biànqì* also assists them;
for those who practice law,
*Fǎlǜqì* also assists them.
Heaven and Earth each direct the spirits according to their kind.
If Heaven is about to assist,
the spirits will hasten toward it;
by deeply contemplating these essential meanings,
the energy of *Tàipíng* can be attained immediately.
May I ask, is supreme good easy to do,
or is supreme evil easy to do?
For the extremity of *Yáng* is good,
and the extremity of *Yīn* is evil;
the extremity of *Yáng* generates immortals,
and the extremity of *Yīn* kills things;
these are the extremities of *Yīn* and *Yáng*.
Now, the common people cannot exhaust their strength in nourishing their parents,
nor seek extraordinary prescriptions or arts of the Way
to provide for their parents,
causing them to harbor melancholy until death;
if they then merely teach one another about fine clothes, food, songs, and dances to amuse them,
these are people of great rebellion;
how could Heaven bless them?
Heaven responds by imitating the writings and correspondence of the common world.
Now Heaven establishes laws,
ordering the people of Heaven not to conspire together in craftiness;
it possesses a Great Art.
It is the same on Earth.
Does the *Zhēnrén* know this now?
From ancient times until now,
there have been many such sycophantic ministers and crafty scoundrels
who toy with literary expressions
to collectively deceive those above them,
grieving their rulers and fathers
in order to obtain official positions;
they have no merit before Heaven and Earth yet consume their stipends;
Heaven greatly detests them,
Earth greatly loathes them,
and Heaven names them the Disruptors of Order.
Now the *Píngqì* of Heaven arrives and wishes to sever them,
fearing these people will again disrupt governance.
People today have accumulated stupidity;
many can be deceived, and thus these people obtain office.
Now natural disasters cannot be deceived into leaving,
nor can they be removed through fraud or falsehood.
Truth and falsehood correspond with Heaven;
if I do not fully show this to the people of later ages
and let them try using it—if disasters are entirely removed,
then these are my true writings,
corresponding with the laws of Heaven,
about which there can be no doubt.
Without words, they will conversely be declared clearly manifest.
If they are used but without success,
then my Way is false,
and this too will be clear without words.
Heaven establishes laws;
it does not model itself on clever words
but rather on the achievement of success and results.
It is like sitting facing the sun or the moon;
both have light.
How does one know their heat or coolness?
They are far removed from humans.
By what is this verified?
It is primarily verified by the result:
sitting facing the sun is warm,
which is sufficient to know heat;
sitting facing the moon
is sufficient to know coolness.
My true writings
are also like this.
Heaven establishes laws:
when the eyes see, they regulate *Yáng*;
when they close, they regulate *Yīn*.
Seeing regulates the formed;
closing regulates the formless.
Seeing regulates the human body;
closing regulates the essence and spirit.
Using this as the verification,
one can therefore cause *Yīn* and *Yáng* to be entirely regulated,
and then no one will fail in their duties.
It is the same on Earth,
acting as the penetrative extremity of *Huángpíng*.
Now, as Heaven sends forth books,
and spirits send forth plans and tallies—the writings of the divine and sagely—
and as sages create writings and scriptures,
the words of the superior worthies,
these are all words.
Therefore, Heaven, Earth, the spirits, sages, and superior scholars exhaust their strength for people;
by using words over many years,
they can establish Heaven and Earth
and remove disasters.
If emperors and kings apply them,
they will then attain a state of wandering at ease without troubles,
attaining the state of an immortal and increased longevity above,
attaining the will of Heaven,
and having descendants to continue their lineage
without end.
A declining age will then turn into a great resurgence,
and the whole world will look up to their commands;
everyone will attain the profound penetration of the six directions and eight distances of Heaven and Earth;
*Yīn* and *Yáng* will both be pleased.
The ailments of Heaven—wind and rain—will occur in their proper seasons;
thunder and lightning will not be harmfully active;
the sun and moon will be even brighter.
The three luminaries will not lose their courses;
the four seasons and five elements will proceed in order,
each attaining its proper place.
This is what results from the good words of the spirits and sages;
is their merit not truly great?
Every part of the heavens is distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The infinite Three Luminaries of the heavens are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
Those dwelling in the center of the heavens are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The Three Luminaries of the heavens are distinct;
they possess natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The clouds and vapors of the heavens are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The sounds of thunder and lightning in the heavens are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The wind and rain beneath the heavens are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
Those dwelling in the center beneath the heavens,
where wind and cloud vapors are distinct,
possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The people upon the earth are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,

The crawling creatures upon the earth are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,

Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The grasses and trees upon the earth are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,

Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,

The mountains and hills upon the earth are distinct;

Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The rivers, valleys, waters, and marshes upon the earth are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
Every part beneath the earth is distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The infinite Yīnyáng beneath the earth are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The Wǔxíng are distinct;
they possess their own natural Qì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The Four Seasons are distinct;
