they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The Liùjiǎ and Shígàn are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The Liùjiǎ and Shí'èrzǐ are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The Bāfāng are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
The Shénlíng are distinct;
they possess their own natural Yuánqì and Yīnyáng,
which are similar to my writings.
Each follows its own customs;
record the words of my books on good and evil and put them into practice,
and then there will be Tàipíng.
If one does not teach them according to their fundamental categories,
then there will be great chaos.
Take heed of this!
Heaven has commanded me to bring forth these writings in full,
in order to dispel the illnesses of heaven and earth, Yīnyáng, emperors, kings, common people, and the myriad things.
Whatever sufferings the people and the myriad things endure,
all should be eliminated.
Therefore, I teach you to use the infinite laws to show them;
thus comparing and collating the divine writings of former and later sages and worthies
with the common words of ordinary people,
combining and thoroughly investigating them,
so that the illnesses of heaven and earth
can all be eliminated.
Once they are eliminated,
the emperors and kings will prolong their years,
ruling with folded hands and without concern.
Heaven
is Tàiyáng.
Earth is Tàiyīn.
Humans dwell in the center,
and the myriad things are likewise.
Heaven is that which constantly bestows from above,
its Qì flowing downward.
Earth is that which constantly seeks from below,
its Qì rising to join.
The two Qì intersect in the center.
Humans
dwell in the center to maintain correctness.
These two Qì constantly interact and operate,
joining in the center,
and together they give birth to the myriad things.
The myriad things all receive these two Qì to form their shapes
and combine them into their nature and disposition;
without these two Qì,
they cannot be generated or completed.
Therefore, the lives of the myriad things are tied to these two Qì;
the two Qì interact within their forms.
Thus, if they do good,
Heaven and Earth know it;
if they do evil,
Heaven and Earth also know it.
Therefore, in ancient times, people of superior goodness and virtue
were the only ones who internally knew the will of Heaven;
thus they were always upright and did good.
The Tiānchèn says:
Those who repeat joy receive joy,
those who repeat goodness receive goodness,
those who repeat evil receive evil,
those who repeat happiness receive happiness,
those who repeat compliance receive compliance,
those who repeat truth receive truth,
those who repeat the Dào receive the Dào,
those who repeat delight receive delight.
Whatever is repeated,
the various gods of Heaven and Earth also repeat it like shadow and echo!
Those who repeat refinement receive refinement in return,
those who repeat falsehood receive falsehood in return,
those who repeat sophistry receive sophistry in return,
those who repeat flattery receive flattery in return,
those who repeat violence receive violence in return,
those who repeat rebellion receive rebellion in return,
those who repeat misfortune receive misfortune in return,
those who repeat heterodoxy receive heterodoxy in return.
Whatever is repeated,
all the gods of Heaven and Earth repeat it.
All the laws of fortune and misfortune, safety and danger,
depend entirely on what is repeated.
Generally, among families where strength is great,
many accumulate private wealth,
but later they often become poor and suffer misfortune;
why is this?
The Shénrén says:
this is because some with much wisdom conversely deceive those who are lacking,
or those with great strength conversely deceive the weak,
or the younger conversely deceive the old;
these are all perversions.
Therefore, Heaven does not protect them for long.
Why is this?
Since the wise should protect and nurture the foolish,
but if they conversely deceive them,
this is the first perversion.
The strong should nurture the weak,
but if they conversely deceive them,
this is the second perversion.
The younger should nurture the old,
but if they conversely deceive them,
this is the third perversion.
This is not in accord with the Mind of Heaven;
thus misfortune is inevitable.
Now, wealth
is the surplus of things between Heaven and Earth.
It is like water:
it constantly flows and follows along,
always humble and remaining below.
Those who obtain much wealth
are the humble ones who obtain much.
Therefore, for those who deceive,
Heaven does not protect them.
Since the Dào was lost regarding the three laws of Heaven and Earth, Yīnyáng, and Zhōnghé,
there have been many surplus lifespan units in Heaven,
accumulated but not put into effect.
Why is this?
I wish to hear its meaning.
Now, as for the lifespans granted by Heaven:
the highest is one hundred and thirty,
which is called the surplus of the solar calendar.
The next is one hundred and twenty,
which is called the division of years and eras.
The next is one hundred years,
which is called the chronicle of harmonious cycles.
Humans should all take these as models for their years.
Since the loss of the three laws,
many do not complete their allotted years.
The surplus lifespan units, one unit for each year,
remain stored in Heaven;
because human conduct has lost the Tiāndào,
no one is able to obtain them.
Now, for those who model themselves on my text
and perform good deeds,
Heaven will send down all these lifespan units to increase their years;
some may transcend the world,
or extend their lives.
Since Heaven and Earth ◇◇,
emperors and kings have been solely preoccupied with the inequality of the world,
taking the failure of duties as their worry.
Apart from this,
there is nothing to worry about.
The good people of the world,
loyal ministers, and filial sons,
all worry about this together.
If they but practice my text,
this worry will be removed.
From Heaven it is said:
When the Yáng energy is greatly flourishing,
ghosts and creatures cannot act recklessly or cause harm.
Why is this?
When Yáng flourishes, Yīn must decline;
therefore, things cannot act recklessly or cause harm.
Who restrains them?
The Yáng essence restrains them.
How does the Yáng essence restrain them?
Now, the Yáng essence is spirit;
it belongs to Heaven,
it belongs to red,
it governs the heart.
The heart-spirit
is indeed the spirit of Heaven.
Essence
is the essence of Earth.
Ghosts
are the ghosts of humans.
Earth is the mother.
Ghosts are the children.
The law of child and mother is that they move together,
dwelling together in the Way of Yīn.
When the Tàipíng energy arrives,
the Yáng energy greatly rises,
the Tiāndào is strict,
and the Shéndào is bright.
When it is bright, Heaven causes people to rise together and utilize it.
When the Shéndào is used,
it then subdues and eliminates the way of ghosts and creatures.
When the Shéndào rises,
it moves together with the jūnzǐ.
The way of ghosts and creatures
moves together with the xiǎorén.
Therefore, the jūnzǐ governs with justice and uprightness,
and the spirits also govern with justice and uprightness.
The xiǎorén governs with heterodoxy and falsehood,
and ghosts and creatures also govern with heterodoxy and falsehood;
this clarifies that they belong to the same category of energy.
Now, the Yángdào raises fire;
weapons and blades should be extinguished,
as fire suppresses them.
Thus weapons accumulate and Yīn energy flourishes,
while fire accumulates and Yáng energy flourishes;
flourishing Yáng eliminates weapons,
which is a natural resonance.
Human life must depend on the energy of Heaven.
Those of superior goodness commit themselves to Heaven,
those of middle goodness commit themselves to humanity,
those of inferior goodness commit themselves to the fields.
Therefore, the shàngshì studies and transcends the world,
the zhōngshì should govern the people,
the xiàshì should manage the fields and wilderness.
The shàngshì should summon cloud-energy,
the zhōngshì rides in carriages,
the xiàshì should walk on foot.
These three types of people each have distinct duties,
and do not obstruct one another.
The shàngshì transcends the world and ascends to Heaven,
acting for Zhōnghé to harmonize wind and rain;
the zhōngshì belongs to the local offices,
and should govern the people;
the xiàshì should manage property.
Each has their respective duty,
and they do not obstruct one another.
Among the various methods of studying the Dào in Heaven,
humans must diligently seek the Dào.
A small accord with the Xiǎodào,
where seeing various spirits constitutes attaining the Dào in a small way;
the gateway does not yet accord with the Zhōngdào,
before one can reach the Dàdào.
Upon reaching the Dàdào,
one is then able to summon the True Spirits.
Those who accord in a small way with the Xiǎodào summon lesser spirits,
those who accord with the Zhōngdào summon middle spirits,
those who accord with the Dàdào summon great spirits.
When the great spirits arrive, one can transcend the world and endure forever.
However, in reaching this point,
there are always great heterodox spirits and ghosts,
who do not want people to transcend the world;
they are skilled at deluding people and causing them to become indolent,
or making them withdraw by speaking of strange transformations themselves,
so that truth and falsehood are mixed together.
If at this point one can distinguish between the heterodox and the upright,
then one will transcend the world.
Those named in Heaven as the Shàngshì,
from birth until the end of life,
do not possess a single evil intention;
thus, they are loved by the common people,
and the people and county officials of the five directions together bestow gifts upon them.
The Zhōngshì are loved by their neighbors,
and their neighbors together bestow gifts upon them.
The Xiàshì do not possess a good heart or intention,
and they can obtain no gifts;
they merely steal the private gifts of their own families.
This is the conduct of the "chaff" among the people of the world.
What is meant by "chaff"?
The Shàngshì are purely good,
with no evil in their hearts;
this is the Shàngyáng.
The heart and intention of the Zhōngshì are half good;
this is the Zhōngyáng.
The heart and intention of the Xiàshì are purely without goodness;
this is the Xiàyáng,
and thus they are named "chaff."
Chaff does not become solid grain;
it is empty inside without rice,
representing a lack of fruitfulness and trust.
A person without trust or substance is a Bǐrén.
That the Shàngshì receive gifts for their families from county officials and the four directions
means they do not forget their original ancestors.
That the Zhōngshì receive gifts for their families from their neighbors
means they do not forget their parents.
When the Xiàshì instead steal their family property to give to neighbors,
they are like the "chaff":
empty inside but appearing full outside,
they turn their backs on their own roots.
These all cause harm to Heaven above;
it means betraying one's family.
That there is disharmony within a family
all stems from such people.
If a minister has external dealings,
the state will surely become empty;
if a family member has external dealings,
the family will surely become empty.
The blame from Heaven all arises from this.
Safety and danger arise within a person's breast;
the Shénlíng are seen in far-off places.
Moving up and down and to the sides,
they penetrate for hundreds of millions of miles;
how can one not be cautious?
The Tàipíng Dào
has concise texts;
its country is wealthy.
It is the Tiānmìng
and the treasure of the self.
It emerges from the breast and heart
and flows throughout the world.
If these texts are practiced,
the country can be at peace
and the family can be wealthy.
According to the Tiāndì géfǎ,
the good should manage the evil,
the upright should manage the heterodox,
and the pure should manage the turbid.
One must not use evil to manage the good,
the heterodox to manage the upright,
or the turbid to manage the pure.
This would be a reversal,
causing bandits and thieves not to cease
and wickedness to arise daily,
even leading to great chaos;
all start from this.
When emperors and kings are about to employ ministers,
they must be detailed in their selection
and should follow the Tiānxīn.
Only when the Lièxiù are in alignment
do they dare employ them.
The Rì
is the Jūndé.
The Yuè
is the Chéndé.
If the Lièxiù are not in alignment,
Tàipíng surely cannot be attained,
and wickedness will arise.
What are the clothing, food, and lodging of the official houses and post houses of Heaven and Earth, above, below, the center, and the eight distances?
Those who practice Dàodé but have doubts
may find the answer in this prophecy.
Now there are official houses and post houses in Heaven to await and house others,
there are official houses and post houses on Earth to await and house others,
and they exist in the center and the eight directions.
The official houses in Heaven
house the Shénxiānrén.
The official houses on Earth
house the Shèngxiánrén.
The underground official houses
house the good spirits and good ghosts of the Tàiyīn.
The official houses at the famous mountains and great rivers of the eight directions
house the spirits and immortals between Heaven and Earth who have not yet been able to ascend to Heaven.
Those in the clouds and wind house Běijí and Kūnlún.
The official houses and post houses await the Shèngxián, good spirits, and those with merit.
Let the Dào be the head,
Dé be the belly,
and Rén be the feet to walk.
Heaven establishes official houses and post houses;
one who attains them may reside there.
Those who wish for the power of Heaven practice the Dào;
those who wish for the power of Earth practice Dé;
those who wish for the power of Humanity practice Rén.
These three
are the infinite path;
losing these three
is the root of chaos;
not following these three
is called opposing Heaven.
Therefore, the Shèngrén embraces Dàodé and practices Rén.
Beyond this,
it belongs to the conduct of the myriad things.
I ask about the Shénqì of the four seasons to assist in achieving good and removing evil:
which brings the Dàshén?
Which brings the Zhōngshén?
Which brings the Xiǎoshén?
Meditating on the Dìqì of the day and month-builder brings the Dàshén;
meditating on the Xiāngqì brings the Zhōngshén;
meditating on the Shāqì brings the Xiǎoshén.
Meditating on the Lǎoqì after the month-builder brings old things;
meditating on the Bìngshuāiqì after the month-builder brings evil ghosts;
meditating on the Sǐqì after the month-builder brings pure ghosts;
meditating on the Pòqì after the month-builder brings destruction, killing, misfortune, and harm.
The Shēngqì belongs to Heaven, to Yang, and to the front.
The Way of Heaven produces through Shénqì,
so the six spirits in front of the Dǒu are all "Living";
the six spirits behind belong to Earth and to Yin.
In the Way of Heaven, Sǐqì becomes ghosts
and causes misfortune for all things.
If you wish for future generations to be always cautious and faithful,
to love their kin and themselves,
and for the Shénmíng jīngqì
not to leave their bodies,
then they will not know old age or death.
The Shénmíng jīngqì
follows one's thoughts and intentions,
and does not leave the physical form.
If the Shénmíng is always present,
then one is not sick or old,
and does not encounter evil when traveling.
If the Shénmíng is lost,
the sick will die immediately,
and one will encounter misfortune when traveling;
this is a great sign.
If a person wishes not to be sick,
they should guard their Jīng.
All things do not exceed Zìrán;
within Zìrán, there is Jīngshén.
If a matter does not become "spiritual,"
it is merely the Dàdào and the nature of Heaven and Earth;
if there is no Dà jīngshén within,
nothing can be completed
or preserved.
Therefore, the Way of Heaven and Earth
moves according to Jīngshén and Zìrán.
Thus, all matters great and small
have Jīngshén.
Great things have great Jīngshén;
small things have small Jīngshén.
If each nourishes their Jīngshén,
they can exist for a long time.
When Jīngshén diminishes, one grows old;
when Jīngshén is lost, one dies.
This is the lot of Zìrán.
How can one struggle against it?
Safety and danger in all matters
depend entirely on Jīngshén.
Thus, the physical body is the house,
Qì is the carriage and horse,
and Jīngshén is the Zhǎngshì
who governs prosperity, decline, coming, and going.
It is the master of management.
To have a physical body without Jīngshén
is like having fields, houses, and city walls without a Zhǎngshì.
The Zhǎngshì
is the Sīmìng of the people;
it is what loyal ministers, filial sons, and greatly obedient people should follow.
For a human body
not to be loyal to superiors
or filial to parents
is to betray one's body,
punish one's form,
and lose one's root.
Constantly thinking of good
causes Jīngshén to gather and follow the person;
thinking of evil
also causes Jīngshén to gather upon the person.
It then enters the person's belly
and follows whatever the person thinks of,
causing them to be distressed and unable to forget it.
May I ask about the child within the womb,
who does not eat yet takes in *qì*.
While in the abdomen,
it is the *qì* of *zìrán*.
Once born,
it breathes the *qì* of *yīn* and *yáng*.
By observing the *Dào* and studying with effort,
one returns to the *qì* of *zìrán*.
Returning to the *qì* of *zìrán*,
if the heart is like that of an infant,
then one lives.
Following only the breathing of the *qì* of *yīn* and *yáng*,
then one dies.
Ordinary people cannot restrain each other,
and thus they govern their own fates.
If one does what is not good,
Heaven will punish them.
Thus the *xiǎorén* is punished by the *zhōngrén*,
the *zhōngrén* is punished by the *shàngrén*,
and the *shàngrén* is punished by the *dàrén*.
If a minor violation of the law is committed,
it brings peril and ruin upon oneself.
The punishments of divine spirits, great or small, are also like this.
If one cannot restrain oneself,
it is certain that Heaven must punish them.
Heaven stands in awe of the *Dào*,
and the *Dào* stands in awe of *zìrán*.
That Heaven stands in awe of the *Dào*
is because Heaven acts with ultimate conduct.
If the *Dào* is abandoned and not practiced,
then the *Dào* of Heaven will be disordered and destroyed.
If the *Dào* of Heaven is disordered and destroyed,
there will be peril and ruin without any remaining laws or measures.
Therefore, *zìrán* causes the *Dào* of Heaven and Earth to be maintained;
by practicing the *Dào* without ceasing,
*yīn* and *yáng* are transmitted to one another,
being entrusted to and producing one another.
The *Dào* thus governs life;
if the *Dào* is cut off, the myriad things will not be produced;
if the myriad things are not produced, then there will be no generations of their kind,
with nothing to be transmitted to one another;
if the myriad things do not produce or transmit to one another, then all is ruined.
How then could Heaven and Earth exist?
Heaven, Earth, *yīn*, and *yáng* ought to transmit to and produce one another.
If they are now cut off and extinguished, then there is destruction and ruin;
thus Heaven fears the cutting off of the *Dào* and the resulting peril and ruin.
That the *Dào* stands in awe of *zìrán* is because
if the *Dào* of Heaven does not follow *zìrán*,
then nothing can be accomplished.
Thus the myriad things are all accomplished by following *zìrán*;
without *zìrán*, all things are difficult to accomplish.
Even if they are made to be accomplished,
it is all through deception and falsehood,
and such accomplishment cannot endure for long.
Although Heaven and Earth are far apart and vast,
there are none who escape their governance of fate.
I ask:
"When the *qì* of *Tàipíng* arrives altogether,
and one wishes to use good intentions to remove villainy and evil,
what should come first?"
"The nature of Heaven and Earth
is half *yáng* and half *yīn*.
*Yáng* is good
and governs rewards.
*Yīn* is evil;
that which is evil constitutes punishments,
and it governs villainy and falsehood.
When those who reward are many
and those who punish are few,
and when the crafty are many
while those who reward are few,
the gate of villainy opens.
The reason for this is
that many punishments
govern killing and injury;
those who violate the law all become crafty criminals,
thus the gate of villainy opens
and the crafty become numerous.
*Yáng* governs rewards;
if giving is abundant,
then the power of *dé* is in effect.
*Yáng* and *dé* govern nourishment and life;
this is the law of *zìrán*.
Thus day is *yáng*, the sun, the ruler, and *dé*;
night is *yīn*, the moon, the minister, and villainy.
The nature of Heaven and Earth
is half good and half evil.
Thus the *jūnzi* prioritizes the good to close off villainy.
Those who promote good obtain good;
those who promote evil obtain evil.
This is like using a peck measure to match a peck measure;
that which is not a peck measure will naturally depart.
Using a foot-rule to match a foot-rule;
that which is not a foot-rule will naturally fall away.
It is like the square and the circle not fitting together,
the compass and the L-square not matching,
or the vertical and the horizontal not joining.
Thus when *yáng* arises, it must move according to its kind.
Thus when fire is abundant, thunder sounds,
and the *zhūquè* is within it.
This is why there is thunder in summer
and it is hidden in winter.
All things each follow their root;
only then can the *Dào* of Heaven be made clear.
If one does not follow their kind,
how could the sages and worthies obtain deep knowledge of it?
Therefore, from the opening of Heaven and Earth until now,
regarding the good and evil, truth and falsehood of people,
one only needs to observe what they do,
seek it according to its kind,
and examine their success;
then good and evil, gain and loss,
the worthy and the unworthy can be seen.
Why is there a need to sit and argue about it?"
I ask:
"From ancient times to the present,
the worthy,
the enlightened,
the wise,
the eloquent,
the strong,
and the brave—
these six types of people all possess ten-thousand-fold talent.
Do they possess good or evil?"
"These six types of people all possess talents ten thousand times that of ordinary men.
If their talents can harmonize Heaven and Earth,
and ensure that those of the wicked and harmful sort are not produced;
if the *dìwáng* is forever without worry and long-lived;
if they can personally eliminate their own diseases
and each complete their natural lifespan,
and their kindness flows to ordinary people—
then this worthiness, enlightenment, wisdom, eloquence, strength, and bravery
are of great good and benefit.
But if they cannot jointly harmonize Heaven and Earth,
nor cause the *dìwáng* to be without worry and long-lived;
if they themselves have diseases,
are unable to dispel calamities they encounter,
or die young,
with no difference from ordinary people—
then these six types of people are of no benefit.
Simply examine their success
and ask no more.
One who succeeds is right;
one who does not succeed is wrong.
Examining matters in this way
deeply attains the intention of August Heaven;
the *dìwáng* will have his lifespan extended
and the myriad things will all be well-ordered."
I ask:
"Among the myriad things, there are sometimes those that are not produced,
and those that are not nourished.
If they grow but do not reach completion,
from where do these great errors all come?"
"That which should be produced but is not produced
is Heaven;
that which should be nourished but is not nourished
is Earth.
Heaven and Earth are the dwelling of the myriad things;
the *xiánrén* is the craftsman of the myriad things.
The *dìwáng* models himself after Heaven
and always desires production;
the *hòufēi* models herself after Earth
and always desires nourishment;
the *dàchén* model themselves after humanity
and always desire to think of completion.
If these three combine their efforts,
then from birth to the end, the myriad things
will suffer no harm.
If one wishes to model oneself after the *Dào* of *píng*,
then those who make the laws must surely act in this way."
May I ask:
"Does the Tiāndào help the weak?
Or help the strong?
Does it help the few?
Or help the many?"
The Shénrén said:
"The Tiāndào helps the weak."
"Why is this?"
"For the weak
are the application of the Dào;
the few
are the essence of the Dào.
Therefore, the Běijí is a single star,
yet the many stars are subordinate to it;
this is using the few to govern the many,
for the essence of the Dào is unity and all paths belong to it.
For this reason, the Guówáng is extremely few,
yet the whole world assists him in governing;
this is the effect of helping the few.
Parents are extremely strong,
yet they conversely assist the infant;
this is the effect of the strong helping the weak.
People of Shàngshàn are few and weak,
while people who are not good are strong and many;
yet the many are indeed the few,
and the strong are indeed the weak.
Therefore, the Jūnzǐ seeks weakness and not strength,
and seeks the few and not the many.
Thus, the Tiāndào protects them.
Therefore, they do not contend with others,
yet others naturally contend on their behalf;
they do not contend for strength with others,
yet others help them to become strong.
Therefore, without contending, they excel at overcoming."
Distinguishing between the refined essence of Tiāndào and Dé without severance.
I ask:
"If the Dào is truly meant to be followed with joy,
what is the clear evidence?"
The Shénrén said:
"I received this text from the various gods in the heavens.
The gods said:
'I have heard that it corresponds with Yīnyáng, wind and rain, cold and heat.'
This is considered the great evidence.
Heaven rejoices when its Dào is practiced,
but people do not clearly believe in it;
hence, praying for rain or for rain to stop serves as clear evidence.
When the Dào of Tàipíng is practiced,
all prayers and requests are answered.
When the Dào of Tàipíng is not practiced,
prayers and requests are not answered.
This clarifies that the Way of Heaven is centered on Tàipíng.
Therefore, if the myriad things do not sprout,
the fault lies with Tàiyáng.
If they sprout but are not nourished,
the fault lies with Tàiyīn.
If they are nourished but do not reach completion,
the fault lies with Zhōnghé.
Thus, the one who brings forth life
is the father;
the one who nourishes
is the mother;
the one who completes
is the child.
Bringing forth life
is the Dào;
nourishing
is Dé;
completing
is Rén.
If one thing is not born,
one path of the Dào is blocked and does not flow.
If one thing is not nourished,
one aspect of Dé is not cultivated.
If one aspect of Dé is not completed,
one aspect of Rén is not practiced.
If you wish to know whether you possess Dào, Dé, and Rén,
you can know by observing the myriad things.
Regarding these five,
Dì, Wáng, Jūn, fathers, and Shī who wish to deeply know the quality of their Dào, Dé, and Rén,
they need only observe this.
Thus, of the foremost goodness in governing,
nothing is like rejoicing in life;
the next best is rejoicing in nourishing;
the next best is rejoicing in bestowing.
Thus, giving life resembles Heaven;
nourishing resembles Earth;
bestowing resembles Rén.
These three
are the great principles of Heaven, Earth, and Man.
For anything below these,
use them only as a last resort when exhausted.
In this way, the Tiānqì will naturally be at peace,
evil Qi will naturally be extinguished,
good people will naturally arrive,
evil people will naturally depart,
and everything will respond like an echo.
The one who clarifies this is the Shī.
To know beforehand is the definition of a Shī.
They should serve as the primary witness and clarify it.
From ancient times to the present,
all texts that emerge come from Heaven and Earth;
thus, Heaven and Earth bring them forth first.
The one who clarifies them is the Shī;
therefore, every text that emerges has a Shī.
The one who implements it is the Xiànguān.
In ancient times, Dìwáng upheld the will of Heaven,
received the teachings of the Shī,
and practiced them diligently to eliminate disasters
and match the heart of Heaven.
Thus they attained longevity and extended their lives;
this is what is meant.
Heaven creates it,
the Shī clarifies it,
and the Dìwáng implements it.
These three matters depend on each other for completion.
If Heaven does not bring forth the text,
the Shī has no means to know it.
If the Shī does not clarify the text,
the Dìwáng has no way to know how to govern.
Thus, when Heaven is about to raise up a Dìwáng,
a miraculous text will surely emerge.
An enlightened Shī is sent to teach the Dìwáng and the Xiànguān,
allowing them to attain longevity;
this is the clear evidence of the assistance given to the Dìwáng.
"If the common people and myriad things are not born,
are born but not nourished,
are nourished but do not grow,
grow but fail to reach completion,
and do not fulfill their natural lifespan,
where does the fault lie?"
"When the common people and myriad things are not born, the fault lies with
Heaven;
when they are not nourished, it lies with
Earth;
when they grow but do not reach completion, it lies with
Man."
"Is the fault then with Man?"
"When the myriad things cannot be born in their proper season, the fault lies with the
Jūn;
when they are born but not nourished, it lies with the
Chén;
when they grow but do not reach completion, it lies with the
Mín.
Heaven, the Jūn, and the father are in charge of birth.
This is the leadership of Tàiyáng,
the ancestor of life.
If Heaven does not wish to give life,
things cannot be born.
If the father does not wish to bestow,
things cannot be born.
If the Jūn does not wish to give life,
things cannot be born.
Thus Heaven, the Jūn, and the father are in charge of birth.
If the Jūn and the father always think of life
and do not delight in killing,
then all things will be born.
With one thought of killing, one thing dies;
with ten thoughts of killing, ten things die;
with a hundred thoughts of killing, a hundred things die;
from there to ten thousand thoughts,
it is all like this."
"Earth as the mother and the Chén receive the bestowals of Yang
and are in charge of growing and nourishing the myriad things.
Do they always think of growing and nourishing?"
"If they have one thought against growing and nourishing,
then one thing is harmed;
ten thoughts mean ten things are harmed;
a hundred thoughts mean a hundred things are harmed;
from there to ten thousand,
it is just like this.
For this reason, when the Dìwáng of high antiquity appointed ministers,
they always sought those who were compassionate and benevolent
and who loved to grow and nourish the myriad things while governing.
In middle antiquity, they were half-compassionate and half-benevolent,
so half of the things were harmed.
In lower antiquity, they did not carefully select ministers before appointing them,
and so the myriad things were all harmed.
The Dé of the Huáng is August;
the words of the Wáng are brilliant.
The Dì
created wisdom between Heaven and Earth
to prevent people from falling into misfortune and evil;
thus they are called Dì.
The Wáng are those
to whom the people and myriad things turn for safety from harm;
thus they are called Wáng.
Wáng
means 'to turn toward.'
The Jūn each bring peace to their respective borders,
and people turn to them without harm;
thus they are called Jūn.
Jūn
means 'to summon.'
The Lì
are in charge of governing
and assist the superiors in governing things,
so that the common people and myriad things, large and small,
do not lose their proper governance;
thus they are called Lì.
Shī are those who fully explain the words of the world;
only such people can be called Dàshī,
which refers to those who can interpret all the texts under Heaven.
Thus they are called Huáng, Dì, Wáng, Jūn, and Shī.
Thus the Huángdào is the head,
the Dìdào is the belly,
the Wángdào is the thighs,
and the Lì are the hands and feet.
The Shīdào
provides the plumb line, the law, and the standard.
Superiors and inferiors depend on each other to stand.
Therefore, those who govern well always think of the Huángdào,
next of the Dìdào,
and lastly of the Jūn, the Lì, and the Lìdào.
They always recite the laws of the Dàshī
and follow his plumb line.
Then the heart of Heaven can be at peace,
the intent of Earth can be attained,
the four seasons will naturally be harmonious,
the Five Elements will not be in conflict,
the Three Luminaries will always be bright,
the refined Qi of ghosts and gods will not cause harm,
the five offices and five lands will each find their proper place,
thieves and bandits will not arise,
the Dìwáng can rule through non-action,
and all will call out 'ten thousand years.'
The Tiāndào is the law in this way.
Without my text,
it is truly difficult!
Carefully contemplate its meaning
and practice these two matters.
Take heed!"
The nature of Tiāndì is that
Jīng, Qì, Guǐ, and Shén act to govern people, learn from people, and teach people.
Shén reside in the Yīn of the human heart,
Jīng reside in the Yīn of the human kidneys,
and Guǐ reside in the Yīn of the human liver.
When a person's thoughts are upright and good,
they consequently teach the person to do good;
they often reside in the Yīn of the human viscera,
and when they urge a person toward evil,
and teach a person to do evil,
they likewise urge the person toward evil.
In the bellies of the ancient Xiánrén and Shèngrén,
they always held hidden thoughts of doing good,
thus they obtained good responses.
Ordinary people often hold hidden thoughts of evil in their bellies,
thus they obtain evil responses,
and they are unable to restrain themselves.
The fault lies in habitually holding hidden thoughts of good or evil;
Guǐ and Shén consequently follow toward good or evil,
and the settling of Guǐ in this can be verified.
During Tàipíng Qì,
wind and rain arrive in their proper seasons,
the myriad things grow and flourish in abundance,
and it is suitable to apply fertilizer to the land,
so the earth becomes stronger and richer by the day,
making long life possible.
In disastrous years, rain and moisture are untimely,
the myriad things produced upon the earth are sparse and few,
short and not growing,
and unable to fertilize themselves,
thus the earth becomes poorer, thinner, and scarcer by the day,
making it impossible to bring the myriad things to completion.
The movement of Tiāndì
still requires Yīnyáng to achieve harmony,
after which Tàipíng is attained,
bringing forth the officials of the Sìshí and Wǔxíng.
The Yuèjiàn stands before and after the Dìwáng;
its duty is to serve as the Dìwáng Qì,
an official who expels the heterodox and evil.
Now, Jiàn Qì and Wàng Qì
are the imperial Qì of Heaven's Sìshí and Wǔxíng.
Xiàng Qì and Chú Qì are in the lead;
the first is to rectify what is in front,
being an official who points directly like a Máotóu.
What they face are hidden villainies,
preventing them from acting again to cause harm;
the Qì of Chú, those in front, Mǎn, Píng, and Dìng
are all good and virtuous officials.
The five Zhí reside in the lead,
preparing in advance for the Dìwáng Qì
to seize and remove great evils.
The Jiànqián Wǔjiàng
all receive the upright Qì of Heaven;
they are all divine officials of Heaven
and should serve as Tiānshǐ.
Regardless of size among the twelve thousand kinds of things,
all must be clothed in their virtue and follow their transformation.
To oppose Wàng Qì is death;
to oppose Yuèjiàn is Pò;
this is the foremost Qì of dignity and gravity,
thus it must not be opposed.
Those who oppose it die;
it is named the Shāqì Dàhào.
After Yuèjiàn is Bì,
which blocks and obstructs evil and villainy,
fearing that stagnant or hidden Qì from behind might come to interfere with the Dìwáng Jiàn Qì.
Therefore, Heaven closes what is behind it;
if the rear is opened,
it is to drive away the stagnant evil Qì.
What follows that is the completion of villainy,
which should then be seized.
The five behind are Wēi;
Wēi is where one is near Heaven’s seizure and great slaughter;
one turn to Pò leads immediately to a strike,
therefore it is Wēi.
Regarding these five rear generals,
Heaven wishes them to rest,
sharing the same Qì as the Earth,
presiding over the closing and concealing of villainy and evil,
where Guǐ and creatures dwell together,
so they must not be employed.
A question was asked:
"The North is the beginning of the Huáng,
the East is the beginning of the Dì,
the South is the beginning of the Wáng,
and the West is the beginning of the Bà.
Now that Heaven has the Liùjiǎ and Shí'èrzǐ,
where should the Huángdào begin?"
"Indeed,
Heaven has Sāntǒng,
each having its own great void.
The first is Tiānhuáng,
the second is Dì,
the third is Wáng,
and the fourth is Bà.
Tiānhuáng begins at the upper Jiǎzǐ,
Dìhuáng begins at Yǐchǒu,
Rénhuáng begins at Bǐngyín,
and the Bàdào begins at Dīngmǎo;
this is the numerical count of the celestial calendar.
As for the terrestrial calendar,
the Huángdào begins at Zǐ,
the Dìdào begins at Chǒu,
the Wángdào begins at Yín,
and the Bàdào begins at Mǎo.
These four
initially received the subtle Qì of Tiāndì to be created and born,
so they must not involve Xíng.
Those involving Xíng harm the Huángdào,
and the law of the Dào must not suffer harm.
Therefore, Zǐ punishes Mǎo,
Chǒu punishes Xū,
and Yín punishes Sì;
these all produce punishing Qì
and do not dwell together."
A question was asked:
"Heaven enfeoffs people with ranks,
Earth enfeoffs people with ranks,
and humans enfeoff people with ranks;
may I hear about this?"
It was said:
"Heaven enfeoffs people with the Dào,
Earth enfeoffs people with the cultivation of Dé,
and humans enfeoff people with Lùshí."
"Why is this?"
"Heaven
is distinct and long-lasting through the Dào,
therefore it enfeoffs them with the Dào,
granting them longevity
so they can consume wind and Qì to be satisfied.
Earth presides over the nurturing of good land.
Earth makes people wealthy,
so it enfeoffs people with the wealth of Dé.
The Ruler enfeoffs people with Lùshí
and bestows them with clothing.
These three matters are all good.
Those who love the Dào without ceasing
are thus enfeoffed by Heaven.
Those who love Dé and cherish the Earth,
knowing how to examine the land and receive it to dwell upon,
avoiding the inauspicious and obtaining the auspicious,
are enfeoffed by Earth.
Those who love learning and are beneficial to the higher administration
cannot be kept at a distance by the Ruler or father;
they are needed to manage affairs,
thus they are enfeoffed by men.
This is why the ancient Shèngrén and Xiánrén applied themselves to learning
and did not dare to lose these three matters.
Thus there were those who obtained the Dào and departed,
those who avoided the world and returned to the land,
and those who obtained the Ruler's Lùshí."
A question was asked:
"Regarding the music of the Wǔyīn,
what is it like to obtain the tone?
what is it like to not obtain the tone?
May I hear about both?"
"Tones
are not empty;
they bring about real matters,
using the void to bring about the solid,
it is the method of using the formless body to summon the formed body.
Music uses resonance to summon events,
just as when a person opens their mouth to emit sound,
there is good and bad;
the good brings good fortune,
and the bad brings misfortune.
These words all come from the human mouth
and thus bring about responses of good and evil;
musical tones are the language of Tiāndì, Yīnyáng, and the Wǔxíng.
By listening to the tones,
one knows the sentiments of Tiāndì,
and whether the Qì of the Sìshí and Wǔxíng is harmonized;
without knowing this, understanding is exhausted.
Therefore, the Shàngshì grasp the meaning
and use it for peaceful measurement;
the Zhōngshì practice it
to assist the Ruler's governance
and to achieve longevity;
the Xiánzhě practice it
to achieve freedom from worry.
Tones
are that which use the One to multiply into ten thousand,
with the ten thousand multiplying into the infinite,
and thus all under Heaven is fully prepared."
Question:
"Why is the *Tàipíng Jīng* intended to be one hundred and seventy volumes?"
The answer says:
"As for the One,
it is the starting point of numbers.
Therefore, in the time before Heaven and Earth were divided,
the accumulated *qì* was entirely as One.
Dividing to become Two,
they formed Husband and Wife.
Heaven bestows down upon Earth,
and conception occurs in *Xuánmíng*;
the name is *Jiǎzǐ*.
It spreads its roots in the northeast;
*Chǒu* is the beginning of *Yín*.
It appears in the East;
the sun rises in *Mǎo*.
Its growth is completed in the southeast;
*Chén* along with *Sì* hang their branches in the south,
and are nourished in *Wǔ*.
It approaches old age in the southwest,
at *Wèi* and *Shēn*.
It reaches completion in the West;
the sun enters *Yǒu*.
It is fully stored in the northwest,
in *Xū* and *Hài*.
Thus, numbers begin at one
and stop at twelve.
These are the basis of the *Gān*
and the root of the *Wǔxíng*.
Thus, one makes ten,
and a hundred makes it complete.
Therefore, when Heaven generates things,
the resonance of spring lasts for a hundred days to reach its end.
Thus, the Heavenly Dipper establishes (*Jiàn*) in *Chén*
and breaks (*Pò*) in *Xū*.
'Establishing'
means setting up;
the myriad things are fully born in *Chén*.
'Breaking'
means ruin;
the myriad things fully die in *Xū*.
Thus, as for numbers,
descending from Heaven to the eight directions of Earth,
ten makes them complete.
The *Jiàn* and *Pò* of *Yīnyáng*
come and go by seven,
returning to their original state.
Following what the Heavenly Dipper points to clarifies matters;
thus the Dipper has seven stars
to clarify the end and beginning of *Yīnyáng*.
Therefore, the *Tàipíng Jīng* was composed in one hundred and seventy volumes,
taking the numbers of Heaven and Earth as its model,
corresponding to the laws of *Yīnyáng*,
and following the Four Seasons and *Wǔxíng* for its conduct,
not daring to err by even a *zhū* or a *fēn*.
To err in this would be to omit the affairs of Heaven,
leaving no basis;
it would not correspond to the intent of Heaven and Earth,
nor follow the numbers of Heaven in forming a scripture,
and would be of no benefit to the use of governing the world.
If it does not model the laws of Heaven and Earth,
it cannot eliminate harm.
If you wish to know its efficacy:
collect the idle writings of the world;
even if you pile them for thirty *lǐ*,
reaching up to the sky,
and put them into practice,
they still cannot eliminate disasters."
Under the great heaven,
in the eighty-one regions
and eleven thousand countries,
each has its own documents,
all desiring to remove evil and bring about good
and to eliminate disasters and calamities.
If one collects and gathers them all now,
covering an area of a hundred lǐ square,
though they could be piled up to the sky,
in the end, they cannot eliminate disasters.
Although this text is brief,
if emperors and kings can practice it,
they must await its clear efficacy.
The first of high antiquity was the Shénrén,
the second the Zhēnrén,
the third the Xiānrén,
and the fourth the Dàorén;
they all modeled themselves after Heaven to obtain the intent of the true Dao.
Dazzling the eyes to look inward,
ordering the interior with the mind,
the Yin-brightness reflects back into the penetration of the Tàiyáng,
and internally and alone they obtain the essentials of the Dao.
It is like fire making light to shine within
and not without,
causing them to endure long without disorder.
Those who study to transcend the world today
model themselves after the ancients to practice inward vision;
this is what it refers to.
Over a long time, as it was passed down, births were followed by decline,
and conversely they grew weary of their actions daily;
the transmission lost the intent of the Dao,
they could no longer shine within,
and daily they became increasingly disordered.
Therefore, Heaven produced the Shèngrén,
modeling after the Tiānwén;
thus, the Tiānwén was seen by itself.
Therefore, when the Tiānwén is correct,
Heaven is also correct;
when the Dìwén is correct,
Earth is also correct;
when the Rénwén is correct,
humanity is also correct;
when Heaven, Earth, and humanity are all correct,
the myriad things are all correct.
Humans
are the leaders of the myriad things.
When humans lose their duty and are harmed,
not dying at their natural longevity,
the myriad things follow suit,
and Heaven and Earth are the same.
Evil qì arises greatly,
and the sick do not complete their heavenly years.
Only in the actions of the past and present,
each has its order
and does not overstep.
Among the venerable ones of the Shànghuáng Shénrén,
one named himself Wěiqì zhī Gōng,
also named Dàshén,
who is always at the left side of the Tiānjūn,
in charge of governing the books of the Míngtáng patterns,
making them distinguishable,
and holding the great office of the Qūlǐng.
He shall facilitate communication with the spirits and immortals for the Ruler,
recording the people not yet born,
each with a name and surname,
setting their years, months, days, and hours.
When the time for ascent arrives,
he sends a spirit to go and master the transformation of their body, and then they ascend.
Each has a name and surname,
setting their years, months, days, and hours;
when the time for ascent arrives,
he sends a spirit to go and master the transformation of their body, and then they ascend.
According to the height of their intelligence and ability,
each is made not to forget their division and distinction,
each made to be known,
making them state their own abilities,
and then they are appointed.
A memorial is presented
and the words say:
The Dàshén is the superior ruler leading the host of spirits.
Each has their own department;
they should submit to and clarify it,
not allowing for doubt.
Make the lifespan long and documented;
one should be diligent in this.
The Sagely and Brilliant have the intent;
they should use all that is born in the daylight.
Furthermore, using registers and calculations to clarify one another,
one may be in the Jìcáo,
presiding over the quantity of money and precious treasures.
All those who are to present their accounts
should announce it beforehand;
together with the Jìcáo,
it is called reporting to the Sīnóng.
On the thirtieth day of a long month
and the twenty-ninth day of a short month,
they assemble at the Míngtáng of the Dàshén.
Do not miss the deadline;
as per the instruction of the Tiānjūn,
none may miss the interval of the three marks after dawn.
The Dàshén of the Míngtáng receives the assembly's memorials at the five marks,
conducting affairs according to the old commands of the Tiānjūn.
The Dàshén receives the decree of the Lord
and commands the Sīnóng;
the Sīnóng receives the decree
and sends it down to the subordinate provinces, commanderies, and states.
Stating what is commanded and governed,
those who should submit registers and enter the Sīnóng's granaries for transport
must each send the documents according to what is produced.
If there are those who are lazy and do not send them in time,
the Sīnóng immediately reports to the Dàshén of the Míngtáng,
who reports to the Tiānjūn.
A teaching is issued down to the Sīnóng,
ordering the commanderies and states to urge them,
so as not to lose the subsequent documents.
Setting the time, day, and water-clock marks to be handed down,
each with distinction,
let there be no disorder;
all are ordered to have the same text,
each with a duplicate text.
In Heaven, there are naturally no disasters of floods or droughts;
there must be no documents of increase or decrease.
The turning wheel is about to arrive;
do not delay due to causes and conditions,
fearing that one alone might receive and take.
Those who realize this have a master;
Heaven hears and knows of it,
and the sin is never pardoned.
Each be cautious in their office;
each be clear in their affairs.
The Tiānjūn knows everything in advance
but does not speak;
one should examine what is asked
and not use these words.
Floods and droughts are irregular,
disasters arise together,
the people have diseases,
and the dead and living are countless;
these are not caused by the instructions and commands of the Tiānjūn.
The Tiānjūn issues instructions to inform the Dàshén,
the documents of the Ministers and the Two Thousand Shi officials,
and the spirits among the various officials in office.
Strive to exhaust their loyalty,
strive to exhaust their conduct,
so as to match the heart of the Tiānjūn above.
The Tiānjūn and the various masters transform it;
those who should attain ascent and transcendence are approached and corrected.
Each is made to become a spiritual radiance,
and according to the spirits transformed by their rank of honor or humility,
all follow the order of their positions and subordinate offices.
The Tiānjūn decrees that the Dàshén constantly transform and complete them.
People each measure themselves;
their will and intent grow higher daily,
greedily longing for ascent.
Their transformation produces radiance,
seen within the sun,
penetrating the correct spirits,
following each other to float and roam through the Bābiǎo.
Observing what Heaven performs,
knowing its movements,
each following what is appropriate.
For the morning audience to meet Heaven,
there are naturally fixed days.
It should be at the beginning of the month;
the Dàshén and the lesser spirits
will differentiate themselves
and rank their honor and humility.
The morning audience with the great ministers does not exceed the assembly at dawn.
The various spirits each clarify their deployments,
inspecting without a fixed time,
striving to clarify their documents
and supervising the officials in charge;
if there is a mistake, they are first held responsible for their affairs,
as per the instructions and commands of the Tiānjūn.
When there is something to report,
the Míngtáng is immediately opened,
and only then can the words be spoken.
Each has something to clarify,
each has something to carry;
none may be without efficacy.
The Tiānjūn decrees to the Dàshén
that the various officials assemble,
each correcting their ritual,
allowing no errors,
differentiating by the laws and commands,
each observing their department.
Heaven realizes and knows,
and their errors are not removed.
Each be cautious in their office,
and do not let the various spirits find any shortcomings.
The Tiānjūn decrees to the Dàshén, saying:
Within the commanderies and states,
there are those with sagely wisdom and will,
who constantly think of the arts of longing for life,
wishing to walk together with the Shēngshén,
and joining their thoughts with Heaven.
They desire to spread kindness to people,
contemplating generation and growth,
assisting Heaven in governing life,
and assisting Earth in nourishing form.
Admiring benevolence and transformation through kindness,
one submits their name to the Dàshén;
causing the departments to possess elegant writings,
frequently submitting records of merit,
being trustworthy and capable of responsibility.
When the departments report their intentions,
the Tiānjūn should naturally have his own reckoning,
and the various spirits should each guarantee those they recommend.
This is the selection process of the Jùnguó,
where the goal is to choose the most excellent.
The Tiānjūn commands the Míngtáng
that all who are to manage various duties for the Tiānjūn
must strive to pacify their hearts.
Each shall travel within their assigned heavenly division,
ensuring there is clear organization;
all should exhaust their loyalty and sincerity,
communicating what they know,
striving to accomplish their merits,
and striving to govern their respective stations.
Let each be praised for their sincerity and thoroughness;
they should advance what they contemplate.
Wherever voices and sounds reach,
even if their intentions are only silent thoughts,
the Tiānjūn hears their words in advance;
how could anything be hidden? One must not fail to be fully sincere.
Question:
"If one now wishes to further illuminate the laws of the Shèngxián and Rén and completely cut off deviant writings,
how can they be further illuminated?"
"Heaven is troubled by these deviant and false writings
and commands their removal,
adopting and illuminating the Tiāndào.
The writings of the Shèngrén of past and present
are the means to order Tiāndì.
When the writings of the Shèngrén are clear,
then the Tiāndào is in great order.
When Huángtiān is angered and displeased,
therefore there is warfare,
and floods, droughts, and disasters never cease.
Rulers are distressed,
and all say the writings of the Shèngrén have gradually become disordered and unclear;
therefore the Tiāndào is said to be chaotic and difficult to govern.
When the writings of the Shèngrén are disordered,
the Tiāndào is also disordered;
when the writings of the Shèngrén are discarded and not used,
the Tiāndào is also discarded and not used."
Question:
"In ancient times there were no writings,
yet the Tiāndào was not disordered.
At that time, the Tiānquàn and writings had not yet appeared;
the Shénrén of the Shànghuáng era governed the ancestors,
originally sharing the same essence with Huángtiān.
As time passed, they distanced themselves from the Tiāndào,
resulting in loss and chaos,
so that they no longer knew the Tiānyì.
Therefore Heaven brought forth the tallies,
and had the Shèngrén write them down and teachers transmit them;
the Shèngrén did not remain for long.
Thus they recorded them and left them behind
to pass on to later generations.
Therefore, when the Tàipíng Qi arrives,
the Tiāndào shall be ordered."
Question:
"Now, if one wishes to manage the matters of Qi and attain longevity,
may one hear of this?"
"Indeed,
meditate carefully on my words.
Huángtiān has its own constant laws.
Those who act as the Jūnshàng of people
should act in the image of Heaven,
by using Dào, Dé, and Rén as the three guiding principles for their conduct.
If the Jūnshàng wishes to enjoy a state of non-action,
he should constantly contemplate Dào in the morning,
constantly contemplate Dé during the day,
and constantly contemplate Rén in the evening,
and then there will be not a single matter of concern."
"I wish to hear why one contemplates Dào in the morning,
why one contemplates Dé during the day,
and why one contemplates Rén in the evening?"
"Indeed,
the Tiāndào can be followed
but it cannot be opposed.
Those who follow Heaven prosper;
those who oppose Heaven perish."
"Now I wish to hear the essential meaning of this."
"Indeed,
Heaven has four seasons and three divisions.
The morning governs birth,
the day governs nourishment,
and the evening governs bestowal.
Thus, the southeast is for birth,
the southwest is for nourishment,
and the northwest is for bestowal.
Therefore, humans should act in the image of Heaven,
planting in the southeast to give birth,
nourishing in the southwest to grow;
after mid-autumn,
staying indoors in summer to marry and bestow procreation—
this is the natural instruction and command of Huángtiān.
Therefore the people silently follow it.
Whoever can consistently govern in this image
will then obtain the Tiānyì;
those who cannot
are said to be opposing the commands of Heaven,
and thus there is much harm.
If the young are harmed, the things of spring are harmed;
if the mature are harmed, the things of summer are harmed;
if the elderly are harmed, the things of autumn are harmed;
if the pregnant are harmed, the things of winter are harmed.
This is the law of nature.
In ancient times, the Shèngwáng
always contemplated the Tiāndào and acted accordingly,
not daring to deviate by even a tiny amount."
Question:
"If one wishes to attain lasting generosity with the Earth,
may one hear of this?"
"Indeed,
those who always follow what Heaven does
will have lasting generosity with Heaven;
those who lightly oppose it
will have lasting enmity with Heaven.
Therefore, in the governance of ancient Shèngwáng,
the first is called 'constant birth,'
the second is called 'constant nourishment,'
the third is called 'constant bestowal.'
By acting in this way,
one carefully upholds the Tiāndào to avoid the reputation of it being unordered.
The fourth is called 'punishment without order,'
the fifth is called 'killing'—
these are the extremes.
Distinguishing by these,
a ruler of the first kind purely gives life,
a ruler of the second kind purely nourishes,
a ruler of the third kind purely bestows,
a ruler of the fourth kind purely punishes,
a ruler of the fifth kind purely kills.
One who gives life extends their years and the state prospers;
one who nourishes increases their lifespan;
one who bestows is without fault;
one who punishes suffers illness;
one who kills meets a sudden and destitute end.
In ancient times, the Shèngwáng
observed Heaven's prohibitions clearly
and did not dare to act recklessly.
In ancient times, on the days when the Shèngwáng attained the subtle Qi of Liùjiǎ and the Wángxiāng,
they did not grow angry and did not speak of evil matters.
When these days arrived,
they spoke of good matters,
ate and drank and made music,
to stop disasters and remove inauspicious and deviant influences.
Therefore, the Wángqì always desires to be respected.
Therefore, those who transcended the world in high antiquity
and the governance of the Shèngwáng followed this;
therefore they could govern while reclining and contemplating,
and in the end there was not a single matter of concern.
In spring, the head faces east;
in summer, the head faces south;
in autumn, the head faces west;
in winter, the head faces north;
in the four transition months, the head faces the corners.
When ruler, minister, and people all know this law,
then all deviant Qi in the world will vanish.
According to the standard laws of Heaven,
on the Wángrì, one should always lower and take the weapons from the armory
and arrange them underground.
On the Xiūfèi days, they are then brought forth;
therefore thieves and rebels do not arise,
and warfare ceases."
The question was asked:
“Heaven is uniquely angry and does not respond to or harmonize with man;
can the reason for this be known?”
“Indeed.
The Principle of Heaven (*Tiānlǐ*) takes *qì* as its language,
which is manifest in the four seasons.
When the *jué* *qì* of spring is unknown,
the liver pulse (*gānmài*) does not move,
the *jué* note and *cù* pitch are not in harmony,
and the pure tones do not respond;
this is Heaven being displeased and not speaking.
When the Sage-Kings (*Shèngwáng*) of old saw this,
they would contemplate the principles of gain and loss to reverse it.
However, where the kingly *qì* resides,
it attains Benevolence (*Rén*) to assist its principle.
These two *qì* together generate life here.
But if instead the retired, exhausted, and ominous *qì* arrives
to assist the principle,
then these are the three *qì*.
The *qì* of petty people (*xiǎorén*) is conversely manifest here;
they do not unify the Heavenly position,
and thus they take the image of petty people.
When Heaven shines its light
and sees its own kind,
it commands the Worthies and Sages (*Xiánshèng*) to strategize and contemplate it;
they should seek out recluses, men of the Way (*Dàorén*), men of Virtue (*Dérén*), and men of Benevolence (*Rénrén*) to restore the *qì*,
and then a response will be established immediately.
Therefore, the Ruler (*Wángzhě*) governs the Heavenly Way (*Tiāndào*),
using the people and ministers as his limbs;
if the governance is not good,
then it disorders its Way.
When the Sages of old were about to govern the Heavenly Way,
they sought out those of the Way and Virtue (*Dào Dé*), the Benevolent (*Rén*), the Worthy (*Xián*), and the Brilliant (*Míng*) to govern it together,
and thus they resided in peace.
Therefore, the Man of the Way (*Dàorén*) belongs to Heaven (*Tiān*),
the Man of Virtue (*Dérén*) belongs to Earth (*Dì*),
and the Man of Benevolence (*Rénrén*) belongs to Central Harmony (*Zhōnghé*).
Thus, when the Three Unities (*Sāntǒng*) are not in harmony,
the three Worthies regulate them.
Thus, when the *qì* of Great Peace (*Tàipíng*) arrives,
the myriad things (*wànwù*) are all regulated.”
The question was asked:
“How can the myriad people (*wànmín*) all be made benevolent?”
“Indeed.
The Heavenly Way (*Tiāndào*) generates Virtue (*dé*),
and Virtue generates Benevolence (*rén*).
Now the Lord (*Jūn*) takes the Man of the Way (*Dàorén*) as his teacher
and takes the Way (*Dào*) as his law.
When the Lord models himself after the Way,
his ministers will be virtuous.
When the people then model themselves after the ministers,
and the ministers are virtuous, then the people will be benevolent.
The lower follows the image and law of the upper,
and the upper models itself after Heaven (*Tiān*).
Revolving and generating one another,
how could the people not all be benevolent?
The Sage-Kings of old who took the Man of the Great Way (*Dàdàorén*) as their teacher
did so because they desired to transform those in the lower streams.
A superior Lord (*shàngjūn*) governs like Heaven,
a middle Lord (*zhōngjūn*) governs like Earth,
and an inferior Lord (*xiàjūn*) governs like man.
Acting like Heaven
means not losing the will of Heaven
and serving the Great Way (*Dàdào*) as a father.
Acting like Earth
means not losing the will of Earth
and serving the Way of Earth (*Dìdào*) as a mother.
Acting like man
means not losing the will of man
and longing to attain the Way of Central Harmony (*Zhōnghé zhī dào*).
When the Sage sees the myriad things (*wànwù*) all being born,
he knows that their principle values the Way (*Dào*);
when he sees things all being nourished,
he knows their True Virtue (*Zhēndé*);
when he sees the myriad things all being completed,
he knows their True Benevolence (*Zhēnrén*).
He who regulates the True Way (*Zhēndào*)
has only a heart for giving life;
he who regulates True Virtue (*Zhēndé*)
has only a heart for nourishing;
he who regulates Benevolence (*Rén*)
has only a heart for bestowing.
If it is not these Three Unities (*Sāntǒng*) of the Way, Virtue, and Benevolence,
one cannot be called a Lord of Great Peace (*Tàipíng zhī jūn*).
The Masters Above Heaven (*Tiānshàng zhī shì*) generate Heaven;
they receive the entrusted *qì* from above and are born without form.
Knowing the Masters Above Heaven—
what is it they do not know?
what is it they do not understand?
what is it they do not see?
They are the spontaneous Original *Qì* (*Yuánqì*),
holding the same office and acting together.
The Masters Above Heaven
are always in the Hall of the Infinite (*Wújì zhī diàn*),
managing documents and principles alongside Heaven.
Above and below, they do not fail in their duties,
so they know the things that can be born;
they return to the form of the Earth (*Dìxíng*) below
to cause them to be completed,
and the myriad things (*wànwù*) are all covered in glory.
The Masters Above Heaven
are respected by Heaven
and looked up to by all the Spirits (*Zhūshén*),
like the Crown Prince of an Emperor;
who would dare to be disrespectful?
The Heavenly Lord (*Tiānjūn*) is the entrusted *qì*,
so he is named the Heavenly Lord;
his honor is supreme.
Whatever he commands or teaches,
who would not follow his orders?”
The question was asked:
“As for the Lord of Great Peace (*Tàipíng zhī jūn*), his Way is flourishing,
and his Virtue is second only to Heaven.
By obtaining the writings and acting alone,
the transformation flows throughout the world,
and then nothing can be unequal.
Great spirits do not exceed Heaven and Earth (*Tiān* and *Dì*),
and great brilliances do not exceed the Sun and Moon (*Rì* and *Yuè*),
yet they are both two halves forming a whole.
Heaven and Earth each exert half their strength;
they unite their hearts and join their desires in harmony
to be able to give birth to the myriad things.
Day and night each exert half their strength
to complete one day.
Spring, summer, autumn, and winter each exert half their strength to complete one year.
The moon begins its birth in the west,
grows towards the east,
and when it reaches the fifteenth day, it is called Yang (*Yáng*);
after the fifteenth day, it wanes
and is called Yin (*Yīn*).
Each exerts half its strength,
and thus completes one month.
Man and woman each exert half their strength;
with shared will and in harmony,
they form one family.
The Way of Heaven and Earth (*Tiān Dì zhī dào*)
is one Yin and one Yang;
each exerts half its strength,
joining into one,
and only then do they together form a whole.
Therefore, when a Lord and minister unite their hearts and join their strengths,
each exerting half their strength
with a sincere desire for unity,
then the Principle of Great Peace (*Tàipíng zhī lǐ*) is completed.”
The question was asked:
“Though the writings of people today are many,
and they claim for themselves that all things are fully prepared,
disasters, thieves, and bandits are always in excess.
They often experience sorrow and suffering,
worrying about these ill-omened days;
though officials and people together try to save the situation,
they cannot.
What was cut off arises again.
Now I can permanently supplement what is insufficient
and ensure that disasters do not recur.
Since the writings of the Heavenly Bond (*Tiānquàn*) appeared in ancient times,
among all the writings of worthies and sages,
are there any that are the same?
They are all different.
Therefore, Heaven (*Tiān*) commanded the Master (*Shī*) to come forth
to eliminate ominous virtue,
protect the people and ministers,
and let light cover the four boundaries;
far and near respond like an echo,
and grace reaches even the plants and trees.
This is because their minds and intentions are opened;
their writings are all different.”
The question was asked:
"The essential Way of ancient and modern times
is always said to be Guarding the One,
which allows one to exist long without aging.
If a person knows how to Guard the One,
it is called the Way of Wújí.
A person has a single body,
which always merges with the essence and spirit.
The form governs death,
while the essence and spirit govern life.
Constant merging leads to good fortune;
separation leads to calamity.
Without essence and spirit, there is death;
with essence and spirit, there is life.
Constant merging constitutes the One,
allowing for long existence.
The constant worry is that essence and spirit will scatter
and not gather within the body,
instead being made to wander following human thoughts.
Therefore, the Sage teaches to Guard the One,
meaning one should guard one's own body.
If one focuses without ceasing,
the essence and spirit will come of their own accord,
none failing to respond.
The hundred diseases will naturally be removed;
this is the token of long life and long vision.
Those of Yáng guard the One;
those of Yīn guard the Two,
which is thus called killing.
Therefore, daytime is Yáng,
when the human souls always dwell together;
darkness is Yīn,
when the souls and spirits struggle and wander to form dreams,
and the thoughts lose their form,
dividing into two
until death is reached.
The essence and spirit are all lost,
and the form alone remains.
Guarding the One
means that the true and the real merge into one.
The essence and spirit of human life
are all fully present;
if one guards them without scattering,
one may even transcend the world,
become a parent to the good people,
see the Lord of Tàipíng,
and be loved by the divine spirits."
The first is called the Shéndào Shū,
the second is called the Héshì Wén,
the third is called the Qùfúhuá Jì;
all are called the Way of Dàshùn.
Tài
means great;
what is great
is Tiān;
Tiān can cover and nurture the myriad things,
its merit being the greatest.
Píng
means Dì;
Dì is level,
and thus can nourish and rear the myriad things.
Jīng
means constancy;
Tiān takes the sun, moon, and five stars as its Jīng;
Dì takes the peaks, drains, mountains, and rivers as its Jīng.
If Tiān and Dì lose their constant Way,
then the myriad things all suffer disasters.
Emperors and kings model themselves above on August Tiān,
below on Queen Dì,
and in the middle on the constants and filaments,
the stars and constellations, the peaks and drains,
to nurture and rear the myriad things.
Therefore, it is called the Way of Dàshùn.
In ancient times, Divine Persons determined right and wrong for themselves;
whether something was attained or not
could be seen immediately in the matter.
It was not only not obscure,
but manifest and clear.
The Divine Way is supreme;
it refines the body and spirit,
corrects the mind and intent,
so that nothing is hidden.
The good comes forth,
the evil is suppressed;
this is the method for knowing good and bad fortune for oneself,
like the pattern of looking into a mirror.
At such a time,
the virtuous and wise are at peace with themselves.
Time does not come again,
and things do not respond repeatedly.
Thus one attains unique prosperity
that reaches distant lands;
the affairs are seen,
their responses are seen.
Be careful not to resist or oppose;
compile them to be precious vessels,
and one can be said to have obtained the heart and mind of Tiān and Dì.
Affairs are timely,
tasks are all fulfilled,
the Divine Way arrives,
the worthy devise plans,
auspicious people arrive,
the heterodox do not come,
clarity is seen,
the four directions are pleased,
recluses and hermits come forth,
the heart of Tiān is obtained,
the arts of governance are obtained,
evil is not triggered,
spontaneity is reached,
Zhēnrén come to assist,
the world responds well,
each comes with their own affairs,
and confusion and disorder are removed.
This response emerges from within the belly
and is issued from the chest and heart,
just like the verification of thunder and lightning.
Auspicious responses actually come from within the chest,
coming and going with thoughts,
and in a brief moment,
they circulate throughout the world.
What is desired in the heart
moves August Tiān;
Yīn and Yáng are shifted by it.
That sincere speech moves Tiān
refers precisely to this.
Thoughts can bring about the upright,
and they can also bring about the heterodox;
all arise from the will and intent.
If they can move Tiān and Dì,
harmonize Yīn and Yáng,
and unite the myriad things,
internally they can save the self,
and externally they can establish a name;
both the worthy and the unworthy arise from this.
Therefore, the worthy are good at steering,
not losing one in ten thousand.
"When a person has a fault within,
why does their face turn red?"
"The heart
is the master of the five viscera;
the master is the king.
The king is in charge of upholding correctness;
when there is a fault, it is reported to Tiān."
"Why does the face turn green when one is startled?"
"The liver is the master of the person;
the 'person' means worry.
When it conflicts with the liver and gallbladder, it causes anger;
therefore, green emerges above."
All the spirits have that which they govern,
corresponding with the myriad things.
Therefore, one should always be cautious and virtuous,
and follow Tiān and Dì,
so that disasters cannot arise again.
External learning is abundant,
internal learning is scarce;
external affairs flourish daily,
internal affairs decline daily.
Therefore, people have many illnesses,
and thus there is much superficiality.
Superficiality is
the surface.
Ostentation is
the branch-end.
When the Tiāndào is distant and one enters into depravity,
one cannot return by oneself.
What are called the books of the Shéndào
are the root and origin;
they harmonize with Yīnyáng
and are one with the Shénmíng.
Those who examine the texts of affairs
investigate similarities, differences, doubts, and errors without fail.
Those who record superficiality and ostentation
are already far from the root;
they dwell in the wild,
and their writings are disorganized and chaotic.
They cannot be used regularly,
though they may occasionally be noted.
Those who guard the root
govern like spirits;
those who guard the center
have little disorder and trouble;
those who guard the ends are muddled.
Therefore, the worthy guard the root and are cautious with the center,
daring not to follow the ends.
If one can guard it without ceasing,
and goodness comes from every direction,
without being rejected or opposed,
it is fashioned into a precious vessel
that shall not be changed for ten thousand generations.
Can human effort applied to goodness be constrained?
Can depravity and the Yídí be repelled?
Can weapons and armor be eliminated?
Can the staff and whip move without sound?
Can the four directions be at peace?
Can the roads be open?
Can the ruler of men be enlightened?
The Shéncè:
the Great Man guards it and moves the four directions;
the middle scholar practices it to make ministers virtuous;
the lesser man practices it and they do not harm each other.
Its words are concise,
its methods are clear.
Can one not practice the divination of the divine texts?
Can one not maintain it?
Should one be careful not to cause harm in order to restrain the wicked?
Follow and use the Sìshí and Wǔxíng,
maintaining correct thoughts internally and externally.
The body dispels evil
and repels the inauspicious.
Visualize the images and meditate on guarding them;
act in accordance with the Qi of the four seasons;
harmonize Yīnyáng,
and encompass and govern the Guǐshén,
ordering them not to act recklessly or harm people.
From Lìdōng until Lìchūn,
the Qi of Tàiyīn prevails and is used,
and the Qi of Shǎoyáng moves subtly.
Constantly observe its intent;
as for which illnesses are caused by being used by others,
its divine officials wear black robes;
meditate on them in a quiet place for forty-five days,
up to ninety days,
and it will make one’s ears and eyes sharp and clear.
At Lìchūn, flourishing virtue lies in Rén;
the Qi governs Shǎoyáng,
and the Wángqì shifts to the East,
arousing the element of Mù.
Its Qi is gentle and benevolent;
its divine officials wear green robes.
Meditate on them in a secluded and quiet place for forty-five days,
up to ninety days,
and it will cause illnesses to vanish.
By continuing this throughout the year without ceasing,
it causes one to practice benevolence and love daily.
Before Chūnfēn,
the Qi of Shǎoyáng flourishes,
and the Qi of Tàiyáng moves subtly
to assist Shǎoyáng.
Observe its intent without doubt;
meditate deeply on its intent,
and all evils will be subdued.
On the day of Lìxià, flourishing virtue lies in Huǒ;
the Wángqì shifts to the South,
and the Qi of Tàiyáng governs with central harmony.
Its divine officials use it and attain its intent;
sweetness arises in the mouth.
The divine officials in red robes guard it,
and a hundred ghosts depart a thousand lǐ away.
On the day of Xiàzhì,
the flourishing virtue is the Qi of Tàiyáng,
which is the Qi of central harmony;
meditating on its divine officials can cure a hundred illnesses.
In the sixth month of Jìxià,
flourishing virtue governs in combination;
the Wángqì shifts to the Southwest
and returns to the Zhōnggōng.
Meditate on its divine officials in yellow robes,
making one's mouth sweet.
Meditate on this for eighteen days during each late season.
On the day of Lìqiū, flourishing virtue lies in Jīn;
the Wángqì shifts to the West,
severing and completing the ten thousand things.
Its divine officials wear white robes;
meditate on them for forty-five to ninety days.
It can eliminate illness,
and attaining its intent
makes the bones strong and brings longevity in old age.
On the day of Qiūfēn, it is the Qi of Shǎoyīn,
and the Qi of Tàiyīn moves subtly;
opposing illnesses are made compliant.
On the day of Lìdōng,
flourishing virtue lies in Shuǐ;
the Wángqì shifts to the North,
and its divine officials wear black robes.
It makes one’s will expansive and ears keen;
guarding it for forty-five to ninety days,
all illnesses are eliminated.
This Qi of the Wǔxíng and Sìshí
can internally cultivate the body
and externally govern evil.
Therefore, when Heaven uses it, there is clarity;
when Earth uses it, there is tranquility.
When Heaven uses it, there is life;
when Earth uses it, there is storage;
when Man uses it, there is prosperity.
Being able to follow the seasonal Qi
is what is meant by a loyal minister and a filial son.
This is called the Great Accord with the Way of Heaven, Earth, Yīnyáng, the Sìshí, and the Wǔxíng.
Therefore, the Dào emerges for the benevolent and worthy
and does not arise for the foolish.
At age ten,
one has twenty years of spirit.
At age twenty,
one has forty years of spirit.
At age thirty,
one has sixty years of spirit.
At age forty,
one has eighty years of spirit.
At age fifty,
one has one hundred years of spirit.
At age sixty,
one has one hundred and twenty years of spirit.
At age seventy,
one has one hundred years of spirit.
From age eighty to one hundred and twenty,
the spirit is exhausted.
In youth the spirit increases;
as one ages and withers, the spirit is extinguished;
this refers to the quintessential spirit of the wǔzàng,
and is the manifestation of the internal center.
One thousand two hundred and twenty benevolent spirits serve as its emissaries,
overseeing advancement, retreat, and observations;
ten thousand spirits are its subjects,
all following the prosperity or decline of the individual.
This is the constant principle of Tiāndì;
if one treats the spirit as if residing in the same city and governs it well,
quieting the body and preserving the spirit,
then illness will not increase,
the lifespan will be long,
and the Shénmíng will bless them.
Therefore, Tiāndì establishes the body through tranquility,
guards it with the spirit,
and flourishes it with the Dào.
Therefore, if a person can be pure and tranquil,
embrace their quintessential spirit,
and not lose their thoughts and reflections,
then malevolence and evil cannot enter.
When the True Spirit is within,
it causes the person to be constantly joyful,
exultant and not desiring to be greedy for treasures,
to argue or litigate,
or compete for merit and fame;
after a long time, one will naturally be able to see the spirit.
The spirit is two feet and five inches tall,
with attire following the wǔxíng and wǔzàng.
When the ruler is benevolent, the Dào flourishes;
when the ruler is gentle, Dé arises.
If there is the slightest evil intent in the central heart,
distant regions will become disordered because of it.
The spirit-energy flows all around,
faster than thunder and lightning;
quickly return the spirit-luminance
to illuminate the inside of oneself;
thus illness heals itself and the person governs themselves.
Therefore, a human life of one hundred and twenty years is superior longevity,
eighty years is medium longevity,
and sixty years is inferior longevity;
to end before these are all premature deaths.
This is because the spirit wanders outside,
while illness attacks within.
Thinking of the root and correcting one's conduct
causes people to love one another.
In ancient times, those who sought longevity
did not lose their Dào.
Tiāndì has constant movements,
and one must not deviate from the root;
therefore, those who seek peace and long existence
must be careful not to forget this fundamental origin of the Dào.
Therefore, a diagram is drawn to show future generations.
It displays the time when humans and things were born and received their mandates,
from the distant past until now,
without losing the transmission of types through Yīnyáng,
mutually generating and lasting a long time,
for over ten thousand myriad generations;
it cannot be lacking.
