Alternating between decline and prosperity,
the high and the low are balanced;
when prosperous, one becomes a ruler;
when declining, one becomes a subject;
prosperity brings attainment of the Dào,
while decline brings punishment.
As for filial piety,
nothing is greater than preserving the form,
for it is the lineage of the ancestors;
spreading one's name to later generations,
this is what is called a good person and a prudent subject.
Tiāndì loves them,
the wǔxíng assist them,
the four seasons benefit them,
a hundred kings employ them,
the myriad people like them,
the Guǐshén bless them,
and the spirits of the wǔzàng remain with them.
Encountering one, one gains life;
but now they are being lost.
Departing from my spiritual vessel,
returning to dust and earth,
changing without constancy,
and returning to become the myriad things.
When the Dào generates humans,
they are originally all quintessential qì,
and all have spirit.
Borrowing a form and being named "human,"
foolish people do not know how to return and complete their spirit and qì;
therefore, they lose the Dào.
If one can return and reverse their spirit and qì,
then they will complete their natural lifespan,
or even double it;
these are all people of high talent.
Or if one seeks to cross over distress,
the method for doing so
is to build a fasting chamber,
secure its doors and windows,
so that no one may enter recklessly;
go there daily to test oneself;
if not pure or not at peace, come out again;
do not force it.
Continue in this way,
gradually becoming pure and practiced, then one will be at peace.
When at peace, one no longer wishes to come out,
the mouth does not wish to speak,
looking at food and drink,
one does not wish to hear human voices.
Closing off and refining, accumulating goodness,
closing the eyes and looking back at one's own form,
the appearance and image are as if in a mirror,
or like peering at a reflection in clear water;
this is already a small achievement.
Being strict without a whip,
being majestic without weapons,
the myriad affairs govern themselves.
Is this not spiritual?
This is called the path of entering the spirit.
Guarding three is not as good as guarding two;
guarding two is not as good as guarding one.
Thinking deeply on these words,
one attains the profundity of the Dào.
When Tiān generates humans,
the myriad things are fully provided.
Thus born after ten months,
in step with the beginning and end of all things,
therefore one can cross over disasters and distress,
and achieve Tàipíng.
Superior scholars study the Dào
to assist emperors and kings;
they should cherish life and accumulate merit to last long.
Middling scholars study the Dào,
wishing to deliver their families.
Lesser scholars study the Dào
only to escape with their own bodies.
The Dào emerges for the worthy and wise,
not for the foolish.
Those who can use it gain good fortune;
for those who cannot use it,
how can there be no harm or injury?
Shàngshì (Superior scholars) and lofty worthies,
in matters regardless of size,
treat all with complete awe and reverence;
Zhòngshì (middle scholars) half-dread them,
and Xiàshì (lower scholars) have nothing at all to dread.
The reason why Shàngshì dread them is that
they reflect upon themselves
rather than looking to others.
Their minds are open and their intentions are clear, harboring no concealment;
they know the root of Yuánqì and nature.
They respect Tiān and value Dì,
as well as the Sun, the Moon, the arrayed stars,
the Wǔxíng, the four seasons,
the Liùjiǎ and Yīnyáng,
and all classes of living things that crawl, move, or stir;
none of these are born in vain.
Within the Liùhé, among the ghosts, spirits, and spectral beings,
internal and external winds, clouds, thunder, and lightning do not move in vain.
All these have Shén and presiding lords,
just as humans have signs that they manifest;
therefore, they dread them
and do not dare to act recklessly.
The reason why Zhòngshì half-dread them is that
above, they do not know that Yuánqì and nature have their methods;
they only know the wind, rain, clouds, and living things that they currently see.
They still often say that Tiān has no Shén,
and they do not dread the arrayed stars, the Sun, or the Moon,
knowing only Dàhuǒ and Běidǒu.
Xiàshì do not know that the vastness of the lands, mountains, and rivers is to be revered;
they only know how to plow the fields,
plant what they have,
and the methods for managing their families.
They do not know how to walk according to the four seasons and Wǔxíng;
they only know to follow them to plant trees
and harvest the benefits.
They do not know that the Liùjiǎ and Yīnyáng are Shén
and commonly claim that they do not exist.
Now, if an ignorant person studies, they become a Worthy;
a Worthy who studies without ceasing becomes a Shèng (Sage);
a Shèng who studies without ceasing attains the Dào;
one who studies the Dào without ceasing becomes a Xiān;
a Xiān who studies without ceasing becomes a Zhēn (Realized Being);
a Zhēn who studies without ceasing becomes a Shén;
all these are achieved through the accumulation of unceasing study.
One method is called extending life.
The Yídí follow ten thousand kinds of their own laws;
though their types are different,
they all obtain longevity.
Tiān and Dì love them,
and their bodies suffer no calamity.
The reason this is so
is called the Dào of Dàshùn (Great Accord).
When the Dào is completed within the body,
one shares the same realm as Tiān and Dì.
The ancients practiced this;
the ten thousand Shén are naturally attained.
If one wishes to know its effects,
auspicious omens will arrive of their own accord
and disasters will naturally subside.
Emperors and kings use this to govern
without using physical strength.
If they can know and practice this,
the Yídí will naturally submit;
practicing it unceasingly, one becomes a Zhēnrén.
Therefore, the teaching of the Shèngrén
does not require harnessing, prodding, or striking to succeed,
but establishes teachings based on natural disposition.
The reason why emperors and kings can pacify Tiānxià
is by pacifying everyone according to the heart of Tiānxià;
thus they win the hearts of Tiānxià.
This Dào cultivates ancient texts.
When humans are first born, they are named Shén;
then they share authority, substance, form, spirit, essence, energy, tasks, professions, and dwellings with Tiān and Dì.
Therefore, there are three places.
One Qì becomes Tiān,
one Qì becomes Dì,
one Qì becomes Man,
and the remaining Qì disperses to provide for the ten thousand things.
For this reason, one respects Tiān, values Dì, and prizes Man.
Thus, the Sānhuáng and Wǔdì all established teachers;
those in doubt would kneel to ask them.
Consequently, the state was always well-governed,
and even disasters and hardships could be healed.
The Road of Dàshùn
enables a ruler to have no worries or troubles and achieve Tàipíng (Great Peace).
If Tiān and Dì do not shake greatly,
winds and rains do not run rampant,
and the hundred Shén are at peace in their dwellings,
then Tiānxià will be free of disaster.
When the ten thousand things each stay in their places,
then there is joy and no worry.
How is this achieved?
Benevolence makes emperors and kings always joyful,
and the Dào makes them free from sorrow and bitterness.
If emperors and kings are sorrowful and bitter,
then Tiānxià is uneasy.
For emperors and kings
are the heart of Tiānxià;
the various ministers
are the limbs and backbone;
and the common people
are the hands and feet.
When the heart is sorrowful, the limbs act recklessly,
the hands and feet move without stopping,
and the common people wander and drift.
This is their natural interaction;
Tiān is also like this.
If Tiān loses the Dào,
the clouds and Qì become chaotic;
if Dì loses the Dào,
it cannot store things.
The King communicates with Tiān.
A son delights in his father,
a minister delights in his lord,
Dì delights in Tiān,
and Tiān delights in the Dào.
Thus the Qì of Tàipíng can be attained,
the Heavenly Qì will be uniformly governed,
and the Tàishànghuáng will pacify and unify all below.
Tiān and Dì harmonize and unite;
if emperors and kings practice my Dào,
what blame could there be?
The Dào
is the heart of Tiān
and the head of Tiān.
When the heart and head have already moved,
how could the limbs and body fail to follow?
Distinguish the strengths of the three Qì,
return the Shén and guard the body.
Tàiyáng is the Heavenly Qì, thus it is called Shén.
As for form,
Tàiyīn governs the Qí,
enveloping and nurturing the ten thousand things;
therefore, the essence and spirit are stored within the belly.
Thus Earthly Shén are called Qí.
As for essence,
it is the essence of the central harmony of the ten thousand things.
Thus its advance and retreat have no constancy;
the essence of Tiān, Dì, and Yīnyáng
together give birth to the ten thousand things.
This is the calendar of the Sāntǒng.
Shén governs birth,
essence governs nurturing,
and form governs completion.
These three form one divine vessel;
the three model themselves after the Ruler, Ministers, and People,
and therefore cannot exist without each other.
Thus, if the mind-Shén is agitated,
it makes the form uneasy.
Preserve it without ceasing.
If it is beneficial for it to be peaceful, it will remain;
if its peace is not utilized, it will leave.
In beginning to learn, use what is possible;
quiet it and teach it.
Over a long time, it will naturally become settled and not leave.
Yīn Qì and Yáng Qì rub and grind against each other,
and then they can generate each other.
Human Qì also cycles up and down the body,
and Shén and essence ride it to go in and out.
Shén and essence have Qì,
just as fish have water.
When Qì is cut off, Shén and essence disperse;
when water is cut off, fish perish.
Therefore, the Dào of nourishing life
lies in quieting the body and nurturing the Qì,
desiring not to be frequently angry or joyful.
In ancient times, enlightened teachers
taught emperors and kings to all quiet their bodies
and have no worries;
then the emperors and kings naturally focused.
When Tiān is joyful, the Qì of Tàipíng emerges,
and there is nothing that is not born and completed.
When Tiān is resentful, the Qì of punishment and penalty emerges,
and nothing escapes being killed or harmed;
none of the ten thousand things escape its poison.
Thus all share in the sorrow.
If Tiān does not guard its Shén,
the three lights will not be bright;
if Dì does not guard its Shén,
mountains and rivers will collapse and sink;
if Man does not guard his Shén,
the body will die and perish;
if the ten thousand things do not guard their Shén,
then they suffer damage and harm.
Therefore, one should return it; this is called strength.
Not returning and guarding oneself is called dissipation and ruin.
Since there is Heaven, there is Earth;
since there is the sun, there is the moon;
since there is *Yīn*, there is *Yáng*;
since there is spring, there is autumn;
since there is summer, there is winter;
since there is day, there is night;
since there is left, there is right;
since there is the exterior, there is the interior;
since there is white, there is black;
since there is light, there is darkness;
since there is hardness, there is softness;
since there is male, there is female;
since there is front, there is back;
since there is up, there is down;
since there is the lord, there is the minister;
since there is *Jiǎ*, there is *Yǐ*;
since there is *Zǐ*, there is *Chǒu*;
since there is five, there is six;
since there are trees, there are grasses;
since there is the female animal, there is the male animal;
since there is the male bird, there is the female bird;
since there are mountains, there are hills.
These are the roots and handles of the *Dào*.
They are the pivotal mechanism of *Yīn* and *Yáng*,
and the ultimate intent of the divine spirits.
The three breaths together form one,
which serves as the divine root (*Shéngēn*).
One is Essence (*Jīng*),
one is Spirit (*Shén*),
and one is Breath (*Qì*).
These three
share a single position,
being the original breath of Heaven, Earth, and Man.
*Shén* is received from Heaven,
*Jīng* is received from Earth,
and *Qì* is received from the Middle Harmony (*Zhōnghé*);
together they form one *Dào*.
Thus, *Shén* rides upon *Qì* to move,
and *Jīng* resides within them.
The three assist each other in governance.
Therefore, those who desire longevity
should cherish *Qì*, honor *Shén*, and value *Jīng*.
Those who wish to rectify great matters
should rectify them through non-interference (*Wúshì*).
Non-interference produces non-interference;
this is the constant law of Heaven and Earth
and the technique of nature (*Zìrán*),
like a shadow or an echo.
The superior scholar uses it to pacify the state,
the middle scholar uses it to extend his years,
and the inferior scholar uses it to manage the family.
This can be called accomplishing without doing
and governing without managing.
The Great *Dào* is level and easy,
and it is not far from one’s person;
if one inwardly cherishes one’s own person,
its governance will return to oneself.
How is it to govern the person with Virtue (*Dé*),
and how is it to govern the ten thousand people to bring about the breath of Great Harmony (*Dàhé*)?
If it is good but not pervasive,
how can there be peace?
How is it to govern the person with Benevolence (*Rén*)
and Righteousness (*Yì*),
and how is it to govern the ten thousand people?
If it is good but not pervasive,
how can there be peace?
How is it to govern the person with Ritual (*Lǐ*),
and how is it to govern the ten thousand people?
If it is good but not pervasive,
how can there be peace?
How is it to govern the person with Culture (*Wén*),
and how is it to govern the ten thousand people?
If it is good but restrictive,
preventing them from doing wrong, how is that?
If it is good but not pervasive,
how can there be peace?
How is it to govern the person [with Law],
and how is it to govern the ten thousand people?
If it is good but not pervasive,
how can there be peace?
How is it to govern the person by abolishing military weapons and armor,
and how is it to govern the ten thousand people?
If it is good but not pervasive,
how can there be peace?
However, these seven matters
cannot be absent,
nor can they be practiced exclusively.
In antiquity, divine people (*Shénrén*) governed their persons
by always having a root;
they had a great technique for governing the people.
They caused the ten thousand things to be born,
each finding its proper place,
and were able to make the six extremes and eight directions (*Bāfāng*), far and near, rejoice,
so that the ten thousand things did not lose their places.
This must be natural (*Zìrán*),
able to bring peace to the eight directions and four distant regions,
practicing grace without losing a hair’s breadth.
Now, if one cannot nourish the roots and branches,
how can one achieve governance?
Now, these seven matters of Superior Virtue (*Dé*),
Benevolence (*Rén*), Righteousness (*Yì*),
Ritual (*Lǐ*), Culture (*Wén*),
Law (*Fǎ*), and Military (*Wǔ*) are each different ways of governing;
though all are good, they may not be pervasive,
yet each has its strengths.
They cannot be discarded,
nor can they be practiced exclusively.
To govern the person, pacify the state, and bring about Great Peace (*Tàipíng*),
one must deeply grasp the secret;
that which drives these is the *Dào*.
Combined, they maintain the One (*Shǒu Yī*);
divided, they are without limit.
The Supreme Deity (*Shàngdì*) practices this;
it is so deep as to be immeasurable,
and it is named the Formula of All-Pervasive Illumination.
Heaven produces humans in three grades:
the first is born of Heaven,
the second is born of Earth,
and the third is of the human species.
The one who receives his mandate from Heaven is the lord (*Jūn*),
the one who receives his mandate from Earth is the minister (*Chén*),
and the ones who receive their mandate from humans are the people (*Mín*).
The lord acts in response to Heaven,
the minister acts in response to Earth,
following and receiving from above;
those who are the people belong to the ministers
and serve them in turn.
Only when these three breaths work together as one governance
can success be achieved.
Therefore, for the one above to be at peace,
his ministers must be excellent.
When the duties of the ministers are orderly,
the people will follow the constant way.
When both people and ministers are good,
their lord will be enlightened,
and his governance will be long-lasting.
Great Peace (*Tàipíng*) is when the *Dào* is practiced,
the three breaths are all good,
and they harmonize with the statutes;
they embrace the *Dào* and Virtue (*Dé*) and do not harm one another.
Thus, the Great Man (*Dàrén*) manages the *Dào*
to pacify all under Heaven,
save the four seas,
and extend grace to the *Yídí* barbarians,
so that calamities cannot arise.
Auspicious signs appear daily,
and misfortune cannot come.
The middle scholar learns the *Dào* to become a minister of the state,
assisting in its governance,
saving his family,
and averting disasters.
The next level of managing the *Dào*
is to neglect one’s parents
and wander far away;
such virtue is uniquely small and thin,
and barely saves one’s own body.
How can such a person assist an enlightened king or help the state?
Those who can pacify the four seas are helped by Heaven;
those who are ministers help with governance
and plan with the Earth.
Those who barely save themselves
have a narrow and small *Dào* that offers nothing to govern.
These three types of people all transcend the world;
do they differ in the greatness of their longevity?
The Shénrén said:
Practice clearly to emulate the Dào,
and observe in whom life resides.
It causes a person to become brilliantly awakened,
knowing from where life originates.
Those who examine the laws
maintain their correctness.
Humans are born according to the law of Yīnyáng;
Yáng is always upright,
Yīn is always perverse;
Yáng is always present,
Yīn is always absent;
Yáng always flourishes,
Yīn always withers;
Yáng always generates,
Yīn always kills.
Humans undergo three changes daily,
symbolizing the three Qì;
their governance is distinct and different,
contending and clashing with one another,
not following each other.
But by practicing to make it constant
and guarding one's physical form,
there is good fortune. Only those who possess the Zhēndào
can focus their essence and distinguish themselves.
Those who do not learn
will not know the effects of the Shén departing or staying;
things that are manifested immediately
cannot be hidden.
Therefore, the Jūnzǐ governs the physical body and does not govern ghosts.
When a person is not sleeping,
walking, sitting, and speaking,
clearly distinguishing white and black,
walking and standing upright,
and using refined language as a standard,
this is the Shén being present within the person.
When they close their eyes and lie down,
the light and shadow are stored within;
what is thought of is obtained,
but they do not speak;
the Shén is inside.
When they are in a deep sleep,
the Jīngshén departs to wander,
the body cannot move,
the mouth cannot speak,
the ears cannot hear;
merging with various perversities,
only the Qì remains;
this is clear evidence.
Therefore, one must not fail to constantly guard the Jīngshén;
guarding it leads to longevity,
losing it leads to the end of life.
Those who attain the Dào
do so through their will and thoughts;
those who lose the Dào
also do so through their will and thoughts.
The Dàdào transforms without constancy,
extending ten thousand lǐ across;
infinite above and below,
flowing through the six directions;
guarding it brings good fortune,
not guarding it brings harm;
the opening and closing of Yīnyáng is the constant.
It is entrusted to those who possess the Dào,
making good people practice it;
their lifespan will match the term of Heaven and Earth.
Virtue has superior and inferior qualities,
and matters have roots and branches;
all matters are governed by the Dào;
those about to flourish obtain the good,
those about to decline obtain the evil.
It is like the land:
obtaining good soil brings goodness,
obtaining thin soil brings evil.
The good aligns above with Heaven,
while the lowly dwell in the marshes.
The one who sits is the host,
the one who travels is the passing guest.
This is the fullness of the Dào;
good people's actions result in blessings,
evil people's actions result in disasters.
Good people obtain it to form blessings and virtue.
The noble obtain it to ride in carriages,
the lowly obtain it to walk on foot.
Sages and worthies obtain it to transcend the world;
when the Xiǎorén obtain it,
they do not harm or rob each other.
All of this is the Dào.
Teaching is not seen twice,
and time does not return.
Urgently teach the Dìwáng,
to make them practice the Dào of Tàipíng.
When the Dào is practiced,
the self attains transcendence from the world,
and merit aids all living beings within the six directions.
